entries.core_meaning_summary: Inflected definite determiner marking a noun phrase, modifier, nominalized element, or infinitive as contextually identifiable, specific, or generic, and also functioning independently as a third-person pronoun.

senses.definition: Marks a common noun or noun phrase as identifiable from prior mention, immediate context, shared knowledge, possession, or as representing a whole class or generic category.
senses.grammatical_frame: article agreeing in gender, number, and case with a common noun (with or without demonstratives or possessives)

senses.definition: Accompanies proper personal, geographic, or ethnic/group names, particularly in direct-object, genitive, or narrative-reference positions, though proper names also appear without it.
glosses: the (untranslated in English with personal names)
senses.grammatical_frame: article + proper personal, geographic, or group noun

senses.definition: Links an adjective, prepositional phrase, or genitive noun attributively to an already definite head noun, either by repeating the article after the noun or by enclosing the modifier between the article and its noun.
senses.grammatical_frame: articular noun + repeated article + modifier (adjective, prepositional phrase, or genitive), or article + genitive modifier + head noun

senses.definition: Turns an adjective, participle, adverb, or prepositional phrase into a noun phrase denoting a person, group, or thing characterized by that word or phrase.
senses.grammatical_frame: article + adjective, participle, adverb, or prepositional phrase without an expressed head noun (or in apposition)

senses.definition: Nominalizes an infinitive verb (with its accusative subject) so the entire verbal clause functions as a case-marked noun phrase, here a genitive complement of a passive verb of decision.
senses.grammatical_frame: genitive singular neuter article (τοῦ) + infinitive (+ accusative subject)

senses.definition: Stands alone without a following noun or modifier as an independent pronoun referring back to previously introduced participants, especially with δέ to mark a shift of actor or response in narrative.
senses.grammatical_frame: article standing alone as pronominal subject + δέ

entries.collocations_and_notes: Co-occurs in predicate-position order with demonstratives (e.g., ὁ ἀσπασμὸς οὗτος in LUK 1:29; Τοῦτον τὸν Μωϋσῆν in ACT 7:35; Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι in ACT 16:20; ἡ ζώνη αὕτη in ACT 21:11; αὕτη ἡ σοφία in JAS 3:15) and with possessive genitives. With αὐτός in attributive position, τῷ αὐτῷ means 'the same' (LUK 23:40). Shows anaphoric tracking across clauses (e.g., πρὸς τὸν κριτήν, καὶ ὁ κριτής... τῷ πράκτορι, καὶ ὁ πράκτωρ in LUK 12:58; τὴν ζώνην... ἡ ζώνη αὕτη in ACT 21:11). Nested articles occur when a genitive modifier sits between the head article and noun (τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων in HEB 9:7). Proper names and titles vary between articular and anarthrous forms even within the same verse (e.g., Ἀβραὰμ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ in MAT 1:2; ὁ Θεός vs. Θεοῦ in ROM 11:33 / 1TH 4:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A high-frequency coordinating conjunction linking parallel words, phrases, and clauses, also functioning as a narrative connector and as an additive or emphatic adverb ('also, even').

senses.definition: Joins grammatically parallel elements—such as nouns, adjectives, prepositional phrases, participles, infinitives, or subordinate clauses—into a coordinated pair or series.
senses.grammatical_frame: Coordinating conjunction linking words, phrases, or parallel clauses; also correlative with τε (τε ... καί)

senses.definition: Connects successive clauses or sentences in narrative, instruction, dialogue, or prophetic speech, marking continuation, temporal sequence, or resulting action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause- or sentence-initial conjunction introducing sequential clauses, statements, or questions

senses.definition: Links statements, attributes, or actions that stand in tension or contradiction with one another, highlighting a contrast despite their pairing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Coordinating conjunction joining semantically opposed clauses, participles, or attributes

senses.definition: Marks an additional participant, action, or circumstance as included alongside others or singled out for emphasis.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverbial focus particle preceding a noun phrase, prepositional phrase, or verb (including after δέ, εἰ, or a relative pronoun)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in correlative pairing ὅ τε ... καί ('both ... and', ACT 17:14) and in recurring transitional combinations such as καὶ νῦν (ACT 7:34; ACT 23:21), καὶ οὕτως (1CO 11:28), καὶ διὰ τοῦτο (LUK 14:20), and εἰ καί (PHP 3:12). Very commonly opens narrative sentences or direct-speech follow-ups (e.g., MRK 6:21; LUK 10:29; JHN 7:1; REV 17:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A third-person pronoun referring to previously mentioned or contextually understood persons, things, or propositions, also functioning intensively ('self') and, with the article, to denote identity ('the same').

senses.definition: Refers anaphorically to a person, group, object, or preceding action as a verbal object, recipient, prepositional complement, or subject of a participial or infinitival clause.
glosses: he/she (in infinitive or genitive absolute clauses)
senses.grammatical_frame: Oblique cases (accusative, dative, genitive) as verbal/prepositional complement, accusative subject of infinitive, or genitive absolute subject

senses.definition: Modifies a noun or substantival phrase in the genitive to indicate possession, kinship, association, or a whole of which something is a part.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adnominal genitive pronoun following or preceding a noun phrase (possessive, associative, or partitive)

senses.definition: Highlights the identity or agency of the grammatical subject, either reinforcing a personal pronoun or contrasting the subject with another party.
senses.grammatical_frame: Nominative pronoun standing alone as contrastive subject or paired with a first-person pronoun (αὐτὸς ἐγώ)

senses.definition: Indicates identity or sameness with what is referenced; with the preposition ἐπί and neuter article (ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό), denotes assembling together in unity or a single place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive position with the definite article (ὁ αὐτός, τὸ αὐτό)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the genitive after nouns to mark possession, kinship, or association (e.g., οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ in MAT 12:1; MRK 5:31; τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ in MAT 1:2). Regularly serves as the dative recipient of speech or giving verbs (εἶπεν αὐτοῖς, λέγει αὐτῷ, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ). In participial and infinitival clauses, it marks the subject via genitive absolute (αὐτοῦ καταβαίνοντος in JHN 4:51) or accusative with infinitive (ἐν τῷ ἱερατεύειν αὐτὸν in LUK 1:8; αὐτὸν δεῖ μεῖναι in REV 17:10). Fixed patterns include the prepositional phrase ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό ('together', ACT 4:26) and attributive ὁ αὐτός ('the same', 1CO 12:5).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The second-person personal pronoun referring to the person or people being addressed.

senses.definition: Refers to a single person (or God) directly addressed by the speaker or writer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular second-person pronoun in nominative (σύ), genitive (σοῦ, σου), dative (σοί, σοι), and accusative (σέ, σε) functioning as subject, possessive modifier, direct or indirect object, or object of prepositions (e.g., ἐν, πρός, εἰς, μετά, ἔμπροσθεν)

senses.definition: Refers to two or more persons directly addressed as a group by the speaker or writer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural second-person pronoun in nominative (ὑμεῖς), genitive (ὑμῶν), dative (ὑμῖν), and accusative (ὑμᾶς) functioning as clause or infinitive subject, possessive or partitive modifier, direct or indirect object, recipient in verbless greetings, or object of prepositions (e.g., ἐν, παρά, ἐξ, πρός, διά, ὑπό, ὑπέρ, ἀπό)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Inflects across singular (σύ, σοῦ/σου, σοί/σοι, σέ/σε) and plural (ὑμεῖς, ὑμῶν, ὑμῖν, ὑμᾶς) forms; enclitic singular oblique forms regularly follow their host noun, verb, or preposition, whereas emphatic or contrastive uses appear explicitly in the nominative (MAT 26:73, MRK 13:9, LUK 3:22, ACT 11:16) or in fronted positions (MAT 13:16, 2PE 2:3). Common patterns include epistolary and liturgical greetings with the dative (Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν, JHN 20:19; χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη, ROM 1:7, GAL 1:3, 1TH 1:1), speech introduction (λέγω ὑμῖν, LUK 12:51), possessive genitives following articular nouns (e.g., τὴν γυναῖκά σου, MAT 1:20), and prepositional phrases (πρὸς σέ, ἐν σοί, μετὰ σοῦ, ἐν ὑμῖν, ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, ὑφ’ ὑμῶν). Note JHN 3:7, where the singular addressee (σοι) and plural group (ὑμᾶς) occur in the same sentence.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A postpositive coordinating particle used to link successive clauses, signal narrative or topical transitions, mark contrast, or pair balanced elements.

senses.definition: Connects successive events, statements, speaker turns, or new topics in narrative and discourse without strong opposition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive conjunction connecting clauses or sentences, often with temporal clauses, genitive absolutes, prepositional topic phrases (e.g., περὶ δέ), or articular pronouns (ὁ δέ, οἱ δέ) marking a shift of subject or speaker

senses.definition: Introduces a contrast, antithesis, exception, or alternative condition relative to a preceding clause or group.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive conjunction contrasting clauses, subjects, participles, or conditional alternatives (including ἐὰν δέ and εἰ δὲ μήγε)

senses.definition: Pairs complementary, parallel, or appositional elements in an argument, description, or title list.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive conjunction pairing balanced phrases or clauses (such as τοῦτο μὲν ... τοῦτο δέ, ὁμοίως δὲ καί, or appositional nouns)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Always postpositive, normally standing in second position in its clause or phrase (or after a preposition + noun/article, as in περὶ δὲ τῆς ἀναστάσεως or ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ μὴ ἔχοντος); elided as δ’ before a vowel (MAT 10:33). Frequently pairs with articular pronouns to mark speaker or subject changes (ὁ δέ, οἱ δέ; MRK 10:26, LUK 15:29, LUK 22:38) and combines in recurring collocations such as εἰ δὲ μήγε (2CO 11:16), ἐὰν δέ (ROM 13:4, 1CO 16:10), ὁμοίως δὲ καί (1CO 7:4), and τοῦτο μὲν ... τοῦτο δέ (HEB 10:33).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Dative-governing preposition marking spatial, social, or inner location, temporal setting, sphere or state, and means or instrument.

senses.definition: Marks physical location, enclosure, or position within a place, region, structure, or object, including physical pregnancy (ἐν γαστρί) and bodily dwelling.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative noun (place, region, building, body part, or physical object)

senses.definition: Marks presence, status, or activity within a community, crowd, assembly, or group of people.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative plural personal pronoun or collective noun

senses.definition: Indicates interior presence in a person's heart or inner self, or spiritual union and relational sphere with Christ.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative personal noun/pronoun or inner faculty (e.g., καρδία)

senses.definition: Identifies a body of scripture or written text as the locus in which statements are recorded.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative noun denoting writings or scripture, with verb of writing

senses.definition: Marks the point, period, or contemporaneous event during which an action takes place, including articular infinitive constructions indicating simultaneous time.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative time noun, or ἐν τῷ + infinitive with accusative subject

senses.definition: Indicates the state, condition, mode of existence, authority, or boundary within which a person acts or exists.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative abstract noun or noun of state/condition (e.g., σάρξ, ἐξουσία, ἀλήθεια)

senses.definition: Marks the instrument, resource, authority, utterance, or evidence by means of which something is accomplished or recognized.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative noun, demonstrative pronoun, or nominalized clause denoting means or basis

senses.definition: Marks the equivalent given in an exchange or the quantitative rate/yield produced by an action.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative noun (with verb of exchanging) or dative numeral (indicating yield)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Governs exclusively the dative case across spatial, temporal, social, psychological, instrumental, and circumstantial relations. Notable recurring patterns include: ἐν τῷ + infinitive expressing contemporaneous action (MAT 13:4, LUK 9:33); ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχειν as an idiom for pregnancy (MAT 1:18); ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ marking union or sphere of relation (ROM 16:3, EPH 3:21); ἐν τούτῳ introducing the basis of recognition (1JN 4:2); and ἐν τριάκοντα / ἑξήκοντα / ἑκατόν indicating yield or proportion (MRK 4:20).

entries.core_meaning_summary: First-person personal pronoun designating the speaker alone in the singular or the speaker together with others in the plural across all grammatical cases.

senses.definition: Refers to the individual speaker as the grammatical subject of a finite verb or infinitive, typically expressing explicit identification, emphasis, or contrast with another participant.
senses.grammatical_frame: nominative singular (ἐγώ) as subject of finite verb, or accusative singular (ἐμέ / με) as subject of infinitive

senses.definition: Refers to the individual speaker as the direct object, indirect object, experiencer, possessor, relational associate, or prepositional complement in a clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: oblique singular cases: accusative (ἐμέ / με), dative (ἐμοί / μοι), or genitive (ἐμοῦ / μου), directly governed by a verb, adjective, noun, or preposition

senses.definition: Refers to the speaker together with one or more associated persons as the subject of a finite verb or infinitive, often marking group identity or contrast.
senses.grammatical_frame: nominative plural (ἡμεῖς) as subject of finite verb, or accusative plural (ἡμᾶς) as subject of infinitive

senses.definition: Refers to the speaker and one or more associated persons as the direct object, recipient, beneficiary, possessor, or prepositional complement.
senses.grammatical_frame: oblique plural cases: accusative (ἡμᾶς), dative (ἡμῖν), or genitive (ἡμῶν), governed by a verb, noun, or preposition

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in idiomatic and contrastive constructions: nominative ἐγώ or ἡμεῖς is expressed explicitly to mark emphasis or contrast with another person (e.g., JHN 3:30, JHN 8:22, MAT 25:27, 1JN 4:10). Forms the crasis κἀγώ (καὶ + ἐγώ) in JHN 10:15. Occurs in prepositional phrases with μετά (MAT 1:23), ὑπέρ (MAT 10:37, MRK 9:40, 2CO 7:7), κατά (MRK 9:40), μεταξύ and πρός (LUK 16:26), ἀπό (LUK 22:42), ἐν (2CO 13:3, PHP 1:26), and διά (2TI 4:17). Enclitic oblique forms (μου, μοι, με) follow their governing head word, while accented forms (ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ) occur after prepositions or for contrast. Also functions as subject of an infinitive in the accusative (ACT 22:17, ACT 27:1, 2CO 7:7) and in a genitive absolute (ACT 22:17).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To exist, be present, or serve as the copula linking a subject to its identity, quality, location, or state.

senses.definition: To link a subject to a predicate noun, adjective, pronoun, articular participle, or adverb of manner (οὕτως) in order to state identity, role, equivalence, character, or condition; includes infinitival clauses with an accusative subject.
senses.grammatical_frame: Finite verb, participle, or infinitive + predicate nominative/accusative (noun, adjective, pronoun, or adverb οὕτως)

senses.definition: To exist, occur, be present, or belong to someone, without a nominal or adjectival predicate; often with a locative expression or a dative of the beneficiary/possessor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Absolute or with locative phrase / dative of beneficiary or possessor (ἡμῖν ἐστιν)

senses.definition: To be situated in a place, dwell within someone, remain in company with someone (σύν + dative), or be available for a purpose (εἰς τό + infinitive).
senses.grammatical_frame: Finite verb or infinitive + locative adverb (ὅπου/ἐκεῖ), ἐν + dative, σύν + dative, or εἰς τό + infinitive

senses.definition: With εἰς + accusative, to come to be or be united into a resulting state or entity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Future finite verb + εἰς + accusative

senses.definition: To serve as an auxiliary verb combined with a present or perfect participle to form a periphrastic imperfect, pluperfect, or perfect construction expressing ongoing activity or resulting state.
senses.grammatical_frame: Imperfect indicative or present subjunctive + present or perfect participle

entries.collocations_and_notes: Highly irregular suppletive paradigm across the sample: present (εἰ, ἐστίν/ἐστιν, ἐσμέν), imperfect (ἦς, ἦν, ἦσαν), future (ἔσται, ἔσονται), imperative (ἔστω), subjunctive (ᾖ), infinitive (εἶναι), and participle (ὄντας). Functions both as an unmarked equational/attributive copula and in idiomatic expressions such as οὐδέν ἐστιν ("is nothing", JHN 8:54), δοκούντων εἶναί τι ("who seem to be something", GAL 2:6), and ἐν + dative for spiritual or spatial indwelling (2TI 1:6; 1JN 5:20). With a dative noun/pronoun, marks possession or benefit (ACT 19:25; ROM 13:4). Frequently pairs with present or perfect participles to form periphrastic verb phrases (LUK 1:21; LUK 5:17; JHN 18:30; JAS 5:15).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To express words vocally or mentally—chiefly to say, tell, ask, command, or refer to someone by a name or title.

senses.definition: To utter words or communicate a statement, declaration, teaching, or claim, with the addressee optionally marked by a dative or by πρός + accusative and the speech introduced directly or with ὅτι.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active finite verb or participle + direct speech or ὅτι-clause; optional dative or πρός + accusative addressee

senses.definition: To direct, instruct, or request that someone perform an action, either by uttering an imperative or by speaking an authoritative word (dative λόγῳ).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb + optional dative or πρός + accusative addressee + imperative speech (or instrumental dative λόγῳ)

senses.definition: To pose a question or give a reply in conversation, including the affirmative/conciliatory formula Σὺ λέγεις ("You say [so]").
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb + optional dative addressee + interrogative or responsive direct speech; or absolute Σὺ λέγεις

senses.definition: To speak a message, discuss a topic, or intend a meaning, taking a noun phrase or relative pronoun as its direct object rather than quoting a full clause directly.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb + accusative object (noun phrase, substantival prepositional phrase, or relative pronoun)

senses.definition: To accompany another verb of speaking (such as crying out, asking, or answering) or a narrative action as a participle introducing direct discourse.
senses.grammatical_frame: Present participle (λέγων / λέγοντες) following a verb of speech or action + direct speech

senses.definition: To reason or tell oneself inwardly without necessarily voicing the words aloud.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active infinitive + ἐν ἑαυτοῖς + direct thought

senses.definition: To be designated, known, or addressed by a particular name, title, or epithet.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive participle (ὁ λεγόμενος) + predicate title or name

entries.collocations_and_notes: Uses suppletive stems across the sample: present/imperfect (λέγω/ἔλεγον) and aorist (εἶπον/εἶπαν, imperative εἰπέ, subjunctive εἴπωμεν/εἴπῃ, genitive participle εἰπόντος). Frequently introduces solemn pronouncements with Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι (MAT 26:21), Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι (JHN 10:7), Ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι (LUK 21:3), and λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι (LUK 3:8). The addressee is marked either by a dative indirect object (εἶπεν αὐτοῖς, λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ, εἶπέν μοι) or by πρός + accusative (εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς, Ἔλεγεν... πρὸς τοὺς... Ἰουδαίους). Recitative ὅτι often marks the transition to direct speech (MRK 14:58; LUK 13:14; JHN 6:42; ACT 28:25) as well as indirect assertions (1JN 1:8). Note the accusative-content object ῥῆμα ἓν in ACT 28:25 and the relative-object constructions in JHN 15:20 and 2TI 2:7.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A preposition governing the accusative case that marks spatial movement into or toward a goal, orientation of attention or trust, intended purpose or result, extent/respect, and temporal duration.

senses.definition: Marks the spatial destination, boundary, or interior into or toward which someone or something moves, is sent, cast, or enters, both literally and metaphorically.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + accusative with verbs of motion, sending, placing, or spreading

senses.definition: Indicates location at or upon a place, or the point reached by a sound or perception, with verbs of sitting or happening.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + accusative with stative or event verbs

senses.definition: Denotes the person or object toward which visual attention, personal trust, or an attitude/boast is directed.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + accusative with verbs of looking, believing, or attitude nouns

senses.definition: Marks the intended goal, purpose, resulting state, or role/status into which someone or something is appointed, sent, or turns out (including with articular infinitives).
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + accusative (noun, pronoun, or articular infinitive τὸ + infinitive)

senses.definition: Specifies the scope, distribution, degree, or point of reference with respect to which an action or quality applies.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + accusative (quantifiers, neuter adjectives, or plural pronouns)

senses.definition: Indicates unending temporal duration or extent in the fixed phrase εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
senses.grammatical_frame: εἰς + accusative temporal noun (τὸν αἰῶνα)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Governs the accusative case exclusively across all attested examples. Frequently paired with ἐκ/ἀπό to mark the endpoint of movement from an origin (JHN 4:47, ROM 5:12). Forms fixed adverbial and idiomatic phrases such as εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ('forever', HEB 5:6, 2JN 1:2), εἰς τὸ παντελές ('completely', LUK 13:11), εἰς κενόν ('in vain', 1TH 3:5), εἰς τὰ ἴδια ('to one's own home', JHN 19:27), and βλέπειν εἰς πρόσωπον ('to regard outward status/show partiality', MAT 22:16). With πιστεύω it marks the personal object of trust (JHN 8:30, JHN 12:37), and with articular infinitives it expresses purpose (1TH 3:5).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A primary negative particle used to deny or negate statements of fact, individual clause constituents, emphatic future possibilities (with μή), and rhetorical or alternative questions.

senses.definition: Negates an indicative verb or declarative clause, asserting that an action, state, or condition does not or did not take place, including in conditional protases with εἰ and counterfactual apodoses with ἄν.
senses.grammatical_frame: modifying an indicative verb in declarative, relative, or conditional clauses (with εἰ or ἄν)

senses.definition: Combines with μή before a subjunctive verb to form an emphatic denial that an event will occur.
senses.grammatical_frame: οὐ μή + aorist subjunctive verb

senses.definition: Negates a specific phrase, noun, pronoun, adjective, participle, or subordinate clause (frequently contrasted with ἀλλά), or reverses the force of a following modifier (as in μετ’ οὐ πολύ).
senses.grammatical_frame: preceding a noun, pronoun, adjective, prepositional phrase, participle, or ὅτι clause

senses.definition: Introduces a question expecting a positive or reflective affirmation, or stands alone as an elliptical negative alternative in a disjunctive question.
senses.grammatical_frame: clause-initial in an interrogative sentence, or accented οὔ after ἤ in an alternative question

entries.collocations_and_notes: Exhibits standard phonological and accentual variation: οὐ before consonants, οὐκ before smooth-breathing vowels (MAT 1:25, LUK 22:60), οὐχ before rough-breathing vowels (LUK 17:18, 2CO 3:5), and accented οὔ when standing independently before punctuation (MRK 12:14). Frequently forms contrastive or exceptive patterns such as οὐ ... ἀλλά ('not ... but', JHN 3:17, ROM 9:16, 1CO 15:10, HEB 2:16, HEB 10:39) and οὐ ... εἰ μή ('not ... except', MAT 13:57, GAL 1:19). Co-occurs with indefinite negative οὐδέν to reinforce negation (JHN 12:19), and pairs with μή + subjunctive in emphatic denials (MAT 10:23, 1TH 5:3). Within the same verses, μή regularly negates non-indicative or participial/subordinate constructions (MRK 12:14, JHN 15:24, 2PE 3:9, 1JN 5:12, REV 9:20) in contrast to οὐ with indicative verbs.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A relative pronoun that introduces a subordinate clause describing or identifying a preceding referent, or stands independently for an unspecified person or thing.

senses.definition: Links a subordinate descriptive or identifying clause to an explicit person, group, object, place, time, or concept in the main clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: relative pronoun agreeing in gender and number with an explicit antecedent and taking case from its grammatical function in the relative clause (or attracted to the antecedent's genitive or dative case)

senses.definition: Introduces a relative clause without an explicit noun antecedent, denoting a general or unspecified person or the content/events referred to by the verb.
senses.grammatical_frame: headless (substantival) relative pronoun functioning without an explicit external noun antecedent (sometimes paired with a correlative demonstrative such as ἐκεῖνος)

senses.definition: Begins a new sentence or major clause to carry forward the narrative about a participant already introduced in preceding discourse.
senses.grammatical_frame: clause-initial or sentence-initial relative pronoun continuing reference across a discourse boundary

entries.collocations_and_notes: Agrees in gender and number with its antecedent while taking the case required by its role in the relative clause, though it is occasionally attracted into the genitive or dative case of its antecedent (e.g., MRK 7:13; ACT 1:21; EPH 4:1). Appears with prepositions (e.g., ἐξ ἧς in MAT 1:16; δι’ οὗ in HEB 1:2; ὑπὲρ ἧς in 2TH 1:5; εἰς ἥν in 1PE 3:20) and in possessive dative constructions with ὄνομα (LUK 2:25). May take a subjunctive verb in purpose or indefinite-like contexts (HEB 8:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A near-deictic demonstrative pronoun and determiner used to point out specific persons, objects, times, or discourse content already mentioned or about to be stated.

senses.definition: Modifies a noun to single out a person, group, object, time period, or event as immediate in the speaker's situation or current narrative context.
senses.grammatical_frame: demonstrative determiner modifying an articular noun (typically in predicate position)

senses.definition: Stands independently in place of a noun to identify a person, group, or concrete item in the scene or discourse, or to resume an immediately preceding participial subject.
senses.grammatical_frame: substantival pronoun (masculine, feminine, or neuter); also used resumptively after a substantival participle

senses.definition: Refers backward to previously spoken words, actions, teachings, or events, or points forward to an explanatory clause or statement.
senses.grammatical_frame: substantival pronoun (commonly neuter singular or plural, or attracted in gender to a predicate noun) referring anaphorically to prior discourse or cataphorically to a clause with ἵνα, ὅτι, or ὅταν

senses.definition: Combines with a preposition to indicate the reason, cause, or grounds for an action or conclusion.
senses.grammatical_frame: neuter singular accusative as object of a causal preposition (διὰ τοῦτο, παρὰ τοῦτο)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently placed in predicate position when modifying an articular noun (e.g., ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη in MRK 8:12; ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα in JHN 10:21). Contrasted with ἐκεῖνος in MAT 23:23 ("these things ... those things"). Can resume a preceding participial subject for emphasis (MRK 13:13). When serving as subject before a copula and a predicate noun, it often agrees in gender with the predicate noun (e.g., αὕτη ... διαθήκη in ROM 11:27; αὕτη ... ἡ μαρτυρία in 1JN 5:9). Common causal prepositional phrases include διὰ τοῦτο (JHN 13:11) and οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο (1CO 12:16).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The supreme divine being, worshipped as Creator, Father, and Judge; also used generally for a deity on an altar inscription.

senses.definition: The supreme, living, and invisible divine being of Israel and the Christian proclamation—creator, sovereign ruler, judge, and source of revelation, peace, and salvation—frequently contrasted with human beings, earthly rulers, or idols.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine singular noun, usually articular (ὁ Θεός) or anarthrous in prepositional and genitive phrases (κατὰ Θεόν, ἀπὸ Θεοῦ, Θεοῦ δοῦλοι)

senses.definition: The supreme deity viewed in covenantal or familial relationship to believers or to Christ, especially in apposition with Πατήρ ("Father") or Κύριος ("Lord") and with possessive pronouns ("our/their God").
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine singular noun in apposition with Πατήρ or Κύριος, or modified by possessive genitive pronoun (ἡμῶν, αὐτῶν)

senses.definition: An unspecified deity or object of religious devotion, used in an Athenian dedicatory inscription that the speaker subsequently connects to the true creator deity.
senses.grammatical_frame: anarthrous masculine singular dative with adjective (ΑΓΝΩΣΤΩ ΘΕΩ) in a dedicatory inscription

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very commonly occurs with the definite article (ὁ Θεός) and in recurring genitive constructions (ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἡ γνῶσις τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐπαγγελίαι τοῦ Θεοῦ) as well as prepositional phrases (ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ, παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ, κατὰ Θεόν, ἀπὸ Θεοῦ). In greeting formulas it is regularly paired with Κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός (2TH 1:2; PHM 1:3). In ACT 17:23 it appears anarthrously in a pagan altar inscription (ΑΓΝΩΣΤΩ ΘΕΩ) before being identified with the deity proclaimed by the speaker.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Subordinating conjunction introducing declarative content clauses, direct quotations, or causal explanations.

senses.definition: Introduces a subordinate clause stating the content, fact, or proposition perceived, known, believed, taught, spoken, or written, including epexegetical clauses explaining a demonstrative pronoun and topicalized clauses placed before the main verb.
senses.grammatical_frame: subordinating conjunction + indicative clause, after verbs of perception, cognition, belief, communication, or impersonal expressions, or epexegetical to a pronoun (τοῦτο)

senses.definition: Introduces direct spoken or written discourse immediately following a verb of saying or speaking, retaining the deictic pronouns, person, and mood (including imperatives) of the original speaker.
senses.grammatical_frame: conjunction after verb of speaking (εἶπεν, εἴρηκεν, λέγω) + verbatim direct speech

senses.definition: Introduces a direct question addressed to listeners, expressing surprise or challenge regarding someone's behavior (either as an interrogative asking for a reason or as a speech marker framing an incredulous question).
senses.grammatical_frame: clause-initial in an interrogative sentence following a verb of speaking (ἔλεγον)

senses.definition: Introduces a clause giving the reason, ground, evidence, or motivation for a preceding or surrounding statement, command, woe, or emotional state (such as joy or compassion).
senses.grammatical_frame: subordinating conjunction + indicative clause, following or opening a main clause to state cause or ground

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often paired with verbs of perception, cognition, and communication (ἰδών, ἀκούω, γινώσκω, οἶδα, λέγω, γέγραπται), where it can introduce either indirect content or verbatim direct speech (e.g., MAT 13:11; JHN 9:23). Frequently pairs with correlative demonstratives or adverbs (e.g., διὰ τοῦτο ... ὅτι, οὕτως ... ὅτι, ἐν τούτῳ ... ὅτι, τοῦτο ὅτι). In MRK 2:16, the second occurrence (Ὅτι μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει;) introduces a direct question posed by critics, functioning either as an interrogative ("why?") or as a direct-speech marker framing a questioning statement. Also appears in asseverative formulas (πιστὸς δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ὅτι, 2CO 1:18).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Quantifier denoting totality, completeness, or every individual member of a set, functioning either adjectivally with nouns and pronouns or substantivally as a pronoun.

senses.definition: Modifies a plural noun, plural pronoun, or plural substantivized expression to indicate the complete set without exception.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective agreeing in gender, number, and case with a plural nominal or pronoun

senses.definition: Modifies a singular noun accompanied by the definite article to express the whole extent or entirety of a collective body or authority.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective in predicate position with an articular singular noun

senses.definition: Modifies an anarthrous singular countable noun or singular substantivized clause/participle to refer distributively to each individual member of a class, or collectively to any member whatsoever.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective agreeing with an anarthrous singular countable noun or generic nominal expression

senses.definition: Modifies an anarthrous singular abstract noun to express complete degree or every form of a quality or disposition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective agreeing with an anarthrous singular abstract noun

senses.definition: Stands alone without an expressed head noun, in the masculine plural to denote all persons in view, or in the neuter plural to denote all things.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival plural without a governing noun

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently stands in predicate position before or after an articular noun (`πᾶς ὁ λαός`, `πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαί`, `τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν ... πάντα`, `τὴν ἐξουσίαν ... πᾶσαν`), with personal pronouns (`πάντας ὑμᾶς`, `πάντες αὐτούς`), or with articular participles and prepositional phrases (`πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων`, `πάντες οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ`). In 1CO 13:7, repeated `πάντα` fronts four consecutive verbs as an inclusive object. In MAT 15:6 / ACT 4:10 / 2PE 3:16 etc., notice both articular and anarthrous plural nouns (`πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαί` vs. `πάσαις ἐπιστολαῖς`).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Primary negative particle used in commands, purpose and conditional clauses, non-finite verb phrases, emphatic future denials, and negative-expectation questions.

senses.definition: Negates an imperative verb or stands elliptically in a directive to forbid or dissuade an action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Particle with imperative verb or elliptical in a directive

senses.definition: Marks negative purpose, desired avoidance, or requested restraint in subordinate clauses introduced by a conjunction or prepositional infinitive phrase.
senses.grammatical_frame: With subjunctive after `ἵνα` or with infinitive after `πρὸς τό`

senses.definition: Negates the condition in a protasis introduced by `ἐάν`, indicating what does not take place as the basis for a consequence.
senses.grammatical_frame: With subjunctive in conditional clause introduced by `ἐάν`

senses.definition: Combines with `εἰ` after a negative or restrictive statement to mark the sole exception or exclusion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Fixed combination `εἰ μή` introducing an exception

senses.definition: Combines with `οὐ` to express an emphatic denial or assurance that an event will not happen.
senses.grammatical_frame: Double negative `οὐ μή` with aorist subjunctive or future indicative

senses.definition: Negates a non-finite verbal form, including participles describing an accompanying or characteristic state and infinitives expressing indirect commands, requests, or aims.
senses.grammatical_frame: Particle preceding a participle or infinitive

senses.definition: Introduces a direct question in a way that signals an expected negative reply.
senses.grammatical_frame: Sentence-initial particle in an interrogative clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently forms fixed grammatical collocations: `ἵνα μή` (negative purpose/request), `ἐὰν μή` (negative condition), `εἰ μή` (exception, often after `οὐ`, `οὐδείς`, or `οὐκ ἔστιν`), `πρὸς τὸ μή` + infinitive (negative purpose/result), and the emphatic double negative `οὐ μή` + aorist subjunctive or future indicative. In MAT 22:29, `μή` is continued by `μηδέ`. In MAT 26:5, `Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ` is an elliptical prohibition without an expressed verb.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A postpositive conjunction that links a clause to what precedes it by supplying a reason, explanation, illustration, or emphatic confirmation.

senses.definition: Introduces the cause, reason, or logical ground justifying a preceding statement, command, warning, or question.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive conjunction introducing an independent finite clause

senses.definition: Introduces explanatory background, elaboration, an illustrative comparison, or a supporting premise within a narrative or line of argument.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive conjunction, often paired with ὥσπερ, ὡς, εἰ, or participial/correlative clauses

senses.definition: In combination with καί, introduces an emphatic or additive confirming point that reinforces the preceding claim.
senses.grammatical_frame: Collocation καὶ γάρ at the head of a clause

senses.definition: In an elliptical negative response with οὐ, emphatically rejects a preceding question or proposal before stating the counter-demand.
senses.grammatical_frame: Elliptical collocation οὐ γάρ followed by ἀλλά

entries.collocations_and_notes: Strictly postpositive, normally standing as the second word in its clause (or third after an article-noun or preposition-noun unit, as in ὁ μὲν γάρ / τὸ μὲν γάρ in ROM 5:16). Regularly collocates with comparative/conditional markers (ὥσπερ γάρ, ὡς γάρ, εἰ γάρ), the additive particle καί (καὶ γάρ), and the negative οὐ (οὐ γάρ in clauses, and elliptically in ACT 16:37). Twice repeated in consecutive clauses to sustain an explanation in 2CO 10:14.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A primary preposition governing the genitive case to mark outward spatial separation or origin, partitive selection from a larger group or substance, personal affiliation, temporal starting point, and cause or means.

senses.definition: Moving outward from within, proceeding out of, or separated away from a physical place, container, body part, or sphere.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive

senses.definition: Designating lateral orientation on the right or left side relative to a person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive (with plural substantive adjectives of side)

senses.definition: Marking escape, rescue, resurrection, or exemption from hostile power, death, or harm.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive

senses.definition: Indicating parentage, lineage, ultimate source, initiative, or membership within a community, military unit, or moral realm.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive

senses.definition: Selecting one or a portion from a larger group, tribe, food, drink, or allotment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive (partitive)

senses.definition: Expressing the inner disposition, motivation, principle, or evidential means from which an action, utterance, or state arises.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive

senses.definition: Marking a distant temporal starting point or continuous day-by-day succession.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Takes only the genitive case; appears as ἐξ before vowels (e.g., MAT 20:21, JHN 1:32, ROM 2:29). Frequently pairs with verbs of motion/exit (ἐξέρχομαι, καταβαίνω, ἀνίστημι, ἐγείρω) and consumption (πίνω, ἐσθίω). Common fixed expressions include ἐκ νεκρῶν ("from the dead", ACT 3:15, EPH 5:14), ἐκ δεξιῶν / ἐξ εὐωνύμων / ἐξ ἀριστερῶν ("on the right / on the left", MAT 20:21, MRK 10:37), ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας ("day after day", 2PE 2:8), and ἐξ ἐμαυτοῦ ("on my own", JHN 12:49). In JHN 6:51 and REV 18:4, multiple occurrences within the same verse shift between spatial origin ("out of heaven") and partitive consumption or sharing ("of this bread", "of her plagues").

entries.core_meaning_summary: A proper personal name identifying Jesus of Nazareth, also used in apposition with royal, messianic, and lordly titles in Christian confession and instruction.

senses.definition: Personal name of the teacher and miracle-worker from Nazareth, son of Mary, who was crucified and whose life and death are proclaimed by his followers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun (articular or anarthrous, in all cases; sometimes qualified by ὁ Ναζωραῖος)

senses.definition: Personal name paired with official or confessional titles (such as Christ/Messiah, Lord, or Son of God) to designate him as the risen Lord, mediator of grace, and focus of Christian allegiance and prayer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun in apposition with Χριστός, Κύριος, or Υἱὸς Θεοῦ; also vocative with Κύριος
senses.semantic_domain: Proper Name / Messianic and Religious Title

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently preceded by the definite article in Gospel narrative (ὁ Ἰησοῦς) and occasionally paired with the epithet ὁ Ναζωραῖος (LUK 18:37; JHN 18:5). In the Epistles and opening/confessional contexts, it regularly combines in apposition with Χριστός (in both orders: Ἰησοῦς Χριστός and Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς) and Κύριος (e.g., ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός in 1TH 5:28; 1TI 6:3), as well as the vocative invocation Κύριε Ἰησοῦ (ACT 7:59). Note also the explicit designation as "another king" in ACT 17:7 and descendant of David and Abraham in MAT 1:1.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A primary preposition governing the genitive, dative, or accusative case to indicate spatial position on or at, motion toward or upon, temporal setting, interpersonal opposition, or the basis and addition of an action or state.

senses.definition: Located upon or resting on the surface or upper side of an object, ground, seat, or body part.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive or dative

senses.definition: Placed onto, leaning against, or stationed at a physical object, surface, or bodily posture.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative

senses.definition: Directed in motion toward, arriving at, or pouring out onto a physical destination, landmark, or public gathering.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative

senses.definition: Positioned in the official presence of a governing council or judicial assembly.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive

senses.definition: Directed toward, descending upon, resting on, or pronounced over persons or human conditions (used of divine wrath, kindness, spirit, blood-guilt, testimony, or ritual invocation).
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative

senses.definition: Directed in hostility, division, seizure, or bold confrontation against a person, household, or faction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative or dative

senses.definition: Marking the historical period of an event (with genitive) or the arrival of the following day (with accusative).
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive or accusative

senses.definition: Indicating the occasion, subject matter, or ground of an emotional response or careful deliberation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + dative

senses.definition: Denoting accumulation or addition beyond existing actions or circumstances.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + dative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Elides to ἐπ’ before smooth-breathing vowels (e.g., LUK 9:62, JHN 7:30) and aspirates to ἐφ’ before rough-breathing vowels (e.g., MAT 23:35, MRK 3:25, ACT 11:15, REV 19:14). Frequently collocates with verbs of sitting/resting (κάθημαι, ἀναπίπτω, ἀναπαύομαι), falling (πίπτω, ἐπιπίπτω), putting/laying (ἐπιβάλλω, ἐπιτίθημι), and coming/pouring (ἔρχομαι, ἐκχέω). Note the fixed idiom ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ("on the earth", MAT 18:18, LUK 5:24) and the syntactic alternation between dative and accusative within a single parallel clause in LUK 12:53 (πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ ... μήτηρ ἐπὶ θυγατέρα) to express interpersonal opposition. In 1PE 4:14, ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς takes the accusative with ἀναπαύεται ("rests upon"), and in REV 16:12 ἐπί + accusative denotes pouring onto/into a river.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A title of ownership, authority, and sovereignty applied to human masters, to Jesus Christ, and to the God of Israel.

senses.definition: A human owner of property or master holding authority over servants or slaves, and a polite form of address to such a superior.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, often with possessive genitive or paired with δοῦλος, or vocative κύριε in address to a human superior

senses.definition: A title of honor, allegiance, and supreme authority used in addressing or referring to Jesus, ranging from respectful entreaty during his earthly ministry to confession of his exalted lordship.
senses.grammatical_frame: Vocative κύριε in direct address to Jesus, or articular/anarthrous noun in narrative and epistolary titles (e.g., ὁ Κύριος Ἰησοῦς, Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν)

senses.definition: The supreme divine title for the God of Israel as creator, ruler, and judge (including apostolic passages where the divine title is used generally of God or without explicit distinction from the exalted Christ).
senses.grammatical_frame: Articular or anarthrous noun, frequently in scriptural quotations or combined with divine epithets (ὁ Θεός, Σαβαώθ, Παντοκράτωρ) and prepositional phrases (ἐν Κυρίῳ, ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in contrast with δοῦλος ("slave/servant", MAT 25:23; JHN 13:16; 1CO 7:22) and ἀνθρώποις ("human beings", COL 3:23). Common divine collocations include Κύριος ὁ Θεός (MRK 12:29; LUK 1:32), Κύριος Σαβαώθ (ROM 9:29), Κύριος Παντοκράτωρ (2CO 6:18), ἄγγελος Κυρίου (MAT 1:20), τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου (ACT 13:48), and ἐν Κυρίῳ ("in the Lord", 1CO 7:22; GAL 5:10; EPH 6:1). In several apostolic contexts (e.g., ACT 13:48; 1CO 16:10; 2TH 1:9; JAS 5:14), Κύριος functions as a shared title where the text either applies Israel's divine title to Jesus or leaves open whether God or Christ is primarily in view.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To possess, hold, experience, or stand in a relationship or condition with respect to something or someone.

senses.definition: To own, hold, carry, or have at one's disposal tangible objects, property, bodily parts, writings, or material resources.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with accusative direct object (including periphrastic imperfect ἦν ἔχων); also absolute participle οἱ μὴ ἔχοντες

senses.definition: To be connected with or keep someone in a familial, communal, authoritative, or spiritual relationship, including being married to a spouse, keeping someone in one's company or affection, or standing in fellowship with God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with personal accusative object, often modified by prepositional phrases (μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν, ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ, ἐπ’ αὐτῶν)

senses.definition: To possess, experience, enjoy, or obtain an abstract quality, capacity, status, emotion, right, need, or spiritual gift (with aorist forms often highlighting coming into possession or experiencing an outcome).
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with abstract noun in the accusative (sometimes with genitive complement, e.g., χρείαν + gen., or complementary infinitive, e.g., ἐξουσίαν + inf.)

senses.definition: To have the ability, means, opportunity, or something available to perform an action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb with complementary infinitive, or with accusative object plus infinitive or relative clause

senses.definition: To be in a specified physical or bodily condition, such as being unwell or being pregnant.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive or idiomatic verb with adverb (κακῶς) or prepositional phrase (ἐν γαστρί)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently forms idiomatic expressions with abstract nouns or modifiers: χρείαν ἔχω + genitive ("have need of", MAT 9:12; JHN 13:29), ἐξουσίαν ἔχω + infinitive ("have authority to", MRK 3:15; HEB 13:10), ἡλικίαν ἔχω ("be of mature age", JHN 9:23), ὄνομα ἔχω ("bear a name", REV 9:11), ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχω ("be pregnant", MAT 1:18), and κακῶς ἔχω ("be sick/unwell", MAT 9:12). The absolute participle οἱ μὴ ἔχοντες designates those lacking material means (1CO 11:22). Aorist forms (ἔσχον, σχῶ, σχῆτε) often express entering into possession of or experiencing something (ROM 1:13; 2CO 1:15; 1TH 1:9).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A preposition governing the accusative case that marks spatial movement toward, proximity beside, personal presence with, the addressee of speech or action, interpersonal stance, purpose or result, or brief temporal duration.

senses.definition: Indicates physical movement or spatial direction toward a person, group, or location.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative with verbs of motion, sending, or falling

senses.definition: Indicates stationary spatial location close to or alongside a physical object.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative with static verbs or participles

senses.definition: Indicates personal presence, companionship, or residence alongside or among people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative with verbs of being, presence, or hosting

senses.definition: Marks the person or group addressed in speech or the recipient toward whom a command or service is directed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative with verbs of speaking (or elliptical speech clauses) and nouns of instruction or service

senses.definition: Marks the party involved in an interpersonal relationship, standing, dispute, or controversy.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative with verbs or nouns of disposition, favor, or conflict

senses.definition: Indicates intended aim, benefit, readiness, reference, or resulting outcome.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative with abstract nouns, substantivized adjectives/participles, or adjectives of readiness

senses.definition: Indicates a limited span or duration of time.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative noun of time

entries.collocations_and_notes: In all 40 sampled occurrences, πρός exclusively governs the accusative case. Frequently appears in speech-introduction formulas (εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν/αὐτούς, λέγειν πρός), sometimes with an omitted verb of speaking (e.g., ὁ δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς αὐτήν in ACT 5:9). Note the temporal idiom πρὸς ὥραν ('for a short time', 2CO 7:8) and the elliptical substantive construction τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην ('terms pertaining to peace', LUK 14:32).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To perceive visually with the eyes, recognize mentally, meet or experience something, become visible (in the passive), or draw attention to something (in the fixed imperative form ἰδού).

senses.definition: To perceive someone or something with physical sight, observe an action or event, or behold in a vision.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active/middle finite verb or participle + accusative object, accusative + participle, or absolute in visionary narrative

senses.definition: To apprehend, recognize, or become aware of a fact, attitude, or situation through observation or inquiry.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active participle or imperative + abstract accusative noun or ὅτι clause

senses.definition: To come into someone's presence in order to meet, visit, or speak with them.
senses.grammatical_frame: Aorist imperative or infinitive + accusative personal object

senses.definition: To undergo, encounter, or personally experience an event, period of time, state, or visionary phenomenon.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active infinitive, perfect, or future middle + accusative event/time/relative object

senses.definition: To become visible or present oneself to someone, especially in a supernatural manifestation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Aorist passive + dative of recipient

senses.definition: Invariant attention-getting marker used to introduce a new character, sudden event, announcement, or solemn declaration.
senses.grammatical_frame: Fixed particle/interjection (ἰδού) introducing a clause or noun phrase

entries.collocations_and_notes: Displays suppletive stem alternation across tenses: present/imperfect stem ὁρα-, aorist active stem ἰδ-/εἰδ- (e.g., εἶδον, ἰδεῖν, ἰδών, ἴδε), perfect active stem ἑωρα-/ἑορα- (ἑώρακα, ἑόρακεν), future middle stem ὀψ- (ὄψεσθε), and aorist passive stem ὀφθ- (ὤφθη, ὀφθείς). The frozen aorist middle imperative ἰδού regularly functions as an invariant particle/interjection, often after καί in narrative transitions (καὶ ἰδού) or paired with εἶδον in visionary reports (καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδού in REV 14:14; REV 19:11). Notable idioms include ἰδεῖν θάνατον ('to experience death', HEB 11:5) and ἐραύνησον καὶ ἴδε ('investigate and verify', JHN 7:52).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A subordinating conjunction primarily introducing clauses of purpose, intended outcome, or verbal complementation, and forming the interrogative phrase ἵνα τί.

senses.definition: Introduces a subordinate clause expressing the goal, intention, or intended outcome of an action; when negated with μή, expresses prevention or avoidance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction governing a subjunctive verb (negated with μή; occasionally elliptical with the main clause implied)

senses.definition: Introduces a content or complement clause specifying what is commanded, urged, prayed for, caused, or defined by a preceding pronoun or verb.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction introducing a subjunctive (or future indicative) clause dependent on verbs of ordering, praying, charging, causing (ποιέω), or explaining a demonstrative (αὕτη)

senses.definition: Used with the neuter interrogative pronoun τί to ask for the reason or aim of an action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative phrase ἵνα τί introducing a question with an indicative verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Standardly governs the subjunctive mood and is negated with μή (e.g., ἵνα μή). Occasionally stands in elliptical purpose clauses after ἀλλά or at sentence start where an antecedent action is understood (MRK 14:49, JHN 18:32, 1CO 16:16). In REV 13:12 it appears with a future indicative verb (προσκυνήσουσιν) after ποιέω. Also forms the fixed interrogative phrase ἵνα τί ("why?") in ACT 4:25.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A verb denoting coming into being, happening, entering a new state or role, or being situated in a place or relationship.

senses.definition: To come into existence, take place, or occur, used of events, actions, natural phenomena, or states arising among people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with eventive or abstract subject; occasionally with prepositional phrases indicating source or agency (παρά or ὑπό + genitive) or recipient (dative)

senses.definition: To enter into a different condition, character, status, or office; to turn out to be something.
senses.grammatical_frame: Copulative verb taking a predicate nominative noun, adjective, participle, or prepositional phrase (εἰς + accusative)

senses.definition: Used as a narrative transition marker indicating that an event took place at a given point or in a specified manner.
senses.grammatical_frame: Impersonal 3rd-person singular (ἐγένετο) introducing a temporal clause (ὅτε), prepositional infinitive (ἐν τῷ + infinitive), or accusative-with-infinitive clause

senses.definition: To arrive at or remain in a place, spend time in someone's company, or enter a personal/marital union with someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with locative or associative prepositional phrase (ἐν + dative, μετά + genitive) or dative of person

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with predicate nouns, adjectives, or participles to denote transition into a new state (e.g., ἔμφοβος, λευκά, σάρξ, ἀποσυνάγωγοι) and with event nouns (e.g., σεισμός, φόβος, φιλονεικία, σκοτία) to report occurrences. In narrative prose, 3rd-person singular ἐγένετο introduces temporal clauses (ὅτε), infinitive phrases (ἐν τῷ + inf), or accusative-with-infinitive constructions. Also appears in a periphrastic construction with ἦν + present participle (ACT 12:5) and with dative of a person in a marital sense (ROM 7:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Preposition governing the genitive for passage, duration, agency, or means, and governing the accusative for cause, reason, or sake.

senses.definition: Indicates spatial movement across, inside, or by way of an area, opening, or region.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (with verbs of motion)

senses.definition: Indicates the temporal span or continuous period during which an action takes place.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (with temporal expressions)

senses.definition: Marks a personal intermediary, messenger, divine Spirit, or mediator through whom an action, message, or benefit is carried out.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (with personal or divine nouns/pronouns)

senses.definition: Marks the instrument, means, quality, or accompanying manner by which something is accomplished or conducted.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (with non-personal instruments or abstract nouns)

senses.definition: Marks the cause, motive, reason, or beneficiary on account of which an event occurs or an action is taken.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + accusative (including articular infinitives and interrogative/demonstrative pronouns)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Elides to δι' before vowels (e.g., LUK 11:24, ROM 4:24, 1CO 4:6, COL 1:20, HEB 3:19, HEB 12:1). Case selection cleanly distinguishes function: with the genitive it marks spatial route, temporal duration, personal intermediary, or instrument/manner; with the accusative it marks cause, motive, or beneficiary. Recurring fixed phrases include διὰ τί ("why?", MAT 9:14, MAT 21:25), διὰ τοῦτο ("for this reason / therefore", MAT 14:2, JHN 13:11, ROM 15:9, PHM 1:15), διὰ τὸ with the infinitive ("because...", LUK 2:4, LUK 23:8, ACT 18:2), διὰ χειρὸς ("through the agency of", ACT 11:30), διὰ παντὸς ("continually", HEB 9:6), and διὰ νυκτὸς ("by night / during the night", ACT 23:31). Both ROM 5:21 and COL 1:20 combine impersonal means (διὰ δικαιοσύνης, διὰ τοῦ αἵματος) with personal mediation (διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι’ αὐτοῦ) in the same sentence.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Preposition governing the genitive to express spatial, temporal, or conceptual point of origin, separation, distance, source, or agency.

senses.definition: Indicates the place, person, or realm from which movement, departure, or sending originates.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (with verbs of motion, departure, or origin)

senses.definition: Indicates physical, relational, or protective separation, distance, release, or avoidance relative to a reference point, danger, or obligation.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (with verbs of separation, distance, rescue, release, or caution)

senses.definition: Marks the temporal or historical starting point from which a span of time or sequence begins.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (with temporal nouns, adverbs, or historical figures)

senses.definition: Marks the source, origin, partitive subset, inner seat, or independent initiative from which something is drawn, heard, given, or spoken.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (expressing source, partitive subset, or reflexive origin)

senses.definition: Indicates the agent or evidentiary basis by which an action or state is brought about or demonstrated.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (with passive verbs)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Elides to ἀπ' before vowels with smooth breathing (e.g., LUK 8:46, LUK 21:11, ACT 13:13, 2TH 1:7, 1JN 2:13) and ἀφ' before rough breathing (e.g., JHN 7:18, 2CO 3:5, COL 1:9, JAS 5:4). Frequently paired with ἕως or ἄχρι to mark spatial or genealogical intervals ("from ... to", MAT 1:17, MRK 16:99). Common fixed phrases include ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ("from now on", ACT 18:6), ἀπ' ἀρχῆς ("from the beginning", 1JN 2:13), ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ / ἀφ' ἑαυτῶν ("on one's own authority/initiative", JHN 7:18, 2CO 3:5), and ἀπὸ τῶν καρδιῶν ὑμῶν ("sincerely / from your hearts", MAT 18:35). With verbs of caution or avoidance (βλέπω, φυλάσσομαι, ἐκκλίνω), it introduces the object to avoid (MRK 12:38, LUK 12:15, ROM 16:17). LUK 16:21 uses the preposition twice in one clause for distinct relations: source of nourishment (χορτασθῆναι ἀπὸ) and spatial separation (πιπτόντων ἀπὸ).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A coordinating conjunction marking contrast, replacement of a negated element, counter-expectation, or emphatic progression between words, phrases, or clauses.

senses.definition: Introduces a positive alternative, correction, or replacement directly after a negated word, phrase, or clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Coordinating conjunction linking parallel elements or clauses after a negative (οὐ, μή, οὐδείς, οὐκέτι, οὐχ ὅτι)

senses.definition: Expands a preceding negated restriction by adding a further group or category alongside the first.
senses.grammatical_frame: Correlative conjunction paired with οὐ ... μόνον and followed by καί

senses.definition: Marks an adversative contrast, unexpected turn, or opposing state of affairs between clauses or at the beginning of a sentence without an immediately preceding explicit negative pair.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause- or sentence-initial coordinating conjunction introducing a contrasting statement or event

senses.definition: Introduces an urgent command or reinforces and intensifies a preceding assertion when paired with `καί`.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial conjunction introducing an imperative (ACT 10:20) or paired with καί to strengthen a statement

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly appears elided as `ἀλλ’` before vowels (e.g., `ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ`, `ἀλλ’ οὐδεὶς`, `ἀλλ’ ἵνα`), though unelided `ἀλλὰ` before vowels also occurs in the packet (e.g., `ἀλλὰ ἦλθεν` in JHN 6:23, `ἀλλὰ ἀναστὰς` in ACT 10:20, `ἀλλὰ ἀδελφὸς` in 1CO 6:6, `ἀλλὰ αὐτοὶ` in 2CO 1:9, `ἀλλὰ ἐκ` in 1JN 2:16). Common correlative frames include `οὐ / μή ... ἀλλά`, `οὐ μόνον ... ἀλλὰ καί`, `οὐχ ὅτι ... ἀλλ’ ὅτι` / `ἀλλ’ ἵνα`, and `ἀλλὰ καί` for emphatic confirmation.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To move toward or arrive at a place, person, or state, used both of physical travel and of the appearance or onset of expected figures, events, and times.

senses.definition: To move from one location to another or reach a destination, whether a person, place, gathering, or vessel's port, including returning to a prior location or passing along a route.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, often with prepositional phrases of goal (εἰς, πρός, ἐγγύς) or origin (ἐκ, ἀπό), purpose infinitives, or accompanying participles

senses.definition: To appear or enter onto the scene in an appointed role or mission, or to confront someone in a promised or threatened visitation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with purpose infinitive, substantival participle (ὁ ἐρχόμενος), or dative of person affected (REV 2:5)

senses.definition: Of natural forces, events, moral dangers, divine rule, or designated periods: to begin, occur, break out, or reach realization.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with non-human or abstract subject (floodwaters, kingdom, stumbling blocks, hour, wrath)

senses.definition: Used as an attributive participle modifying a unit of time to mark immediate succession.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive present participle agreeing with a temporal noun in the dative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes prepositional phrases indicating goal (`εἰς` + accusative for places/events, `πρός` + accusative for persons, `ἐγγύς` + genitive for proximity) or origin (`ἐκ` / `ἀπό` + genitive), as well as the idiom `εἰς ἀπάντησιν` + dative ("to meet", ACT 28:15) and purpose infinitives (MAT 2:2, MAT 10:34). The substantival present participle `ὁ ἐρχόμενος` functions as a title for an anticipated figure (LUK 7:19, LUK 19:38, HEB 10:37). Morphology in the packet shows first-aorist-type endings alongside second-aorist stems in `ἦλθαν` (ACT 28:15) and imperative `ἐλθάτω` (LUK 11:2).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A general verb of action, performance, and production meaning to do, carry out, practice, make, or bring about a state or event.

senses.definition: To carry out an activity, course of behavior, or instructed task, used either with a general pronominal object or intransitively with adverbs and comparative clauses of manner.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive with general/pronominal object (τοῦτο, ταῦτα, τί, ὅσα), or intransitive with manner adverb or comparative clause (ὡς, καθώς, οὕτως)

senses.definition: To perform, practice, commit, or execute specific deeds, miraculous signs, charitable acts, moral conduct, commands, or judicial sentences.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive with abstract, event, or deed noun as direct object (e.g., σημεῖα, ἔργα, ἐλεημοσύνην, φόνον, τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, τὴν δικαιοσύνην, κρίσιν, τὸν λόγον)

senses.definition: To act toward or treat a person in a particular way, whether beneficially or harmfully.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive with affected person marked by dative case or ἐν + dative

senses.definition: To fashion, craft, or naturally produce a tangible object or agricultural yield.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive with concrete physical object or natural product as direct object

senses.definition: To cause a person or thing to become, be characterized by, or assume a specified state, quality, or status.
senses.grammatical_frame: Double accusative (direct object + predicate noun or predicate adjective)
senses.semantic_domain: Causation / Transformation of State or Status

senses.definition: To arrange or bring it about that a particular action takes place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + ἵνα + subjunctive clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Shows wide syntactic flexibility: takes general pronominal objects (τοῦτο, ταῦτα, τι, οὐδέν, ὅσα), action/ethical nouns (σημεῖα, ἔργα, ἐλεημοσύνην, φόνον, ἁμαρτίαν, δικαιοσύνην, κρίσιν, τὸν λόγον), manner adverbs or comparative clauses (φρονίμως, οὕτως, ὡς, καθώς), and double accusatives expressing resultant state or role. Participial framing such as Τί ποιεῖτε κλαίοντες ("What are you doing, weeping?", ACT 21:13) pairs the verb with an accompanying participle to question ongoing behavior. In 2CO 8:11, the articular infinitive τὸ ποιῆσαι denotes actual execution in contrast to willing/desiring (τοῦ θέλειν).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An interrogative pronoun and determiner asking after the identity, nature, quality, or cause of persons, things, or actions in direct and indirect questions.

senses.definition: Used in direct questions as a masculine/feminine pronoun (including genitive τίνος for possession or relationship) to ask about the identity of a person, often with rhetorical force.
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative pronoun (masculine/feminine), subject, predicate, or genitive modifier in direct questions

senses.definition: Used in direct questions as a neuter pronoun to ask about an action, speech, situation, outcome, or abstract matter.
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative pronoun (neuter nominative/accusative), subject, object, or predicate in direct questions

senses.definition: Used adjectivally or predicatively with an explicit noun to ask which particular member, kind, or instance is in view.
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative determiner or predicate agreeing in gender, number, and case with a noun

senses.definition: Introduces an embedded or reported question after verbs of knowing, asking, pondering, being perplexed, or hearing, referring to a person, thing, or meaning.
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative pronoun or determiner introducing an indirect question (with indicative, subjunctive, or optative)

senses.definition: Used adverbially in the neuter accusative (alone as τί, or in the phrases διὰ τί and ἵνα τί) to inquire about the reason, motive, or purpose of an action or state, frequently expressing surprise, rebuke, or perplexity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverbial neuter accusative τί, or prepositional/conjunctional phrases διὰ τί and ἵνα τί

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently combines with prepositions in causal or purpose questions, especially διὰ τί ("why?", MAT 17:19, MRK 2:18, LUK 5:30, LUK 24:38) and ἵνα τί ("to what end? why?", MAT 9:4). Neuter τί also appears in fixed or elliptical expressions such as Τί πρὸς ἡμᾶς; ("What is that to us?", MAT 27:4), Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ...; ("What do you think?", MAT 22:42), Τί θέλει τοῦτο εἶναι; ("What does this mean?", ACT 2:12), and Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; ("What then shall we say?", ROM 7:7). Rhetorical questions frequently employ τίς to assert a negative or self-evident point (ACT 11:17, ROM 9:20, ROM 11:35, 1CO 9:7, HEB 13:6). In indirect questions following verbs of knowing, asking, wondering, or hearing, the verb may appear in the optative with or without ἄν (LUK 8:9, LUK 15:26) or subjunctive (MRK 9:6).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A human being or person, used generically for humanity, individually for a particular person or man, and in the fixed title 'the Son of Man'.

senses.definition: A member of the human species or people collectively, often viewed as mortal, morally accountable, and distinct from God, unclean spirits, or animals.
senses.grammatical_frame: Count noun (singular generic or plural), with or without the definite article; often opposed to Θεός or non-human beings

senses.definition: A particular individual or man, frequently introduced in narratives and parables or pointed out with a demonstrative or descriptive phrase.
senses.grammatical_frame: Count noun (singular), modified by τις, οὗτος, a gentilic/name, or a participial/descriptive phrase

senses.definition: Component of the fixed title 'the Son of Man', used by or of Jesus to denote his authority, service, suffering, and future coming or glorification.
senses.grammatical_frame: Articular genitive singular governed by ὁ Υἱός (ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often contrasted explicitly with God (τῷ Θεῷ ... τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, παρὰ ἀνθρώπου) or with animals (σὰρξ ἀνθρώπων ... σὰρξ κτηνῶν). Frequently combines with the indefinite determiner τις (ἄνθρωπός τις) or demonstratives (ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος) to introduce or track a narrative participant. The genitive singular appears repeatedly in the fixed title ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A title for the expected Messiah promised in Israel's scriptures, used both with the article as an official designation and alone or compounded with 'Jesus' as a personal and confessional name-title for Jesus Christ.

senses.definition: The expected figure of Jewish scripture and hope, explicitly equated with the Messiah (JHN 1:41), identified as the Son of God who suffers, rises from the dead, abides forever, and serves as high priest and head over the church.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun, predominantly with the definite article (ὁ Χριστός), as predicate or subject

senses.definition: A personal and titular designation standing alone for Jesus in his saving death, resurrection, active agency, and relational union with believers.
senses.grammatical_frame: anarthrous (or genitive articular) masculine noun used alone as subject, direct object, object of prepositions (ἐν, εἰς, διά, ὑπέρ), or possessive/attributive genitive

senses.definition: A compounded name-title paired with Ἰησοῦς ('Jesus Christ' or 'Christ Jesus'), frequently alongside Κύριος ('Lord') or Σωτήρ ('Savior'), identifying Jesus of the lineage of David and Abraham as the agent of salvation, grace, resurrection, and coming glory.
senses.grammatical_frame: anarthrous masculine noun in apposition/compound with Ἰησοῦς (Ἰησοῦς Χριστός / Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς), often with Κύριος or Σωτήρ

entries.collocations_and_notes: Translated explicitly as the equivalent of Μεσσίας in JHN 1:41. Very frequent in fixed prepositional phrases such as ἐν Χριστῷ (Ἰησοῦ) ('in Christ [Jesus]'), εἰς Χριστόν ('into/in Christ'), διὰ (Ἰησοῦ) Χριστοῦ ('through [Jesus] Christ'), and ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ ('for Christ'), as well as in the expanded confessional title ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός ('our Lord Jesus Christ'). Genitive collocations include ὁ σταυρὸς τοῦ Χριστοῦ ('the cross of Christ'), τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ ('the gospel of Christ'), ὁ λόγος τοῦ Χριστοῦ ('the word of Christ'), ἡμέρα Χριστοῦ ('day of Christ'), and ἡ διδαχὴ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ('the teaching of Christ').

entries.core_meaning_summary: Enclitic indefinite pronoun and determiner referring to an unspecified, unnamed, or newly introduced person, thing, or amount.

senses.definition: An unspecified or unnamed person or group of people, used in general or conditional statements, to introduce an unidentified subject, or with a partitive phrase to single out members of a larger group; in predicate constructions, someone of notable standing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indefinite pronoun (masculine/feminine singular or plural), standalone or with partitive genitive / ἐκ + genitive; also predicate accusative/nominative

senses.definition: An unspecified thing, matter, gift, or grievance; when paired with adjectives of degree or used adverbially with verbs, it indicates a small measure or extent, and in predicate position it denotes something of consequence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indefinite pronoun (neuter singular), used as direct object, predicate, or adverbial accusative of extent/respect

senses.definition: Modifies a noun to mark an entity, person, place, or quality as unspecified or newly introduced in the discourse.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indefinite determiner agreeing in gender, number, and case with a noun or proper name

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears after conditional particles (εἴ τις, ὅταν ... τις, μή τις), with partitive genitives or ἐκ + genitive (τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν, τινες ἐκ τῶν Ἱεροσολυμειτῶν), and in narrative openings paired with an indefinite noun or proper name (ἀνήρ τις, ἄνθρωπός τις, Ἀνανίας δέ τις). In predicates (εἶναί τι, εἶναί τινα μέγαν), it denotes significance or stature; with neuter comparatives or quantity adjectives (περισσότερόν τι, μικρόν τι), it functions quantitatively or adverbially.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A comparative, temporal, approximative, and complementizing particle or conjunction expressing likeness, manner, role or assumed status, time, approximate measure, or how an event occurs.

senses.definition: Marks similarity or likeness in appearance, quality, sound, or behavior between one entity or state and another.
senses.grammatical_frame: comparative particle + noun phrase, pronoun, adjective, or prepositional phrase

senses.definition: Introduces a clause or elliptical clause indicating correspondence in manner or action with a command, pattern, or parallel group.
senses.grammatical_frame: comparative conjunction + finite verb clause (sometimes correlative with οὕτως, or elliptical with καί)

senses.definition: Marks the capacity, role, status, or assumed condition in which a person or thing is regarded, treated, or acts, including counterfactual or paradoxical stances ('as if').
senses.grammatical_frame: particle + predicate noun, adjective, or participle (often with verbs of considering, treating, or being)

senses.definition: Introduces a clause marking the point in time at which an event happens, prompting an immediate subsequent action.
senses.grammatical_frame: temporal conjunction + aorist indicative clause

senses.definition: Modifies a number or measure of distance or duration to indicate an approximate estimate.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverbial particle + numeral or prepositional phrase of measure (ἀπό, ἐπί)

senses.definition: Introduces a complement clause after verbs of knowing, remembering, or indicating to specify the content or manner of what is known or spoken.
senses.grammatical_frame: conjunction + indicative clause after verbs of cognition or speech

senses.definition: Introduces an exclamation emphasizing a striking quality.
senses.grammatical_frame: exclamative particle + predicate adjective + noun phrase

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with a correlative οὕτως ('so') in comparative clauses (ACT 23:11). Often introduces participles or noun phrases expressing assumed status, manner, or paradoxical description (2CO 6:9; COL 2:20). Combines with numerals and prepositions (ἀπό, ἐπί) to mark approximate distance, quantity, or duration (JHN 6:10; JHN 21:8; ACT 19:34), and with καί to include a parallel group or event (EPH 2:3; 1PE 3:7; 2PE 2:1).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A conditional and interrogative conjunction used primarily to introduce conditional clauses (open, assumed, or counterfactual), exceptive phrases with μή, and direct or indirect questions.

senses.definition: Introduces the protasis of an open condition or a condition treated as a known or shared premise from which an inference, question, or command follows.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial conjunction with present, future, or past indicative (or verbless clause) in the protasis

senses.definition: Introduces the protasis of a counterfactual condition, stating what did not happen or was not the case, paired with an apodosis expressing an unrealized result (often with ἄν and a past indicative).
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial conjunction with past indicative in protasis, typically paired with ἄν + past indicative (or an evaluative past statement) in apodosis

senses.definition: Combined with καί (εἰ καί) to introduce a concessive or additive condition alongside a main assertion.
senses.grammatical_frame: εἰ καί + indicative clause

senses.definition: Combined with μή (εἰ μή, εἰ μὴ μόνον, εἰ μὴ ὅταν, εἰ δὲ μήγε) to specify an exception after a negative statement, introduce an elliptical negative alternative ('otherwise'), or mark a restrictive transition ('only').
senses.grammatical_frame: εἰ μή (+ noun/prepositional phrase/temporal clause), εἰ δὲ μήγε, or clause-initial restrictive εἰ μή

senses.definition: Introduces a direct yes/no question, an indirect deliberative question (with the optative), an idiomatic parenthetical expression of possibility (εἰ τύχοι), or a wish-like exclamation/question (LUK 12:49).
senses.grammatical_frame: Direct question (with indicative), indirect question (with optative), or idiomatic εἰ τύχοι / wish construction
