entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears with indefinite τι / τις ('if anything / if anyone', MAT 18:28, 1CO 3:14, PHP 2:1, 1TI 6:3, JAS 1:5) and often combines with postpositive οὖν or δέ or γάρ (PHP 2:1, COL 3:1, ROM 6:8, HEB 4:8, JAS 1:5, 2PE 2:4). Fixed combinations include εἰ μή ('except, unless, only'), εἰ δὲ μήγε ('otherwise'), εἰ καί ('even if, if also'), and εἰ τύχοι ('perhaps'). In LUK 12:49 (καὶ τί θέλω εἰ ἤδη ἀνήφθη), the combination τί θέλω εἰ is syntactically unusual and can be read either as expressing an earnest wish ('how I wish it were already kindled') or a rhetorical conditional ('what do I wish if it has already been kindled?').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A postpositive inferential and continuative particle used to draw a logical conclusion, mark a consequence or question arising from prior context, or advance a narrative or discourse sequence.

senses.definition: Marks a statement, summary, command, or exhortation as the logical result or practical conclusion of what has just been stated; also combined with ἄρα as ἄρα οὖν or with νῦν as νῦν οὖν.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle in declarative, summary, or imperative/hortatory clauses; also in the combinations ἄρα οὖν and νῦν οὖν

senses.definition: Introduces an inferential force into a question, asking what follows or remains true in light of the preceding situation or claim.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle following an interrogative pronoun/adverb or verb of asking

senses.definition: Advances a narrative by linking an action, speech, or reaction directly to the preceding event or command as its natural sequel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle following an initial verb, subject, or object in narrative clauses

senses.definition: Combines with μέν (μὲν οὖν, ἀλλὰ μὲν οὖν γε, εἰ μὲν οὖν) to mark a discourse transition, summarize a state of affairs before a contrast with δέ, or reinforce an emphatic affirmation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle clustered with μέν (μὲν οὖν, ἀλλὰ μὲν οὖν γε, εἰ μὲν οὖν)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Almost always postpositive (placed second in its clause or immediately after a negative, interrogative, or conjunction). Frequently combines with other particles: ἄρα οὖν ('so then', ROM 7:25, GAL 6:10), μὲν οὖν ('so indeed / now', ACT 12:5, ACT 17:17, ACT 26:9, HEB 7:11), ἀλλὰ μὲν οὖν γε ('yes indeed / more than that', PHP 3:8), and νῦν οὖν ('now therefore', ACT 23:15). Frequently pairs with interrogatives (πόθεν, διὰ τί, τί, πῶς) and imperatives/hortatory subjunctives. In Johannine narrative, it functions pervasively as a standard connective advancing consecutive actions and speech responses.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A preposition indicating opposition when governing the genitive, and spatial or temporal distribution, standard, manner, or respect when governing the accusative.

senses.definition: Marks hostility, interpersonal division, complaint, or legal action directed in opposition to someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun or pronoun in the genitive case

senses.definition: Indicates extension across a region, distribution from one place to another, or orientation toward a compass direction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a spatial or directional noun in the accusative case

senses.definition: Marks either regular distributive recurrence over time units or an approximate point in time.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a temporal noun in the accusative case

senses.definition: Indicates conformity to a norm, custom, text, pattern, will, measure, or empowering source.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun in the accusative case

senses.definition: Forms adverbial expressions specifying the medium, isolation, privacy, or degree in which something takes place or exists.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun, adjective, or reflexive pronoun in the accusative case (often in fixed adverbial phrases)

senses.definition: Identifies the aspect, domain, perspective, or person with reference to which a statement or state applies.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun or pronoun in the accusative case (including substantivized phrases with the article τά)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Elided to κατ' before smooth breathing and καθ' before rough breathing. Recurring fixed adverbial expressions with the accusative include κατ' ὄναρ (in a dream, Matt 1:20; 27:19), κατ' ἰδίαν (privately/by oneself, Mark 9:2; Acts 23:19), κατὰ μόνας (alone, Luke 9:18), καθ' ἡμέραν (daily, Acts 2:46), κατὰ κράτος (powerfully, Acts 19:20), and καθ' ἑαυτήν (by itself, Jas 2:17). With the neuter plural article, τὰ κατά + accusative forms substantivized phrases denoting circumstances or outward affairs (τὰ κατὰ πρόσωπον in 2 Cor 10:7; τὰ κατ' ἐμέ in Eph 6:21).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A preposition marking accompaniment, shared activity, alignment, or manner when governing the genitive, and temporal succession when governing the accusative.

senses.definition: Indicates spatial presence alongside, personal companionship, joint participation in an action or status, or having something in one's possession.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun or pronoun in the genitive case

senses.definition: Marks loyalty, supportive presence, divine favor, or mutual agreement between parties, contrasted with opposition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun or pronoun in the genitive case

senses.definition: Specifies objects carried, conferred authorization, or the attitude and manner that accompany an action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing an abstract or concrete noun in the genitive case

senses.definition: Indicates that an event, time period, or descendant follows subsequently in time after another event, period, or person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun, pronoun, or articular infinitive in the accusative case

entries.collocations_and_notes: Elided to μετ' before smooth breathing and μεθ' before rough breathing. With the genitive, Luke 24:29 pairs μεῖνον μεθ' ἡμῶν directly with μεῖναι σὺν αὐτοῖς, showing functional overlap with σύν for personal accompaniment, while Luke 11:23 contrasts ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ' ἐμοῦ with κατ' ἐμοῦ (opposition). Common temporal phrases with the accusative include μετὰ ταῦτα and μετὰ τοῦτο (often introducing a new narrative scene, e.g., John 5:1; Rev 7:1; 19:1), as well as the articular infinitive construction μετὰ τὸ λαβεῖν in Heb 10:26.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To perceive sound with the ears, listen attentively to speech or instruction, or receive a report or information.

senses.definition: To perceive voices, sounds, spoken words, or audible phenomena through the sense of hearing.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive (accusative of sound/words, or genitive of speaker/source with participle) or intransitive/passive

senses.definition: To give deliberate attention to a speaker, teaching, message, or judicial statement, often with the expectation of understanding, learning, or responding in obedience.
senses.grammatical_frame: accusative of message/teaching, genitive of speaker (sometimes + περί), or with παρά + genitive of source

senses.definition: To listen favorably to someone's appeal or prayer and respond accordingly.
senses.grammatical_frame: genitive of person (specifically of God toward worshipers)

senses.definition: To become aware of news, a report, or a fact about someone or something via spoken communication or rumor.
senses.grammatical_frame: with ὅτι clause, accusative of report/topic, passive ἠκούσθη + ὅτι, or absolute participle (especially ἀκούσας)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of understanding, trusting, or acting upon what is heard (e.g., ἀκούετε καὶ συνίετε in MAT 15:10; ἀκούει ... καὶ ποιεῖ in MAT 7:24; ἀκούων καὶ πιστεύων in JHN 5:24), and explicitly connected with the ears (ὦτα / ὠσίν, LUK 8:8; ACT 28:27). In narration, the aorist participle ἀκούσας commonly functions as a transitional link introducing a character's reaction to news or speech (MAT 2:3; MAT 12:24; LUK 18:22; LUK 23:6). Objects denoting the sound or message generally take the accusative, while persons being listened to or testifying often take the genitive (MRK 6:20; JHN 9:31; ACT 14:9; ACT 24:24).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Adjective and substantive indicating a large quantity, number, degree, or extent, including comparative forms denoting a greater amount or majority.

senses.definition: Denoting a large number of countable individuals, groups, or things, either modifying a plural noun or standing substantively (with the article, 'the many').
senses.grammatical_frame: plural adjective modifying countable nouns, or plural substantive (with or without article)

senses.definition: Denoting large size, abundance, or high intensity when modifying collective, mass, or abstract singular nouns.
senses.grammatical_frame: singular adjective modifying collective, mass, or abstract nouns

senses.definition: Indicating an advanced point in the day when used with the noun ὥρα ('hour').
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine singular adjective modifying ὥρα

senses.definition: Indicating a high monetary value or price in a commercial transaction.
senses.grammatical_frame: genitive singular neuter expressing price with verb of selling

senses.definition: Indicating high degree, intensity, or earnestness in an action, or reinforcing a comparative adjective.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverbial neuter (singular πολύ or plural πολλά) modifying a verb, or dative of degree (πολλῷ) with a comparative

senses.definition: Referring to a large number of lashes or blows in an elliptical expression with a verb of beating.
senses.grammatical_frame: elliptical feminine plural accusative (πολλάς) as cognate-like object of δέρω

senses.definition: Comparative degree denoting a larger quantity, greater importance, or further extent in space, time, or action.
senses.grammatical_frame: comparative adjective/substantive (πλείων, πλεῖον, πλείονα, πλείους), often with genitive of comparison or in prepositional phrase ἐπὶ πλεῖον

senses.definition: Comparative plural with the article referring to the larger part of a group or assembly.
senses.grammatical_frame: articular plural comparative substantive (οἱ πλείους, οἱ πλείονες)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with εἷς ('one', e.g., ROM 5:19; 1CO 12:20; GAL 3:16) and ὀλίγον ('little', LUK 7:47). Common collocations include ὄχλος πολύς / ὄχλοι πολλοί ('a large crowd' / 'great crowds', MAT 8:1; LUK 5:29; JHN 12:9; REV 7:9) and the prepositional comparative phrase ἐπὶ πλεῖον ('further, longer', ACT 4:17; ACT 24:4). The comparative also combines with the dative of degree πολλῷ in JHN 4:41 (πολλῷ πλείους, 'far more').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A male human parent, a forefather or ancestor, a spiritual progenitor, or God as Father and creator/source.

senses.definition: A male human parent or household father who exercises care, authority, or familial responsibility toward his children.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine; singular (often with possessive genitive, paired with μήτηρ, υἱός, or τέκνα, or in vocative Πάτερ)

senses.definition: A founding forefather or earlier generation of ancestors from whom a lineage, people, or royal line descends.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine; singular (in apposition with proper names like Δαυείδ or Ἀβραάμ) or plural (with possessive genitive or definite article)

senses.definition: A spiritual or moral progenitor whose pattern of faith or conduct defines a community of followers or spiritual descendants.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine; singular (with genitive of a group or in contrast with divine fatherhood)

senses.definition: God conceived as Father, both in his unique, intimate relationship with Jesus Christ the Son and as the loving, sovereign, and worshiped Father of believers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine; singular (frequently articular ὁ Πατήρ, in apposition with Θεός, in vocative address, or with possessive genitive μου/σου/ἡμῶν)

senses.definition: God as the originator, creator, or ultimate source of a quality or created order (such as mercies, glory, or celestial lights).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine; singular governing a genitive noun (τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν, τῆς δόξης, τῶν φώτων)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly paired with μήτηρ ('mother') or υἱός/τέκνα ('son/children') in family contexts, and in the plural with possessive pronouns (οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν/σου) for Israel's ancestors. In theological usage it frequently appears in apposition with Θεός (Θεὸς Πατήρ) or in the articular vocative/nominative address (ὁ Πατήρ, Πάτερ), as well as in the formula 'God of our/your fathers'.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Daylight, a twenty-four-hour calendar day, an extended historical or future period, or a specific appointed time of divine judgment or revelation.

senses.definition: The sunlit portion of the twenty-four-hour cycle, including daybreak and daytime heat, often paired with night to express uninterrupted activity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine; singular (in genitive absolute or with γίνομαι for dawn, or paired with νύξ in accusative or genitive of time)

senses.definition: A single calendar day or twenty-four-hour unit of time, whether counted in a span, designated by an ordinal or observance, or expressed distributively as daily recurrence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine; singular or plural with numerals, ordinals, or prepositions (ἐν, μετά, κατά, ἐπί, ἀπό), or in dative/accusative of time

senses.definition: An extended stretch of time, historical era, or predicted future period associated with a ruler, notable figure, or sequence of events.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine; predominantly plural (with genitive of a person or activity, relative clauses, or adjectives such as ἔσχατος)

senses.definition: An appointed, decisive occasion of divine judgment, resurrection, testing, or vindication at the culmination of the present age.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine; singular (modified by ἐσχάτη, ἐκείνη, or genitives such as κρίσεως, Κυρίου, Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ)

senses.definition: The figurative sphere of light and moral alertness, contrasted with night and darkness as the realm of ignorance or wrongdoing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine; singular genitive governed by υἱοί, parallel to φῶς and opposed to νύξ and σκότος

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with νύξ ('night') in adverbial expressions of continuous duration (νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν, ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτός). Common temporal idioms include καθ' ἡμέραν ('daily'), ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἡμέρᾳ ('day by day'), πᾶσαν ἡμέραν ('every day'), ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ('all day long'), and ἐλεύσονται/ἔρχονται ἡμέραι ('days are coming'). In eschatological contexts it takes modifiers like ἐσχάτη ('last'), ἐκείνη ('that'), or genitives such as κρίσεως, Κυρίου, and Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A neuter noun denoting the divine Spirit of God, a spiritual mode of existence or inner human faculty, an animating life-force, or a non-bodily spiritual being.

senses.definition: The divine Spirit associated with God and Christ, portrayed as a personal and empowering presence who conceives, leads, teaches, speaks, gives gifts, indwells believers, and bears witness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter singular noun, often articular (τὸ Πνεῦμα), modified by Ἅγιον or a genitive referring to God, or in instrumental/locative phrases (ἐν Πνεύματι, διὰ Πνεύματος)

senses.definition: A spiritual quality, nature, or inward mode of existence and service, explicitly contrasted with physical flesh or written legal code.
senses.grammatical_frame: Anarthrous neuter singular noun in predicate or genitive/prepositional constructions contrasted with σάρξ or γράμμα

senses.definition: The immaterial inner self or personal faculty of a human being—the seat of joy, non-physical presence, or ecstatic speech—contrasted with the physical body.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter singular noun with possessive pronoun or dative of respect/means (τῷ πνεύματι), often contrasted with σῶμα or intelligible speech

senses.definition: The animating vital force or breath that sustains or restores physical life, movement, and speech to a body or image.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter singular noun as subject of ἐπιστρέφω or direct object of δίδωμι

senses.definition: An autonomous, non-bodily spiritual entity—in the attested occurrences, an afflicting or deceiving being associated with demonic influence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter singular or plural noun, either subject of violent action against a person or modified by πλάνος and paired with δαιμόνια

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very frequently modified by ἅγιον (e.g., Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον, τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον) or qualified by Θεοῦ / μου / αὐτοῦ when referring to the divine Spirit. Often occurs in prepositional phrases of agency or sphere (διὰ Πνεύματος, ἐν Πνεύματι, ὑπὸ Πνεύματος) and as the subject of verbs of speaking, teaching, leading, searching, and dwelling (λέγει, διδάξει, ἐραυνᾷ, οἰκεῖ). Frequently contrasted with σάρξ (JHN 3:6), γράμμα (ROM 7:6), or σῶμα (1CO 5:3). In JAS 4:5 (τὸ πνεῦμα ὃ κατῴκισεν ἐν ἡμῖν), syntax allows either the human spirit placed within people by God or the indwelling divine Spirit; similarly, ἐν καινότητι πνεύματος (ROM 7:6) bridges inward spiritual disposition and life empowered by the divine Spirit.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A male sibling by birth, extended broadly to denote a fellow member of a religious community, co-worker, or fellow coreligionist, especially in direct address.

senses.definition: A male sibling sharing the same parent or family lineage, appearing in genealogies, household descriptions, and legal provisions concerning marriage and family.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, singular or plural, often with a possessive genitive or grouped with other family members

senses.definition: A fellow adherent of the same religious faith, local congregation, or shared mission, used in the singular for a co-worker or fellow member in moral/communal relations and in the plural for the body of believers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, singular (often with proper name or possessive pronoun) or plural (typically with definite article)

senses.definition: Used in direct address to appeal to listeners or readers as fellow members of a Christian congregation, coreligionists, or fellow Israelites.
senses.grammatical_frame: Vocative singular or plural, alone or with modifiers (ἀγαπητοί, ἄνδρες)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly paired in biological contexts with μήτηρ ('mother'), ἀδελφαί ('sisters'), τέκνα ('children'), φίλοι ('friends'), and συγγενεῖς ('relatives'). In community and epistolary usage, frequently modified by adjectives such as πιστός ('faithful') or ἀγαπητός ('beloved'), and appears in the address formula ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί (ACT 13:38) before a Jewish synagogue audience as well as ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί (JAS 1:19) to Christian recipients. In MAT 5:24 (reconciliation before an altar offering) and ACT 13:38, it extends to fellow members of the Israelite religious community, parallel to its widespread use among disciples and congregations.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A coordinating and comparative conjunction used to present alternatives, introduce rhetorical challenges, mark corrective exceptions after negation, and link the second element of a comparison or temporal sequence.

senses.definition: Coordinates two or more alternative words, phrases, clauses, or questions, indicating a choice, possibility, or disjunction between items.
senses.grammatical_frame: Disjunctive conjunction linking coordinated nouns, adjectives, verbs, prepositional phrases, or clauses

senses.definition: Introduces a standalone question or directive that challenges an assumption or proposes an alternative line of argument.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial conjunction introducing an interrogative or imperative clause

senses.definition: Combined with ἀλλά after a preceding negation to introduce the true or contrasting alternative.
senses.grammatical_frame: In the fixed collocation ἀλλ’ ἤ following negation (οὐχί)

senses.definition: Marks the second term of a comparison of degree or preference following a comparative form, μᾶλλον, or a positive expression carrying comparative force.
senses.grammatical_frame: Comparative particle after comparative adjectives/adverbs, μᾶλλον, or positive predicates with comparative force

senses.definition: Combined with πρίν before an infinitive clause to locate an event prior in time to another action.
senses.grammatical_frame: In the temporal collocation πρὶν ἤ + accusative and infinitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently links parallel interrogative clauses (MAT 6:31; MRK 4:30; ACT 7:49) or yes/no alternatives with οὔ / μή (MAT 22:17; MRK 12:14). Often reinforced by καί ("or even / or also" in LUK 18:11; ROM 4:9) or paired with μᾶλλον ("rather than" in MAT 18:13; 1CO 9:15; 2TI 3:4). Noticeably used in comparative constructions even with positive καλόν ("good/better ... than" in MRK 9:47) or implied comparison (LUK 15:7), and in 1CO 9:15 anacoluthon interrupts the clause immediately after ἤ. In LUK 12:51, ἀλλ’ ἤ follows οὐχί to mark a sharp corrective contrast.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The cardinal numeral denoting a single unit, individual, or undivided entity, used both to count one item among others and to emphasize uniqueness, unity, or distributive individuality.

senses.definition: Modifies a noun to specify an exact count of one, a single instance, or a shared unified entity (such as one day, one hour, one meal, one husband, or one undivided body/flock/Spirit).
senses.grammatical_frame: Cardinal numeral agreeing in gender, number, and case with a noun

senses.definition: Refers independently to a single person, animal, or object, often identifying one member out of a larger group (with a partitive genitive or preposition ἐξ) or contrasting one party with another (with ἕτερος).
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival numeral, frequently with partitive genitive, ἐξ + genitive, or paired with ὁ ἕτερος

senses.definition: Predicated of a subject to assert sole existence, exclusivity, or unique status, indicating that only one such being or party exists.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate nominal or genitive of possession with copulative verb εἰμί

senses.definition: Used in prepositional or pronominal combinations to mark individual members of a group acting or receiving sequentially or one by one.
senses.grammatical_frame: Combined with κατά (καθ’ ἕνα, καθ’ ἓν, ἓν καθ’ ἓν) or ἕκαστος

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently inflected for gender (masculine εἷς, feminine μία, neuter ἕν) to agree with its referent. Commonly appears in partitive constructions with a genitive noun/pronoun or ἐξ + genitive (e.g., εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν, εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα), in contrastive pairs with ὁ ἕτερος ('the one ... the other' in MAT 6:24, LUK 16:13, LUK 17:34, 1CO 4:6), and in distributive expressions with ἕκαστος or κατά (καθ’ ἕνα, καθ’ ἓν ἕκαστον, ἓν καθ’ ἓν, ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ). In theological and ecclesial contexts (JHN 10:16, 1CO 12:13, EPH 2:18), modifying collective nouns like ποίμνη, σῶμα, or Πνεῦμα highlights shared unity across formerly distinct groups. Also used in temporal idioms (μιᾷ ἡμέρᾳ 'in a single day', μιᾷ ὥρᾳ 'in a single hour', ὡσεὶ ὥρας μιᾶς 'about one hour') and negative emphatic statements (οὐκ ἔστιν ἕως ἑνός 'there is not even one' in ROM 3:12).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Preposition indicating subject matter, reference, or ground/benefit with the genitive, and approximate time or sphere of activity with the accusative.

senses.definition: Identifies the person, event, or subject matter that speech, writing, thought, inquiry, testimony, accusation, or care is directed toward or about; also introduces a discourse topic.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive (modifying verbs, nouns, or substantivized article τά, or standing sentence-initially as a topic marker)

senses.definition: Indicates the beneficiary on whose behalf petition or prayer is made, or the occasion/ground prompting an offering, thanksgiving, or consolation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive (with verbs of praying, asking, offering, giving thanks, or consoling)

senses.definition: Marks an approximate point or period of time.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative (with temporal nouns)

senses.definition: Denotes the trade, craft, or sphere of work in which a person is engaged.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative (modifying an agent noun)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Governs the genitive in the vast majority of occurrences, regularly pairing with verbs and nouns of communication, testimony, thought, inquiry, scripture citation, or judicial accusation (e.g., λέγω, γράφω, μαρτυρέω, ἐρωτάω, προσεύχομαι, κατηγορέω, μαρτυρία). Frequently forms a substantivized phrase with the neuter plural article (τὰ περὶ + genitive, "the things concerning...", LUK 24:27; ACT 13:29; ACT 28:31; PHP 2:20) and introduces a new discourse topic at the beginning of a sentence (Περὶ δέ, 1CO 16:12). With the accusative, it occurs only for approximate time (MAT 20:3; MRK 6:48) or occupational sphere (ACT 19:25).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A spoken or written utterance, a circulated report, a proclaimed divine message, a matter or reason/account, and, as a title, the divine Word.

senses.definition: An articulated thought expressed in speech or writing, encompassing a single remark, a question, a command, a prophecy, or an extended discourse.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (singular or plural), often object of verbs of speaking, asking, hearing, or keeping, or in dative of instrument/manner (e.g., λόγῳ πολλῷ)

senses.definition: News, account, or report circulating among people concerning someone or an event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (singular), subject of verb of spreading (διέρχομαι) or object of διαφημίζω

senses.definition: A proclaimed body of religious teaching or revelation from God, frequently denoting the Christian message about Christ and its reception or growth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (typically articular singular, often with genitive modifier such as τοῦ Θεοῦ, τοῦ Κυρίου, τοῦ σταυροῦ, τῆς χάριτος)

senses.definition: A ground, case, affair, or reckoning/account to be rendered before another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in prepositional phrases (παρεκτὸς λόγου, ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ) or relational clause (πρὸς ὃν ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος)

senses.definition: A personal title for a preexistent, tangible, and divine figure identified with God and bearing the name "The Word of God."
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (articular singular, functioning as a proper title, sometimes modified by τοῦ Θεοῦ or τῆς ζωῆς)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Common genitive constructions specify the source, agent, or content of the message (`ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ`, `ὁ λόγος τοῦ Κυρίου`, `ὁ λόγος ὁ τοῦ σταυροῦ`, `τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος`, `τοῦ λόγου τῆς παρακλήσεως`, `τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας`). Frequently occurs as the object of `ἀκούω` (hear), `τηρέω` (keep/observe), `κηρύσσω` (proclaim), `ἐρωτάω` (ask), and `λέγω` (say), or in the dative of means with `παρακαλέω` (`λόγῳ πολλῷ`, ACT 20:2). In 1PE 3:1, two distinct uses appear in one verse: `ἀπειθοῦσιν τῷ λόγῳ` (the proclaimed message) followed by `ἄνευ λόγου` (without spoken speech). Note that in brief clauses like `ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ` (ACT 8:21) and `πρὸς ὃν ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος` (HEB 4:13), the boundary between "matter/affair" and "message" or "account/reckoning" is closely tied to the surrounding clause.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject of a clause as a verbal object, prepositional complement, possessive modifier, or standard of comparison.

senses.definition: Refers back to the grammatical or logical subject as the direct object, indirect object, beneficiary, or infinitive subject of an action; plural forms also serve for first- and second-person plural subjects.
senses.grammatical_frame: Accusative or dative reflexive complement of a verb, or accusative subject of an infinitive

senses.definition: Follows a preposition to express location, accompaniment, source, opposition, responsibility, or internal thought/speech relative to the subject, or interaction among members of a plural subject.
senses.grammatical_frame: Genitive, dative, or accusative governed by a preposition (ἀπό, εἰς, ἐν, ἐπί, μετά, παρά, πρός)

senses.definition: Modifies a noun phrase or substantivized article in the genitive to denote possession or personal belonging tied to the subject of the clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Genitive possessive modifier of a noun or substantivized article (τά)

senses.definition: Marks the subject itself as the standard of comparison after a comparative adjective.
senses.grammatical_frame: Genitive of comparison following a comparative adjective

entries.collocations_and_notes: Exhibits a contracted form αὑτόν in JHN 2:24. Although grammatically third-person reflexive, plural forms frequently refer back to first-person plural (2CO 4:5; 1TH 2:8) and second-person plural subjects (MAT 3:9; LUK 22:17; JHN 12:8; ACT 5:35; ROM 12:16; 2CO 13:5; JAS 1:22; 2JN 1:8). In plural contexts with prepositions such as πρός (MRK 12:7) or εἰς (LUK 22:17), it denotes interaction or distribution among members of a group. Recurring expressions include ἐν ἑαυτῷ / ἐν ἑαυτοῖς with verbs of speaking or reasoning (MAT 3:9; LUK 12:17), ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ ("on one's own initiative", JHN 7:18), δίδωμι ἑαυτόν ("give oneself", 2CO 8:5; 1TI 2:6; TIT 2:14), and substantivized τὰ ἑαυτῶν ("one's own interests", PHP 2:4).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To possess mental awareness, factual knowledge, personal acquaintance, or practical understanding regarding an event, state of affairs, or person.

senses.definition: To hold information, certainty, or comprehension concerning a fact, truth, future event, or the meaning and implications of what is said or done.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + ὅτι clause, indirect question (τί, πόθεν, ποῦ, τίς, εἴ), relative clause (ὧν, ὃ), pronoun (τοῦτο, ἓν), or absolute

senses.definition: To observe, discern, or be fully informed about someone's deeds, circumstances, inner thoughts, or motives.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + accusative noun phrase (denoting actions, thoughts, dispositions, or affairs)

senses.definition: To be acquainted with a person, identify who someone is, recognize a person's character, or acknowledge God in relationship and allegiance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + accusative of person (occasionally with a predicate accusative or proleptic accusative + ὅτι clause)

senses.definition: To possess the practical skill, judgment, or capability to carry out an action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb in comparative manner clause (ὡς οἴδατε)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in rhetorical questions (`οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι...`, 1CO 6:3; 1CO 9:13) and shared-knowledge formulas (`οἴδαμεν [γὰρ/δὲ] ὅτι...`, ROM 2:2; ROM 8:22; 1JN 3:2; 1JN 5:20). Contrasts with partial or uncertain human awareness in `ὁ Θεὸς οἶδεν` (2CO 11:11; 2CO 12:3). In JHN 7:28 and JHN 8:19, knowing a person (`οἶδα` + acc.) encompasses both recognizing origin/identity and relational acknowledgment of God. In 1CO 16:15, `οἴδατε` takes a proleptic accusative (`τὴν οἰκίαν Στεφανᾶ`) followed by an explanatory `ὅτι` clause.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To produce vocal speech, express thoughts or words to others, proclaim a message, or speak in ecstatic tongues.

senses.definition: To exercise the faculty of speech, converse, or produce audible words or sounds (including thunderous utterances in apocalyptic vision).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, often modified by manner adverbs or prepositional phrases (παρρησίᾳ, στόμα πρὸς στόμα, μετά + genitive) or with a dative addressee

senses.definition: To articulate, state, or tell specific words, truths, teachings, or reports to an audience, or (in the passive) to be recounted.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with accusative object (words, things, truth) or passive subject, or intransitive with περί + genitive (topic) and optional dative or πρός/εἰς addressee

senses.definition: To proclaim or declare a prophetic or divine message, such as the word of God, the gospel, or Spirit-inspired speech.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with message object (τὸν λόγον, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, ὧν) or passive with διά + genitive agent, or paired with prophetic/Spirit-led speech

senses.definition: To utter ecstatic or unfamiliar languages (tongues), often in a Spirit-filled or worship context.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + instrumental dative plural γλώσσαις (with or without καιναῖς)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasts or pairs with λέγω (e.g., JHN 12:49, 1CO 12:3) and ἀκούω (e.g., JHN 16:13, ACT 4:20, JAS 1:19). Common adverbial and prepositional collocations include παρρησίᾳ (speaking openly, JHN 7:26, JHN 18:20), ἐν κρυπτῷ (JHN 18:20), ἐν παραβολαῖς (MAT 13:13), ἐξ ἐμαυτοῦ / ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ (speaking on one's own authority, JHN 12:49, JHN 16:13), στόμα πρὸς στόμα (face-to-face conversation, 2JN 1:12), and the instrumental dative γλώσσαις (speaking in tongues, MRK 16:17, ACT 19:6, 1CO 14:5). Direct objects commonly include τὰ ῥήματα, τὸν λόγον, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, and ἀλήθειαν.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The expanse above the earth (the sky and upper cosmos) as well as the transcendent realm where God and angels dwell and rule.

senses.definition: The visible expanse above the earth where birds fly, clouds, rain, lightning, and celestial signs appear, or the upper created cosmos paired with earth and sea.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun, often as object of prepositions (ἐν, ὑπό, ἀπό), in genitive phrases (νεφελῶν/πετεινὰ/στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ), or coordinated with γῆ (and θάλασσα)

senses.definition: The transcendent dwelling place and sphere of God and angels, from which divine voices, messengers, bread, and spiritual blessings or dwellings originate, and to which Christ or visions ascend.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun, chiefly with locative or directional prepositions (ἐν, ἐκ, ἀπό, εἰς), or in the genitive phrase ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

senses.definition: In the fixed genitive phrase ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν, the sphere or source characterizing God's sovereign reign and community.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural genitive noun modifying ἡ βασιλεία (τῶν οὐρανῶν)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in both singular (e.g., ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ) and plural (e.g., ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, τῶν οὐρανῶν) forms with overlapping referential scope, especially for the divine realm. Common pairings and collocations include οὐρανός coupled with γῆ (and occasionally θάλασσα) to express cosmic totality (MAT 16:19, MAT 28:18, MRK 13:27, ACT 17:24, REV 5:13, REV 14:7); the recurring Matthean phrase ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν (MAT 3:2, MAT 7:21, MAT 11:11, MAT 13:31, MAT 13:52, MAT 16:19, MAT 19:14); directional prepositional phrases indicating divine origin or destination (ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ, εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν); and genitive modifiers such as τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ (LUK 9:58), αἱ νεφέλαι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ (MAT 24:30), ἡ στρατιὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ (ACT 7:42), and ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ οὐρανοῦ (REV 11:13).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To take hold of, bring along, or claim something or someone, and correspondingly to receive, accept, experience, or be overtaken by something given or encountered.

senses.definition: To grasp, take in hand, pick up, or bring along a physical object, often as a preparatory action before distributing or using it.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb + accusative object (frequently as an aorist participle before a finite verb)

senses.definition: To take away, exact, or collect dues or possessions from someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb + accusative object (optionally with ἀπό + genitive of source)

senses.definition: To take a woman as one's wife in marriage.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb + accusative object (a woman)

senses.definition: To receive, obtain, or accept something bestowed, paid, entrusted, commanded, or inflicted, including rewards, spiritual gifts, forgiveness, testimony, or stripes.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb + accusative object (or absolute in PHP 3:12; with παρά or ὑπό + genitive of source/agent)

senses.definition: To welcome or accept a person, especially a sent representative or messenger.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb + accusative personal object

senses.definition: To come upon, seize, or overtake someone (with a condition or trial as grammatical subject).
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb with abstract subject + accusative personal object

senses.definition: To engage in an activity or undergo an experience expressed by the accompanying noun object (such as taking counsel or experiencing trial).
senses.grammatical_frame: idiomatic collocation with accusative noun (συμβούλιον or πεῖραν + genitive)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very frequently used as an aorist participle (λαβών, λαβοῦσα, λαβόντες) preceding a main action verb to indicate taking hold of an object before using or distributing it (MRK 14:23, JHN 12:3, HEB 9:19). Takes παρά + genitive ('from') for the source of testimony, repayment, or commands (LUK 6:34, JHN 5:34, 2JN 1:4), ἀπό + genitive ('from') for tax collection (MAT 17:25), and ὑπό + genitive ('by/from') for receiving punishment (2CO 11:24). Forms fixed idiomatic phrases with συμβούλιον ('take counsel', MAT 28:12) and πεῖραν + genitive ('experience/undergo', HEB 11:36).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Confident trust or reliance placed in God, Jesus, or divine promises, extending to steadfast faithfulness, convincing assurance, and the shared body of Christian belief.

senses.definition: Active trust, reliance, or confident conviction directed toward God, Jesus, or unseen divine realities and promises, often serving as the basis for healing, righteous standing, or obedient action.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun; often with ἔχω, or in prepositional phrases (ἐκ, διά, ἐν), instrumental dative (πίστει), or with genitive/ἐν + object of trust

senses.definition: Steadfast loyalty, trustworthiness, or enduring fidelity as a moral and relational quality in conduct and devotion.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun; often in lists of personal virtues or with verbs of enduring and not failing

senses.definition: The established message, teaching, or shared system of Christian belief and allegiance handed down to believers.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun with definite article (ἡ πίστις) or possessive modifier; with verbs of departing from, contending for, or being sound in

senses.definition: A convincing pledge, proof, or ground of certainty offered to establish truth.
senses.grammatical_frame: direct object of παρέχω + dative of recipient

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in prepositional phrases such as ἐκ πίστεως ('on the basis of trust'), διὰ πίστεως ('through trust'), ἐν πίστει ('in trust/faithfulness'), and in the instrumental dative πίστει ('by trust'). Often paired or contrasted with νόμος ('law', ROM 4:16, GAL 3:11, PHP 3:9), ἔργα ('works', JAS 2:14, JAS 2:22), εἶδος ('sight', 2CO 5:7), ἀγάπη ('love', EPH 1:15, 1TH 1:3, 1TI 4:12), and ἀλήθεια ('truth', 1TI 2:7, 2TI 3:8). The genitive construction πίστις Ἰησοῦ / Χριστοῦ (ROM 3:26, GAL 2:20, PHP 3:9) allows both objective ('trust in Jesus/Christ') and subjective ('faithfulness of Jesus/Christ') readings. With παρέχω + dative (ACT 17:31), it forms the idiom 'give assurance/proof to'.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To accept a message or claim as true, place trust and allegiance in someone, or (in the passive) be entrusted with a responsibility.

senses.definition: To regard a statement, report, testimony, or proposition as true and reliable, or to accept someone's word as credible.
senses.grammatical_frame: active voice with `ὅτι` content clause, dative of message or speaker, or both

senses.definition: To place personal reliance, confidence, and religious allegiance in God, Christ, or the message of the gospel.
senses.grammatical_frame: active voice with `εἰς` + accusative, `ἐν` + dative, or dative of a divine person

senses.definition: To have faith or come to trust (with object implied by context); in substantival participial forms, to designate believers as an identifiable group.
senses.grammatical_frame: active voice used intransitively without explicit complement, or as substantival participle

senses.definition: To be given charge of or assigned responsibility for a task or stewardship.
senses.grammatical_frame: passive voice with accusative of the thing entrusted

entries.collocations_and_notes: Shows distinct syntactic patterns: `εἰς` + accusative (`εἰς αὐτόν`, `εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ`, `εἰς τὸν Υἱόν`) predominates in Johannine texts and 1PE 1:8 for personal commitment/allegiance; dative objects range from a speaker or message (`τῷ λόγῳ`, `τοῖς ῥήμασιν`, `τῇ ἀκοῇ`, `τῇ ἀληθείᾳ`) to God or the Lord (`τῷ Κυρίῳ`, `τῷ Θεῷ`); and `ὅτι` clauses express propositional conviction. Contrasts directly with `ἀπειθέω` ('disobey/refuse trust', JHN 3:36), `φοβέομαι` ('fear', LUK 8:50, ACT 9:26), and `εὐδοκέω τῇ ἀδικίᾳ` ('take pleasure in unrighteousness', 2TH 2:12), while correlating with `ὑπακούω` ('obey', ROM 10:16), `μετανοέω` ('repent', MRK 1:15), and `βαπτίζομαι` ('be baptized', MRK 16:16, ACT 18:8). Substantival participles (`ὁ πιστεύων`, `οἱ πιστεύσαντες`, `οἱ πεπιστευκότες`, `οἱ πιστεύοντες`) serve as a standard label for members of the Christian community.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Negative pronoun denoting the complete absence of any person, thing, value, or degree.

senses.definition: Not a single person; used as a personal negative pronoun in subject, object, or prepositional positions, sometimes with a partitive genitive or followed by an exception clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine singular pronoun (nominative, genitive, dative, or accusative), alone or with partitive genitive or adjective

senses.definition: Not a single thing, action, word, or circumstance; used as an impersonal negative pronoun, often modified by a participle, adjective, or partitive genitive.
senses.grammatical_frame: neuter singular pronoun (nominative, genitive, or accusative), as subject, direct object, or with partitive genitive or modifier

senses.definition: That which lacks substance, validity, or usefulness, appearing in prepositional phrases (`εἰς οὐδέν`) or equative clauses (`οὐδέν ἐστιν`).
senses.grammatical_frame: neuter singular in `εἰς` + accusative or predicate nominative with `εἰμί`

senses.definition: To no extent or degree; modifying verbs of benefiting or making a difference.
senses.grammatical_frame: neuter singular accusative used adverbially with verbs

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently follows or pairs with a negated verb (`οὐ` / `οὐκ`) to express or reinforce total negation (MRK 14:61, LUK 4:2, JHN 5:19, JHN 14:30, 1CO 6:5), or doubles with another form of `οὐδείς` (`οὐδενὶ ... οὐδέν`, LUK 9:36). Commonly paired with `εἰ μή` (or `ἂν μή`) to introduce the sole exception to a general negation (MAT 5:13, MAT 11:27, JHN 5:19, 1CO 1:14, 1CO 12:3), and with `πώποτε` ('ever', JHN 1:18, 1JN 4:12) or `οὔπω` ('not yet', MRK 11:2). Frequent verbal collocations include `οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο` ('answered nothing', MAT 27:12, MRK 14:61, LUK 23:9) and `ποιεῖν ... οὐδέν` ('do nothing', JHN 5:19, JHN 8:28, ACT 28:17). In MAT 22:16 (`περὶ οὐδενός`), the genitive form could be read as either personal ('anyone') or impersonal ('anything'), though the following clause (`πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων`) points toward human partiality.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Set apart to God and marked by divine purity or consecration, used of God, the Holy Spirit, devoted people, and sacred objects or spaces.

senses.definition: Possessing divine purity and transcendence; set apart as sacred, especially as the regular epithet of the Spirit of God and as a title for God or Christ.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective modifying Πνεῦμα or Πατήρ, or substantivized singular (ὁ Ἅγιος)

senses.definition: Consecrated to God and marked by upright, blameless conduct; when substantivized, those belonging to God's devoted community of believers or prophets.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective with human nouns, or substantivized masculine plural (οἱ ἅγιοι) / singular (πᾶς ἅγιος)

senses.definition: Dedicated to divine service or characterized by ritual and moral purity; when substantivized in the neuter plural, the sacred sanctuary or innermost shrine.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective with inanimate nouns (νόμος, ἐντολή, ναός, φίλημα), or substantivized neuter plural (τὰ ἅγια, Ἅγια ἁγίων)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most frequently occurs in the fixed collocation Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον / τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ('Holy Spirit'), appearing with verbs of filling (πίμπλημι), giving (δίδωμι), receiving (λαμβάνω), and baptizing (βαπτίζω). When substantivized in the masculine plural (οἱ ἅγιοι), it serves as a standard collective term for members of the Christian community (e.g., in greetings, collections for the poor, and prayers). In the neuter plural (τὰ ἅγια, Ἅγια ἁγίων), it designates the sacred precincts or innermost sanctuary.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The proper name or title by which a person or being is identified, also extending to the reputation, character, or delegated authority represented by that name.

senses.definition: The specific proper name or appellation by which a person or being is called, identified, or recorded.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (nominative, accusative, or genitive) with verbs of calling, having, or writing; or dative ὀνόματι specifying an individual's name

senses.definition: A title, label, or rank of honor conferred upon or borne by someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun modified by a demonstrative or prepositional qualifier (e.g., ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ, τὸ ὄνομα τὸ ὑπὲρ πᾶν ὄνομα)

senses.definition: A person's name considered as embodying their character, reputation, identity, or cause, especially as revered, proclaimed, invoked, or opposed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Object of verbs of sanctifying, making known, confessing, glorifying, bearing, or calling upon; or governed by prepositions διά, ἕνεκεν, or πρός

senses.definition: The authority, power, or representative capacity of another under which one acts, speaks, heals, requests, or welcomes, or into whose allegiance one is baptized.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrases ἐν (τῷ) ὀνόματι, ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι, or εἰς τὸ ὄνομα with a genitive or possessive pronoun

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in prepositional phrases expressing agency, basis, or allegiance: ἐν (τῷ) ὀνόματι ('in the name/authority of'), ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι ('on the basis of / in the name of'), εἰς τὸ ὄνομα ('into the name/allegiance of' with βαπτίζω), and διὰ τὸ ὄνομα / ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματος ('on account of the name'). In Acts, the bare dative ὀνόματι regularly introduces a named individual ('by name X'). Common verbal collocations include καλέω τὸ ὄνομα ('call/give a name'), ἐπικαλέομαι τὸ ὄνομα ('call upon the name'), δοξάζω τὸ ὄνομα ('glorify the name'), and γράφω/ἐξαλείφω τὸ ὄνομα ('write/blot out a name' in the book of life).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A verb denoting cognitive understanding, coming to realize or ascertain a fact, personal relational knowledge of God or people, and, euphemistically, sexual intercourse.

senses.definition: To understand, grasp intellectually, or have thorough awareness of a concept, inner state, or reality.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive (with accusative object of a thing, meaning, or inner state) or intransitive

senses.definition: To perceive, realize, learn, or ascertain a fact, situation, or truth, including ingressive discovery and confident recognition based on evidence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active (with ὅτι clause, indirect question, περὶ + genitive, or pronoun τοῦτο/ἐκεῖνο)

senses.definition: To become known, be discovered, or be made evident and recognized by others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive (with optional ὑπό + genitive or dative of recipient)

senses.definition: To know a person, God, or Christ relationally, including acknowledging and responding to their identity and character.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive (with personal accusative object)

senses.definition: To have sexual intercourse with someone, used as a polite or idiomatic expression of marital intimacy.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive (with personal accusative object in negated statements)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasts or pairs with οἶδα (JHN 13:7, JHN 21:17, ROM 7:7, EPH 5:5) and once contrasts with the compound ἐπιγινώσκω (1CO 13:12). Tense distinctions carry aspectual nuance, as when the aorist subjunctive and present subjunctive are paired in JHN 10:38 (ἵνα γνῶτε καὶ γινώσκητε) to express coming to know and continuing to know. Common patterns include the imperative τοῦτο/ἐκεῖνο γινώσκετε ὅτι introducing a warning or doctrinal point (MAT 24:43, LUK 12:39, 2TI 3:1) and ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν/γνωσόμεθα ὅτι expressing a test of assurance (1JN 2:3, 1JN 3:19).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A preposition that marks the agent, force, or source of an action when governing the genitive, and spatial position beneath or hierarchical subjection when governing the accusative.

senses.definition: Marks a human, collective, or divine agent by whom the action of a passive verb or participle is performed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive (with passive verb or participle)

senses.definition: Marks an inanimate force, instrument, written authority, or abstract concept acting as the agent or means of a passive verb or participle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive (inanimate or abstract noun with passive verb or participle)

senses.definition: Identifies the personal or divine source from which authority originates or from whom an experienced action proceeds without an explicit passive verb.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive (with existential verb or active verb of enduring)

senses.definition: Indicates spatial location or movement into a position beneath or underneath a physical cover or expanse.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative (with verbs of motion, gathering, or spatial reference)

senses.definition: Indicates subordination, jurisdiction, or subjection under a ruler, authority, or legal system, sometimes using the spatial image of placement beneath someone's feet.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative (expressing rank, dominion, or legal status)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Elides to ὑπ’ before vowels with smooth breathing (e.g., LUK 3:7, ACT 2:24) and ὑφ’ before vowels with rough breathing (e.g., 2CO 1:16, 2CO 12:11). With the genitive, it contrasts with διὰ + genitive in MAT 1:22 to distinguish the ultimate agent (the Lord) from the human intermediary (the prophet). With the accusative, it occurs both in spatial idioms (ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν in LUK 17:24; ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας in EPH 1:22) and in fixed expressions of legal or hierarchical status (ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν in LUK 7:8; ὑπὸ νόμον in GAL 3:23, GAL 4:5). No dative occurrences appear in the sample.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To move out of an enclosed space, locality, or group, set out toward a destination or task, depart from a host (of spirits), or originate and spread outward from a source.

senses.definition: To move physically out of or away from an interior space, building, city, region, or community (including metaphorical separation from a group in 2CO 6:17).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, used absolutely or with ἐκ + genitive, ἀπό + genitive, bare genitive, or adverbial source (ἐκεῖθεν)

senses.definition: To set out from a starting point toward a specified destination, on a journey, or to perform an intended action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with εἰς + accusative, ἐπί + accusative, σύν + dative, or an infinitive of purpose

senses.definition: Of an unclean spirit or demon, to depart from and cease inhabiting a possessed person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with ἐκ + genitive or ἀπό + genitive of the person

senses.definition: To emerge, arise, or be sent forth from a source, lineage, inner faculty, or divine origin into public appearance or the world.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with ἐκ + genitive of origin/source and/or εἰς + accusative (τὸν κόσμον)

senses.definition: Figuratively, of an intangible entity such as a report or expectation, to spread outward across a region (MAT 9:26) or to depart and come to an end (ACT 16:19).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with abstract subject (φήμη, ἐλπίς), with or without εἰς + accusative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes prepositional phrases indicating the point of departure (`ἐκ` + genitive, `ἀπό` + genitive, `ἐκεῖθεν`) or destination (`εἰς` + accusative, `ἐπί` + accusative), as well as a bare genitive of separation (MAT 13:1) or an infinitive of purpose (`θεάσασθαι` MAT 11:7; `σπεῖραι` MRK 4:3; `προσεύξασθαι` LUK 6:12; `ἰδεῖν` LUK 7:26, LUK 8:35; `ἀναζητῆσαι` ACT 11:25; `πορεύεσθαι` ACT 20:1). Repeatedly paired in contrast with `εἰσέρχομαι` or `εἰσελθεῖν` (MRK 9:25; LUK 14:23) and `ἥκω` or `ἔρχομαι` (JHN 8:42; JHN 16:28). In exorcism accounts, it regularly takes `ἐκ` or `ἀπό` + genitive of the affected person (MRK 1:25; MRK 7:29; LUK 4:35; LUK 11:24).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To have the power, capacity, or authorization to perform an action, or for an action or state to be possible under given circumstances.

senses.definition: To possess the inherent power, strength, skill, mental grasp, or functional efficacy required to bring something about.
senses.grammatical_frame: deponent verb + complementary infinitive; or participle + infinitive (including substantival participle); or articular infinitive + infinitive

senses.definition: To be possible, permissible, tolerable, or consistent given external constraints, authority, moral character, spiritual requirements, or logical conditions (including passive potentiality).
senses.grammatical_frame: deponent verb + complementary infinitive (active or passive), frequently negated or in conditional/interrogative clauses

senses.definition: To be able or have the capacity to perform or endure an action implied by the immediate context without an explicitly repeated infinitive.
senses.grammatical_frame: absolute or elliptical verb without an overt infinitive complement (including optative with ἄν)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly takes a complementary aorist or present infinitive (e.g., ἀποκτεῖναι, θεραπεῦσαι, ποιῆσαι, ἐλθεῖν, νοῆσαι); occasionally used with an articular infinitive (τοῦ δύνασθαι, 1CO 10:13; PHP 3:21) or as a substantival participle (τὸν δυνάμενον, MAT 10:28; τῷ δυναμένῳ, JUD 1:24). Frequently negated with οὐ/μή or used in rhetorical questions expecting a negative answer (e.g., τίς δύναται, MAT 6:27, MRK 2:7, JHN 6:60; μὴ δύναται, JHN 10:21, JAS 3:12) or paired with εἰ μή ('except', MRK 2:7, MRK 9:29). In 1CO 10:13 and PHP 3:21 it appears alongside δύναμις-related contexts of endurance and active working (ἐνέργεια), and in MRK 6:5 it takes ποιῆσαι δύναμιν as its complement. Both ἠδυν- (MAT 17:16, MRK 14:5, LUK 19:3) and ἐδυν- (MRK 6:5, 1CO 3:2, REV 7:9) augmented imperfect/aorist forms occur.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A demonstrative and correlative adverb indicating manner, circumstance, degree, or analogy ('in this way', 'thus', 'so').

senses.definition: Referring back to a manner, behavior, condition, or circumstance just mentioned or observed ('in this manner', 'like this', 'in such a state'; with negation, 'not even so').
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying a verb or serving as predicate with εἰμί (or elliptical predicate), with anaphoric reference; also with οὐδέ or μέν ... δέ

senses.definition: Pointing forward to an account, quotation, or qualifying explanation that immediately follows ('as follows', 'in the following way').
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying verbs of being, speaking, or occurring, with cataphoric reference (sometimes paired with ὡς)

senses.definition: Marking an analogy, correspondence, or logical sequence in relation to a preceding illustration, comparison, or event ('in the same way', 'accordingly', 'so also').
senses.grammatical_frame: correlative or transitional adverb introducing a main clause (often paired with ὥσπερ, καθώς, καθ’ ὃν τρόπον, or followed by καί / οὖν)

senses.definition: Indicating a high degree, intensity, or surprising extent ('to such an extent', 'so very', 'really').
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb of degree modifying an adjective, or modifying a verb with a result clause (ὥστε) or in an exclamation/reproachful question

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears predominantly in the form οὕτως before vowels and at clause/sentence boundaries, and as οὕτω before a consonant in HEB 12:21 (οὕτω φοβερὸν). Regularly forms correlative pairs with ὥσπερ (MAT 24:27, ROM 5:12, ROM 6:4, 1CO 11:12), καθώς (2CO 8:6, 1TH 2:4), ὡς (MRK 4:26, 1CO 3:15), and καθ’ ὃν τρόπον (ACT 27:25), and pairs with ὥστε to introduce a result (JHN 3:16). Common fixed expressions include καὶ οὐδὲ / οὐδ’ οὕτως ('and not even so', MRK 14:59, 1CO 14:21), ὁ μὲν οὕτως, ὁ δὲ οὕτως ('one this way, another that way', 1CO 7:7), and οὕτως καί / οὖν καί ('so also / accordingly', LUK 17:10, ROM 11:5, 1CO 15:45, JAS 3:5).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A postpositive enclitic coordinating particle used to link parallel words, phrases, or clauses, either in correlative pairs ("both ... and ...") or singly to add a closely connected item or subsequent narrative clause ("and", "and so").

senses.definition: Correlatively pairs two or more grammatically parallel nouns, adjectives, pronouns, infinitives, or clauses to present them as closely joined together.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle paired with καί (τε ... καί) or with another τε (τε ... τε)

senses.definition: Links a coordinate noun phrase, infinitive, or verb phrase to a preceding parallel element without an immediately paired καί.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle joining a coordinate phrase or infinitive to a preceding element

senses.definition: Introduces a new clause or sentence closely connected to the preceding statement as a continuation, accompanying circumstance, or next step in a narrative or argument.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle placed after the first constituent of a clause (verb, participle, pronoun, or noun phrase)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Postpositive enclitic particle placed immediately after the first word or phrase of the element or clause it joins (e.g., after an article, pronoun, noun, participle, or finite verb). Heavily concentrated in Acts in narrative clause transitions (ACT 4:33; ACT 8:31; ACT 13:46; ACT 24:10). Common fixed combinations in the sample include correlative `τε ... καί` (MAT 22:10; ACT 1:1; ROM 3:9; 1CO 1:24), `ὅ τε ... καί` linking articular proper names (LUK 23:12; ACT 17:14), `ἔτι τε καί` ("and furthermore also", ACT 21:28), `ὁμοίως τε καί` ("and likewise also", ROM 1:27), and repeated `τε ... τε` (ACT 26:10; ACT 27:3). In ACT 17:14, two occurrences appear in one clause: the first connects the clause to the preceding sentence, while the second pairs the two subjects with `καί`.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To desire, wish, or be willing to do or have something; also used of deliberate choice, fondness, or communicative intent.

senses.definition: To desire, wish, want, or be willing for something to happen or to perform an action; when negated, to be unwilling, reluctant, or refuse.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, followed by complementary infinitive, accusative + infinitive, ἵνα + subjunctive, deliberative subjunctive, or neuter pronoun object; also used absolutely, as a substantival participle, or as an articular infinitive (τοῦ θέλειν).

senses.definition: To decide, choose, or sovereignly purpose, especially of divine will and appointment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb with divine subject (ὁ Θεός), used either absolutely after καθώς or with a complementary infinitive.

senses.definition: To like, enjoy, or take delight in a practice or honor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival participle governing both a complementary infinitive and a direct noun object.

senses.definition: To intend to say or signify; to mean.
senses.grammatical_frame: Optative with ἄν, interrogative pronoun τί, and complementary infinitive λέγειν.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently negated with οὐ/μή to express unwillingness or refusal (MAT 18:30; MAT 22:3; MAT 27:34; LUK 13:34; LUK 18:13; 2TH 3:10; 3JN 1:13). The negated epistolary expression οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν introduces an important teaching point (1CO 12:1). Contrasted with actual capability (δύναμαι in MAT 8:2; MRK 6:19) and with carrying out an action (ποιῆσαι/ἐπιτελέσαι in 2CO 8:11; ROM 7:16).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An authoritative code of regulations, especially the Mosaic legal-religious system and the Scriptures containing it, or by extension any governing principle or standard of conduct.

senses.definition: The Mosaic code of commandments, ritual ordinances, and legal obligations governing religious and moral life.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, articular or anarthrous, often modified by Μωϋσέως, governed by prepositions (κατά, ἐν, διά, ἐκ, ὑπό), or serving as object of verbs of observing, doing, or transgressing.

senses.definition: The sacred Jewish Scriptures containing that code, appealed to as written authority and read aloud.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, articular (ὁ νόμος), used in ἐν τῷ νόμῳ with verbs of writing or reading (γέγραπται, ἀνέγνωτε), or paired with τοὺς προφήτας.

senses.definition: A governing rule, normative standard, or controlling principle of life, thought, or inner compulsion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, articular or anarthrous, modified by descriptive adjectives (ἕτερος, τέλειος) or specifying genitives (πίστεως, τοῦ νοός μου, τῆς ἁμαρτίας, τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τῆς ἐλευθερίας), or used predicatively.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with Μωϋσέως (LUK 2:22; ACT 15:5) or juxtaposed with τοὺς προφήτας (MAT 5:17) and χάρις/πίστις/ἐπαγγελία (JHN 1:17; ROM 3:27; GAL 3:18). Common verbal collocations include keeping/doing/fulfilling (τηρεῖν, φυλάσσειν, πράσσειν, ποιεῖν, πληρῶσαι, ἀναπληρώσετε) and transgressing/abolishing (παραβάτης, καταλῦσαι). Common prepositional phrases include κατὰ τὸν νόμον, ἐν (τῷ) νόμῳ, διὰ νόμου, ἐκ νόμου, and ὑπὸ νόμον. In ROM 2:14, the word shifts within a single sentence between the revealed code (νόμον ἔχοντα / τὰ τοῦ νόμου) and an internal moral standard (ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To form written words or characters on a surface or document, especially to record events, compose letters or instructions, enroll names, or cite authoritative Scripture.

senses.definition: To mark letters, words, or statements onto a physical surface, scroll, or book in order to produce a permanent record, legal document, notice, or account of events and utterances.
senses.grammatical_frame: active or passive verb; often with accusative of text/document (e.g., αἰτίαν, βιβλίον, ὄνομα) or prepositional phrase of location (ἐπί + accusative, ἐν + dative)

senses.definition: In passive usage, to have a person's name or identity entered and preserved in an official or heavenly register.
senses.grammatical_frame: perfect passive indicative or participle + ἐπί + accusative or ἐν + dative (βιβλίον/βίβλῳ τῆς ζωῆς)

senses.definition: To compose and send a letter, directive, or written message to an individual or community.
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb + dative of recipient; optionally with accusative object (ἐπιστολήν, ἐντολήν, ταῦτα, τι), infinitive of command, or περί + genitive

senses.definition: To set down or stand recorded as authoritative sacred text, law, or prophecy, predominantly in passive formulas introducing quotations from Scripture.
senses.grammatical_frame: chiefly perfect passive indicative (γέγραπται) or participle, or aorist passive (ἐγράφη), often introduced by καθώς/ὡς/ὅτι; occasionally active with named author (JHN 5:46)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very frequently appears in the perfect passive indicative (`γέγραπται`, often introduced by `καθώς`, `ὡς`, `καθάπερ`, `ὥσπερ`, `γάρ`, or `ὅτι`) and as a substantival or attributive perfect passive participle (`τὸ γεγραμμένον`, `τὰ γεγραμμένα`, `ὁ λόγος ὁ γεγραμμένος`) as a standard formula for citing Israelite Scriptures and prophetic books. In epistolary contexts, frequently takes a dative indirect object for the recipient (`γράφω ὑμῖν`, `ἔγραψά σοι`) along with `περί` + genitive for the topic, or direct objects such as `ἐπιστολήν`, `ἐντολήν`, and `ταῦτα`. In legal or official contexts, occurs with `βιβλίον ἀποστασίου` (MRK 10:4) and `αἰτίαν` (MAT 27:37), and in apocalyptic imagery with `τὸ ὄνομα` and `βιβλίον/βίβλῳ τῆς ζωῆς` (REV 17:8, REV 20:15).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A preposition indicating spatial proximity alongside something, personal presence or estimation with someone, origin/source from a person, or comparison and deviation beyond a standard.

senses.definition: Indicating the personal source, origin, sender, or giver from whom information, gifts, decrees, or messengers proceed or are received.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (typically a personal noun or pronoun)

senses.definition: Indicating location immediately beside someone, or staying and keeping possessions in a person's company or home.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative (personal noun or pronoun)

senses.definition: Indicating the perspective, moral standard, capability, or judgment of someone (especially God or humans) in whose estimation a matter holds true.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative (personal noun, especially θεῷ/πατρί or ἀνθρώποις)

senses.definition: Indicating position beside or movement along the edge of a geographical feature or path.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + accusative (non-personal spatial noun such as θάλασσαν, λίμνην, ὁδόν, ποταμόν)

senses.definition: Marking the standard of comparison after comparative adjectives or evaluative terms, indicating superiority or greater degree.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + accusative following a comparative expression

senses.definition: Indicating excess or divergence outside an expected rule, measure, or received teaching.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + accusative (e.g., relative clause ὃ δεῖ / ὃ παρελάβετε)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Governs three grammatical cases with distinct semantic profiles: genitive marks source or origin (almost exclusively personal); dative marks spatial presence with a person or evaluative perspective/judgment; accusative marks spatial location/motion alongside places, comparative superiority, or deviation beyond a norm. Frequently paired with verbs of receiving, hearing, asking, or coming from (`λαμβάνω`, `δέχομαι`, `ἀκούω`, `αἰτέω`, `ἐξέρχομαι`) in the genitive, and verbs of staying/dwelling (`μένω`, `μονὴν ποιέομαι`) or adjectives of evaluation (`δίκαιος`, `δυνατός`, `ἀδύνατος`, `ἐκλεκτός`) in the dative.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The inhabited earth or earthly sphere of human existence, the collective human inhabitants within it, and the present earthly or social order viewed in contrast to God.

senses.definition: The physical earth or inhabited world as the spatial realm of nations, earthly possessions, and mortal human life (entered at birth, inhabited, inherited, or destroyed).
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, frequently in spatial prepositional phrases (εἰς τόν, ἐν τῷ, ἐκ τοῦ) or modified by ὅλος or οὗτος

senses.definition: Humankind collectively, or the general public and society on earth, as the object of divine action or as acting, believing, hating, or judging.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun used as subject of personal verbs (e.g., πιστεύω, μισέω, εἰμί ἄξιος) or as object/genitive denoting people generally

senses.definition: The present earthly, social, or spiritual system and its values, wisdom, or elemental order, viewed as transient and alienated from or opposed to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, often with οὗτος or in genitive/prepositional phrases indicating origin, wisdom, elements, or allegiance (e.g., ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου, σοφία/στοιχεῖα/φιλία τοῦ κόσμου)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with the demonstrative οὗτος ("this world", e.g., JHN 8:23; JHN 12:25; JHN 18:36; 1CO 5:10; EPH 2:2; 1JN 4:17) and with ὅλος ("the whole world", e.g., MRK 8:36; ROM 1:8; 1JN 5:19). Common prepositional collocations include ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ("in the world"), εἰς τὸν κόσμον ("into the world"), and ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ("out of / from the world"). In Johannine and Pauline texts, senses 1b and 1c frequently overlap where human society as a collective is viewed as estranged from God (e.g., JHN 15:19; 1CO 1:20). Paralleled with ὁ αἰὼν οὗτος ("this age", 1CO 1:20; EPH 2:2) and contrasted with ὁ Πατήρ ("the Father", JHN 13:1; JHN 16:28; 1JN 2:15), ὁ Θεός ("God", 1CO 2:12; JAS 4:4), and τὰ ἄνω ("what is above", JHN 8:23).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A postpositive discourse particle that marks a clause, element, or subset as preliminary, conceded, or one side of a distribution or contrast, typically anticipating a balancing clause.

senses.definition: Marks the first member of a pair or contrast, presenting a statement or concession that is balanced or countered by a subsequent clause (usually introduced by δέ or ἀλλά, or by a negated parallel).
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle paired with a following contrasting clause (most often with δέ, occasionally ἀλλά or a negated contrast)

senses.definition: Paired with repeated or contrasting pronouns and articles to partition a whole into distinct individuals, portions, or subgroups.
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle following an article, demonstrative, or relative pronoun in a distributive series (e.g., ὁ μὲν ... ὁ δέ, οἱ μὲν ... ἄλλοι δέ, οὓς μὲν ... οὓς δέ)

senses.definition: Stands without a matching δέ-clause in the immediate sentence to introduce a first item in a sequence, mark a narrative transition or summary (often as μὲν οὖν), or present a conceded or supporting premise (often as μὲν γάρ or εἰ μέν).
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle without a paired δέ-clause in the same sentence, frequently combined with οὖν, γάρ, πρῶτον, or εἰ

entries.collocations_and_notes: Postpositive particle typically placed in second position in its clause or immediately after the contrasted word or article. Most commonly correlates with a following δέ (e.g., MAT 3:11; ACT 27:41; HEB 7:8), though occasionally balanced by ἀλλά (ROM 14:20) or an implied/negated contrast (COL 2:23). Frequently pairs with pronouns or articles to divide a group (e.g., ὁ μὲν ... ὁ δέ in 1CO 7:7, GAL 4:23; οἱ μὲν ... οἱ/ἄλλοι δέ in MAT 16:14, ACT 17:32; οὓς μὲν ... οὓς δέ in MRK 12:5; οἷς μὲν ... οἷς δέ in 2CO 2:16). Regularly combines with other particles: μὲν οὖν for narrative transitions or logical conclusions (ACT 5:41; ACT 16:5; ACT 25:4; PHP 2:23; HEB 8:4), μὲν γάρ for supporting or explanatory clauses (ACT 13:36; ROM 3:2; 2CO 11:4), and πρῶτον μὲν for enumerations (ROM 3:2; cf. πρῶτον λόγον in ACT 1:1). Doubled within a single clause in HEB 12:11 (πᾶσα μὲν ... πρὸς μὲν ... ὕστερον δέ).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A subordinating conjunction expressing comparison of manner, conformity to a standard or word, degree, ground, or concurrent time ('just as, according as, as').

senses.definition: Introduces a clause (often elliptical or paired with correlative οὕτως, ὁμοίως, or καί) comparing two actions, qualities, or states, or presenting one as the pattern, standard, or reality corresponding to the other.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction + finite indicative clause (or elliptical phrase with omitted verb), frequently correlated with οὕτως, ὁμοίως, or καί

senses.definition: Indicates agreement or fulfillment in accordance with a command, custom, prior speech, or written Scripture.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction + verb of commanding, writing, or speaking (e.g., γέγραπται, συνέταξεν, ἐνετείλατο) or nominal phrase with ἔθος ('custom')

senses.definition: Indicates the degree or capacity to which an action occurs, or introduces an evidential ground appealing to shared knowledge or experience.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction + indicative clause (with verb of ability or cognition such as δύναμαι, οἶδα, ἐπιγινώσκω)

senses.definition: Marks concurrent time as an anticipated point or period approaches.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction + imperfect indicative verb of approaching (ἤγγιζεν)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently stands in correlative constructions with οὕτως ('thus/so', LUK 24:24; JHN 12:50; 14:31; 2CO 8:6; 10:7; PHP 3:17), ὁμοίως ('likewise', LUK 6:31; 17:28), or καί ('also', JHN 17:18; ACT 15:8; ROM 1:13; 1CO 10:6; 11:1; 13:12; EPH 4:17; 5:25; 2TH 3:1; 1JN 4:17). Standard introductory formula for Scripture citations and prophetic fulfillment: καθὼς γέγραπται ('just as it is written', MRK 14:21; ROM 15:9; 1CO 2:9), καθὼς εἶπεν ἡ γραφή (JHN 7:38), καθὼς προείρηκεν / προείρηται (ROM 9:29; HEB 4:7). Also occurs in elliptical verbless clauses (ACT 15:8; ROM 1:13; 1CO 11:1; 2CO 10:7; 2TH 3:1; HEB 10:25).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To locate, encounter, discover, prove to be, or obtain someone or something through searching, observation, or circumstance.

senses.definition: To locate, come upon, or recover a person or thing that is sought, expected, or previously lost; in the passive with negation, to cease to be present or exist.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb + accusative object (often paired with ζητέω 'seek' or ἀπόλλυμι 'lose'); passive verb (with subject of person/thing sought or lost)

senses.definition: To come across or meet a person unexpectedly or in the course of going somewhere.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb + accusative of person (often following a participle of motion such as ἐξέρχομαι 'go out') + optional circumstantial participle

senses.definition: To observe, verify, or prove someone or something to be in a particular state, condition, or course of action, including establishing grounds or character in evaluative or judicial settings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb + accusative object + circumstantial participle/predicate adjective (or καθώς clause); passive verb + predicate noun, adjective, participle, or εἰς + accusative

senses.definition: To obtain, gain, or attain a desired condition, provision, favor, or way of life; also to identify and select a suitable person or place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb + accusative of abstract quality, provision, place, or person (e.g., χάριν 'favor', ἀνάπαυσιν 'rest', ψυχήν 'life')

senses.definition: To figure out, determine, or devise a method or means for accomplishing something.
senses.grammatical_frame: Negated active participle + indirect deliberative question (ποίας + aorist subjunctive)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with ζητέω ('seek', LUK 11:24; JHN 7:34; ACT 17:27) and contrasted with ἀπόλλυμι ('lose/perish', MAT 16:25; LUK 15:6, 24). Idiomatic combinations include εὑρίσκω χάριν ('find/obtain favor', ACT 7:46; HEB 4:16), εὑρίσκω ἀνάπαυσιν ('find rest', MAT 11:29; LUK 11:24), and οὐχ εὑρίσκω αἰτίαν ('find no basis for a charge', JHN 19:6). In passive negations (REV 12:8; 18:21), 'not be found any longer' denotes ceasing to exist or remain. Often takes a double-accusative-style object + circumstantial participle or predicate adjective/noun (e.g., εὑρίσκω + acc. + participle in MRK 14:37; LUK 12:43; 23:2; passive + predicate in MAT 1:18; 1CO 4:2; GAL 2:17).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An action, deed, or pattern of conduct; an assigned task, labor, or enterprise; or the finished product of making or building.

senses.definition: An individual act, miraculous feat, or (usually plural) actions, moral practices, and religious observances by which a person or group lives and is evaluated.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun; commonly plural (τὰ ἔργα), object of ποιέω, πράσσω, or ἐργάζομαι, or governed by prepositions such as ἐξ, κατά, χωρίς, and ἐν.

senses.definition: Assigned labor, active service, mission, or an ongoing undertaking and enterprise.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun; predominantly singular in prepositional phrases (εἰς τὸ ἔργον, ἐν τῷ ἔργῳ, ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων) or paired with terms for effort or planning (κόπος, βουλή).

senses.definition: A physical or cosmic product brought into existence by building or making; handiwork.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun; modified by a verb of construction (ὃ ἐποικοδόμησεν) or a genitive of agency (τῶν χειρῶν σου).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired or contrasted with λόγος (word/speech; COL 3:17, 2TH 2:17) and πίστις (faith; JAS 2:17–24), and combined with adjectives such as καλός, ἀγαθός, or πονηρός. Common idioms include ἐργάζεσθαι τὰ ἔργα (to perform deeds/tasks) and ἔργα νόμου (observances/deeds prescribed by the law; ROM 3:20, GAL 3:10). Singular τὸ ἔργον in 1PE 1:17 refers collectively to each person's whole course of conduct.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Visible radiance or splendor, honor and praise ascribed to or sought from others, or an exalted state of majesty and excellence.

senses.definition: Visible brightness, radiance, or outward magnificence, especially as displayed by God, Christ, heavenly beings, or earthly kingdoms and mortal creatures.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; often modified by a genitive of possessor or in prepositional phrases (ἐν δόξῃ, διὰ δόξης) describing appearance or manifestation.

senses.definition: Honor, praise, renown, or favorable recognition offered to God in worship or sought and received among people (contrasted with dishonor).
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; direct object of δίδωμι, ζητέω, or λαμβάνω, or nominative subject in doxological acclamations with a dative recipient (δόξα Θεῷ, αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα).

senses.definition: Exalted status, majesty, or surpassing excellence characterizing God, Christ, a ministry, or the promised future condition of believers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; frequently in descriptive genitive phrases (θρόνου δόξης, Κύριον τῆς δόξης, πλοῦτος τῆς δόξης) or after εἰς/ἐν denoting an exalted condition.

senses.definition: As a title or metonym, the Majestic One (referring to God) or, in the plural, exalted dignitaries or powers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; singular with adjective as agent of a passive participle (ὑπὸ τῆς μεγαλοπρεποῦς δόξης), or plural accusative object of βλασφημέω.
