entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with τιμή (honor), ἔπαινος (praise), εὐχαριστία (thanksgiving), and πλοῦτος (riches), and directly contrasted with ἀτιμία (dishonor) in 2CO 6:8. Common verbal collocations include δοῦναι δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ (to give praise/honor to God) and ζητεῖν τὴν δόξαν (to seek honor/recognition). In 1TH 2:20, it denotes persons who are a source of pride and honor. In JUD 1:8, the plural δόξας as the object of βλασφημέω refers to exalted beings or dignitaries, though the verse alone does not specify whether angelic or human authorities are meant.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A particle indicating contingency, indefiniteness, potentiality, or counterfactuality depending on the clause type and verbal mood, and also functioning as a conditional conjunction meaning 'if'.

senses.definition: Marks an indefinite, generalizing, or prospective sense in relative clauses and temporal/manner clauses introduced by ὡς, usually with the subjunctive mood (occasionally with the future indicative in LUK 17:33 or the imperfect indicative for repeated past action in 1CO 12:2).
senses.grammatical_frame: Postpositive particle following relative pronouns, relative adjectives/adverbs (ὅς, ὅστις, ὅσος, ὡς), typically governing the subjunctive mood (occasionally future or imperfect indicative).

senses.definition: Marks contingency or expected future realization in temporal clauses with ἕως ('until') and purpose clauses with ὅπως ('so that') taking the subjunctive mood.
senses.grammatical_frame: Particle immediately following the conjunctions ἕως or ὅπως with a verb in the subjunctive mood.

senses.definition: Marks the consequence (apodosis) of a contrary-to-fact condition as unrealized or counterfactual, indicating what would be occurring or would have happened if the condition in the protasis had been fulfilled.
senses.grammatical_frame: Particle in the apodosis of an unreal conditional sentence (protasis with εἰ + past indicative), accompanying an imperfect, aorist, or pluperfect indicative verb (often directly following οὐκ).

senses.definition: Marks potentiality, conjecture, or deliberation in direct and indirect questions with the optative mood.
senses.grammatical_frame: Particle following an interrogative pronoun (τί, τίς) in direct questions or articular indirect questions (τὸ τί / τὸ τίς), governing the optative mood.

senses.definition: Functions as a conditional conjunction introducing a hypothetical condition or exception ('if', 'unless', 'except perhaps').
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial conditional conjunction (with subjunctive, including negative ἂν μή) or modifying the elliptical exception phrase εἰ μήτι.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly combines with relative pronouns and adverbs (ὃς ἄν, ὅστις ἄν, ὅ τι ἄν, ὅσα ἄν, ἃ ἄν, ὡς ἄν) and temporal/final conjunctions (ἕως ἄν, ὅπως ἄν); frequently follows the conjunction or relative immediately, with postpositive δέ or γάρ intervening (ὃς δ’ ἄν, ὃς γὰρ ἄν, ἃ γὰρ ἄν). In LUK 9:24 and LUK 17:33, ὃς ἄν alternates directly with ὃς ἐάν in parallel clauses. In 1CO 7:5, εἰ μήτι ἄν introduces an elliptical qualifying phrase without a finite verb.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A masculine Roman personal name borne in these texts both by the Christian apostle and letter-writer Paul and, in one instance, by the proconsul Sergius Paulus.

senses.definition: Personal name of the Christian apostle, missionary, Roman citizen, prisoner, and letter-writer associated with Barnabas, Silas, and Timothy, who proclaimed Jesus and addressed churches and individuals.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine proper noun, 2nd declension (nom. Παῦλος, gen. Παύλου, dat. Παύλῳ, acc. Παῦλον, voc. Παῦλε), used with or without the definite article; often in apposition with ἐγώ or titles such as ἀπόστολος and δέσμιος.

senses.definition: Cognomen of Sergius Paulus, the Roman proconsul described as an intelligent man who summoned Barnabas and Saul to hear the word of God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine proper noun in the dative singular paired with Σεργίῳ and in apposition to τῷ ἀνθυπάτῳ, governed by the preposition σύν.

entries.collocations_and_notes: In Acts, the name is frequently articular (ὁ Παῦλος, τὸν Παῦλον, τοῦ Παύλου, τῷ Παύλῳ) in narrative, whereas anarthrous forms occur especially in epistolary self-identifications (EPH 3:1; PHM 1:1), in conjunction with companions (Βαρνάβας καὶ Παῦλος, ACT 14:14), in direct address (Παῦλε, ACT 26:24), and in the signature formula τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου (COL 4:18; 2TH 3:17). In ACT 13:7, Σεργίῳ Παύλῳ refers to the proconsul who summoned Barnabas and Saul, distinguishing him from the apostle. The apostle is described as an ἀπόστολος (ACT 14:14), a Roman citizen (ACT 22:25), a διάκονος (1CO 3:5), and a δέσμιος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ (EPH 3:1; PHM 1:1).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The hidden inner center of a person, encompassing thought, perception, moral will, conscience, and emotion.

senses.definition: The inner seat of thought, reasoning, spiritual perception, and understanding.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, subject of παχύνω, dative of means (τῇ καρδίᾳ) with συνίημι, or in prepositional phrases (ἐν, ἐπί) with verbs of thinking, pondering, or illuminating

senses.definition: The inner center of will, resolve, intention, moral character, and self-evaluating conscience.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, object of σκληρύνω, γινώσκω, κρίνω, or ἔχω, dative of respect/means, or governed by prepositions (ἐν, ἐκ, εἰς, ἐπί)

senses.definition: The inner seat of feeling, desire, devotion, affection, sorrow, or encouragement.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, object of πληρόω, ἐμπίμπλημι, παρακαλέω, or στηρίζω, or in phrases ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας, ἐκ καρδίας, and ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις

entries.collocations_and_notes: In this sample, καρδία never refers to the physical anatomical organ; it consistently denotes the hidden inner self—the locus of thought, moral choice, and emotion—frequently contrasted with external speech or outward appearance (MAT 15:18, LUK 16:15, ROM 10:10). Common phrases include ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ('inwardly / to oneself', MAT 24:48, LUK 2:19), ἐκ καρδίας or ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας ('sincerely / wholeheartedly', MRK 12:33, 1PE 1:22), ἁπλότης / ἀφελότης καρδίας ('sincerity of heart', ACT 2:46, EPH 6:5), and verbs of hardening or dulling such as σκληρύνω, πωρόω, and παχύνω (MAT 13:15, MRK 6:52, HEB 3:8). Paralleled with διάνοια ('understanding/mind') in HEB 10:16 and paired with σύνεσις ('understanding') and ἰσχύς ('strength') in MRK 12:33.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Indicates priority in time, sequence, or order, or preeminence in rank, status, or importance.

senses.definition: Used as an ordinal adjective with a noun (or articular with an implied noun) to mark the initial item, day, event, or arrangement in a temporal or counted sequence, often contrasted with what is later or new.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective (or articular with implied noun)

senses.definition: Used substantivally or predicatively (including with a genitive of comparison) to identify the person or agent who acts, arrives, or exists prior to others in a sequence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival or predicative adjective (sometimes with genitive of comparison)

senses.definition: Denotes highest standing, importance, authority, or quality, whether applied to commands, garments, social status, or leading citizens of a community.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or substantival/predicative adjective (often with partitive/superlative genitive)

senses.definition: Used adverbially in the neuter singular to specify that an action, condition, or point in an argument takes place before another or holds procedural priority.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter singular adverbial modifying a verb or clause (sometimes with genitive of comparison)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with 'ἔσχατος' ('last', MAT 19:30; MRK 10:31), 'δεύτερος/τρίτος/τέταρτος' ('second/third/fourth', REV 4:7), 'καινός' ('new', HEB 9:15; REV 21:1), 'ἄλλος' ('another', 1CO 14:30), 'δοῦλος' ('servant', MAT 20:27), and sequential adverbs 'τότε' ('then', MAT 5:24; MRK 3:27) and 'ἔπειτα' ('then/next', 1CO 15:46; JAS 3:17). In 'ἀπὸ (τῆς) πρώτης ἡμέρας' ('from the first day', ACT 20:18; PHP 1:5) it marks an initial temporal boundary. With a genitive of comparison ('πρῶτός μου', JHN 1:30; 'πρῶτον ὑμῶν', JHN 15:18), it expresses temporal priority over another party; with a partitive/superlative genitive ('πρώτη πάντων', MRK 12:28; 'οἱ πρῶτοι τοῦ λαοῦ / τῆς πόλεως', LUK 19:47; ACT 13:50), it marks preeminence or leadership. In 1TI 1:16 ('ἐν ἐμοὶ πρώτῳ'), temporal/sequential priority as an initial pattern overlaps with the sense of foremost example. In LUK 15:22 ('στολὴν τὴν πρώτην'), context indicates a special garment of honor or finest quality brought out for the returning son.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Favorable regard, unmerited divine kindness or empowering gift, and the grateful response or blessing associated with such generosity.

senses.definition: Favorable regard, approval, or goodwill shown by a superior or God toward someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, subject or object of εὑρίσκω, δίδωμι, or κατατίθημι, or predicate nominative with παρά + dative or ἐναντίον + genitive

senses.definition: A pleasing, attractive, or winsome quality characterizing speech.
senses.grammatical_frame: genitive modifier (τῆς χάριτος) following ὁ λόγος

senses.definition: Unmerited kindness, generosity, or saving favor bestowed by God or Christ, often contrasted with law or human deeds and experienced as a sphere of standing or an empowering aid.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, frequently modified by τοῦ Θεοῦ or τοῦ Κυρίου, in instrumental dative (χάριτι), or governed by prepositions (εἰς, ὑπό, διά, ἐν, κατά)

senses.definition: A particular spiritual endowment, privilege, or generous act of service granted to or shared among believers.
senses.grammatical_frame: direct object or genitive complement with δίδωμι, ἔχω, κοινωνία, or συγκοινωνός

senses.definition: An invoked wish or pronouncement of divine blessing and goodwill in epistolary openings and closings.
senses.grammatical_frame: nominative in verbless, optative, or future blessing formulas with dative recipient (ὑμῖν) or μετά + genitive

senses.definition: Gratitude or thankful acknowledgment directed toward a benefactor for an action or gift.
senses.grammatical_frame: accusative object of ἔχω + dative, or nominative in verbless exclamation with dative of recipient (τῷ Θεῷ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with εἰρήνη ('peace') and ἔλεος ('mercy') in epistolary greetings and blessings (ROM 1:7, 1CO 1:3, 2JN 1:3). Commonly contrasted with νόμος ('law', JHN 1:17, ROM 6:15, GAL 2:21) and ἔργα ('works', ROM 11:6, 2TI 1:9). Standard idioms include εὑρίσκω χάριν παρά + dat. ('find favor with', LUK 1:30; cf. HEB 4:16), ἔχω χάριν + dat. ('be grateful to', LUK 17:9), χάρις τῷ Θεῷ ('thanks be to God', 2CO 2:14, 2CO 8:16, 2CO 9:15), and χάριτα κατατίθημι + dat. ('gain favor with', ACT 24:27, using the alternate accusative form χάριτα). Note that in HEB 13:9, χάριτι ('by grace') is contrasted with βρώμασιν ('foods/dietary practices').

entries.core_meaning_summary: Denotes an additional, distinct, or remaining person or thing relative to one or more already mentioned or implied.

senses.definition: Used attributively with a noun (or modifying a noun implied from immediate context) to mark an additional, separate, or different entity of the same general class.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective modifying a noun (or with an implied noun)

senses.definition: Used with the definite article (with or without an overt noun) to identify the second or remaining member of a pair or counted sequence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Articular adjective (attributive or substantival) in a pair or sequence

senses.definition: Used substantivally in the singular without a noun to refer to another individual person or a different thing, often in contrast with a previously mentioned person or item.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival singular (pronoun-like)

senses.definition: Used substantivally in the plural to denote other people or other things, frequently contrasting one group's actions, speech, or fate with another's.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival plural (pronoun-like)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently used in correlative or distributive sequences: 'ἄλλοι ... ἄλλοι' ('some ... others', e.g., MRK 8:28; JHN 9:9), 'πολλοὶ ... ἄλλοι δὲ' ('many ... and others', MRK 11:8), 'ἄλλῳ δὲ ... ἄλλῳ δὲ' ('to one ... and to another', 1CO 12:10), and 'ἄλλοι δὲ ἄλλο τι' ('some shouted one thing and others another', ACT 21:34). Paired with 'πρῶτος' ('first') in MAT 21:36, JHN 19:32, and 1CO 14:30, and with 'ἕτερος' in a list in 1CO 12:10. Combined with an indefinite pronoun in 'ἄλλος τις' ('someone else', LUK 22:59) and with numerals in 'ἄλλα δύο' ('two more', MAT 25:17) and 'ἄλλοι ... δύο' ('two others', JHN 21:2). Negative contrast with 'εἰ μή' appears in JHN 6:22 ('no other boat except one') and with 'παρά' + accusative in 1CO 3:11 ('no other foundation besides the one laid').

entries.core_meaning_summary: Marks a beneficiary, motivating cause, or subject of discourse when used with the genitive, and a standard exceeded or surpassed when used with the accusative.

senses.definition: For the benefit, advantage, or protection of someone, or aligned in support of a person or group (in contrast to opposition).
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive (typically with verbs of dying, giving, suffering, praying, or being aligned)

senses.definition: On account of, in response to, or for the purpose of something, indicating the motivating ground or goal of an action or suffering.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive (with abstract nouns, names, or relative pronouns)

senses.definition: With reference to or regarding a person or matter as the topic of speech, knowledge, or boasting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + genitive (with verbs or nouns of speaking, knowing, or boasting)

senses.definition: Surpassing a limit, degree, status, or point of comparison, including use with comparative adjectives.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition + accusative (expressing excess, rank, or comparison)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Governs the genitive in the great majority of occurrences to express benefit, support, cause, or topic, and governs the accusative to express degree or comparison beyond a standard. Stands in explicit opposition to κατά with the genitive ("against") in MRK 9:40 and LUK 9:50. Frequently appears in formulaic descriptions of death, suffering, or prayer on someone's behalf (ἀποθνῄσκω, πάσχω, τίθημι τὴν ψυχήν, παραδίδωμι, προσεύχομαι, δέομαι, εὐχαριστέω). In 1CO 15:29, βαπτίζομαι ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν expresses action on behalf of the dead, though the verse itself does not explain the details of the practice. In 1TI 2:2, the governing clause precedes the verse snippet, while the attached purpose clause (ἵνα...) reflects intercessory benefit. In 2CO 1:8, the word appears twice in the same sentence: first with the genitive ("concerning our affliction") and then with the accusative ("beyond our strength").

entries.core_meaning_summary: Indicates the present moment, the current era or state of affairs, the immediate past, or a logical transition grounded in current reality.

senses.definition: At the present time or current moment, often contrasting the speaker's or audience's present situation with an earlier condition or a future event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Temporal adverb modifying a verb, participle, or clause

senses.definition: In the immediate past, referring to an action that has just taken place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Temporal adverb modifying a past-tense verb (imperfect or aorist)

senses.definition: The present time treated as a temporal reference point or boundary in prepositional and adverbial expressions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized adverb with the neuter article, as object of a preposition (ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν, ἕως τοῦ νῦν) or in the accusative plural (τὰ νῦν)

senses.definition: Existing or operating at the present time, characterizing an age, world order, or ongoing activity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb in attributive position between a definite article and a noun or participle

senses.definition: Introduces the actual state of affairs in contrast to a hypothetical or contrary condition, or marks a logical or hortatory transition in argument and address.
senses.grammatical_frame: Discourse adverb, frequently paired with δέ, οὖν, or an imperative particle (ἄγε)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with δέ (JHN 8:40, LUK 16:25, EPH 5:8, 1PE 2:10) or contrasted with ποτέ ("once"), ὥσπερ ("just as"), or future verbs to mark a decisive shift in state or circumstance. Occurs in fixed prepositional phrases with the neuter singular article, ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ("from now on": LUK 1:48, 2CO 5:16) and ἕως τοῦ νῦν ("until now": MAT 24:21), and in the adverbial accusative plural τὰ νῦν ("for the present": ACT 27:22). Combined with οὖν in ACT 23:15 to urge action, with καί to introduce a new command or remark (ACT 10:5, ACT 20:25), and with ἄγε in JAS 4:13 as a direct exhortation. In 2CO 5:16, both the prepositional phrase ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν and the simple adverb νῦν appear in the same verse.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Physical bodily tissue, the mortal human body and earthly existence, humankind as a whole, human lineage and worldly standards, or the unspiritual side of human nature prone to sinful desires.

senses.definition: The soft physical tissue or bodily substance of humans and other living creatures, often paired with blood or bones.
senses.grammatical_frame: Concrete noun, singular or plural, often paired with αἷμα or ὀστέα

senses.definition: The physical human body or mortal bodily existence on earth, including outward bodily state, presence, suffering, or ritual purity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun, frequently in dative (σαρκί, τῇ σαρκί) or with ἐν / εἰς, often contrasted with πνεῦμα

senses.definition: Human beings collectively or mortal humanity, especially in the phrases πᾶσα σάρξ and σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun modified by πᾶς or coordinated with αἷμα

senses.definition: Natural human birth, blood kinship, earthly social standing, or ordinary human standards and effort as distinct from divine promise or spiritual status.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrases (especially κατὰ σάρκα, ἐκ τῆς σαρκός, ἐν σαρκί) or instrumental dative contrasted with spiritual or divine terms

senses.definition: Human frailty or the unspiritual, desire-driven aspect of human nature that opposes God's Spirit and tends toward sin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subject, object, genitive modifier (often with ἐπιθυμίαι or φρόνημα), or governed by κατά / ὀπίσω, frequently contrasted with πνεῦμα or νοῦς

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly paired with αἷμα ("blood") or ὀστέα ("bones") for physical body parts, and with πνεῦμα ("spirit") or νοῦς ("mind") in contrasts between the physical/human and spiritual spheres. Key fixed expressions include πᾶσα σάρξ ("all humanity"), σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα ("mortal human beings"), μία σάρξ / εἰς σάρκα μίαν (marital bodily union), and prepositional phrases such as κατὰ σάρκα ("according to human descent/standards/impulses") and ἐν σαρκί ("in physical bodily existence").

entries.core_meaning_summary: An indefinite or characterizing relative pronoun used for unspecified persons or things ("whoever", "whatever"), to describe or identify a specific antecedent ("who", "which"), or in the fixed temporal phrase ἕως ὅτου ("until").

senses.definition: Used without a specific named antecedent (or after πᾶς) to refer generically to any person or group meeting a condition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indefinite or generalizing relative pronoun without a specific antecedent (sometimes following πᾶς)

senses.definition: Introduces a relative clause that identifies, describes, or characterizes a stated person, group, or thing by an action, trait, or status.
senses.grammatical_frame: Relative pronoun agreeing in gender and number with a preceding noun or pronoun antecedent

senses.definition: Functions at the start of a new clause or sentence to continue a narrative or explain the consequence or nature of a previously mentioned person, group, or situation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial or continuative relative pronoun referring back to a prior participant or whole clause

senses.definition: In the neuter genitive after ἕως, marks the point in time up to which an action or state continues.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter genitive singular ὅτου governed by the preposition ἕως before a subjunctive verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears with an indefinite or generic force (sometimes reinforced by πᾶς in MAT 10:32) when no specific antecedent is named. With a stated antecedent, it often introduces a defining characteristic, explanation, or continuative narrative clause. The neuter genitive form ὅτου occurs in the fixed temporal phrase ἕως ὅτου ("until") in LUK 12:50. In PHP 1:28, feminine ἥτις agrees in gender with the predicate noun ἔνδειξις while referring back to the preceding clause.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To wake from sleep, lift or get up into an upright or active posture, restore a dead person to life, or bring something into existence, construction, or hostile motion.

senses.definition: To rouse someone from sleep (active) or to awaken from sleep (passive).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive with personal object; or passive intransitive, sometimes with ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου

senses.definition: To lift someone or an animal up to a higher or upright position (active transitive), or to rise, stand up, or get moving from a lying, sitting, bowed, or inactive state (passive, middle, or intransitive active imperative).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive with personal/animal object; or passive/middle (and active imperative ἔγειρε) used intransitively, often paired with verbs of standing or going

senses.definition: To bring a deceased person back to life (active transitive) or to be restored to life from death (passive, or intransitive imperative in LUK 8:54).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive with personal object or νεκρούς (often + ἐκ νεκρῶν); or passive (aorist/present/perfect) often with ἐκ/ἀπὸ (τῶν) νεκρῶν or temporal dative τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ

senses.definition: To erect or rebuild a physical structure.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive with architectural object (ναός)

senses.definition: To bring people or descendants into existence from an unexpected source.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive with personal object + ἐκ (source) + dative of beneficiary

senses.definition: To mobilize or initiate armed hostility against another group or realm.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive intransitive + ἐπί + accusative of opponent

senses.definition: To stir up or inflict distress or hardship upon someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive with abstract object (θλῖψιν) + dative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Shows a clear syntactic division between active transitive uses (raising/waking/building someone or something) and passive or intransitive active imperative uses (rising/waking/getting up). In resurrection contexts, frequently occurs with ἐκ νεκρῶν or ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, or with direct object τοὺς νεκρούς, and is paired with ζωοποιέω (JHN 5:21). In the healing and waking imperatives (MAT 9:6; MRK 2:11; LUK 6:8; LUK 8:54), the active imperative ἔγειρε functions intransitively ("get up!"), alternating with middle/passive imperatives ἐγείρεσθε (MRK 14:42; JHN 14:31) and ἐγέρθητε (MAT 17:7). Note LUK 8:54 where the command Ἡ παῖς, ἔγειρε bridges waking/standing up and restoring a dead child to life.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A physical body (living or dead) of a person or organism, and by extension the sacramental bread representing Christ's body or the collective community of believers united under Christ.

senses.definition: The physical organism or material form of a living human being (or Christ in earthly or transformed existence), viewed as a unified whole composed of parts and serving as the vehicle of earthly life and action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun; singular or plural; frequently with possessive genitives, ὅλον, or contrasted with ψυχή, πνεῦμα, or μέλη; also as accusative of respect (HEB 10:22)

senses.definition: The lifeless physical remains of a deceased person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun; object of verbs of taking, wrapping, or laying down in burial contexts

senses.definition: The ritual bread in the Lord's meal identified with or representing Christ's physical person given in death.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun; predicate nominative with τοῦτό ἐστιν or genitive object of ἔνοχος paired with αἷμα

senses.definition: The distinct outward form or physical structure bestowed by God on seeds or created entities.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun; direct object of δίδωσιν, modified by ἴδιον

senses.definition: The collective community of believers conceived as a unified organic whole connected to and nourished by Christ as its head.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun; qualified by genitive τοῦ Χριστοῦ or αὐτοῦ, or paired with Κεφαλή

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with ψυχή (MAT 6:25; LUK 12:23) and paired with πνεῦμα and ψυχή as distinct facets of a human being (1TH 5:23; JAS 2:26). Often paired with μέλη ("members/parts") to express unity in diversity, both literally of a human organism and analogically for the Christian community (MAT 5:29; ROM 12:4; 1CO 12:12–24; JAS 3:6). Prepositional phrases include ἐν (τῷ) σώματι and ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματος (1CO 6:18; 2CO 12:2), and διὰ τοῦ σώματος for earthly bodily agency (2CO 5:10) or Christ's death (ROM 7:4). Note genitive qualifiers such as τὸ σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως / δόξης (PHP 3:21) and τὸ σῶμα τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ (COL 1:22).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adverb indicating the repetition of an action or event ("again"), movement or restoration back to a prior place or state ("back"), or transition to an additional statement or citation in discourse ("again, furthermore").

senses.definition: Indicates that an action, speech, or condition takes place another time or repeatedly.
senses.grammatical_frame: Temporal adverb modifying finite verbs, participles, or infinitives

senses.definition: Indicates reversal or movement returning to a previous location, posture, possession, or condition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Directional or restitutive adverb modifying verbs of motion, posture, receiving, or returning

senses.definition: Introduces a further teaching, parable, counterbalancing statement, or additional Scripture citation within an argument or narrative.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial discourse adverb, often with και, δε, or an elliptical citation formula before direct speech or Scripture quotation

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often collocates with verbs of motion, speech, and sending (e.g., αποκρινομαι, αποστελλω, επερωταω, λαλεω, επανερχομαι/επιστρεφω/υποστρεφω). In GAL 4:9, two distinct occurrences appear in one sentence: first marking a backward return to prior elements, then reinforced as παλιν ανωθεν ("all over again"). Frequently appears with conjunctions (και παλιν, παλιν ουν, παλιν δε) at sentence or quotation boundaries, sometimes without an explicit verb of speaking when introducing Scripture (ROM 15:11; HEB 1:5; HEB 4:5).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To exist as a living being, recover or return from death, conduct one's daily life, or experience eternal and spiritual vitality in relation to God.

senses.definition: To possess biological existence, stay alive on earth, or sustain physical life.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb (finite forms, articular infinitive τὸ ζῆν, or substantive/attributive participle), sometimes modified by prepositional phrases of bodily sphere (ἐν σαρκί) or sustenance (ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ)

senses.definition: To survive or recover from mortal illness, or to return from death to life.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb (aorist, present, or future indicative, subjunctive, or participle), frequently paired with ἀνίστημι or σῴζω, or contrasted with νεκρός

senses.definition: To exist eternally as the active, true God, in contrast to lifeless idols or mortal beings, including use in divine oath formulas.
senses.grammatical_frame: Present active participle modifying Θεός or Πατήρ, or first-person present indicative in the oath formula Ζῶ ἐγώ

senses.definition: To conduct one's daily life or direct one's behavior and allegiance in a specified moral manner or in devotion to someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb modified by adverbs of manner (σωφρόνως, δικαίως, εὐσεβῶς), prepositional phrases (κατὰ σάρκα, ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι), or a dative of devotion/reference (τῷ Θεῷ, τῷ Κυρίῳ, ἑαυτοῖς)

senses.definition: To possess or attain enduring spiritual and eschatological life through faith, obedience, or union with God and Christ.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb (frequently future indicative or subjunctive), accompanied by phrases of means, sphere, or agency (ἐκ πίστεως, ἐν αὐτῇ, δι’ ἐμέ, δι’ αὐτοῦ)

senses.definition: (Participle used figuratively of non-human objects or abstractions) Active, flowing, enduring, or imparting vitality.
senses.grammatical_frame: Present active participle used attributively with non-human or abstract nouns (ὕδωρ, ἐλπίς, λίθοι)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with ἀποθνῄσκω ("to die", ROM 7:2, 8:13, 14:8, HEB 7:8), τέθνηκα ("to be dead", 1TI 5:6), or νεκρός ("dead", MAT 22:32, LUK 15:32, JHN 5:25, ROM 6:11, REV 2:8). Forms recurring theological epithets with Θεός ("living God", 2CO 6:16, 1TH 1:9, REV 7:2, 15:7) and Πατήρ (JHN 6:57), as well as the divine oath formula Ζῶ ἐγώ ("As I live", ROM 14:11). Also appears in the Old Testament citation Ὁ (δὲ) δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται ("the righteous will live by faith", ROM 1:17, GAL 3:11) and Οὐκ ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ("man shall not live by bread alone", MAT 4:4, LUK 4:4).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A negative coordinating and scalar adverbial particle that continues a negation across clauses or phrases ("and not, nor") or emphasizes the exclusion of an extreme or minimal case ("not even").

senses.definition: Connects a negated word, phrase, or clause to a preceding negation or negative context, or introduces a parallel negative statement or apodosis.
senses.grammatical_frame: Coordinating negative conjunction linking clauses, verbs, infinitives, nominals, or prepositional phrases; also introduces an independent negative clause or conditional apodosis

senses.definition: Marks a minimal, extreme, or unexpected item as excluded from a statement, condition, or rhetorical question.
senses.grammatical_frame: Scalar negative adverb modifying a noun phrase, verb, prepositional phrase, conditional clause, or interrogative clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently continues an earlier negation with ου (ouk) or ουδεις, and pairs contrastively with αλλα or δε (MAT 5:15; ROM 9:16; GAL 1:1; 1TI 2:12; HEB 9:12). Common collocations include ουδε γαρ (JHN 7:5; ACT 4:12), αλλ' ουδε (1CO 3:2; GAL 2:3), and elided ουδ' before a vowel (MAT 24:21, with strengthened negation ουδ' ου μη). Pleonastic negation occurs in MRK 5:3 (ουδε ... ουκετι ουδεις). Several instances lie near the boundary between simple continuation and scalar emphasis (e.g., MRK 16:13; JHN 11:50; REV 9:20).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Existence as a living being during earthly time, or unending, God-given spiritual and eschatological existence centered in Christ and contrasted with death and judgment.

senses.definition: Physical existence on earth or the temporal span of a person's mortal lifetime.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine, singular), frequently with a possessive pronoun or demonstrative in prepositional phrases (ἐν τῇ ζωῇ σου / ταύτῃ) or as subject of verbs of removal

senses.definition: Unending, blessed existence granted by God beyond death and condemnation, often characterized as eternal or indissoluble.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine, singular), frequently modified by αἰώνιος or ἀκατάλυτος, serving as object of ἔχω, δίδωμι, or κληρονομέω, or governed by prepositions such as εἰς and ἐκ

senses.definition: The divine vital reality and source of existence, embodied in and directly identified with Christ.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine, singular), used as predicate nominative, appositive, or subject of verbs of being and manifestation (εἰμί, φανερόω)

senses.definition: Manner of daily conduct or pattern of moral living.
senses.grammatical_frame: Genitive noun dependent on an abstract noun (ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς) with a verb of walking/conduct (περιπατέω)

senses.definition: Qualifying designation for symbolic objects (tree, book, springs, water) that signify, sustain, or pertain to unending divine existence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Genitive noun (with or without article) modifying concrete or figurative nouns (ξύλον, βιβλίον, πηγαί, ὕδωρ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently modified by αἰώνιος ("eternal", e.g., MAT 19:16, JHN 3:36, TIT 1:2) and directly contrasted with θάνατος ("death", JHN 5:24, ROM 7:10, 1JN 3:14), κόλασις ("punishment", MAT 25:46), κρίσις ("judgment", JHN 5:29), and τὸ θνητόν ("what is mortal", 2CO 5:4). Commonly serves as the direct object of ἔχω ("to have", MAT 19:16, JHN 3:36, 5:24, 6:47, 6:53, 20:31) and δίδωμι ("to give", 1JN 5:11, 5:16). In Johannine writings and Colossians, it is directly predicated of Christ (JHN 11:25, 14:6, COL 3:4). In Revelation, the genitive (τῆς) ζωῆς forms recurring symbolic phrases such as ξύλον (τῆς) ζωῆς ("tree of life", REV 2:7, 22:2), βιβλίον τῆς ζωῆς ("book of life", REV 17:8), and πηγὴ τοῦ ὕδατος τῆς ζωῆς ("spring of the water of life", REV 21:6).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To exercise physical sight, direct one's gaze toward or perceive a person or thing, mentally observe, or take heed against danger.

senses.definition: To possess or exercise the physical faculty of eyesight, as opposed to being blind or unable to see.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, absolute or in genitive absolute (βλεπόντων αὐτῶν); often negated or contrasted with blindness

senses.definition: To direct one's eyes toward or visually perceive a person, object, light, or visionary scene (and in the passive, to be visible).
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with accusative object (or with εἴς + accusative in ACT 3:4), or passive participle (βλεπόμενος)

senses.definition: To pay close attention to, recognize, or observe mentally/spiritually a situation, condition, or truth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with accusative noun, indirect question (τί), ὅτι-clause, or accusative + participle

senses.definition: To be on guard, beware of someone or something, or take care to ensure or avoid an outcome.
senses.grammatical_frame: Imperative or jussive with μή + subjunctive, ἀπό + genitive, reflexive accusative (ἑαυτούς), or ἵνα + subjunctive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with ἀκούω ('hear') in prophetic citations and contrasts between physical sensation and comprehension (MAT 13:14; MRK 8:18; ACT 28:26), and contrasted with blindness (τυφλός in MAT 12:22; JHN 9:39) or with κατανοέω ('notice/consider deeply' in LUK 6:41). The figurative pairing βλέποντες βλέψετε ('seeing you will see') in MAT 13:14 and ACT 28:26 contrasts outward eyesight with lack of inner perception. In imperative/jussive warnings, commonly governs μή + subjunctive (MAT 24:4; LUK 21:8; ACT 13:40; 1CO 10:12; GAL 5:15).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The cardinal number two, used attributively, substantively, or in distributive pairs.

senses.definition: Designating a count of two persons, items, or units of time modifying a plural noun.
senses.grammatical_frame: Cardinal numeral modifying a plural noun (indeclinable δύο in nom./gen./acc., or dative δυσί[ν])

senses.definition: Standing alone as a substantive or with a partitive genitive to refer to two persons, things, or alternatives.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival numeral standing alone, with the definite article (οἱ/τὰ/τῶν δύο), or governing a partitive genitive

senses.definition: Expressing a distributive grouping of two at a time, in pairs, or two units each.
senses.grammatical_frame: Reduplicated (δύο δύο) or preceded by prepositions ἀνά or κατά + accusative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Declined only in the dative plural (δυσί / δυσίν), while remaining indeclinable (δύο) for nominative, genitive, and accusative. Commonly paired with τρεῖς in 'δύο ἢ τρεῖς' ('two or three') to express a small number or the minimum threshold for valid legal testimony (MAT 18:16; MAT 18:20; JHN 2:6; 1CO 14:27; HEB 10:28).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Physically dead or deceased (of persons or bodies), and figuratively lifeless, unresponsive, or inoperative.

senses.definition: Having ceased to live physically; being in the state of bodily death or appearing lifeless.
senses.grammatical_frame: predicate adjective (with γίνομαι, ὡσεί)

senses.definition: A person who has died, a corpse, or collectively those who have died, frequently in contexts of burial, resurrection, or judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: substantival plural (with or without article), often governed by ἐκ or ἀπό or as objective/possessive genitive

senses.definition: Figuratively alienated from true life or spiritually unresponsive, contrasted with coming to life or awakening.
senses.grammatical_frame: substantival plural or predicate adjective (with εἰμί)

senses.definition: Of an abstract quality (faith), lacking vitality, effectiveness, or active expression.
senses.grammatical_frame: predicate adjective with εἰμί (modifying a feminine abstract noun)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears as a substantival plural in resurrection formulas: ἀνάστασις (τῶν) νεκρῶν (MAT 22:31; ACT 23:6; ACT 26:23; 1CO 15:21; HEB 6:2), ἀνάστασις ἐκ νεκρῶν (LUK 20:35; 1PE 1:3), and with ἐγείρω or ἀνίστημι + ἐκ (τῶν) νεκρῶν or ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν (MAT 27:64; MRK 6:14; LUK 9:7; JHN 12:9; JHN 21:14; ACT 4:10; ACT 17:31; ROM 6:9; ROM 7:4; ROM 8:11; EPH 1:20; COL 2:12; HEB 11:19). Often paired in direct contrast with ζῶντες ('the living') or ζάω ('to live') (MRK 12:27; LUK 15:32; LUK 24:5; ACT 10:42; REV 1:18). In MAT 8:22, the word shifts within a single sentence from a figurative use ('leave the [spiritually] dead') to a literal use ('to bury their own dead').

entries.core_meaning_summary: Preposition governing the dative case, indicating personal accompaniment, joint participation in an action or condition, or the inclusion of accompanying items.

senses.definition: In the physical company, presence, or retinue of someone, often with verbs of being, remaining, or traveling.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative of person (with verbs of being/motion or attributive article)

senses.definition: Jointly participating with others in an action, group, status, or shared destiny (such as worship, greetings, suffering, death, or resurrection).
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative of person or group (linking participants in an action or address)

senses.definition: Marking something included, added, or carried along with another item or person (such as interest on money, accompanying traits, or shared fate of possessions).
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + dative of thing or person (indicating addition or accompaniment)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Always governs the dative case in the sample. Frequently forms the substantival phrase οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ / ἐμοί ('those with him/me', i.e., companions or associates: ACT 5:21; ACT 22:9; GAL 1:2; PHP 4:21). Occasionally reinforces compound verbs prefixed with συν- (e.g., συνσταυρωθέντες σὺν αὐτῷ in MAT 27:44; MRK 15:32) or pairs with the adverb ἅμα (ἅμα σὺν αὐτοῖς in 1TH 4:17). Appears in the fixed commercial phrase σὺν τόκῳ ('with interest': MAT 25:27; LUK 19:23).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A person legally or socially bound to serve a master or owner, and by extension one devoted in service to God or Christ or figuratively mastered by a controlling power.

senses.definition: A person subject to the authority of an owner or household head, responsible for carrying out orders, managing property, or performing tasks, in contrast to a free person, son, or friend.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, often with a possessive genitive or pronoun (of a master, householder, or high priest), or in absolute contrast with 'free' or 'son'

senses.definition: A devoted follower, worshipper, or commissioned agent belonging to God or Jesus Christ and committed to their service.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun with genitive of God, Jesus Christ, or a pronoun referring to God

senses.definition: One who is figuratively bound, controlled by, or subservient to an abstract force (such as sin or corruption) or to the will of other human beings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate or appositional masculine noun with genitive of an abstract noun (sin, corruption) or of human beings

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with κύριος (lord/master, e.g., MAT 18:32, MAT 25:21, LUK 12:46, JHN 15:15), οἰκοδεσπότης (head of a household, MAT 13:27, LUK 14:21), and δεσπότης (owner/master, 1TI 6:1, TIT 2:9). Contrasted directly with ἐλεύθερος (free person: 1CO 7:21, EPH 6:8, COL 3:11, REV 13:16), υἱός (son: GAL 4:7), and φίλος (friend: JHN 15:15). Common modifiers include ἀγαθὸς καὶ πιστός (good and faithful, MAT 25:21; cf. LUK 19:17), πονηρός (wicked, MAT 18:32), κακός (evil, MAT 24:48), and ἀχρεῖος (unworthy/unprofitable, MAT 25:30, LUK 17:10). In 2PE 2:19, being a δοῦλος of corruption is explicitly equated with being mastered/enslaved (δεδούλωται) by whatever defeats a person. Note also the title format 'δοῦλος (II)' from the lemma header.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A solemn word of affirmation meaning 'truly' when introducing authoritative declarations, 'so be it' when ratifying doxologies and blessings, and used once as a title for Christ.

senses.definition: An emphatic introductory particle spoken by Jesus to certify the certainty, reliability, and importance of the statement that follows.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable clause-initial particle (single or doubled) preceding the verb 'I say to you' (λέγω ὑμῖν / σοι)

senses.definition: An exclamation or substantivized utterance expressing solemn agreement, endorsement, and ratification at the end (or framing) of a blessing, prayer, or ascription of praise to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable exclamation concluding a doxology or benediction (also opening one in REV 7:12), or substantivized with the neuter definite article 'τὸ Ἀμήν' (2CO 1:20)

senses.definition: A personal title applied to the risen Christ, characterizing him as completely reliable and true in parallel with 'the faithful and true witness.'
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable noun substantivized with the masculine singular definite article (ὁ Ἀμήν) as subject of 'says' (λέγει)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Indeclinable particle/interjection that never inflects for case, number, or gender, even when substantivized with the neuter article τὸ Ἀμήν (2CO 1:20) or masculine article ὁ Ἀμήν (REV 3:14). In the Synoptic Gospels it stands singly before λέγω ὑμῖν (with γάρ in MAT 5:18 and πάλιν in MAT 18:19); in the Gospel of John it consistently appears doubled (ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν/σοι). In 2CO 1:20 it is paired with τὸ Ναί ('the Yes') to express communal affirmation of God's promises. In REV 7:12 it both opens and closes a heavenly hymn of praise.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An extended period of time or cosmic epoch—whether past, present, or future—including the present world order and, in prepositional idioms, unlimited duration or eternity.

senses.definition: A distinct, bounded epoch or cosmic era of time (past, future, or successive periods in the plural), often viewed as having a beginning, a culmination, or a succession of ages.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural); frequently modified by demonstratives, participles indicating futurity (mellōn, eperchomenos), or governed by nouns denoting end or totality (synteleia, telos, pas).

senses.definition: The present temporal order or world system, characterized by its current rulers, anxieties, and values, in contrast with the coming age or life of light and godliness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular); typically modified by houtos ("this") or nyn ("now"), functioning as direct object, in prepositional phrases with en, or as possessive/descriptive genitive.

senses.definition: Unlimited duration, perpetuity, or the remote past; used in prepositional phrases (especially with eis, and reduplicated genitive constructions) to denote "forever" or "eternally", with apo to denote "from of old", and under strong negation (ou mē ... eis ton aiōna) to express "never".
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural); almost exclusively object of prepositions eis or apo, frequently in doxologies and statements of permanence.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears most frequently in prepositional phrases expressing unlimited duration: εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ("forever"), εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας ("forever / for the ages"), and the emphatic reduplicated genitive expressions εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦ αἰῶνος, and εἰς αἰῶνας αἰώνων ("forever and ever"). When combined with the strong negation οὐ μή ("certainly not"), εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα functions idiomatically to mean "never" (JHN 8:51; JHN 10:28; JHN 13:8). The present order is marked by demonstrative or temporal modifiers: οὗτος ὁ αἰών ("this age", MAT 12:32; LUK 16:8; 1CO 2:8) and ὁ νῦν αἰών ("the present age", 2TI 4:10; TIT 2:12), often contrasted with ὁ μέλλων / ἐκεῖνος ὁ αἰών ("the coming / that age", MAT 12:32; LUK 20:35) or οἱ ἐπερχόμενοι αἰῶνες ("the coming ages", EPH 2:7). Other notable phrases include συντέλεια τοῦ αἰῶνος ("consummation/end of the age", MAT 13:40; MAT 24:3), ἀπ' αἰῶνος ("from long ago / eternity past", ACT 15:18), and πρὸ παντὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος ("before all time", JUD 1:25).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The cessation of physical life or the act of dying, extending to judicial execution, mortal danger, spiritual ruin, and death personified as a hostile power.

senses.definition: The end of earthly biological life or the event of dying, including the specific manner of someone's death (such as Christ's crucifixion), figurative expressions of experiencing death, and prepositional phrases marking extremity to the point of dying.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; used as object of verbs of experiencing or proclaiming, in dative of manner or cause, and in prepositional phrases of limit or result (eis, heōs, mechri, pros, dia).

senses.definition: Execution or capital punishment imposed as a legal or commanded penalty.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; genitive modifying adjectives or nouns of guilt and legal cause (axios, aitia), or instrumental dative with a verb of dying (teleutaō).

senses.definition: Extreme peril of dying, deadly affliction, or a fatal plague/calamity (including the plural for repeated brushes with death, and poetic imagery of the shadow of death).
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural); in prepositional phrases (eis, en), genitive modifying skia ("shadow"), or coordinated with calamities such as mourning and famine.

senses.definition: Spiritual or eschatological ruin; a state of alienation from God's life or final condemnation (directly contrasted with life or peace, and identified in its final form as the "second death").
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; predicate nominative, object of prepositions indicating state or outcome (ek, en, eis, pros), or dative of goal/beneficiary; directly contrasted with zōē ("life").

senses.definition: Death portrayed as an active cosmic power, reigning force, enemy, or realm that exercises authority over humanity and is ultimately defeated or destroyed (sometimes paired with Hades).
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, usually articular; subject of active verbs (reigning, entering, fleeing) or passive verb of abolition (katargeō), or genitive of possession/authority (keys of, power of, sting of).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with ζωή ("life", e.g., JHN 5:24; ROM 5:17; ROM 8:6; 2CO 2:16; 1JN 3:14). Common verbal idioms for dying include γεύομαι θανάτου ("taste death", MRK 9:1; HEB 2:9) and ὁράω/εἶδον θάνατον ("see death", LUK 2:26; HEB 11:5). Legal collocations include ἄξιος θανάτου ("deserving death", LUK 23:15; ACT 25:11) and αἰτία θανάτου ("ground/charge for death", ACT 13:28; ACT 28:18). Prepositional phrases ἕως θανάτου (MAT 26:38; MRK 14:34) and μέχρι θανάτου (PHP 2:8) express utmost degree or limit, while πρός θάνατον denotes fatal trajectory or consequence (JHN 11:4; 1JN 5:16). Paired with Ἅιδης ("Hades") as cosmic powers or realms in REV 1:18 and REV 20:14, and further specified as ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερος ("the second death") in REV 20:14.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Inherent strength, capacity, or effective power; also an act demonstrating such power, a cosmic or ruling force, or a title for God.

senses.definition: Ability, strength, or effective force enabling action, endurance, rule, or transformation, whether attributed to God, spiritual agency, human capacity, or natural phenomena.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun (frequently with genitive possessor or prepositional ἐν/μετά/ὑπέρ)

senses.definition: A concrete deed or manifestation displaying extraordinary or divine power, often grouped with signs and wonders or listed among spiritual gifts.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun (often plural, object of ποιέω or subject of γίνομαι)

senses.definition: Celestial forces or spiritual and ruling authorities viewed collectively as entities subject to shaking or abolition.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun (plural in MAT 24:29; singular paired with ἀρχή and ἐξουσία in 1CO 15:24)

senses.definition: A reverent designation or title for God, or for a person regarded as embodying divine power.
senses.grammatical_frame: articular feminine noun functioning as a title or predicate nominative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with ἐξουσία ('authority', LUK 4:36, 1CO 15:24, REV 17:13) and δόξα ('glory', MRK 13:26, LUK 21:27, REV 5:12). In 1a, the term covers divine empowerment (e.g., δύναμις Θεοῦ), royal/governing might, human endurance (ὑπὲρ δύναμιν, 'beyond one's capacity', 2CO 1:8), and intense natural force (δύναμιν πυρός, 'power of fire', HEB 11:34; REV 1:16). In 1b, usually plural δυνάμεις with ποιέω ('do/perform') or γίνομαι ('take place'), and grouped with σημεῖα ('signs') and τέρατα ('wonders') in 2CO 12:12. In MAT 26:64, 'at the right hand of the Power' serves as a reverent designation for God.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To stay in a location or with someone, remain closely united with a person or teaching, endure over time, or wait for someone.

senses.definition: To remain in a physical place or lodge with someone temporarily or as a resident.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with locative adverb (ὧδε, ἐκεῖ, ποῦ) or prepositional phrase (ἐν / παρά / σύν + dative, μετά / ἐπί + genitive, κατά + accusative)

senses.definition: To remain steadfastly connected to a person, message, or spiritual reality, expressing mutual indwelling, allegiance, or perseverance in faith and love.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb + ἐν + dative (of person, word, love, faith, or truth)

senses.definition: To continue in the same condition or possession, persist unchanged, or endure permanently over time.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb used absolutely, with predicate adjective/dative, with εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, or as an attributive participle

senses.definition: To stay in place expecting someone's arrival; to await a person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb + accusative object (person) + locative phrase (ἐν + dative)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In Johannine writings, ἐν + dative frequently expresses reciprocal personal attachment or spiritual indwelling (e.g., ἐν ἐμοὶ ... κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ in JHN 6:56; JHN 15:4-5; 1JN 4:16). Contrasts with departing, passing away, or being removed (e.g., παράγεται in 1JN 2:17; καταργεῖται in 2CO 3:14; μέλλουσαν in HEB 13:14). Used once transitively in ACT 20:5 with a personal object in the sense of waiting for someone's arrival.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Interrogative, exclamatory, and indefinite adverb denoting the manner, means, or possibility of an action or state.

senses.definition: Introduces a direct question asking about the manner, means, or possibility of an event or statement, often functioning rhetorically to challenge an inconsistency or express astonishment.
senses.grammatical_frame: direct interrogative adverb introducing a main clause question

senses.definition: Introduces a dependent clause or indirect question specifying the manner, course of action, or condition of something, following verbs of knowing, perceiving, recounting, seeking, watching, or caring.
senses.grammatical_frame: subordinating adverb introducing an indirect question or complement clause

senses.definition: Marks an exclamation emphasizing the high degree or intensity of a quality or emotional state.
senses.grammatical_frame: exclamatory adverb modifying an adjective or verb

senses.definition: Used as an enclitic indefinite adverb after conditional or cautionary conjunctions to express an unspecified possibility or means.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic adverb (πως) following εἴ or μή

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs both as stressed interrogative πῶς and enclitic indefinite πως. Frequently introduces rhetorical questions expressing surprise, disbelief, or logical impossibility (e.g., JHN 4:9, JHN 6:42, ROM 10:14, 2CO 3:8, HEB 2:3). Often paired with δύναμαι ('how can...?'), λέγω ('how do you say...?'), or verbs of perception and care (βλέπω, καταμανθάνω, μεριμνάω). In ACT 15:36, πῶς ἔχουσιν is an idiomatic inquiry into someone's condition or well-being. Combined with conjunctions in εἴ πως ('if somehow', ROM 1:10) and μή πως ('lest somehow', 2CO 11:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To look for someone or something, strive after a goal or condition, attempt to carry out an action, or request something from another.

senses.definition: To look for or search carefully for a person, animal, or physical item in order to locate or reach them.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb + accusative object (person or thing), or absolute; often paired with εὑρίσκω

senses.definition: To strive after, pursue, or direct one's aims toward an immaterial goal, benefit, honor, opportunity, or relationship.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb + accusative of abstract noun/pronoun, or + ἵνα-clause

senses.definition: To try, attempt, or look for a way to accomplish an action, including plotting or worrying over how to obtain or achieve something.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + complementary infinitive, or verb + indirect question (πῶς / τί + subjunctive)

senses.definition: To ask for, demand, or expect something from someone as proof or as an obligation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb + accusative (often with παρά + genitive of source), or passive + ἵνα-clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired or contrasted with εὑρίσκω ("to find") in contexts of searching for lost objects, people, or desired states (MAT 12:43; LUK 11:9; LUK 13:6; LUK 15:8; JHN 7:34; ROM 10:20; 1CO 4:2). Common objects include δόξα ("honor/glory," JHN 7:18; JHN 8:50; 1TH 2:6) and σημεῖον ("sign," MRK 8:12; LUK 11:16). With ἀποκτεῖναι or clauses of killing, it expresses hostile intent or plotting (MAT 2:13; MRK 14:1; LUK 22:2; JHN 5:18; JHN 7:20; JHN 8:37). Appears in the passive voice in 1CO 4:2 to denote an expected standard.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Selfless, loyal devotion and active goodwill—expressed by God and Christ toward people, by believers toward God, and among people in mutual care and service.

senses.definition: Sincere, self-giving care, affection, and practical goodwill shown by people toward others—especially neighbors and fellow believers—characterized by patience, kindness, and absence of harm or self-seeking.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, as subject, direct object (with ἔχω, διώκω), or in prepositional phrases of manner/sphere (ἐν ἀγάπῃ, δι’ ἀγάπης, ἐξ ἀγάπης), often with εἰς + accusative for the recipients

senses.definition: The gracious, self-sacrificing affection and loyal care demonstrated by God, Christ, or the Spirit toward people, especially manifested in Christ giving his life and sustaining believers.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun with subjective genitive (τοῦ Θεοῦ, τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ Πνεύματος, μου, αὐτοῦ) or as predicate of Θεός

senses.definition: Loyal devotion and affection directed by humans toward God or Christ, expressed concretely through keeping his commands and serving his people.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun with objective genitive (τοῦ Θεοῦ) or prepositional phrase of direction (πρὸς τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν, εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in virtue lists with πίστις (faith), δικαιοσύνη (righteousness), ὑπομονή (endurance), εἰρήνη (peace), χρηστότης (kindness), and μακροθυμία (patience) (e.g., 2CO 6:6; 1TI 1:14; 1TI 6:11; 2TI 2:22). Often governs or occurs with prepositional phrases indicating direction toward recipients (εἰς + accusative in 2CO 2:4; COL 1:4; 1PE 4:8; πρὸς + accusative in PHM 1:5) or sphere/manner (ἐν ἀγάπῃ, μένειν ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ). Genitive phrases such as ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ Θεοῦ can be either subjective (God's love toward people, e.g., ROM 8:35 with τοῦ Χριστοῦ) or objective (human love/devotion toward God, e.g., 1JN 5:3), with some passages allowing overlap. In 1CO 13:4–8 and 1JN 4:16, the term is personified or predicated directly of God (Ὁ Θεὸς ἀγάπη ἐστίν).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Adjective denoting being unaccompanied or the sole member of a class, and adverbially (in the neuter accusative) restricting scope to one item or condition, especially in "not only ... but also" constructions.

senses.definition: Without companions, separated from others, or left by oneself in isolation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate or appositive adjective modifying a noun or pronoun

senses.definition: Being the single or exclusive referent within a category or action, to the exclusion of all others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective (often with article or εἰ μή)

senses.definition: Apart from the public crowd; in a private setting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional idiom κατὰ + feminine accusative plural (κατὰ μόνας)

senses.definition: Limiting an action, object, or statement to nothing more than what is specified; also introducing a single qualifying condition or proviso.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverbial neuter accusative singular (μόνον), modifying a phrase, verb, or clause (including with ἵνα or elliptical clauses)

senses.definition: Used in negated correlative constructions ("not only ... but also") to indicate that the scope extends beyond the first stated item to include an additional one.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverbial μόνον paired with οὐ / μή and a following ἀλλά (καί)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very commonly appears in the neuter accusative singular μόνον paired with negations and adversatives: οὐ μόνον ... ἀλλὰ καί (e.g., ACT 19:26; ROM 9:24; 2CO 8:21; PHP 1:29; 1TH 1:8; 1JN 2:2) or elliptical οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καί (ROM 5:11). Also occurs with εἰ μή ("except") to mark exclusivity (MAT 21:19; LUK 5:21; PHP 4:15) and in the fixed adverbial phrase κατὰ μόνας ("in private," MRK 4:10; LUK 9:18). In GAL 6:12 and 2TH 2:7, clause-initial μόνον introduces a limiting condition or elliptical qualification.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A gathered assembly or organized community, referring either to a local congregation of believers, an assembled meeting of believers, the universal body of Christ's followers, or a lawful civic assembly.

senses.definition: A distinct local or regional community of believers meeting in a specific city, region, or household, capable of acting collectively, sending delegates, receiving letters, and supporting ministry.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, singular or plural, often with articular location phrases (ἐν + dative, κατ’ οἶκον) or genitive of region/people

senses.definition: The gathered meeting or convened session of a community of believers for worship, teaching, mutual testimony, or addressing disputes.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, often anarthrous in prepositional phrases (ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἐνώπιον ἐκκλησίας, ἐν μέσῳ ἐκκλησίας), or as object of verbs of gathering or addressing

senses.definition: The entire collective body of believers belonging to God or Christ without limitation to a single locality, depicted as a household or as a body under Christ's headship.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine singular noun with the article (often with genitive τοῦ Θεοῦ or possessive pronoun, or in apposition to σῶμα / οἶκος Θεοῦ)

senses.definition: An officially recognized civic assembly of citizens convened under law to adjudicate public matters.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine singular noun modified by adjective ἔννομος in prepositional phrase (ἐν τῇ ἐννόμῳ ἐκκλησίᾳ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears with geographic qualifiers (ἐν + dative city/region or genitive region/people, e.g., τῆς Ἀσίας, Θεσσαλονικέων) or household qualifiers (τὴν κατ’ οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίαν in ROM 16:5, 1CO 16:19). Often modified by τοῦ Θεοῦ (ACT 20:28; 1CO 1:2; 1TI 3:15). In liturgical and gathering contexts, frequently occurs anarthrously after prepositions (ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ in 1CO 11:18; 1CO 14:28, 35; ἐν μέσῳ ἐκκλησίας in HEB 2:12; ἐνώπιον ἐκκλησίας in 3JN 1:6). Metaphorically equated with a body (σῶμα) having Christ as head (κεφαλή) in EPH 1:22, 5:23; COL 1:18, a household of God (οἶκος Θεοῦ) in 1TI 3:15, and golden lampstands (λυχνίαι) in REV 1:20. Paired with the adjective ἔννομος in ACT 19:39 to denote a legally constituted civic assembly.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To cease living physically, whether naturally, violently, or sacrificially, and by extension to undergo spiritual ruin, seed dissolution, or figurative separation from a controlling power.

senses.definition: To come to the end of physical life; used of humans and animals ceasing to live, being in the process of dying (imperfect), or of the act of dying itself (articular infinitive).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb (all finite tenses, infinitive, articular infinitive)

senses.definition: To lose one's life through violence, judicial execution, or voluntary self-sacrifice, especially on behalf of others or a cause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, often with ὑπέρ + genitive, dative of manner, or legal/locative modifiers

senses.definition: Of a sown seed, to break down in the soil as a necessary condition for new growth to emerge.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb (subject: sown seed)

senses.definition: To suffer ultimate spiritual ruin, perish in a state of sin, or (of remaining spiritual works) be on the point of complete collapse.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, often with ἐν + dative or μέλλω + infinitive

senses.definition: To enter a definitive break from the claim or sphere of a power (such as sin or law), or hyperbolically to face mortal danger continually.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with dative of reference (τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, νόμῳ) or temporal adverbial (καθ’ ἡμέραν)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in contrast with ζάω ("to live") or ζωοποιέω ("to make alive") (JHN 6:58; ROM 6:10; ROM 8:13; ROM 14:7, 9; 1CO 15:36; 2CO 5:15; PHP 1:21) and with ἀνίστημι / ἐγείρομαι ("to rise / be raised") in statements about Jesus (2CO 5:15; 1TH 4:14). Common collocations include ὑπέρ + genitive for dying on someone's behalf (JHN 11:50; ACT 21:13; ROM 5:7; 2CO 5:15), μέλλω + infinitive for impending death (JHN 12:33; ROM 8:13; REV 3:2), and the articular infinitive τὸ ἀποθανεῖν (ACT 7:4; PHP 1:21). In LUK 8:42 the imperfect ἀπέθνῃσκεν describes the process of dying ("was dying").

entries.core_meaning_summary: A relative and correlative pronoun/determiner denoting an inclusive quantity, number, degree, or duration matching a given condition or standard.

senses.definition: Every person or thing within an implied or stated set, specifying the full extent or total membership of that group.
senses.grammatical_frame: plural relative/correlative pronoun (masculine ὅσοι/ὅσους for persons, neuter ὅσα/ὅσων for things), often with πᾶς or ἄν/ἐάν + subjunctive

senses.definition: A matching measure, degree, or proportion between two actions, qualities, or situations.
senses.grammatical_frame: neuter accusative (ὅσον, ὅσα), dative of degree (ὅσῳ), or prepositional phrase (ἐφ’ ὅσον, καθ’ ὅσον), often paired with a comparative or τοσοῦτος

senses.definition: An extent or brief span of time during which a state holds or before an event occurs.
senses.grammatical_frame: prepositional phrase ἐφ’ ὅσον (with or without χρόνον), or reduplicated adverbial ὅσον ὅσον modifying μικρόν

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently reinforced by πᾶς (πάντα ὅσα, πάντες ὅσοι, e.g., MAT 7:12, MRK 6:30, ACT 5:37) and followed by the conditional particle ἄν/ἐάν with the subjunctive to generalize (e.g., MAT 7:12, LUK 9:5, ACT 2:39). In comparisons of degree or extent, it often correlates with τοσοῦτος / τοσοῦτον (HEB 1:4, REV 18:7) or μᾶλλον περισσότερον (MRK 7:36). In ROM 11:13, ἐφ’ ὅσον may indicate either extent ("inasmuch as") or duration ("as long as"). In HEB 10:37, the doubled form ὅσον ὅσον reinforces μικρόν to express a very brief span of time.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To address someone earnestly in order to entreat for help or action, urge toward conduct, or bring comfort and encouragement in distress.

senses.definition: To ask, beg, or earnestly appeal to someone for assistance, mercy, permission, presence, or a specific favor or action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive with accusative of person (plus ἵνα clause, infinitive, τοῦ + infinitive, περί + genitive, or direct speech); also passive with infinitive

senses.definition: To urge, exhort, or encourage individuals or a community toward faithful conduct, unity, perseverance, or mutual support.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive with accusative of person (often followed by ἵνα clause, infinitive, or ὑπέρ + genitive), or absolute in instructional/pastoral discourse

senses.definition: To comfort, console, or cheer someone experiencing grief, affliction, anguish, or inner need.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive (often absolute or with ἐπί + dative or cognate dative παράκλησις), or active transitive with accusative of person and ἐπί + dative of affliction

entries.collocations_and_notes: Shows a smooth continuum between earnest petition (1a), pastoral exhortation (1b), and consolation/encouragement (1c); contexts such as ACT 16:40, 1CO 14:31, 1TH 3:2, and COL 2:2 bridge exhortation and comfort. In 2CO 1:4 and 2CO 7:7 it appears alongside the cognate noun παράκλησις (also ROM 12:8). Frequently occurs with ἵνα + subjunctive (or negated μή) to express desired action, or with direct address (ἀδελφοί) and ἐν Κυρίῳ (1TH 4:1; 2TH 3:12) in epistolary appeals. Paired with verbs of asking/commanding (ἐρωτάω, παραγγέλλω) or corrective teaching (ἐλέγχω, ἐπιτιμάω, στηρίζω, οἰκοδομέω). Passive forms in ACT 28:14 reflect invitation/entreaty, whereas passive forms in MAT 2:18, LUK 16:25, 2CO 1:4, 2CO 7:7, and COL 2:2 express receiving comfort or encouragement.

entries.core_meaning_summary: That which corresponds to reality or fact, encompassing truthful speech, the authoritative message concerning God and Christ, and genuine sincerity or faithful conduct.

senses.definition: Accuracy or conformity to fact in speech or character, standing in direct opposition to lying, deception, or fabrication.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (chiefly anarthrous object of λέγω, or articular subject/object contrasted with ψεῦδος/ψεῦσμα)

senses.definition: The authoritative revelation or body of teaching concerning God, Jesus, and the gospel, serving as an object of knowledge, obedience, testimony, or rejection.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (chiefly articular; object of verbs of knowing, obeying, or rejecting, or genitive modifier with Πνεῦμα, λόγος, ἐπίγνωσις, or εὐαγγέλιον)

senses.definition: Genuineness, honesty, or actual fact as the manner or basis of an action, worship, teaching, or affection, without pretense or partiality.
senses.grammatical_frame: prepositional phrase (ἐν + dative, ἐπί + genitive) or bare dative functioning adverbially

senses.definition: Upright, faithful conduct that aligns in practice with what is right and declared.
senses.grammatical_frame: articular noun as object of ποιέω or in ἐν τῇ + dative with περιπατέω

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with falsehood or deceit (τὸ ψεῦδος, ψεύδομαι, ψεῦσμα, ψεύστης in JHN 8:44, ROM 3:7, EPH 4:25, 1TI 2:7, JAS 3:14, 1JN 2:21), pretense (πρόφασις in PHP 1:18), unrighteousness (ἀδικία in ROM 1:18, ROM 2:8), and myths (μῦθοι in 2TI 4:4, TIT 1:14). Common phrases include τὸ Πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας (JHN 14:17, JHN 16:13), ἐπίγνωσις ἀληθείας (1TI 2:4, 2TI 2:25), ἐν ἀληθείᾳ / ἐπ’ ἀληθείας (e.g., MAT 22:16, MRK 12:14, ACT 4:27, 2JN 1:1), and ποιεῖν τὴν ἀλήθειαν / περιπατεῖν ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ (1JN 1:6, 3JN 1:4). In ROM 3:7 and 2CO 11:10, it denotes God's or Christ's reliability/truthfulness as guaranteed by speech or character.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Denotes the complete, undivided extent or entirety of an object, person, group, region, faculty, or duration of time.

senses.definition: Designating an entire physical body, substance, or event as a complete whole without remainder.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective modifying a singular concrete noun, demonstrative pronoun, or implicit subject

senses.definition: Describing a person in full, without exception or partiality, with respect to a moral or ritual state.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate adjective agreeing with a personal subject or pronoun

senses.definition: Designating the full geographical extent of a territory, region, island, or the inhabited world.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective in predicate position modifying a geographical or cosmic noun, often after εἰς, ἐν, κατά + genitive, or ἐπί + genitive

senses.definition: Designating an entire collective group, household, city population, assembly, or body of authoritative writings as a unified whole.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective in predicate position modifying a singular collective noun (e.g., σπεῖρα, συνέδριον, λαός, οἶκος, οἰκία, ἐκκλησία, πόλις, νόμος)

senses.definition: Designating the full, undivided engagement of inner human faculties such as heart, understanding, and strength.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective in predicate position inside ἐξ + genitive phrases modifying abstract nouns of inner capacity

senses.definition: Designating the unbroken, complete span of a period of time.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective in predicate position or with an anarthrous temporal noun in the accusative of duration

entries.collocations_and_notes: Almost always appears in predicate position relative to the definite article (preceding article + noun, e.g., ὅλον τὸ σῶμα, or following noun, e.g., τὸν κόσμον ὅλον, ἡ οἰκία αὐτοῦ ὅλη), or with an anarthrous noun (διετίαν ὅλην). In the proverb μικρὰ ζύμη ὅλον τὸ φύραμα ζυμοῖ (1CO 5:6; GAL 5:9) it contrasts with μικρά ('small'). Frequently paired with prepositions of spatial extent or sphere: ἐν (MAT 26:13; LUK 1:65; LUK 7:17; 1TH 4:10; HEB 3:2), εἰς (MAT 4:24; MAT 9:26), κατά + genitive (ACT 9:42; ACT 10:37), and ἐπί + genitive (REV 3:10). Metonymy of place for inhabitants appears in MRK 1:33 and ACT 19:27.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The animating life of a living being, the inner self as the seat of emotion, thought, and moral-spiritual existence, or by extension an individual human person.

senses.definition: Physical, animating existence of a living person, sustained by nourishment and capable of being threatened, protected, risked, sacrificed, or lost in death (sometimes placed in paradoxical contrast with enduring life).
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, often with possessive genitive as object of ζητεῖν, σῴζειν, ἀπολλύναι, τιθέναι, or subject of εἶναι; also in prepositional oath/risk phrases (ὑπέρ, ἐπί)

senses.definition: The inner self of a person (or, anthropomorphically, of God) as the seat of deep emotion, distress, desire, resolve, devotion, and moral or spiritual well-being, distinct from the physical body.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, as subject of emotion/state verbs (e.g., περίλυπός ἐστιν, τετάρακται, εὐοδοῦται), object of psychological/spiritual actions (σῴζειν, ἁγνίζειν, ταράσσειν), or in adverbial phrase ἐκ ψυχῆς

senses.definition: An individual human being or person, counted as a unit in a population, addressed as a moral agent, or listed among commodities.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, quantified with πᾶσα or numerals, or plural with genitive ἀνθρώπων

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired or contrasted with σῶμα (body; MAT 6:25; LUK 12:22; 1TH 5:23), πνεῦμα (spirit; 1TH 5:23), and καρδία / διάνοια / ἰσχύς (heart, mind, strength; LUK 10:27). Common idiomatic collocations include ζητεῖν τὴν ψυχήν ('seek someone's life' to kill; MAT 2:20), τιθέναι τὴν ψυχήν ὑπέρ ('lay down one's life for'; JHN 10:11; JHN 13:38; 1JN 3:16), σῴζειν / ἀπολλύναι τὴν ψυχήν (paradoxical contrast between preserving earthly life and gaining true/lasting life; MAT 10:39; MAT 16:25; MRK 8:35; LUK 17:33), ἐκ ψυχῆς ('from the inner self / wholeheartedly'; EPH 6:6; COL 3:23), and πᾶσα ψυχή ('every person'; ACT 3:23; ROM 2:9). In REV 18:13, ψυχὰς ἀνθρώπων stands at the climax of a list of trade cargo alongside σωμάτων, denoting trafficked human beings.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Having positive moral, functional, or beneficial quality: upright, kind, sound, helpful, or advantageous.

senses.definition: Describing human beings or God as morally upright, virtuous, benevolent, or fair and kind in character and treatment of others.
senses.grammatical_frame: adjective modifying personal nouns (ἄνθρωπος, διδάσκαλος, δεσπότης), predicate adjective with εἶναι/λέγειν, or masculine plural/singular substantive (οἱ ἀγαθοί, ὁ ἀγαθός)

senses.definition: Describing non-personal things, actions, speech, or inner dispositions as healthy, sound, morally right, constructive, or fitting for their purpose.
senses.grammatical_frame: attributive or predicative adjective modifying inanimate/abstract nouns (δένδρον, θησαυρός, μερίς, συνείδησις, ἐντολή, θέλημα, ἔργον, λόγος, ἀναστροφή)

senses.definition: That which is morally right, helpful, beneficial, or advantageous in action, speech, or outcome.
senses.grammatical_frame: substantivized neuter singular (with or without article, e.g., τὸ ἀγαθόν, εἰς ἀγαθόν, ἐν παντὶ ἀγαθῷ) or neuter plural ἀγαθά as object of speech/action verbs

senses.definition: Stored material wealth and produce, or promised spiritual benefits and blessings realized through Christ.
senses.grammatical_frame: substantivized neuter plural τὰ ἀγαθά (with possessive pronoun or modifying participle)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly paired in direct contrast with πονηρός (MAT 5:45; MAT 12:35; MAT 22:10; LUK 6:45), κακός (MRK 3:4; ROM 12:21; ROM 13:4; 1TH 5:15; 1PE 3:11), σαπρός (MAT 7:17; EPH 4:29), and σκολιός (1PE 2:18). Frequent collocations include ἔργον ἀγαθόν / ἔργα ἀγαθά (2CO 9:8; PHP 1:6; 2TH 2:17; 1TI 2:10; 2TI 2:21; TIT 3:1), συνείδησις ἀγαθή (ACT 23:1; 1PE 3:16), ἀγαθὸς θησαυρός (MAT 12:35; LUK 6:45), and τὸ ἀγαθόν with verbs of doing, working, or pursuing (ἐργάζεσθαι, ποιεῖν, διώκειν) or with εἰς indicating beneficial purpose/outcome (ROM 8:28; ROM 13:4; ROM 15:2). In MAT 19:17, MRK 10:18, and LUK 18:19, absolute goodness is predicated uniquely of God.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A temporal conjunction introducing a subordinate clause that locates an event or state at a particular point or period in time.

senses.definition: Introduces a clause marking a specific event or narrative point in time at which or immediately after which the main action occurs.
senses.grammatical_frame: temporal conjunction + aorist (or historical present) indicative verb

senses.definition: Introduces a clause describing a past duration, ongoing circumstance, or stage of life during which a state or habitual action took place.
senses.grammatical_frame: temporal conjunction + imperfect (or perfect) indicative verb

senses.definition: Follows a time noun such as 'hour' or 'night' to specify an expected or dawning period when an action will or can happen.
senses.grammatical_frame: temporal noun (ὥρα, νύξ) + temporal conjunction + future or present indicative verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently introduces narrative transitions in Matthew (καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς...), Mark, Luke, Acts, and Revelation (καὶ ὅτε ἤνοιξεν... / καὶ ὅτε εἶδον...), as well as temporal clauses after ἔρχεται ὥρα or ἔρχεται νύξ in John. Often paired with δέ or οὖν in second position (ὅτε δέ, ὅτε οὖν) to advance a sequence of events, and contrasted with ὅταν in JHN 21:18 (past ὅτε + imperfect vs. future ὅταν + subjunctive).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A plural reciprocal pronoun expressing mutual action, relationship, or exchange among members of a group.

senses.definition: Marks the recipients or participants in a mutual action, attitude, or obligation performed back and forth among members of a group.
senses.grammatical_frame: reciprocal pronoun, accusative or dative as verbal object

senses.definition: Indicates mutual possession or association with a noun shared among members of a group.
senses.grammatical_frame: reciprocal pronoun, possessive genitive modifying a noun

senses.definition: Serves as the object of a preposition to mark mutual conversation, separation, shared mindset or affection, mutual agency, or intercession within a group.
senses.grammatical_frame: reciprocal pronoun as object of a preposition (πρός, μετά, εἰς, ἐν, ἀπό, ὑπό, ὑπέρ, μεταξύ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs after the preposition πρὸς with verbs of speaking, questioning, or disputing (e.g., λέγοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους, διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἀλλήλους, συνελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους, ἐμάχοντο πρὸς ἀλλήλους). Often serves as direct object of ἀγαπάω ("love one another") and ἀσπάζομαι ("greet one another", paired with ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ or ἐν φιλήματι ἀγάπης), and follows εἰς to express communal disposition or love (εἰς ἀλλήλους). In GAL 5:15 it shifts from direct object to passive agent (ὑπ’ ἀλλήλων), and in JAS 5:16 from dative indirect object (ἀλλήλοις) to prepositional object (ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A biological offspring of human parents, or by extension a descendant, inhabitant, spiritual protégé, or person characterized by a relationship or quality.
