senses.definition: A son or daughter born to human parents, without restriction to young age; human offspring within a household or family.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun (singular or plural, often with possessive pronoun or paired with πατήρ, γονεῖς, or γυνή)

senses.definition: A form of affectionate or paternal direct address used by a father to his son or by an authoritative speaker toward a person being helped or reassured.
senses.grammatical_frame: Vocative singular (Τέκνον)

senses.definition: Descendants or rightful heirs of a patriarch or ancestress, or inhabitants and followers belonging corporately to a city or symbolic figure.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural neuter noun with genitive or dative of ancestor, city, or symbolic mother (or possessive pronoun)

senses.definition: One who stands in a relationship of spiritual kinship to God or of close discipleship and devotion to a spiritual mentor or apostle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun with genitive of God or personal possessive, dative with γνήσιος, or in comparative phrases with ὡς

senses.definition: People characterized by, belonging to, or destined for an indicated condition or outcome (specifically, a curse).
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural neuter noun governing an abstract genitive (κατάρας τέκνα)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with πατήρ (MAT 10:21; MRK 13:12; LUK 1:17; PHP 2:22), γονεῖς (MAT 10:21; MRK 13:12; LUK 18:29; 2CO 12:14; EPH 6:1), γυνή (MAT 18:25; LUK 18:29; ACT 21:5), and ἀδελφοί (MRK 10:30; LUK 18:29). In MRK 7:27, literal household children are contrasted with little dogs (κυνάρια) within a saying. In spiritual and figurative contexts, it commonly takes a genitive of source, relationship, or character (τέκνα Θεοῦ, τέκνα τοῦ Ἀβραάμ, κατάρας τέκνα) or appears with γνήσιος (1TI 1:2; TIT 1:4) and ἀγαπητός (1CO 4:14; EPH 5:1).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A member of, or collectively the members of, a prominent Jewish religious and legal party active in Judea, Galilee, and the Jerusalem council.

senses.definition: An individual adherent or member of the Jewish religious-legal group known as the Pharisees.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular masculine noun (often anarthrous, articular after prior mention, or partitive with τῶν Φαρισαίων)

senses.definition: Collectively, the Jewish religious-legal party or faction distinguished by strict observance of ancestral traditions, tithing, fasting, and resurrection belief, often acting alongside scribes or chief priests or in contrast with Sadducees.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural masculine noun (typically articular οἱ Φαρισαῖοι, or genitive τῶν Φαρισαίων modifying nouns such as ζύμη, διδαχή, μαθηταί, γραμματεῖς, ἄρχοντες, μέρος)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with other Jewish groups or officials: γραμματεῖς (MAT 15:1, 23:13, 23:25, 23:27; MRK 7:5; LUK 5:30, 6:7; JHN 8:3), Σαδδουκαῖοι (MAT 3:7, 16:6, 16:12; ACT 23:6, 23:7), ἀρχιερεῖς (MAT 21:45; JHN 7:45, 11:47), νομοδιδάσκαλοι (LUK 5:17; ACT 5:34), and Ἡρῳδιανοί (MRK 3:6). Observed in collocations such as οἱ γραμματεῖς τῶν Φαρισαίων (MRK 2:16), οἱ μαθηταὶ τῶν Φαρισαίων (MRK 2:18), τῶν ἀρχόντων τῶν Φαρισαίων (LUK 14:1), τὸ μέρος τῶν Φαρισαίων (ACT 23:6, 23:9), and ἡ ζύμη τῶν Φαρισαίων (MAT 16:6; MRK 8:15; LUK 12:1, interpreted as teaching in MAT 16:12 and hypocrisy in LUK 12:1). Characterized in the texts by adherence to ancestral tradition, fasting, tithing, pre-meal washing, Sabbath scrutiny, participation in the council (συνέδριον), and affirmation of resurrection hope (ACT 23:6).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Designating another member of a pair, an additional or distinct person or thing, or something qualitatively different.

senses.definition: Identifying the second or remaining member of a pair in contrast with the first.
senses.grammatical_frame: Pronoun or adjective in correlative pairs (e.g., ὁ εἷς ... ὁ ἕτερος, τὸ ἓν ... τὸ ἕτερον, ἑτέρα μὲν ... ἑτέρα δέ)

senses.definition: Referring to an additional or distinct person or thing apart from the subject or items already in view, including one's neighbor or fellow.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized pronoun (singular or plural, with or without the article; occasionally with τις or πολλοί, or contrasted with ἑαυτοῦ)

senses.definition: Marking an additional, separate, or remaining item within a named category.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective modifying a noun, sometimes accompanied by τις or a numeral

senses.definition: Denoting the day immediately following in a narrative sequence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized feminine dative singular (τῇ ἑτέρᾳ) used temporally without an expressed noun

senses.definition: Indicating an altered appearance or a distinct kind or character rather than simple numerical addition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective describing form, appearance, or message/spirit

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with εἷς in binary contrasts (ὁ εἷς ... ὁ ἕτερος, τὸν ἕνα ... τὸν ἕτερον, τὸ ἓν ... τὸ ἕτερον) or paired with itself (ἑτέρα μὲν ... ἑτέρα δέ in 1CO 15:40). Often contrasted with the reflexive pronoun ἑαυτοῦ to mark another person outside oneself (ACT 8:34, ROM 2:21, 1CO 10:29, GAL 6:4, PHP 2:4). Appears alongside ἄλλος without a rigid semantic boundary in 2CO 11:4 (ἄλλον Ἰησοῦν ... πνεῦμα ἕτερον ... εὐαγγέλιον ἕτερον) and 1CO 10:29 (τοῦ ἑτέρου ... ὑπὸ ἄλλης συνειδήσεως). In ACT 27:3, the feminine dative singular τῇ ἑτέρᾳ functions idiomatically without an explicit noun for 'the next day'.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To utter, state, or declare words in speech or writing, including prophetic or scriptural pronouncements and rhetorical responses.

senses.definition: To communicate a message, instruction, prediction, or statement in speech or authoritative utterance, typically introducing direct discourse or an indirect statement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active indicative, participle, or infinitive; commonly with dative of addressee or πρός + accusative, followed by direct speech or ὅτι clause; occasionally with περί + genitive (topic)

senses.definition: To formulate a conclusion, reply, or anticipated objection in the course of an argument or dialogue.
senses.grammatical_frame: Future active indicative, often with interrogative τί (οὖν) or indefinite τις, introducing a question or imagined interlocutor's claim

senses.definition: To be spoken, proclaimed, or commanded (frequently of prophetic or scriptural statements and divine directives), or, with a personal subject, to be spoken of.
senses.grammatical_frame: Aorist or perfect passive indicative or participle; often with ὑπό + genitive (ultimate agent), διά + genitive (intermediary), ἐν + dative (written source), or dative of recipient followed by direct speech or ἵνα clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: In this evidence packet, the highlighted tokens under this lemma consist of future active (ἐρῶ, ἐρεῖς, ἐρεῖ, ἐροῦμεν, ἐρεῖτε, ἐροῦσιν), perfect active (εἴρηκα, εἰρηκότος, εἰρήκει, εἰρηκέναι), perfect passive (εἴρηται, εἰρημένον), and aorist passive (ἐρρέθη, ῥηθέν, ῥηθείς) forms, alongside unhighlighted aorist active forms (e.g., εἶπεν, εἴπῃ, εἴπωμεν) in several of the same verses. Frequent patterns include scriptural citation formulas (τὸ ῥηθὲν [ὑπὸ Κυρίου] διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος; τὸ εἰρημένον διὰ/ἐν...), pleonastic ἐρεῖ λέγων (LUK 13:27) and ἀποκριθεὶς ... ἐρεῖ (MAT 25:40), deliberative/rhetorical questions (τί [οὖν] ἐροῦμεν; in Romans), and passive commands with ἵνα (ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα... in REV 6:11, REV 9:4).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To walk on foot or move about in physical space, and figuratively to conduct one's life or behave according to a moral, religious, or spiritual standard.

senses.definition: To move on foot, exercise the physical capacity to walk, stroll about, or travel around within a region.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb; occurs absolutely (including imperatives of healing), with locative or spatial prepositional phrases (παρά + acc, ἐπί + gen, ἐν + dat, ἐν μέσῳ + gen), or with modal phrases (ἐν στολαῖς).

senses.definition: To order one's way of life, conduct oneself, or live consistently with a given standard, sphere, custom, or spiritual principle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb; characteristically modified by κατά + acc (standard), ἐν + dat (sphere or manner), instrumental dative (e.g., Πνεύματι, τοῖς ἔθεσιν), comparative ὡς/καθώς clauses, or adverbs of manner (ἀξίως, οὕτως, ἀτάκτως).
senses.semantic_domain: Behavior / Moral Conduct / Way of Life

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used heavily across two distinct domains: physical locomotion in the Gospels, Acts, and Revelation, and moral/spiritual conduct in the Epistles and Johannine writings. Common collocations for physical motion include ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης ('on the sea', MAT 14:26; MRK 6:48; JHN 6:19), ἐν στολαῖς ('in long robes', MRK 12:38; LUK 20:46), and pairing with Ἔγειρε ('get up', MRK 2:9; LUK 5:23). Common collocations for conduct include κατά + accusative (e.g., κατὰ σάρκα, κατὰ πνεῦμα, κατὰ ἀγάπην, κατὰ τὰς ἐντολάς), ἐν + dative (e.g., ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ / ἐν τῷ σκότει, ἐν ἀληθείᾳ, ἐν σοφίᾳ), instrumental dative (τοῖς ἔθεσιν, Πνεύματι), and adverbs of manner (ἀξίως, οὕτως, ἀτάκτως). JHN 8:12 and 12:35 bridge physical imagery of walking in darkness versus light with spiritual direction.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A physical building or dwelling used as a home, and by extension the household or family members associated with it or a metaphorical dwelling.

senses.definition: A constructed dwelling or residential building in which people live, lodge, or gather, including a house viewed as real property or an estate containing household goods.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; frequently governed by prepositions of location or motion (εἰς, ἐν, ἐκ, ἔξω, ἐπί), modified by a possessive genitive of the owner or host, or serving as object of verbs of building, entering, leaving, or owning.

senses.definition: The inhabitants or social unit belonging to a residence, such as a family, household, or royal staff, and by extension their domestic resources or livelihood.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; subject of verbs of believing (JHN 4:53), object of verbs of greeting or exploiting (MAT 10:12, LUK 20:47), or governed by ἐν or ἐκ with a genitive identifying the family member or ruler.

senses.definition: A metaphorical dwelling or state of embodiment, applied both to mortal earthly existence and to an enduring heavenly existence prepared by God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; modified by descriptive adjectives (ἐπίγειος, ἀχειροποίητος, αἰώνιος) and an explanatory genitive (τοῦ σκήνους), paired with οἰκοδομή.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of entering (εἰσέρχομαι, ἔρχομαι εἰς) and building (οἰκοδομέω), and with a possessive genitive identifying the owner or host (e.g., Σίμωνος, τοῦ Φαρισαίου, Ἰάσονος). Compounded concepts appear in context via οἰκοδεσπότης ('master of the house', MAT 24:43; LUK 22:11) and parallel usage with οἶκος in LUK 10:5 ('into whatever οἰκία you enter, first say: Peace to this οἶκος'). In lists of renounced or owned assets it pairs with ἀγροί ('fields', MAT 19:29; MRK 10:30) and χωρία ('lands', ACT 4:34). In 2CO 5:1 it appears in contrast and apposition with σκῆνος ('tent') and οἰκοδομή ('building') as a metaphor for mortal vs. heavenly embodiment.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adverb indicating temporal continuation or persistence, remaining addition, cessation when negated, or intensification of degree and discourse connection.

senses.definition: Marks an action or state as ongoing or already in progress at a reference point in time.
senses.grammatical_frame: Temporal adverb; modifies a finite verb, a nominative participle, or a genitive absolute construction

senses.definition: Indicates a remaining span of time, an additional occurrence, or further action beyond what has already taken place, including in rhetorical questions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Temporal/additive adverb; modifies nouns of duration (χρόνος, μικρόν), numerals/quantifiers (εἷς, δύο, ἅπαξ), or verbs in questions (τί ἔτι, πῶς ἔτι)

senses.definition: In negated clauses, denotes the end of a state or the absence of any further occurrence (or, with νῦν, continuing inability up to the present).
senses.grammatical_frame: Temporal adverb in clauses negated by οὐ, οὐ μή, οὐδέ, or οὐδέν

senses.definition: Adds a further, often climactic item to a list or statement, or intensifies a comparative adverb or adjective.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb of degree or discourse addition; precedes comparative expressions (μᾶλλον, περισσότερον) or forms the connective phrase ἔτι τε καί

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very frequently introduces a genitive absolute participle (ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος / προσερχομένου / ἀπέχοντος / οὔσης, MAT 17:5; MRK 5:35; LUK 9:42; LUK 15:20; LUK 22:47; JHN 20:1; ACT 10:44; ROM 5:6; HEB 9:8) or modifies a nominative participle (ἔτι ὤν, LUK 24:6, 44). In ROM 5:6 it appears twice in the same clause (ἔτι ... ὄντων ἡμῶν ἀσθενῶν ἔτι). Commonly paired with temporal expressions of small duration (ἔτι μικρόν / χρόνον μικρόν, JHN 7:33; 12:35; 14:19; HEB 10:37), with negatives (οὐ / οὐ μή / οὐδέν ... ἔτι, especially throughout Revelation), and in the fixed connective phrase ἔτι τε καί (LUK 14:26; ACT 21:28).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A state of freedom from conflict or disturbance, harmonious relationship, inner tranquility, and overall well-being or blessing.

senses.definition: Freedom from war, hostility, persecution, or external threat; public calm, diplomatic settlement, or undisturbed safety.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; direct object of verbs such as ἔχω or αἰτέω, object of prepositions (ἐν, πρός), or paired with ἀσφάλεια

senses.definition: Concord, unity, and amicable relation between persons or groups, or a reconciled standing between humans and God, contrasted with division or disorder.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; object of ποιέω or ζητέω, with πρός + accusative (toward God), or in prepositional phrases (μετά, ἐν)

senses.definition: Inner calm, steadiness of heart and mind, and freedom from fear or distress, especially as an attribute or gift from God or Christ.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; subject of active verbs (φρουρέω, βραβεύω), object of δίδωμι/ἀφίημι, or genitive modifier of Θεός/Κύριος

senses.definition: General wholeness, favorable condition, and divine blessing invoked in greetings, farewells, and epistolary salutations.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; verbless greeting/benediction with dative recipient or ἐπί + accusative, or with εἰς/ἐν after verbs of departure (ὑπάγω, πορεύομαι)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the standard New Testament epistolary salutation χάρις (καὶ ἔλεος) ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς... (1CO 1:3; 2CO 1:2; GAL 1:3; 2TH 1:2; 2TI 1:2; PHM 1:3; 2PE 1:2; 2JN 1:3; JUD 1:2). Common verbal and prepositional collocations include ποιεῖν εἰρήνην ('make peace', EPH 2:15; JAS 3:18), ἐν εἰρήνῃ ('in peace/security', LUK 11:21; ACT 16:36; JAS 3:18), εἰς εἰρήνην ('into peace', MRK 5:34; LUK 7:50), τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην ('the things pertaining to peace', LUK 14:32; LUK 19:42), and μετ' εἰρήνης ('peaceably', HEB 11:31). God or Christ is repeatedly designated as its source or possessor via the genitive (ὁ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης, HEB 13:20; ὁ Κύριος τῆς εἰρήνης, 2TH 3:16; ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ Θεοῦ, PHP 4:7; ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ Χριστοῦ, COL 3:15). Directly contrasted with ἀκαταστασία ('disorder') in 1CO 14:33 and paired with ἀσφάλεια ('safety') in 1TH 5:3, χαρά ('joy') in ROM 14:17; 15:13, and ἔλεος ('mercy') in GAL 6:16; 2TI 1:2; 2JN 1:3; JUD 1:2.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Moral uprightness and right conduct in accordance with God's standard, as well as the status of being accepted as right before God and God's own fairness or justice.

senses.definition: Conduct, character, or governance that conforms to moral integrity, fairness, and what God requires, often contrasted with deceit, lawlessness, or wrongdoing and encompassing generous care for the needy (2CO 9:9).
senses.grammatical_frame: Abstract feminine noun, frequently object of ποιέω, ἐργάζομαι, or διώκω, or genitive modifier (ὁδός, καρπός, διάκονοι)

senses.definition: The status of being accepted as right or vindicated before God, contrasted with sin and condemnation, and described as credited through faith or as a gift rather than achieved through law-observance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Abstract feminine noun, frequently with εἰς + accusative (λογίζομαι εἰς, πιστεύεται εἰς), ἐκ + genitive (ἐκ πίστεως, ἐκ νόμου), or as predicate nominative

senses.definition: Fairness, moral integrity, and saving faithfulness as an attribute and action of God or Jesus Christ, contrasted with unfairness or human wrongdoing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Abstract feminine noun followed by possessive genitive (Θεοῦ, τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in constructions with verbs of doing or practicing (ποιέω in MAT 6:1; 1JN 2:29; 1JN 3:10; ἐργάζομαι in HEB 11:33; JAS 1:20), pursuing or attaining (διώκω in ROM 9:30; 1TI 6:11; καταλαμβάνω in ROM 9:30), and crediting (λογίζομαι in ROM 4:3, 4:6, 4:11; GAL 3:6). Metaphorical and spatial collocations include ὁδὸς δικαιοσύνης ('way of uprightness', MAT 21:32; 2PE 2:21), θώραξ τῆς δικαιοσύνης (EPH 6:14), and καρπὸς δικαιοσύνης (JAS 3:18). The phrase δικαιοσύνη Θεοῦ (ROM 3:5, 3:22; ROM 10:3; 2CO 5:21; JAS 1:20; 2PE 1:1) spans both God's own fairness or moral standard and the right standing granted by God.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A negative pronoun and determiner meaning 'no one', 'nothing', or 'no', used predominantly in commands, wishes, purpose/result clauses, infinitival constructions, and participial phrases to exclude every person, thing, or degree.

senses.definition: Pronoun referring to any human being or personal agent, excluding every person in non-indicative statements, prohibitions, wishes, or subordinate clauses.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival pronoun (masculine singular), as subject, direct object, indirect object, or subject of infinitive

senses.definition: Neuter pronoun denoting the absence of any object, matter, action, or extent; in prepositional phrases with ἐν it expresses 'in no respect', and in verbless dative clauses (MAT 27:19) it expresses complete dissociation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival pronoun (neuter singular), as subject, object, prepositional object (ἐν μηδενί), or adverbial accusative

senses.definition: Negative determiner agreeing with a noun in gender, number, and case to exclude every instance of the item or quality named.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjectival determiner modifying an explicit noun (masculine, feminine, or neuter singular)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Consistently appears in non-indicative or subordinate environments (imperatives, subjunctives, optatives, infinitives, participles, and purpose/result clauses introduced by ἵνα or ὥστε). Frequently paired with partitive genitives (μηδενὶ ἀνθρώπων in ACT 4:17; μηδένα ... τῶν ἰδίων αὐτοῦ in ACT 24:23) or contrasted with exception clauses introduced by εἰ μή or πλήν (MRK 6:8; ACT 11:19; ACT 15:28; ROM 13:8). Double negation with another form of μηδείς reinforces exclusivity (μηδενὶ μηδὲν in MRK 1:44; ROM 13:8; μηδεμίαν ἐν μηδενὶ in 2CO 6:3). Note also the verbless dative idiom μηδὲν σοὶ καὶ τῷ δικαίῳ ἐκείνῳ in MAT 27:19, and ambiguous cases where neuter accusative μηδέν with participles (LUK 6:35; 1CO 10:27) can be read either as direct object ('nothing') or adverbially ('not at all').

entries.core_meaning_summary: To fill a space, container, or person to capacity, or to bring a period of time, spoken prophecy, law, or appointed task to full realization and completion.

senses.definition: To fill a container, physical location, or quantitative measure completely, including figuratively filling a city with teaching.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive (+ accusative of place or measure; + optional genitive of contents) or passive (intransitive)

senses.definition: To cause a person, heart, or inner experience (such as joy, sorrow, wisdom, knowledge, comfort, or moral quality) to become abundant, whole, or fully supplied.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive (+ accusative of heart) or passive (+ dative, genitive, accusative of content, ἐν, εἰς, or absolute)

senses.definition: To reach the end or full span of a designated number of years.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive participle (genitive absolute with noun of time)

senses.definition: To bring to pass or realize in events what was previously spoken by prophets, written in Scripture, or declared beforehand.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive (subject: τὸ ῥηθέν, ἡ γραφή, ὁ λόγος) or active transitive (+ accusative of prophetic speech)

senses.definition: To carry out, finish, or satisfy a moral requirement, law, mission, or appointed course of action to its intended end.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive (+ accusative of task, law, or purpose) or passive (subject: law or ritual meal)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in the passive voice with τὸ ῥηθέν, ἡ γραφή, or ὁ λόγος to mark the historical realization of prophetic or scriptural utterances (MAT 1:22; MRK 14:49; JHN 12:38; JAS 2:23). In passive descriptions of inner states or spiritual supply, the content or agent of filling is expressed by the dative (LUK 2:40; ROM 1:29; 2CO 7:4), genitive (ROM 15:14; ACT 5:28), accusative of respect (COL 1:9), ἐν (EPH 5:18; COL 2:10), or εἰς (EPH 3:19). Paired with verbs of increasing/strengthening (ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐκραταιοῦτο, LUK 2:40) and contrasted with καταλῦσαι in MAT 5:17. ACT 7:30 uses the genitive absolute πληρωθέντων ἐτῶν τεσσεράκοντα for elapsed time.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To speak to or petition God in devotion, worship, or intercession on behalf of oneself or others.

senses.definition: To address God in personal devotion, communal worship, thanksgiving, or spoken prayer, whether silently, aloud, or in the Spirit/a tongue.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive, + dative of deity, + instrumental dative (γλώσσῃ), or introducing direct speech

senses.definition: To ask or appeal to God for a specific outcome, deliverance, or requested object.
senses.grammatical_frame: With ἵνα clause, infinitive, τοῦ + infinitive, or neuter plural accusative of thing requested

senses.definition: To intercede with God on behalf of or over other people for their blessing, healing, protection, or ministry, sometimes accompanied by laying on of hands or anointing.
senses.grammatical_frame: With ὑπέρ + genitive, περί + genitive, ἐπί + accusative (or with purpose clause ἵνα / ὅπως)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Deponent verb used strictly for religious address to God (explicitly τῷ Πατρί or τῷ Θεῷ in MAT 6:6; 1CO 11:13). Commonly paired with γρηγορεῖτε (MAT 26:41; MRK 14:38), νηστεύσαντες (ACT 13:3), θεὶς/θέντες τὰ γόνατα (ACT 9:40; ACT 21:5), laying on of hands (MAT 19:13; ACT 28:8), and singing hymns (ACT 16:25). JAS 5:17 uses the cognate dative intensifier προσευχῇ προσηύξατο ("prayed earnestly"). Intercession uses περί + genitive extensively, alongside ὑπέρ + genitive (MAT 5:44) and ἐπί + accusative (JAS 5:14).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A first-person singular pronoun combined with a coordinating or additive marker, introducing the speaker in continuation, addition, or correspondence with another person or action.

senses.definition: Joins a clause or predicate to what precedes while placing prominence on the first-person singular participant as subject or indirect object, often in a balanced or contrasting pair of statements.
senses.grammatical_frame: Coordinating pronoun (nominative κἀγώ or dative κἀμοί) introducing a coordinated clause, apodosis, or parallel verbless predicate

senses.definition: Aligns the first-person speaker with another individual or group as sharing the same action, condition, attitude, or treatment, sometimes with emphatic force ('even I').
senses.grammatical_frame: Additive pronoun (nominative κἀγώ, dative κἀμοί, or accusative κἀμέ as direct object or subject of an infinitive)

senses.definition: Marks the speaker's action as a reciprocal, matching, or proportional response to another's action, frequently in correlation with a comparative conjunction ('just as') or a conditional/relative clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Nominative pronoun (κἀγώ) in the main clause of a comparative construction with καθώς, a conditional sentence, or an elliptical parallel clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Inflected forms attested in the sample include nominative κἀγώ/Κἀγώ, dative κἀμοί (LUK 1:3; JHN 17:6; ACT 8:19), and accusative κἀμέ (JHN 7:28; 1CO 16:4). Frequently paired with καθώς to mark reciprocal or parallel action (JHN 10:15; JHN 15:9; JHN 17:18; 1CO 11:1), with δέ as a discourse-continuative marker (MAT 16:18; 1CO 7:40), and in verbless reciprocal formulas such as ἐν ἐμοὶ ... κἀγὼ ἐν ὑμῖν (JHN 14:20; JHN 15:4) or ἐμοὶ ... κἀγὼ κόσμῳ (GAL 6:14). Often used in clause-initial position to give prominence to the first-person referent in contrast or response to another party.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A subordinating and inferential conjunction introducing either the actual or intended result of a preceding action or a logical conclusion and exhortation drawn from what precedes.

senses.definition: Introduces a subordinate clause stating the actual consequence or outcome brought about by the preceding action or situation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction followed by an infinitive (often with an accusative subject; negated by μή or μηκέτι)

senses.definition: Introduces a subordinate clause expressing an intended, enabled, or potential outcome rather than an accomplished fact.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction followed by an infinitive expressing purpose or capacity after a verb of giving or performing

senses.definition: Introduces the factual outcome resulting from the degree or manner of a preceding action when paired with a correlative adverb ('so ... that').
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction followed by a finite indicative verb, correlative with οὕτως

senses.definition: Stands at the beginning of an independent statement to draw a logical inference or conclusion from the preceding argument or narrative.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial inferential conjunction followed by a finite indicative verb or verbless indicative predication

senses.definition: Introduces an exhortation, appeal, or command grounded in the preceding theological or practical reasoning.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial inferential conjunction followed by an imperative or hortatory subjunctive (often with a vocative)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In infinitival result clauses, the subject of the infinitive is regularly expressed in the accusative (e.g., ὥστε τὸν ὄχλον θαυμάσαι in MAT 15:31; ὥστε με μᾶλλον χαρῆναι in 2CO 7:7), and negation uses μή or μηκέτι (MRK 1:45; MRK 3:20; 2CO 3:7; 1TH 1:8). When used as a sentence-initial inferential marker in epistolary discourse, it often combines with vocative addresses such as ἀδελφοί μου or ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί (ROM 7:4; 1CO 11:33; 1CO 15:58; PHP 4:1).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A distributive pronoun and adjective identifying every individual person, part, or unit within a group or series taken separately ("each," "each one," "every").

senses.definition: Every single person or item within a group considered individually rather than collectively.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantive pronoun (masculine, feminine, or neuter; singular or plural), used independently, with a partitive genitive, in apposition to a plural subject, or combined with εἷς

senses.definition: Modifying a noun to single out every individual part or recurring unit of time in a sequence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective agreeing with a singular noun, including temporal phrases governed by κατά

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly reinforced by the numeral εἷς (εἷς ἕκαστος) to emphasize individuality (LUK 4:40; ACT 2:3; ACT 20:31; ACT 21:26; 1CO 12:18; EPH 4:16; COL 4:6). Frequently paired with possessive ἴδιος or ἑαυτοῦ (e.g., 1CO 3:8; 1CO 7:2; GAL 6:5) and often stands in singular apposition to a plural verb or subject (e.g., ACT 2:8; ACT 11:29; REV 5:8; REV 20:13). Attested in feminine (1CO 7:2; HEB 3:13), neuter (1CO 12:18), and plural (PHP 2:4) forms, and with κατά in recurring temporal phrases (HEB 3:13; REV 22:2).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adverb expressing higher degree, comparative preference, or contrastive replacement ("more," "rather," "instead").

senses.definition: To a higher degree, greater extent, or with greater certainty, often intensified by a preceding expression of measure in lesser-to-greater arguments.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying verbs or clauses, frequently preceded by dative or accusative expressions of degree (πολλῷ, πόσῳ, πολύ, τοσούτῳ)

senses.definition: In preference to or to a greater extent than an explicit or implied alternative.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb with verbs, adjectives, or nouns, typically followed by ἤ or ἤπερ introducing the compared alternative

senses.definition: Marking contrast, substitution, or corrective refinement against a preceding negated, rejected, or narrower statement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb introducing a contrasting or corrective clause, frequently paired with δέ, ἀλλά, or τοὐναντίον

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with dative or accusative expressions of degree (πολλῷ μᾶλλον, πόσῳ μᾶλλον, πολὺ μᾶλλον, τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὅσῳ) in lesser-to-greater arguments, and once stacked with a comparative adverb (περισσοτέρως μᾶλλον in 2CO 7:13). In comparisons it commonly correlates with ἤ or ἤπερ. In contrastive and corrective contexts it often combines with δέ (μᾶλλον δέ), ἀλλά (ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον), or τοὐναντίον.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Conforming to moral and divine standards of rightness, uprightness, fairness, or innocence, applied to people, God, deeds, and judgments.

senses.definition: Of human beings and the inner life: morally upright, devout, and faithful to God's standards of conduct, standing in contrast to the wicked, lawless, or sinful.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective describing persons or the soul, or substantivized with or without the definite article (ὁ δίκαιος, οἱ δίκαιοι)

senses.definition: Of God or Christ: faithful, morally pure, and fair in rule and judgment; in Acts, used substantively as a title for Jesus.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate or attributive adjective applied to God/Christ (2TI 4:8; 1JN 1:9; 2:29; REV 16:5), or substantivized with the masculine singular article as a title (ὁ Δίκαιος)

senses.definition: In contexts of bloodshed or legal accusation: free from wrongdoing or guilt, undeserving of condemnation or death.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective modifying αἷμα (MAT 23:35) or substantivized in a forensic/trial context (MAT 27:19)

senses.definition: Of judgments, commands, deeds, or courses of action: fair, equitable, morally sound, or proper to do.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective modifying κρίσις, ἐντολή, or ἔργα; or neuter predicate adjective (δίκαιον) with εἰμί or ἡγέομαι and an infinitive complement

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with ἄδικος (MAT 5:45; 1PE 3:18), πονηρός (MAT 5:45; 13:49; 1JN 3:12), ἁμαρτωλός (LUK 5:32), ἀπειθής (LUK 1:17), and ὑπόκρισις/ἀνομία (MAT 23:28), and paired with ἅγιος (MRK 6:20; ACT 3:14; ROM 7:12), ἀγαθός (LUK 23:50; ROM 7:12), πιστός (1JN 1:9), and ἀληθινός (REV 19:2). Common phrases include ὁ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται (ROM 1:17; HEB 10:38), ἀνὴρ δίκαιος (MRK 6:20; LUK 23:50), δικαία κρίσις (JHN 7:24; 2TH 1:5; REV 19:2), and the christological title ὁ Δίκαιος in Acts (ACT 3:14; 7:52; 22:14).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To dispatch or commission a person, object, or force toward a destination or recipient.

senses.definition: To direct or dispatch a person, group, or military force to go to a place or person for a task, message, or custody; also used without an explicit object to mean sending word or messengers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + acc (person/group) + εἰς/πρός + acc or dat; passive; or absolute with πρός/διά

senses.definition: To commission and send forth a divine agent or authorized representative (such as God sending the Son, the Father or Son sending the Holy Spirit/Paraclete, or Jesus commissioning followers), often in the substantivized participle designating the sender as authority.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized aorist participle (ὁ πέμψας + acc) or verb + acc (Spirit/representative) + dat/πρός + acc

senses.definition: To convey or forward material goods, financial support, or gifts to someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + acc (gift) + dat (recipient), or absolute with εἰς + acc (need) + dat

senses.definition: To cause an inner spiritual condition or deluding power to come upon people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + dat (recipient) + acc (abstract force)

senses.definition: To thrust out or put an implement (specifically a sickle) into action for harvesting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Imperative verb + acc (implement)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes a personal direct object with prepositional goal phrases (εἰς + accusative for places, πρός + accusative for persons) or a dative recipient (ὑμῖν). In narrative requests and official reports, the direct object is sometimes omitted in absolute usage ("send word/messengers": MAT 11:2; LUK 20:12; ACT 10:33; ACT 19:31; ACT 23:30). In John's Gospel, the substantivized aorist participle ὁ πέμψας με ("the one who sent me") serves as a recurring periphrasis for the Father. In JHN 13:16, an ἀπόστολος is contrasted with τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτόν in parallel with δοῦλος and κύριος. In ACT 10:5, πέμψον ("send") pairs with μετάπεμψαι ("summon").

entries.core_meaning_summary: An authorized representative or commissioned messenger, especially of Jesus Christ or of a Christian congregation.

senses.definition: One of the core group of twelve disciples chosen and instructed by Jesus during his earthly ministry, who subsequently served as authoritative leaders and miracle-working witnesses in Jerusalem.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun (often with article οἱ ἀπόστολοι or numeral δώδεκα)

senses.definition: A commissioned herald and witness of Jesus Christ (including Paul, Barnabas, Andronicus and Junia, and Peter in epistolary self-designation), holding primary authority in teaching, founding congregations, and receiving revelation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, often with genitive of Christ (Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ) or juxtaposed with κῆρυξ/διδάσκαλος/προφῆται

senses.definition: A commissioned delegate or representative sent by local congregations to carry aid or perform ministry on their behalf.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun + genitive of congregation or pronoun (ἐκκλησιῶν / ὑμῶν)

senses.definition: Title applied to Jesus as the supreme commissioned representative and high priest of Christian confession.
senses.grammatical_frame: Articular singular noun paired with Ἀρχιερέα in apposition to Ἰησοῦν

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with πρεσβύτεροι ("elders") as the governing leadership in Jerusalem (ACT 15:2, 6, 23) and with προφῆται ("prophets") and διδάσκαλοι ("teachers") in lists of church roles (1CO 12:28; EPH 3:5; 1TI 2:7; 2TI 1:11; REV 18:20). Common genitive modifiers identify the authorizing source: ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ / Κυρίου (EPH 1:1; 2PE 1:1; JUD 1:17), Χριστοῦ ἀπόστολοι (2CO 11:13; 1TH 2:7), or ἀπόστολοι ἐκκλησιῶν (2CO 8:23; cf. PHP 2:25 ὑμῶν ἀπόστολον). Associated with performing confirming wonders and signs (ACT 2:43; 5:12; 2CO 12:12).

entries.core_meaning_summary: First-person singular possessive adjective denoting belonging to, originating from, or associated with the speaker ('my', 'mine').

senses.definition: Belonging to, originating from, or personally associated with the speaker, whether designating body parts, inner faculties, utterances, authority, possessions, or relational ties.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective modifying a noun (preceding the noun with or without an article, following a noun with a repeated article, or modifying an anarthrous predicate noun)

senses.definition: Directed toward the speaker as the object of the action expressed by an action-noun.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective modifying an action-noun in a prepositional phrase (εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν)

senses.definition: Belonging to the speaker by ownership, source, or rightful prerogative.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate adjective with a copula (εἰμί), including with an infinitive subject clause (MAT 20:23)

senses.definition: Used substantively in the neuter to denote the things, domain, or followers belonging to the speaker.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized adjective with the neuter singular or plural definite article (τὸ ἐμόν, τὰ ἐμά)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in post-head attributive position with a repeated article (e.g., ἡ κρίσις ἡ ἐμή, ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμός, ἡ βασιλεία ἡ ἐμή) as well as pre-head position with an article (τὸ ἐμὸν ὄνομα, τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους), and is often contrasted with second- or third-person possessives (e.g., ὁ καιρὸς ὁ ἐμὸς ... ὁ δὲ καιρὸς ὁ ὑμέτερος in JHN 7:6; τὰ ἐμὰ πάντα σά ἐστιν καὶ τὰ σὰ ἐμά in JHN 17:10; τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα καὶ τὸ ὑμῶν in 1CO 16:18) or with τοῦ πέμψαντός με (JHN 5:30; 6:38; 7:16; 14:24). In LUK 22:19 and 1CO 11:25, εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν expresses an objective relation ('in remembrance of me'). In COL 4:18 and PHM 1:19, τῇ ἐμῇ χειρί emphasizes personal autograph ('with my own hand').

entries.core_meaning_summary: The proclaimed message of God's kingdom, grace, and Jesus Christ, and by extension the ministry or cause of spreading that message.

senses.definition: The announced message of salvation concerning God's kingdom, grace, and the risen Jesus Christ, which is preached, received, believed, obeyed, and defended.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun; object of verbs of proclamation or reception (κηρύσσω, εὐαγγελίζομαι, καταγγέλλω, παραλαμβάνω), dative with ἀπειθέω, or in prepositional phrases (κατά + accusative, διά + genitive)

senses.definition: The ongoing work, ministry, or cause of proclaiming and advancing that message, including the sphere in which workers labor, receive support, or endure hardship.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun; predominantly in prepositional phrases (ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ, ἐκ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, ἕνεκεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου) or as dative of advantage/association

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly modified by genitives indicating origin or content, including τοῦ Θεοῦ (MRK 1:14; ROM 15:16; 1TH 2:2, 8; 1PE 4:17), τοῦ Χριστοῦ (1CO 9:12; 2CO 10:14; PHP 1:27; 1TH 3:2), τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ (ROM 1:9), τῆς βασιλείας (MAT 4:23; 9:35), and τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Θεοῦ (ACT 20:24), as well as possessive pronouns referring to the messenger's proclamation (ROM 2:16; 16:25; 2CO 4:3; 2TH 2:14; 2TI 2:8). Frequently serves as the direct object of speaking/proclamation verbs (κηρύσσω, εὐαγγελίζομαι, καταγγέλλω, λαλέω, διαμαρτύρομαι) and appears in fixed phrases such as ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ εὐαγγελίου (GAL 2:5, 14) and ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ (ROM 1:9; 1CO 9:18; 2CO 8:18; 10:14; PHP 4:3; 1TH 3:2).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To experience or express gladness and delight, and in conventional imperative or infinitive formulas, to greet or salute someone.

senses.definition: To feel or manifest joy, gladness, or delight in response to an event, person, or situation, or as an ongoing disposition in relation to the Lord.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb; used absolutely, with ἐπί + dative or ἐν + dative (indicating the basis or sphere of joy), with διά + accusative or ἀπό + genitive (source), or with ὅτι / ὅταν clauses

senses.definition: To address someone with a conventional formula of salutation upon meeting, approaching, or opening a letter.
senses.grammatical_frame: Imperative singular/plural in direct address, or infinitive (χαίρειν) in epistolary headings with dative recipient or as complement of λέγω + dative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of strong gladness or celebration such as ἀγαλλιάομαι (MAT 5:12; JHN 8:56; 1PE 4:13), εὐφραίνομαι (LUK 15:32; REV 11:10), σκιρτάω (LUK 6:23), and συνχαίρω (1CO 13:6; PHP 2:18), and contrasted with weeping or grief (λύπη in JHN 16:22; 2CO 2:3; κλαίω in ROM 12:15; 1CO 7:30). Takes cognate accusative or dative forms with χαρά (MAT 2:10; 1TH 3:9) and adverbs of degree such as λίαν (LUK 23:8; 2JN 1:4) and μᾶλλον (2CO 7:7, 13). As a direct greeting (MAT 26:49; 28:9; MRK 15:18; LUK 1:28; 2JN 1:11) or epistolary opening formula (ACT 15:23; 23:26), the imperative or infinitive functions socially rather than purely as a command to feel joy.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The proper name for the people, nation, and land of Israel, used both for the historical ethnic-covenantal community and, in theological argument, for the faithful community defined by God's promise rather than physical descent alone.

senses.definition: The historical people, nation, and covenant community descended from Jacob/Israel, viewed as an ethnic, political, or religious body (often explicitly as 'the house,' 'people,' 'race,' or 'sons of Israel').
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable proper noun, with or without the masculine singular article (ὁ/τὸν/τοῦ/τῷ), functioning as subject, direct object, indirect object, prepositional object (e.g., ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, πρὸς τὸν Ἰσραήλ), or descriptive/possessive genitive modifying terms such as λαός, υἱοί, οἶκος, γένος, Θεός, βασιλεύς, and διδάσκαλος.

senses.definition: The geographical territory, towns, or realm inhabited by the Israelite people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable proper noun in the genitive modifying a spatial noun (γῆν Ἰσραήλ, τὰς πόλεις τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ) or object of ἐν τῷ designating a historical setting/region.

senses.definition: The spiritually or covenantally defined community belonging to God, explicitly distinguished from mere physical descent or ethnic membership.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable proper noun, either predicate nominative in contrast with ancestral descent (οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραήλ ... οὗτοι Ἰσραήλ) or articular object of ἐπί modified by τοῦ Θεοῦ.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Indeclinable proper noun whose grammatical role is marked by preceding articles (ὁ, τὸν, τοῦ, τῷ), prepositions, or surrounding syntax. Common recurring expressions include υἱοὶ Ἰσραήλ (MAT 27:9; ACT 5:21, 7:37, 9:15, 10:36; ROM 9:27; 2CO 3:7; HEB 11:22; REV 7:4), οἶκος Ἰσραήλ (MAT 10:6; HEB 8:8, paired with οἶκον Ἰούδα), λαὸς Ἰσραήλ (MAT 2:6; ACT 4:10), Θεὸς Ἰσραήλ (MAT 15:31), and Βασιλεὺς [τοῦ] Ἰσραήλ (MAT 27:42; MRK 15:32; JHN 1:49). In ROM 9:6, the noun is used twice in immediate contrast: first for ancestral/ethnic descent (οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραήλ) and second for those who truly constitute the promised community (οὗτοι Ἰσραήλ). Similarly, 1CO 10:18 adds the modifier κατὰ σάρκα to specify physical/earthly Israel.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The produce or harvest yielded by plants, trees, and land, extended broadly to human offspring, moral and spiritual outcomes, spoken praise, and the beneficial proceeds of labor or generosity.

senses.definition: The edible or agricultural produce yielded by trees, vines, sown crops, or the earth, including harvested grain and orchard fruit.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular or plural; commonly direct object of verbs of producing, bearing, or gathering (ποιέω, φέρω, δίδωμι, ἀποδίδωμι, συνάγω, λαμβάνω, ἐσθίω), often with a genitive of source (e.g., τῆς γῆς, αὐτοῦ).

senses.definition: Moral, behavioral, or spiritual outcomes, deeds, or character virtues resulting from repentance, discipleship, discipline, or spiritual influence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular or plural; object of ποιέω, φέρω, ἔχω, συνάγω, or ἀποδίδωμι, or subject of εἰμί/σπείρομαι; frequently modified by a genitive of source or quality (τοῦ Πνεύματός, τοῦ φωτός, δικαιοσύνης, αὐτῆς) or by ἄξιος + genitive (τῆς μετανοίας).

senses.definition: Productive benefit, gain, proceeds, or credit resulting from apostolic labor, completed service, or generous giving.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular; object of ἔχω, σφραγίζομαι, or ἐπιζητέω, or predicate noun with a genitive (καρπὸς ἔργου), sometimes qualified as increasing to someone's account (εἰς λόγον ὑμῶν).

senses.definition: Verbal expression or offering of praise and confession produced by the lips.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular, in apposition to θυσίαν αἰνέσεως (sacrifice of praise) and modified by the genitive χειλέων (of lips).

senses.definition: Human offspring or biological descendant, expressed through anatomical idioms for conception and lineage.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular, modified by a genitive of an anatomical term (τῆς κοιλίας σου, τῆς ὀσφύος αὐτοῦ).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears as the direct object of verbs of production and bearing, especially ποιέω (MAT 3:10, 7:17, 13:26, 21:43; LUK 3:8, 6:43, 13:9; REV 22:2), φέρω (JHN 12:24, 15:2, 15:4, 15:8, 15:16), δίδωμι (MAT 13:8; MRK 4:7), and ἀποδίδωμι (HEB 12:11; REV 22:2). Moral and spiritual usages build directly on agricultural metaphors: good or rotten trees indicate a person's character by their produce (MAT 7:17-20, 12:33; LUK 6:43-44), and vine branches bear produce only by remaining in the vine (JHN 15:2-8). Notable fixed or theological collocations include καρπὸν ἄξιον τῆς μετανοίας (MAT 3:8; LUK 3:8), ὁ καρπὸς τοῦ Πνεύματός (GAL 5:22), ὁ καρπὸς τοῦ φωτὸς (EPH 5:9), καρπὸν ... δικαιοσύνης (HEB 12:11; JAS 3:18), καρπὸν χειλέων (HEB 13:15), and anatomical expressions for biological offspring (LUK 1:42; ACT 2:30). In ROM 15:28, τὸν καρπὸν τοῦτον refers to a completed task or delivered benefit/contribution without naming its exact contents within that single verse.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A disjunctive and conditional conjunction used mainly in correlative pairs ('whether ... or') to link alternative items, circumstances, or clauses, and occasionally singly ('if').

senses.definition: Used repeatedly in correlation to introduce two or more alternative nouns, pronouns, adjectives, participles, or prepositional phrases whose distinction does not alter the validity or scope of the main statement.
senses.grammatical_frame: correlative conjunction (εἴτε ... εἴτε ...) linking coordinate words or phrases

senses.definition: Used in correlation to introduce alternative finite clauses representing different possible conditions, states, or actions leading to a common outcome or obligation.
senses.grammatical_frame: correlative conjunction (εἴτε ... εἴτε ...) introducing indicative or subjunctive clauses

senses.definition: Used singly without a correlative partner to introduce a specific conditional case or situation.
senses.grammatical_frame: single conjunction + indicative verb in a conditional protasis

entries.collocations_and_notes: Almost always occurs in correlative pairs or series (εἴτε ... εἴτε ...), often framing exhaustive or contrasting pairs such as 'Jews or Greeks', 'slave or free', 'in the body or out of the body', 'by word or by letter', or 'awake or asleep'. Frequently depends on a summarizing main clause with πᾶς/πάντα ('all things', e.g., 1CO 3:22; 10:31; COL 1:16, 20) or an expression of uncertainty such as οὐκ οἶδα ('I do not know', 2CO 12:2–3). In 1CO 14:27 it appears singly without a second εἴτε to introduce a specific case in a series of church-order instructions.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To ask someone a question for information or to make a request, appeal, or petition to someone (including to God).

senses.definition: To put a question to someone in order to learn information, clarify a teaching, or elicit an explanation or judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb + accusative of person (with direct/indirect question, accusative of topic, or περί + genitive), or absolute

senses.definition: To request, urge, or appeal to someone to perform an action, grant a favor, or adopt a course of conduct.
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb + accusative of person (sometimes implicit) + infinitive, ἵνα/ὅπως + subjunctive, direct imperative, or περί + genitive

senses.definition: To address a petition or intercessory request to God on behalf of someone or concerning a matter.
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb + optional accusative of God + περί + genitive of person or matter

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes an accusative of the person addressed, followed by a direct question (often introduced by λέγων/λέγοντες), an indirect question (e.g., πῶς in JHN 9:15), περί + genitive of topic or person (LUK 4:38; 9:45; JHN 16:26; 17:9, 20; 18:19), an infinitive (LUK 8:37; JHN 4:40; ACT 3:3; 16:39; 23:18; 1TH 5:12), or a purpose/content clause with ἵνα or ὅπως + subjunctive (LUK 7:3; 16:27; JHN 19:31; ACT 23:20; 1TH 4:1). Contrasts with ἀποκρίνομαι ('answer') in LUK 22:68, parallels or pairs with παρακαλέω ('urge, appeal') in 1TH 4:1, and alternates with αἰτέω ('ask, request') in JHN 16:26 and 1JN 5:16. Note the polite formula ἐρωτῶ σε ('I ask you / please') in LUK 14:18–19 and 16:27.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To form a judgment or supposition, to appear or be regarded a certain way by others, or impersonally to seem fitting or be decided.

senses.definition: To hold an opinion, assume, expect, or consider oneself or another to be something, frequently indicating an unverified or mistaken judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: personal verb with ὅτι-clause, infinitive (or accusative + infinitive), or relative/interrogative clause

senses.definition: To give the impression of being, appear to observers, or be held in esteem or reputation (including substantivized οἱ δοκοῦντες for people of standing).
senses.grammatical_frame: personal verb or participle with complementary infinitive (often εἶναι or ὑπάρχειν)

senses.definition: Impersonally, to strike someone as true, reasonable, or fitting; used especially in questions soliciting an audience's opinion.
senses.grammatical_frame: impersonal 3rd singular verb with dative of person (with interrogative τί or predicate adjective)

senses.definition: Impersonally, to seem good or advisable to someone so as to result in a deliberate choice, resolution, or personal discretion.
senses.grammatical_frame: impersonal 3rd singular aorist with dative of person + infinitive, or neuter articular participle τὸ δοκοῦν + dative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly contrasts mistaken human assumptions with reality (e.g., MRK 6:49; JHN 11:13; JHN 20:15; GAL 6:3; JAS 1:26). In LUK 8:18 and 1CO 11:16, personal supposition ('thinks he has / thinks to be') borders closely on outward appearance ('seems to have / seems to be'). In GAL 2:6, the substantivized participle οἱ δοκοῦντες (εἶναί τι) refers to people recognized as having high standing or reputation. The impersonal question Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ; ('What do you think?') regularly introduces a call for judgment (MAT 18:12; MAT 21:28; MAT 22:42; MAT 26:66; JHN 11:56).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To make a public announcement or openly declare a religious message, person, or report.

senses.definition: To deliver a public announcement or religious proclamation openly before listeners, without an explicit accusative object of the message.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, often with locative phrase, dative of audience, or λέγων introducing direct speech

senses.definition: To announce publicly or advocate a specific message, event, or religious practice (such as the gospel, the kingdom, repentance, or circumcision).
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb + accusative of message/topic (or passive), sometimes with dative or εἰς + accusative of recipients or ὅτι clause

senses.definition: To declare a person (such as Jesus Christ or Moses) as the central subject and content of a public religious message.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb + accusative of person (or passive with personal subject), optionally with dative of audience or ὅτι clause

senses.definition: To tell widely or broadcast news, deeds, or previously private words in public.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb (absolute, with relative clause object, or passive with ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with διδάσκω ('teach': MAT 11:1, ACT 28:31) and εὐαγγελίζομαι ('bring good news': LUK 8:1). Common direct objects are τὸ εὐαγγέλιον (MAT 9:35, MAT 24:14, MRK 13:10, MRK 16:15, 1TH 2:9), ἡ βασιλεία (τοῦ Θεοῦ) (LUK 8:1, ACT 20:25, ACT 28:31), and τὸν Χριστόν / τὸν Ἰησοῦν (ACT 8:5, ACT 9:20, 1CO 1:23, 2CO 11:4, PHP 1:15). Audience is marked by the dative (e.g., LUK 4:18, ACT 8:5, ACT 10:42, 1CO 9:27, 1PE 3:19), ἐν + dative (e.g., MAT 3:1, ACT 9:20, 1TI 3:16), or εἰς + accusative (e.g., MRK 13:10, 1TH 2:9).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Deeply loved, cherished, or held dear by God or another person, frequently used both descriptively for favored individuals and as an affectionate direct address among believers.

senses.definition: Held in deep affection, cherished, or specially favored by God or by another person; used of God's chosen son or servant, of believers in relation to God, and of close friends or spiritual kin.
senses.grammatical_frame: attributive, predicative, or substantivized adjective (often with possessive genitive μου or Θεοῦ)

senses.definition: Term of warm affection used to address an individual or community of fellow believers in exhortations, warnings, and encouragement.
senses.grammatical_frame: vocative plural or singular (alone, with μου, or modifying ἀδελφοί)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently modifies kinship and relational nouns such as υἱός ('son', MAT 3:17; MRK 1:11; LUK 20:13), παῖς ('servant/child', MAT 12:18), τέκνον ('child', 1CO 4:14; EPH 5:1; 2TI 1:2), ἀδελφός ('brother', 1CO 15:58; COL 4:7; PHM 1:16), and σύνδουλος ('fellow servant', COL 1:7). In heavenly declarations about Jesus (MAT 3:17; MAT 12:18; MRK 1:11; LUK 3:22; 2PE 1:17), it regularly pairs with the verb εὐδοκέω ('to take delight in'). In epistles, the plural vocative ἀγαπητοί (or ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί) routinely marks transitions to direct exhortation or reassurance (e.g., 1CO 10:14; PHP 2:12; 1PE 4:12; 1JN 4:1).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Temporal and discourse adverb indicating that an action, state, or point in time has been reached by or before the moment under consideration.

senses.definition: Indicates that an event has occurred, a condition has been completed, or a span of time or sequence count has elapsed prior to or by the reference point.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying past, perfect, or pluperfect verbs, temporal participles, or duration/ordinal phrases

senses.definition: Marks a present or unfolding situation as immediately in effect, underway, or at hand at the moment of speaking or narrative focus.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying present or imperfect verbs, present participles, or predicate adjectives/nouns

senses.definition: Functions in idiomatic combinations to express long-awaited realization ("now at last" with ποτέ) or to introduce an immediate baseline judgment in an argument ("as it is" / "right away" with μὲν οὖν).
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb in fixed particle collocations (ἤδη ποτέ, ἤδη μὲν οὖν)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly paired with genitive absolutes to mark background time already reached (e.g., ἤδη ὀψίας γενομένης, ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ καταβαίνοντος) and with time-duration or ordinal expressions (ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς, τέσσαρας ἤδη ἡμέρας, ἤδη τρίτον, ἤδη δευτέραν). Appears in fixed combinations ἤδη ποτέ (ROM 1:10) and ἤδη μὲν οὖν (1CO 6:7).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be in a particular state, role, or location, to exist or be present, and in the substantivized neuter plural to denote a person's property or belongings.

senses.definition: To hold a status, identity, quality, or condition, linking a subject to a predicate noun, adjective, or prepositional phrase.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb (often participle) + predicate nominative, predicate adjective, or prepositional phrase

senses.definition: To exist, be present, or take place in a given setting, situation, or community.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, often with ἐν + dative or in a genitive absolute

senses.definition: To belong to someone or be available at someone's disposal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb or participle + dative of possessor

senses.definition: Material goods, wealth, or assets belonging to a person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized neuter plural participle (τὰ ὑπάρχοντα) + genitive or dative possessor

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears as a participle (ὑπάρχων) expressing a state, status, or condition as background to a main clause (e.g., ACT 2:30, ACT 7:55, GAL 2:14). Often paired with εἰμί in surrounding verses (e.g., LUK 7:25, LUK 9:48, ACT 16:37, ACT 21:20, 1CO 11:7). In HEB 10:34, τὰ ὑπάρχοντα is explicitly contrasted with the cognate noun ὕπαρξις ('a better and abiding possession'). In ACT 27:34, the phrase πρὸς τῆς ὑμετέρας σωτηρίας ὑπάρχει expresses conduciveness ('contributes to your safety').

entries.core_meaning_summary: An emotion or state of gladness and delight, as well as a person or anticipated blessing that brings such gladness.

senses.definition: A feeling or condition of gladness, delight, or rejoicing experienced by a person or community, often contrasted with sorrow or grief.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun as subject, direct object, cognate accusative/dative with χαίρω, or predicate genitive

senses.definition: Gladness functioning as the manner in which an action is performed or as the internal motive prompting a response.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrases μετὰ (πάσης) χαρᾶς, ἐν χαρᾷ, or ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς modifying verbs of action, reception, or return

senses.definition: A person, community, or anticipated celebratory state that serves as the source, embodiment, or goal of gladness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate nominative or vocative identifying people, or object of εἰσέρχομαι εἰς / ἀντί denoting an anticipated state or reward

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with the verb πληρόω ('to be filled/made full', e.g., JHN 3:29, JHN 15:11, JHN 16:24, 2TI 1:4, 1JN 1:4, 2JN 1:12) and in cognate constructions with χαίρω (MAT 2:10, JHN 3:29). Directly contrasted with λύπη ('grief/sorrow', JHN 16:20, 2CO 2:3, HEB 12:11) and paired with πένθος/κατήφεια in reversals (JAS 4:9). Common prepositional collocations include μετὰ χαρᾶς ('with joy') and ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς ('out of/because of joy'). In epistolary praise it is joined with στέφανος ('crown') and δόξα ('glory', PHP 4:1, 1TH 2:19–20).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To greet or extend goodwill to someone, either in person upon meeting or arrival, or through written and mediated salutations.

senses.definition: To offer a spoken or customary greeting or welcome to someone when encountering them on the road, entering a home, or arriving at a community gathering.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle verb + accusative of person, household (οἰκία), or assembly (ἐκκλησία)

senses.definition: To convey greetings to designated individuals or to exchange greetings mutually within a community, often specified with an affectionate gesture such as a holy kiss or individually by name.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle imperative + accusative of person, group, or reciprocal pronoun (ἀλλήλους), often with ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ or κατ’ ὄνομα

senses.definition: To send written expressions of goodwill and remembrance from an author, companion, or distant congregation to the recipients of a letter.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle indicative + accusative personal pronoun (ὑμᾶς, σε), occasionally modified by πολλά or ἐν Κυρίῳ

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently used in epistolary closings, pairing reciprocal imperatives (e.g., ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ) with indicative greetings from third parties (ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς...). Occasionally modified by ἐν Κυρίῳ, πολλά, or κατ’ ὄνομα. In narratives, appears with motion or entry verbs (εἰσέρχομαι, προστρέχω, ἀναβαίνω) and takes either a person, a household (οἶκος/οἰκία), or a congregation (ἐκκλησία) as its direct object.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Situated in the middle, center, or midpoint of a space, group, or period of time.

senses.definition: Located at or moving into the central area of an object, place, region, or gathered assembly, or positioned between two points.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective (predicative or adverbial accusative) or substantivized neuter in prepositional phrases (ἐν [τῷ] μέσῳ, εἰς [τὸ] μέσον, ἀνὰ μέσον, διὰ μέσον), absolute or with genitive of place/object

senses.definition: Situated within, surrounded by, or present among a group of people or living beings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrase (ἐν μέσῳ + genitive plural/collective) or predicative/adverbial adjective (μέσος, μέσον + genitive)

senses.definition: Removed, separated, or departing from the company or presence of a group or from active involvement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrase ἐκ μέσου (+ genitive plural or absolute with verbs of motion, removal, or separation)

senses.definition: Occurring at the central point of a period of time, specifically noon or midnight.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive genitive modifying a temporal noun (ἡμέρας μέσης) or prepositional phrase κατὰ μέσον + genitive of time

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears as a substantivized neuter singular in prepositional phrases with a dependent genitive: ἐν (τῷ) μέσῳ ('in the midst of / among'), εἰς (τὸ) μέσον ('into the middle / out before everyone'), ἐκ μέσου ('out from among / out of the way'), ἀνὰ μέσον ('among / in the middle of'), and διὰ μέσον ('between / through the middle of'). Also occurs predicatively (μέσος, μέσον) or adverbially in the accusative (μέσον) before a genitive (PHP 2:15). With temporal nouns it marks the midpoint of day (ἡμέρας μέσης, ACT 26:13) or night (κατὰ μέσον τῆς νυκτός, ACT 27:27).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Negative coordinating conjunction and adverb used to link negated clauses, verbs, nouns, or modifiers, to introduce negative commands or exhortations, and to mark an extreme or minimal item ('not even').

senses.definition: Connects a subsequent negated verb, clause, noun phrase, participle, infinitive, or modifier to a preceding negation, extending the scope of a prohibition, negative condition, or denial.
senses.grammatical_frame: Coordinating negative conjunction following a preceding negation (e.g., μή, μηδέν, μηδενί), joining verbs, clauses, nouns, or modifiers

senses.definition: Introduces a negative command, prohibition, or hortatory clause without an immediately preceding negation in the same clause, including the conclusion of a negated conditional statement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial negative conjunction with an imperative or prohibitive/hortatory subjunctive verb

senses.definition: Highlights an extreme or minimal instance included under a preceding negation, indicating that even that minimal action or location is excluded.
senses.grammatical_frame: Negative adverbial particle following a preceding negation (e.g., μηκέτι, μή), modifying a prepositional phrase or infinitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently continues a chain of negations introduced by μή (e.g., MAT 10:9-10, LUK 14:12, COL 2:21) or negated pronouns such as μηδέν (PHP 2:3) and μηδενί (1TI 5:22). Appears elided as μηδ’ before a vowel in 1PE 5:3. In MRK 8:26 (Μηδὲ εἰς τὴν κώμην εἰσέλθῃς), the clause-initial prohibition may also carry a scalar nuance ('do not even enter the village'). In 2TH 3:10, it introduces a negative third-person imperative in the apodosis following a negated condition (εἴ τις οὐ θέλει... μηδὲ ἐσθιέτω).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Qualitative demonstrative adjective and pronoun denoting a person, object, quality, or circumstance of the kind just described or exemplified ('such', 'of this sort').

senses.definition: Identifies a noun as possessing the kind, character, or degree indicated by the surrounding context or an accompanying relative or result clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or appositive adjective modifying a noun, often followed by a qualifying relative or result clause

senses.definition: Expresses qualitative correspondence or likeness in a predicate position, matching a standard introduced by a correlative relative adjective.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate adjective in correlative clauses paired with οἷος

senses.definition: Refers substantivally to an individual or group of people characterized by the conduct, status, or qualities described in the context.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival masculine or feminine adjective (typically articular, singular or plural)

senses.definition: Refers substantivally to actions, reports, qualities, or circumstances of the kind previously mentioned or exemplified.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival neuter plural adjective (articular or anarthrous)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Correlates explicitly with the relative adjective οἷος in MRK 13:19, 1CO 15:48, and 2CO 10:11, and with ἥτις... ὥστε in 1CO 5:1. Neuter nominative/accusative singular takes the form τοιοῦτο in MAT 18:5. Articular singular forms (ὁ τοιοῦτος, τὸν τοιοῦτον, τοῦ τοιούτου) are frequently used in Pauline epistles as a general or distancing reference to an individual under discussion (e.g., 1CO 5:5, 2CO 2:7, 2CO 10:11, 2CO 12:5, GAL 6:1, TIT 3:11). Frequently occurs in the expression οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντες (ROM 1:32, ROM 2:2). In GAL 5:23, τῶν τοιούτων is morphologically ambiguous between neuter plural ('such qualities/things') and masculine plural ('such people').

entries.core_meaning_summary: To take, receive, welcome, or accept an object, person, or message.

senses.definition: To take hold of a physical object into one's hand or arms, or to receive items or documents transmitted from another person.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb + accusative object (sometimes with εἰς + accusative or παρά + genitive)

senses.definition: To welcome a person, messenger, traveler, or departing spirit with hospitality, respect, or acceptance, or to admit someone into a home, place, or realm.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb + accusative personal object (often with εἰς + accusative, ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι, or ὡς + accusative)

senses.definition: To willingly accept, embrace, or believe a spoken message, teaching, truth, divine gift, or spiritual reality.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb + accusative abstract object (or absolute infinitive)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently used in reciprocal hospitality sayings ("whoever welcomes X welcomes me / the one who sent me," MAT 10:40; MRK 9:37; LUK 9:48) and in missionary departure instructions paired negatively with ἀκούω (MAT 10:14; MRK 6:11) or shaking dust from the feet (LUK 9:5). Often takes ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ("in my name," MAT 18:5; MRK 9:37; LUK 9:48), ὡς + accusative ("as a child / angel / fool," MRK 10:15; LUK 18:17; 2CO 11:16; GAL 4:14), εἰς + accusative indicating destination ("into arms / homes / eternal dwellings," LUK 2:28; LUK 16:4, 9), and παρά + genitive for the human intermediary or source of items received (ACT 22:5; PHP 4:18). Commonly takes τὸν λόγον (τοῦ Θεοῦ) in Acts and Pauline letters (ACT 11:1; 17:11; 1TH 1:6).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A beginning, origin, edge/corner, or governing authority/ruler.

senses.definition: The temporal starting point, outset, or earliest stage of creation, history, an era, a message, or an event.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (frequently in prepositional phrases ἀπ’/ἐξ/ἐν/κατ’ ἀρχῆς/ἀρχῇ/ἀρχάς, with genitive modifier, or as object of λαμβάνω + infinitive)

senses.definition: The elementary or foundational stage of instruction or spiritual practice, contrasted with maturity and likened to a foundation.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (genitive modifier of λόγος, contrasted with τελειότης)

senses.definition: Used adverbially in an elliptical question to indicate "at all," "from the beginning," or "in the first place" (exact nuance depends on how the elliptical clause is construed).
senses.grammatical_frame: adverbial accusative (τὴν ἀρχήν)

senses.definition: An outer corner, edge, or extremity of a physical object such as a large sheet.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (plural instrumental dative modified by numeral τέσσαρσιν)

senses.definition: A position of rule or authority, or an official, magistrate, or cosmic/spiritual power exercising rule.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (singular or plural, coordinated with ἐξουσία, δύναμις, κυριότης, or θρόνος)

senses.definition: The originating source, initiator, or preeminent first one (applied as a title to Christ in relation to creation or resurrection from the dead).
senses.grammatical_frame: predicate or appositive noun (sometimes with genitive τῆς κτίσεως)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most often appears in temporal prepositional phrases without an article: ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς (20+ occurrences across Gospels, Acts, Paul, Hebrews, and Johannine letters), ἐξ ἀρχῆς (JHN 6:64; 16:4), ἐν ἀρχῇ (JHN 1:1, 2; ACT 11:15; PHP 4:15), and κατ’ ἀρχάς (HEB 1:10). Frequently paired with or contrasted with τέλος ("end," HEB 3:14; 7:3; REV 21:6). In the plural (and once singular in EPH 1:21), regularly coordinated with ἐξουσία ("authority") to designate human or supernatural governing powers (LUK 12:11; EPH 1:21; 3:10; COL 1:16; 2:15). In JHN 8:25, the adverbial accusative τὴν ἀρχήν occurs in an elliptical interrogative construction whose exact sense ("at all" vs. "from the beginning") is syntactically debated. In COL 1:18 and REV 3:14, christological usage blends temporal/causal origin with preeminence or sovereignty.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Remaining or other (of people, things, or members of a class), and adverbially marking remaining/subsequent time or a transition to concluding remarks.

senses.definition: Left over or additional within a specified group or category, distinct from members already singled out.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective in attributive position modifying a plural noun (usually with the definite article)

senses.definition: The remaining people, survivors, outsiders, or other things/matters not yet addressed or included in a preceding group.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival plural adjective with the definite article (masculine or feminine for persons; neuter for things, kinds, or matters), sometimes followed by a partitive genitive or πᾶς

senses.definition: For the remaining time, from this point onward, or eventually after a preceding stretch of time.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter singular accusative (anarthrous λοιπόν or articular τὸ λοιπόν) functioning as a temporal adverb modifying a clause

senses.definition: Introduces a closing section, final exhortation, or additional point following what has already been said.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter singular accusative (λοιπόν, τὸ λοιπόν) or genitive (τοῦ λοιποῦ) functioning as a clause-level discourse marker, often paired with imperatives or οὖν

entries.collocations_and_notes: When used substantivally with the article (οἱ λοιποί, αἱ λοιπαί, τὰ λοιπά), it frequently contrasts an unspecified remainder with a previously named person or group (e.g., Peter and 'the rest of the apostles' in ACT 2:37; Israel's elect vs. 'the rest' in ROM 11:7; believers vs. 'the rest' outside the community in EPH 2:3 and 1TH 5:6). Adverbial forms vary between articular (τὸ λοιπόν, τοῦ λοιποῦ) and anarthrous (λοιπόν), serving either temporal or discourse-transitional roles; in some epistolary passages (such as 1CO 4:2 and 1TH 4:1), the boundary between 'furthermore/finally' and 'from now on' is slightly fluid.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An inferential conjunction indicating a factual result, logical conclusion, or consequent exhortation based on what precedes.

senses.definition: Introduces a factual outcome, resulting state, or logical conclusion following from preceding statements or events.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial inferential conjunction introducing a declarative clause or quotation

senses.definition: Introduces an exhortation, command, or appeal grounded in the preceding narrative or theological argument.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial inferential conjunction introducing an imperative, hortatory subjunctive, or verb of urging/requesting

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly stands in clause-initial position (sometimes immediately followed by a vocative as in GAL 4:31, or a circumstantial participle preceding the main verb as in EPH 4:25, HEB 6:1, HEB 12:28, JAS 1:21, 1PE 1:13). Frequently combines with καί (διὸ καί, e.g., LUK 1:35, ACT 10:29, ROM 4:22, PHP 2:9, HEB 13:12) to highlight a fitting correspondence ("for this reason also"). Also introduces cited scriptural statements in EPH 5:14, HEB 3:7, and HEB 10:5.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Confident forward-looking expectation or trust (especially directed toward God and promised future salvation), as well as the awaited reality or person in whom that expectation is placed.

senses.definition: Confident expectation or anticipation of a future outcome, whether ordinary (such as business gain or survival) or religious (trust directed toward God and promised blessings).
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun used as subject, direct object (often with verbs of having or attaining), or in prepositional phrases (especially with epi + dative, en + dative, eis + accusative, kata + accusative, para + accusative), frequently modified by a genitive specifying the basis or outcome expected

senses.definition: The unseen future blessing, promise, or eschatological outcome that is awaited and hoped for.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun functioning as direct object of verbs of awaiting or seizing, or in prepositional phrases (peri, dia, apo, heineken), often treated as an objective reality stored up or set before believers

senses.definition: A person or group who serves as the embodiment, ground, or source of confident expectation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in predicate or appositional construction referring to Christ or believers

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with πίστις ('faith') and ἀγάπη ('love') (1CO 13:13; 1TH 5:8; 1PE 1:21). Common verbs: ἔχω ('have', e.g., ACT 24:15; ROM 15:4; 2CO 3:12; μὴ ἔχω 'be without hope', EPH 2:12; 1TH 4:13), ἀπεκδέχομαι / προσδέχομαι ('eagerly await', GAL 5:5; TIT 2:13), and κρατέω ('lay hold of', HEB 6:18). Frequent prepositional phrases include ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι ('in hope / on the basis of expectation', ACT 2:26; ROM 4:18; ROM 5:2; TIT 1:2; also written ἐφ’ ἑλπίδι in ROM 8:20) and παρ’ ἐλπίδα ('beyond expectation', ROM 4:18). Often takes an objective or characterizing genitive such as σωτηρίας ('of salvation'), ζωῆς αἰωνίου ('of eternal life'), δόξης ('of glory'), or τῆς κλήσεως ('of the calling').

entries.core_meaning_summary: To persuade or win over someone in the active voice, to be convinced or comply in the middle/passive, and to trust or have confidence in the perfect active.

senses.definition: To influence someone through reasoning, speech, or urging so that they accept a view or undertake an action; frequently conative in the imperfect or present participle ("seek to persuade/convince").
senses.grammatical_frame: Active voice; takes accusative of person, often with ἵνα, an infinitive, or περί + genitive

senses.definition: To win someone over, appease an official, or seek human favor and approval (paired with ἀρέσκω in GAL 1:10).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active voice; transitive with accusative of person (or object implied)

senses.definition: To become convinced or hold a firm conviction that something is true or reliable (paired with οἶδα in ROM 14:14 and contrasted with ἀπιστέω in ACT 28:24).
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/middle voice (especially perfect πέπεισμαι); absolute or with ὅτι-clause, accusative-infinitive, dative of thing, or περί + genitive

senses.definition: To yield to, comply with, follow, or obey a person, advice, or standard of conduct.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle/passive voice with dative object

senses.definition: To place one's trust, reliance, or confidence in a person, God, oneself, or some ground of security, or to be confident of a future outcome.
senses.grammatical_frame: Perfect/pluperfect active used intransitively; with ἐπί + dative/accusative, ἐν + dative, εἰς + accusative, dative noun, infinitive, or ὅτι-clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Voice and stem distinctions follow clear syntactic patterns: the active voice takes a personal direct object (sometimes with ἵνα, an infinitive, or περί + genitive) for persuading or winning someone over; the middle/passive expresses either being convinced of a fact/claim (with ὅτι, accusative-infinitive, or περί + genitive) or yielding/obeying (with a dative object, contrasted with ἀπειθέω in ROM 2:8 and paired with ὑπείκω in HEB 13:17); the perfect/pluperfect active (πέποιθα, ἐπεποίθει) is regularly intransitive, expressing settled trust or confidence with ἐπί + dative/accusative, ἐν + dative, εἰς + accusative, a dative noun, or a ὅτι-clause. Often paired with ἐν Κυρίῳ in epistolary expressions of confidence (GAL 5:10, PHP 2:24, 2TH 3:4).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The anatomical tongue, human or Spirit-inspired speech and language, a linguistic people group, or a tongue-like shape.

senses.definition: The muscular organ inside the mouth used in speaking and affected by physical healing or pain.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in literal anatomical descriptions

senses.definition: The faculty of speech or manner of speaking, especially as an instrument of moral good or harm.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun used metonymically as subject, object, or instrumental dative/prepositional phrase

senses.definition: A distinct human language or an inspired, often unintelligible ecstatic utterance given by the Spirit that requires interpretation in communal worship.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular or plural), commonly dative of instrument with λαλέω or genitive with γένη / ἑρμηνεία

senses.definition: A community or people group distinguished by a shared language.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun grouped in series with φυλή, λαός, and ἔθνος

senses.definition: A visual phenomenon resembling a tongue in form, specifically flickering flames.
senses.grammatical_frame: Nominative plural noun modified by ὡσεὶ πυρός

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with `λαλέω` in the dative (`λαλεῖν γλώσσῃ` / `γλώσσαις`) to denote either speaking in human languages (ACT 2:11) or Spirit-enabled utterance requiring `ἑρμηνεία` (1CO 12:10; 1CO 14:2, 5, 13, 26). In 1CO 14:9 (`διὰ τῆς γλώσσης`), the term bridges the spoken tongue/speech and unintelligible ecstatic utterance. In Revelation, `γλῶσσα` regularly appears in fourfold lists alongside `φυλή`, `λαός`, and `ἔθνος` to encompass all human populations.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Morally corrupt, wicked, or wrong, as well as harm, injury, or misfortune.
