senses.definition: Morally wicked, corrupt, vicious, or harmful in character, applied to people, inner thoughts, or associations.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective or substantivized masculine plural adjective

senses.definition: Morally wrong conduct, wrongdoing, or evil in the abstract, often contrasted with what is good or right.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized neuter singular or plural adjective, frequently as object of ποιέω or πράσσω

senses.definition: Harm, injury, damage, or painful misfortune experienced or inflicted on someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicative neuter adjective or substantivized neuter singular/plural adjective, especially in κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ

entries.collocations_and_notes: Repeatedly stands in direct contrast with `ἀγαθός` (LUK 16:25; ROM 3:8; ROM 12:21; ROM 13:4; 1TH 5:15) and `καλός` (ROM 7:21; compare `χρηστά` in 1CO 15:33). Recurrent idioms include the prohibition of retaliation `κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἀποδιδόναι` (ROM 12:17; 1TH 5:15; 1PE 3:9) and phrases with `ποιέω` or `πράσσω` (`τὸ κακὸν ποιῇς`, `ποιοῦντας κακά`, `ὅσα κακὰ ... ἐποίησεν`). MAT 21:41 pairs the adjective with its cognate adverb (`Κακοὺς κακῶς ἀπολέσει`) for rhetorical emphasis.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To take someone along as a companion or in custody, take someone to oneself, or receive transmitted teaching and tradition.

senses.definition: To take someone along with oneself on a journey, aside in private, under one's authority, or into custody; in the passive, to be taken away or along.
senses.grammatical_frame: active or passive verb + personal direct object (often with εἰς + acc or κατ' ἰδίαν)

senses.definition: To take a wife into one's home in marriage, or to welcome and take disciples to oneself.
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb + personal direct object (sometimes with πρὸς ἐμαυτόν)

senses.definition: To receive an authoritative message, teaching, or tradition passed down from a source (and by extension, to receive Christ as proclaimed).
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb + direct object (often with ἀπό or παρά + genitive of source)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In Gospel narratives, frequently appears as a circumstantial participle (παραλαβών / παραλαβόντες) paired with a main verb of motion or speech to indicate bringing companions along or taking them aside privately (often with κατ' ἰδίαν). In the epistles, regularly pairs with παραδίδωμι (1CO 11:23; 1CO 15:3) and takes ἀπό or παρά + genitive of the source from whom teaching or tradition is received.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A necessity, requirement, or state of lacking resources, assistance, or a needed action.

senses.definition: A requirement or necessity for some item, person, or action, most often expressed in the verb phrase χρείαν ἔχω with a genitive complement, infinitive, or ἵνα clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun as direct object of ἔχω, with genitive noun/pronoun, infinitive, or ἵνα clause

senses.definition: A condition of poverty, want, or practical lack of food, supplies, or support, used either absolutely with ἔχω or independently in singular or plural.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun used absolutely with ἔχω or independently as subject/object/dative complement

senses.definition: A particular situation or moment that calls for an appropriate response.
senses.grammatical_frame: Genitive singular noun dependent on πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν

entries.collocations_and_notes: Strongly idiomatic with ἔχω (`χρείαν ἔχω`), occurring both with negation (`οὐ χρείαν ἔχω`) and in rhetorical questions (`τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν ...;`). Syntactic complements of `χρείαν ἔχω` include genitive nouns/pronouns (MAT 26:65; LUK 19:34; HEB 10:36), simple or articular infinitives (MAT 3:14; MAT 14:16; 1TH 4:9; HEB 5:12), and `ἵνα` purpose/content clauses (JHN 16:30; REV 21:23). Without `ἔχω`, it appears as object of `πληρόω` (PHP 4:19) and dative complement of `ὑπηρετέω` (ACT 20:34) and `κοινωνέω` (ROM 12:13). In EPH 4:29, `πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χρείας` functions as a prepositional phrase denoting whatever constructive speech the situation calls for.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A preposition and temporal conjunction marking a limit or boundary in time, space, or degree.

senses.definition: Marking a temporal endpoint or boundary up to which an action or state continues, or a time span within which an event is completed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a genitive noun, time expression, or substantivized adverb

senses.definition: Marking a spatial boundary, geographical limit, or extreme degree reached by an action or object.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a genitive place name, pronoun, or noun of extent

senses.definition: Introducing a subordinate clause that specifies the event or point in time at which the main action ends or changes.
senses.grammatical_frame: Conjunction (alone or as ἄχρι οὗ / ἄχρις ἂν) introducing a clause with subjunctive, future, aorist, or imperfect indicative

senses.definition: Introducing a subordinate clause that marks continuous duration throughout an ongoing condition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Conjunction (ἄχρις οὗ) with a present indicative verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in the form `ἄχρις` before a vowel (GAL 3:19; HEB 3:13). Frequently pairs with `ἀπό` to mark a full span (`ἀπὸ ... ἄχρι ...` in MRK 16:99; PHP 1:5). Fixed temporal expressions include `ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης` (ACT 2:29; ACT 23:1), `ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν` (ROM 8:22; PHP 1:5), and `ἄχρι τοῦ δεῦρο` (ROM 1:13). In ACT 20:6 (`ἄχρι ἡμερῶν πέντε`), the genitive plural of duration indicates arriving within a five-day span. As a conjunction, it commonly combines with the genitive relative `οὗ` (`ἄχρι οὗ`, `ἄχρις οὗ`), taking subjunctive, aorist, imperfect, or present indicative depending on whether the boundary is prospective, past, or ongoing (HEB 3:13).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Spatially or figuratively in front of or in the presence of someone or something; ahead in position, direction, or rank.

senses.definition: In front of, ahead of, or in the physical or metaphorical presence and sight of a person, object, assembly, tribunal, or God.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive

senses.definition: Superior in rank, status, or precedence to another (contrasted with ὀπίσω and explained by πρῶτος).
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (with γίνομαι)

senses.definition: Forward or ahead in space or course; when substantivized with the neuter article, the space ahead or the things that lie ahead.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb, or substantivized with neuter singular/plural article

entries.collocations_and_notes: Contrasted with ὀπίσω in both rank (JHN 1:15, JHN 1:30) and spatial/goal orientation (PHP 3:13). Frequently occurs with τοῦ Θεοῦ or τοῦ Πατρός to express doing or experiencing something in God's sight or presence (MAT 10:32; MAT 18:14; ACT 10:4; 1TH 1:3; 1TH 3:9).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An inner response ranging from alarm, dread, or anxiety before danger to awe at divine power or reverent respect toward authorities and God.

senses.definition: Alarm, terror, dread, or anxiety triggered by perceived threat, hostile people, punishment, or death (including the plural for internal anxieties, and metonymically for intimidation in 1PE 3:14).
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (singular or plural; often with διά + acc, ἀπό + gen, or genitive of thing/person feared)

senses.definition: Profound awe or astonishment evoked by miraculous events or manifestations of divine power.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (subject of γίνομαι or ἐπιπίπτω; cognate accusative with φοβέομαι; genitive with πίμπλημι)

senses.definition: Deep reverence, respectful deference, or careful caution shown toward God, rulers, masters, or spiritual peril.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (often with ἐν or μετά + genitive; paired with τρόμος)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often paired with τρόμος in the phrase μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου (2CO 7:15; EPH 6:5) to mark earnest, humble obedience or reception. Appears with ἀπό or διά to indicate cause (ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου, διὰ τὸν φόβον), with an objective genitive indicating what is feared (τῶν Ἰουδαίων, θανάτου, τοῦ βασανισμοῦ), and as a cognate accusative with φοβέομαι (MRK 4:41; 1PE 3:14).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Deliverance, rescue, or preservation from danger, destruction, or sin, often denoting God's ultimate spiritual rescue.

senses.definition: Physical rescue, survival, or preservation of life from danger, oppression, or catastrophe.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (accusative object of verb, or object of prepositions εἰς / πρός + genitive)

senses.definition: Divine deliverance from sin, judgment, or destruction, encompassing the resulting state of eternal blessing and restoration with God.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (nominative subject, accusative after εἰς denoting goal/result, or genitive modifier)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently governed by εἰς to mark outcome or purpose (δύναμις... εἰς σωτηρίαν, μετάνοιαν εἰς σωτηρίαν, αὐξηθῆτε εἰς σωτηρίαν). Also occurs in recurring genitive phrases such as ἡμέρα σωτηρίας, γνῶσιν σωτηρίας, ἐλπίδα σωτηρίας, αἴτιος σωτηρίας αἰωνίου, and κέρας σωτηρίας. In PHP 1:19, εἰς σωτηρίαν may carry dual nuance of Paul's deliverance from imprisonment and his ultimate spiritual vindication.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To go after or chase physically, to harass or oppress people out of hostility, or to strive earnestly toward a virtue or goal.

senses.definition: To follow or run after someone in physical pursuit.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb in command/prohibition paired with ἀπέρχομαι

senses.definition: To harass, oppress, or pursue with hostility, often involving driving people from place to place or subjecting them to violence on account of faith or message.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb + accusative of person or group (also passive, or absolute with contextually implied object)

senses.definition: To strive earnestly after, practice, or press forward toward a moral quality, course of action, or prize.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb + accusative of virtue, practice, or state; or intransitive with κατά / εἰς + accusative of goal or prize

entries.collocations_and_notes: When taking a personal direct object, διώκω predominantly denotes hostile mistreatment or persecution (JHN 5:16, ACT 9:5, GAL 1:13), sometimes explicitly involving physical expulsion from town to town (MAT 23:34, ACT 26:11). When taking an abstract virtue, practice, or goal, it denotes deliberate moral or athletic striving (ROM 12:13, 1CO 14:1, PHP 3:14), contrasted with φεύγω in 1TI 6:11 and paired with ζητέω in 1PE 3:11.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Severe external hardship, oppression, or calamity, as well as inward emotional anguish or bodily pain.

senses.definition: External hardship, adversity, oppression, or severe calamity arising from persecution, famine, poverty, social vulnerability, or divine judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun used in singular or plural, often with ἐν, διά, εἰς, or as object of ἔχω

senses.definition: Inward emotional anguish, sorrow of heart, or bodily pain such as that of childbirth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun, paired with λύπη or συνοχὴ καρδίας, or as object of ἐγείρω

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired or listed alongside terms for persecution, distress, famine, poverty, or physical danger, such as διωγμός (MAT 13:21, 2TH 1:4), στενοχωρία (ROM 2:9, ROM 8:35), ἀνάγκη (2CO 6:4), λιμός (ACT 7:11, ROM 8:35), πτωχεία (REV 2:9), and συνοχὴ καρδίας (2CO 2:4). In 2TH 1:6 it occurs with its cognate verb θλίβω in a reciprocal judgment formula, and in ROM 5:3 it is contrasted as producing ὑπομονή.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A step in genealogical descent, the body of people living at the same time, or an extended age or historical period.

senses.definition: A counted step or link in family descent from an ancestor to descendants.
senses.grammatical_frame: Countable noun in genealogical reckoning

senses.definition: The collective body of people living at the same time; one's contemporaries or peers, often addressed or evaluated as a moral group.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular collective noun, frequently with demonstrative αὕτη or adjective of character

senses.definition: A historical era or successive span of time corresponding to a human lifespan, especially in plural expressions denoting past eras or endless succession.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun, often in temporal prepositional phrases (ἐν, εἰς, ἀπό) or dative of time

entries.collocations_and_notes: In the Gospels and Acts, the demonstrative phrase ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη frequently appears with negative moral or spiritual descriptors such as πονηρά, μοιχαλίς, ἄπιστος, διεστραμμένη, ἁμαρτωλός, and σκολιά (MAT 16:4, MAT 17:17, MRK 8:38, ACT 2:40). In LUK 16:8, εἰς τὴν γενεὰν τὴν ἑαυτῶν refers to dealing with one's own contemporaries or peers. In EPH 3:21 and COL 1:26, γενεαί appears alongside αἰῶνες in expressions of sweeping historical or eternal duration, and LUK 1:50 uses the emphatic plural εἰς γενεὰς καὶ γενεάς.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Noun denoting the raising or rising of the dead back to life, and once a metaphorical rising or restoration in contrast to downfall.

senses.definition: The act, event, or state of rising from death back to life, whether of Christ, of individuals restored to life, or of the general raising of the dead.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, frequently modified by genitive νεκρῶν, ἐκ νεκρῶν, or a personal genitive, or serving as object of prepositions (ἐν, περί, ἐξ, εἰς, διά)

senses.definition: A rising up or restoration of people in status or spiritual condition, contrasted directly with downfall (πτῶσις).
senses.grammatical_frame: noun in prepositional phrase εἰς + accusative, coordinated with πτῶσιν ("falling") and modified by subjective genitive πολλῶν

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly qualified by genitives νεκρῶν (MAT 22:31, ACT 17:32, ACT 24:21, ACT 26:23, 1CO 15:12, 1CO 15:21), ἐκ νεκρῶν (ACT 4:2, 1PE 1:3), or personal genitives referring to Christ (ACT 2:31, PHP 3:10, 1PE 1:3). In JHN 11:25, Jesus identifies himself metaphorically/metonymically as ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή (the source and agent of resurrection). In HEB 11:35, the word appears twice in one verse: first of dead persons restored to earthly life, and second modified by κρείττονος ("a better resurrection"). In ACT 17:18, Athenian hearers appear to interpret τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν as unfamiliar entities/deities being proclaimed.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To move closer in space, become imminent in time, or enter into nearness to someone or some condition.

senses.definition: To move physically closer to a place, person, or object; to arrive near a destination or step up to someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb used absolutely, with dative of place or person, or with εἰς + accusative of place

senses.definition: To become imminent or close in time, said of an appointed period, expected event, or divine reign.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with temporal or event subject (used absolutely or with ἐπί + accusative of person)

senses.definition: To enter into close spiritual or relational proximity with God, or of God responding with nearness to worshippers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb + dative of deity or person

senses.definition: To come right up to the threshold of a condition or extremity such as dying.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb + μέχρι + genitive of condition

entries.collocations_and_notes: Constructed with a dative complement for a person, place, or deity (LUK 7:12, LUK 15:25, LUK 22:47, ACT 10:9, HEB 7:19, JAS 4:8), with εἰς + accusative for a city or village (MAT 21:1, MRK 11:1, LUK 18:35, LUK 19:29), with ἐπί + accusative for the arrival of God's reign upon hearers (LUK 10:9), with μέχρι + genitive for coming close to death (PHP 2:30), and absolutely in participial, infinitive, or perfect clauses (MAT 3:2, MAT 26:45, LUK 24:15, ACT 21:33). Frequently used in the perfect tense with ἡ βασιλεία, ἡ ὥρα, ὁ καιρός, or ἡ παρουσία to announce impending arrival.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Temporal adverb meaning at all times, continually, or on every occasion.

senses.definition: Throughout all time without interruption; continuously or perpetually.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying finite verbs, participles, or verbless clauses indicating ongoing state or uninterrupted action

senses.definition: Habitually or regularly on every occasion, especially in recurring practices such as prayer, thanksgiving, or rejoicing.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying verbs or participles of recurring or habitual action

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears with verbs of prayer and thanksgiving (προσεύχομαι, δέομαι, εὐχαριστῶ, μνείαν ποιοῦμαι) as well as rejoicing (χαίρετε) and obedience/endurance. Negated as οὐ πάντοτε ("not always") in MAT 26:11 and MRK 14:7 in direct contrast with positive πάντοτε. Paired with ἐν παντί ("in everything / in every circumstance") in 2CO 9:8. In 1TH 2:16, it stands at the end of an infinitival clause describing continual accumulation of sin.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Noun denoting a temporal end or termination, a final outcome or goal, or a toll/tax payment.

senses.definition: The closing point, cessation, or final consummation of a period, existence, or the present order.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun as subject, object of ἔχω/εἰμί, or object of prepositions ἕως, μέχρι, ἄχρι + genitive

senses.definition: The final limit or full extent, whether temporal ("to the very end") or qualitative ("completely, to the uttermost").
senses.grammatical_frame: noun in the prepositional phrase εἰς + accusative (εἰς τέλος) modifying a verb or participle

senses.definition: The final result, consequence, or intended aim toward which an action, course of life, or instruction leads.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (often with genitive modifier or possessive relative pronoun) as subject or predicate nominative/accusative

senses.definition: An indirect tax, toll, or custom duty levied by ruling authorities.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (singular or plural τέλη) as direct object of verbs of collecting or paying (λαμβάνω, ἀποδίδωμι)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Common prepositional phrases include εἰς τέλος (MAT 10:22, MAT 24:13, MRK 13:13, JHN 13:1, 1TH 2:16), ἕως τέλους (1CO 1:8, 2CO 1:13), μέχρι τέλους (HEB 3:14), and ἄχρι τέλους (HEB 6:11). Explicitly paired as an antonym with ἀρχή ("beginning") in HEB 7:3 and REV 21:6. In ROM 10:4, context allows either "termination/cessation" or "goal/culmination" of the law in Christ. In JHN 13:1 and 1TH 2:16, εἰς τέλος may express either temporal finality ("to the end" / "finally") or degree ("completely" / "to the uttermost"). In tax contexts, plural τέλη pairs with κῆνσον (MAT 17:25) and singular τὸ τέλος pairs with φόρον (ROM 13:7).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Improper preposition and adverb indicating absence, separation, exclusion from a count, or independent placement.

senses.definition: Lacking the presence, accompaniment, involvement, or enabling condition of the person or thing named.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive (occasionally postpositive after relative pronoun, or predicate with εἰμί)

senses.definition: Excluded from a count or mentioned in addition to other items or burdens.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + genitive expressing exclusion from a tally or addition to a list

senses.definition: Placed apart or in a separate location by itself rather than together with other items.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying a participle of physical position/arrangement

entries.collocations_and_notes: Governs the genitive in 24 of the 25 sampled verses; once follows a relative pronoun (οὗ χωρίς, HEB 12:14) and once serves as predicate with εἰμί + genitive (HEB 12:8). Frequently appears in negations ("without X, nothing / impossible / dead / none"), e.g., MAT 13:34, MRK 4:34, JHN 15:5, PHM 1:14, HEB 9:22, HEB 11:6, HEB 12:14, or in double negation οὐ χωρίς ("not without", HEB 7:20). Contrasts directly with μετά + genitive ("with") in JHN 20:7 when used adverbially.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To shed tears, cry aloud in grief or distress, or mourn for someone.

senses.definition: To shed tears and express sorrow, remorse, or lamentation audibly, either generally or over a person or calamity.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive active, often absolute, or with an adverb (πικρῶς), ἐπί + accusative/dative (object of sorrow), or μετά + genitive (companions in grief)

senses.definition: To weep over or mourn the loss of specific persons.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive active with an accusative object of the person mourned

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly paired with verbs of mourning, lamenting, and wailing such as πενθέω (LUK 6:25; JAS 4:8; REV 18:15), κόπτομαι (LUK 8:52; REV 18:9), θρηνέω (LUK 7:32), and ὀλολύζω (JAS 5:1), and directly contrasted with γελάω (LUK 6:21, 6:25) and χαίρω (ROM 12:15; 1CO 7:30). Modified by πικρῶς ("bitterly") in MAT 26:75 and LUK 22:62, and explicitly linked with shedding tears (δάκρυσιν) in LUK 7:38.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To credit or count something to someone's account, classify someone as having a status, consider or judge a matter, think/reason, or intend to act.

senses.definition: To credit, reckon, or charge something (such as righteousness or guilt) to someone, or to count and classify someone or something as having a particular status.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle/deponent transitive with accusative and dative; or passive with dative of recipient/person affected, often with εἰς + accusative, μετά + genitive, or ὡς + nominative

senses.definition: To engage in reasoning, reflection, or focused mental consideration.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle/deponent intransitive (absolute) or transitive with a neuter pronoun object (τι, ταῦτα)

senses.definition: To consider, suppose, take into account, or regard someone or a situation as being of a certain character.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle/deponent with a ὅτι clause, accusative + infinitive (εἶναι), accusative + ὡς + noun/participle, or εἰς + accusative

senses.definition: To plan, decide, or intend to undertake an action.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle/deponent with a complementary infinitive (τολμῆσαι)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the passive with a dative of the person and εἰς + accusative (especially δικαιοσύνην in ROM 4:3, 4:5, 4:9, 4:22; GAL 3:6; JAS 2:23) to express divine reckoning or status attribution. In 1CO 13:11 it stands alongside λαλέω and φρονέω as a basic cognitive/verbal faculty. In 2CO 10:2 it occurs twice with distinct syntactic frames: first with a complementary infinitive (intention) and second with accusative + ὡς + participle (evaluation).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To suffer or undergo pain, mistreatment, hardship, harm, or death.

senses.definition: To endure pain, affliction, persecution, or death, often for a cause or on someone's behalf.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive active (often absolute or as an articular infinitive), with ὑπό + genitive (agent), ὑπέρ + genitive (sake/behalf), διά + accusative (reason), or dative of respect (σαρκί)

senses.definition: To undergo or experience specific hardships, injuries, or adverse events (or, potentially in GAL 3:4, notable experiences generally).
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive active with a neuter pronoun/adjective object (πολλά, ὅσα, τοσαῦτα, οὐδὲν κακόν, or relative ὧν), often with ἀπό/ὑπό + genitive (agent)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in Gospel passion predictions with ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ("be rejected") and ἀποκτανθῆναι ("be killed"), and in the articular infinitive (LUK 22:15; ACT 1:3) or absolute aorist (LUK 24:46; HEB 13:12; 1PE 2:21) serves as a summary term for Christ's passion and death. Often accompanied by ὑπέρ + genitive (on behalf of someone or for a cause) or διά + accusative. Note that in GAL 3:4 (τοσαῦτα ἐπάθετε εἰκῇ), the single sentence in the sample does not clarify whether τοσαῦτα refers to hardships or more general experiences, though every other occurrence in the packet denotes negative affliction or harm.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To remain over as a surplus, exist or increase in great measure, have plenty, or cause something to abound lavishly.

senses.definition: To remain over after consumption or needs have been satisfied; to be left over as surplus.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, commonly as a neuter articular participle (τὸ περισσεῦον / τὰ περισσεύσαντα) with partitive genitive or dative of possessor

senses.definition: To exist in great measure, grow substantially, overflow, or exceed a comparative standard (such as righteousness, numbers, joy, or comfort).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with inanimate or abstract subject, often with dative of respect, εἰς + accusative, or comparative πλεῖον + genitive

senses.definition: To possess more than enough, live in plenty, or excel and be richly active in a virtue, attitude, or task.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with personal subject, frequently with ἐν + dative, εἰς + accusative, or adverb μᾶλλον

senses.definition: To be provided with an abundant excess beyond what one already possesses.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive verb with personal subject (implied recipient of what is given)

senses.definition: To cause something to abound or multiply; to bestow a gift or quality lavishly upon someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive active verb with accusative object (or attracted relative pronoun ἧς) and εἰς + accusative of recipient or goal

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in contrast with ὑστερέω ('lack, fall short') or πεινάω ('be hungry') in 1CO 8:8 and PHP 4:12, and with the cognate noun περισσεία ('abundance') in 2CO 8:2. Often takes ἐν + dative to specify the sphere of abundance (e.g., hope, the Lord's work, thanksgiving) or εἰς + accusative to mark the resulting goal or recipients. In 2CO 9:8, the verb occurs twice in one sentence: first transitively ('cause all grace to abound to you') and then intransitively ('abound for every good work'). In EPH 1:8, ἧς shows relative attraction to its antecedent (grace) for an expected accusative object.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To carry out, perform, or habitually practice actions (often morally evaluated), to fare in a certain way, or to collect payments.

senses.definition: To carry out, commit, or habitually engage in specific deeds, behaviors, or standards of conduct (frequently evaluated as good, wicked, rash, or deserving punishment).
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive active (or periphrastic passive with dative of agent) with an accusative object (neuter pronoun/adjective, ἔργον, νόμον, or relative clause)

senses.definition: To act or conduct oneself in opposition to a decree or authority.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive active with a prepositional phrase (ἀπέναντι + genitive)

senses.definition: To be in a favorable condition or experience a good outcome (used with the adverb εὖ in an epistolary closing).
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive active with an adverb of manner (εὖ)

senses.definition: To collect or exact money, fees, or interest owed.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive active with an accusative object denoting money or an appointed amount (ἀργύριον, μηδὲν πλέον)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes evaluative neuter plural objects (e.g., τὰ τοιαῦτα, φαῦλα, ἄξιον θανάτου, κακόν, ἀγαθόν) to denote habitual or morally significant conduct. Occasionally contrasted or paired with ποιέω (JHN 5:29; ROM 1:32; ROM 7:19). In ACT 15:29, the idiom εὖ πράξετε appears as a closing wish in a letter. In LUK 3:13 and LUK 19:23, the financial context indicates collecting money or interest.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To express gratitude or give thanks to God or a human benefactor, including offering a prayer of thanks over food or drink before eating or distributing it.

senses.definition: To express gratitude or render thanks to God or a person for benefits, answered prayer, or the condition of others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb used with a dative recipient (or absolutely), often with περί or ὑπέρ + genitive, ἐπί + dative, or a ὅτι clause

senses.definition: To offer a spoken prayer of thanks to God over bread, a cup, or other food prior to breaking, distributing, or eating it.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb (typically aorist participle or finite verb) used absolutely or with dative τῷ Θεῷ in meal contexts

senses.definition: To be acknowledged with thanksgiving by others (of a gracious gift or deliverance).
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive verb with the gracious gift (χάρισμα) as subject and διά + genitive indicating the agents of thanksgiving

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes a dative recipient (most often τῷ Θεῷ or τῷ Πατρί), paired with περί or ὑπέρ plus the genitive for the person or matter thanked for, ἐπί plus the dative for the occasion, διά plus the genitive for an intermediary (such as Jesus Christ), and a ὅτι clause stating the reason. Often modified by temporal adverbs of frequency such as πάντοτε ('always') or ἀδιαλείπτως ('without ceasing'). In meal narratives, the aorist participle εὐχαριστήσας regularly stands between λαβών ('having taken') and ἔκλασεν/ἔδωκεν ('broke/gave').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A strong internal longing or craving, ranging from earnest affectionate wish to self-indulgent, forbidden, or morally corrupt appetite.

senses.definition: An earnest, deeply felt longing or affectionate desire to do something or see someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in the dative singular (cognate instrumental with ἐπιθυμέω or governed by ἐν πολλῇ)

senses.definition: A disordered, self-centered, or forbidden craving, appetite, or coveting that drives sinful behavior and resists divine order.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (frequently plural), often modified by a genitive of source or object (e.g., σαρκός, ὀφθαλμῶν) or evaluative adjectives

entries.collocations_and_notes: In LUK 22:15, the dative singular is paired with the cognate verb ἐπεθύμησα to intensify the statement ('with earnest desire I desired'). Most occurrences are plural and appear in vice lists or moral warnings, commonly paired with genitives such as σαρκός ('of the flesh'), ὀφθαλμῶν ('of the eyes'), ἀπάτης ('of deceit'), μιασμοῦ ('of defilement'), or with adjectives like κακή ('evil'), κοσμικαί ('worldly'), νεωτερικαί ('youthful'), and ἀνόητοι καὶ βλαβεραί ('foolish and harmful'). Frequently governed by κατά + accusative with verbs of walking or living (πορεύομαι, ἀναστρέφομαι).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To place someone or something under another's authority or control, and in middle/passive usage to be brought under control or to submit oneself obediently.

senses.definition: To place or bring persons, cosmic powers, or the created order under the authority, control, or rule of another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive verb with accusative direct object and dative of the ruler or ὑπό/ὑποκάτω + foot phrase

senses.definition: To be brought under the power, authority, or orderly control of another (of creation, all things, spirits, or supernatural beings).
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive verb with dative of the controlling authority or used absolutely

senses.definition: To submit oneself willingly or yield obedience to parents, governing authorities, household leaders, fellow believers, God, or God's law.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle/passive verb (often imperative, infinitive, or participle) with dative of the person, institution, or standard (or ἀλλήλοις)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Active forms focus on the superior agent (chiefly God or Christ) placing all things or creation under an appointed ruler, frequently using the spatial idiom ὑπὸ / ὑποκάτω τοὺς πόδας / τῶν ποδῶν ('under the feet'). Middle/passive forms regularly govern a dative of the person, spiritual power, institution, or divine standard to which one yields or is subjected; in household and civic instructions (COL 3:18, TIT 2:9, TIT 3:1, ROM 13:1, 1PE 2:18, 1PE 3:1), imperatives and participles call for voluntary subordination.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To desire, be willing, or deliberately intend and decide to do something.

senses.definition: To have an inclination, desire, or willingness toward an action or outcome.
senses.grammatical_frame: Deponent verb; takes a complementary infinitive, a subjunctive without conjunction (JHN 18:39), or stands with an understood infinitive (LUK 22:42, 3JN 1:10)

senses.definition: To form a deliberate purpose, choose, decide, or direct as an act of settled will or authority.
senses.grammatical_frame: Deponent verb; takes a complementary infinitive, accusative + infinitive (1TI 5:14), accusative pronoun (2CO 1:17), or stands absolutely in relative/conditional clauses (MAT 11:27, 1CO 12:11, JAS 3:4)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Almost always takes a complementary infinitive. In MAT 1:19 and LUK 22:42 it appears alongside θέλω / θέλημα ("will, desire"), and in 2CO 1:17 alongside the cognate verb βουλεύομαι ("plan") and noun context of decision-making. The imperfect ἐβουλόμην in ACT 25:22 and PHM 1:13 expresses a polite or unfulfilled inclination ("I was wanting / I would like"). In epistolary disclosure formulas (PHP 1:12: γινώσκειν δὲ ὑμᾶς βούλομαι) and apostolic directives (1TI 5:14), it states the writer's earnest wish or instruction.

entries.core_meaning_summary: First-person singular reflexive pronoun referring back to the speaker as object, recipient, source, or possessor.

senses.definition: Refers back to the first-person singular subject as the direct target, beneficiary, or internal frame of reference of an action or thought.
senses.grammatical_frame: First-person singular reflexive pronoun in accusative (direct object, sometimes with predicate noun/adjective or infinitive) or dative (recipient, advantage, or reference with verbs such as δοκέω and σύνοιδα)

senses.definition: Identifies the speaker as the object of a spatial, relational, or topical preposition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Reflexive pronoun governed by prepositions (ὑπό, πρός, εἰς + accusative; περί + genitive)

senses.definition: Indicates the speaker as an independent, self-originating source of speech or action, routinely negated to express dependence on God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Genitive reflexive pronoun governed by prepositions of source (ἀπό, ἐκ)

senses.definition: Denotes personal ownership or self-interest pertaining strictly to the speaker.
senses.grammatical_frame: Genitive reflexive pronoun placed in attributive position between article and substantivized adjective (τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ σύμφορον)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs only in oblique cases (genitive ἐμαυτοῦ, dative ἐμαυτῷ, accusative ἐμαυτόν), always referring back to the first-person singular speaker ("I"). In John's Gospel, the negated prepositional phrases ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ and ἐξ ἐμαυτοῦ repeatedly contrast self-originated speech or action with being sent and instructed by the Father (JHN 7:17, 8:42, 12:49, 14:10). With σύνοιδα (1CO 4:4), the dative expresses self-awareness regarding one's own conduct.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Evaluates an action, condition, speech, or arrangement as proper, skillful, accurate, honorable, or physically well.

senses.definition: In a good, skillful, honorable, proper, or commendable manner with respect to deeds, conduct, construction, or arrangement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying verbs or participles of action, management, or condition (frequently καλῶς ποιέω)

senses.definition: Accurately, truthfully, fittingly, or capably in speaking, prophesying, or answering, or standing alone as an expression of agreement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying verbs of speaking/answering/praying, or standing independently as an affirmative response

senses.definition: With praise or favorable words when speaking about someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb with εἶπον + accusative of the person spoken about

senses.definition: In good physical health; recovered from illness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb in the idiom καλῶς ἔχω

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently collocates with ποιέω (MAT 12:12, MRK 7:37, 1CO 7:38, PHP 4:14, JAS 2:19, 2PE 1:19, often introducing a participle of the commendable action) and with verbs of speaking (εἶπον, λέγω, λαλέω, ἀπεκρίθη, προφητεύω). Contrasts with κακῶς in JHN 18:23 and is paired with comparative κρεῖσσον in 1CO 7:38. The set phrase καλῶς ἔχω in MRK 16:18 expresses physical recovery.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To speak proudly, boast, or take confident pride and exultation in someone or something, whether legitimately in God and Christ or improperly in human status and achievements.

senses.definition: To boast, brag, or speak with pride about oneself, another person, external distinctions, or even one's weaknesses.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle verb; used absolutely, with accusative of content, or with ἐν + dative, ὑπέρ + genitive, κατά + accusative, or εἰς + accusative

senses.definition: To exult, rejoice, or place confident pride in God, Christ, the cross, hope of glory, or spiritual exaltation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle verb with ἐν + dative or ἐπί + dative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Almost exclusively middle/deponent in these contexts (with aorist passive-form or middle forms; note active-looking 1st aorist middle καυχήσωνται/καυχήσασθαι). Takes a wide range of prepositional complements to mark the ground or target of pride: ἐν + dative (most common), ἐπί + dative (ROM 5:2), ὑπέρ + genitive (2CO 7:14, 2CO 9:2, 2CO 12:5), κατά + accusative (2CO 11:18), and εἰς + accusative (2CO 10:13, 2CO 10:15). The OT citation pattern Ὁ καυχώμενος ἐν Κυρίῳ καυχάσθω occurs in both 1CO 1:31 and 2CO 10:17. Frequently paired with cognates καύχημα and καύχησις (2CO 5:12, 2CO 7:14).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The physical rite or bodily state of circumcision, used by extension for inward spiritual transformation and collectively for the circumcised people.

senses.definition: The physical ritual of removing the foreskin as practiced under ancestral and Mosaic law, or the resulting bodily state and status of being circumcised.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; direct object of verbs of giving or receiving (δίδωμι, λαμβάνω), in genitive phrases (διαθήκη περιτομῆς, σημεῖον περιτομῆς), or with ἐν + dative to express condition

senses.definition: A figurative, non-physical inward renewal and stripping away of the fleshly nature, contrasted with outward bodily circumcision.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; modified by genitive (καρδίας, τοῦ Χριστοῦ) or dative of manner/means (ἀχειροποιήτῳ) with the verb περιτέμνω

senses.definition: A collective designation for circumcised people (specifically Jews or Jewish believers in Christ), and in one transferred instance applied to believers worshipping by the Spirit of God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, usually articular (ἡ περιτομή) or in prepositional phrases (οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς, εἰς τὴν περιτομήν)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired and contrasted with ἀκροβυστία ("uncircumcision") in Pauline letters (e.g., ROM 2:25–26, 4:9–10, 1CO 7:19, GAL 5:6, 6:15, COL 3:11). Associated with Moses, the fathers, and the eighth day (JHN 7:22, ACT 7:8), and described as "sign" (σημεῖον) and part of a "covenant" (διαθήκη, ACT 7:8, ROM 4:11). Contrastive qualifiers distinguish physical/outward circumcision ("in the flesh", "in the visible realm", "made by hands") from inward/spiritual circumcision ("of the heart, in spirit not letter", "not made by hands", "of Christ"). In the collective sense, the idiom οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς ("those of the circumcision") designates Jewish people or Jewish-background believers (ACT 10:45, GAL 2:12, COL 4:11).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Direct address or communion with God in petition and devotion, and by extension a recognized place or gathering for praying.

senses.definition: The act, practice, or spoken expression of addressing God in petition, intercession, or sustained devotion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, singular or plural; occurs with ἐν + dative, as dative object of verbs of persistence (προσκαρτερέω, προσμένω), in genitive modifiers (οἶκος προσευχῆς, ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν), and in cognate dative with προσεύχομαι (JAS 5:17)

senses.definition: A designated site or regular gathering where people assemble to pray.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun; predicate/subject of εἶναι in indirect statement (ACT 16:13) and object of motion preposition εἰς (ACT 16:16)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently governed by προσκαρτερέω ("devote oneself steadily to"; ACT 1:14, 2:42, 6:4, ROM 12:12, COL 4:2) and προσμένω (1TI 5:5), and paired with δέησις ("petition/entreaty"; EPH 6:18, 1TI 5:5) and ἐλεημοσύναι ("alms"; ACT 10:4, 31). Appears in the fixed phrase οἶκος προσευχῆς ("house of prayer"; MAT 21:13, LUK 19:46) and μνείαν ποιούμενος ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν ("making mention during my/our prayers"; EPH 1:16, 1TH 1:2, PHM 1:4). In REV 5:8 and 8:3, prayers of the saints are associated with incense on the heavenly altar. In ACT 16:13 and 16:16, the term designates a specific site or regular gathering outside the city gate by a river where people assembled on the sabbath.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A person or deity who observes, confirms, or publicly testifies to the truth of events, words, or conduct, ranging from legal verification to proclamation of Christ and solemn oaths.

senses.definition: A person who provides corroborating testimony or is present to verify a legal charge, statement, or public commitment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (often plural, in genitive after prepositions or nouns of need, e.g., χρείαν ἔχομεν + genitive, ἐπὶ στόματος + genitive, ἐνώπιον + genitive)

senses.definition: An eyewitness or authorized proclaimer who bears public testimony to Jesus's deeds, sufferings, resurrection, or prophetic message, including one killed in connection with that testimony.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (frequently predicate nominative with genitive or dative of the person or events attested, and πρός + accusative for the audience)

senses.definition: God or a human audience invoked in a solemn affirmation as guarantor and confirmer of the speaker's truthfulness or sincerity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (predicate nominative with ἐστίν or verbless clause, or accusative object of ἐπικαλοῦμαι; often with genitive of the speaker)

senses.definition: Figuratively, a surrounding observer or exemplar viewed as watching believers run a race of endurance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (genitive plural after νέφος in an athletic metaphor)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs as a predicate noun with εἰμί (sometimes omitted in brief oaths, e.g., PHP 1:8, 1TH 2:5) taking a genitive of the person or facts attested, and in Acts with πρός + accusative for the audience addressed (ACT 13:31, ACT 22:15). In 2CO 1:23, it is the predicate object of ἐπικαλοῦμαι ('call upon God as witness'). In REV 1:5 and REV 3:14, ὁ μάρτυς ὁ πιστός serves as a title for Jesus Christ. In ACT 22:20, Stephen is called Στεφάνου τοῦ μάρτυρός σου in the immediate context of his blood being shed during execution.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A spatial, temporal, and relational marker indicating position or direction behind someone or something, or following after a leader in discipleship or allegiance.

senses.definition: Indicates a physical location behind someone or movement in a backward direction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb (alone or in the prepositional phrase εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω) or improper preposition + genitive

senses.definition: Indicates following after a person, leader, or impulse as a disciple, supporter, or adherent.
senses.grammatical_frame: Improper preposition + genitive of person or abstract entity, with verbs of motion or following

senses.definition: Indicates coming after another person in temporal order of appearance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Improper preposition + genitive of person, with ἔρχομαι

senses.definition: Figuratively refers to past achievements and experiences left behind, or to turning back and withdrawing from prior commitment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized adverb (τὰ ὀπίσω as direct object, or in εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of motion and discipleship (δεῦτε, ἔρχομαι, ἀπέρχομαι, ἀκολουθέω, πορεύομαι, ἐκτρέπομαι). Contrasts directly with ἔμπροσθεν ('before/in front of') in JHN 1:15, JHN 1:30, and PHP 3:13. In MRK 8:33, Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ uses the spatial command ('get behind me / out of my way') as a sharp rebuke. Substantivized with the article (τὰ ὀπίσω, εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω), it denotes either physical backward direction or turning back from commitment.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An affirmative particle expressing agreement, emphatic confirmation, or reliable assent ('yes', 'indeed').

senses.definition: Expresses direct agreement, assent, or acknowledgment in answer to a question or preceding remark.
senses.grammatical_frame: Response particle (standing alone or with a vocative/clarifying clause)

senses.definition: Serves as an emphatic or confirmatory particle reinforcing a declaration, rhetorical question, prayer, or earnest appeal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial discourse particle (often preceding λέγω ὑμῖν, vocatives, commands, or requests)

senses.definition: Denotes an affirmative statement, commitment, or reliable pledge when quoted or substantivized, typically contrasted with οὔ ('no').
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable noun/quoted word (often with neuter article τό)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly paired with a vocative (Ναί, Κύριε; ναί, ὁ Πατήρ; ναί, ἀδελφέ) in replies and prayers, with λέγω ὑμῖν (MAT 11:9; LUK 7:26; LUK 12:5) to underscore a point, and with ἀμήν in liturgical affirmation (REV 1:7). In ethical and theological discourse regarding truthfulness (MAT 5:37; 2CO 1:17–19; JAS 5:12), it is repeatedly paired in direct antithesis with οὔ ('no') and can be substantivized with the neuter article τό.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To suffer physical illness or infirmity, or more broadly to lack strength, power, capability, or firm conviction.

senses.definition: To experience bodily illness, disease, or physical infirmity (frequently used as a substantival participle for sick persons).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb or substantival participle

senses.definition: To lack strength, power, authority, or capability; to be weak, vulnerable, or in need.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb or participle (sometimes with ἐν + dative or διά + genitive)

senses.definition: To be tentative, scrupulous, or lacking firm assurance in faith or conscience, especially concerning religious scruples.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb or participle (with dative of respect τῇ πίστει or modifying συνείδησις)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In narrative contexts (Gospels, Acts, Philippians, 2 Timothy), it consistently denotes bodily illness, often appearing as a substantival participle (οἱ ἀσθενοῦντες, ὁ ἀσθενῶν) alongside θεραπεύω and νόσοι (MAT 10:8; ACT 19:12) or leading to death (ACT 9:37; PHP 2:27). In Paul's letters, it frequently contrasts with power or boldness (δυνατός, δυνατέω, δύναμις, τολμάω in 2CO 11:21; 12:10; 13:3–4) and ἀδύνατον (ROM 8:3). In ACT 20:35, τῶν ἀσθενούντων occurs in the context of hard labor and generosity, likely encompassing the physically frail as well as the economically or socially vulnerable.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A person, group, or spiritual being standing in active hostility or opposition, or being hostile and estranged in attitude or relationship.

senses.definition: A personal, social, military, or spiritual adversary who opposes, hates, or seeks to harm another person, people, or ruler.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival masculine noun (singular or plural, often with possessive genitive)

senses.definition: Hostile in disposition or estranged in relationship; an opponent of a person, deity, or moral and religious principle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicative adjective/noun or substantival noun with objective genitive or dative of respect

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often paired or contrasted with terms of affection, kinship, and friendship: contrasted with πλησίον (MAT 5:43), ἀγαπητοί (ROM 11:28), ἀδελφόν (2TH 3:15), and φίλος (JAS 4:4), and associated with μισέω (MAT 5:43; LUK 1:71; LUK 6:27) and διώκω (MAT 5:44). Repeatedly occurs in the Psalm-citation formula θῶ/τεθῶσιν τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου/αὐτοῦ ὑποκάτω/ὑποπόδιον/ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας (MAT 22:44; MRK 12:36; LUK 20:43; ACT 2:35; 1CO 15:25; HEB 10:13). Used with the definite article in the singular for the spiritual adversary/devil (MAT 13:25, 39; LUK 10:19).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Openness, plainness of speech, fearless boldness in action or proclamation, or unashamed confidence before God or others.

senses.definition: Plain, direct, and unambiguous speech, contrasted with veiled or figurative language.
senses.grammatical_frame: Dative noun (bare or after ἐν) modifying verbs of speaking or declaring

senses.definition: Public visibility and unhidden conduct or speech, contrasted with acting in secret.
senses.grammatical_frame: Dative noun (bare or after ἐν) modifying verbs of speaking, walking, or being

senses.definition: Fearless courage and outspoken frankness in speaking, teaching, or exercising authority despite threats, opposition, or low status.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun as direct object or after μετά + genitive / ἐν + dative, often modified by πᾶς or πολύς

senses.definition: Inner assurance, steadfast confidence, or unashamed freedom of approach toward God, Christ, or a community.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (commonly object of ἔχω, κατέχω, or after μετά + genitive), often paired with πρός + accusative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in adverbial constructions: bare dative (`παρρησίᾳ`), `ἐν παρρησίᾳ`, and `μετὰ (πάσης) παρρησίας`, especially with verbs of speaking (`λαλέω`, `εἶπον`, `ἀπαγγέλλω`, `γνωρίζω`, `διδάσκω`). Contrasts explicitly with `ἐν κρυπτῷ` ("in secret", JHN 7:4; 18:20), `ἐν παροιμίαις` ("in figures of speech", JHN 16:25, 29), and `αἰσχύνομαι` ("to be put to shame", PHP 1:20; 1JN 2:28). With `ἔχω`, it expresses confident standing before God, Christ, or a community (`πρός`, `ἐν Χριστῷ`, `ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῆς κρίσεως`). In MRK 8:32 and JHN 7:13, plainness/openness and boldness overlap in context.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A contrastive conjunction or preposition indicating opposition, qualification, transition, or exception ("however," "nevertheless," "except").

senses.definition: Introduces a statement, question, or command that qualifies, counters, or corrects what immediately precedes.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial adversative conjunction connecting finite clauses or imperatives

senses.definition: Signals a solemn, climactic declaration, practical summary, or resumptive conclusion following prior discussion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial discourse conjunction introducing declarative assertions or hortatory summaries

senses.definition: Marks a person or item excluded from the scope of a preceding universal or negative statement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun phrase in the genitive case

senses.definition: Introduces the single qualification or overriding fact that remains true despite surrounding circumstances or uncertainty.
senses.grammatical_frame: Conjunction combined with ὅτι (πλὴν ὅτι) introducing a content clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Predominantly stands at the beginning of a clause as a sentence conjunction, frequently in Luke and Matthew. In prepositional use (`πλὴν` + genitive, limited to Acts in this sample), it always follows a universal or negative expression (`πάντες`, `μηδέν`, `οὐδεμία`) to mark the sole exception. In ACT 20:23 and PHP 1:18, the fixed combination `πλὴν ὅτι` introduces a restricting or overriding fact.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An enclitic temporal and generalizing particle denoting an indefinite point in time—most often an unspecified past ("once, formerly"), an unspecified general or future occasion ("ever, at any time"), or, in combination with other particles, culmination ("at last") or apprehension ("perhaps").

senses.definition: At some earlier, unspecified time prior to the present situation.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic adverb modifying past-tense verbs, participles, or substantivized phrases (often contrasted with νῦν/νυνί)

senses.definition: At any unspecified point in time, whether in a rhetorical question, a negative statement, or a future-oriented command.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic adverb in interrogative clauses, negated clauses (with οὐδείς, οὔτε, οὐ μή), or future-oriented clauses

senses.definition: After a period of waiting or delay, marking the arrival or anticipated arrival of an opportunity.
senses.grammatical_frame: collocation ἤδη ποτέ modifying a verb

senses.definition: In combination with μή, expressing an unwanted possibility ("lest perhaps") or an emphatic denial of occurrence at any time ("never").
senses.grammatical_frame: collocation μή ποτε introducing a subjunctive clause of apprehension or an explanatory indicative clause

senses.definition: Added after a qualitative relative adjective to make its reference completely open-ended or indifferent.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic particle following a relative pronoun/adjective (ὁποῖοί ποτε)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in contrast with νῦν or νυνί ("now") to mark a past state versus a present condition (GAL 1:23; EPH 2:13; EPH 5:8; PHM 1:11; 1PE 2:10). Also collocates with ἤδη ("already, now at last") in ROM 1:10 and PHP 4:10, and with negative words (οὐδείς, οὔτε, οὐ μή) to express "never / not at any time". In HEB 9:17, μή ποτε stands in an explanatory ἐπεί clause with an indicative verb, whereas in MAT 25:9 it introduces a hesitant or apprehensive subjunctive clause.

entries.core_meaning_summary: In the active voice, to emit light or shine; in the middle and passive forms, to become visible, appear to an observer, or seem to be a certain way.

senses.definition: To give off light or illuminate surroundings, used of literal light sources, heavenly bodies, day, or figurative spiritual light.
senses.grammatical_frame: active voice, intransitive (subject: light, lamp, sun, or day)

senses.definition: To come into sight, become observable, or present oneself visually before others (including in dreams, in the sky, or publicly).
senses.grammatical_frame: middle/passive voice or aorist passive, intransitive, often + dative of observer or locative phrase

senses.definition: To give a certain impression, look like, be revealed as, or strike someone as being (in judgment or outward appearance).
senses.grammatical_frame: middle/passive voice or aorist passive with predicate adjective, noun, ὡσεί phrase, or impersonal + dative (τί ὑμῖν φαίνεται)
senses.semantic_domain: Cognition and Appearance / Impression and Judgment

entries.collocations_and_notes: Clear voice distinction across the corpus: the active voice is used strictly for emitting light (with subjects such as φῶς, λύχνος, ἥλιος, ἡμέρα), while the middle/passive forms and passive aorist ἐφάνην denote becoming visible, appearing to someone (often with a dative experiencer or κατ’ ὄναρ, "in a dream"), or seeming to be something. In PHP 2:15 (φαίνεσθε ὡς φωστῆρες) and MAT 24:27 (ἡ ἀστραπὴ... φαίνεται), the visible-appearance sense overlaps closely with shining brightly.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A large kinship-based or ancestral subdivision of a people, most commonly one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and more broadly any ethnic group or clan among the peoples of the earth.

senses.definition: One of the twelve ancestral divisions or lineages descending from the sons of Israel, used for identifying heritage, priestly eligibility, or the whole covenant people.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, often in ἐκ φυλῆς + proper name or with δώδεκα / τοῦ Ἰσραήλ
senses.semantic_domain: Kinship and Social Organization / Israelite Lineage

senses.definition: An ethnic community, clan, or population group among the inhabitants of the earth in general.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, in πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς or coordinated in fourfold lists with γλῶσσα, λαός, and ἔθνος

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the fixed phrase αἱ δώδεκα φυλαὶ (τοῦ Ἰσραήλ) and in genealogical identification (ἐκ φυλῆς + tribal name). In Revelation and Matthew 24:30, it also functions both in the plural phrase πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς ("all the tribes/peoples of the earth") and in fourfold universal lists grouping φυλή with λαός ("people"), γλῶσσα ("tongue/language"), and ἔθνος ("nation").

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adverb and improper preposition denoting close proximity in space, imminence in time, or closeness to an impending state or relationship.

senses.definition: Located at a short physical distance from a landmark or person, or figuratively brought into close access and fellowship (contrasted with being far away).
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb/predicate with εἰμί or γίνομαι, or improper preposition + genitive (or dative in ACT 27:8)

senses.definition: Soon to arrive or take place, used of seasons, festivals, appointed times, or awaited events (and in the comparative form ἐγγύτερον, "nearer").
senses.grammatical_frame: predicate adverb with εἰμί (or verbless clause) with temporal or event subject; comparative ἐγγύτερον in ROM 13:11

senses.definition: On the verge of or liable to experience an impending outcome or condition.
senses.grammatical_frame: improper preposition + genitive of an abstract noun (κατάρας, ἀφανισμοῦ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used both independently as a predicate adverb with εἰμί/γίνομαι and as an improper preposition governing the genitive (or dative in ACT 27:8). In EPH 2:13 it is contrasted with μακράν ("far off") to express spiritual/relational nearness, and in ROM 10:8 it describes the immediate accessibility of the message. In PHP 4:5 (ὁ Κύριος ἐγγύς), the elliptical clause may refer either to temporal imminence (the Lord's coming) or relational presence. In ROM 13:11 it occurs in the comparative form ἐγγύτερον ("nearer").

entries.core_meaning_summary: To look forward to future or unseen realities with expectation or desire, and by extension to place confident trust and reliance in a person or source of security.

senses.definition: To anticipate or look forward to a future event, outcome, or unseen reality with desire or expectation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + infinitive, ὅτι-clause, or accusative object; also used absolutely or as passive participle

senses.definition: To place confident reliance, trust, or expectation in a person, deity, or source of security.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + ἐπί + dative/accusative, εἰς + accusative, ἐν + dative, or simple dative (frequently in the perfect tense)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently construed with infinitives or ὅτι-clauses for expected actions/events, and with prepositions (ἐπί + dative or accusative, εἰς + accusative, ἐν + dative) or the dative case for the person or ground of trust (especially God, Christ, his name, Moses, or wealth). In 2CO 1:10, εἰς ὃν ἠλπίκαμεν combines with an ὅτι-clause, bridging personal trust and future expectation. Paired with ἀπεκδέχομαι and contrasted with present sight (βλέπω) in ROM 8:24–25 and HEB 11:1; paired with πιστεύω and ὑπομένω in 1CO 13:7. Noticeably frequent in the perfect tense (ἠλπίκαμεν, ἠλπικότες, etc.) to denote an enduring posture of reliance.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A servant, attendant, agent, or recognized minister who carries out duties or renders practical or spiritual service on behalf of another person, community, or cause.

senses.definition: A household attendant or royal servant who waits at a meal or carries out direct orders.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun used in narrative without genitive modifier

senses.definition: One who voluntarily humbles oneself to serve others or loyally follows and assists a master or teacher.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate nominative or subject noun, commonly with a possessive genitive or possessive pronoun

senses.definition: An authorized representative, instrument, or minister acting on behalf of God, Christ, a message, or another power.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (singular or plural) typically governing a genitive of the person, entity, or message represented

senses.definition: A recognized servant or appointed helper holding a distinct role within a local Christian congregation, grouped alongside overseers (`ἐπίσκοποι`) or given specific character qualifications.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (used of both men and a woman) with a congregational genitive or in institutional lists

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly takes a genitive modifier indicating the person, group, message, or principle served (`Θεοῦ`, `Χριστοῦ`, `ὑμῶν`, `πάντων`, `καινῆς διαθήκης`, `δικαιοσύνης`, `ἁμαρτίας`). In the Synoptics it is contrasted with seeking greatness or first place (`μέγας`, `πρῶτος`) and paired with `ἔσχατος` ("last", MRK 9:35). In ROM 16:1 (`οὖσαν διάκονον τῆς ἐκκλησίας`), grammatical agreement marks a female subject, and the usage sits on the boundary between general congregational service (1b/1c) and a recognized local church role (1d).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Title and designation of the supreme Roman ruler and emperor, both as civil sovereign and as highest judicial authority.

senses.definition: The reigning Roman emperor in his capacity as supreme civil ruler, sovereign king, and recipient of imperial taxes, decrees, and political allegiance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun/title, often anarthrous, in dative of recipient (taxes), genitive of possession (image/inscription/domain), or apposition with personal name (Αὔγουστος)

senses.definition: The Roman emperor specifically as the highest judicial tribunal and final court of appeal for Roman legal cases.
senses.grammatical_frame: Direct object of ἐπικαλοῦμαι ('appeal to'), object of prepositions (εἰς, ἐπί, πρός), or genitive modifying βῆμα ('tribunal')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used without a personal name as an established royal/imperial title (except in LUK 2:1 with Αὐγούστου). Regularly appears in formulas of civic obligation (δοῦναι κῆνσον/φόρον Καίσαρι, τὰ Καίσαρος ἀπόδοτε Καίσαρι) and in legal appeal formulas in Acts (Καίσαρα ἐπικαλεῖσθαι, ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος Καίσαρος). In ACT 25:21 it alternates with ὁ Σεβαστός.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Knowledge, insight, or comprehension, especially spiritual understanding of God, Christ, and salvation, as well as intellectual grasp or considerate discernment.

senses.definition: Intellectual comprehension, claimed insight, or reasoned awareness regarding matters of belief or practice, whether genuine or falsely asserted.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun as object of ἔχω, subject of φυσιοῖ, or qualified by ψευδώνυμος

senses.definition: Spiritual, theological, or experiential knowledge of God, Christ, salvation, or divine truth, including as a Spirit-given gift or Christian virtue.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun often followed by objective or subjective genitive (σωτηρίας, Θεοῦ, Χριστοῦ), or in virtue/gift lists with ἐν or dative

senses.definition: Considerate understanding or practical discernment guiding one's behavior toward another person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrase κατὰ γνῶσιν modifying a participle of conduct

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often paired with σοφία ('wisdom'), λόγος ('speech/message'), πίστις ('faith'), or ἀλήθεια ('truth'). In 1CO 8 it denotes an intellectual grasp of monotheistic liberty that can cause pride (φυσιοῖ) if divorced from love, whereas in Paul's broader letters and Luke-Acts it denotes true saving or spiritual understanding of God and Christ. In 1TI 6:20 it is qualified by ψευδώνυμος ('falsely so named').

entries.core_meaning_summary: Comfort and consolation in distress, earnest exhortation or encouraging instruction, or a specific personal request.

senses.definition: Comfort, consolation, or spiritual relief and encouragement given in the midst of suffering, affliction, or expectation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun frequently paired with θλῖψις/παθήματα as contrast, or with ὑπομονή/χαρά/ἐλπίς; often with genitive of source (Θεοῦ, γραφῶν, Ἁγίου Πνεύματος)

senses.definition: Earnest exhortation, moral urging, or an encouraging spoken or written address/instruction to a community or individual.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in ministry/teaching lists (with διδασκαλία/ἀνάγνωσις), or genitive modifying λόγος or υἱός

senses.definition: A specific personal request or urging directed to someone to undertake a task.
senses.grammatical_frame: Direct object of δέχομαι ('accept/receive')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in cognate constructions with the verb παρακαλέω (ROM 12:8; 2CO 1:4; 2CO 1:6; 2CO 7:7) and in coordination with χαρά ('joy'), ὑπομονή ('endurance'), ἐλπίς ('hope'), and θλῖψις ('affliction'). In 2CO 1 it repeatedly stands as the divine counterpart to suffering (παθήματα). In ACT 4:36 it translates the name Barnabas.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To show compassionate care, relief, or unmerited pardon toward someone in distress, need, or guilt, and in the passive to receive such compassion or pardon.

senses.definition: To feel compassion for and act to relieve someone who is suffering, afflicted, ill, or in urgent distress.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive verb (often aorist imperative in petitions) with accusative direct object

senses.definition: To grant clemency, pardon, or gracious favor to someone, especially by releasing a debt or refraining from judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive verb with accusative direct object (including relative pronouns)

senses.definition: To be the recipient of compassion, pardon, or gracious calling, chiefly from God or the Lord.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive verb (finite forms and participles), occasionally with ὑπό + genitive agent

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the aorist active imperative (`ἐλέησον`) in urgent cries for help (`ἐλέησόν με` / `ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς`), often paired with vocatives (`Κύριε`, `υἱὲ Δαυείδ`, `Ἐπιστάτα`, `Πάτερ Ἀβραάμ`). In ROM 9:15 it stands in parallel with `οἰκτείρω`, and in ROM 9:18 it is contrasted with `σκληρύνω` ("to harden"). In passive constructions, the agent is marked by `ὑπό` + genitive (1CO 7:25) or left implicit with God/Christ as the understood subject. In MAT 18:33, both the active infinitive and active aorist indicative appear in the same verse to link divine/royal clemency with human obligation.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An offering or sacrifice presented to God (or an idol), ranging from ritual animal/bird offerings to Christ's atoning self-offering and believers' metaphorical offerings of devotion, generosity, or praise.

senses.definition: A ritual offering—such as a slaughtered animal or prescribed birds—presented at an altar or sanctuary to God (or, in ACT 7:41, to an idol), or the cultic act of presenting such offerings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun, frequently as direct object of verbs of offering (προσφέρω, ἀναφέρω, ἀνάγω, δίδωμι) or eating (1CO 10:18)

senses.definition: The single, decisive self-offering of Christ in death for the removal of sin, contrasted with repeated priestly offerings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun with possessive pronoun (αὐτοῦ), numeral μίαν, or comparative qualifier (κρείττοσιν) in contexts of sin removal

senses.definition: A metaphorical offering pleasing to God, consisting of consecrated bodily service, faith-ministry, material support, verbal praise, or acts of kindness and sharing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate accusative (ROM 12:1), appositional noun (PHP 4:18), object of ἀναφέρω (HEB 13:15), or instrumental dative (HEB 13:16)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with δῶρα ('gifts and sacrifices' in HEB 5:1, 8:3, 9:9), προσφορά (HEB 10:5, 10:8), ὁλοκαυτώματα (MRK 12:33, HEB 10:8), and σφάγια (ACT 7:42), and governed by offering verbs (προσφέρω, ἀναφέρω, ἀνάγω, δίδωμι). Contrasted with mercy (ἔλεος) in MAT 9:13 and MAT 12:7, and with love of God and neighbor in MRK 12:33. In metaphorical/ethical contexts, qualified by adjectives like ζῶσαν ἁγίαν ... εὐάρεστον (ROM 12:1), δεκτήν, εὐάρεστον (PHP 4:18), or a genitive such as αἰνέσεως (HEB 13:15).

entries.core_meaning_summary: In participial/substantival uses, to lead or act as a ruler or leader; in finite and transitive clauses, to consider, regard, or judge someone or something to be a certain way.

senses.definition: To exercise leadership, authority, or a leading role over a people, territory, community, or activity; used primarily as a substantival participle denoting a ruler, governor, or community leader.
senses.grammatical_frame: Present middle participle (ὁ ἡγούμενος, οἱ ἡγούμενοι, or predicate/attributive ἡγούμενον/ἡγουμένους), with genitive or prepositional complement (ἐπί, ἐν)

senses.definition: To form a mental judgment about something or someone—regarding a person, thing, or situation as having a particular quality or value, or deeming a course of action necessary or right.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with object + predicate accusative (or εἶναι), or with predicate adjective (ἀναγκαῖον, δίκαιον) + infinitive clause

senses.definition: To hold someone in high regard or esteem.
senses.grammatical_frame: Infinitive with personal accusative object and adverbial modifier (ὑπερεκπερισσῶς ἐν ἀγάπῃ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Divides sharply by syntax: (1) participial forms (especially ὁ ἡγούμενος / οἱ ἡγούμενοι) function substantivally for leaders, rulers, or chief speakers, sometimes paired with ἐν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς (ACT 15:22), ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον (ACT 7:10), or τοῦ λόγου (ACT 14:12); (2) finite verbs and non-substantival participles take a direct object plus a predicate noun/adjective (e.g., μακάριον, ἁρπαγμόν, ζημίαν, σκύβαλα, πιστόν, κοινόν, πλοῦτον, χαράν, ἡδονήν, βραδύτητα) or an adjective + infinitive clause (ἀναγκαῖον ἡγησάμην in 2CO 9:5 and PHP 2:25; δίκαιον δὲ ἡγοῦμαι in 2PE 1:13).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be healthy, capable, strong enough, prevailing, or effective/valid depending on syntactic construction.

senses.definition: To be physically healthy or in bodily vigor, as contrasted with being ill and needing a physician.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival active participle (οἱ ἰσχύοντες) contrasted with οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες

senses.definition: To have the physical, mental, or circumstantial capacity to carry out an action or endure something.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + complementary infinitive (or elliptical infinitive), or + neuter accusative object (πάντα)

senses.definition: To gain mastery over an opponent or to grow in strength and influence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, or + κατά + genitive of person

senses.definition: To have practical usefulness, spiritual efficacy, or legal force and validity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb + neuter pronoun/adverb (τι, πολύ) or εἰς οὐδέν, or absolute in legal/evaluative contexts

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently constructed with a complementary infinitive (often negated with οὐκ or μή) to express ability or inability, and in elliptical responses with the infinitive understood from the preceding clause (MRK 9:18; LUK 13:24). In absolute/participle use (MAT 9:12; MRK 2:17) it contrasts with οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες ('those who are ill'). With neuter pronouns or adverbs (τι, οὐδέν, πολύ), it expresses degree of effectiveness or validity.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Temporal adverb indicating that an action, state, or expected event has not occurred up to the present moment or a stated point in time ('not yet').

senses.definition: Negates a verb or predicate (often with an explicit or implied copula) to indicate that an anticipated or potential event, action, or condition has not taken place up to the time of speaking or up to a past narrative point.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying finite verbs, periphrastic verb forms, or an implied copula

senses.definition: Reinforces a negative pronoun (οὐδείς) to express that no person has ever performed the action up to the time described.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb paired with negative pronoun οὐδείς (and οὐκ in LUK 23:53) modifying a finite or periphrastic verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently modifies verbs of knowing/understanding (νοέω, συνίημι in MAT 16:9, MRK 8:17, MRK 8:21; γινώσκω in 1CO 8:2) and verbs of arriving/occurring, especially with ὁ καιρὸς ὁ ἐμός or ἡ ὥρα μου/αὐτοῦ (JHN 2:4, JHN 7:6, JHN 7:8, JHN 7:30, JHN 8:20). Contrasted with ἤδη ('already') in JHN 6:17, ἔτι ('still') in JHN 11:30, οὐδὲ ἔτι νῦν ('nor even now') in 1CO 3:2, and νῦν ('now') in HEB 2:8 and 1JN 3:2. Paired closely with οὐδέπω in JHN 7:39. In MRK 11:2 and LUK 23:53, follows οὐδείς to emphasize that something has never happened up to that moment.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A wooden execution device on which a person is fastened to die, used also figuratively for costly discipleship and metonymically for Christ's crucifixion and its redemptive significance.

senses.definition: The physical wooden structure used for public execution, carried to the place of execution by the condemned person (or a pressed bearer) and from which the executed body hangs.
senses.grammatical_frame: Countable noun, typically articular, as direct object of carrying verbs or object of spatial prepositions (ἀπό, παρά, ἐπί)

senses.definition: Figurative expression in sayings of Jesus denoting the willingness to endure rejection, hardship, or death as a condition of following him.
senses.grammatical_frame: Articular noun with reflexive/possessive pronoun (τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ/ἑαυτοῦ) as object of λαμβάνω, αἴρω, or βαστάζω

senses.definition: Metonymy for the crucifixion death of Jesus Christ, including the reconciliation accomplished through it and the proclaimed message centered upon it.
senses.grammatical_frame: Usually articular noun in genitive modifiers (τοῦ σταυροῦ) or instrumental/locative prepositional phrases (διά, ἐν) and dative constructions

entries.collocations_and_notes: In execution narratives, objects of carrying verbs (αἴρω in MAT 27:32, MRK 15:21; φέρω in LUK 23:26; βαστάζω in JHN 19:17) and prepositional phrases of location/separation (ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ, παρὰ τῷ σταυρῷ, ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ). In discipleship sayings, follows λαμβάνω/αἴρω/βαστάζω + τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ/ἑαυτοῦ alongside ἀκολουθεῖν/ἔρχεσθαι ὀπίσω μου (with καθ’ ἡμέραν in LUK 9:23). In epistolary texts, appears in genitival and prepositional constructions (ὁ λόγος ὁ τοῦ σταυροῦ, τὸ σκάνδαλον τοῦ σταυροῦ, θανάτου δὲ σταυροῦ, διὰ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ σταυροῦ αὐτοῦ); COL 2:14 combines this redemptive sense with the physical imagery of nailing (προσηλώσας αὐτὸ τῷ σταυρῷ).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To inform someone of a fact or message, reveal hidden realities or attributes, or (rarely) discern/state a choice.

senses.definition: To communicate information, news, a message, or requests so that another person learns of them.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active with accusative object, περὶ + genitive, or ὅτι-clause, usually with dative recipient; or passive with πρὸς + accusative

senses.definition: To disclose previously hidden divine plans, wisdom, or attributes, or to make a person's identity openly recognizable.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active with accusative object or indirect question and dative or ἐπὶ + accusative; or passive with dative recipient or εἰς + accusative

senses.definition: To discern, know, or be able to declare which option to take.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active with indirect question (τί + future indicative), without recipient

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently used in epistolary disclosure formulas with a dative plural recipient (γνωρίζω ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, 1CO 15:1; 2CO 8:1; GAL 1:11) and in messenger summaries (πάντα γνωρίσει ὑμῖν Τυχικός, EPH 6:21; COL 4:7). Often paired or used in parallel with φανερόω (ACT 7:13; ROM 16:26), ἐνδείκνυμι (ROM 9:22), and ἀποκαλύπτω (EPH 3:5). Objects frequently include τὸ μυστήριον (EPH 1:9; EPH 3:3; EPH 6:19; COL 1:27) and τὸ εὐαγγέλιον (1CO 15:1; GAL 1:11). In PHP 1:22, the verb lacks a recipient and takes an indirect question (τί αἱρήσομαι οὐ γνωρίζω), functioning either cognitively ("I do not know/discern") or communicatively ("I cannot state/declare").

entries.core_meaning_summary: To think, hold an attitude or conviction, direct one's values toward something, share unity of mind, or show thoughtful care.

senses.definition: To hold a particular opinion, mental outlook, or self-assessment; to reason or think in a certain way.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active with neuter pronoun (ἅ, τοῦτο, οὐδὲν ἄλλο), adverb (ἑτέρως), ὡς + noun, or absolute

senses.definition: To set one's mind, interest, or aspirations on a specific sphere of values or lofty status.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active with substantivized neuter plural accusative (τὰ + genitive or adjective, or ὑψηλά)

senses.definition: To share a common outlook and purpose with others, living in mutual harmony.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active with τὸ αὐτό or τὸ ἕν, often with εἰς ἀλλήλους, ἐν ἀλλήλοις, or ἐν Κυρίῳ

senses.definition: To hold someone in thoughtful concern or care for their well-being.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active with ὑπέρ + genitive or ἐπί + dative (and optional τοῦτο)

senses.definition: To esteem and observe a specific calendar day out of religious devotion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active with accusative (τὴν ἡμέραν) + dative of reference (Κυρίῳ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly forms the idiomatic expression τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ("to share the same mindset", ROM 12:16; ROM 15:5; 2CO 13:11; PHP 2:2; PHP 4:2) and the parallel τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες (PHP 2:2). Contrasted in ROM 12:3 with compound/cognate verbs ὑπερφρονεῖν ("think too highly") and σωφρονεῖν ("think sensibly"). When paired with (τὰ) ὑψηλά (ROM 11:20; ROM 12:16), it expresses arrogance or lofty ambition, contrasted with humility (τοῖς ταπεινοῖς συναπαγόμενοι) or reverent fear (φοβοῦ). In 1CO 13:11 it stands alongside λαλέω and λογίζομαι to describe childhood thought and reasoning.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Accurate, reliable, or legally valid in speech and testimony; honest and trustworthy in character; or real and genuine rather than illusory.

senses.definition: Corresponding accurately to facts, trustworthy, or legally valid as witness and instruction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate, attributive, or substantival adjective modifying μαρτυρία, παροιμία, or spoken statements

senses.definition: Speaking and acting with integrity and sincerity, free from deceit, falsehood, or partiality.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate or substantival adjective describing God or human beings
