senses.definition: Actually existing or occurring in reality, as opposed to something merely apparent, visionary, or counterfeit.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective describing events, grace, food/drink, or realized commands

entries.collocations_and_notes: Heavily concentrated in Johannine literature with μαρτυρία ("testimony/witness", JHN 5:31, 32; 8:13, 14, 17; 21:24; 3JN 1:12), where legal validity and reliability are in view (cf. two-witness rule in JHN 8:17). Frequently defined through explicit antonyms: ψεύστης ("liar", ROM 3:4), ψεῦδος ("falsehood", 1JN 2:27), ἀδικία ("unrighteousness", JHN 7:18), πλάνοι ("deceivers", 2CO 6:8), and ὅραμα ("vision/apparition", ACT 12:9). In MAT 22:16 and MRK 12:14, being ἀληθής is linked to teaching God's way sincerely without showing partiality (οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To uncover what was hidden, impart divine insight or prophetic truth to recipients, or openly manifest eschatological realities or figures.

senses.definition: To expose or bring into plain view thoughts, works, or hidden matters that were covered or concealed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive with inanimate subjects (e.g., διαλογισμοί, κεκαλυμμένον, τὸ ἔργον)

senses.definition: To disclose or grant understanding of divine truths, mysteries, or prophetic messages to human recipients.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active or passive (including impersonal passive) with dative recipient, often with διὰ/ἐν Πνεύματι or ὅτι-clause

senses.definition: To manifest openly or bring onto the public stage a divine attribute, redemptive reality, or prominent eschatological figure.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive (with personal or abstract subjects and often temporal markers) or active with personal object (GAL 1:16)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of concealing as explicit contrasts: κρύπτω/ἀποκρύπτω (MAT 11:25; LUK 10:21), καλύπτω (MAT 10:26), and συγκαλύπτω (LUK 12:2), and paralleled with γνωρίζω (EPH 3:5) and γινώσκω (MAT 10:26; LUK 12:2). Divine agency is typical, often mediated by the Spirit (διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος, 1CO 2:10; ἐν Πνεύματι, EPH 3:5). In 1CO 14:30, the passive ἐὰν δὲ ἄλλῳ ἀποκαλυφθῇ functions impersonally without an expressed subject ("if a revelation is given to another"). In eschatological contexts (LUK 17:30; 2TH 2:3, 6, 8), passive forms with personal subjects denote the open arrival and public appearance of a figure.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be in bondage or subjection as a servant or slave, or to render obedient, devoted service to a master, deity, community, or controlling force.

senses.definition: To be enslaved to, in legal or social bondage to, or politically subordinate to a master, household head, or foreign nation.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb, intransitive or with dative of master/superior (δυσὶ κυρίοις, οὐδενί, ᾧ, τῷ ἐλάσσονι)

senses.definition: To work dutifully for or act in willing, humble service toward a family member, fellow believers, or a shared mission without literal slavery.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb with dative of beneficiary (σοι, ἀλλήλοις), or absolute with σύν + dative and εἰς + accusative goal (σὺν ἐμοὶ ... εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον)

senses.definition: To render loyal devotion, allegiance, and obedient service to God or Christ.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb with dative of deity/Lord (Θεῷ, τῷ Κυρίῳ, τῷ Χριστῷ), or absolute with manner phrase (ἐν καινότητι πνεύματος)

senses.definition: Figuratively, to be dominated by, controlled by, or devoted to an abstract power, desire, law, wealth, or false deity.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb with dative of controlling force, desire, or object of devotion (μαμωνᾷ, τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, νόμῳ, τῇ ἑαυτῶν κοιλίᾳ, ἐπιθυμίαις, στοιχείοις, τοῖς... θεοῖς)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Almost always takes a dative complement indicating the master, deity, person, or controlling force served; rarely used absolutely without a dative (GAL 4:25; ROM 7:6; PHP 2:22; 1TI 6:2). Frequently appears in explicit contrasts: serving God versus wealth (MAT 6:24; LUK 16:13), serving Christ versus one's own appetite (ROM 16:18), serving the law of God versus the law of sin (ROM 7:25), or living in freedom versus returning to bondage (JHN 8:33; GAL 4:9; GAL 5:13). In ACT 7:7 it describes forced subjugation to a foreign nation, standing alongside λατρεύω for subsequent worship of God.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To acquire knowledge or instruction from a source, to discover a specific fact or meaning, or to come to practice an attitude or behavior.

senses.definition: To gain knowledge, receive religious or formal instruction, or master a teaching, lesson, or song from a teacher or source.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb, absolute or with accusative of thing/person learned (τὴν παραβολήν, τὴν διδαχήν, τὸν Χριστόν, τὴν ᾠδήν), often accompanied by ἀπό or παρά + genitive of source

senses.definition: To find out, ascertain, or come to understand a particular fact, answer, or textual meaning by inquiry or investigation.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb with ὅτι clause, indirect question (τί ἐστιν...), pronoun (τι, τοῦτο) + direct question, often with ἀπό + genitive of informant

senses.definition: To become accustomed to, adopt, or master a pattern of behavior, character trait, or practical skill through training or experience.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb with complementary infinitive (εἶναι, εὐσεβεῖν, προΐστασθαι), predicate adjective (ἀργαί), or accusative of quality (τὴν ὑπακοήν) + ἀπό

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently pairs with ἀπό or παρά + genitive to mark the teacher or source of instruction (e.g., MAT 11:29; MAT 24:32; JHN 6:45; GAL 3:2; COL 1:7; 2TI 3:14; HEB 5:8). In PHP 4:9 it is grouped with παραλαμβάνω, ἀκούω, and ὁράω to describe receiving apostolic teaching and example. In JHN 7:15 the perfect participle μὴ μεμαθηκώς indicates lack of formal schooling. In 1TI 5:13, ἀργαὶ μανθάνουσιν is syntactically ambiguous between taking ἀργαί as a predicate complement ("learn to be idle") or as an attribute of the subject ("being idle, they learn...").

entries.core_meaning_summary: Proper name of a Christian believer from Lystra/Derbe who served as a close companion, messenger, coworker, and co-sender of letters with Paul.

senses.definition: A male disciple of Jewish-Greek parentage (ACT 16:1) who traveled with and assisted Paul, carried out missions to churches as an envoy, joined Paul as a co-sender and co-preacher, and received personal pastoral letters.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun, masculine (nominative, genitive, dative, accusative, and vocative)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly accompanied by descriptive titles or relational terms such as ὁ ἀδελφός ('the brother': 2CO 1:1; COL 1:1; 1TH 3:2; PHM 1:1; HEB 13:23), τέκνον ('child', modified by γνησίῳ or ἀγαπητῷ: 1CO 4:17; 1TI 1:2, 18; 2TI 1:2), ὁ συνεργός ('coworker': ROM 16:21), and διάκονος τοῦ Θεοῦ ('servant of God': 1TH 3:2). Frequently paired with Paul and Silas/Silvanus in narrative travel accounts and epistolary salutations.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Causal conjunction introducing a reason, ground, or supporting explanation for a preceding statement or command.

senses.definition: Introduces a subordinate clause stating the direct cause, motive, or reason for the action or state in the preceding main clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating causal conjunction following a main clause and governing an indicative clause

senses.definition: Stands at the beginning of a sentence or major clause to introduce a supporting ground, explanatory proof, or scriptural quotation backing up a prior claim or exhortation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial explanatory conjunction introducing an indicative statement or quotation formula

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often introduces scriptural citations or theological explanations (ACT 13:35; 1PE 1:16, 24; 2:6). In verse-initial occurrences such as ACT 20:26 and ROM 8:21, the preceding sentence lies outside the verse boundary provided; in ACT 18:10, it appears twice in succession to stack reasons.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Stative verb expressing physical resting or placement, spatial situation, figurative condition, or being appointed/enacted for a role.

senses.definition: To rest in a horizontal or stationary position, or to be placed, stored, or standing in a physical location (used of infants, dead bodies, garments, vessels, tools, stored provisions, a fire, or a throne).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb or participle, typically with a locative adverb (ὅπου) or prepositional phrase (ἐν, πρός, μετά)

senses.definition: To be situated or laid out in a particular geographical location or geometric shape (used of a city).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb or participle with a spatial phrase (ἐπάνω + genitive) or predicate adjective (τετράγωνος)

senses.definition: To exist in an established or figurative condition, such as a foundation already laid, a veil resting over hearts, or the world lying within the sphere of evil.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb or substantival participle with prepositional phrases (ἐπί + accusative, ἐν + dative)

senses.definition: To be appointed, destined, or assigned to a role or experience (with εἰς + accusative), or of a legal code, to be enacted or laid down for someone (with dative).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with εἰς + accusative of purpose/result, or with dative of person (with νόμος)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Functions in several contexts as the stative or passive counterpart to τίθημι ('to place/lay'; compare ἔθηκεν ... κείμενος in LUK 23:53 and θεῖναι ... τὸν κείμενον in 1CO 3:11). Frequently takes locative prepositional phrases (ἐν, πρός, ἐπάνω, ἐπί) or purpose phrases with εἰς + accusative (LUK 2:34; PHP 1:16; 1TH 3:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The rational faculty of understanding and thought, as well as a person's moral disposition, settled judgment, or divine counsel.

senses.definition: The cognitive capacity to comprehend, reason, discern wisdom, or speak and pray intelligibly.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, often as object of verbs of opening/having (διανοίγω, ἔχω) or in instrumental dative (τῷ νοΐ)

senses.definition: The inner moral and spiritual orientation or way of thinking, capable of being renewed or, conversely, corrupted, defiled, futile, or dominated by the flesh.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun in genitive, dative, nominative, or accusative of respect (with passive participles of corruption)

senses.definition: A person's settled conviction, shared outlook, or mental composure.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun in prepositional phrases (ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ νοῒ, ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ νοῒ, ἀπὸ τοῦ νοὸς)

senses.definition: The thought, purpose, or counsel belonging to God or Christ.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun as direct object of ἔγνω or ἔχομεν with possessive genitive (Κυρίου, Χριστοῦ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In 1CO 14:14–15, contrasted with τὸ πνεῦμα ('the spirit') in relation to intelligible prayer and singing. Paired with σάρξ ('flesh') in ROM 7:25 and COL 2:18, and with συνείδησις ('conscience') in TIT 1:15. In 1TI 6:5 and 2TI 3:8, takes an accusative of respect (διεφθαρμένων/κατεφθαρμένοι τὸν νοῦν, 'corrupted in mind').

entries.core_meaning_summary: The physical presence of a person at a location, or the arrival, visit, or awaited public coming of a person or decisive day.

senses.definition: The state of a person being physically in the same place as others, in contrast to being away or communicating only by letter.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, absolute or with genitive of person/body (τοῦ σώματος) or possessive pronoun; often in prepositional phrase ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ

senses.definition: The arrival or return visit of a person to a community, resulting in personal fellowship or encouragement.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun with genitive of person or possessive pronoun, sometimes with directional prepositional phrase (πάλιν πρὸς ὑμᾶς)

senses.definition: The awaited, decisive arrival or public manifestation of a figure of cosmic significance—specifically Jesus Christ (the Son of Man / Lord) or an opposing lawless figure.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun with genitive of person (τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, τοῦ Κυρίου, αὐτοῦ) or relative pronoun; frequently governed by ἐν, ἕως, εἰς, or ὑπέρ

senses.definition: The arrival or onset of an expected time or decisive epoch.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun as direct object of verbs of waiting/hastening, with genitive of time (τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμέρας)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in the dative with ἐν (ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ) to mark the occasion or time of an event, or as the subject/genitive with ἕως and εἰς to denote an awaited point in time. In PHP 2:12 it is explicitly paired with its antonym ἀπουσία (absence), and in 2CO 10:10 ἡ παρουσία τοῦ σώματος contrasts physical, in-person appearance with written letters. In 2TH 2:8 it appears in the phrase τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, and in 1JN 2:28 it parallels ἐὰν φανερωθῇ. In 2PE 1:16, δύναμιν καὶ παρουσίαν is linked with being eyewitnesses of majesty, which in context could refer either to Christ's displayed majesty or to the certainty of his awaited coming.

entries.core_meaning_summary: One who rescues, preserves, and grants deliverance and life, used exclusively as a designation and title for God and Jesus Christ.

senses.definition: One who brings rescue, spiritual deliverance, forgiveness, or preservation to a specified group, community, or the whole world.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun, used predicatively or appositionally, often with an objective genitive (τοῦ κόσμου, πάντων ἀνθρώπων, τοῦ σώματος) or dative of beneficiary (ὑμῖν, τῷ Ἰσραήλ)

senses.definition: A confessional, liturgical, or epistolary title for God or Jesus Christ recognizing him as the people's deliverer and source of salvation.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun, regularly modified by a possessive genitive pronoun (μου, ἡμῶν) and paired or in apposition with Θεός, Κύριος, or Ἰησοῦς Χριστός

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used exclusively in these texts for God or Jesus Christ (never for ordinary human rulers or rescuers). Frequently occurs in fixed genitive phrases with possessive pronouns (τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Θεοῦ; τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν καὶ Σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ). In TIT 2:13 and 2PE 1:1, a single definite article governs both Θεοῦ and Σωτῆρος (e.g., τοῦ μεγάλου Θεοῦ καὶ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ), syntactically linking the two nouns closely. Contexts associate this role with granting repentance and forgiveness of sins (ACT 5:31), overcoming death and bringing life (2TI 1:10), kindness and care for humanity (TIT 3:4), and rescuing from worldly corruption (2PE 2:20).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An internal bodily cavity—specifically the stomach or womb—used also by extension for physical appetite or a person's innermost being.

senses.definition: The digestive organ or internal abdominal cavity that receives food and drink (including the interior belly of a large sea creature in MAT 12:40).
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; often governed by prepositions (εἰς, ἐν) or paired with verbs of eating and filling (γεμίζω, κατεσθίω, πικραίνω)

senses.definition: The female reproductive organ where offspring are conceived and carried prior to birth; often used with ἐκ ('from') to signify the start of life or existence from birth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; frequently in the prepositional phrase ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός ('from a mother's womb') or with ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ ('in the womb')

senses.definition: Physical appetite or bodily self-indulgence, personified or metonymically treated as an object of service or devotion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; dative indirect object of δουλεύω ('serve') or predicate nominative with θεός ('god')

senses.definition: The inner core or spiritual center of a person, depicted figuratively as the source from which living water flows.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; governed by ἐκ ('out of') with a verb of flowing (ῥέω)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the prepositional phrase ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός ('from a mother's womb') to mark origin from birth or before birth (MAT 19:12, LUK 1:15, ACT 3:2, ACT 14:8, GAL 1:15). In digestive contexts, it is contrasted with στόμα ('mouth') and ἀφεδρών ('latrine') or καρδία ('heart') in MAT 15:17, MRK 7:19, REV 10:9, REV 10:10. In LUK 11:27 and LUK 23:29, κοιλία is paired with μαστοί ('breasts') to represent maternal childbearing and nursing.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To experience physical hunger or lack of food, and metaphorically to feel intense spiritual longing or need.

senses.definition: To feel the physical need for food or to suffer deprivation and lack of nourishment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb; also used as a substantival participle (οἱ πεινῶντες, 'those who are hungry')

senses.definition: To desire intensely or experience spiritual need and longing, either directed toward a moral quality (accusative object) or in contrast to spiritual satisfaction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive with accusative object (MAT 5:6), or intransitive in metaphorical contrast with 'the bread of life' (JHN 6:35)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often paired with διψάω ('to thirst') to express combined physical need or intense spiritual longing (MAT 5:6, JHN 6:35, ROM 12:20, 1CO 4:11, REV 7:16), and contrasted with verbs of being filled or satisfied such as χορτάζομαι and ἐμπίπλημι (MAT 5:6, LUK 1:53, LUK 6:21, LUK 6:25, PHP 4:12). In LUK 1:53, the substantival participle πεινῶντας stands in contrast to πλουτοῦντας ('the rich').

entries.core_meaning_summary: To bring a task, period, or prophecy to completion, or to bring a person, quality, or relationship to fullness, maturity, or spiritual wholeness before God.

senses.definition: To finish or carry out completely a span of time, an assigned work or course of service, or a prophetic scripture.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active voice with accusative object (days, work, course); passive voice with Scripture or personal course as subject

senses.definition: To bring a person, group, or quality (such as faith or love) to full maturity, realization, or complete unity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive voice; often modified by prepositional phrases indicating manner or goal (εἰς ἕν, ἐκ τῶν ἔργων, ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ)

senses.definition: In cultic and redemptive contexts, to bring someone to full qualification, spiritual wholeness, or lasting acceptability before God (contrasted with the inability of ritual offerings to cleanse the conscience).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active voice with personal object (or οὐδέν) and instrumental phrase (διὰ παθημάτων, μιᾷ προσφορᾷ); passive voice referring to Christ or believers

entries.collocations_and_notes: In John's Gospel, frequently takes τὸ ἔργον or τὰ ἔργα ('work/works') as its object (JHN 4:34, JHN 5:36, JHN 17:4). In LUK 13:32, the passive/middle τελειοῦμαι appears alongside ἀποτελῶ ('finish/accomplish') and may carry the sense of completing his earthly course or reaching his appointed end. In 1 John, the perfect passive of τελειόω repeatedly pairs with ἡ ἀγάπη ('love') to describe love reaching its full maturity or expression (1JN 2:5, 1JN 4:12, 1JN 4:17, 1JN 4:18).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To freely grant or bestow something, to hand over or restore a person as a favor, or to cancel a debt or forgive a wrong.

senses.definition: To freely give or generously bestow a gift, ability, privilege, or benefit without obligation or payment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle verb with dative recipient and accusative gift or infinitive; passive with dative recipient and subject gift or articular infinitive

senses.definition: To grant, release, spare, or hand over a person to someone as a favor or act of grace (whether yielding an accused person, releasing a prisoner, sparing lives, or restoring a companion).
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle verb with dative recipient and accusative person; passive with dative recipient and personal subject

senses.definition: To cancel a financial debt or to pardon and forgive an offense, wrong, or trespass.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle verb with dative person forgiven (LUK 7:42, EPH 4:32, COL 3:13), optional accusative debt/offense (LUK 7:43, 2CO 2:10, 2CO 12:13, COL 2:13), or absolute (2CO 2:7)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Middle/deponent forms function actively with a dative recipient (and optional accusative gift, person, or wrong), while aorist and future passive forms (ACT 3:14, 1CO 2:12, PHP 1:29, PHM 1:22) express being granted or restored to someone. In EPH 4:32 and COL 3:13, believers' mutual forgiveness (χαριζόμενοι ἑαυτοῖς) is explicitly modeled on divine forgiveness (καθὼς καὶ ὁ Θεὸς/Κύριος ἐχαρίσατο ὑμῖν).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Macedonia, a geographical region and province north of Achaia containing Philippi and other Christian congregations, or by metonymy the believers residing there.

senses.definition: The territory and Roman administrative region north of Achaia, including the district containing Philippi, viewed as a place of travel, mission, and Christian congregations.
senses.grammatical_frame: proper noun (anarthrous or articular), in prepositional phrases (εἰς, ἀπό, διά, ἐν), direct object of διέρχομαι, or genitive modifier

senses.definition: The Christian believers or congregations located in Macedonia, acting collectively as a single body.
senses.grammatical_frame: proper noun as grammatical subject of an action verb (ηὐδόκησαν)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with Ἀχαΐα (ACT 19:21; ROM 15:26; 1TH 1:7, 8) and connected with Philippi as a leading city of one of its districts (ACT 16:12). Occurs both with and without the definite article across prepositional phrases indicating destination (εἰς), origin (ἀπό), route (διά), and location (ἐν), as well as in the genitive modifying τῆς μερίδος (ACT 16:12) and ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις (2CO 8:1).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To examine or test something or someone in order to determine its quality, genuineness, or meaning, and thus to discern or approve after evaluation.

senses.definition: To test, scrutinize, or assay an object, person, action, or claim in order to ascertain its quality, genuineness, or reliability.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with direct object (person, work, heart, spirit, oxen, or reflexive pronoun), passive (with instrumental phrase such as 'through fire'), or followed by an indirect question ('whether...')

senses.definition: To discern, interpret, or evaluate carefully what is true, fitting, or most important in a given situation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with direct object (weather signs, the present time, things that differ/matter) or indirect question ('what is...')

senses.definition: To approve, endorse, or deem fit and worthwhile as a result of testing or judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with direct object, predicate participle, or infinitive complement; also passive with infinitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in contexts of evaluation or proving genuineness: with reflexive objects (1CO 11:28; 2CO 13:5, alongside πειράζω), with διὰ πυρός or τὸ πῦρ of testing metal or work (1CO 3:13; 1PE 1:7), and with τὰ διαφέροντα (ROM 2:18; PHP 1:10), which can carry the nuance of distinguishing what differs or recognizing what is superior/essential. In ROM 1:28 and 2CO 13:5 it contrasts with the related adjective ἀδόκιμος. In 1TH 2:4 it appears twice in the same verse, first passively for being vetted/approved by God for a trust, and second actively for God examining human hearts.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To carry out, perform, or accomplish an action, and by extension to bring about or produce a resulting state or condition.

senses.definition: To do, perform, carry out, or commit a deed, practice, or miraculous work, whether good or evil.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with direct object (deed, good, evil, shameless act, will, pronoun, or signs); passive in 2CO 12:12

senses.definition: To produce, generate, or bring about an outcome, condition, or response in or for someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with abstract or outcome object (wrath, endurance, desire, death, glory, eagerness, thanksgiving), often with a dative of beneficiary or prepositional phrase ('in me', 'through us')

senses.definition: To work out to completion or to prepare and fit someone for a specific purpose.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with object (salvation; or personal object + 'eis' + purpose)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often used in Pauline prose with abstract subjects such as the law, affliction, sin, or godly sorrow to express causal production (ROM 4:15; 5:3; 7:8, 13; 2CO 7:10–11; JAS 1:3), and in ROM 7:15–20 it alternates closely with πράσσω and ποιῶ. In 2CO 7:10 it stands in parallel with the simple verb ἐργάζομαι. Two contexts show distinct nuances: in 2CO 5:5 the direct object is personal ('us'), indicating God preparing or shaping believers for a destiny, and in EPH 6:13 ἅπαντα κατεργασάμενοι may mean either having carried out all required actions or having overcome all opposition before taking a stand.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To work hard or exert strenuous effort, and in some contexts to become weary or worn out from exertion.

senses.definition: To toil, work hard, or exert strenuous physical, practical, or ministerial effort.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, often modified by adverbs ('much', 'more', 'in vain'), participles ('working', 'struggling'), or prepositional phrases ('for you', 'in the Lord', 'in word and teaching')

senses.definition: To grow weary, fatigued, or worn out from labor, travel, or prolonged hardship.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb (present or perfect), used absolutely or with a prepositional phrase of cause ('from the journey')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with other verbs of effort or manual work such as ἐργάζομαι ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσίν (1CO 4:12; EPH 4:28), ἀγωνίζομαι (COL 1:29; 1TI 4:10), τρέχω (PHP 2:16), νήθω (MAT 6:28), and συνεργέω (1CO 16:16). In Paul and 1 Timothy it commonly describes strenuous ministry or congregational service, modified by πολλά, εἰκῇ, εἰς κενόν, εἰς ὑμᾶς, ἐν Κυρίῳ, or ἐν λόγῳ καὶ διδασκαλίᾳ. In JHN 4:38 it is paired with the cognate noun κόπος. In MAT 11:28, JHN 4:6, and REV 2:3 the sense shifts toward the resulting state of exhaustion or weariness.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Material wealth or riches, and metaphorically a great abundance or fullness of spiritual qualities and blessings.

senses.definition: Material wealth, earthly possessions, or abundant resources (also metaphorically compared with treasure in HEB 11:26 and listed as an honorific attribute in REV 5:12).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (masculine), used alone or with possessive or descriptive modifiers

senses.definition: A vast abundance, richness, or fullness of divine qualities, blessings, or human virtue.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (masculine or neuter), typically governing a descriptive genitive ('of grace', 'of glory', 'of kindness', 'of generosity') or a genitive of possessor/beneficiary ('of Christ', 'of the world')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Exhibits both masculine forms (e.g., ROM 9:23; EPH 1:18; HEB 11:26; JAS 5:2; REV 5:12; 18:17) and neuter forms (e.g., 2CO 8:2; EPH 1:7; 2:7; 3:8, 16; PHP 4:19; COL 1:27; 2:2) in the texts. In the Synoptic parable of the sower and in 1TI 6:17 and JAS 5:2, material wealth is portrayed as deceptive, uncertain, or perishable. In Pauline letters and 2 Corinthians, by contrast, it is predominantly used with genitive qualifiers (e.g., grace, glory, kindness, generosity, wisdom, understanding) to express bountiful spiritual abundance. In REV 5:12, wealth appears in a sevenfold doxological list of royal attributes ascribed to the Lamb.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To render religious devotion, worship, or sacred service to God, another spiritual entity, or within a ritual sanctuary.

senses.definition: To offer exclusive religious allegiance, reverence, and sacred service to a deity or to false objects of devotion such as created things or heavenly bodies.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb + dative of deity or object of devotion

senses.definition: To engage in ongoing acts of piety, prayer, fasting, or sacrificial worship, or (as a substantivized participle) a person engaged in such worship.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive verb, often with dative of manner/means or as a substantivized participle

senses.definition: To perform priestly or ritual ministry connected with the earthly tabernacle and its pattern.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb + dative of the sanctuary or ritual copy

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most commonly takes a dative complement naming the deity or object of devotion (e.g., τῷ Θεῷ, αὐτῷ, τῇ κτίσει, τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ). Paired with προσκυνέω (MAT 4:10; LUK 4:8) and σέβομαι (ROM 1:25), and contrasted with ordinary enslavement to a nation (δουλεύω in ACT 7:7). Frequently modified by temporal expressions of continual devotion (νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν in LUK 2:37; ACT 26:7; ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός in REV 7:15) and phrases specifying the manner or locus of devotion (νηστείαις καὶ δεήσεσιν, ἐν τῷ πνεύματί μου, Πνεύματι Θεοῦ, ἐν καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει, μετὰ εὐλαβείας καὶ δέους). Substantivized participles (οἱ λατρεύοντες, τὸν λατρεύοντα) denote worshipers participating in sacrificial ritual in Hebrews.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be actively at work, operate effectively, or bring about and produce results through inner or divine power.

senses.definition: To produce, accomplish, or put into effective operation, such as divine power, miraculous deeds, or human willing and action.
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb + accusative direct object

senses.definition: To operate, be active, or work effectively within or on behalf of someone (with the second occurrence in PHP 2:13 used as a substantivized infinitive denoting effective action).
senses.grammatical_frame: active intransitive verb, often with ἐν + dative or dative of person

senses.definition: To exert ongoing influence, operate, or prove effective in someone or through a medium (used of powers, sinful passions, death, comfort, faith, the divine word, lawlessness, or prayer).
senses.grammatical_frame: middle/passive intransitive verb, often with ἐν + dative or διά + genitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears with ἐν + dative indicating the sphere or person within whom an agent, spirit, passion, or power acts (e.g., ἐν αὐτῷ, ἐν ὑμῖν, ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν). Cognate with ἐνέργεια (COL 1:29) and ἐνέργημα (1CO 12:6). When passive/middle in form, it functions intransitively to describe forces, spiritual realities, or prayer exerting an ongoing effect rather than receiving external action. In GAL 2:8, the dative of person (Πέτρῳ, ἐμοί) marks the recipients in or for whom God worked effectively.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To obey, submit to, or comply with a person, authority, message, or call, or to answer a knock at a door.

senses.definition: To carry out the will or command of a person or authority, or to yield compliance to a supernatural command (used of children, servants, wives, believers, and natural or spiritual forces).
senses.grammatical_frame: verb + dative of person/entity, verb + infinitive, or absolute

senses.definition: To heed, accept, or submit oneself to a proclamation, body of teaching, faith, or inner impulse.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb + dative of message/teaching/impulse, or εἰς + accusative

senses.definition: To come to a door in response to someone knocking.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive infinitive of purpose without expressed object

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly governs a dative complement naming the person, authority, command, message, or force obeyed; paired with ἐπιτάσσω in miracle narratives (MRK 1:27; LUK 8:25) and linked with δοῦλος/κύριος authority relationships (ROM 6:16; EPH 6:5; COL 3:22). In household instructions it is modified by κατὰ πάντα (COL 3:20, 22) and ἐν ἁπλότητι καρδίας (EPH 6:5). In ROM 6:17, the verb appears with εἰς + accusative via relative attraction (εἰς ὃν παρεδόθητε τύπον διδαχῆς).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Denotes shared origin or classification, ranging from offspring and family lineage to an ethnic people, birthplace, or general category.

senses.definition: Offspring, descendant, or extended family and ancestral lineage.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (often with a genitive of ancestor/parent or in ἐκ γένους)

senses.definition: A people, nation, or ethnic community bound by shared descent (e.g., Israel, or the covenant community in 1PE 2:9).
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (often with possessive pronoun, ethnic genitive, or adjective)

senses.definition: Birthplace, extraction, or ancestral origin as a point of personal identification.
senses.grammatical_frame: dative of respect (τῷ γένει) modifying a regional or ethnic adjective/noun

senses.definition: A class, sort, or variety of objects, beings, or phenomena.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (singular with πᾶς or τοῦτο, or plural γένη + genitive plural)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In Acts and Mark, the dative of respect τῷ γένει regularly follows an ethnic or geographical designation to indicate birthplace or ancestral origin (MRK 7:26; ACT 4:36; ACT 18:2; ACT 18:24). In 1 Corinthians (12:10, 12:28, 14:10), the plural γένη pairs with genitives (γλωσσῶν, φωνῶν) to denote diverse kinds of speech or languages. In 1PE 2:9, γένος ἐκλεκτόν stands in parallel with ἔθνος ἅγιον ("holy nation") and λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν ("people for possession").

entries.core_meaning_summary: To move rapidly on foot or charge forward, and figuratively to exert earnest effort toward a goal or spread swiftly.

senses.definition: To move swiftly on foot (or of horses charging into battle), whether hurrying to a person/place or competing in a footrace.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive verb (often with directional phrase ἐπί/εἰς + accusative or a participle + finite verb)

senses.definition: To strive, exert oneself, or carry out one's course of faith or apostolic labor (drawn from the imagery of an athletic race).
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive (often with manner adverbials like καλῶς, εἰς κενόν, οὐκ ἀδήλως) or transitive with cognate/object ἀγῶνα in HEB 12:1

senses.definition: Of a message or word: to spread rapidly and advance without hindrance.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive verb with inanimate subject (ὁ λόγος τοῦ Κυρίου)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Suppletive aorist stem δрам- (ἔδραμον, δραμών) supplies past/aorist forms alongside present/imperfect stem τρέχ-. Often paired with verbs of arriving or coming (ἔρχεται, JHN 20:2), purpose infinitives (ἀπαγγεῖλαι, MAT 28:8), or directional prepositions (ἐπί, εἰς). Metaphorical uses frequently involve athletic imagery (ἐν σταδίῳ, 1CO 9:24; ἀγῶνα, HEB 12:1) or the idiom εἰς κενὸν τρέχω/ἔδραμον ("run in vain", GAL 2:2; PHP 2:16, paralleled with ἐκοπίασα "labored"). In 1CO 9:24, the first two occurrences depict literal stadium runners while the imperative τρέχετε transfers the image to spiritual striving.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Clear knowledge, understanding, or recognition, particularly of God, Christ, divine truth, or moral reality.

senses.definition: Knowledge, comprehension, or insight, especially concerning divine truth, God's will, or spiritual mysteries.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (frequently with objective genitive such as ἀληθείας, τοῦ θελήματος, τοῦ μυστηρίου, or absolute in prepositional phrases)

senses.definition: Personal knowledge or acknowledgment of God or Jesus Christ as the basis of relationship and godly conduct.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun with personal objective genitive (e.g., τοῦ Θεοῦ, τοῦ Κυρίου) or as object of ἔχειν ἐν in ROM 1:28

senses.definition: Awareness, discernment, or practical recognition of a moral condition or blessing (such as sin or shared good).
senses.grammatical_frame: noun + genitive of the thing recognized (ἁμαρτίας, παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Highly concentrated in Pauline, Pastoral, and Petrine epistles. Regularly appears in prepositional phrases with ἐν (ROM 1:28; EPH 1:17; PHP 1:9; PHM 1:6; 2PE 1:2; 2PE 2:20), εἰς (COL 2:2; COL 3:10; 1TI 2:4; 2TI 2:25; 2TI 3:7; 2PE 1:8), and κατά (ROM 10:2; TIT 1:1). Repeatedly occurs in the fixed phrase εἰς (or τὴν) ἐπίγνωσιν (τῆς) ἀληθείας (1TI 2:4; 2TI 2:25; 2TI 3:7; TIT 1:1; HEB 10:26). Frequently paired with wisdom/perception terms such as σοφία, σύνεσις, αἴσθησις, and πίστις.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Mutual fellowship and close relational bond, active participation or partnership in a shared reality, and material sharing or charitable contribution.

senses.definition: A close relational bond, shared communal life, or spiritual fellowship uniting people with one another or with God, Christ, or the Spirit (and denied between incompatible realities such as light and darkness).
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, commonly with μετά + genitive of persons (μεθ' ἡμῶν, μετ' ἀλλήλων, μετὰ τοῦ Πατρός), dative + πρός + accusative (φωτὶ πρὸς σκότος), or associative genitive (τοῦ Υἱοῦ, τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος)

senses.definition: Shared participation or active partnership in a common endeavor, experience, or sacred reality, such as the cup and bread of Christ, his sufferings, or gospel mission.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, taking a genitive of what is shared (τοῦ αἵματος, τοῦ σώματος, παθημάτων, τῆς πίστεως), serving as a qualifying genitive (δεξιὰς ... κοινωνίας), or taking εἰς + accusative for a shared goal (εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον)

senses.definition: Material sharing, financial contribution, or generous aid given to support others in need.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, object of ποιέομαι (κοινωνίαν τινὰ ποιήσασθαι), coordinated with terms of relief service or beneficence (διακονία, εὐποιΐα), often with εἰς + accusative designating recipients (εἰς τοὺς πτωχούς, εἰς αὐτούς)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often takes a genitive specifying either the person/entity with whom fellowship is held (τοῦ Υἱοῦ, τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος, Πνεύματος) or the thing shared (τοῦ αἵματος, τοῦ σώματος, παθημάτων, τῆς πίστεως, τῆς διακονίας), or uses μετά + genitive for relational partners (μεθ' ἡμῶν, μετ' αὐτοῦ, μετ' ἀλλήλων, μετὰ τοῦ Πατρός). In 2CO 13:13 and PHP 2:1, the genitive of the Spirit may express either mutual participation in the Spirit or fellowship imparted by the Spirit; in PHM 1:6, ἡ κοινωνία τῆς πίστεώς σου may refer to generous sharing prompted by faith or shared participation in faith. Parallel to μετοχή in 2CO 6:14 and paired with εὐποιΐα in HEB 13:16.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Comparative adjective and adverb denoting greater quality, rank, value, or advantage in comparison with another thing, person, or course of action.

senses.definition: Surpassing another in quality, worth, effectiveness, or spiritual benefit, used attributively with nouns or as a substantivized neuter denoting superior things or conditions.
senses.grammatical_frame: comparative adjective, attributive with nouns or substantivized neuter (sometimes with παρά + accusative)

senses.definition: Holding higher rank, dignity, or authority than another person or spiritual being.
senses.grammatical_frame: comparative adjective, predicative with genitive of comparison or substantivized

senses.definition: More advantageous, desirable, or fitting as a course of action or state when weighed against an alternative.
senses.grammatical_frame: impersonal predicative neuter (with ἐστίν or ἦν, or elliptical), often with infinitive + ἤ

senses.definition: In a more excellent, favorable, or effective manner than an alternative.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverbial neuter singular modifying a verb (sometimes with παρά + accusative)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired as an antonym with ἧσσον in 1CO 11:17 (εἰς τὸ κρεῖσσον ... εἰς τὸ ἧσσον) and with τὸ ἔλαττον in HEB 7:7. Frequently compares two things or actions using ἤ (1CO 7:9, 1PE 3:17, 2PE 2:21) or παρά + accusative (HEB 9:23, HEB 12:24), or a genitive of comparison (HEB 1:4). Strengthened by πολλῷ μᾶλλον in PHP 1:23. Occurs predominantly in Hebrews (12 of 19 instances), especially modifying covenantal terms (διαθήκη, ἐλπίς, ἐπαγγελίαι, θυσίαι, ἀνάστασις).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To feel anxious distress about future needs or difficulties, or to direct attentive care and concern toward someone or a set of responsibilities.

senses.definition: To be troubled, fretful, or anxiously preoccupied about material needs, future circumstances, or impending trials.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive verb, absolute or with dative of reference, indirect question, περί + genitive/accusative, εἰς + accusative, or neuter accusative μηδέν

senses.definition: To give earnest thought, attention, or devoted care to the interests, needs, or responsibilities of a person or sphere of life.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb with accusative object (e.g., τὰ τοῦ...), genitive (ἑαυτῆς), or ὑπέρ + genitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in negated imperatives/prohibitive subjunctives (μὴ μεριμνᾶτε / μὴ μεριμνήσητε) regarding food, drink, clothing, tomorrow, or legal defense (MAT 6:25, 31, 34; 10:19; LUK 12:11, 22; PHP 4:6). Paired with θορυβάζω in LUK 10:41 and contrasted with prayerful thanksgiving in PHP 4:6. In 1CO 7:32-34 it connects conceptually with ἀμέριμνος and μερίζω (μεμέρισται), highlighting focused attention or divided devotion. In MAT 6:34 ("tomorrow will care for itself"), tomorrow is personified with the genitive ἑαυτῆς.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Complete, whole, and lacking no essential quality, or full-grown and mature in understanding and character.

senses.definition: Complete, whole, and free from deficiency or flaw, used of actions, gifts, law, love, divine will, or a heavenly sanctuary (including comparative form in HEB 9:11).
senses.grammatical_frame: attributive adjective, substantivized neuter (τὸ τέλειον), or comparative attributive

senses.definition: Whole and lacking nothing morally or spiritually, characterizing God or a person who fulfills what is required without defect.
senses.grammatical_frame: predicative or attributive adjective describing God or persons

senses.definition: Having reached full spiritual or intellectual adulthood and discernment, contrasted with childhood or elementary status.
senses.grammatical_frame: predicative, attributive (with ἀνήρ), or substantivized masculine plural adjective

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with ὁλόκληρος and glossed by ἐν μηδενὶ λειπόμενοι in JAS 1:4; paired with ἀγαθός and εὐάρεστος in ROM 12:2, with ἀγαθή in JAS 1:17, and with πεπληροφορημένος in COL 4:12. Contrasted with τὸ ἐκ μέρους in 1CO 13:10, with παιδία and νηπιάζω in 1CO 14:20, and implicitly with infancy (needing milk rather than solid food) in HEB 5:14. Comparative τελειότερος occurs once in HEB 9:11 alongside μείζων.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To receive in full or have back, to be distant from, or (in the middle voice) to abstain from; once used as an isolated exclamation signaling sufficiency or readiness.

senses.definition: To receive completely what is due or given, already possess one's full share, or get someone back permanently.
senses.grammatical_frame: active transitive verb + accusative direct object

senses.definition: To be separated by a physical distance or to be metaphorically estranged and remote in devotion.
senses.grammatical_frame: active intransitive verb + adverb of distance or accusative of extent + ἀπό + genitive

senses.definition: To keep oneself away from or refrain from engaging in specified foods, practices, or desires.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle verb + genitive object or ἀπό + genitive

senses.definition: Used as an abrupt, elliptical exclamation indicating that enough time has passed or that the present period of resting is over as the decisive hour arrives.
senses.grammatical_frame: active impersonal or elliptical 3rd person singular verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Voice and syntax sharply distinguish the senses: active transitive with an accusative object denotes receiving in full or having back (often formulaic ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν in MAT 6:2, 5, 16); active intransitive with distance expressions (πόρρω, μακράν, οὐ μακράν, or accusative of stadia + ἀπό) denotes spatial or relational remoteness; middle voice (with genitive or ἀπό + genitive) consistently denotes abstaining from prohibited items or behaviors.
entries.uncertainty_note: Senses 1a, 1b, and 1c are firmly established across 18 verses; however, the isolated single-word impersonal use (ἀπέχει) in MRK 14:41 is syntactically elliptical, so its precise nuance ("it is enough," "time is up," or "it is settled") can only be broadly inferred from the surrounding clauses.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Relating to, located in, or characteristic of heaven or the transcendent spiritual realm, frequently contrasted with what is earthly or mortal.

senses.definition: Belonging to, originating from, or associated with heaven as opposed to the earthly sphere.
senses.grammatical_frame: attributive or predicate adjective modifying nouns (e.g., σώματα, βασιλείαν, κλήσεως, δωρεᾶς, Ἱερουσαλήμ)

senses.definition: The heavenly realm, realities, or transcendent spiritual sphere (contrasted with earthly matters or physical copies).
senses.grammatical_frame: substantivized neuter plural adjective (often in the prepositional phrase ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις)

senses.definition: A heavenly being or those belonging to the heavenly order (contrasted with mortal beings of earth or the underworld).
senses.grammatical_frame: substantivized masculine singular or plural (or tripartite cosmic plural in PHP 2:10)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in direct contrast with ἐπίγειος ("earthly", JHN 3:12; 1CO 15:40; PHP 2:10), χοϊκός ("of dust", 1CO 15:48-49), and καταχθόνιος ("under the earth", PHP 2:10). In Ephesians (1:3, 1:20, 2:6, 3:10, 6:12), the fixed prepositional phrase ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις designates the transcendent spiritual sphere where Christ is enthroned, believers share spiritual blessings, and cosmic powers operate. In 1CO 15:40, the second occurrence (τῶν ἐπουρανίων) refers elliptically back to σώματα ἐπουράνια.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A physical chain or restraint, a state of imprisonment, or a disabling bodily affliction.

senses.definition: Physical chains, fetters, or restraints used to bind a captive or prisoner, including supernatural detention.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (plural, masculine or neuter)

senses.definition: Imprisonment or custody as a legal penalty or condition of confinement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (plural, masculine or neuter; frequently with ἐν or μέχρι, or with genitive pronoun μου)

senses.definition: A disabling physical impediment or affliction restricting normal bodily function.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (singular masculine; object of λύω)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Exhibits both neuter plural (τὰ δεσμά in LUK 8:29, ACT 16:26, ACT 20:23) and masculine plural forms (τοῖς δεσμοῖς, τοὺς δεσμούς, δεσμῶν). Commonly paired with λύω ("to loose/untie", MRK 7:35, LUK 13:16), θλῖψις ("affliction", ACT 20:23, PHP 1:17), θάνατος ("death", ACT 23:29, ACT 26:31), and φυλακή ("prison", HEB 11:36). In PHP 1:7, 13–14, 17, COL 4:18, 2TI 2:9, and PHM 1:10, 13, the plural regularly refers to Paul's imprisonment for the gospel.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An earnest petition, plea, or supplication directed to God, often on behalf of others.

senses.definition: An earnest personal or devotional petition, plea, or supplication addressed to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (singular or plural; subject of εἰσακούω/ἰσχύω, object of ποιέομαι/προσφέρω, or instrumental dative)

senses.definition: An intercessory prayer or petition offered to God on behalf of other people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (often modified by ὑπέρ + genitive or περί + genitive)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with προσευχή ("prayer", EPH 6:18, PHP 4:6, 1TI 2:1, 1TI 5:5), νηστεία ("fasting", LUK 2:37, LUK 5:33), and ἱκετηρία ("supplication", HEB 5:7). Commonly used with the verb ποιέομαι ("to offer/make", LUK 5:33, PHP 1:4, 1TI 2:1). Intercessory instances regularly take ὑπέρ + genitive (ROM 10:1, 2CO 1:11, 2CO 9:14, PHP 1:4, 1TI 2:1) or περί + genitive (EPH 6:18, 2TI 1:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To declare, announce, or make known publicly a message, person, practice, or report.

senses.definition: To publicly announce, declare, or proclaim a message, event, reality, or person to an audience (whether by speech, prophetic utterance, or symbolic action).
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb taking an accusative object (message, event, or person) and optionally a dative recipient; also passive with the proclaimed subject and optional agent phrase (ὑπό + genitive).

senses.definition: To publicly introduce, promote, or advocate customs or practices for others to adopt and follow.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb taking an accusative plural object (ἔθη), contrasted with παραδέχεσθαι and ποιεῖν.

senses.definition: To report widely or spread news abroad concerning someone's conduct or faith.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive verb with subject ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν and locative phrase ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes religious or salvific objects such as τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ (ACT 13:5, ACT 17:13), τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου (ACT 15:36), τὸ εὐαγγέλιον (1CO 9:14), Χριστόν / Ἰησοῦν (ACT 17:3, PHP 1:17, PHP 1:18, COL 1:28), τὴν ἀνάστασιν (ACT 4:2), ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν (ACT 13:38), ὁδὸν σωτηρίας (ACT 16:17), τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ Θεοῦ (1CO 2:1), and τὸν θάνατον τοῦ Κυρίου (1CO 11:26). Often paired with a dative of audience (e.g., ὑμῖν, τῷ τε λαῷ καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν). In 1CO 11:26, proclamation occurs through a communal liturgical meal rather than solely verbal speech. In ACT 17:13, the passive takes ὑπό + genitive of agent.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Empty-handed, devoid of truth or substance, or lacking any effective outcome or result.

senses.definition: Having received nothing; carrying away no goods, produce, or reward.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicative adjective (accusative complement of the direct object) with verbs of sending away (ἀποστέλλω, ἐξαποστέλλω).

senses.definition: Devoid of truth, substance, or real value; hollow, baseless, or futile.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective modifying nouns of speech or deception (λόγοις, ἀπάτης); neuter plural substantive as direct object (κενά); predicate adjective describing preaching or faith.

senses.definition: Without effect, productive outcome, or lasting result; unsuccessful or to no purpose.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate adjective with εἰμί or γίνομαι; prepositional phrase εἰς κενόν functioning adverbially or predicatively.

senses.definition: Lacking discernment or moral substance; foolish or shallow in understanding.
senses.grammatical_frame: Vocative adjective modifying ἄνθρωπε in direct address.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly appears in three syntactic patterns: (1) as an accusative object complement with ἀποστέλλω / ἐξαποστέλλω (MRK 12:3, LUK 1:53, LUK 20:10, LUK 20:11), (2) as a predicate adjective with εἰμί or γίνομαι (1CO 15:10, 1CO 15:14, 1CO 15:58, 1TH 2:1), and (3) in the fixed adverbial phrase εἰς κενόν modifying verbs of running, laboring, receiving, or happening (2CO 6:1, GAL 2:2, PHP 2:16, 1TH 3:5). Often contrasted with abundance, fruitfulness, or effective labor (e.g., ἐνέπλησεν ἀγαθῶν in LUK 1:53; ἐκοπίασα in 1CO 15:10).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A marker of limit or boundary meaning 'until' (in time), 'as far as' (in space), or 'to the point of' (in degree).

senses.definition: Marking the temporal endpoint or boundary up to which an action, era, or state continues.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing the genitive of a time expression, event, or person representing an era (often paired with ἀπό).

senses.definition: Marking the spatial boundary or farthest geographical point reached.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing the genitive of a geographical region (paired with ἀπό).

senses.definition: Marking the extreme degree, cost, or intensity to which an action, obedience, or suffering extends.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing the genitive of an extreme state, hardship, or bodily cost (θανάτου, δεσμῶν, αἵματος).

senses.definition: Introducing a subordinate clause that specifies the future event or state up to whose realization the main action persists.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subordinating conjunction (μέχρι alone or μέχρις οὗ) followed by the aorist subjunctive.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in the form μέχρις before a vowel in MRK 13:30, GAL 4:19, and HEB 12:4. Frequently paired with ἀπό to mark an interval from start to endpoint (ACT 10:30, ROM 5:14, ROM 15:19). Common fixed expressions include μέχρι τῆς σήμερον (ἡμέρας) (MAT 11:23, MAT 28:15), μέχρι τέλους (HEB 3:6, HEB 3:14), and μέχρι θανάτου (PHP 2:8, PHP 2:30). As a conjunction, it takes the aorist subjunctive either in the compound μέχρις οὗ (MRK 13:30, GAL 4:19) or alone (EPH 4:13).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adverb of frequency indicating that an action, state, or event occurs often or repeatedly.

senses.definition: On many occasions or at frequent intervals over time.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying verbs, participles, or (in elliptical lists) dative nouns and ἐν + dative phrases.

senses.definition: Iteratively or over and over again, in explicit contrast to a once-for-all occurrence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying verbs or participles of cultic offering or suffering (προσφέρω, πάσχω), contrasted with ἅπαξ.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Functions as a frequency adverb modifying finite verbs, infinitives, participles (including attributive participle in HEB 6:7), and elliptical noun or prepositional phrases in hardship catalogues (2CO 11:23, 2CO 11:26, 2CO 11:27). In HEB 9:25-26 and HEB 10:11, it is explicitly contrasted with ἅπαξ ('once') and associated with cyclical expressions like κατ’ ἐνιαυτόν and καθ’ ἡμέραν.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A wreath or crown placed on the head as a mark of royalty, victory, or mockery, and figuratively an eschatological reward or person who brings honor and joy.

senses.definition: A circular band, wreath, or crown worn on the head, made of woven thorns to mock royal claims or of gold or stars in visionary scenes to signify royal status, honor, or victory.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, object of verbs of placing, wearing, having, giving, or casting (ἐπιτίθημι, περιτίθημι, φορέω, ἔχω, δίδωμι, βάλλω), commonly with ἐπί + genitive/accusative of the head (κεφαλή)

senses.definition: A victor's prize or promised eschatological reward granted for athletic self-discipline, endurance under trial, or faithful service.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, object of verbs of receiving or awarding (λαμβάνω, κομίζω, ἀποδίδωμι, δίδωμι), often qualified by adjectives of durability (φθαρτός, ἄφθαρτος, ἀμαράντινος) or descriptive genitives (δικαιοσύνης, ζωῆς, δόξης)

senses.definition: A figurative title for persons whose faithfulness constitutes another's pride, honor, and vindication.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, used predicatively or appositionally with personal reference, accompanied by a possessive genitive (μου) or genitive of quality (καυχήσεως)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in prepositional phrases with ἐπί indicating placement on the head (ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς / ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς, MAT 27:29, JHN 19:2, REV 4:4, REV 9:7, REV 12:1, REV 14:14) and with verbs of weaving (πλέκω, MAT 27:29, MRK 15:17, JHN 19:2), giving (δίδωμι, ἀποδίδωμι), and receiving (λαμβάνω, κομίζω). Contrasted as perishable versus imperishable in athletic imagery (φθαρτόν / ἄφθαρτον, 1CO 9:25) and paired with χαρὰ (PHP 4:1, 1TH 2:19). Descriptive genitives specify the nature or content of the eschatological reward (τῆς δικαιοσύνης, 2TI 4:8; τῆς ζωῆς, JAS 1:12, REV 2:10; τῆς δόξης, 1PE 5:4).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Openly visible, clear, or widely known, and in neuter prepositional phrases denoting public exposure or outward, external appearance.

senses.definition: Readily perceived, obvious, clearly recognizable, or publicly known by people, rather than concealed or ambiguous.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate adjective with εἰμί, γίνομαι, or ποιέω, often taking a dative of the observer (τῷ Φαραώ, πᾶσιν) or a locative phrase (ἐν αὐτοῖς, ἐν ὑμῖν, ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ πραιτωρίῳ)

senses.definition: The open sphere of public awareness or visibility, used in the expression denoting disclosure of what was hidden.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival anarthrous neuter singular adjective after εἰς with ἔρχομαι (εἰς φανερὸν ἔλθῃ)

senses.definition: What is outward, external, or observable on the physical surface rather than inward.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantival articular neuter singular adjective after ἐν (ἐν τῷ φανερῷ), modifying nouns adjectivally/adverbially
senses.semantic_domain: Appearance / Contrast of Outer and Inner

entries.collocations_and_notes: Repeatedly contrasted with hiddenness terms κρυπτόν and ἀπόκρυφον (MRK 4:22, LUK 8:17, 1CO 14:25) and paired with verbs of knowing or revealing such as γνωρίζω, δηλόω, and ἀποκαλύπτω (LUK 8:17, ACT 4:16, ACT 7:13, 1CO 3:13). Commonly occurs with γίνομαι (MRK 6:14, LUK 8:17, ACT 7:13, 1CO 3:13, 1CO 11:19, 1CO 14:25, PHP 1:13) or ποιέω (MAT 12:16, MRK 3:12).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Final ruin or destruction, especially as divine judgment, and in two Gospel passages the wasteful loss of a costly commodity.

senses.definition: Complete ruin, destruction, or perdition—especially as the final outcome of divine judgment or false teaching—including descriptive genitive uses marking persons doomed to ruin or teachings that bring it about.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, often in directional prepositional phrases (εἰς ἀπώλειαν, πρὸς ... ἀπώλειαν), as predicate nominative, or as a qualifying genitive (υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας)

senses.definition: Needless squandering or unproductive loss of a valuable material substance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, subject of an indignant question (εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη) with optional objective genitive of the item expended (τοῦ μύρου)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most frequently appears in the directional prepositional construction εἰς (τὴν) ἀπώλειαν (MAT 7:13, ACT 8:20, ROM 9:22, HEB 10:39, REV 17:8, REV 17:11) or πρὸς ... ἀπώλειαν (2PE 3:16). Contrasted directly with σωτηρία (PHP 1:28) and περιποίησις ψυχῆς (HEB 10:39), and paired with ὄλεθρος (1TI 6:9) and κρίσις (2PE 3:7). In JHN 17:12 and 2TH 2:3, the Hebraic-style genitive phrase ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας designates an individual marked out for ruin.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To earn profit, acquire something of value, win people over, or spare oneself harm or loss.

senses.definition: To earn money or make a commercial profit through trade or investment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active (transitive with monetary object or absolute)

senses.definition: To acquire or obtain something treated as a supreme prize or possession, contrasted with suffering loss.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active, transitive with accusative object

senses.definition: To win a person over to reconciliation, faith, or salvation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active (transitive with personal object) or passive (with personal subject)

senses.definition: To spare oneself or avoid incurring an unwelcome hardship or loss by refraining from a course of action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active, transitive with accusative objects of harm/loss following a negated infinitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with ζημιόω ("to suffer loss/forfeit") and ζημία ("loss") in MAT 16:26, MRK 8:36, LUK 9:25, ACT 27:21, and PHP 3:8. In 1CO 9:19–22 it occurs five times in purpose clauses (ἵνα) parallel to σώσω ("that I might save", 1CO 9:22). Notice the rare aorist subjunctive form κερδάνω in 1CO 9:21 alongside the sigmatic aorist forms elsewhere.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Intense emotional ardor or passion that manifests positively as devoted enthusiasm or concern, negatively as envious rivalry and hostility, or metaphorically as fierce, consuming intensity.

senses.definition: Ardent devotion, eager enthusiasm, or protective concern directed toward God, another person, or a cause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (masculine, or neuter in 2CO 9:2); occurs with objective genitives (τοῦ οἴκου σου, Θεοῦ), with κατά + accusative or ὑπέρ + genitive, and as an instrumental dative with the cognate verb ζηλῶ.

senses.definition: Hostile jealousy, resentment, or contentious rivalry toward others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; used as genitive complement of ἐπλήσθησαν ('were filled with'), object of ἔχω (modified by πικρός in JAS 3:14), or coordinated in lists with ἔρις and ἐριθεία.

senses.definition: Fierce, consuming intensity or fury, predicated of fire in judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun modified by the genitive πυρός ('of fire') and acting as subject of the infinitive ἐσθίειν ('to consume').

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often paired in vice lists or conflicts with ἔρις ("strife") and ἐριθεία ("selfish ambition/rivalry") (ROM 13:13; 1CO 3:3; 2CO 12:20; GAL 5:20; JAS 3:14, 3:16), and appears as the genitive complement of ἐπλήσθησαν ("were filled with") in ACT 5:17 and 13:45. In 2CO 11:2 it serves as a cognate dative with ζηλῶ (Θεοῦ ζήλῳ), expressing protective, betrothal-like devotion. Note the grammatical variation in 2CO 9:2, where it takes the neuter singular article τὸ (τὸ ὑμῶν ζῆλος), whereas elsewhere it is masculine (e.g., ὁ ζῆλος in JHN 2:17; τὸν ζῆλον in 2CO 7:7).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Inner sorrow, emotional grief, physical or situational distress, or grudging reluctance.

senses.definition: Deep emotional sorrow, grief, or heartache, whether felt internally or caused by another's conduct.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun; serves as subject of verbs (εἰμί, πληρόω, γίνομαι, ἐργάζομαι), direct object of ἔχω, or object of prepositions (ἀπό, ἐν); modified by adjectives (μεγάλη, περισσοτέρα) or qualifying phrases (κατὰ Θεόν, τοῦ κόσμου).

senses.definition: Pain, hardship, or distress arising from physical labor, discipline, or unjust mistreatment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, singular (object of ἔχω, or predicate genitive contrasted with χαρᾶς) or plural (object of ὑποφέρω in 1PE 2:19); paralleled with θλῖψις in JHN 16:21.

senses.definition: Grudging reluctance or inner unwillingness in giving, contrasted with cheerfulness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun in the prepositional phrase ἐκ λύπης, coordinated with ἐξ ἀνάγκης ('out of compulsion').

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted directly with χαρά ("joy") or χαίρω ("to rejoice") (JHN 16:20–22; 2CO 2:3; HEB 12:11) and paired with weeping, lamentation, or anguish (κλαύσετε καὶ θρηνήσετε in JHN 16:20; ἀδιάλειπτος ὀδύνη in ROM 9:2). In 2CO 7:10, two kinds are contrasted: ἡ κατὰ Θεὸν λύπη (producing repentance toward salvation) and ἡ τοῦ κόσμου λύπη (producing death). Idiomatic accumulation appears in PHP 2:27 (λύπην ἐπὶ λύπην, "sorrow upon sorrow"). In 2CO 9:7, ἐκ λύπης is paired with ἐξ ἀνάγκης ("out of compulsion") and contrasted with a cheerful giver (ἱλαρὸν δότην).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Adverb of degree meaning exceedingly or intensely in its positive form, and even more, far more, or especially in its comparative form.

senses.definition: To an extraordinary degree or intense pitch, characterizing vehement shouting, astonishment, or rage.
senses.grammatical_frame: Positive adverb (περισσῶς) modifying verbs of vocalization or intense emotion (κράζω, ἐκπλήσσομαι, ἐμμαίνομαι).

senses.definition: To a greater or more abundant degree than others or than before; all the more or especially.
senses.grammatical_frame: Comparative adverb (περισσοτέρως) modifying finite verbs, infinitives, predicative nouns (ζηλωτής), or prepositional phrases (πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐν κόποις, ἐν φυλακαῖς); once reinforced by μᾶλλον (2CO 7:13) and once contrasted with ἧσσον (2CO 12:15).

entries.collocations_and_notes: All occurrences in MAT, MRK, and ACT use the positive adverb περισσῶς, whereas all occurrences in 2CO, GAL, PHP, 1TH, and HEB use the comparative form περισσοτέρως. In MAT 27:23 and MRK 15:14, περισσῶς ἔκραζον/ἔκραξαν describes the crowd shouting all the more vehemently in response to Pilate's question. Comparative περισσοτέρως appears pleonastically with μᾶλλον in 2CO 7:13 (περισσοτέρως μᾶλλον ἐχάρημεν), parallel with ὑπερβαλλόντως ("beyond measure") in 2CO 11:23, and contrasted with ἧσσον ("less") in 2CO 12:15.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Afflictions or hardships endured—especially physical suffering, persecution, or death—or strong inner impulses and desires oriented toward sin.

senses.definition: Hardships, afflictions, or painful experiences endured, including persecution and the suffering of death.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun, usually plural (singular only in HEB 2:9 with τοῦ θανάτου); frequently followed by τοῦ Χριστοῦ/αὐτοῦ or εἰς Χριστόν, governed by nouns/verbs of sharing (κοινωνία, κοινωνός, κοινωνέω) or endurance (ὑπομονή, ὑπομένω), or used with διά and ἐν.

senses.definition: Strong inner impulses, cravings, or desires associated with sinful conduct and the flesh.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter plural noun; modified by the genitive τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ('of sins') in ROM 7:5, or coordinated with ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις ('desires') after σύν in GAL 5:24.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in the plural (παθήματα) in 15 of 16 occurrences; the sole singular (τὸ πάθημα τοῦ θανάτου) occurs in HEB 2:9. When denoting affliction (sense 1a), it frequently collocates with τοῦ Χριστοῦ / αὐτοῦ / εἰς Χριστόν, with words of sharing or endurance (κοινωνός, κοινωνία, κοινωνέω, ὑπομονή, ὑπομένω), and with the cognate verb πάσχω (2CO 1:6), and is contrasted with δόξα ("glory") or παράκλησις ("comfort") (ROM 8:18; 2CO 1:5, 1:7; 1PE 1:11, 4:13, 5:1). In sense 1b, it is paired with ἐπιθυμίαι ("desires") in GAL 5:24 and linked to ἁμαρτίαι ("sins") in ROM 7:5.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To seize or arrest someone, catch prey, conceive offspring in the womb, or come alongside someone to help.

senses.definition: To lay hold of and apprehend a person by force or authority, typically to take into custody, bind, or bring to trial or harm.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active or middle verb taking a personal accusative object; passive with ὑπό + genitive indicating the arresting agents.

senses.definition: To capture or haul in fish or other prey during hunting or fishing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb with an implied accusative object (attracted to dative in relative clause).

senses.definition: To become pregnant with or conceive a child in the womb (or, in the passive, for a child to be conceived).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active or middle verb used absolutely, with ἐν γαστρί, or with an accusative object (υἱόν); passive infinitive with the conceived child as accusative subject and ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ.

senses.definition: Figuratively, for an inward desire to conceive and generate an ensuing moral outcome, depicted through childbirth imagery.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active participle used absolutely with an abstract subject (ἐπιθυμία).

senses.definition: To join with and lend assistance to someone in carrying out a demanding task or shared endeavor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle verb taking a personal object in the dative.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Distinct voice patterns correlate with sense: active (and once middle in ACT 26:21) or passive (ACT 23:27) with a personal accusative object expresses arrest/seizure; active/middle with ἐν γαστρί or ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ (or υἱόν as object) expresses biological conception; middle with a dative object (LUK 5:7, PHP 4:3) expresses lending aid. In JAS 1:15, συλλαβοῦσα pairs with τίκτει ("gives birth to") and ἀποκύει ("brings forth") in an extended birth metaphor. In arrest contexts, it frequently co-occurs with leading away (ἤγαγον), binding (ἔδησαν), or weapons (μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To summon the courage to act despite fear or risk, or to presume to do something bold or audacious.

senses.definition: To overcome fear, awe, or danger and summon the courage to perform an action; often negated when people shrink back from acting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb followed by a complementary infinitive, or participle accompanying a finite verb of action (MRK 15:43).

senses.definition: To have the audacity or presumption to cross a proper moral, social, or spiritual boundary (whether criticized in others or disavowed by the speaker).
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb followed by a complementary infinitive.

senses.definition: To act boldly, adopt a forceful stance against opponents, or speak with daring self-assertion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Infinitive with ἐπί + accusative indicating those confronted, or finite verb used absolutely or with ἐν + dative specifying the ground of boldness.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently negated (οὐδὲ ... τις, οὐδεὶς οὐκέτι, οὐκ, οὐ γάρ) to mark hesitation out of awe, fear, or restraint (MAT 22:46, MRK 12:34, LUK 20:40, JHN 21:12, ACT 5:13, ACT 7:32, ROM 15:18, 2CO 10:12, JUD 1:9). Often pairs with verbs of questioning (ἐπερωτάω, ἐξετάζω) or speaking (λαλέω, κρίσιν ἐπενεγκεῖν). In 2CO 10:2 it parallels θαρρῆσαι τῇ πεποιθήσει ("act boldly with confidence"), and in PHP 1:14 it collocates with πεποιθότας ("confident") and ἀφόβως ("fearlessly").

entries.core_meaning_summary: To stay in a place or with someone for a time, continue an action, or persevere in a state, attitude, or teaching.

senses.definition: To stay or remain at a location or in someone's company for a period of time.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb often accompanied by an accusative of time duration, an adverb of place, or prepositional phrases (ἐν + dative, παρά + dative, πρός + accusative).

senses.definition: To remain alive in bodily existence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Articular infinitive with a dative of sphere (τῇ σαρκί).

senses.definition: To continue doing an action persistently without stopping.
senses.grammatical_frame: Finite verb followed by a supplementary present participle.

senses.definition: To continue steadfastly or persist in an inner disposition, moral course, faith, or instruction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb (indicative, subjunctive, or imperative) taking a dative complement specifying the condition, practice, or teaching.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Syntactic construction clearly distinguishes spatial/temporal remaining from behavioral/spiritual persistence: spatial uses take accusatives of duration (e.g., ἡμέρας τρεῖς/ἑπτά/δεκαπέντε, χρόνον τινά) and locative/associative expressions (αὐτοῦ, ἐν Ἐφέσῳ, παρ’ αὐτοῖς, πρὸς ὑμᾶς/αὐτόν); ongoing action takes a supplementary present participle (JHN 8:7, ACT 12:16); moral or spiritual persistence takes a dative complement (τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, τῇ χρηστότητι, τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ, τῇ πίστει, αὐτοῖς). In COL 1:23, it is reinforced by τεθεμελιωμένοι καὶ ἑδραῖοι καὶ μὴ μετακινούμενοι ("established, steadfast, and not shifting").

entries.core_meaning_summary: A hired laborer or artisan who works for pay, figuratively a minister or missionary, or a doer of a specified moral quality.

senses.definition: A person hired for manual, agricultural, or skilled trade work in exchange for wages or sustenance (including proverbial references to such workers applied to Christian ministers).
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun used alone, with a prepositional modifier (περὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα), or with an attributive participle (τῶν ἀμησάντων).

senses.definition: Figuratively, a person engaged in spiritual mission, teaching, or ministry (depicted either as a harvester sent by God or characterized by adjectives as faithful or deceitful).
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun used in harvest metaphors or modified by evaluative adjectives (δόλιοι, κακούς, ἀνεπαίσχυντον).

senses.definition: A practitioner or doer of a particular kind of moral behavior.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun governing an abstract noun in the genitive (ἀδικίας).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with terms for remuneration or support: μισθός ("wages" in MAT 20:8, LUK 10:7, 1TI 5:18, JAS 5:4), μισθόομαι ("hire" in MAT 20:1), δηναρίου ("a denarius" in MAT 20:2), and τροφή ("food" in MAT 10:10). The saying ἄξιος (γὰρ) ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ/τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ appears in MAT 10:10, LUK 10:7, and 1TI 5:18. In harvest sayings (MAT 9:37–38, LUK 10:2), it pairs with θερισμός ("harvest"). In epistles, evaluative modifiers distinguish faithful workers (ἀνεπαίσχυντον in 2TI 2:15) from harmful ones (δόλιοι in 2CO 11:13, κακούς in PHP 3:2).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To lack, run short of, experience scarcity, or fall short of a standard or comparison.

senses.definition: To be missing, be without, or run out of something needed or expected.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active (intransitive, with accusative or genitive of the thing lacking, or in a genitive absolute)

senses.definition: To experience material want, scarcity, or poverty.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle or passive, absolute

senses.definition: To fall short of, be deficient in, or fail to attain a spiritual gift, promise, or divine standard.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active (absolute or with ἀπό + genitive) or middle/passive (with genitive or ἐν + dative)

senses.definition: To be inferior to, rank behind, or stand at a disadvantage compared to another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active (with accusative of respect and genitive of comparison) or middle/passive (absolute)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with περισσεύω ("to have an abundance/advantage", 1CO 8:8, 1CO 12:24, PHP 4:12) and paired with verbs of hardship such as θλίβομαι, κακουχέομαι, and πεινάω (PHP 4:12, HEB 11:37). Takes a genitive of comparison when expressing rank relative to others (2CO 11:5, 2CO 12:11), a genitive of the thing lacking (LUK 22:35, JHN 2:3, ROM 3:23), or ἀπό + genitive (HEB 12:15). In MRK 10:21 the thing lacking (ἕν) stands as subject with the person in the accusative (σε). In 2CO 11:9 it appears alongside the cognate noun ὑστέρημα.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An enclitic focusing particle that emphasizes, restricts, or adds pointed force to the preceding word, clause, or conjunction ("at least," "indeed," "even").

senses.definition: Restricts attention to a minimal sufficient reason or partial concession in contrast to a broader statement.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic particle following a preposition (διά) or adversative conjunction (ἀλλά)

senses.definition: Adds emphatic or assertive weight to a contrast, addition, relative clause, direct question, or wish.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic particle following conjunctions (ἀλλά, καί, ἀλλὰ μὲν οὖν), interrogatives (ἆρα), optative particles (ὄφελον), or relative pronouns (ὅς)

senses.definition: Highlights a conditional clause as an essential qualification, a minimal possibility, or a condition treated as presumed true.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic particle following a conditional conjunction (εἰ or εἰ ἄρα)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Always postpositive (placed after the word or phrase it highlights). Frequent combinations include εἴ γε (marking an assumed or crucial condition, 2CO 5:3, GAL 3:4, EPH 3:2, EPH 4:21, COL 1:23), εἰ ἄρα γε (ACT 17:27), διά γε (LUK 11:8, LUK 18:5), ἀλλά γε (LUK 24:21, 1CO 9:2), ἀλλὰ μὲν οὖν γε (PHP 3:8), καί γε (ACT 17:27), ἆρά γε (ACT 8:30), ὄφελόν γε (1CO 4:8), and ὅς γε (ROM 8:32). Often reinforces an accompanying καί (LUK 24:21, 2CO 5:3, GAL 3:4, PHP 3:8).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Grateful acknowledgment, thankfulness, or a verbal/liturgical expression of thanks offered to a benefactor or to God.

senses.definition: An attitude, disposition, or expression of gratitude and appreciation directed toward a human ruler or toward God.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, singular or plural, often with μετά, ἐν, or dative indirect object (τῷ Θεῷ)

senses.definition: A spoken prayer, blessing, or liturgical ascription of thanks offered to God in worship, petition, or over food.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, singular or plural, paired with prayer or doxological nouns or governed by μετά / ἐν / ἐπί

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in prepositional phrases with μετά (ACT 24:3, PHP 4:6, 1TI 4:3, 1TI 4:4) or ἐν (COL 2:7, COL 4:2), and with the dative recipient τῷ Θεῷ (2CO 9:11, 2CO 9:12, 1TH 3:9; compare REV 4:9, REV 7:12). Often paired with terms for prayer such as προσευχή, δέησις, and ἔντευξις (PHP 4:6, COL 4:2, 1TI 2:1) or with doxological terms like δόξα, τιμή, and εὐλογία (REV 4:9, REV 7:12). Uses in prayer over food (1TI 4:3, 1TI 4:4) and in petition (PHP 4:6, COL 4:2) bridge inward gratefulness and spoken expressions of thanks.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To lay hold of, overtake, or catch someone or something; to attain a goal; or, especially in the middle voice, to grasp mentally and perceive.

senses.definition: To seize, overtake, or come upon someone suddenly or overwhelmingly, whether by an external force, darkness, a day of judgment, or Christ.
senses.grammatical_frame: active or passive transitive verb with personal or concrete direct object (or passive with ὑπό + agent)

senses.definition: To catch or apprehend someone in the act of wrongdoing.
senses.grammatical_frame: passive verb with prepositional phrase (ἐν μοιχείᾳ) or participle/adverbial modifier (ἐπαυτοφώρῳ μοιχευομένη)

senses.definition: To reach, win, or successfully attain a sought-after goal or prize, often in athletic or pursuit imagery.
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb, used either transitively with an abstract object (δικαιοσύνην) or absolutely in contexts of running (τρέχω) or pursuing (διώκω)

senses.definition: To grasp mentally, recognize, ascertain, or comprehend a fact or dimension.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle verb taking a ὅτι clause, an accusative-infinitive clause, or an indirect question (τί ...)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Shows clear voice patterns: the middle voice regularly denotes mental perception or grasping (ACT 4:13, ACT 10:34, ACT 25:25, EPH 3:18), whereas active and passive forms denote physically seizing, catching, overtaking, or attaining a goal (MRK 9:18, JHN 8:3, JHN 8:4, JHN 12:35, ROM 9:30, 1CO 9:24, PHP 3:12, PHP 3:13, 1TH 5:4). In PHP 3:12, the active (καταλάβω) and passive (κατελήμφθην ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ) are juxtaposed in the same sentence to contrast Paul's ongoing pursuit with Christ's prior seizure of him. In JHN 1:5, the active verb with ἡ σκοτία ("the darkness") as subject is contextually ambiguous between "overtake/overcome" (as in JHN 12:35) and "comprehend/grasp" (sense 1d).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To feed to the full or, in the passive, to eat one's fill and have hunger or deep desire satisfied.
