senses.definition: To provide enough food for people so that their hunger is completely satisfied.
senses.grammatical_frame: active transitive verb with accusative of person and optional genitive of food (ἄρτων)

senses.definition: To eat until full, be well fed, or have one's appetite satisfied (used of humans and scavenging birds).
senses.grammatical_frame: passive verb, often coordinated with ἐσθίω or contrasted with πεινάω, occasionally with ἀπό or ἐκ + genitive of the food source

senses.definition: To have a deep moral or spiritual longing completely fulfilled, expressed under the metaphor of hunger and thirst.
senses.grammatical_frame: passive verb predicated of those who hunger and thirst for righteousness (οἱ πεινῶντες καὶ διψῶντες τὴν δικαιοσύνην)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with ἐσθίω ("eat") in narrative accounts of miraculous feedings (MAT 14:20, MAT 15:37, MRK 6:42, MRK 8:8, LUK 9:17, JHN 6:26) and contrasted directly with πεινάω ("be hungry": MAT 5:6, LUK 6:21, PHP 4:12). In LUK 6:21, the promise to "those who hunger now" parallels beatitudes about weeping, pointing primarily to literal hunger reversed by God's provision while also resonating with MAT 5:6. Source of food in passive constructions can be marked by ἀπό (LUK 16:21) or ἐκ (REV 19:21).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Inner thought, reasoning, or questioning of the mind or heart, as well as interpersonal argument or dispute.

senses.definition: Inward thought, reasoning, deliberation, or intention occurring within a person's heart or mind, often hidden from other humans and judged morally.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (usually plural), frequently modified by τῆς καρδίας or possessive genitives, or paired with moral adjectives (πονηροί, κακοί, μάταιοι).

senses.definition: Troubled questioning or doubt arising within a person's heart in response to distress or disbelief.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural subject with verb of arising (ἀναβαίνουσιν) + ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ, parallel to τεταραγμένοι ('troubled').

senses.definition: Dispute, argument, or contentious opinion among people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural), used with ἐν αὐτοῖς introducing an indirect question (LUK 9:46), in genitive depending on διακρίσεις (ROM 14:1), or after χωρίς paired with words for grumbling or anger (PHP 2:14, 1TI 2:8).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Strongly associated with the 'heart' (καρδία) as the inner seat of thought (MAT 15:19, MRK 7:21, LUK 2:35, LUK 5:22, LUK 9:47, LUK 24:38, ROM 1:21). Often qualified negatively as πονηροί ('evil', MAT 15:19, JAS 2:4), κακοί ('bad', MRK 7:21), or μάταιοι ('futile', 1CO 3:20; cf. ἐματαιώθησαν in ROM 1:21). Note the overlap between 1a and 1c in LUK 9:46–47, where an interpersonal argument among the disciples (9:46) is referred to as 'the reasoning of their heart' (9:47). Paired with γογγυσμῶν ('grumblings', PHP 2:14) and ὀργῆς ('anger', 1TI 2:8).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Qualitative relative or exclamative pronoun/adjective indicating the kind, character, or degree of someone or something ('such as', 'of what sort').

senses.definition: Of such a kind, character, or magnitude as; introducing a qualitative comparison or characterization relative to an antecedent or correlative demonstrative.
senses.grammatical_frame: Relative qualitative adjective/pronoun agreeing in gender and number with its referent or antecedent, often correlated with τοιοῦτος, οὕτως, or ὁ αὐτός.

senses.definition: What kind of or how great, expressing character or intensity in an indirect question or exclamation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qualitative adjective/pronoun in indirect question after οἴδατε (1TH 1:5) or modifying a noun (οἵους διωγμούς, 2TI 3:11).

senses.definition: Used in the negated neuter phrase οὐχ οἷον ὅτι to reject a potential inference ('not as though', 'it is not the case that').
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter singular nominative/adverbial pronoun in the fixed phrase οὐχ οἷον + ὅτι-clause.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly correlates with demonstratives or adverbs of manner such as τοιοῦτος (MRK 13:19, 1CO 15:48, 2CO 10:11), οὕτως (MRK 9:3), or ὁ αὐτός (PHP 1:30). Frequently introduces hyperbolic or superlative comparisons of unprecedented scale (οἷα/οἷος οὐ γέγονεν/οὐκ ἐγένετο in MAT 24:21, MRK 13:19, REV 16:18). The negated neuter construction οὐχ οἷον ὅτι appears once (ROM 9:6) as a clause-level disclaimer.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To look forward to something with expectation, or to welcome and accept a person, offer, or circumstance.

senses.definition: To wait eagerly and expectantly for the arrival or realization of someone or something promised or anticipated.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle/deponent verb + accusative object (thing or person); occasionally with indirect question or relative pronoun referencing an anticipated event

senses.definition: To welcome a person hospitably into one's company, household, or community fellowship.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle/deponent verb + accusative personal object (often modified by ἐν Κυρίῳ)

senses.definition: To accept or consent to an offered outcome or difficult treatment without refusal or resistance.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle/deponent verb + accusative abstract noun (with negation in HEB 11:35)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes accusative objects denoting eschatological or promised realities (the kingdom of God, consolation of Israel, redemption of Jerusalem, blessed hope, mercy) in expectant contexts. In hospitable contexts it pairs with eating together (LUK 15:2) or receiving someone 'in the Lord' (ROM 16:2, PHP 2:29), and in HEB 10:34 it co-occurs with 'with joy' (μετὰ χαρᾶς) to express willing endurance of loss.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To bring down or lower in elevation, social standing, pride, or material circumstances, either voluntarily or through outside action.

senses.definition: To reduce the physical height of raised landforms so that terrain becomes level.
senses.grammatical_frame: passive verb with inanimate geographical subjects (mountain and hill)

senses.definition: To lower oneself voluntarily in status, self-importance, or pretension, adopting an attitude of submission or modest service.
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb + reflexive pronoun (ἑαυτόν / ἐμαυτόν), or passive imperative with middle/reflexive force (often with ἐνώπιον or ὑπό + accusative)

senses.definition: To be brought down in standing or humbled by God or another agent, especially in reversal of self-exaltation or failure.
senses.grammatical_frame: passive future verb (with personal subject) or active transitive verb + personal object

senses.definition: To experience lowly, straitened, or needy material circumstances.
senses.grammatical_frame: passive/middle infinitive contrasted with περισσεύειν ('have abundance')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Repeatedly paired as an antonym with ὑψόω ('exalt/lift up') in proverbial reversals (MAT 23:12, LUK 14:11, LUK 18:14) and exhortations (2CO 11:7, JAS 4:10, 1PE 5:6). Note the voice distinction: active forms consistently take an explicit object (most often a reflexive pronoun for voluntary self-lowering, or a personal object in 2CO 12:21 for being humbled by God), whereas passive imperatives (JAS 4:10, 1PE 5:6) function reflexively/middle-like as calls to willing submission.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A visible mark, sculpted representation, guiding design, written form, prefiguring counterpart, or behavioral model.

senses.definition: A physical impression or scar left behind in a surface by an object.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun + genitive of the object leaving the mark (τῶν ἥλων)

senses.definition: A manufactured physical figure or image crafted for religious veneration.
senses.grammatical_frame: plural noun as object of ποιέω ('make') with purpose infinitive προσκυνεῖν ('worship')

senses.definition: A revealed design, structural blueprint, or standard form to which construction or instruction conforms.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun governed by κατά + accusative (construction blueprint) or modified by genitive διδαχῆς ('standard of teaching')

senses.definition: The form, wording, or general contents of a written letter.
senses.grammatical_frame: accusative noun with demonstrative τοῦτον as object of ἔχουσαν modifying ἐπιστολήν

senses.definition: A historical person or past event serving as a prefiguring counterpart or cautionary lesson for later people.
senses.grammatical_frame: predicate nominative with ἐστίν or γίνομαι + genitive of reference

senses.definition: A person or community whose conduct serves as a model or standard for others to imitate.
senses.grammatical_frame: predicate or appositional noun with γίνομαι, ἔχω, δίδωμι, or παρέχομαι, often with dative or genitive of the observers/virtues

entries.collocations_and_notes: In pattern/design contexts it co-occurs with κατὰ τόν ('according to the pattern', ACT 7:44, HEB 8:5). In moral exhortation it regularly takes a genitive of the group or virtues exemplified or appears with verbs of imitation (συνμιμηταί in PHP 3:17; μιμεῖσθαι in 2TH 3:9). In ACT 23:25, 'having this form/tenor' introduces the verbatim or summary text of an official letter.

entries.core_meaning_summary: One single time, either as a numerical count or as a decisive, unrepeatable event, as well as in fixed phrases meaning 'more than once' or 'yet one more time'.

senses.definition: On one single occasion, as a count of frequency or within a recurring period.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying a verb or infinitive, optionally with genitive of time period (τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ)

senses.definition: On a single decisive occasion without need or possibility of repetition.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying aorist or perfect verbs/participles denoting completed or definitive action

senses.definition: In the coordinated expression καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δίς, indicating multiple or repeated occasions.
senses.grammatical_frame: fixed coordinated phrase καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δίς modifying an action verb

senses.definition: In the expression ἔτι ἅπαξ, denoting one additional and final occasion still to come.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverbial phrase ἔτι ἅπαξ modifying a future verb (or cited substantively with τό)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Contrasted explicitly with τρίς ('three times', 2CO 11:25), πολλάκις ('many times', HEB 9:26), and ἐκ δευτέρου ('a second time', HEB 9:28). Forms two fixed expressions in this corpus: καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δίς ('more than once' / 'repeatedly', PHP 4:16, 1TH 2:18) and ἔτι ἅπαξ ('yet once more', HEB 12:26, HEB 12:27). In JUD 1:5 (εἰδότας ἅπαξ πάντα), it appears with a participle indicating that the recipients already/once for all know the facts being recalled.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To carry or spread through, be driven about, differ from another, surpass in value, or matter to someone.

senses.definition: To carry an object through a space, or (in the passive) to be spread and circulated throughout a region.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active + accusative + διά + genitive; or passive + διά + genitive

senses.definition: To be driven back and forth or tossed about on open water during a storm.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive + ἐν + dative of location

senses.definition: To be distinct or different from another entity in quality or status.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive active + genitive of comparison (with ἐν + dative or οὐδέν)

senses.definition: To surpass in worth or importance; as a substantivized neuter plural participle (τὰ διαφέροντα), things that are superior or truly essential.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive active + genitive of comparison; or substantivized participle τὰ διαφέροντα

senses.definition: To make a difference or be of personal concern to someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Impersonal active (with οὐδέν) + dative of person

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly appears with a genitive of comparison and adverbs of degree (μᾶλλον, πόσῳ, οὐδέν). In ROM 2:18 and PHP 1:10, τὰ διαφέροντα occurs as the object of δοκιμάζω ('test/approve'); while context favors 'what is superior / what matters most', the phrase could also carry the sense of discerning differences or distinctions.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To arrive at a geographical destination, reach a person or group, or attain to a promised goal or state.

senses.definition: To reach or arrive at a city, port, or coastal point at the end of a journey or sea voyage.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive + εἰς + accusative of place (or ἄντικρυς + genitive)

senses.definition: Of a message or historical era, to reach or come upon a people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive (abstract subject) + εἰς + personal accusative

senses.definition: To attain to or arrive at a promised hope, spiritual maturity, or future resurrection.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive + εἰς + accusative of abstract goal or state

entries.collocations_and_notes: Almost always construed with εἰς + accusative (once with ἄντικρυς + genitive in ACT 20:15). In Acts it is a recurring travel verb for arriving at cities and ports (often paired with sailing vocabulary like ἀποπλέω, τὸν πλοῦν διανύω, περιέρχομαι); in Paul and ACT 26:7 it describes reaching historical eras, audiences, or eschatological and spiritual goals.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Manner, way, or means by which something is done or happens, and by extension a person's habitual conduct or way of life.

senses.definition: The manner, method, respect, or means in which an action occurs or a comparison holds.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun in adverbial accusative, dative of manner, or prepositional phrase with κατά (acc.) or ἐν (dat.), often introducing comparative clauses (ὃν τρόπον, καθ’ ὃν τρόπον).

senses.definition: A person's characteristic way of life, conduct, or moral disposition, specifically in relation to money and contentment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine nominative subject with predicate adjective (ἀφιλάργυρος) and accompanying participle.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most occurrences appear in adverbial or prepositional constructions rather than as an independent subject. Frequently forms relative clauses of comparison: accusative ὃν τρόπον ('in the way that, just as', MAT 23:37, LUK 13:34, ACT 1:11, ACT 7:28, 2TI 3:8; paired with οὕτως in ACT 1:11, 2TI 3:8) and καθ’ ὃν τρόπον (ACT 15:11, ACT 27:25). Also appears in universal or negated expressions of manner: κατὰ πάντα τρόπον ('in every way', ROM 3:2), παντὶ τρόπῳ (PHP 1:18), ἐν παντὶ τρόπῳ (2TH 3:16), κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον ('in no way', 2TH 2:3), and τὸν ὅμοιον τρόπον + dative ('in a similar way to', JUD 1:7). Sense 1b (HEB 13:5) is attested once as a nominative subject linked to financial contentment.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To search for, strive after, or earnestly desire and request someone or something.

senses.definition: To look for or try to locate a person who is absent or missing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive active verb with personal accusative direct object.

senses.definition: To strive after, pursue, or earnestly desire to obtain something (whether material provisions, a spiritual goal, or a future homeland).
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive active verb with non-personal accusative object (or relative object in ROM 11:7).

senses.definition: To ask for, demand, or seek to hear or have a matter investigated and settled.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive active verb with accusative object (σημεῖον, τι περαιτέρω) or complementary infinitive (ἀκοῦσαι).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of finding or attaining (contrasted with μὴ εὑρών in ACT 12:19 and οὐκ ἐπέτυχεν in ROM 11:7). In MAT 6:32 and LUK 12:30, it characterizes the pursuit of daily provisions (τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν). In MAT 12:39 and MAT 16:4, it takes σημεῖον ('a sign') as its object. In PHP 4:17, the speaker contrasts seeking a gift (τὸ δόμα) with seeking spiritual fruit (τὸν καρπόν).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The knee of the body, especially in idioms of kneeling or bowing in prayer, homage, or submission.

senses.definition: The anatomical joint of the leg, whether as the place at which a supplicant falls or as a bodily part needing strength for endurance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, as dative indirect object of `προσπίπτω` or accusative object of `ἀνορθόω`

senses.definition: Used with verbs of placing (`τίθημι`) or bending (`κάμπτω`) to express the act of kneeling or bowing down in prayer, worship, homage, or submission.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in the accusative with `τίθημι` or `κάμπτω`, or nominative subject (`πᾶν γόνυ`) of `κάμπτω`

entries.collocations_and_notes: Predominantly appears in two set expressions for kneeling: `τίθημι τὰ γόνατα` (lit. "place the knees", especially in Acts and Luke/Mark for praying or mock homage) and `κάμπτω [τὸ/τὰ] γόνυ/γόνατα` (lit. "bend the knee[s]", in Paul for worship, prayer, or allegiance). In ROM 14:11 and PHP 2:10, `πᾶν γόνυ` functions synecdochically for every person or cosmic being bowing in submission. In HEB 12:12, `τὰ παραλελυμένα γόνατα` is paired with `τὰς παρειμένας χεῖρας` as an image of physical and spiritual weariness.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adverb singling out a particular item, person, or subgroup for special emphasis, or marking the highest degree of a quality or feeling.

senses.definition: Singles out a specific person, subgroup, object, or circumstance from a wider context for special focus or prominence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb (often with `καί` or `δέ`), introducing a noun phrase, prepositional phrase, or participial clause

senses.definition: Indicates the greatest intensity or highest degree of an emotion, action, or quality.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying a participle or adjective

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly pairs with `δέ` (`μάλιστα δέ`) or follows `καί` (`καὶ μάλιστα`) to narrow focus from a universal or broader group (e.g., `πάντας`, `πάντες οἱ ἅγιοι`, `πάντων ἀνθρώπων`, `τῶν ἰδίων`) to a specific subset or individual. In PHM 1:16, `μάλιστα ἐμοί` is explicitly contrasted with `πόσῳ δὲ μᾶλλον σοὶ`. In ACT 26:3, it introduces the specific circumstance qualifying the addressee (`μάλιστα γνώστην ὄντα σε`).

entries.core_meaning_summary: One who works alongside others in a shared effort or contributes actively toward a person, community, or goal.

senses.definition: A colleague or partner who labors together with another person or belongs to a shared service, especially in gospel ministry.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun/substantive with personal genitive (e.g., μου, ἡμῶν, Θεοῦ)

senses.definition: One who acts in support of or contributes effort toward a specific person, benefit, or cause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun/substantive with objective genitive, dative, or εἰς + accusative

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with possessive genitives (μου, ἡμῶν) in Pauline greetings and commendations, sometimes alongside ἀδελφός or συνστρατιώτης (PHP 2:25) and κοινωνός (2CO 8:23), or qualified by ἐν Χριστῷ (Ἰησοῦ) (ROM 16:3, ROM 16:9). In 1CO 3:9, Θεοῦ ... συνεργοί stands alongside Θεοῦ γεώργιον and Θεοῦ οἰκοδομή, which allows either 'co-workers belonging to God' or 'fellow workers with God'. In 2CO 1:24, cooperation toward others' joy is explicitly contrasted with exercising dominion (κυριεύομεν).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To hold together, press in on, confine, grip with illness or emotion, or inwardly constrain and compel.

senses.definition: To close tightly or stop up a bodily opening, such as covering one's ears to shut out sound.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive + accusative of body part (τὰ ὦτα)

senses.definition: To crowd around, hem in militarily, or hold a person in custody.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive + personal accusative

senses.definition: To be seized, gripped, or afflicted by physical illness, pain, or intense fear.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive + instrumental/causal dative (illness or emotion)

senses.definition: To compel or control inwardly, or (in the passive) to be distressed, wholly absorbed in a task, or torn between two possibilities.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active (abstract subject + personal accusative) or passive (absolute, + dative, or + ἐκ + genitive)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In medical and emotional contexts, the passive pairs with instrumental datives such as νόσοις, βασάνοις, πυρετῷ/πυρετοῖς, δυσεντερίῳ, and φόβῳ. In ACT 18:5, συνείχετο τῷ λόγῳ can mean either that Paul was wholly absorbed in or compelled/pressed by the message as he testified. In military/crowd contexts, it appears alongside περικυκλόω (LUK 19:43) and ἀποθλίβω (LUK 8:45).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A ground or reason for pride and boasting, or the boastful claim and confident pride itself.

senses.definition: A basis, reason, or object (including achievements or people) in which someone can take pride or boast.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun as object of ἔχω, predicate nominal, or prepositional object (εἰς)

senses.definition: An expression of pride, a boastful claim, or confident exultation about oneself, others, or a hope.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subject/object noun or genitive modifier (e.g., after ἀφορμή)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently modified by possessive pronouns/genitives (`μου`, `ὑμῶν`, `ἡμῶν`) or prepositional phrases marking the topic (`ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν/ὑμῶν`, `εἰς ἑαυτὸν`). Commonly appears as the object of `ἔχω` (`ROM 4:2`, `GAL 6:4`) and `κενόω` ("empty/nullify", `1CO 9:15`, `2CO 9:3`). In `2CO 5:12`, `ἀφορμὴν καυχήματος` is contrasted with opponents who boast (`καυχωμένους`) in outward appearance. Paired with `παρρησία` ("confidence/boldness") in `HEB 3:6`.

entries.core_meaning_summary: God's summons or invitation into Christian salvation and relationship, or the life-situation in which one receives that summons.

senses.definition: The divine act of summoning or inviting people to salvation, hope, and fellowship with God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun often modified by divine genitives/adjectives, paired with καλέω, or governed by ἀξίως / ἀξιόω / μέτοχος

senses.definition: The social condition, station, or circumstances in which a person is situated when called by God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun as object of βλέπω or governed by ἐν + cognate verb καλέω

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears with the cognate verb `καλέω` (`1CO 7:20`, `EPH 4:1`, `EPH 4:4`, `2TI 1:9`) and with descriptors emphasizing its divine origin or goal (`τοῦ Θεοῦ`, `ἄνω`, `ἐπουρανίου`, `ἁγίᾳ`). Twice linked with `ἐλπίς` ("hope of calling", `EPH 1:18`, `EPH 4:4`), and paired with `τὰ χαρίσματα` (`ROM 11:29`) and `ἐκλογή` (`2PE 1:10`). In `1CO 1:26`, "your calling" refers to the profile and status of the believers when called, overlapping with the divine summons itself.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Literal internal bodily organs, or figuratively the inner seat of deep affection, tender compassion, and care.

senses.definition: The internal physical organs or intestines of the human body.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun as subject of ἐκχέω

senses.definition: The inner center of emotion, deep affection, tenderness, and compassionate care toward others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun often with genitive of quality (ἐλέους, οἰκτιρμοῦ) or verbs of emotion/refreshment

senses.definition: A cherished person regarded as deeply dear to oneself, akin to one's own heart.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun with possessive pronoun in apposition to a person

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs exclusively in the plural (`τὰ σπλάγχνα`, `σπλάγχνα`, `σπλάγχνοις`) in all attested passages. Figuratively, it collocates closely with mercy and compassion vocabulary (`ἔλεος` in `LUK 1:78`, `οἰκτιρμός` in `PHP 2:1`, `COL 3:12`), with `ἀναπαύω` ("refresh", `PHM 1:7`, `PHM 1:20`), `στενοχωρέω` ("restrict", `2CO 6:12`), `ἐπιποθέω` ("long for", `PHP 1:8`), and `κλείω ἀπό` ("shut off from", `1JN 3:17`).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To stand upright in a physical location, or figuratively to remain steadfast, faithful, or approved.

senses.definition: To be in an upright bodily posture or physically stationed in a place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, often with a locative adverb/phrase or a circumstantial participle

senses.definition: To hold steady, remain steadfast, or persevere faithfully in a sphere, allegiance, or way of life.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb, used absolutely (often imperative) or with `ἐν` + dative

senses.definition: To maintain one's standing or prove acceptable and approved before an authority, contrasted with failing or falling.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with dative of reference (`τῷ ἰδίῳ κυρίῳ`)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the imperative (`στήκετε`) with `ἐν` + dative (`ἐν τῇ πίστει`, `ἐν ἑνὶ πνεύματι`, `ἐν Κυρίῳ`) to urge communal or spiritual endurance. In JHN 8:44, the form `ἔστηκεν` occurs with `ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ`. In ROM 14:4, it is explicitly contrasted with `πίπτει` ("falls") and paired with `στῆσαι` from a related verb. In 2TH 2:15, it is coordinated with `κρατεῖτε` ("hold fast").

entries.core_meaning_summary: Favorable recognition, commendation, or praise bestowed on someone for good conduct, or honor directed toward God.

senses.definition: Commendation, approval, or favorable recognition granted to people by God, governing authorities, or fellow believers for faithfulness or good deeds.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, as subject or object, or in `εἰς ἔπαινον`, frequently with `ἐκ`/`ἀπό` + genitive of source or an objective genitive

senses.definition: Acclaim, honor, and adoration directed toward God or his glorious grace.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in the prepositional phrase `εἰς ἔπαινον` + genitive of the one praised

senses.definition: A quality or deed that deserves commendation or favorable mention.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in a conditional clause (`εἴ τις ἔπαινος`), paired with `ἀρετή`

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often occurs in prepositional phrases with `εἰς` (`εἰς ἔπαινον`, especially `εἰς ἔπαινον [τῆς] δόξης αὐτοῦ` in Ephesians) and is coordinated with `δόξα` ("glory") and `τιμή` ("honor"). When designating approval received by humans, the source is marked by `ἐκ` or `ἀπό` + genitive (`ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ`, `ἐξ αὐτῆς`, `ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ`). In 1PE 2:14, `ἔπαινον ἀγαθοποιῶν` contrasts directly with `ἐκδίκησιν κακοποιῶν`.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A written document, book, or scroll—whether a literary record, a collection of sacred writings, or a figurative register of names.

senses.definition: A physical written work, scroll, or volume, including an introductory genealogical record, a collection of authoritative or prophetic writings, or a book of esoteric practices.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, singular or plural, used in headings, as direct object, or after ἐν + dative with a genitive modifier

senses.definition: A figurative or heavenly register in which individuals' names are recorded as belonging to life.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine singular noun in the phrase (τῇ) βίβλῳ (τῆς) ζωῆς, governed by ἐν + dative or ἐκ + genitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the prepositional phrase ἐν (τῇ) βίβλῳ with a genitive modifier indicating author, content, or category (e.g., Μωϋσέως, λόγων Ἡσαΐου, ψαλμῶν, τῶν προφητῶν), often introduced by γέγραπται ('it is written') to cite authoritative writings. In PHP 4:3, REV 3:5, and REV 20:15, occurs in the fixed expression βίβλος (τῆς) ζωῆς ('book of life'), where names are written in or erased from it. In ACT 19:19, the plural τὰς βίβλους refers to physical volumes/scrolls with monetary value that can be burned.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Quickly, without delay, within a short time, or with undue haste.

senses.definition: With physical speed or promptness of action, without delay.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying an imperative or aorist indicative verb of action

senses.definition: Within a short interval of time from the present; in the near future.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying a future indicative verb or an infinitive of anticipated arrival or sending

senses.definition: Readily, rashly, or prematurely, without sufficient caution or stability.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying present/aorist verbs or imperatives, often with οὕτως or a negation (μή, μηδείς)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In GAL 1:6, οὕτως ταχέως ('so quickly / so soon') can carry both temporal force (short time elapsed) and qualitative force (readily/rashly). In 2TH 2:2 and 1TI 5:22, negated contexts (μὴ ταχέως, μηδενὶ ταχέως) warn against acting or reacting prematurely or without careful discernment. Collocates frequently with verbs of motion or sending (ἐξέρχομαι, ἔρχομαι, πέμπω).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To openly acknowledge or confess (sins, deeds, or a truth), to give thankful praise to God, or (in the active voice) to agree/consent.

senses.definition: To admit or disclose one's sins or past practices openly.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle voice, typically with an accusative direct object (τὰς ἁμαρτίας) and optionally a dative recipient (ἀλλήλοις), or paired with ἀναγγέλλω

senses.definition: To declare or acknowledge openly a truth or status.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle voice followed by a ὅτι clause stating the content of the declaration

senses.definition: To offer thankful praise or reverent acknowledgment to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: middle voice with a dative recipient referring to God (σοι, τῷ Θεῷ), sometimes followed by a ὅτι clause giving the reason

senses.definition: To agree or consent to a proposed arrangement.
senses.grammatical_frame: active voice, used intransitively without an expressed object

entries.collocations_and_notes: Nine of the ten occurrences are in the middle voice, spanning admission of sins/deeds (MAT 3:6, MRK 1:5, ACT 19:18, JAS 5:16), open declaration of a core belief (PHP 2:11), and thankful praise or acknowledgment directed to God (MAT 11:25, LUK 10:21, ROM 14:11, ROM 15:9). The single active occurrence (LUK 22:6) lacks a direct object and denotes agreeing or consenting to a proposal. Notice the parallel verbs δοξάσαι and ψαλῶ in ROM 15:9, κάμψει πᾶν γόνυ in ROM 14:11, and ἀναγγέλλοντες in ACT 19:18.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A subordinating conjunction introducing a known reason or premise ('since, because'), or occasionally a completed prior event ('when, after').

senses.definition: Introduces an established fact, situation, or premise serving as the reason or ground for a following or preceding statement, question, or course of action.
senses.grammatical_frame: subordinating conjunction introducing a causal clause with an indicative verb, sometimes paired with γάρ or καί

senses.definition: Introduces a prior event that has been completed before the action of the main clause takes place.
senses.grammatical_frame: subordinating conjunction introducing a temporal clause with an aorist indicative verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Predominantly causal (9 of 10 occurrences), introducing a premise or established circumstance that motivates a statement, question, or action; often combined with γάρ (1CO 1:21, 15:21) or καί (1CO 1:22). In ACT 15:24, it opens a formal statement introducing the background reason. Only in LUK 7:1 does it function purely temporally with an aorist verb to mark the completion of a prior event before the next narrative action.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To carry out an undertaking, ritual duty, or process to its full completion, or (in the middle/passive) to reach completion or be experienced.

senses.definition: To bring an action, task, gracious project, or moral quality to full completion or realization.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb + accusative object or substantival infinitive

senses.definition: To construct a sacred structure or regularly perform prescribed acts of worship and priestly service.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active verb + accusative of sacred structure or ritual service

senses.definition: To reach completion or perfection by some means, or (of sufferings) to be imposed on and undergone by a group.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle or passive verb + dative of means or affected group

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of beginning (`ἐνάρχομαι`, `προενάρχομαι`) to contrast starting an endeavor with bringing it to full completion (`2CO 8:6`, `GAL 3:3`, `PHP 1:6`). In `2CO 8:11`, it contrasts with willing/desiring (`θέλειν`) and takes a substantival infinitive (`τὸ ποιῆσαι`) as its object. In `GAL 3:3`, the middle/passive form `ἐπιτελεῖσθε` allows either a middle reading ("finish for yourselves") or passive reading ("be brought to completion"); in `1PE 5:9`, the passive infinitive with `τὰ αὐτὰ τῶν παθημάτων` expresses hardships being carried out upon or experienced by the Christian community.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Favorable disposition, gracious approval, or earnest goodwill toward someone or some purpose.

senses.definition: God's approving choice, gracious purpose, or favorable disposition toward humanity or a course of action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate nominative with γίνομαι + ἔμπροσθέν + genitive; genitive modifier of ἀνθρώποις; or object of κατά or ὑπέρ in theological statements about divine purpose

senses.definition: Benevolent attitude, sincere goodwill, or earnest inner desire toward others or for what is good.
senses.grammatical_frame: Nominative subject modified by genitive (τῆς ἐμῆς καρδίας); object of διά expressing motive; or direct object of πληρόω with genitive (ἀγαθωσύνης)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Co-occurs with θελήματος ('will', EPH 1:5), προέθετο ('purposed', EPH 1:9), ἔμπροσθέν σου ('before you', MAT 11:26; LUK 10:21), δέησις ('prayer/entreaty', ROM 10:1), and ἀγαθωσύνης ('goodness', 2TH 1:11). In PHP 1:15, δι’ εὐδοκίαν stands in direct contrast to διὰ φθόνον καὶ ἔριν ('out of envy and rivalry').
entries.uncertainty_note: In LUK 2:14 (ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκίας) and PHP 2:13 (ὑπὲρ τῆς εὐδοκίας), no possessive pronoun specifies whether the favorable disposition belongs to God toward humans or characterizes human goodwill; similarly, 2TH 1:11 (εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης) may denote human resolve for goodness or God's delight in goodness.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Pleasing, acceptable, or satisfactory to God or to human superiors.

senses.definition: Well-pleasing, acceptable, or approved in relation to God or the Lord, describing sacrifices, moral conduct, God's will, or faithful servants.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive, predicate, or substantivized adjective, typically with dative complement (τῷ Θεῷ, τῷ Κυρίῳ, αὐτῷ), ἐν Κυρίῳ, or ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ

senses.definition: Agreeable or satisfactory in conduct toward human masters.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate adjective (accusative plural with εἶναι) in household instructions regarding slaves and masters

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with the dative τῷ Θεῷ or τῷ Κυρίῳ (ROM 12:1; 14:18; EPH 5:10; PHP 4:18) and coordinated with ἀγαθόν, τέλειον (ROM 12:2), δεκτήν (PHP 4:18), and δόκιμος (ROM 14:18). Applied to θυσία ('sacrifice') in ROM 12:1 and PHP 4:18.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To increase, multiply, or become abundant, or (causatively) to make someone abound in something.

senses.definition: To grow in quantity, intensity, or degree; to become plentiful or abundant.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with abstract or collective subjects (e.g., τὸ παράπτωμα, ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἡ χάρις, ὁ καρπός, ἡ ἀγάπη, ταῦτα)

senses.definition: To have more than enough or a surplus, in contrast to lacking.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intransitive verb with personal substantivized subject (ὁ τὸ πολύ) in antithesis to ἐλαττονέω

senses.definition: To cause someone to increase or become abundant in a quality.
senses.grammatical_frame: Transitive verb with personal direct object (ὑμᾶς) and dative of respect (τῇ ἀγάπῃ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often paired with περισσεύω (2CO 4:15; 1TH 3:12), ὑπερεπερίσσευσεν (ROM 5:20), and ὑπεραυξάνει (2TH 1:3), and contrasted with ἠλαττόνησεν ('fell short', 2CO 8:15). Used with abstract nouns such as παράπτωμα, ἁμαρτία, χάρις, καρπός, and ἀγάπη.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Resentful envy or begrudging rivalry toward others, and in one contested passage intense jealous yearning.

senses.definition: Resentful begrudging or hostile envy directed at others' standing or success, acting as a vice or malicious motive.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular or plural noun after διά (expressing motive), after ἐν, after μεστός, as subject of γίνομαι, or in vice lists

senses.definition: Envious or intensely jealous longing, as an orientation or manner of yearning.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverbial prepositional phrase πρὸς φθόνον modifying ἐπιποθεῖ with τὸ πνεῦμα as subject

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly appears in vice lists alongside κακία ('malice'), ἔρις ('strife'), φόνος ('murder'), δόλος ('deceit'), and καταλαλιά ('slander') in ROM 1:29; GAL 5:21; 1TI 6:4; TIT 3:3; 1PE 2:1. With διὰ + accusative, indicates the hostile motive behind handing Jesus over (MAT 27:18; MRK 15:10) or preaching Christ competitively (PHP 1:15, contrasted with εὐδοκία).
entries.uncertainty_note: In JAS 4:5 (Πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα ὃ κατῴκισεν ἐν ἡμῖν), the single occurrence of πρὸς φθόνον with ἐπιποθεῖ leaves it uncertain whether it denotes a sinful human spirit yearning toward envy or God's indwelling spirit yearning with intense jealousy.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Upward in direction or highest spatial limit, and by extension located above in the heavenly realm.

senses.definition: Indicates vertical movement or orientation toward a higher point, or the uppermost limit of a container.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb modifying a verb of motion/lifting, or object of the preposition ἕως

senses.definition: Indicates position in the upper or heavenly sphere, or origin from that sphere, either reinforcing a locative phrase or standing in attributive position with a noun.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb in apposition to a locative prepositional phrase, or in attributive position between article and noun

senses.definition: Denotes the heavenly domain or the realities belonging to God's sphere where Christ is seated, contrasted with earthly existence.
senses.grammatical_frame: substantivized neuter plural with the definite article (τὰ ἄνω / ἐκ τῶν ἄνω)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with κάτω ("below") in JHN 8:23 and ACT 2:19, and with τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ("the things on the earth") in COL 3:2. In PHP 3:14, τῆς ἄνω κλήσεως may denote either the call's heavenly origin ("from above") or its goal/direction ("upward"). In JHN 2:7, ἕως ἄνω forms a fixed spatial phrase indicating the rim of a vessel.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To feel a deep longing, earnest desire, or strong craving for someone or something.

senses.definition: To experience a strong desire or yearning to carry out an action or reach a desired state.
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb or participle with a complementary infinitive

senses.definition: To feel deep affection and longing for absent people, or to crave something earnestly like an infant wanting milk.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb (or periphrastic participle) + accusative object of person or thing

senses.definition: To yearn or desire intensely in a jealous or envious manner (used in a syntactically disputed clause concerning the spirit dwelling within).
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb used without a clear direct object, modified by the prepositional phrase πρὸς φθόνον

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly governs an infinitive of seeing (ἰδεῖν in ROM 1:11, 1TH 3:6, 2TI 1:4) or takes personal pronouns as direct object in affectionate epistolary contexts (2CO 9:14, PHP 1:8, PHP 2:26). Paired with στενάζω ("groan") in 2CO 5:2 and ἀδημονέω ("be distressed") in PHP 2:26, highlighting emotional intensity. In JAS 4:5, the clause Πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα is syntactically ambiguous as to whether τὸ πνεῦμα is subject or object and whether πρὸς φθόνον expresses jealous devotion or envious craving.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Hostile rivalry, contentiousness, or interpersonal conflict and quarreling.

senses.definition: An attitude or condition of antagonistic rivalry, discord, and contentiousness that fractures relationships or motivates hostile action.
senses.grammatical_frame: singular abstract noun in vice lists, prepositional phrases (διά + acc), or paired coordinate nouns

senses.definition: Concrete instances or outbreaks of argument and factional conflict within a community.
senses.grammatical_frame: plural noun functioning as subject of εἰμί with ἐν + dative of group

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with ζῆλος ("jealousy/rivalry" in ROM 13:13, 1CO 3:3, 2CO 12:20, GAL 5:20) and φθόνος ("envy" in ROM 1:29, PHP 1:15, 1TI 6:4). In PHP 1:15, διὰ φθόνον καὶ ἔριν contrasts directly with δι’ εὐδοκίαν ("out of goodwill"). In 1TI 6:4 and TIT 3:9, it appears alongside ζητήσεις ("controversies"), λογομαχίαι ("word-battles"), and μάχαι ("fights").

entries.core_meaning_summary: A state of scarcity, material need, or a gap and deficiency that remains to be supplied or completed.

senses.definition: Material or financial poverty and scarcity of basic resources, contrasted with surplus and relieved by others' contributions.
senses.grammatical_frame: singular or plural noun, modified by a possessive genitive or contrasted with περίσσευμα, often object of προσαναπληρόω

senses.definition: A non-material gap, shortcoming, or unfulfilled portion in personal presence, service, suffering, or faith that another person supplies or completes.
senses.grammatical_frame: singular or plural noun with a possessive pronoun or objective genitive, functioning as object of ἀναπληρόω, ἀνταναπληρόω, or καταρτίζω

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often stands in direct contrast to abundance or surplus (τὸ περισσεῦον in LUK 21:4; περίσσευμα in 2CO 8:14) and frequently serves as the object of verbs of filling up or supplying (ἀναπληρόω in 1CO 16:17, PHP 2:30; προσαναπληρόω in 2CO 9:12, 2CO 11:9; ἀνταναπληρόω in COL 1:24; καταρτίζω in 1TH 3:10). In 1CO 16:17, τὸ ὑμέτερον ὑστέρημα specifically refers to what was lacking due to the recipients' physical absence. In COL 1:24, τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν θλίψεων τοῦ Χριστοῦ refers to what remains unfilled or still to be endured in connection with Christ's afflictions.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To have a share in, participate in, or contribute to something together with others.

senses.definition: To partake of or actively participate in a shared condition, experience, spiritual benefit, or course of action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb with dative of the thing shared, or verb with genitive of the thing shared

senses.definition: To contribute toward others' material needs or enter into reciprocal sharing and partnership with someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Verb with dative of needs, or verb with dative of person (with prepositional phrase indicating goods or financial account)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes a dative complement denoting either the entity/experience shared in (needs, spiritual things, sufferings, sins, evil deeds) or the person with whom one shares (often further specified with en + dative or eis + accusative). In HEB 2:14 it takes a genitive (haimatos kai sarkos) and stands in parallel with metechō. PHP 4:15 uses the commercial idiom eis logon doseōs kai lēmpseōs ('for an account of giving and receiving').

entries.core_meaning_summary: To make larger in physical size, to increase or display richly, or to exalt and hold in high honor.

senses.definition: To increase the physical size or length of an object.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive verb with accusative noun denoting a physical item

senses.definition: To show or exercise a quality or disposition on a great scale toward someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive verb with accusative abstract noun and meta + genitive of person

senses.definition: To speak highly of, praise, or regard and display with great honor (used of God, Christ, a name, or respected persons).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active transitive verb with accusative of person/deity, or passive verb with nominative subject

senses.definition: To have one's sphere of activity, influence, or standing greatly expanded among a community.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive verb with en + dative of community and eis + accusative of degree

entries.collocations_and_notes: In MAT 23:5 it pairs with platynō ('widen') regarding garment items. In LUK 1:46 and ACT 10:46 it takes God/Lord as direct object; in ACT 19:17 the passive subject is to onoma tou Kyriou Iēsou. In 2CO 10:15 the passive infinitive appears alongside auxanomenēs ('growing'), kata ton kanona ('according to our measure/rule'), and eis perisseian ('to abundance'), pointing toward an expansion of apostolic scope or standing.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The official residence or headquarters of a governor or ruler, or the personnel/guard body associated with such an official seat.

senses.definition: The official residence, palace, or military headquarters of a Roman governor or client ruler, having an inner courtyard and facilities for troops or custody.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun with definite article, frequently following spatial prepositions (eis, en) or qualified by a possessive genitive

senses.definition: An official imperial guard corps or headquarters personnel among whom a prisoner's situation becomes known.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter noun with definite article and adjective holos after preposition en, coordinated with plural personal dative

entries.collocations_and_notes: In the Gospels (MAT 27:27, MRK 15:16, JHN 18:28, JHN 18:33, JHN 19:9), it is the Roman governor's headquarters/residence containing an interior courtyard (aulē) where an entire cohort (speira) can assemble and which Judean leaders avoid entering to preserve ritual purity. In ACT 23:35 it is specified as 'of Herod' (tou Hērōdou) and serves as a place of detention. In PHP 1:13 it is coordinated with 'all the rest' (tois loipois pasin), referring to persons or a military/official body.
entries.uncertainty_note: In PHP 1:13, the coordination of en holō tō praitōriō with tois loipois pasin ('and to all the rest') strongly points to a group of people (such as an imperial guard or military corps), but the single sentence does not definitively rule out a spatial reference to a palace or military headquarters complex as the setting where those people are found.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Required by duty or circumstance, indispensable, urgent, or closely connected in relationship.

senses.definition: Required, fitting, or obligatory in light of a purpose, duty, or circumstance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate adjective (often impersonal with eimi or with verb of considering hēgeomai) governing an infinitive clause; also comparative

senses.definition: Essential, indispensable, or pressing for proper functioning or well-being.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate adjective with noun subject, or attributive adjective modifying a noun of need (chreias)

senses.definition: Bound by close ties of intimacy or personal loyalty (of friends).
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective modifying a plural noun denoting friends (philous)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly appears with hēgeomai ('consider it necessary', 2CO 9:5, PHP 2:25) or forms of eimi governing an infinitive clause. In PHP 1:24 the comparative anankaioteron contrasts remaining in the flesh with departing. In ACT 10:24 it stands alongside syngeneis ('relatives') to describe close social bonds.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To stand in opposition to or conflict with someone or something, frequently used as a participle to designate an opponent or adversary.

senses.definition: To be contrary to, conflict with, or stand in opposition to another entity or standard.
senses.grammatical_frame: finite middle/passive verb + dative complement (person or thing opposed)

senses.definition: One who actively opposes, resists, or stands against a person or group; an adversary or opponent.
senses.grammatical_frame: substantival present participle (with or without dative complement)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears as a substantival present participle (often with a dative complement indicating the person opposed, e.g., αὐτῷ, ὑμῖν, or alone in the plural οἱ ἀντικείμενοι or singular ὁ ἀντικείμενος). Paired with ἀντιστῆναι and ἀντειπεῖν in LUK 21:15, with ἐπιθυμεῖν κατά in GAL 5:17, and with ὑπεραιρόμενος in 2TH 2:4. contrasted with the rejoicing crowd in LUK 13:17 and an open, effective door in 1CO 16:9.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To wait expectantly or patiently for a future person, event, or promised outcome.

senses.definition: To look forward to or await eagerly a future deliverance, hoped-for status, revelation, or returning figure.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive middle/deponent verb or participle + accusative direct object

senses.definition: To wait with endurance or patient forbearance without an explicit direct object.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive middle/deponent verb (or with implied referent), sometimes modified by prepositional phrase of manner or time

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly takes future eschatological objects such as ἀποκάλυψις (ROM 8:19; 1CO 1:7), υἱοθεσία / ἀπολύτρωσις τοῦ σώματος (ROM 8:23), ἐλπὶς δικαιοσύνης (GAL 5:5), or Christ as returning Savior (PHP 3:20; HEB 9:28). Associated with eager expectation (ἀποκαραδοκία in ROM 8:19), inward groaning (ROM 8:23), hope and endurance (δι’ ὑπομονῆς in ROM 8:25), and patience (μακροθυμία in 1PE 3:20).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A spoken or reasoned defense, answer, or vindication offered against accusations, questioning, or challenges.

senses.definition: A formal speech or legal hearing in which an accused person answers charges before authorities or a hostile crowd.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun in judicial or public-assembly contexts (object of verbs like ἀκούω, λαμβάνω τόπον, or with ἐν)

senses.definition: A reasoned explanation, reply, or effort to clear oneself or vindicate a message or hope before questioners or critics.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun with dative of addressee, objective genitive, or prepositions εἰς / πρός

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often paired with judicial or argumentative vocabulary such as κατηγορούμενος, κατήγοροι, ἔγκλημα (ACT 25:16), ἀνακρίνω (1CO 9:3), and αἰτέω λόγον (1PE 3:15). Constructed with πρός + accusative (ACT 22:1; 1PE 3:15), εἰς + accusative (PHP 1:16), dative of audience (1CO 9:3), and objective genitive τοῦ εὐαγγελίου (PHP 1:7, 16). Paired with βεβαίωσις in PHP 1:7 and listed among expressions of clearing oneself (ἁγνοὺς εἶναι) in 2CO 7:11.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Free from moral stain, guilt, or sexual impropriety; pure, innocent, or chaste.

senses.definition: Free from culpability or wrongdoing regarding a particular incident; cleared of blame.
senses.grammatical_frame: predicative adjective + dative of reference (τῷ πράγματι)

senses.definition: Morally unblemished, sincere, and free from sin or corruption in character, thought, or conduct.
senses.grammatical_frame: attributive, predicative, or substantival adjective describing character, wisdom, conduct, or things

senses.definition: Sexually or maritally faithful and undefiled; modest and devoted within marriage or betrothal.
senses.grammatical_frame: attributive or predicative feminine adjective referring to a virgin or married women

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in virtue lists (PHP 4:8; TIT 2:5; JAS 3:17) alongside adjectives such as ἀληθής, σεμνός, δίκαιος, σώφρων, εἰρηνικός, and ἀνυπόκριτος. Used with τήρει in 1TI 5:22 in contrast to sharing in others' sins, and paired with its cognate verb ἁγνίζω in 1JN 3:3. Modifies παρθένος in 2CO 11:2 and ἀναστροφή in 1PE 3:2.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Being free from defect, stain, or moral fault, whether applied to the moral purity of believers before God or the unblemished quality of a sacrifice.

senses.definition: Free from moral stain, fault, or guilt in conduct and character, especially as presented before God or living among others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective used predicatively with verbs of being, becoming, standing, or presenting, or attributively modifying a noun phrase

senses.definition: Free from physical or ritual defect as required for a sacrificial victim or offering to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective used predicatively with a verb of offering (προσφέρω) or attributively modifying a sacrificial animal (ἀμνός)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with ἅγιος (EPH 1:4, EPH 5:27, COL 1:22), ἀνέγκλητος (COL 1:22), ἄμεμπτος and ἀκέραιος (PHP 2:15), ἄσπιλος (1PE 1:19), and ἀπταίστους in the same sentence (JUD 1:24). Repeatedly occurs with the prepositional phrase κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ or κατενώπιον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ('before him' / 'before his glory', EPH 1:4, COL 1:22, JUD 1:24) and as complement of verbs of presenting/standing (παρίστημι, ἵστημι). Contrasted with having a stain or wrinkle (σπίλον ἢ ῥυτίδα, EPH 5:27), a crooked and perverted generation (PHP 2:15), and falsehood in the mouth (REV 14:5).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The active working, effective exercise of power, or operative influence that brings about an intended result.

senses.definition: The active operation or effective working of power, ability, or functional capacity by God, Christ, Satan, or the parts of a body.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun usually governed by the preposition κατά with a genitive of the agent or power, or functioning as a genitive modifier

senses.definition: An operative force or powerful influence sent upon people so that they accept falsehood.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun as direct object of πέμπω governing a genitive of the resulting condition (πλάνης)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Seven of eight occurrences appear in the prepositional phrase κατὰ [τὴν] ἐνέργειαν (EPH 1:19, EPH 3:7, EPH 4:16, PHP 3:21, COL 1:29, 2TH 2:9) or as a genitive dependent on πίστις (COL 2:12). Frequently combined with terms for power and strength (κράτος, ἰσχύς, δύναμις, δύναμαι) and once with the cognate participle ἐνεργουμένην (COL 1:29). In 2TH 2:11 it is the direct object of πέμπω with a genitive of content/result (πλάνης).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To fail to remember something, neglect a person or duty, or intentionally leave past things out of mind.

senses.definition: To fail to remember or lose recall of an action to be performed or an observation just made.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle verb taking an infinitive complement or an indirect question clause

senses.definition: To overlook, disregard, or neglect a creature, past deed, or moral obligation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle verb taking a genitive object (or infinitive with genitive), or passive periphrastic participle with εἰμί

senses.definition: To deliberately put past matters out of mind in order to press toward what lies ahead.
senses.grammatical_frame: Middle participle taking a direct accusative object in contrast with ἐπεκτείνομαι

entries.collocations_and_notes: Takes an infinitive (MAT 16:5, MRK 8:14) or indirect question (JAS 1:24) for failing to remember facts or actions, and a genitive noun for overlooking or neglecting duties and deeds (HEB 6:10, HEB 13:2, HEB 13:16). In HEB 13:2 and HEB 13:16 it occurs in negated present imperatives (μὴ ἐπιλανθάνεσθε). In PHP 3:13 it takes an accusative plural (τὰ μὲν ὀπίσω) and stands in μέν...δέ contrast with ἐπεκτείνομαι ('straining forward').

entries.core_meaning_summary: Being equal in status, treatment, quantity, or dimension, or being consistent and in agreement with one another.

senses.definition: Having the same standing, status, treatment, or share as another person or group.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective used as object complement with ποιέω or predicate with εἰμί (often with a dative of comparison), or attributively with ὡς

senses.definition: Matching in numerical amount, value, or spatial measurement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Neuter plural adjective used substantively with the article as direct object, or as predicate adjective of measurement nouns

senses.definition: Matching or agreeing in content, used negatively of witnesses' testimonies that contradict or fail to align with one another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine adjective used predicatively with εἰμί modifying μαρτυρία

entries.collocations_and_notes: Takes a dative complement for the person with whom equality is shared or claimed (MAT 20:12, JHN 5:18, PHP 2:6), or the comparative particle ὡς (ACT 11:17). Used as a neuter plural substantive with the article (τὰ ἴσα) for an equivalent return on a loan (LUK 6:34), and as a neuter plural predicate with εἰμί for equal dimensions (REV 21:16) or equal standing (PHP 2:6). In MRK 14:56 and MRK 14:59 it describes testimonies that do not match one another.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To turn someone or a people aside from loyalty or faith, to twist what is straight, or (in the passive) to be morally or spiritually distorted and perverse.

senses.definition: To lead a people or individual astray from civic allegiance or religious faith, subverting or turning them away.
senses.grammatical_frame: active participle or infinitive + accusative personal/collective object, optionally + ἀπὸ + genitive (τῆς πίστεως)

senses.definition: To twist or distort established straight ways or true principles.
senses.grammatical_frame: active participle + accusative object (τὰς ὁδοὺς ... τὰς εὐθείας)

senses.definition: In the passive participle, morally or spiritually twisted and corrupt (modifying a generation alongside 'faithless' or 'crooked'), or substantivally denoting distorted teachings.
senses.grammatical_frame: perfect passive participle, attributive modifying γενεά or substantival neuter plural as object of λαλοῦντες

entries.collocations_and_notes: In MAT 17:17 and LUK 9:41 the perfect passive participle pairs with ἄπιστος modifying γενεά, and in PHP 2:15 it pairs with σκολιᾶς ('crooked') modifying γενεᾶς. In ACT 13:10 τὰς ὁδοὺς ... τὰς εὐθείας ('the straight ways') provides an explicit spatial-moral contrast. Active forms govern human/collective objects (τὸ ἔθνος, τὸν ἀνθύπατον) or paths (τὰς ὁδούς).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A testing ordeal, tangible proof or verification, or the proven character and reliability demonstrated through endurance and faithful service.

senses.definition: A severe process or ordeal of testing experienced under affliction.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun after ἐν + dative (ἐν πολλῇ δοκιμῇ) + genitive (θλίψεως)

senses.definition: Verifying proof, evidence, or tangible demonstration of obedience, ministry, or divine speech.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun as object of γινώσκω or ζητέω, or after διὰ + genitive, with genitive (ὑμῶν, τῆς διακονίας, Χριστοῦ)

senses.definition: Proven character, tested worth, or demonstrated reliability resulting from endurance or faithful service.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun as object/subject in causal sequence (ROM 5:4) or object of γινώσκω with personal genitive (αὐτοῦ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears exclusively in Paul (Romans, 2 Corinthians, Philippians). In ROM 5:4 it stands in a chain between ὑπομονή ('endurance') and ἐλπίς ('hope'). In 2CO 8:2 it takes the genitive θλίψεως ('affliction') after ἐν πολλῇ. In 2CO 2:9, 2CO 9:13, 2CO 13:3, and PHP 2:22 it pairs with verbs of knowing or seeking (γινώσκω, ζητέω) or denotes an outward demonstration through service (διακονία).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The act of remembering someone or mentioning them, especially before God in prayer.

senses.definition: The act of bringing someone before God by name or holding them in thought during prayer and intercession.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun as object of ποιέομαι (+ genitive, often with ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν) or ἔχω (+ περὶ + genitive + ἐν ταῖς δεήσεσιν)

senses.definition: Mental recollection or affectionate memory of another person.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun as object of ἔχω (+ genitive + adjective) or governed by ἐπί (+ dative + genitive)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in the phrase μνείαν ποιεῖσθαι ("make mention") with a genitive object and prepositional phrase ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν ("in [my/our] prayers"), often modified by ἀδιαλείπτως ("unceasingly") or πάντοτε ("always") in contexts of thanksgiving to God (εὐχαριστῶ / εὐχαριστοῦμεν). Also paired with ἔχω ("have"): ἔχω τὴν περὶ σοῦ μνείαν ἐν ταῖς δεήσεσίν μου (2TI 1:3) and ἔχετε μνείαν ἡμῶν ἀγαθὴν (1TH 3:6). In PHP 1:3, ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ μνείᾳ ὑμῶν appears at the opening of thanksgiving and could encompass both mental remembrance and prayerful mention.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To share in another's gladness or rejoice together with someone or something.

senses.definition: To experience and express shared joy with another person or fellow members over good fortune, divine mercy, or mutual faithfulness.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive verb + dative of person (or absolute with collective plural subject)

senses.definition: To take shared delight in or align joyfully with a moral quality or reality, in contrast to delighting in wrongdoing.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive verb + dative of abstract noun

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly takes a dative complement indicating the person (or personified quality) with whom joy is shared. Appears alongside the simple verb χαίρω (PHP 2:17, PHP 2:18; contrasted with οὐ χαίρει ἐπὶ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ in 1CO 13:6) and in parallel with συνπάσχω ("suffer together," 1CO 12:26). In LUK 15:6 and LUK 15:9, it occurs in the imperative Συνχάρητέ μοι followed by an explanatory ὅτι clause announcing a recovery. Note orthographic variation with νχ (συνχ-) in several occurrences in the packet.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An unassuming, lowly disposition of mind toward God and others, or, negatively, ascetic self-abasement.

senses.definition: A modest, unpretentious attitude that avoids self-exaltation and treats others with deference and service.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, often governed by μετά (+ genitive), dative of manner, or direct object of clothing metaphors

senses.definition: Self-imposed ascetic or ritual self-abasement criticized as an outward show disconnected from genuine spiritual restraint.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun governed by ἐν (+ dative) in lists of criticized religious practices

entries.collocations_and_notes: In positive ethical contexts, frequently appears after μετὰ πάσης ("with all," ACT 20:19, EPH 4:2) and alongside πραΰτης ("gentleness") and μακροθυμία ("patience"). It stands in direct contrast to ἐριθεία ("selfish ambition") and κενοδοξία ("empty conceit") in PHP 2:3, and to ὑπερήφανοι ("the proud") in 1PE 5:5, where it is metaphorically "put on" like clothing (ἐνδύσασθε in COL 3:12; ἐγκομβώσασθε in 1PE 5:5). In Colossians 2, it is grouped with θρησκεία τῶν ἀγγέλων ("worship of angels"), ἐθελοθρησκία ("self-imposed religion"), and ἀφειδία σώματος ("harsh treatment of the body") in polemical critique.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To arrive upon, reach a goal or location, or come temporally ahead of someone else.

senses.definition: To arrive upon or come onto people with decisive effect, used of the kingdom of God or divine wrath.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive verb + ἐπί + accusative of person

senses.definition: To reach or attain a geographic destination, standard, or stage of progress.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive verb + εἰς + accusative or ἄχρι + genitive

senses.definition: To arrive before or gain temporal precedence over someone else.
senses.grammatical_frame: transitive verb + accusative of person

entries.collocations_and_notes: When followed by ἐπί + accusative (MAT 12:28, LUK 11:20, 1TH 2:16), the subject is an authoritative divine reality (the kingdom of God or wrath) coming upon people. In 2CO 10:14 it parallels the participle ἐφικνούμενοι ("reaching"). In 1TH 4:15 it takes a direct accusative object of persons in an emphatic negated subjunctive (οὐ μὴ φθάσωμεν) to express temporal priority.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be physically away or absent from a person or group.

senses.definition: To be physically distant or not present in person with others, often contrasted with physical arrival or spiritual closeness.
senses.grammatical_frame: intransitive verb (finite indicative or adverbial present participle), optionally with a dative of respect (e.g., τῷ σώματι, τῇ σαρκί)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in direct contrast with words for presence, especially πάρειμι ("be present": 1CO 5:3, 2CO 10:11, 13:2, 13:10), ἔρχομαι ("come": 2CO 13:2, PHP 1:27), or σὺν ὑμῖν εἰμι ("be with you": COL 2:5). In 1CO 5:3 (τῷ σώματι) and COL 2:5 (τῇ σαρκί), a dative noun specifies bodily/physical absence in contrast to being present in spirit (τῷ πνεύματι). In 2CO 10:11 and 13:10, being absent is associated with communicating by letter (δι’ ἐπιστολῶν, γράφω).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To impart strength or capability to someone, or (in passive/middle) to be strengthened and grow strong.

senses.definition: To supply someone with strength, ability, or inner power to endure or carry out an assigned task.
senses.grammatical_frame: active transitive verb + accusative direct object

senses.definition: To receive strength, become fortified, or grow stronger in resolve, faith, or spiritual capacity.
senses.grammatical_frame: passive or middle intransitive verb, often with an instrumental dative or ἐν + dative specifying the sphere or source

entries.collocations_and_notes: In the active voice, the subject is consistently Christ/the Lord and the object is the first-person pronoun με (PHP 4:13, 1TI 1:12, 2TI 4:17), empowering the recipient for endurance, ministry (εἰς διακονίαν), or proclamation (τὸ κήρυγμα). In the passive/middle, the source or sphere of strength is marked by the dative τῇ πίστει (ROM 4:20) or by ἐν + dative: ἐν Κυρίῳ καὶ ἐν τῷ κράτει τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ (EPH 6:10) and ἐν τῇ χάριτι (2TI 2:1).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Belonging to, situated on, or characteristic of the earthly realm as contrasted with what is heavenly.

senses.definition: Belonging to, constituted for, or originating within the mortal earthly sphere rather than the heavenly realm.
senses.grammatical_frame: two-termination adjective (attributive, elliptical, or predicate)

senses.definition: Matters, realities, or concerns belonging to the present earthly world, as opposed to heavenly truths or spiritual realities.
senses.grammatical_frame: substantival neuter plural with definite article (τὰ ἐπίγεια)

senses.definition: Beings inhabiting the earth, listed in a threefold cosmic division between heavenly beings and those under the earth.
senses.grammatical_frame: substantival plural genitive adjective

entries.collocations_and_notes: Repeatedly placed in explicit contrast with heavenly or transcendent terms: τὰ ἐπουράνια (JHN 3:12), ἐπουράνια / τῶν ἐπουρανίων (1CO 15:40), οἰκοδομὴν ... ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς (2CO 5:1), ἐπουρανίων καὶ ... καταχθονίων (PHP 2:10), and ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη (JAS 3:15). In JAS 3:15, it forms a negative triad with ψυχική ("unspiritual/natural") and δαιμονιώδης ("demonic") to characterize counterfeit wisdom.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A self-interested, rivalrous disposition or factious behavior that opposes humility and produces communal strife.

senses.definition: An inner motive or attitude of self-promoting rivalry, contentiousness, or factious ambition, opposed to humility, sincerity, and truth.
senses.grammatical_frame: singular abstract noun (as direct object, subject, or in prepositional phrases with ἐκ or κατά)

senses.definition: Outward acts or manifestations of rivalrous strife and factional division within a community.
senses.grammatical_frame: plural noun in lists of communal vices

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with ζῆλος ("jealousy/zeal": 2CO 12:20, GAL 5:20, JAS 3:14, 3:16), ἔρις ("strife": 2CO 12:20, GAL 5:20), θυμοί ("outbursts of anger": 2CO 12:20, GAL 5:20), and ἀκαταστασία/ἀκαταστασίαι ("disorder": 2CO 12:20, JAS 3:16). Contrasted directly with ταπεινοφροσύνη ("humility": PHP 2:3), sincere purity (ἁγνῶς: PHP 1:17), and obedience to the truth (ROM 2:8, JAS 3:14). Prepositional phrases ἐξ ἐριθείας (ROM 2:8, PHP 1:17) and κατ’ ἐριθείαν (PHP 2:3) denote acting out of or according to this motive.
entries.uncertainty_note: From these seven contexts alone, the word overlaps with both internal self-seeking ambition (contrasted with humility and paired with vain conceit in PHP 2:3) and outward contentious factionalism (listed with strife, jealousy, dissensions, and disorder in 2CO 12:20, GAL 5:20, JAS 3:16), making it uncertain whether the primary focus is self-advancement or partisan rivalry.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Public disgrace, humiliation, or shameful conduct that brings reproach.

senses.definition: A state of public humiliation, ignominy, or embarrassment experienced by a person or attached to a condition or event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine), in prepositional phrase μετὰ + genitive, as genitive object of καταφρονέω, or as subject modified by a genitive

senses.definition: Disgraceful behavior, hidden wrongdoing, or shameful deeds that merit reproach.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine), singular as genitive modifier or in prepositional phrase ἐν + dative; plural as direct object of verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in contrasts with honor/glory (δόξα in PHP 3:19) or truth (φανέρωσις τῆς ἀληθείας in 2CO 4:2). Collocations include μετὰ αἰσχύνης ("with shame", LUK 14:9), τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς αἰσχύνης ("hidden things of shame", 2CO 4:2), and ἡ αἰσχύνη τῆς γυμνότητος ("the shame of nakedness", REV 3:18). Used in the plural in JUD 1:13 (τὰς ἑαυτῶν αἰσχύνας) for shameful acts.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Two times or on two occasions, indicating repeated action or recurring frequency.

senses.definition: On two separate occasions, a second time, or twice within a specified recurring period (when paired with a genitive of time).
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying a verb or participle; with genitive of time (τοῦ σαββάτου) to express frequency per period

senses.definition: In the idiomatic pairing καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δίς: more than once, repeatedly, on multiple occasions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb in the fixed coordinate phrase καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δίς modifying a main verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often paired with ἀλέκτωρ φωνέω ("a rooster crows", MRK 14:30, MRK 14:72) and contrasted with τρίς ("three times"). Appears in the idiomatic pairing καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δίς ("both once and twice", PHP 4:16; 1TH 2:18). In JUD 1:12, δὶς ἀποθανόντα ("twice dead") characterizes uprooted fruitless trees metaphorically as completely or doubly dead.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To suffer loss, be deprived of, or forfeit something of value (attested in the passive voice).

senses.definition: To suffer the loss of, forfeit, or be deprived of one's life, self, or possessions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive verb taking an accusative of the thing lost (or paired with a reflexive accusative in parallel construction)

senses.definition: To incur loss, disadvantage, or detriment in a general or specified respect.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive verb used absolutely or with ἐν + dative specifying the area of loss and ἐξ + genitive indicating source

entries.collocations_and_notes: All six occurrences in the packet are in the passive voice. Frequently contrasted directly with κερδαίνω ("to gain", MAT 16:26; MRK 8:36; LUK 9:25; PHP 3:8) and paired with the cognate noun ζημία ("loss") in PHP 3:8. Parallel to ἀπόλλυμι ("to destroy/lose") in LUK 9:25.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Official sacred or priestly service, or practical ministry and relief rendered on behalf of others.

senses.definition: Sacred, priestly, or cultic service and ministry performed in relation to God or a sanctuary (including figurative sacrificial service of faith).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine), frequently in genitive constructions (e.g., τὰ σκεύη τῆς λειτουργίας, αἱ ἡμέραι τῆς λειτουργίας) or paired with θυσία

senses.definition: Practical ministry, aid, or material contribution rendered to supply the needs of others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine), as genitive dependent on διακονία or ὑστέρημα, sometimes with πρός + accusative for recipient

entries.collocations_and_notes: Associated with temple/tabernacle duties and equipment (LUK 1:23; HEB 9:21) and Christ's covenantal ministry (HEB 8:6). In PHP 2:17, paired with θυσία ("sacrifice") and σπένδομαι ("be poured out as a drink offering"). In 2CO 9:12 and PHP 2:30, connected with filling up needs/lacks (ὑστέρημα) via ἀναπληρόω / προσαναπληρόω.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The human mind or faculty of understanding, an individual thought or conception, or a calculated scheme of an adversary.

senses.definition: The mind or faculty of perception and thought, viewed as something capable of being dulled, blinded, led astray, or guarded.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun with genitive of person, as subject of passive verbs or direct object of transitive verbs

senses.definition: An individual thought, mental conception, or reasoning that can be brought into submission.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun modified by πᾶν ('every'), as direct object of αἰχμαλωτίζοντες ('taking captive')

senses.definition: A plan, intention, or scheme devised to take advantage of others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun with genitive of an adversary (αὐτοῦ, referring to Satan), as direct object of ἀγνοοῦμεν ('be ignorant of')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently used in the plural with a genitive of the person whose mental life is affected (e.g., τὰ νοήματα αὐτῶν / τῶν ἀπίστων / ὑμῶν). Paired with καρδία ('heart') as an object guarded by God's peace in PHP 4:7 (cf. also νοῦς in the same verse). In 2CO 11:3 and PHP 4:7, the plural may encompass both the mind as a faculty and its thoughts. In 2CO 2:11, the plural with Satan as genitive denotes hostile designs rather than a cognitive faculty.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A state of confident assurance, trust, or reliance placed in God, other people, one's course of action, or external credentials.

senses.definition: Confident assurance or trust, whether directed toward God or others, characterizing approach to God, or emboldening action and confrontation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun as direct object of ἔχω, in ἐν + dative, or in bare dative of manner/cause; sometimes with πρός + acc, εἰς + acc, or διά + gen

senses.definition: Reliance or a basis for confidence placed in human or fleshly status.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun as direct object of ἔχων followed by ἐν + dative (ἐν σαρκί)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs with ἔχω ('have') in 2CO 3:4 and PHP 3:4, and in the dative of manner, means, or accompaniment in 2CO 1:15, 2CO 8:22, and 2CO 10:2. Paired with παρρησία ('boldness') and προσαγωγή ('access') in EPH 3:12, and with θαρρέω ('be bold') and τολμάω ('dare') in 2CO 10:2. In 2CO 1:15, the referent of ταύτῃ τῇ πεποιθήσει depends on preceding discourse not included in the verse itself. In PHP 3:4, the noun parallels the cognate infinitive πεποιθέναι ἐν σαρκί in the immediately following clause.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An outward pretense or pretext concealing an ulterior motive, or a valid excuse offered for wrongdoing.

senses.definition: A false show, pretext, or insincere pretense put forward to disguise an ulterior motive or self-interest.
senses.grammatical_frame: Bare dative of manner (προφάσει) or prepositional phrase (ἐν προφάσει), sometimes followed by ὡς + participle or a genitive specifying the concealed vice

senses.definition: A valid excuse, plea, or justification that would absolve someone from guilt or blame.
senses.grammatical_frame: Accusative singular as direct object of ἔχω ('have'), with περί + genitive ('concerning')

entries.collocations_and_notes: In 5 of 6 occurrences, appears in the dative (either bare dative προφάσει or ἐν προφάσει) to express false show or ulterior motive. Explicitly contrasted with ἀληθείᾳ ('in truth/sincerely') in PHP 1:18. MRK 12:40 and LUK 20:47 preserve nearly identical phrasing contrasting pious display with exploiting widows. In 1TH 2:5, the genitive πλεονεξίας ('of greed') identifies the hidden vice masked by the pretext.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To direct one's attention toward things or interests, to observe people closely, or to watch carefully lest something harmful occur.

senses.definition: To direct one's attention, focus, or concern toward specific realities or interests.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active participle with neuter plural articular direct objects (τὰ βλεπόμενα, τὰ ἑαυτῶν, etc.) in μὴ ... ἀλλά contrasts

senses.definition: To observe carefully or keep watch on people, either to guard against and avoid them or to follow their example.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active infinitive or imperative with accusative plural personal object (τούς + participle)

senses.definition: To examine carefully or keep guard over oneself so that an undesirable condition does not happen.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active imperative or participle followed by a cautionary μή ('lest') clause, with or without reflexive object σεαυτόν

entries.collocations_and_notes: In 2CO 4:18 and PHP 2:4, used in negated-and-contrasted pairs (μὴ ... ἀλλά) to redirect attention from visible/self-focused concerns to unseen/others-focused ones. In ROM 16:17 and PHP 3:17, governs an articular participle denoting a group of people characterized by specific conduct, either to avoid (ROM 16:17) or to imitate (PHP 3:17). In LUK 11:35 and GAL 6:1, pairs with a warning clause introduced by μή ('lest').

entries.core_meaning_summary: An athletic contest or intense struggle involving strenuous exertion, endurance, or opposition.

senses.definition: A competitive contest or race requiring sustained discipline and endurance, used metaphorically for persevering in faith.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (accusative); cognate object of ἀγωνίζομαι or object of τρέχω

senses.definition: An intense struggle, conflict, or strenuous exertion endured amid opposition or on behalf of others.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (accusative as object of ἔχω, or dative after ἐν)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears as the direct object of verbs of possessing (ἔχω, PHP 1:30; COL 2:1), competing (cognate verb ἀγωνίζομαι, 1TI 6:12; 2TI 4:7), or running (τρέχω, HEB 12:1). In 1TI 6:12 and 2TI 4:7 it forms the set phrase τὸν καλὸν ἀγῶνα, and in 2TI 4:7 and HEB 12:1 it stands alongside footrace imagery (δρόμος, τρέχω). In 1TH 2:2 ἐν πολλῷ ἀγῶνι describes intense external opposition and hardship accompanying preaching after prior mistreatment.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To fill up a deficiency, occupy a position, or bring a prophecy, obligation, or measure to completion.

senses.definition: To supply what is missing or make up for another's absence or shortfall in service.
senses.grammatical_frame: active verb + accusative (τὸ ὑστέρημα)
