senses.definition: To occupy or fill a particular role, position, or status in a gathering.
senses.grammatical_frame: active participle + accusative (τὸν τόπον + genitive)

senses.definition: To bring a spoken prophecy or moral obligation to full realization or obedience.
senses.grammatical_frame: passive with ἡ προφητεία as subject, or active + accusative (τὸν νόμον)

senses.definition: To fill up the measure of wrongdoing to its full limit.
senses.grammatical_frame: active infinitive (εἰς τὸ + inf) + accusative (τὰς ἁμαρτίας)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Takes varied direct objects depending on context: ὑστέρημα ("what is lacking", 1CO 16:17; PHP 2:30), τόπος ("place/role", 1CO 14:16), νόμος ("law", GAL 6:2), and ἁμαρτίαι ("sins", 1TH 2:16). In MAT 13:14 it appears in the passive with ἡ προφητεία as subject and a dative of reference (αὐτοῖς).

entries.core_meaning_summary: In a manner fitting, appropriate, or corresponding in value and character to someone or something.

senses.definition: In a way that matches and honors the character, calling, or standard of the person or message named in the genitive.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb + genitive, modifying verbs of conduct (περιπατέω, πολιτεύομαι)

senses.definition: With honor, care, and hospitality appropriate to God's character or to the community of believers.
senses.grammatical_frame: adverb + genitive, modifying verbs of receiving or sending travelers (προσδέχομαι, προπέμπω)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly governs a genitive specifying the person, calling, or standard to which the action corresponds (τῶν ἁγίων, τῆς κλήσεως, τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, τοῦ Κυρίου, τοῦ Θεοῦ). Most commonly modifies verbs denoting a way of life (περιπατέω in EPH 4:1; COL 1:10; 1TH 2:12; πολιτεύομαι in PHP 1:27).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Without delay; at once or at that very moment.

senses.definition: Immediately, without intervening delay, or right at a specified moment.
senses.grammatical_frame: temporal adverb modifying a finite verb, participle, or infinitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of sending (ἔπεμψα in ACT 10:33; ACT 23:30; πέμψαι in PHP 2:23). In MRK 6:25 it reinforces a demand already marked by εὐθὺς μετὰ σπουδῆς, and in ACT 11:11 it follows καὶ ἰδού to highlight sudden arrival at that exact moment. In PHP 2:23 it stands at the end of a conditional-temporal clause (ὡς ἂν ἀφίδω τὰ περὶ ἐμὲ ἐξαυτῆς) to express prompt action once the outcome is known.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A perceptible scent or fragrance, used both literally of perfumed ointment and figuratively of a spreading influence or a sacrifice pleasing to God.

senses.definition: The physical scent or fragrance given off by a fragrant substance such as perfumed ointment that fills an enclosed space.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun after ἐκ + genitive, with genitive of source (τοῦ μύρου)

senses.definition: Figuratively, a perceptible spiritual influence or manifestation spread through messengers, producing either death or life among those who encounter it.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun as direct object with abstract genitive (τῆς γνώσεως), or predicate nominative with ἐκ/εἰς prepositional phrases

senses.definition: Figuratively, a pleasing sacrificial fragrance representing a self-giving act or gift offered to God and accepted by him.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun in the phrase ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας, after εἰς + accusative or in apposition to θυσίαν, with τῷ Θεῷ

entries.collocations_and_notes: In JHN 12:3 it takes a concrete genitive (τοῦ μύρου, 'of the perfume') after ἐκ with πληρόω ('be filled from the scent'). In 2CO 2:14–16 it is used metaphorically with an abstract genitive (τῆς γνώσεως αὐτοῦ) and contrasting ἐκ ... εἰς phrases (ἐκ θανάτου εἰς θάνατον / ἐκ ζωῆς εἰς ζωήν). In EPH 5:2 and PHP 4:18 it forms the fixed collocation ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας ('fragrance of a sweet smell') paired explicitly with θυσία ('sacrifice') and προσφορά ('offering') directed toward God.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A visible form, crafted representation, shared outward condition, or structural correspondence between one entity or event and another.

senses.definition: The visible form, appearance, or crafted representation of living creatures or visionary beings.
senses.grammatical_frame: neuter noun (singular after ἐν + dative with genitive εἰκόνος, or plural subject with genitive τῶν ἀκρίδων)

senses.definition: A shared human form, nature, or outward condition in which someone is sent or comes to be.
senses.grammatical_frame: neuter noun after ἐν + dative with genitive (σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας, ἀνθρώπων)

senses.definition: A correspondence in pattern, manner, or counterpart to an earlier event or act such as transgression or death.
senses.grammatical_frame: neuter dative noun after ἐπὶ or as complement of σύμφυτοι, with genitive (τῆς παραβάσεως, τοῦ θανάτου)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in prepositional phrases with ἐν + dative (ROM 1:23; ROM 8:3; PHP 2:7) or ἐπὶ + dative (ROM 5:14), and as a dative complement with σύμφυτοι (ROM 6:5). In ROM 1:23 it combines with εἰκόνος to denote an idolatrous representation; in PHP 2:7 it parallels μορφὴν δούλου and σχήματι; in REV 9:7 the plural τὰ ὁμοιώματα pairs with ὅμοιοι and ὡς to describe visionary appearances.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Proper name of Thessalonica, a city in Macedonia with a Jewish synagogue and Christian community.

senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun, feminine singular governed by prepositions εἰς, ἐν, or ἀπό
senses.definition: Thessalonica, a Macedonian city visited by Paul where he received aid from the Philippians.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Connected geographically with Amphipolis, Apollonia, and Beroea (ACT 17:1, 13) and mentioned as the place where the Philippians repeatedly sent aid to Paul (PHP 4:16).

entries.core_meaning_summary: In the middle/passive, to feel ashamed of something or to be put to shame and disgraced.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present middle/passive indicative or imperative, with infinitive (ἐπαιτεῖν) or conditional role (ὡς Χριστιανός)
senses.definition: To feel embarrassment or shame over an action or identity.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, future or aorist passive (οὐκ αἰσχυνθήσομαι; μὴ αἰσχυνθῶμεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ), contrasted with παρρησία ('boldness')
senses.definition: To be put to shame, disgraced, or disappointed in one's hope or confidence.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Contrasted with παρρησία ('boldness/confidence') in PHP 1:20 and 1JN 2:28, and with δοξαζέτω δὲ τὸν Θεόν in 1PE 4:16.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Acceptable and pleasing to someone, or designating an appointed, favorable time.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective describing a prophet, person, or sacrifice, often with dative αὐτῷ / τῷ Θεῷ
senses.definition: Welcomed, approved, or pleasing to a community or to God.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective modifying time nouns (ἐνιαυτὸν Κυρίου δεκτόν; καιρῷ δεκτῷ)
senses.definition: Favorable or chosen as a season of divine grace and deliverance.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Glossed by εὐπρόσδεκτος ('well-accepted/favorable') in 2CO 6:2 and paired with εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ in θυσίαν δεκτήν (PHP 4:18).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Concessive conjunction introducing a participle to mean 'although' or 'even though.'

senses.grammatical_frame: Concessive particle/conjunction always followed by a participle (ἔχων, ὤν, ἐξεληλυθότας, ἐκζητήσας, εἰδότας)
senses.definition: Marks a fact or circumstance in spite of which the main clause holds true.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Consistently introduces a concessive participial phrase (e.g., καίπερ ὢν Υἱός, HEB 5:8; καίπερ ἐγὼ ἔχων πεποίθησιν, PHP 3:4).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To make empty, void, or ineffective, or reflexively to empty oneself of status.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, active or passive with abstract subjects/objects (ἡ πίστις, ὁ σταυρὸς τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τὸ καύχημα)
senses.definition: To render hollow, void, or devoid of force and validity.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, aorist active indicative with reflexive object ἑαυτόν, elaborated by modal participles (μορφὴν δούλου λαβών)
senses.definition: To empty oneself by voluntarily laying aside privilege and taking a lowly condition.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with κατήργηται ('is nullified') in ROM 4:14 and frequently takes τὸ καύχημα ('boasting') as object/subject (1CO 9:15; 2CO 9:3). In PHP 2:7 ἑαυτὸν ἐκένωσεν has no genitive of content, being explained by μορφὴν δούλου λαβών.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A dog (scavenger animal), or figuratively a derogatory term for impure or dangerous people.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular or plural referring to literal scavenging animals
senses.definition: A dog, depicted as an unclean scavenger or street animal.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine plural used polemically of dangerous opponents or excluded evildoers
senses.definition: Figurative label of contempt for harmful, morally impure, or excluded persons.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with swine (χοῖροι / ὗς) in MAT 7:6 and 2PE 2:22; grouped with κακοὺς ἐργάτας and κατατομήν in PHP 3:2 and with sorcerers, murderers, and idolaters outside the city in REV 22:15.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A public servant, cultic/spiritual minister of God, or commissioned envoy meeting someone's needs.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular or plural with genitive Θεοῦ / Χριστοῦ / τῶν ἁγίων / αὐτοῦ
senses.definition: A servant or minister appointed to carry out divine, priestly, or public service (of rulers, Paul, angels, or Christ).

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular accusative with genitive τῆς χρείας μου, paired with ἀπόστολον
senses.definition: A commissioned attendant or envoy sent by a congregation to care for someone's practical need.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Linked with priestly action ἱερουργοῦντα in ROM 15:16, the sanctuary in HEB 8:2, and practical supply (λειτουργὸν τῆς χρείας μου) in PHP 2:25.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To transform in form/condition, to disguise oneself, or to apply a figure to oneself.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, aorist active indicative with direct object ταῦτα and εἰς + personal accusative (εἰς ἐμαυτὸν καὶ Ἀπολλῶν)
senses.definition: To apply a pattern or figure of speech to specific persons by way of illustration.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present middle/passive indicative or participle with εἰς + accusative or ὡς
senses.definition: To disguise oneself or take on a deceptive outward guise.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, future active indicative with direct object (τὸ σῶμα) and predicate adjective σύμμορφον
senses.definition: To transform or change the bodily form and condition into conformity with Christ's glorious body.

entries.collocations_and_notes: All three senses involve shifting form or presentation: rhetorical transfer (1CO 4:6), deceptive self-disguise (2CO 11:13–15), and eschatological bodily transformation (PHP 3:21).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Compassion, mercy, or pity shown by God or between people.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine (usually plural οἰκτιρμοί), paired with σπλάγχνα ('affection') or governed by διά / χωρίς
senses.definition: Deeply felt compassion, mercy, or pity toward others or from God.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with σπλάγχνα (PHP 2:1; σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ in COL 3:12); used of God as ὁ Πατὴρ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν (2CO 1:3) and negated in χωρὶς οἰκτιρμῶν ('without pity/mercy', HEB 10:28).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To walk in step with, follow consistently, or order one's conduct according to a standard or path.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present or future active governing a dative of standard/path (τοῖς ἴχνεσιν, Πνεύματι, τῷ κανόνι, τῷ αὐτῷ) or with participle φυλάσσων τὸν νόμον
senses.definition: To live in line with, follow steadily, or conform one's way of life to a rule, footsteps, or the Spirit.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Takes datives τοῖς ἴχνεσιν ('in the footsteps', ROM 4:12), Πνεύματι ('by the Spirit', GAL 5:25), τῷ κανόνι τούτῳ ('by this rule', GAL 6:16), and τῷ αὐτῷ ('by the same [standard]', PHP 3:16).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Trembling or awe-filled dread accompanying fear, reverence, or earnest obedience.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular; paired with ἔκστασις or regularly in the prepositional pair ἐν / μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου
senses.definition: Physical or inward trembling caused by terror, awe, or serious reverent obedience.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Four of five occurrences appear in the fixed phrase (ἐν / μετὰ) φόβου καὶ τρόμου ('with fear and trembling', 1CO 2:3; 2CO 7:15; EPH 6:5; PHP 2:12).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Moral excellence or virtue in human character, or the mighty excellence and praiseworthy deeds of God.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular; paired with ἔπαινος ('praise') or listed between πίστις and γνῶσις
senses.definition: Moral goodness, excellence, or noble character cultivated by believers.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular or plural attributed to God (τὰς ἀρετάς ... τοῦ καλέσαντος; ἰδίᾳ δόξῃ καὶ ἀρετῇ)
senses.definition: God's glorious power, excellence, or praiseworthy acts to be proclaimed.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with ἔπαινος in PHP 4:8 and with δόξῃ in 2PE 1:3; stands between faith and knowledge in 2PE 1:5.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Certain and reliable (of facts), or safe, secure, and firm.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, neuter singular (τὸ ἀσφαλές; ἀσφαλές τι) as object of γνῶναι ('to know') or γράψαι ('to write')
senses.definition: What is certain, verified, and reliable as fact.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, neuter predicate with dative (ὑμῖν δὲ ἀσφαλές) or feminine modifying ἄγκυραν ('anchor') alongside βεβαίαν
senses.definition: Safe, protective, or firm and unfailing as a safeguard.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used in Roman investigative contexts in Acts (γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλές, ACT 21:34; 22:30); contrasted with ὀκνηρόν in PHP 3:1 and paired with βεβαίαν ('firm') for an anchor in HEB 6:19.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Blameless, faultless, or free from defect in conduct or covenant standing.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective describing persons (with πορευόμενοι, γενόμενος, στηρίξαι) or a covenant (ἡ πρώτη)
senses.definition: Free from blame or defect in obedience, moral life, or structural adequacy.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used with πορευόμενοι ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐντολαῖς (LUK 1:6), κατὰ δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐν νόμῳ (PHP 3:6), paired with ἀκέραιοι and ἄμωμα (PHP 2:15), and negated conditionally of the first covenant (HEB 8:7).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Gentle, reasonable, forbearing, and considerate toward others.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective in ethical lists (paired with ἄμαχον, εἰρηνική, ἀγαθοῖς) or neuter substantive τὸ ἐπιεικὲς ὑμῶν
senses.definition: Gentle, fair-minded, and patient rather than quarrelsome, harsh, or insistent on strict rights.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with ἄμαχον ('peaceable', 1TI 3:3; TIT 3:2), πραΰτητα (TIT 3:2), εἰρηνική and εὐπειθής (JAS 3:17), and ἀγαθοῖς as contrast to σκολιοῖς (1PE 2:18).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To pay close attention to, to stay/delay for a time, or to hold fast/hold forth.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present active participle or imperative with indirect question (πῶς...), dative of person (αὐτοῖς), or dative of care (σεαυτῷ καὶ τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ)
senses.definition: To watch closely, give heed to, or focus expectant attention on someone or something.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, aorist active indicative with temporal accusative χρόνον and εἰς + place
senses.definition: To remain, stay behind, or delay for a period of time in a region.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present active participle governing direct object λόγον ζωῆς
senses.definition: To hold fast to or hold forth the word of life.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Note the ambiguity in PHP 2:16 (λόγον ζωῆς ἐπέχοντες), which contextually fits either clinging firmly to the word of life or holding it out as a light to the world.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An overseer or guardian entrusted with pastoral care and stewardship of a church or of souls.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular or plural; paired with διακόνοις, linked to ποιμαίνειν ('shepherd') and Θεοῦ οἰκονόμον ('God's steward')
senses.definition: A leader charged with spiritual oversight, pastoral care, and stewardship in a Christian congregation.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular paired with Ποιμένα ('Shepherd') and genitive τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν
senses.definition: Guardian or protector watching over believers' souls (applied to Christ).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Closely linked with pastoral imagery (ποιμαίνειν in ACT 20:28; Ποιμένα in 1PE 2:25), paired with διακόνοις ('deacons') in PHP 1:1, and compared to Θεοῦ οἰκονόμον ('God's steward') in TIT 1:7.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Honored, highly regarded, or precious in value and rank.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective (positive or comparative ἐντιμότερος), predicate with εἶναι / ἔχειν or dative of esteem (αὐτῷ)
senses.definition: Highly regarded, dear, or honored in status and esteem among people.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective modifying λίθον ('stone') alongside ἐκλεκτόν ('chosen') and ἀκρογωνιαῖον ('cornerstone')
senses.definition: Precious, prized, and of high worth in God's sight.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Forms the idiom ἐντίμους ἔχετε ('hold in honor', PHP 2:29); comparative ἐντιμότερός σου ('more distinguished/higher in rank than you', LUK 14:8); paired with ἐκλεκτόν ('chosen') in 1PE 2:4, 6.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To hold superior authority or rank, or to surpass in excellence or exceed comprehension.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present active participle (ὑπερεχούσαις, ὑπερέχοντι, ὑπερέχοντας) modifying rulers/authorities or with genitive of comparison (ἑαυτῶν)
senses.definition: To be above others in rank, governing authority, or personal regard.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, neuter participle substantive (τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως) or active participle governing accusative πάντα νοῦν
senses.definition: To surpass in worth or exceed the limits of human understanding.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Applied to civil rulers in ἐξουσίαις ὑπερεχούσαις (ROM 13:1) and βασιλεῖ ὡς ὑπερέχοντι (1PE 2:13); substantivized in τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως Χριστοῦ (PHP 3:8); governs πάντα νοῦν in PHP 4:7.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Proper name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable proper noun in the genitive phrase ἐκ φυλῆς / φυλῆς Βενιαμείν ('of the tribe of Benjamin')
senses.definition: Benjamin, one of the tribes of Israel from which King Saul and Paul descended.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Every occurrence appears in the genealogical formula (ἐκ) φυλῆς Βενιαμείν (spelled Βενιαμείν in the text).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Proper name of Philippi, a leading city and Roman colony in Macedonia.

senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun, masculine plural, governed by prepositions εἰς, ἀπό, or ἐν
senses.definition: Philippi, a prominent city and colony in the region of Macedonia where a Christian congregation was established.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Identified in ACT 16:12 as πρώτη τῆς μερίδος Μακεδονίας πόλις, κολωνία; addressed as the location of the saints, overseers, and deacons in PHP 1:1.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Genuine, true, or authentic, applied to spiritual kin, a loyal colleague, and sincere love.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective modifying τέκνῳ ('child') or σύνζυγε ('partner'), or neuter substantive τὸ ... γνήσιον ('genuineness')
senses.definition: True, genuine, and authentic (in spiritual kinship, partnership, or love).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Substantivized in τὸ τῆς ὑμετέρας ἀγάπης γνήσιον ('the genuineness of your love', 2CO 8:8); modifies τέκνῳ in 1TI 1:2 and TIT 1:4, and σύνζυγε in PHP 4:3.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Discontented grumbling or complaining, or hushed murmured discussion among a crowd.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular or plural; subject of ἐγένετο (with πρός + acc) or after prepositions χωρίς / ἄνευ
senses.definition: Complaining, grumbling, or expression of dissatisfaction toward others or while carrying out duties.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular nominative (γογγυσμὸς ... πολὺς ἐν τοῖς ὄχλοις) introducing conflicting opinions
senses.definition: Hushed, divided murmuring or whispered talk among a crowd.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with διαλογισμῶν ('disputes/arguments') after χωρίς (PHP 2:14); negated with ἄνευ regarding hospitality (1PE 4:9); arises over neglected widows in ACT 6:1.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A concrete gift or present given to children, people, or a minister.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, neuter singular or plural; direct object of διδόναι / ἔδωκεν / ἐπιζητῶ
senses.definition: Something given as a gift or present, whether by parents to children, by Christ to humanity, or by a church to support Paul.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Modified by ἀγαθά with the cognate verb διδόναι in MAT 7:11 and LUK 11:13; contrasted with τὸν καρπὸν τὸν πλεονάζοντα εἰς λόγον ὑμῶν in PHP 4:17.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Material damage or loss, or spiritual/personal forfeit contrasted with gain.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular; paired with ὕβρις ('disaster/injury') and genitives τοῦ φορτίου καὶ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ τῶν ψυχῶν
senses.definition: Material loss, damage, or harm to cargo, ship, and human lives.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular accusative; predicate object of ἡγέομαι ('consider/count as'), contrasted with κέρδη ('gains')
senses.definition: Loss or detriment, used figuratively for former privileges reckoned worthless compared to knowing Christ.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with ὕβρις in ACT 27:10, 21 (with the ironic phrase κερδῆσαι ... τὴν ζημίαν, 'spared yourself this loss'); directly contrasted with κέρδη and followed by cognate ἐζημιώθην in PHP 3:7–8.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To bend or bow the knee in worship, prayer, or homage.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, active indicative or subjunctive always taking γόνυ / τὰ γόνατα ('knee/knees') as object or subject, with dative or πρός of the one honored
senses.definition: To kneel or bow the knee as an act of religious devotion, prayer, or universal homage.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Consistently collocates with γόνυ ('knee'): ἔκαμψαν γόνυ τῇ Βάαλ (ROM 11:4), ἐμοὶ κάμψει πᾶν γόνυ (ROM 14:11), κάμπτω τὰ γόνατά μου πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα (EPH 3:14), and ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ πᾶν γόνυ κάμψῃ (PHP 2:10).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Dignified, honorable, and worthy of respect in character or quality.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective describing church leaders, women, or older men in lists of moral qualifications
senses.definition: Dignified, earnest, and respectable in personal bearing and conduct.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, neuter plural nominative in an ὅσα series of praiseworthy qualities
senses.definition: Honorable, noble, or worthy of reverence.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears alongside νηφαλίους and σώφρονας in Pastoral virtue lists (1TI 3:8, 11; TIT 2:2) and between ἀληθῆ and δίκαια in PHP 4:8.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Physically crooked or winding, or morally perverse and harsh.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, neuter plural substantive (τὰ σκολιά) contrasted with εὐθείας ('straight [roads]')
senses.definition: Crooked or winding (of terrain or paths), to be made straight.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective modifying γενεά ('generation') or substantivized of masters (contrasted with ἀγαθοῖς καὶ ἐπιεικέσιν)
senses.definition: Morally crooked, perverse, or harsh and unjust in treatment of others.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Contrasted with εὐθείας in LUK 3:5; modifies γενεά in ACT 2:40 and PHP 2:15 (paired with διεστραμμένης); contrasted with ἀγαθοῖς καὶ ἐπιεικέσιν ('good and gentle') masters in 1PE 2:18.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Eagerly, earnestly, diligently, or promptly.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb (positive σπουδαίως or comparative σπουδαιοτέρως) modifying verbs of requesting, sending, or searching
senses.definition: With earnestness, diligent effort, or prompt eagerness.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Modifies παρεκάλουν ('pleaded', LUK 7:4), ἔπεμψα (comparative σπουδαιοτέρως, 'the more eagerly/promptly', PHP 2:28), ἐζήτησεν ('searched', 2TI 1:17), and πρόπεμψον ('send on their way', TIT 3:13).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A fellow sharer, partaker, or partner with others in blessings, the gospel, or affliction.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular or plural; takes genitive of the thing shared (τῆς ῥίζης, αὐτοῦ, τῆς χάριτος) or ἐν + dative (ἐν τῇ θλίψει)
senses.definition: One who shares alongside others in a spiritual blessing, mission, or suffering.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with ἀδελφός in REV 1:9; takes both personal genitive μου and object genitive τῆς χάριτος in συνκοινωνούς μου τῆς χάριτος (PHP 1:7).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Lowly or humble condition, or humiliation and being brought low.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular accusative or genitive (τὸ σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως ἡμῶν), describing lowly estate or mortal weakness
senses.definition: Lowly, humble, or fragile mortal condition (contrasted with glory).

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular dative after ἐν (ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει), denoting suffering injustice or loss of status
senses.definition: Humiliation, degradation, or being brought low in status or suffering.

entries.collocations_and_notes: In PHP 3:21 τὸ σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως ἡμῶν stands in direct contrast to τῷ σώματι τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ; in JAS 1:10 applied to a rich person fading like a flower.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To guard or keep under watch/confinement, or to protect and keep safe.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, active with city object (τὴν πόλιν) or passive with ὑπὸ νόμον and συνκλειόμενοι ('shut up/confined')
senses.definition: To keep under armed watch or restrictive custody.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, active future (with subject ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ Θεοῦ and object τὰς καρδίας ... καὶ τὰ νοήματα) or passive (ἐν δυνάμει Θεοῦ φρουρουμένους)
senses.definition: To guard, protect, and keep secure against harm or threat.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used literally of guarding Damascus to arrest Paul (2CO 11:32), metaphorically of confinement under the law (GAL 3:23), and metaphorically of divine protection by God's peace or power (PHP 4:7; 1PE 1:5).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To step out of a boat onto land, or to turn out / result in a particular outcome.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, aorist active participle or indicative with ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ('from the boats') or εἰς τὴν γῆν ('onto the land')
senses.definition: To get out of a boat or come ashore.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, future middle indicative (ἀποβήσεται) with dative of person (ὑμῖν / μοι) and εἰς + accusative (εἰς μαρτύριον / εἰς σωτηρίαν)
senses.definition: To turn out or result in a specific outcome for someone.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Note the clear syntactic split: literal motion from boats in Gospel narratives (LUK 5:2; JHN 21:9) vs. future impersonal/neuter result construction ἀποβήσεται [dative] εἰς [noun] (LUK 21:13; PHP 1:19).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Without fear, boldly, or without reverent restraint.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying verbs of serving, visiting, or speaking (λατρεύειν, γένηται, τολμᾶν ... λαλεῖν)
senses.definition: Without fear, calmly, or boldly.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying συνευωχούμενοι ('feasting together') in a polemical denunciation
senses.definition: Without fear of judgment or reverent restraint; brazenly.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with τολμᾶν ('to dare') in PHP 1:14 and with rescue from enemies in LUK 1:74; takes a negative moral sense in JUD 1:12 alongside ἑαυτοὺς ποιμαίνοντες ('shepherding themselves').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A clear demonstration, proof, or visible sign of a quality or outcome.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular; after prepositions εἰς / πρός, object of ἐνδεικνύμενοι, or predicate nominative with dative of persons
senses.definition: Proof, visible demonstration, or unmistakable evidence showing something to be true.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used with τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ (ROM 3:25, 26), with cognate participle ἐνδεικνύμενοι for τῆς ἀγάπης ὑμῶν (2CO 8:24), and of a sign pointing to destruction and salvation in PHP 1:28.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A Hebrew, denoting an Israelite by ancestral heritage and/or traditional Aramaic-Hebrew Jewish community.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular or plural; contrasted with Ἑλληνισταί or grouped with Ἰσραηλεῖται, σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ, and φυλῆς Βενιαμείν
senses.definition: A member of the Jewish/Israelite people, especially emphasizing ancestral lineage or traditional Hebrew/Aramaic identity as distinguished from Greek-speaking Jews.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Contrasted with Ἑλληνισταί ('Hellenists') in ACT 6:1; parallels Ἰσραηλεῖται and σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ in 2CO 11:22; appears in the lineage phrase Ἑβραῖος ἐξ Ἑβραίων ('a Hebrew of Hebrews') in PHP 3:5.

entries.core_meaning_summary: In the middle voice, to choose, select, or prefer one person or course of action over another.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, middle voice (future αἱρήσομαι, aorist εἵλατο / ἑλόμενος) with interrogative τί, personal object ὑμᾶς ... εἰς σωτηρίαν, or comparative infinitive μᾶλλον ... ἤ
senses.definition: To choose, select, or decide in favor of one option or people.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used of deliberating between options (τί αἱρήσομαι οὐ γνωρίζω, PHP 1:22), divine election (εἵλατο ὑμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς εἰς σωτηρίαν, 2TH 2:13), and choosing hardship over fleeting pleasure (μᾶλλον ἑλόμενος ... ἤ, HEB 11:25).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A request, petition, or demand presented to a ruler or to God.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, neuter singular or plural; subject of γενέσθαι / γνωριζέσθω, or object of ἔχομεν modified by relative clause ἃ ᾐτήκαμεν
senses.definition: A specific request, petition, or demand made to a governing authority or in prayer to God.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used of a crowd's demand granted by Pilate (LUK 23:24), believers' prayer requests made known to God (PHP 4:6), and petitions asked of God (τὰ αἰτήματα ἃ ᾐτήκαμεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, 1JN 5:15).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A sweet fragrance or pleasing aroma, especially in sacrificial imagery of an offering acceptable to God.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular nominative or genitive in the phrase ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας ('a fragrant aroma'), associated with θυσίαν ('sacrifice')
senses.definition: Pleasant fragrance or sweet-smelling aroma, used figuratively of Christ's self-offering, believers' ministry, and gifts pleasing to God.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs twice in the cultic expression ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας alongside θυσίαν (EPH 5:2; PHP 4:18) and once in Χριστοῦ εὐωδία ἐσμὲν τῷ Θεῷ (2CO 2:15).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Gain, advantage, or profit, whether spiritual/personal or financial.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, neuter singular or plural; predicate nominative contrasted with ζημίαν ('loss') or paired with τὸ ἀποθανεῖν
senses.definition: Advantage, benefit, or gain (including prior status or assets counted as loss for Christ, or dying as gain).

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, neuter singular genitive modified by αἰσχροῦ ('shameful') with postposition χάριν ('for the sake of')
senses.definition: Monetary profit or material gain sought improperly.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Directly contrasted with ζημίαν ('loss') in PHP 3:7; paired with αἰσχροῦ ... χάριν ('for shameful gain') in TIT 1:11.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Form, outward appearance, or characteristic mode of existence/manifestation.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular dative after ἐν (ἐν ἑτέρᾳ μορφῇ; ἐν μορφῇ Θεοῦ) or accusative object of λαβών (μορφὴν δούλου)
senses.definition: Visible form or characteristic mode of manifestation, whether in changed physical appearance or in divine versus servile status.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used with ἐφανερώθη ἐν ἑτέρᾳ μορφῇ (MRK 16:12) and in the contrast ἐν μορφῇ Θεοῦ ὑπάρχων ... μορφὴν δούλου λαβών (PHP 2:6–7).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only three times; while MRK 16:12 refers to outward appearance, PHP 2:6–7 leaves open whether μορφή emphasizes essential nature, visible glory/form, or characteristic station alongside ὁμοίωμα and σχῆμα.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To think, suppose, assume, or expect something to be the case.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, deponent indicative, imperative, or participle taking an infinitive complement or ὅτι clause
senses.definition: To suppose, imagine, or assume something (often an expectation or personal estimate).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Takes an accusative-infinitive clause in JHN 21:25, a complementary infinitive (οἰόμενοι θλῖψιν ἐγείρειν) in PHP 1:17, and a ὅτι clause in JAS 1:7.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To remain, stay on with others or in an office, or to persevere faithfully in a teaching.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, active future or infinitive, with dative of persons (πᾶσιν ὑμῖν) or absolute (contrasted with death)
senses.definition: To stay on, continue alive, or remain present with people or in a role.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, aorist active participle (παραμείνας) following παρακύψας εἰς νόμον τέλειον
senses.definition: To persevere or abide steadfastly in what one has examined and heard.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with μενῶ in μενῶ καὶ παραμενῶ πᾶσιν ὑμῖν (PHP 1:25); prevented by death in θανάτῳ κωλύεσθαι παραμένειν (HEB 7:23); contrasted with a forgetful hearer in JAS 1:25.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Progress, advancement, or forward growth in ministry or faith.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular accusative after εἰς (εἰς προκοπὴν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου; εἰς τὴν ὑμῶν προκοπήν) or nominative subject of φανερὰ ᾖ
senses.definition: Advancement or measurable progress in the spread of the gospel or in spiritual maturity and faith.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears with genitives τοῦ εὐαγγελίου (PHP 1:12) and τῆς πίστεως (PHP 1:25, paired with χαράν), and as visible growth in ἵνα σου ἡ προκοπὴ φανερὰ ᾖ πᾶσιν (1TI 4:15).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To share in or participate together with others in actions, sins, or hardships.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, active imperative, participle, or subjunctive governing a dative object (τοῖς ἔργοις, μου τῇ θλίψει, ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις)
senses.definition: To take part in or share alongside another in deeds, sins, or affliction.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used positively of supporting someone in trouble (συνκοινωνήσαντές μου τῇ θλίψει, PHP 4:14) and negatively in warnings against complicity in evil deeds or sins (EPH 5:11; REV 18:4).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be deeply distressed, troubled, or anguished.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present active infinitive (after ἤρξατο) or participle, paired with λυπεῖσθαι, ἐκθαμβεῖσθαι, or ἐπιποθῶν
senses.definition: To experience intense inner distress, agitation, or heavy-hearted anxiety.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Coordinated with λυπεῖσθαι ('be grieved', MAT 26:37) and ἐκθαμβεῖσθαι ('be deeply alarmed', MRK 14:33) in Gethsemane, and with ἐπιποθῶν ('longing') over readers' worry in PHP 2:26.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Innocent, pure, or untainted by guile or evil.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, masculine plural nominative or accusative, paired with ἄμεμπτοι / ἄμωμα or contrasted with φρόνιμοι / σοφούς
senses.definition: Guileless, innocent, and unmixed with evil or corruption.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Simile ἀκέραιοι ὡς αἱ περιστεραί ('innocent as doves', MAT 10:16); contrasted with wise toward good in ἀκεραίους δὲ εἰς τὸ κακόν (ROM 16:19); paired with ἄμεμπτοι (PHP 2:15).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Blameless and free from offense, or not causing others to stumble.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective modifying συνείδησιν ('conscience') or coordinated with εἰλικρινεῖς ('pure/sincere')
senses.definition: Clear, blameless, and without fault or stumbling before God and people.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, masculine plural nominative with dative of groups (Ἰουδαίοις ... Ἕλλησιν ... τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ)
senses.definition: Giving no occasion for stumbling or offense to others.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Qualifies συνείδησιν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους (ACT 24:16), governs datives of communities (1CO 10:32), and pairs with εἰλικρινεῖς (PHP 1:10).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs three times; in PHP 1:10 (εἰλικρινεῖς καὶ ἀπρόσκοποι εἰς ἡμέραν Χριστοῦ) context allows either intransitive 'blameless/without stumbling' or transitive 'not causing offense to others.'

entries.core_meaning_summary: Lazy or lagging when describing people, and irksome or troublesome when describing a task.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective applied to persons (vocative δοῦλε ... ὀκνηρέ; predicate τῇ σπουδῇ μὴ ὀκνηροί)
senses.definition: Lazy, idle, or reluctant to exert effort in duty or zeal.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, neuter singular predicate with infinitive subject (τὰ αὐτὰ γράφειν) and dative of person (ἐμοὶ μὲν οὐκ ὀκνηρόν)
senses.definition: Troublesome, irksome, or burdensome for someone to do.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with πονηρέ in MAT 25:26, negated with τῇ σπουδῇ in ROM 12:11, and contrasted with ἀσφαλές ('safe/safeguard') in PHP 3:1.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Obedient or submissive to authority or instruction.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective used predicatively with γενέσθαι or ἐστέ, with dative of person (ᾧ), εἰς πάντα, or extent μέχρι θανάτου
senses.definition: Willing to listen and submit to another's authority or command.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Negated in οὐκ ἠθέλησαν ὑπήκοοι γενέσθαι (ACT 7:39), tested in εἰ εἰς πάντα ὑπήκοοί ἐστε (2CO 2:9), and intensified in γενόμενος ὑπήκοος μέχρι θανάτου (PHP 2:8).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Confirmation, validation, or authoritative establishing of truth or an agreement.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular dative/accusative after ἐν (paired with ἀπολογίᾳ) or εἰς (as purpose of an oath ending dispute)
senses.definition: Confirmation or validation that establishes the truth of a message or puts an end to dispute.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with ἀπολογίᾳ in ἐν τῇ ἀπολογίᾳ καὶ βεβαιώσει τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ('in the defense and confirmation of the gospel', PHP 1:7), and used with πέρας ἀντιλογίας in πάσης αὐτοῖς ἀντιλογίας πέρας εἰς βεβαίωσιν ὁ ὅρκος ('an oath is the end of all dispute for confirmation', HEB 6:16).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; both legal-argumentative contexts converge cleanly on 'confirmation/validation,' though limited attestation leaves finer institutional or legal nuances unexamined.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The prize or award won by a runner in a race, used figuratively for the reward of God's call.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, neuter singular accusative; direct object of λαμβάνει or prepositional goal after εἰς with διώκω
senses.definition: The prize awarded to the victor in a stadium race, extended metaphorically to the goal of Christian calling.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used literally of stadium runners in λαμβάνει τὸ βραβεῖον (1CO 9:24) and metaphorically with κατὰ σκοπὸν διώκω εἰς τὸ βραβεῖον τῆς ἄνω κλήσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ (PHP 3:14).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice, both in athletic-race contexts; while 'prize/award' is clear, any non-athletic usage is unattested.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The act of giving (paired with receiving) or a good gift bestowed from above.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular genitive paired with λήμψεως in the phrase εἰς λόγον δόσεως καὶ λήμψεως
senses.definition: The act of giving, as one side of a mutual account or partnership alongside receiving.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular nominative modified by ἀγαθή and paired with πᾶν δώρημα τέλειον
senses.definition: A gift or act of giving that comes down from God.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in the partnership formula εἰς λόγον δόσεως καὶ λήμψεως (PHP 4:15) and in parallel with δώρημα in πᾶσα δόσις ἀγαθὴ καὶ πᾶν δώρημα τέλειον (JAS 1:17).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; in JAS 1:17 it is somewhat ambiguous whether δόσις refers to the act of giving (contrasting with δώρημα as the concrete gift) or functions synonymously with 'gift.'

entries.core_meaning_summary: Pure, sincere, and unmixed in moral character or mental disposition.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, masculine plural nominative (paired with ἀπρόσκοποι) or feminine singular accusative modifying διάνοιαν
senses.definition: Pure, sincere, and free from hidden corruption or mixed motives, whether of persons or of the mind.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Coordinated with ἀπρόσκοποι ('blameless/without offense') in ἵνα ἦτε εἰλικρινεῖς καὶ ἀπρόσκοποι (PHP 1:10), and modifies διάνοιαν ('mind/understanding') in τὴν εἰλικρινῆ διάνοιαν (2PE 3:1).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; both passages indicate moral/mental purity and sincerity, yet two brief occurrences do not sharply distinguish its nuance from other terms for purity or blamelessness.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To conduct one's life or fulfill one's duties as a member of a community in relation to God or the gospel.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, middle/passive indicative or imperative, modified by manner phrases (πάσῃ συνειδήσει ἀγαθῇ τῷ Θεῷ; ἀξίως τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τοῦ Χριστοῦ)
senses.definition: To live, conduct oneself, or discharge one's communal obligations in a manner fitting God or the gospel.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used by Paul before the Sanhedrin with πάσῃ συνειδήσει ἀγαθῇ πεπολίτευμαι τῷ Θεῷ (ACT 23:1), and as an imperative to the community: ἀξίως τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τοῦ Χριστοῦ πολιτεύεσθε, linked to standing firm in one spirit (PHP 1:27).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; both passages clearly indicate moral/communal conduct before God or as a Christian community, though it remains somewhat open how strongly a civic/political metaphor ('live as citizens') is felt versus general 'conduct one's life.'

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be poured out as a drink offering, used figuratively of giving up one's life in sacrificial service or approaching death.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present passive indicative (σπένδομαι), used figuratively with ἐπὶ τῇ θυσίᾳ ('upon the sacrifice') or absolutely of impending death
senses.definition: To be poured out like a sacrificial libation, metaphorically depicting the surrender of one's life in service or death.
glosses: be poured out as a drink offering

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired with cultic terms θυσίᾳ καὶ λειτουργίᾳ ('sacrifice and priestly service') in PHP 2:17 and linked to impending departure (ὁ καιρὸς τῆς ἀναλύσεώς μου ἐφέστηκεν) in 2TI 4:6.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice, both times in the passive voice and figurative self-reference to Paul's life/death; literal ritual usage is unattested in the corpus.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To strive, contend, or labor side by side with others in the cause of the gospel.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, active participle or aorist indicative with dative complement (τῇ πίστει τοῦ εὐαγγελίου; μοι ... ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ)
senses.definition: To struggle or work energetically alongside others for the sake of the gospel and its faith.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears with μιᾷ ψυχῇ ('with one soul/mind') in PHP 1:27 and with personal dative μοι + ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ alongside συνεργῶν μου ('my fellow workers') in PHP 4:3.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; in PHP 1:27 the dative τῇ πίστει is slightly ambiguous between dative of advantage ('striving together for the faith') and associative dative ('contending alongside the faith').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A fellow soldier or comrade-in-arms, used metaphorically for a companion sharing hardships in gospel work.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular accusative or dative with possessive genitive (μου, ἡμῶν), coordinated with ἀδελφόν and συνεργόν
senses.definition: Comrade-in-arms or fellow campaigner, denoting a Christian colleague who shares struggles and service.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Applied to Epaphroditus alongside ἀδελφὸν καὶ συνεργόν (PHP 2:25) and to Archippus (PHM 1:2).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice, both metaphorically for Christian co-workers; literal military usage does not appear in the corpus.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The outward appearance, form, or passing external order of something.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, neuter singular dative (σχήματι) with passive participle εὑρεθείς and comparative ὡς ἄνθρωπος
senses.definition: Outward form, bearing, or visible appearance as recognized by others.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, neuter singular nominative with genitive τοῦ κόσμου τούτου, subject of παράγει ('is passing away')
senses.definition: The present outward structure, order, or configuration of the world.

entries.collocations_and_notes: In PHP 2:7 follows μορφὴν δούλου and ἐν ὁμοιώματι ἀνθρώπων γενόμενος; in 1CO 7:31 appears in παράγει γὰρ τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; while both denote outward form or configuration, PHP 2:7 leaves open the exact distinction between σχῆμα and neighboring terms μορφή and ὁμοίωμα.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Sharing the same form or fashioned to be like another model or body.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, accusative with genitive (τῆς εἰκόνος τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ) or dative (τῷ σώματι τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ)
senses.definition: Conformed to or having the same form and likeness as another.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Object complement of προώρισεν in ROM 8:29 (συμμόρφους τῆς εἰκόνος) and of μετασχηματίσει in PHP 3:21 (σύμμορφον τῷ σώματι τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice, both in theological transformation contexts; whether it implies visible external likeness, ontological conformity, or both depends on the surrounding nouns (εἰκών vs. σῶμα).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A shining light-bearer or brilliant radiance.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine plural nominative after comparative ὡς with φαίνεσθε ('you shine') and locative ἐν κόσμῳ
senses.definition: A luminous body or light-giver shining brightly in the world.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular nominative with genitive αὐτῆς, compared to a precious crystal-clear stone
senses.definition: Brilliance or light-emitting splendor of a city.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used with φαίνεσθε ὡς φωστῆρες ἐν κόσμῳ (PHP 2:15) and to describe the glory-filled appearance of the heavenly city (REV 21:11).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; in PHP 2:15 it could evoke celestial lights (stars/luminaries) or lamps generally, while in REV 21:11 it refers to the city's gem-like radiance.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To return from a gathering, or to depart from this life.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, aorist active subjunctive with ἐκ + genitive (ἐκ τῶν γάμων)
senses.definition: To return home or come back from an event or place.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, aorist active infinitive in εἰς τὸ ἀναλῦσαι, coordinated with καὶ σὺν Χριστῷ εἶναι
senses.definition: To depart from earthly life, viewed as passing to be with Christ.

entries.collocations_and_notes: In LUK 12:36 awaits the master returning ἐκ τῶν γάμων; in PHP 1:23 paired with σὺν Χριστῷ εἶναι in contrast to remaining in the flesh.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice, with one sense each; whether PHP 1:23 carries a specific metaphor (such as weighing anchor or breaking camp) cannot be determined from these two verses alone.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Earnest, eager expectation directed toward a hoped-for future outcome.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular nominative (subject of ἀπεκδέχεται) or accusative after κατά paired with ἐλπίδα ('hope')
senses.definition: Intense anticipation or eager longing for a promised future event.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Subject of ἀπεκδέχεται ('waits eagerly for') in ROM 8:19, and paired directly with ἐλπίδα ('hope') in κατὰ τὴν ἀποκαραδοκίαν καὶ ἐλπίδα μου (PHP 1:20).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; pairing with ἀπεκδέχεται and ἐλπίς clearly establishes eager anticipation, though two occurrences leave open how intense or distinct from standard 'expectation/hope' the word felt in usage.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To see clearly how a situation stands, or to fix one's attention steadily on someone.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, aorist active subjunctive (ἀφίδω) with direct object τὰ περὶ ἐμέ in temporal clause ὡς ἄν
senses.definition: To see clearly or ascertain how one's circumstances turn out.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present active participle (ἀφορῶντες) with εἰς + accusative (εἰς τὸν ... Ἰησοῦν)
senses.definition: To fix one's eyes or focused attention steadily on someone as an example and leader.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Takes a direct object τὰ περὶ ἐμέ ('my situation') in PHP 2:23 and prepositional complement εἰς ... Ἰησοῦν ('unto Jesus') in HEB 12:2.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice with two distinct syntactic patterns; in PHP 2:23 it could mean either 'find out for certain' or 'look away/turn attention to see.'

entries.core_meaning_summary: To begin or initiate a course of action or work, contrasted with bringing it to completion.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, aorist middle participle (ἐναρξάμενοι / ὁ ἐναρξάμενος) with instrumental dative Πνεύματι or direct object ἔργον ἀγαθόν
senses.definition: To start or initiate an undertaking or spiritual course.

entries.collocations_and_notes: In both occurrences directly paired with ἐπιτελέω ('complete/bring to perfection'): ἐναρξάμενοι Πνεύματι νῦν σαρκὶ ἐπιτελεῖσθε (GAL 3:3); ὁ ἐναρξάμενος ἐν ὑμῖν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἐπιτελέσει (PHP 1:6).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; antonymous pairing with ἐπιτελέω cleanly establishes 'begin/initiate,' while broader syntactic contexts remain unattested.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Supply, provision, or supportive contribution enabling growth or deliverance.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular genitive modifying ἁφῆς ('joint/ligament') or governed by διά with genitive τοῦ Πνεύματος
senses.definition: Generous supply, provision, or supportive aid provided by the Spirit or within the body.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in διὰ πάσης ἁφῆς τῆς ἐπιχορηγίας (EPH 4:16) and διὰ τῆς ὑμῶν δεήσεως καὶ ἐπιχορηγίας τοῦ Πνεύματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ (PHP 1:19).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; in PHP 1:19 the genitive τοῦ Πνεύματος may be subjective ('the Spirit's provision') or objective ('the provision of the Spirit'), and in EPH 4:16 ἁφῆς τῆς ἐπιχορηγίας may mean 'every supporting joint' or 'every joint that supplies.'

entries.core_meaning_summary: A personal name of the messenger sent by the Philippian church who delivered their gift to Paul and served him in his need.

senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun, masculine singular accusative or genitive after παρά
senses.definition: Personal name of a Christian co-worker and envoy from the Philippian community.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Described as τὸν ἀδελφὸν καὶ συνεργὸν καὶ συνστρατιώτην μου, ὑμῶν δὲ ἀπόστολον καὶ λειτουργὸν τῆς χρείας μου (PHP 2:25), and as the courier of the gifts received παρὰ Ἐπαφροδίτου (PHP 4:18).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Lack, poverty, or material need, contrasted with abundance or self-sufficiency.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular genitive after ἐκ or accusative after κατά (καθ’ ὑστέρησιν)
senses.definition: State of want, poverty, or being without sufficient resources.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Contrasted directly with ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος ('out of abundance') in MRK 12:44 and with αὐτάρκης ('content/self-sufficient') in PHP 4:11.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice; both contexts focus on material/financial lack as contrasted with abundance or sufficiency.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A personal name of an individual in the addressed Christian community who is urged alongside Syntyche to share a common mindset in the Lord.

senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun, feminine singular accusative; direct object of παρακαλῶ, paired with Συντύχην
senses.definition: Personal name of an individual addressed with an appeal to be of one mind with Syntyche in the Lord.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in parallel construction: Εὐοδίαν παρακαλῶ καὶ Συντύχην παρακαλῶ τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ἐν Κυρίῳ.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once in the corpus; syntax clearly marks it as a personal name, though this verse alone provides no further biographical details beyond her need for agreement with Syntyche.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A personal name of one of the speaker's fellow workers in the gospel.

senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun, masculine singular genitive after μετὰ καί, grouped with τῶν λοιπῶν συνεργῶν μου
senses.definition: Personal name of a co-worker who struggled alongside the speaker and others in the gospel.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs in the phrase μετὰ καὶ Κλήμεντος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν συνεργῶν μου ('with Clement also and the rest of my fellow workers'), linked to the verb συνήθλησάν μοι ('labored/contended alongside me').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; context clearly identifies Klēmēs as a named co-worker in the gospel whose name is said to be in the book of life, though no further biographical information is given.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A personal name of an individual in the addressed community who is urged alongside Euodia to share the same mindset in the Lord.

senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun, feminine singular accusative; direct object of παρακαλῶ, paired with Εὐοδίαν
senses.definition: Personal name of an individual urged together with Euodia to think the same thing in the Lord.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in the paired appeal Εὐοδίαν παρακαλῶ καὶ Συντύχην παρακαλῶ τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ἐν Κυρίῳ.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once in this packet; clearly a personal name, though this verse alone reveals nothing further about her identity or background.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A collective designation for the members of the addressed congregation associated with the region of Macedonia.

senses.grammatical_frame: Vocative plural masculine noun in direct address, in apposition to ὑμεῖς and corresponding to ἐκκλησία
senses.definition: Collective name for the addressees as members of the particular church that partnered financially with the speaker after his departure from Macedonia.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used in direct vocative address (οἴδατε δὲ καὶ ὑμεῖς, Φιλιππήσιοι) and picked up later in the sentence by οὐδεμία μοι ἐκκλησία ... εἰ μὴ ὑμεῖς μόνοι.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; syntax establishes it as the collective name of the addressed church community, though the underlying place name is not explicitly mentioned in this verse.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A perceptive or discerning capacity paired with knowledge as a sphere in which love is prayed to abound.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular dative after ἐν, coordinated with ἐπιγνώσει and modified by πάσῃ
senses.definition: Insight, perceptive judgment, or discerning awareness that accompanies knowledge in guiding love.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Coordinated with ἐπιγνώσει after ἐν (ἐν ἐπιγνώσει καὶ πάσῃ αἰσθήσει) as the sphere or accompaniment of growing love (ἵνα ἡ ἀγάπη ὑμῶν ... περισσεύῃ).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; pairing with ἐπιγνώσει ('knowledge') places it in the cognitive-perceptive domain, but this single verse does not narrow whether the emphasis is on moral discernment, practical sensitivity, or spiritual perception.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A learned state of being satisfied or able to get along in whatever circumstances one faces, contrasted with speaking out of lack.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, masculine singular nominative; predicate complement with εἶναι after ἔμαθον and qualified by ἐν οἷς εἰμι
senses.definition: Content or having enough in whatever external situation one is in, rather than being governed by need or deprivation.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Follows the disclaimer οὐχ ὅτι καθ’ ὑστέρησιν λέγω ('not that I speak according to need/lack') and appears in the clause ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔμαθον ἐν οἷς εἰμι αὐτάρκης εἶναι.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; contrast with ὑστέρησις ('lack') and qualification by ἐν οἷς εἰμι point to contentment or sufficiency across varying circumstances, though a single occurrence cannot distinguish internal emotional satisfaction from practical independence.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adverb describing the sincere or authentic manner in which a like-minded person cares for the concerns of others.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying the future verb μεριμνήσει ('will care for / be concerned about')
senses.definition: In a genuine, sincere, or wholehearted way, characterizing authentic concern for others' welfare.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Spoken of someone described as ἰσόψυχον ('like-minded / of equal spirit'): ὅστις γνησίως τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν μεριμνήσει.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; context links it to authentic, non-superficial care for the addressees' affairs, but a single instance does not fix exact nuance among 'sincerely,' 'genuinely,' or 'devotedly.'

entries.core_meaning_summary: To experience encouragement, relief, or lifted spirits upon receiving news about others.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, 1st person singular present active subjunctive in a ἵνα purpose clause, accompanied by the participle γνοὺς τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν
senses.definition: To be cheered, encouraged, or in good spirits as a result of learning how others are faring.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in the purpose clause ἵνα κἀγὼ εὐψυχῶ γνοὺς τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν ('so that I too may [verb] upon learning about your affairs'), motivated by sending Timothy quickly.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; the purpose clause and link to receiving news about the community show a positive inward response, though one occurrence does not specify between general cheerfulness, emotional relief, or courage.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A positive, commendable quality included in a series of virtues worthy of reflection and praise.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, neuter plural nominative in an anaphoric series introduced by ὅσα, summarized by ἀρετή and ἔπαινος
senses.definition: Admirable, reputable, or worthy of good report, listed among qualities believers are urged to dwell on.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Final member of six ὅσα clauses (ἀληθῆ, σεμνά, δίκαια, ἁγνά, προσφιλῆ, εὔφημα), followed by the summary clause εἴ τις ἀρετὴ καὶ εἴ τις ἔπαινος, ταῦτα λογίζεσθε.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once inside a six-item virtue list; while the list and summary terms ἀρετή ('excellence') and ἔπαινος ('praise') mark it as morally admirable, this single verse does not specify whether it targets good reputation, fitting speech, or honorable conduct.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A pejorative term for an opposing group or harmful practice against which the audience is sharply warned.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular accusative with the definite article τήν; third parallel direct object of the warning imperative βλέπετε
senses.definition: A derogatory designation for an opposed party or harmful practice that the readers are warned to watch out for.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Forms a threefold anaphoric warning: Βλέπετε τοὺς κύνας, βλέπετε τοὺς κακοὺς ἐργάτας, βλέπετε τὴν κατατομήν ('Beware of the dogs, beware of the evil workers, beware of the ...').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; syntax clearly marks it as a strongly negative label for opponents alongside 'the dogs' and 'the evil workers,' but this single sentence alone does not identify the specific concrete practice or group referred to.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The third category of beings in a cosmic triad alongside heavenly and earthly beings whose knees bow at the name of Jesus.

senses.grammatical_frame: Substantive adjective, plural genitive modifying or specifying πᾶν γόνυ ('every knee') in a three-part series with ἐπουρανίων and ἐπιγείων
senses.definition: Beings belonging to the third cosmic realm paired with those in heaven and on earth in an exhaustive merism of submission.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in the triadic merism πᾶν γόνυ κάμψῃ ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ καταχθονίων ('every knee should bow, of heavenly and earthly and ... beings').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; coordination with ἐπουρανίων ('heavenly') and ἐπιγείων ('earthly') shows it completes a three-tier cosmic totality of bowing beings, though this single verse does not specify whether these are the dead, underworld spirits, or other realms.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A self-exalting or boastful motive forbidden alongside rivalry and directly contrasted with humility.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular accusative after κατά, coordinated with κατ’ ἐριθείαν and contrasted via ἀλλά with τῇ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ
senses.definition: Self-centered pride, conceit, or pursuit of empty prestige, opposed to humility and regarding others as more important than oneself.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Paired negatively with ἐριθείαν (μηδὲν κατ’ ἐριθείαν μηδὲ κατὰ κενοδοξίαν) and contrasted with τῇ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ ἀλλήλους ἡγούμενοι ὑπερέχοντας ἑαυτῶν ('in humility considering one another superior to yourselves').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; pairing with ἐριθείαν and direct contrast with humility and elevating others establish a meaning in the domain of pride or self-promotion, though one occurrence does not pinpoint its exact distinction from neighboring terms for arrogance.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The reciprocal counterpart to giving within a partnership or mutual exchange account.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular genitive paired with δόσεως ('giving') in the prepositional phrase εἰς λόγον δόσεως καὶ λήμψεως
senses.definition: Receiving, as the reciprocal side paired with giving in an ongoing partnership or account.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs in the idiomatic commercial/partnership expression ἐκοινώνησεν εἰς λόγον δόσεως καὶ λήμψεως ('shared/partnered in the matter of giving and receiving').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; pairing with δόσεως ('giving') and ἐκοινώνησεν ('partnered') clearly defines it as the receiving side of mutual exchange, though this single verse does not clarify whether the phrase refers strictly to material/financial accounting or also includes spiritual reciprocity.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adverb of high degree intensifying an emotional verb of rejoicing.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying the aorist passive deponent verb Ἐχάρην ('I rejoiced')
senses.definition: To a great degree or very much, intensifying the speaker's joy in the Lord.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Modifies Ἐχάρην in Ἐχάρην δὲ ἐν Κυρίῳ μεγάλως ὅτι ... ('I rejoiced greatly in the Lord because ...').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; syntax clearly shows it functions as an intensifier of Ἐχάρην ('rejoiced'), though a single attestation leaves any stylistic register or further range of collocations unattested.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To have been thoroughly trained, initiated, or accustomed through experience in handling all kinds of circumstances.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, 1st person singular perfect passive/middle indicative (μεμύημαι) with dative adverbials ἐν παντὶ καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν, followed by paired infinitives
senses.definition: To have learned the secret or become thoroughly experienced and accustomed to facing every extreme of condition.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Stands in parallel with οἶδα ... οἶδα ('I know how to ... I know how to ...') and introduces four paired infinitives of contrasting states: χορτάζεσθαι καὶ πεινᾶν, καὶ περισσεύειν καὶ ὑστερεῖσθαι ('both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; parallel with οἶδα and contrasting infinitives of plenty and want indicates acquired practical mastery across all conditions, though this single occurrence cannot determine whether it retains a specialized nuance of secret initiation or simply means thorough practical experience.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To risk or expose one's life to danger for the sake of a mission or service.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, aorist middle participle (παραβολευσάμενος) with dative complement τῇ ψυχῇ ('with his life'), modifying ἤγγισεν μέχρι θανάτου
senses.definition: To jeopardize, hazard, or expose one's life to peril on behalf of Christ's work and service to others.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used with τῇ ψυχῇ ('his life/soul') in explanation of coming close to death: μέχρι θανάτου ἤγγισεν παραβολευσάμενος τῇ ψυχῇ.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; the surrounding clause μέχρι θανάτου ἤγγισεν ... τῇ ψυχῇ clearly establishes risking one's life, though a single attestation leaves open the exact nuance between deliberate self-exposure to peril and negligent disregard for personal safety.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A comforting, cheering, or encouraging influence arising from love.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, neuter singular nominative modified by the genitive ἀγάπης, in a series of parallel εἴ τις / εἴ τι clauses
senses.definition: Consolation, encouragement, or tender reassurance produced by love within a community.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs in the fourfold appeal: Εἴ τις οὖν παράκλησις ἐν Χριστῷ, εἴ τι παραμύθιον ἀγάπης, εἴ τις κοινωνία Πνεύματος, εἴ τις σπλάγχνα καὶ οἰκτιρμοί.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; parallelism with παράκλησις ('encouragement/comfort') and σπλάγχνα καὶ οἰκτιρμοί ('affection and compassion') locates it in the domain of supportive comfort, though this single verse does not clarify how it differs specifically from παράκλησις.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Close to or nearly reaching a state or point, used adverbially with a dative of the limit approached.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, neuter singular accusative used adverbially with dative θανάτῳ, modifying the verb ἠσθένησεν ('he fell ill')
senses.definition: Near to or bordering on (death), indicating the extreme severity of an illness.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Forms the expression ἠσθένησεν παραπλήσιον θανάτῳ ('he was sick close to death'), followed by God's mercy sparing him.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; syntax with ἠσθένησεν and θανάτῳ clearly indicates nearness in degree or severity ('close to death'), while broader adjectival uses ('similar to / comparable') remain unattested in the corpus.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The heavenly civic belonging, commonwealth, or homeland to which believers belong and from which they await a Savior.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, neuter singular nominative with possessive pronoun ἡμῶν, subject of ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὑπάρχει and antecedent of ἐξ οὗ
senses.definition: The heavenly state, citizenship, or homeland to which the community belongs and from which the Lord Jesus Christ is awaited as Savior.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs in ἡμῶν γὰρ τὸ πολίτευμα ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὑπάρχει, ἐξ οὗ καὶ Σωτῆρα ἀπεκδεχόμεθα Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; the locative ἐν οὐρανοῖς ('in heaven') and relative reference ἐξ οὗ ('from which [place]') point toward a civic realm or status of belonging, yet this single verse does not distinguish precisely between legal citizenship, a corporate commonwealth/colony, or a heavenly seat of government.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An admirable, endearing, or pleasing quality commended among virtues worthy of reflection.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, neuter plural nominative in an anaphoric series introduced by ὅσα and summarized by ἀρετή and ἔπαινος
senses.definition: Lovely, agreeable, or winning goodwill and affection, listed among admirable things believers are urged to consider.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Fifth item in the list ὅσα ἐστὶν ἀληθῆ, ὅσα σεμνά, ὅσα δίκαια, ὅσα ἁγνά, ὅσα προσφιλῆ, ὅσα εὔφημα, summed up by εἴ τις ἀρετὴ καὶ εἴ τις ἔπαινος.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once in a broad list of commendable qualities; context clearly identifies it as a positive, praiseworthy trait, though one verse does not specify whether it emphasizes personal charm/kindliness, social goodwill, or moral beauty.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be frightened, intimidated, or panicked by opponents.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present passive participle (μὴ πτυρόμενοι) with ἐν μηδενί and agent phrase ὑπὸ τῶν ἀντικειμένων
senses.definition: To be terrified, alarmed, or intimidated by adversaries.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears negated in μὴ πτυρόμενοι ἐν μηδενὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀντικειμένων ('in no way intimidated/frightened by the opponents'), contrasted as a sign of salvation versus the opponents' destruction.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; the passive construction with ὑπὸ τῶν ἀντικειμένων ('by the opponents') clearly places it in the domain of fear or intimidation, though a single attestation does not distinguish sudden panic/startle from sustained dread.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The goal, target, or finish mark toward which one strives in a race-like pursuit.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular accusative after κατά (κατὰ σκοπὸν διώκω), paired with εἰς τὸ βραβεῖον ('for the prize')
senses.definition: The mark, finish line, or objective toward which a runner presses on to obtain the prize.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs in κατὰ σκοπὸν διώκω εἰς τὸ βραβεῖον τῆς ἄνω κλήσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ ('I press on toward the goal for the prize of God's upward call').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; pairing with διώκω ('pursue/press on') and βραβεῖον ('prize') firmly establishes an athletic goal or target, though one verse does not determine whether it specifically pictures a physical finish marker or a broader mental aim.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Worthless refuse or discarded rubbish, used figuratively for everything renounced to gain Christ.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, neuter plural accusative; predicate object of ἡγοῦμαι ('I regard [things] as ...'), paralleling ζημίαν ('loss')
senses.definition: Utterly worthless waste or rubbish, contrasted with the surpassing value of knowing and gaining Christ.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Escalates ἡγοῦμαι πάντα ζημίαν εἶναι ('I consider all things to be loss') in καὶ ἡγοῦμαι σκύβαλα ἵνα Χριστὸν κερδήσω ('and I consider [them] refuse so that I may gain Christ').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; contrast with κερδήσω ('gain') and parallel with ζημίαν ('loss') clearly indicate worthless waste, though this single verse does not narrow the concrete physical referent (e.g., table scraps, sweepings, or excrement).

entries.core_meaning_summary: One who imitates an example alongside others, or joins in following a pattern of conduct.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine plural nominative (Συνμιμηταί) with genitive μου and imperative γίνεσθε, linked to καθὼς ἔχετε τύπον ἡμᾶς
senses.definition: Joint imitators or fellow followers of an exemplary pattern of life.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs in Συνμιμηταί μου γίνεσθε, ἀδελφοί, followed by καὶ σκοπεῖτε τοὺς οὕτως περιπατοῦντας καθὼς ἔχετε τύπον ἡμᾶς ('and observe those walking thus, just as you have us as an example').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; pairing with καθὼς ἔχετε τύπον ἡμᾶς establishes imitation of an example, yet syntax leaves open whether μου is objective ('join together in imitating me') or associative ('be imitators together with me [of Christ]').

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be conformed or patterned after something, specifically Christ's death.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, present passive/middle participle (συμμορφιζόμενος) governing dative τῷ θανάτῳ αὐτοῦ, expanding κοινωνίαν παθημάτων αὐτοῦ
senses.definition: To be shaped like, conformed to, or made to share the pattern of his death.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Follows κοινωνίαν παθημάτων αὐτοῦ ('fellowship/sharing of his sufferings') in the participial phrase συμμορφιζόμενος τῷ θανάτῳ αὐτοῦ.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; linkage with κοινωνίαν παθημάτων αὐτοῦ and dative τῷ θανάτῳ αὐτοῦ shows participation in or likeness to Christ's death, though a single occurrence does not narrow whether it denotes ongoing spiritual/moral conformity or literal suffering unto a similar death.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A vocative address for a trusted colleague or companion asked to assist fellow workers (or possibly a personal name).

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular vocative (σύνζυγε) modified by γνήσιε ('genuine/true'), addressed alongside σέ and followed by imperative συνλαμβάνου αὐταῖς
senses.definition: Trusted partner or companion in ministry (or, if taken as a proper name, Syzygus) appealed to for help on behalf of co-workers.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Addressed as γνήσιε σύνζυγε ('true/genuine partner' or 'genuine Syzygus') and asked to assist women who contended in the gospel alongside Clement and τῶν λοιπῶν συνεργῶν μου.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; context clearly identifies the referent as a trusted helper in the Christian community, but this single verse leaves uncertain whether σύνζυγε is a common noun meaning 'partner/colleague' or a proper personal name ('Syzygus') played upon by γνήσιε.

entries.core_meaning_summary: United in mind, spirit, or purpose within a community.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, masculine plural nominative (σύνψυχοι) in an appositional series between τὴν αὐτὴν ἀγάπην ἔχοντες and τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες
senses.definition: Harmonious, like-minded, or united in spirit and inner disposition with one another.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Expands ἵνα τὸ αὐτὸ φρονῆτε ('that you think the same thing') alongside τὴν αὐτὴν ἀγάπην ἔχοντες ('having the same love') and τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες ('thinking the one thing').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; tight parallelism with τὸ αὐτὸ φρονῆτε, τὴν αὐτὴν ἀγάπην ἔχοντες, and τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες clearly indicates communal unity, though a single occurrence does not distinguish emphasis on shared affection from shared intention or purpose.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To lack a suitable opportunity or occasion to act on an existing concern.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, 2nd person plural imperfect middle/passive indicative (ἠκαιρεῖσθε) contrasted via δέ with ἐφ’ ᾧ καὶ ἐφρονεῖτε
senses.definition: To be without opportunity or favorable occasion, explaining why prior concern could not be expressed in action.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Contrasted directly with ongoing care in ἐφ’ ᾧ καὶ ἐφρονεῖτε, ἠκαιρεῖσθε δέ ('for whom you were indeed concerned, yet you lacked opportunity').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; the contrast with ἐφρονεῖτε ('you were concerned') indicates a practical barrier to expressing care, though this single verse does not specify whether the obstacle was timing, lack of a messenger, or lack of material means.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To revive, renew, or bring back to active expression a concern that had been unable to show itself.

senses.grammatical_frame: Verb, 2nd person plural aorist active indicative (ἀνεθάλετε) governing the articular infinitive object τὸ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ φρονεῖν
senses.definition: To revive or cause to flourish again (active concern or care for someone) after a period without opportunity.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Modified by ἤδη ποτέ ('now at length') and takes τὸ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ φρονεῖν ('your thinking/care on my behalf') as direct object, followed by explanation of prior lack of opportunity (ἠκαιρεῖσθε δέ).
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; syntax with ἤδη ποτέ and τὸ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ φρονεῖν clearly denotes renewing active expression of care, though a single instance cannot confirm whether the verb retains vivid botanical imagery ('bud/bloom again') or is a faded metaphor for 'revive.'

entries.core_meaning_summary: The state of being away or absent from a community, contrasted directly with personal presence.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, feminine singular dative (ἐν τῇ ἀπουσίᾳ μου) directly contrasted via μὴ ὡς ... μόνον ἀλλὰ ... with ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ μου
senses.definition: Absence, specifically the speaker's physical separation from the addressed community.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Stands in explicit antithesis to παρουσία: μὴ ὡς ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ μου μόνον ἀλλὰ νῦν πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἐν τῇ ἀπουσίᾳ μου ('not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence').
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; direct antithesis with παρουσίᾳ μου ('my presence') narrows the meaning clearly to physical absence, though a single attestation leaves any secondary or extended senses unattested in the corpus.

entries.core_meaning_summary: In a pure or sincere manner, without self-serving or harmful motives.

senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb negated by οὐχ, modifying καταγγέλλουσιν ('they proclaim') alongside ἐξ ἐριθείας and οἰόμενοι θλῖψιν ἐγείρειν
senses.definition: Purely, sincerely, or with upright intent in carrying out proclamation.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in the negative phrase οὐχ ἁγνῶς, contrasted with acting ἐξ ἐριθείας ('out of rivalry/selfish ambition') and intending to stir up trouble for the speaker's chains.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; pairing with ἐξ ἐριθείας and malicious intent makes clear that οὐχ ἁγνῶς denotes impure/insincere motivation, though one verse does not clarify broader shades of 'purely' or 'blamelessly.'

entries.core_meaning_summary: Something to be seized or exploited for one's own advantage, negated in describing how one in the form of God regarded equality with God.

senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular accusative; predicate complement of ἡγήσατο with direct object τὸ εἶναι ἴσα Θεῷ, negated by οὐχ
senses.definition: A prize to be grasped, seized, or exploited to one's own benefit rather than relinquished.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs in οὐχ ἁρπαγμὸν ἡγήσατο τὸ εἶναι ἴσα Θεῷ ('did not regard being equal with God as ...'), followed by self-emptying/humbling action.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once; syntax shows it is a negative predicate negated by οὐχ ('did not consider equality with God as X'), but this single clause leaves open whether it denotes grasping at something not yet possessed ('robbery/usurpation') or clinging to/exploiting a status already possessed.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Free from grief or less burdened by sorrow, used in the comparative degree alongside the readers' rejoicing.
