senses.grammatical_frame: Plural-form noun as object of verbs of drinking, drawing, giving, or lacking (שָׁתָה, הִשְׁקָה, שָׁאַב, נָתַן, אֵין), or in construct with containers and provisions (צַפַּחַת, מִשְׁעַן)

senses.definition: Water used for physical washing, bathing, ritual purification, judicial ordeal, or cultic pouring.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural-form noun governed by instrumental/locative בְּ with verbs of washing, dipping, or cleansing (רָחַץ, כִּבֵּס, טָבַל), or as subject/object in ritual actions

senses.definition: Water used figuratively to depict overwhelming peril, swift transience, deep/abundant speech, or physical collapse from terror.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural-form noun in metaphorical predicates, prepositional phrases (עַל פְּנֵי מַיִם), or adverbial/result expressions (תֵּלַכְנָה מָּיִם)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Always appears with plural morphology and takes plural verb and pronominal agreement (e.g., הָיוּ, חָרְבוּ, יָשֻׁבוּ, יָצְאוּ, לִשְׁתּוֹתָם, אֹתָם). Occurs in construct as מֵי (e.g., מֵי הַמַּבּוּל, מֵי הַיַּרְדֵּן, מֵי מְרִיבָה) and with pronominal suffixes on the reduplicated stem מֵימ־ (מֵימֶיהָ, מֵימֵינוּ, מֵימֵיהֶם). Common collocations include פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם (surface of the water), מַעְיְנֵי/מַבּוּעֵי/נַחֲלֵי מַיִם (springs/streams of water), לֶחֶם וּמַיִם (bread and water), and רָחַץ בַּמַּיִם (wash/bathe in water).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Humankind collectively or an individual human being, including the construct idiom for a mortal human and the personal name of the first man.

senses.definition: Human beings considered collectively as a species or population, especially in contrast to animals or to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine singular used collectively with or without the definite article; takes plural or singular verb agreement according to context, and appears in construct as a modifier (e.g., human hands, human foot).

senses.definition: An individual human being or any person in general, including a specific single human figure when determined by context or the definite article.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine singular functioning as an indefinite or definite singular subject, object, or genitive modifier (e.g., a person's bone), often paired with singular verbs and pronouns.

senses.definition: A mortal human being, occurring in the construct expression 'son of humankind / children of humankind', used both generally for mortals and as a direct form of address to a prophet.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine singular as the second element in the construct phrase בֶּן אָדָם (singular) or בְּנֵי אָדָם (plural), used as a noun phrase or standalone vocative.

senses.definition: Adam, the proper name of the first human ancestor in genealogical and historical reference.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun masculine without article, functioning as the named ancestor in a genealogical heading (or in comparison with a named figure).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Invariably singular in form (never takes a plural suffix); functions both as a collective noun for humankind and as an indefinite singular for a person. Frequently paired or contrasted with בְּהֵמָה (livestock/beasts: GEN 7:21; EXO 9:9; NUM 8:17; NUM 31:11; JER 32:43; EZK 32:13) and with אֵל (God/deity: ISA 31:3; EZK 28:2) to underscore human mortality and non-divine status. In the construct phrase בֶּן אָדָם / בְּנֵי אָדָם, it designates mortal humans generally or serves as a direct vocative to Ezekiel. In HOS 6:7 (כְּאָדָם), context allows either comparison to humankind generally or to the individual Adam.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A prominent elevated landform such as a mountain, hill, or highland region, often serving as a geographical landmark, regional territory, or sacred site.

senses.definition: A distinct elevated natural landform rising steeply above the surrounding terrain, whether a single peak, named mountain, or hill.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine, singular or plural, absolute or construct with a proper name (e.g., Mount Sinai, Mount Hor) or modified by adjectives such as high; often governed by spatial prepositions (on, to, from, in).

senses.definition: An extended mountainous area, mountain range, or upland territory inhabited or named as a geographical district, often contrasted with valleys, lowlands, or plains.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine singular or plural, frequently in construct before a territorial or tribal name (e.g., Gilead, Ephraim, Seir, Samaria, Israel) or listed alongside regional terrain zones.

senses.definition: A mountain designated as a sacred place of divine presence, worship, or pilgrimage (especially Zion/Jerusalem), and by poetic extension an emblem of God-given stability.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun masculine singular, typically in construct with divine, cultic, or Zion-related nouns (e.g., mountain of God, mountain of the house of the LORD, holy mountain) or with first-person pronominal suffix.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs in singular (הַר), plural (הָרִים), construct plural (הָרֵי), and suffixed poetic stem form הַרְרִי (PSA 30:8). Common construct expressions include הַר סִינַי (Mount Sinai: EXO 19:23; EXO 31:18; LEV 7:38; NEH 9:13), הַר שֵׂעִיר (Mount/hill country of Seir: DEU 2:1; EZK 35:15), הַר אֶפְרַיִם (hill country of Ephraim: JDG 2:9; JDG 19:16; 2KI 5:22), רֹאשׁ הָהָר / רָאשֵׁי הֶהָרִים (summit/tops of the mountain[s]: JOS 15:8; JDG 9:25; ISA 2:2; ISA 30:17; EZK 6:13; MIC 4:1), הַר בֵּית יְהוָה (mountain of the house of the LORD: ISA 2:2; MIC 4:1), and הַר קָדְשִׁי / הַר הַקֹּדֶשׁ (holy mountain: ISA 66:20; JER 31:23; ZEP 3:11). Often paired or contrasted with other terrain terms such as גִּבְעָה (hill), בִּקְעָה (valley), שְׁפֵלָה (lowland), עֲרָבָה (plain), and נֶגֶב (southern steppe). In PSA 30:8, הַרְרִי is used metaphorically for secure standing or stability granted by God.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To cross over a barrier or waterway, travel through or pass by, overflow, elapse or perish, violate or overlook a norm, or (in causative and reflexive stems) bring across, proclaim, or erupt in anger.

senses.definition: To move from one side of a river, wadi, sea, boundary, or ritual division to the other.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active); transitive with direct object of the waterway/barrier, or intransitive with `אֶל` (into/to), `בְּ` (across), or `בֵּין` (between)

senses.definition: To travel through a territory or city, pass by or ahead of someone, outrun another runner, or (of a territorial boundary) run along and extend from one point to another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active); intransitive with `בְּ` / `בְּתוֹךְ` / `בְּקֶרֶב` (through), `עַל` / `עַל־פְּנֵי` (by/before), or `מֵאֵת` (from); transitive when overtaking a person

senses.definition: To surge over or sweep irresistibly through, used of floodwaters or a metaphorical overwhelming calamity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; absolute or with `עַל` (over)

senses.definition: To go by or come to an end (of a time of day or agricultural season), or to pass away and perish (of mortal life).
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; absolute or with `בְּ` indicating the instrument of death

senses.definition: To step beyond and violate a binding covenant, or conversely to pass over and disregard an offense without retaliation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active); transitive with `בְּרִית` (covenant) for violating, or intransitive with `עַל` (over) + `פֶּשַׁע` (offense) for forgiving/overlooking

senses.definition: To cause something or someone to pass across or through: to make wind blow over the earth, escort or guide someone across water or through provinces, carry a horn blast throughout a country, or hand over children as a ritual offering.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative), transitive with direct object (`אֵת` or suffix); with prepositions `עַל` (over), `בְּ` (through/across), or `לְ` (to)

senses.definition: To overflow with anger or become enraged (parallel to fire kindling and wrath rising).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael (reflexive/intensive), intransitive; absolute

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with `לִפְנֵי` (before/ahead of), `בְּתוֹךְ` / `בְּקֶרֶב` (through the midst of), `עַל` (over/by), and direct objects of waterways or barriers (`הַיַּרְדֵּן`, `נַחַל`). Stem distinctions: Qal expresses active crossing, passing, overflowing, elapsing, or transgressing; Hiphil expresses causing to pass/blow, escorting across, proclaiming by horn throughout a land, or ritually handing over children; Hithpael (attested in PSA 78:21) expresses overflowing with anger/becoming enraged.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Large in physical size or number, intense in degree or severity, or exalted in rank, authority, and majesty.

senses.definition: Large in physical dimensions, spaciousness, weight, or numerical size, applied to objects, structures, cities, animals, or large groups of people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective (including construct with body part, e.g., גְּדוֹל כְּנָפַיִם)

senses.definition: High in degree, intensity, abundance, or gravity, describing sounds, rain, emotions, calamities, battles, loyal kindness, or grave offenses.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective modifying event or abstract nouns, often intensifying cognate nouns

senses.definition: Exalted in status, wealth, power, or authority, used of God, monarchs, prominent individuals, and the chief priest.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective (sometimes comparative with מִן, or in the fixed title הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל)

senses.definition: Used as a noun for older or higher-ranking persons (in paired contrast with 'small'), or in the feminine for major matters and mighty deeds.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized adjective (masculine singular for persons in merisms with קָטֹן; feminine singular or plural for deeds or matters)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in contrast with קָטֹן / קְטַנָּה ('small, young, junior', e.g., GEN 1:16, GEN 19:11, NUM 22:18, DEU 25:13, 2CH 31:15, EST 1:5, AMO 6:11), where merisms like מִקָּטֹן וְעַד גָּדוֹל express totality across age or social rank. Often combined with רַב ('many, great', DEU 2:21) or גִּבּוֹר / נוֹרָא ('mighty, awesome', NEH 1:5, JER 32:18). Forms the official title הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל ('the high priest', 2KI 22:4) and cognate intensity phrases with nouns of emotion or outcry (תְּרוּעָה גְדוֹלָה, JOS 6:5; שִׂמְחָה גְדוֹלָה, NEH 8:17, JON 4:6; קִנְאָה גְדוֹלָה, ZEC 1:14). Appears in construct with a body part to express size (גְּדוֹל כְּנָפַיִם, 'large-winged', EZK 17:7).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To take or maintain an upright or stationary position, stop moving, serve in attendance, withstand opposition, or (in the causative stem) station and appoint others.

senses.definition: To take or maintain an upright posture or stationary spatial position (used of people, feet, waters, or upright structures), often accompanied by a prepositional phrase specifying location.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; absolute or with prepositions (`עַל` upon/beside, `בְּ` in/at, `אֵצֶל` beside, `לְנֶגֶד` opposite)

senses.definition: To cease moving, come to a halt, stay behind, or remain abiding in a place or course of conduct (including non-physical persistence such as lingering in a way of life, persisting in practices, or a spirit remaining among a community).
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; absolute or with `תַּחַת` (in one's place), `מֵרָחוֹק` (at a distance), `אֵת` (with), or `בְּ` (in)

senses.definition: To stand in attendance before a ruler, superior, or deity in service, cultic ministry, or intercession, or to step into an office in someone's place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; typically with `לִפְנֵי` (before), `עַל` (in attendance upon / at one's post), or `תַּחַת` (in place of)

senses.definition: To take a hostile stand against someone in battle, or to hold one's ground and withstand an attacker's assault.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), intransitive; with `עַל` (against) or `לִפְנֵי` (before), often negated with `לֹא` or `אֵין כֹּחַ` (no strength to)

senses.definition: To cause someone or a group to stand in a designated place, present a person before an authority or deity, station military guards or choirs, or appoint officials to a role.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative), transitive with direct object (`אֵת` or pronominal suffix); often with `לִפְנֵי` (before) or `לְ` (for/as)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with prepositions indicating spatial orientation or social hierarchy: `לִפְנֵי` (before, in service, appearance, or opposition), `עַל` (beside, upon, or against), `תַּחַת` (in one's place, including succession), and `אֵצֶל` / `לְנֶגֶד` (beside / opposite). The idiomatic phrase `עָמַד עַל עָמְדָם` (2CH 30:16) denotes taking one's appointed station. Contrasts between stems: Qal is intransitive/stative (standing, halting, attending, resisting), while Hiphil is causative (making someone stand, stationing personnel, or appointing officials).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Good, pleasant, or desirable in quality, character, or benefit, used across physical, aesthetic, ethical, and advantageous contexts.

senses.definition: Possessing high quality, fertility, beauty, or pleasantness, applied to created things, land, produce, fragrance, or personal appearance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective (including construct before nouns of appearance such as תֹּאַר and מַרְאֶה)

senses.definition: Morally upright, faithful, or benevolently gracious, characterizing divine disposition and action or human conduct acceptable to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative adjective, often with prepositional phrases (לְ, לִפְנֵי, עַל)

senses.definition: Beneficial, fitting, acceptable, or preferable in someone's estimation or experience, including comparative superiority over something else.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicative adjective with לְ ('for'), בְּעֵינֵי ('in the eyes of'), or מִן ('than' in comparisons)

senses.definition: Used as a noun for what is morally right, advantageous, prosperous, or glad tidings (singular), or for upright and virtuous people (plural).
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantivized adjective (singular abstract or masculine plural for persons), often object of verbs of doing, speaking, or seeking

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in contrast with רַע / רָעָה ('evil, bad, harmful', e.g., GEN 3:5, GEN 26:29, NUM 13:19, JOS 23:15, JOB 30:26, PSA 34:15, JER 24:2) and in parallel with נָעִים ('pleasant', GEN 49:15), צַדִּיקִים ('righteous', PRO 2:20), and שָׁלוֹם / יְשׁוּעָה ('peace, deliverance', ISA 52:7). Common idioms include טוֹב בְּעֵינֵי ('pleasing/right in the eyes of', 1SA 29:9, 2SA 15:26, 1CH 21:23, EST 8:8), טוֹב לְפָנָיו ('acceptable before him [God]', ECC 2:26, ECC 7:26), דִּבֶּר בְּ... טוֹב ('speak favorably about', 1SA 19:4), and comparative טוֹב ... מִן ('better than', PSA 63:4, PSA 119:72, PRO 16:8, JON 4:3). Appears in construct with aspect nouns for physical appearance (טוֹב תֹּאַר, 1KI 1:6; טוֹבוֹת מַרְאֶה, EST 2:2).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A spatial and relational preposition indicating a position beneath or below something, subordination under authority, or substitution and exchange in place of something else.

senses.definition: At or into a lower spatial position relative to a person, object, sky, or structure; includes compound forms indicating location below or motion beneath, as well as the idiom 'under the sun' for the earthly realm and suffixed forms meaning 'in one's spot / without moving'.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing nouns or pronominal suffixes; also in compound expressions מִתַּחַת (לְ) and אֶל תַּחַת (לְ)

senses.definition: Under the authority, control, domination, or immediate disposal of someone, regularly paired with יָד ('hand') or verbs of subjugation and deliverance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition with יָד ('hand') or pronominal suffix, following verbs of subduing, delivering, or possessing

senses.definition: In place of, as a successor to, or in exchange, compensation, or recompense for another person, object, injury, or condition; used especially in royal succession formulas, legal restitution, and reversals of state.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition governing a noun or pronominal suffix, often with verbs of reigning, repaying, giving, or becoming

senses.definition: Used with a following relative marker to introduce a causal or retributive clause explaining the ground for a restriction or action.
glosses: in return for the fact that
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound conjunction תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר + finite clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently combines with preceding prepositions such as מִן (מִתַּחַת, מִתַּחַת לְ 'from under, beneath, below') and אֶל (אֶל תַּחַת, אֶל תַּחַת לְ 'to underneath'). Recurring idiomatic expressions include תַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ ('under the sun', denoting the earthly mortal sphere in Ecclesiastes), תַּחַת יַד ('under the hand/control/power of', or 'on hand / in one's possession'), יָשַׁב תַּחְתָּו ('stay in one's place'), and מָלַךְ תַּחַת ('reign in place of / succeed as king').

entries.core_meaning_summary: To move from one place to another on foot or by flow, and figuratively to conduct one's life, follow a way or allegiance, or progress continuously.

senses.definition: To move physically from place to place, travel along a route, depart, come toward someone, accompany, or traverse an area; used in the simple active stem for general movement, in the intensive/iterative stem for going about persistently or as a roving traveler, and in the reflexive/iterative stem for traversing territory.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal), intensive/iterative stem (Piel), and reflexive/iterative stem (Hithpael); intransitive or with prepositions (אֶל, עַל, אֵת, מִפְּנֵי, לְ, בְּ) or direct object of path/way

senses.definition: Of water, wine, news, or inner attention/beings: to flow along a course, spread abroad, pass smoothly, attend in thought, or pass onward to a final destination such as death.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal), with inanimate or abstract subjects (river, water, wine, fame, heart, all beings)

senses.definition: To conduct one's life, behave habitually, or maintain religious and moral allegiance; commonly framed as walking before God or people, walking in someone's ways or statutes, going after other gods, or going about as a slanderer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) and reflexive/iterative stem (Hithpael); with prepositions לִפְנֵי ('before'), בְּ ('in'), אַחֲרֵי ('after'), or nominal complement רָכִיל ('slander')

senses.definition: Used as a progressive auxiliary paired with a following adjective or participle to express steady, continuous increase or intensification in a condition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem participle (הוֹלֵךְ) followed by וְ + adjective or participle

entries.collocations_and_notes: Across the sampled verses, three verbal stems appear: (1) the simple active stem (Qal), used for basic locomotion, spatial flow, figurative conduct, and the progressive auxiliary construction הֹלֵךְ וְ־ + adjective/participle indicating steady increase (2SA 3:1; EST 9:4); (2) the intensive/iterative stem (Piel), used for going about persistently in a condition such as mourning (JOB 30:28) or as an agent noun for a traveler/rover (PRO 6:11); and (3) the reflexive/iterative stem (Hithpael), used for walking about or surveying an area (JOS 18:4) and especially for habitual conduct or living faithfully before God or the community (GEN 17:1; 1SA 2:35; 1SA 12:2; PSA 35:14; PSA 82:5; ISA 38:3). Common collocations include הָלַךְ לְדַרְכּוֹ ('go on one's way'), הָלַךְ אַחֲרֵי ('follow after' another deity), הָלַךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ / בְּחֻקּוֹת ('live according to a way/statutes'), הָלַךְ לִפְנֵי ('live/serve before' God or people), הָלַךְ רָכִיל ('go about slandering'), and הֹלֵךְ הָלוֹךְ וְ־ ('continue going and...' for ongoing action, JER 41:6).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An audible voice, sound, noise, cry, thunderclap, or public report/proclamation, also used idiomatically with 'hear' to express obedience or compliance.

senses.definition: The audible speaking voice or vocal utterance of a human being or deity, including cries of distress, weeping, joyful shouting, or prayer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, often in construct (קוֹל + speaker or emotion), with prepositional בְּ/לְ, or as object of נָשָׂא / נָתַן / שָׁמַע

senses.definition: In combination with the verb שָׁמַע ('listen') and בְּ or לְ, the spoken command, counsel, or plea to which one responds with obedience, compliance, or favorable consent.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun governed by שָׁמַע בְּ־ / שָׁמַע לְ־ + speaker

senses.definition: Any non-speech audible sound or noise, such as footsteps, bells, horns, millstones, crowds, wings, rushing water, crashing structures, or animal calls.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, typically in construct (קוֹל + sound source) or as object of שָׁמַע / נָשָׂא

senses.definition: Thunder or a booming atmospheric rumble, especially in the plural (קֹלוֹת) alongside rain or in descriptions of divine manifestation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun (קֹלוֹת) or singular construct referring to divine meteorological roaring

senses.definition: Spoken news or rumor circulating in a household, or an official oral proclamation issued throughout a kingdom.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun as subject of passive נִשְׁמַע (be heard) or object of causative הֶעֱבִיר (circulate)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs with the verb שָׁמַע ('hear, listen'): with direct object (שָׁמַע אֶת קוֹל) it normally denotes perceiving a sound or hearing a plea, whereas with the prepositions בְּ or לְ (שָׁמַע בְּקוֹל / לְקוֹל) it consistently denotes heeding, obeying, or granting someone's request. Other recurring idioms include נָשָׂא קוֹל ('raise one's voice', JOB 2:12; PSA 93:3), נָתַן קוֹל ('utter a cry/voice', JER 48:34), בְּקוֹל גָּדוֹל ('in a loud voice', PRO 27:14), and הֶעֱבִיר קוֹל ('circulate a proclamation', 2CH 36:22).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To strike, beat, hit, or fatally smite a person, animal, object, or military force, spanning physical blows, lethal violence, battlefield defeat, and divine or natural affliction.

senses.definition: To deliver physical blows to or beat a person, whether in assault, corporal punishment of a servant, or judicial flogging, without inherently causing immediate death.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) + direct object (person) or partitive מִן, optionally with instrumental בְּ (with)

senses.definition: To strike or hit an inanimate object (such as rock, water, or an architectural structure) with an implement or hand; with כַּף ('palm/hand') as object, to clap or strike one's hand in an expressive gesture of anger.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) + direct object (inanimate object or body part), optionally with instrumental בְּ or directional אֶל

senses.definition: To strike a fatal blow to, slay, assassinate, or execute an individual human or wild animal; in the simple passive/middle (Niphal) and causative passive (Hophal) stems, to be fatally wounded or struck down.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) + direct object (person or animal); passive in simple passive/middle stem (Niphal) or causative passive stem (Hophal)

senses.definition: To defeat, attack, capture, or slaughter opposing armies, rulers, cities, or territories in warfare, often paired with לְפִי חֶרֶב ('at the edge of the sword') or with a cognate noun.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) + direct object (army, king, people, city, or land), or with בְּ / partitive מִן

senses.definition: To devastate, discipline, blight, or kill people, livestock, or vegetation through severe weather or divine judgment; in the causative passive stem (Hophal), to be blighted or withered.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) with natural force or deity as subject; causative passive stem (Hophal) in figurative comparison

senses.definition: In an idiom with לֵב ('heart') as subject, to strike someone internally with remorse or pangs of conscience.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) with לֵב (heart) as subject + direct object (person)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In the sampled corpus, active forms occur exclusively in the causative active stem (Hiphil), while passive counterparts occur in the simple passive/middle stem (Niphal, 2SA 11:15) and the causative passive stem (Hophal, NUM 25:18; PSA 102:5). Frequent collocations include instrumental בְּ (e.g., בַּשֵּׁבֶט 'with a rod', EXO 21:20; בְּמַטֵּהוּ 'with his staff', NUM 20:11), לְפִי חֶרֶב ('by the edge of the sword', JOS 10:32; 2KI 10:25), cognate accusative מַכָּה גְדוֹלָה ('a great blow/defeat', 1SA 19:8; 1KI 20:21), and partitive מִן indicating casualties out of a larger group (JOS 7:5; JDG 20:45; NEH 13:25). In 2SA 24:10, לֵב ('heart') serves as the subject of the verb in an idiom for feeling guilt. In EZK 22:13, הִכֵּיתִי כַפִּי ('I struck my palm') expresses indignation.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adverb indicating continuation ('still, yet'), repetition or addition ('again, further'), or, when paired with negation or rhetorical questions, cessation ('no longer, no more').

senses.definition: Indicates the repetition of an action, a renewed future occurrence, or something additional beyond what already exists.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying verbs or interrogative clauses

senses.definition: Indicates the ongoing persistence of a state, existence, or simultaneous action at the time of reference.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb in nominal/participial clauses or with pronominal suffix (עוֹדֶנּוּ)

senses.definition: With negative particles (לֹא, אֵין, oath אִם) or in rhetorical questions, marks the end, absence, or non-recurrence of a state or action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb following negation (לֹא / אֵין / אִם) or in rhetorical questions

senses.definition: In the phrase כָּל עוֹד, expresses the entire duration during which a condition continues to hold.
senses.grammatical_frame: Conjunctional phrase (כָּל עוֹד) introducing a temporal/conditional clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in negative constructions with לֹא, אֵין, or the oath particle אִם, often paired with the auxiliary verb יָסַף ('do again/continue', e.g., 2SA 2:28; 2KI 6:23; PSA 77:8; ISA 10:20; ISA 52:1; HOS 1:6) to express 'no longer / never again'. Takes pronominal suffixes when indicating ongoing state in nominal or participial clauses (עוֹדֶנּוּ, GEN 18:22; NUM 11:33). Also combines with כָּל in כָּל עוֹד to mean 'as long as' (JOB 27:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Encompasses both a Qal verb meaning to tend, pasture, or graze livestock (and figuratively to shepherd or govern people) and a feminine noun denoting moral wickedness, harm, distress, or disaster.

senses.definition: To tend, pasture, or feed a flock or herd; also used reflexively/critically of leaders feeding themselves rather than the flock.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb (transitive with direct object)

senses.definition: Of animals (flocks, cattle, donkeys, gazelles), to graze or browse in pasture or among vegetation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb (intransitive)

senses.definition: Figuratively, to shepherd, guide, care for, or rule over a people (applied to kings or God); also extended to agricultural produce nourishing people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb (transitive, metaphorical)

senses.definition: One who tends flocks; frequently used metaphorically for a ruler, political leader, or God as protector and guide of Israel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal active participle (used substantively, singular and plural)

senses.definition: Moral wrong, wickedness, or an evil deed committed by individuals, leaders, or a nation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular, construct, and plural)

senses.definition: Harm, danger, distress, misfortune, or calamity experienced by people or brought upon a community as judgment or hostility.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (often with prepositions לְ / בְּ or as object of verbs like הֵבִיא)

entries.collocations_and_notes: The evidence packet groups two distinct but homographic lexical usages under this lemma: (1) a Qal verb meaning to tend/graze/shepherd (with its participle functioning substantively as 'shepherd' or figuratively 'leader/ruler', e.g., EZK 34:2, 10, 23; MIC 5:4; PSA 80:2), and (2) a feminine noun denoting moral evil/wickedness or harm/calamity. Common nominal expressions include בְּיוֹם רָעָה / לְיוֹם רָעָה ('in/for the day of disaster', PSA 41:2; PRO 16:4), הֵבִיא רָעָה עַל ('bring disaster upon', 1KI 21:29; JER 19:3; JER 23:12; JER 49:37), לְרָעָה ('for harm/calamity', JDG 2:15; 2SA 18:32; JER 28:8), and contrast with שָׁלוֹם ('peace/welfare', JER 38:4). In the plural (רָעוֹת), it denotes either wicked deeds (JER 3:5; JER 44:9; EZK 6:9) or experienced calamities (1SA 10:19, paired with צָרוֹת 'distresses').

entries.core_meaning_summary: Many, numerous, great, or abundant in number, extent, or degree; also used substantively for a multitude, predicatively for "enough," and in construct as a title meaning "chief" (as well as in the city name Rabbah).

senses.definition: Large in number; consisting of many individuals, items, occurrences, or units of time, modifying plural nouns or collective singular nouns.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective, attributive or predicative, plural or singular with collective nouns

senses.definition: Large in extent, volume, intensity, or degree, modifying mass nouns, abstract qualities, wealth, crowds, or waters.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective (attributive, predicative, or construct before a noun), singular or plural with מַיִם

senses.definition: A large number of people, a crowd, or the majority/multitude.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantive plural adjective, with or without the definite article

senses.definition: Sufficient or enough, used as an exclamation or predicate indicating that no more is needed or that an action should cease.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicative/exclamatory singular adjective at clause start

senses.definition: High-ranking leader, commander, or chief officer over a group of subordinates.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct singular noun preceding a plural noun (רַב טַבָּחִים)

senses.definition: Proper geographic name (Rabbah), designating the capital city of the Ammonites when in construct with בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular construct form (רַבַּת) in a place name

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently modifies countable plural nouns such as יָמִים ("days"), עַמִּים ("peoples"), גּוֹיִם ("nations"), and מַיִם ("waters," conveying abundance or mighty volume), as well as collective singular nouns like עַם ("people"), גּוֹי ("nation"), and עֵץ ("trees"). In construct with a plural noun of functionaries (רַב טַבָּחִים), it denotes an official title ("chief of the guard"). In DEU 3:11 and 2SA 17:27, the feminine singular construct form רַבַּת appears as the place name Rabbah (רַבַּת בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן, "Rabbah of the Ammonites"), which is grouped under this lemma in the corpus. Note also the elliptical feminine plural רָאוֹת רַבּוֹת ("seeing many things," ISA 42:20).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Sacredness or consecrated status belonging to God, also designating holy places, consecrated objects or offerings, and in superlative constructions the innermost sanctuary or most sacred things.

senses.definition: The state or status of being sacred, consecrated, and set apart to God, predicated of persons (priests, Levites), days (Sabbath), consecrated animals, sacrificial portions, vessels, land, or dedicated wealth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun as predicate or subject with הָיָה / verbless clause (often with לַיהוָה)

senses.definition: Used as the second element in a construct chain to qualify a preceding noun as belonging to the divine or cultic realm—such as ground, garments, temple vessels, standard weights, dwelling, mountain, throne, spirit, name, words, or covenant.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun (absolute or with pronominal suffix) as nomen rectum in construct chain

senses.definition: With the definite article, the consecrated precinct or sanctuary where cultic service and libations take place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Definite singular noun (הַקֹּדֶשׁ) as object of construct or following locative preposition בְּ

senses.definition: In the plural, consecrated things, sacred offerings, or dedicated temple gifts and treasures.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun (קֳדָשִׁים / קָדָשַׁי) in construct chains or with pronominal suffix

senses.definition: Superlative construction (singular or construct plural governing the definite or indefinite plural) denoting either the innermost sacred chamber of the tabernacle or temple (behind the veil / inside the דְּבִיר) or objects and sacrificial offerings of the highest degree of sanctity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct superlative phrase: קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים / קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים / קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently functions as the nomen rectum in construct chains to characterize nouns as sacred or belonging to the divine sphere (e.g., אַדְמַת קֹדֶשׁ 'holy ground', שֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ 'sanctuary shekel', בִּגְדֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ 'holy garments', שֵׁם קָדְשִׁי 'my holy name', רוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ 'his holy spirit', הֵיכַל קָדְשֶׁךָ 'your holy temple', בְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ 'holy covenant'). Forms the superlative construction קֹדֶשׁ (הַ)קָּדָשִׁים / קָדְשֵׁי הַקֳּדָשִׁים ('holy of holies' / 'most holy') for both the innermost chamber of the tabernacle/temple and the most restricted sacrificial offerings. Appears in explicit contrast with זָר ('outsider/layperson', EXO 29:33) and in parallel/opposition to profaning (חִלֵּל, LEV 21:6, EZK 36:20).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To guard, watch over, observe, or keep (physically protecting, monitoring, fulfilling obligations, or, in the Niphal, taking care and being on guard).

senses.definition: To watch over, protect, tend, or keep under guard, whether caring for a place or property, protecting lives, maintaining custody over people or objects, or standing sentry at a post; as a participle, a watchman or custodian.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), transitive with direct object, with עַל, or substantival participle

senses.definition: To observe closely, monitor, or pay close attention to conditions, paths, or one's own conduct and speech, including watching out for and steering clear of harmful ways.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), transitive with direct object or with לְ + noun

senses.definition: To observe, obey, carry out, or fulfill faithfully, applied to divine commandments, statutes, covenants, sacred days, vows, promises, justice, and priestly or sanctuary duties.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active basic stem (Qal), transitive with direct object or followed by infinitive construct לַעֲשׂוֹת

senses.definition: To watch oneself, be careful, or be on guard against doing something wrong or dangerous, appearing in warnings and prohibitions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Reflexive/passive stem (Niphal), imperative with ethical dative לְךָ/לָכֶם or בְּנַפְשׁוֹתֵיכֶם, often followed by פֶּן or אַל

senses.definition: To pay regard to, cling to, or devote oneself to something (specifically worthless idols or vanities, contrasted with forsaking loyalty).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive stem (Piel), participle governing a direct object

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly pairs with legal/covenantal objects such as מִצְוָה (commandment), חֻקָּה (statute), תּוֹרָה (law), בְּרִית (covenant), מִשְׁפָּט (justice), and שַׁבָּת (Sabbath), often alongside עָשָׂה (do) or שָׁמַע (listen). In cultic contexts, frequently governs מִשְׁמֶרֶת or מִשְׁמָר (charge, watch, guard duty). In Niphal warning formulas, appears in the imperative followed by לְךָ/לָכֶם and פֶּן (lest) or a negative prohibition. Idiomatic expressions include שָׁמַר לְפִי מַחְסוֹם ("keep a muzzle on my mouth," PSA 39:2) and שָׁמַר אָרְחוֹת פָּרִיץ ("avoid/keep clear of the paths of a violent person," PSA 17:4). The participle serves substantively as a title for a guard, watchman, or custodian (e.g., שֹׁמְרֵי הַסִּפִּים "threshold-keepers," שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּגָדִים "keeper of the garments"). Note stem distinctions: Qal expresses outward guarding, observing, or fulfilling; Niphal expresses reflexive caution ("be careful, watch oneself"); Piel (JON 2:9) expresses devoted attachment or regard toward objects of worship.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Cardinal number four, used independently, in compound numerals, and in the plural form to denote forty.

senses.definition: The basic cardinal quantity four, quantifying nouns (preceding or following the noun, or in construct state), taking pronominal suffixes to refer to a group of four, or functioning substantivally (such as for four limbs in walking or in graded poetic sequence).
senses.grammatical_frame: Cardinal numeral (absolute, construct before noun/thousand, post-nominal, with pronominal suffix, or substantivized after preposition)

senses.definition: Component of compound cardinal and calendar numerals, combining with ten (fourteen), multiples of ten (twenty-four, thirty-four, sixty-four), or hundred (four hundred) to count years, days, objects, livestock, or people, including ordinal-like designation of the twenty-fourth day of a month.
senses.grammatical_frame: Numeral in compound expressions with עָשָׂר/עֶשְׂרֵה, tens, or מֵאוֹת

senses.definition: Plural form denoting the multiple forty, used alone or in combination with smaller or larger numerals to specify durations of days and years, troop or population counts, and reign lengths.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural numeral אַרְבָּעִים preceding counted nouns (usually singular for יוֹם, שָׁנָה, לַיְלָה, אֶלֶף) or coordinated with units

entries.collocations_and_notes: Exhibits gender-polarized agreement patterns common to Hebrew numerals (masculine-form אַרְבָּעָה with masculine nouns such as רָאשִׁים, אֲנָשִׁים, שֻׁלְחָנוֹת, אוֹפַנֵּי; feminine-form אַרְבַּע with feminine nouns such as טַבְּעֹת, רוּחוֹת, עָרִים, קַרְנֹתָיו). Appears in construct (אַרְבַּעַת) before definite/counted plural nouns such as יָמִים (JDG 11:40) and אֲלָפִים (1CH 23:5, EZK 48:30), and takes pronominal suffixes (לְאַרְבַּעְתָּם/לְאַרְבַּעְתָּן, EZK 1:10). Idiomatic expressions include הֹלֵךְ עַל אַרְבַּע ('walking on all fours', LEV 11:21), אַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת / אַרְבַּע קְצוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם ('four winds / four ends of the heavens', JER 49:36), graded numerical parallelism שְׁלֹשָׁה... וְעַל אַרְבָּעָה ('three... and for four', AMO 1:3), and the recurring duration formula אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם וְאַרְבָּעִים לַיְלָה ('forty days and forty nights', EXO 34:28, DEU 9:9).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To locate, encounter, reach, or attain something or someone (active), or to be discovered, detected, or present (passive).

senses.definition: To locate, come upon, or meet a physical object, person, place, or material resource, either through deliberate search or by chance encounter.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with a direct object or relative clause

senses.definition: To reach, overtake, or strike an unintended or hostile target (such as spreading fire catching thorns, a flying axe-head hitting a person, or archers overtaking a fleeing warrior).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with a nonhuman or hostile subject and direct object

senses.definition: To discover, attain, or experience an abstract quality, inner state, explanation, fault, or person of a specific character; also to muster the resolve to act (with an infinitive complement).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with abstract nouns, character descriptions, or an infinitive complement

senses.definition: To be discovered, detected, caught, recorded, or present on hand, shifting the grammatical focus from the finder to the person, item, or record that turns up.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive stem (Niphal), intransitive with the located item, person, or written statement as grammatical subject

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in the active simple stem (Qal) to describe locating, encountering, attaining, or striking an object or goal, and in the passive stem (Niphal) to describe being discovered, caught, detected, or present on hand. Frequently pairs with `בִּקֵּשׁ` ("to seek", e.g., 1KI 1:3, PSA 37:36, ECC 12:10). Common idioms include `מָצָא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי` ("to find favor in the eyes of", GEN 33:15), `לֹא מָצָא בְּיָד` ("to find nothing [wrong] in someone's hand", 1SA 12:5), and `נִמְצָא בְיָד` / `אִתּוֹ` ("to be found in one's possession", GEN 44:9, 1SA 9:8). In 1CH 17:25, `מָצָא` takes an infinitive complement (`לְהִתְפַּלֵּל`) to express finding the resolve or boldness to pray.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An indefinite or unbounded span of time, denoting either perpetual future duration, enduring permanence, or remote antiquity.

senses.definition: Perpetual future duration without a foreseen end, whether spanning a person's ongoing existence, successive generations, or unlimited time; with negation it indicates "never."
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in prepositional phrases (with lamed or ad) or adverbial accusative of time

senses.definition: Lasting permanence or unending character as an attribute of institutions, covenants, conditions, or divine titles; in the plural, all successive ages.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (singular or plural) as the second member of a construct chain modifying another noun or adjective

senses.definition: Remote past time or distant antiquity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun after the preposition min ("from") or as the second member of a construct chain denoting ancient peoples or sites

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in prepositional phrases marking unending duration (`לְעוֹלָם`, `עַד־עוֹלָם`, `עַד־הָעוֹלָם`, `מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם`) or distant past (`מֵעוֹלָם`). Often stands in poetic parallelism with `דֹּר וָדֹר` ("generation and generation", e.g., PSA 89:2, PSA 100:5, PSA 106:31, PSA 145:13) or `עַד` ("perpetuity", PSA 21:5, ISA 26:4). In construct chains it regularly qualifies legal ordinances (`חֻקַּת עוֹלָם`, `חָק־עוֹלָם`), covenants (`בְּרִית עוֹלָם`), emotional states (`שִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם`, `כְּלִמַּת עוֹלָם`), and divine titles (`אֵל עוֹלָם`, `צוּר עוֹלָמִים`). In PSA 73:12, `שַׁלְוֵי עוֹלָם` describes the wicked as perpetually carefree or always at ease.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A verb meaning to move downward or collapse in its simple active stem (Qal)—including prostrating, perishing in battle, or defecting—and to cause to drop, strike down, or cast lots in its causative active stem (Hiphil).

senses.definition: To drop from a higher place, lose footing and collapse, or crumble down (of people, animals, hairs, walls, or mountains).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal), intransitive, often with locative adverbials (בְּ, אָרְצָה)

senses.definition: To throw oneself downward intentionally, whether prostrating face down in reverence or awe, embracing someone's neck, or casting oneself onto a sword.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal) + עַל or אֶל + body part or weapon (פָּנִים, צַוָּארִים, חֶרֶב)

senses.definition: To die violently or be slain in combat or slaughter.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal), often with instrumental or locative phrases (בַּחֶרֶב, לְפִי חֶרֶב, בְּיַד) or with חָלָל ("slain"); participle frequently used substantivally for battle casualties

senses.definition: To suffer political or military ruin and overthrow, said metaphorically of a city or nation (contrasted with rising again).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal), intransitive with city or personified nation as subject

senses.definition: To desert one's own side and go over or surrender to an opposing ruler or army.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal) + עַל or אֶל + opposing ruler or people

senses.definition: To descend or come suddenly upon someone, whether of a raiding destroyer or an overwhelming sensation such as terror.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal) + עַל + object affected

senses.definition: To cause something or someone to drop, bring down trees, knock out a tooth, bring about someone's death by the sword, or cause a deep sleep to come upon a person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) + direct object (often with אֶת or object suffix), sometimes + עַל, בַּחֶרֶב, or בְּיַד

senses.definition: To throw or cast lots in order to reach a decision or join a shared undertaking, or to apportion territory by measuring line as an inheritance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) + direct object גּוֹרָל / פּוּר ("lot"), or object suffix + בְּחֶבֶל נַחֲלָה ("by a measuring line of inheritance")

entries.collocations_and_notes: Shows a clear grammatical contrast between the simple active stem (Qal), where the subject moves downward, collapses, prostrates, defects, or perishes, and the causative active stem (Hiphil), where an agent causes something or someone to drop, be cut down, be slain, or casts lots/apportions territory. Common idiomatic frames include נָפַל עַל/אֶל פָּנָיו ("fall on one's face" in awe or supplication), נָפַל עַל צַוָּארָיו ("fall upon one's neck" in greeting), נָפַל בַּחֶרֶב / לְפִי חֶרֶב ("fall by the sword"), נָפַל אֶל / עַל + ruler/nation ("defect to"), and הִפִּיל גּוֹרָל / פּוּר ("cast lots"). Paired with כָּשַׁל ("stumble") in PSA 27:2 and contrasted with קוּם ("rise") in AMO 5:2.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A temporal adverb meaning "now" or "at this time" that also functions widely as a discourse particle marking a logical transition to a command, request, or conclusion.

senses.definition: Refers to the present moment, current circumstances, or an imminent turning point in time, sometimes explicitly contrasted with past time (אָז) or preceding events.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverb modifying a clause or verb; occasionally paired with pronouns or temporal contrasts

senses.definition: With the preposition מִן, marks the present moment as the starting point of an ongoing or unbounded duration.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition מִן + עַתָּה (מֵעַתָּה), paired with וְעַד עוֹלָם

senses.definition: Signals a logical or rhetorical shift in speech from prior statements or conditions to a resulting command, plea, warning, conditional clause, or declaration.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial discourse marker, typically prefixed with וְ (וְעַתָּה) or וְגַם (וְגַם עַתָּה), preceding imperatives, jussives, prohibitions, or questions

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very frequently prefixed with conjunction וְ as וְעַתָּה (and occasionally וְגַם עַתָּה in JOL 2:12) at the opening of a clause to pivot from an observation or narrative condition to an imperative, jussive, prohibition (אַל), plea (with נָא), or rhetorical question. In temporal usage, it contrasts directly with אָז ("then") in JOS 14:11 and combines with the preposition מִן as מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם ("from now and forever") in PSA 131:3. Appears in pausal form עָתָּה in JOS 14:11. Sometimes introduces a presentative הִנֵּה (1SA 12:2; 2CH 18:22) or causal/conclusive לָכֵן (JER 32:36).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Personal interrogative pronoun asking "who?" or "whose?" in direct and indirect questions, rhetorical challenges implying "no one," and wish formulas meaning "would that!".

senses.definition: Interrogative pronoun inquiring after the identity, possessor, or agent of a person or group in direct or embedded questions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable interrogative pronoun (subject or predicate of verbal or nominal clauses, direct object with אֶת־, second member of a construct chain, prepositional complement, or introducing an indirect question after verbs of knowing or seeing)

senses.definition: Rhetorical interrogative used in challenges, boasts, laments, expressions of humility, or claims of incomparability to imply that no one exists or is able to act (or, when paired with negation, that everyone must do so); occasionally stands before a noun in the sense "what/which?" (DEU 4:7, MIC 7:18).
senses.grammatical_frame: Indeclinable interrogative pronoun in rhetorical clauses (clause-initial, sometimes preceded by כִּי/וְכִי, with imperfect, perfect, participial, or nominal predicates, or immediately preceding an indefinite noun)

senses.definition: Particle introducing an ardent wish or longing, especially in the fixed phrase מִי יִתֵּן ("who will give?" = "if only! / would that!").
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative pronoun in optative constructions (fixed phrase מִי יִתֵּן + noun/clause, or מִי + imperfect verb with suffix)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Indeclinable and uninflected for gender or number, though used with masculine, feminine (RUT 3:16, ISA 51:12), and plural (2KI 10:13) referents. Frequently joins with prepositions (לְמִי, עַל מִי, מִיַּד מִי) or direct object marker (אֶת־מִי), and follows a construct noun to ask "whose?" (שׁוֹר מִי, חֲמוֹר מִי in 1SA 12:3). Can be reinforced by demonstrative זֶה ("who is this?": ISA 63:1) or pronoun הוּא ("who is he/there?": JOB 17:3). The fixed sequence מִי יִתֵּן functions idiomatically to introduce an ardent wish ("O that! / would that!": DEU 28:67, PSA 53:7).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The upper expanse or sky above the earth, extending to the transcendent abode of God and occasionally personified as cosmic witnesses or worshippers.

senses.definition: The visible sky, upper atmosphere, or physical cosmos above the earth—where birds fly, clouds form and release rain, and celestial bodies are set—frequently paired with the earth to encompass all creation or to denote extreme height and universal scope.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (with or without definite article הַ־, in construct phrases as second member, after spatial prepositions בְּ־/מִן/אֶל/תַּחַת/עַד, or with directional ה־ ending הַשָּׁמַיְמָה)

senses.definition: The transcendent heavenly realm conceived as God's dwelling place and seat of rule, from which God and his messenger look down, speak, hear prayer, and send sustenance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (typically definite with spatial prepositions בְּ־ or מִן, in nominal clauses locating God's throne, or as adverbial accusative of place with a verb of hearing)

senses.definition: The heavens personified or associated with celestial beings, summoned as witnesses or depicted as praising, rejoicing, or falling short of purity before God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (vocative or subject of plural verbs of speech, praise, or evaluation, or direct object of verbs summoning witnesses alongside the earth)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with אֶרֶץ ("earth/land") as a cosmic merism for the whole created order (GEN 1:1, GEN 2:1, DEU 31:28, 1CH 29:11, PSA 146:6). Common construct phrases include עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם ("birds of the sky": GEN 7:23, 1KI 21:24, PSA 104:12, JER 34:20, EZK 32:4, HOS 4:3, ZEP 1:3) and צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם ("host of the sky," referring to sun, moon, and stars: DEU 4:19, 2KI 17:16). Spatial expressions include תַּחַת (כָּל) הַשָּׁמַיִם ("under [all] the sky," i.e., anywhere on earth: DEU 4:19, DEU 9:14), the directional ending in הַשָּׁמַיְמָה ("skyward": EXO 9:8, DEU 4:19), and adverbial accusative הַשָּׁמַיִם ("in/from heaven" with verbs of hearing: 1KI 8:34, alternating with מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם in 2CH 6:21, 2CH 7:14). Always plural in morphology and takes plural verb agreement (e.g., נָטָפוּ JDG 5:4, יִרְגָּזוּ 2SA 22:8, לֹא זַכּוּ JOB 15:15, וְיוֹדוּ PSA 89:6, יִתְּנוּ JER 14:22).

entries.core_meaning_summary: In the basic active (Qal) stem, to answer, respond, speak up, or testify; in the intensive/factitive (Piel), passive (Pual), and reflexive (Hithpael) stems, to afflict, oppress, humble, or be afflicted.

senses.definition: To answer, reply, or respond verbally to a person, question, argument, or summons.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active); transitive with direct object (אֶת or suffix) or intransitive, frequently followed by וַיֹּאמֶר/וַיְדַבֵּר

senses.definition: To speak up, address, declare, or respond in turn, including liturgical acclamation and responsive singing or chanting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active); intransitive or with direct quotation / suffix, often paired with אָמַר

senses.definition: Of God (or a deity), to answer a call, prayer, or appeal by acting, delivering, or granting a favorable outcome.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active); transitive with person or outcome (אֶת / suffix), often with instrumental בְּ־ (e.g., בָאֵשׁ, בֶּאֱמֶת)

senses.definition: To testify or give formal witness in a dispute or legal proceeding, either on behalf of or against someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (basic active); verb + בְּ־ (indicating the person testified for or against) + optional object (e.g., סָרָה)

senses.definition: To afflict, oppress, or mistreat a people or community through harsh treatment or subjugation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (factitive/intensive active); transitive with direct object (אֶת or noun phrase)

senses.definition: To humble or afflict oneself through prescribed self-denial and fasting on a sacred day.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (factitive/intensive active); transitive with אֶת נֶפֶשׁ (reflexive object "one's soul/self")

senses.definition: To violate sexually, abuse, or humiliate a woman.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (factitive/intensive active); transitive with אֶת + female person as object

senses.definition: To be afflicted, humbled, or endure hardship alongside another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael (reflexive/mediopassive, with בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר) and Pual (passive infinitive construct with pronominal suffix)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In this dataset, the verb עָנָה exhibits a sharp stem-based semantic division: the Qal stem expresses communication, answering, testifying, or responding (senses 1a–1d), whereas the Piel, Pual, and Hithpael stems express affliction, oppression, self-denial, or violation (senses 2a–2d). In Qal narrative dialogue, וַיַּעַן ... וַיֹּאמֶר ("he answered and said") is a standard formula both for replies and for initiating a formal speech or response to a situation (e.g., 1SA 26:6; JOB 8:1; ISA 21:9; ZEC 4:4). When divine action is in view, Qal עָנָה frequently pairs with קָרָא ("to call," JOB 12:4; PSA 20:10; ISA 50:2; ISA 65:12; JER 33:3) and takes בְּ־ to indicate the means of response (e.g., בָאֵשׁ "with fire," 1KI 18:24; 1CH 21:26; בְקוֹל "with a voice," EXO 19:19). In Piel, the idiom עִנָּה אֶת נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם ("afflict your souls/selves") is fixed for ritual fasting and self-denial on the Day of Atonement (LEV 23:27; NUM 29:7).

entries.core_meaning_summary: As a noun, denotes the nose, nostrils, face, or anger/wrath; as an adverbial or conjunctive particle, marks addition or intensification ("also," "even," "indeed").

senses.definition: The nose or nostrils as the physical organ of breathing and smelling (used both literally of breath entering the body and figuratively of wind/blast or receiving the scent of incense).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular or dual (often with pronominal suffix and preposition בְּ־)

senses.definition: The face or countenance, especially in expressions of prostration to the ground or haughtiness ("loftiness of face/nose").
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, dual or singular (with preposition עַל in prostration idioms, or in construct גֹּבַהּ אַפּוֹ)

senses.definition: Fierce displeasure, anger, or wrath (human or divine), frequently depicted as burning, kindling, or being turned back, and contrasted with patience ("long of anger").
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, singular (or dual in אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם), subject of חָרָה/שׁוּב, object of הֵשִׁיב/שָׁלַח/הֶחֱזִיק, or with בְּ־ / חֲרוֹן / חֳרִי

senses.definition: Additive particle introducing an additional participant, item, or parallel action alongside what has already been stated.
senses.grammatical_frame: Particle (often וְאַף), preceding a pronoun, noun phrase, prepositional phrase, or clause

senses.definition: Emphatic or corroborative particle heightening a statement, introducing a climactic, confirming, or contrasting assertion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial or phrase-initial particle modifying a clause, verb, or predicate adjective

entries.collocations_and_notes: This entry encompasses two distinct grammatical categories sharing the same spelling: a noun and a conjunctive/adverbial particle. As a noun, אַף frequently appears in the dual (אַפַּיִם) for nostrils or face (GEN 2:7; 1KI 1:23), and in the idiom אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם ("slow to anger," literally "long of nostrils/anger," PRO 15:18). For anger, it commonly collocates with verbs of burning (חָרָה, e.g., GEN 30:2; NUM 11:33; JDG 6:39; 2SA 12:5) and turning back (שׁוּב/הֵשִׁיב, JOB 9:13; ISA 9:20), as well as the construct phrases חֳרִי אָף ("burning anger," 1SA 20:34; 2CH 25:10) and חֲרוֹן אַף ("heat of anger," JOB 20:23; PSA 85:4; HOS 11:9), and is paired with חֵמָה ("wrath") and קֶצֶף ("fury") (JER 32:37; EZK 5:15; EZK 22:20). As a particle, it frequently combines with the conjunction וְ־ (וְאַף) or personal pronouns (אַף אָנִי, אַף הֵמָּה, אַף הִיא) to add a parallel or intensified statement.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A preposition expressing an intermediate position, interval, mutual relationship, or distinction separating or connecting two or more entities, groups, categories, or points in time.

senses.definition: Spatial preposition marking a location, gap, boundary, or movement situated in the interval separating two or more places, objects, or body parts; includes the compound מִבֵּין (and מִבֵּינוֹת לְ) denoting origin or emergence from an intervening space.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + X + וּבֵין / וְלְ + Y; preposition + plural/dual noun; or compound מִבֵּין / מִבֵּינוֹת לְ

senses.definition: Preposition with a single plural noun or plural pronominal suffix denoting presence, comparison, sharing, or standing within a larger group.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + plural noun or plural pronominal suffix

senses.definition: Preposition denoting a reciprocal bond, legal status, covenant, peace, conflict, or judicial arbitration involving two or more persons, families, or peoples.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + X + וּבֵין / לְ + Y (personal nouns or pronominal suffixes)
senses.semantic_domain: Social Relations / Covenant, Conflict, and Law

senses.definition: Preposition marking a conceptual boundary or differentiation between distinct categories or states, or pairing contrasting extremes exhaustively ("whether ... or").
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition + X + וּבֵין / לְ + Y (abstract or categorical nouns)

senses.definition: Temporal preposition in the fixed expression בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם ("between the two evenings"), designating the transitional period at the close of day.
senses.grammatical_frame: fixed temporal phrase בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly constructs with pronominal suffixes in either singular-like base forms (e.g., בֵּינִי, בֵּינְךָ, בֵּינוֹ) or plural-like base forms (e.g., בֵּינֵיכֶם, בֵּינֵיהֶם), and once in the compound feminine-plural form מִבֵּינוֹת לְ (EZK 10:6). Two main correlative patterns appear: בֵּין X וּבֵין Y (most frequent) and בֵּין X לְ Y (NUM 30:17, 2CH 14:10, EZK 22:26) or בֵּין X וְלְ Y (JOL 2:17). Compounds with מִן as מִבֵּין ("from between"; DEU 28:57, EZK 47:18, ZEC 6:1). Frequently governed by verbs of separating or distinguishing (הִבְדִּיל in GEN 1:4, LEV 10:10, EZK 22:26; הִפְלָה in EXO 11:7), covenant-making (כָּרַת בְּרִית in 2KI 11:17, 2CH 23:16; נָתַן בְּרִית in GEN 17:2), and judging (שָׁפַט in DEU 1:16).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An enclitic particle of entreaty, urgency, or present focus attached chiefly to imperatives, cohortatives, jussives, and interjections.

senses.definition: Particle attached to an imperative (or a consecutive perfect expressing a request, as in GEN 40:14) to soften a command into a polite request or to add earnest urgency to a directive, plea, or summons.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic particle following an imperative (or volitional consecutive perfect)

senses.definition: Particle attached to cohortative (first-person) or jussive (third-person) verb forms to mark a polite proposal, earnest wish, prayer, or (in ISA 47:13) an ironic challenge.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic particle following a cohortative or jussive verb

senses.definition: Particle following the presentative interjection הִנֵּה or an interrogative word (אַיֵּה), drawing immediate attention to a current circumstance or sharpening an inquiry.
senses.grammatical_frame: enclitic particle following הִנֵּה or an interrogative adverb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently induces gemination (conjunctive dagesh) in the initial nun (נָּא) after certain verbal or pronominal suffixes (e.g., GEN 19:8, GEN 27:21, GEN 40:14, GEN 50:5, 2SA 14:17, 2SA 18:22, 2KI 7:12, 1CH 21:13, NEH 1:11, PSA 122:8). Commonly follows וְעַתָּה ("and now"; GEN 50:5, EXO 10:17, JOS 2:12, JDG 7:3, 1SA 28:22, JER 18:11) or הִנֵּה ("behold"; GEN 12:11, GEN 19:8, JDG 19:9, 1SA 9:6, JOB 33:2), and co-occurs with plea formulas such as בִּי אֲדוֹנָי (JDG 13:8) and אָנָּא (NEH 1:11). Used across social registers: by petitioners to superiors or to God (GEN 40:14, 1KI 20:32, NEH 1:11, JOB 10:9), between equals (GEN 12:11, JDG 19:9), and by superiors or God in urgent directives (JDG 7:3, 2SA 13:17, ISA 7:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A sea, ocean, or large inland body of water, and by extension the western cardinal direction.

senses.definition: A large body of water, whether an ocean, sea, or large inland lake, conceived as a domain of waves, marine life, navigation, and coastal boundaries, and named in specific geographical designations.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (masculine, singular יָם, plural יַמִּים); frequently definite (הַיָּם), in construct chains (יַם סוּף, יָם הַמֶּלַח, חוֹל הַיָּם, יוֹדְעֵי יָם), or with locative/directional prepositions (בַּיָּם, עַל הַיָּם, מִיָּם עַד יָם, יָמָּה in 1KI 5:23)

senses.definition: The western cardinal direction or western side/border, paired with east, north, and south (and in PSA 107:3 paired with north after east and west).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (masculine) with directional ending -āh (יָמָּה), in prepositional phrases (מִיָּם, מִגְּבוּל יָם), or in construct with פְּאַת ('west side/quarter', פְּאַת יָם / פְּאַת יָמָּה)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Plural יַמִּים occurs for bodies of water in general or turbulent seas (GEN 1:10, PSA 8:9, EZK 27:34). With directional suffix -āh (יָמָּה), it denotes either literal movement 'to the sea' (1KI 5:23) or the cardinal direction 'westward / on the west' (GEN 28:14, EXO 36:32, EZK 48:8). Frequent constructs designate specific waters or features: הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל ('the Great Sea', i.e. the Mediterranean), יַם סוּף ('Sea of Reeds'), יָם הַמֶּלַח / יָם הָעֲרָבָה ('Salt Sea / Sea of the Arabah'), הַיָּם הַקַּדְמֹנִי ('eastern sea'), הַיָּם הָאַחֲרוֹן ('western/hinder sea'), לְשׁוֹן הַיָּם ('bay/tongue of the sea'), חוֹל הַיָּם ('sand of the sea'), דְּגֵי הַיָּם ('fish of the sea'), חֶבֶל הַיָּם ('coastal region'), מְצֻלוֹת יָם ('depths of the sea'), and יוֹדְעֵי יָם ('those knowledgeable of the sea', i.e. seafarers). In PSA 107:3, מִיָּם pairs with מִצָּפוֹן after מִמִּזְרָח וּמִמַּעֲרָב, where it either refers to a southern sea or functions poetically as the fourth compass point.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To feel fear or dread toward danger or enemies, to revere and stand in awe of God, or (in the passive/stative stem) to be fearsome and awe-inspiring.

senses.definition: To experience fear, alarm, or dread because of enemies, threats, calamity, or exposure, or to shrink back hesitantly from an action or speaking out of deference or apprehension.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stative/active stem (Qal) and adjectival/participial forms (יָרֵא / יְרֵאִים), absolute or with אֶת, מִן, מִפְּנֵי, or לְ + infinitive

senses.definition: To stand in reverent awe of God (or his name and presence), expressed through worship, covenant loyalty, keeping commandments, and turning from evil; as a verbal adjective or substantive, one who reveres and is devoted to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stative/active stem (Qal) with direct object (אֶת or pronominal suffix) or מִן, and construct/suffixed adjectival-substantive forms (יְרֵא, יְרֵאָיו, יְרֵאֶיךָ)

senses.definition: To be fearsome, terrible, or awe-inspiring (describing God or a sacred place); in the feminine plural as a noun, awesome or mighty deeds.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/stative participle (Niphal: נוֹרָא, fem. pl. נֹרָאוֹת / נוֹרָאוֹת), used attributively, predicatively, or substantively

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in negated reassurance formulas (אַל־תִּירָא / אַל־תִּירְאוּ "do not be afraid"), often paired with "be strong and courageous" (חִזְקוּ וְאִמְצוּ) or "do not be dismayed" (אַל־תֵּחָת / אַל־תִּשְׁתָּע). Objects of fear or reverence are introduced either by the direct-object marker אֶת (or suffix) or by the prepositions מִן / מִפְּנֵי. Across stems, the basic stative/active stem (Qal) and related adjectival forms express experiencing fear or holding God in reverence, whereas the passive/stative stem (Niphal participle נוֹרָא / נֹרָאוֹת) describes a place, deity, or deeds that inspire awe and dread.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Moving air or wind, life-sustaining breath, an inner human disposition or attitude, the active spirit of God, or a divinely dispatched spiritual agent or impulse.

senses.definition: Moving air or atmospheric wind, ranging from a gentle breeze or directional air current to a destructive storm blast; also used figuratively for emptiness or futility, and metonymically for cardinal directions ('every wind', 'four winds').
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (typically feminine); subject of motion verbs (e.g., בָּאָה, בֹּאִי, שְׁבָרֵךְ), object of שֹׁמֵר, or in directional prepositional phrases (לְכָל רוּחַ, מֵאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת) and construct expressions (רְעוּת רוּחַ, כַּנְפֵי רוּחַ, רוּחַ הַקָּדִים)

senses.definition: The animating breath or vital life-force within living beings, sustained or withdrawn by God, upon whose departure a creature dies.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine) with pronominal suffixes or in construct (רוּחַ הַחַיָּה); object of verbs of keeping, gathering, or taking away (שָׁמְרָה, יֶאֱסֹף, תֹּסֵף), and paired with נִשְׁמָתוֹ

senses.definition: A person's inner disposition, seat of emotion, courage, resolve, patience, integrity, or mental inclination.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine) with personal suffixes or in construct (רוּחַ חָכְמָה, עֲצֻבַת רוּחַ, רוּחַ נְגִידִים), frequently with בְּ ('in') or as subject of stative/affective verbs (קָמָה, תִקְצַר, כָּלְתָה) and paired with לֵב ('heart')

senses.definition: The active spirit or power of God, hovering over primordial waters, resting upon or rushing into individuals to impart wisdom, prophecy, strength, or visionary transport.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine) in construct with אֱלֹהִים, יְהוָה, or קָדְשׁוֹ, or absolute with definite article (אִישׁ הָרוּחַ); subject of verbs of motion/empowerment (מְרַחֶפֶת, תִּצְלַח עַל, תִּשָּׂאֵנִי) and object of נָתַן ('give/put') or עִצְּבוּ ('grieve')

senses.definition: An unseen spiritual agent or divinely dispatched impulse that acts in the heavenly council or enters human beings to produce terror, deception, stupor, or sudden compliance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine in 1SA 16:15; masculine in 1KI 22:21) with article (הָרוּחַ), modifying adjective (רָעָה), or in construct denoting effect (רוּחַ שֶׁקֶר, רוּחַ תַּרְדֵּמָה); object of נָתַן ('put') or נָסַךְ ('pour out')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Usually takes feminine verbal and adjectival agreement (e.g., מְרַחֶפֶת GEN 1:2, קָמָה JOS 2:11, גְּדוֹלָה JOB 1:19, רָעָה 1SA 16:15, וַתִּשָּׂאֵנִי EZK 43:5), though masculine agreement occurs when denoting a heavenly agent (וַיֵּצֵא הָרוּחַ 1KI 22:21). Frequent construct and prepositional collocations include רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים / רוּחַ יְהוָה ('spirit of God/YHWH'), רוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ ('his holy spirit'), אַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת ('four winds/directions'), כַּנְפֵי רוּחַ ('wings of wind'), רְעוּת רוּחַ / רַעְיוֹן רוּחַ ('pursuit/striving after wind', paired with הֶבֶל 'vapor/futility'), and construct phrases characterizing a disposition or effect (רוּחַ חָכְמָה, רוּחַ שֶׁקֶר, רוּחַ תַּרְדֵּמָה, רוּחַ מַשְׁחִית, עֲצֻבַת רוּחַ, רוּחַ נְכֵאָה). Often paired with לֵב ('heart') for inner life and with נְשָׁמָה ('breath') for mortal vitality.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To move, flow, or extend downward from a higher position to a lower one, or (in the causative stem) to bring, lead, or cast someone or something down.

senses.definition: To move physically from a higher place to a lower one, dismount, withdraw from an area or shelter, travel to another region (especially Egypt), or march down toward someone in encounter or battle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), intransitive, often with directional -āh, direct place name, or prepositions (אֶל, עַל, בְּ, מִן, מֵעַל)

senses.definition: Of God or heavenly fire, to descend from heaven to earth, a mountain, or a meeting place to reveal presence, speak, inspect, or consume.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal) with divine subject or fire (אֵשׁ), with עַל, בְּ, or מִן

senses.definition: Of liquids, tears, shadows, or geographical boundaries, to flow downward, shed streams, move down steps, or slope/extend downward toward a landmark.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal) with non-personal subjects (water, eyes, shadow, border), often with עַל, אֶל, מִתַּחַת, or directional -āh

senses.definition: To go down, be brought down, or cause someone to go down to the realm of the dead (Sheol/the pit), or of violence/retribution, to come down upon an offender's head.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), causative active stem (Hiphil), and causative passive stem (Hophal) with אֶל־שְׁאוֹל, שְׁאֹלָה, or עַל קָדְקֳדוֹ

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to move downward, take or lower an object from an elevated support, guide or bring people down to a lower place, or bring down enemies, peoples, or strongholds in defeat and judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) taking a direct object (with אֶת or pronominal suffix), often with אָרְצָה, אֶל, מֵעַל, or מִשָּׁם

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in contrast or sequence with ascending ("go up", עָלָה), as in 1SA 6:21, 2CH 20:16, and PRO 21:22. Common directional constructions include the directional ending -āh (e.g., מִצְרָיְמָה "to Egypt", אָרְצָה "to the ground", שְׁאוֹלָה "to Sheol", הַיַּרְדֵּנָה "to the Jordan"), prepositions אֶל, עַל, בְּ, and מִן / מֵעַל. In poetic lament, eyes "run down" with streams of water (פַּלְגֵי־מַיִם, PSA 119:136, LAM 3:48). Across stems, the basic active stem (Qal) expresses intransitive downward motion of people, water, fire, borders, or shadows, whereas the causative active stem (Hiphil) expresses bringing/taking/leading someone or something down or bringing enemies/strongholds low, and the causative passive stem (Hophal, ISA 14:15) expresses being brought down to Sheol.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To make known, report, or declare facts, secrets, divine messages, or events (in the Hiphil), and to be reported or revealed (in the Hophal).

senses.definition: To communicate news, facts, answers, or confidential information to someone, including reporting events or divulging a matter.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil stem (active transitive); recipient normally marked by לְ, with content expressed by a direct object, כִּי clause, לֵאמֹר + direct speech, or עַל + topic; participle used substantivally as 'informer/messenger'

senses.definition: To disclose, explain, or reveal something hidden, puzzling, or previously unknown, such as a riddle, a secret, a name, divine counsel, or future events.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil stem (active transitive); takes a direct object (e.g., riddle, name, word, course) and optionally a recipient marked by לְ

senses.definition: To proclaim publicly, testify, instruct, declare praise, or denounce wrongdoing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil stem (active, transitive or absolute); with direct object (e.g., faithfulness, uprightness, transgression) and optional recipient marked by לְ

senses.definition: To be reported, made known, or revealed to someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hophal stem (passive); impersonal or with a grammatical subject naming the message/vision and the recipient marked by לְ

entries.collocations_and_notes: Only Hiphil (active) and Hophal (passive: JDG 9:47; ISA 21:2) stems appear in the attested sample; no Qal forms occur. The recipient is routinely marked by לְ ('to'), while the message may be a direct object, a כִּי clause (GEN 3:11; JDG 9:47), direct speech introduced by לֵאמֹר (1SA 14:33; 19:2; 1KI 1:23; 2KI 5:4), or a topic introduced by עַל (1CH 19:5). The Hiphil infinitive absolute paired with the finite verb expresses certainty (הַגֵּד יַגִּיד, 1SA 22:22). Participial forms function substantivally for a messenger or reporter (2SA 1:5; 18:11; JER 51:31). Frequently paired with verbs of hearing, asking, or knowing (שָׁאַל in 1SA 25:8; שָׁמַע in ISA 41:26; 45:21; יָדַע in NEH 2:16; ISA 41:26; JER 33:3; רָץ in JER 51:31).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Bodily blood of humans and animals, sacrificial blood used in ritual, and by extension lifeblood, violent bloodshed, or legal accountability for killing.

senses.definition: The red fluid sustaining life within human or animal bodies, whether flowing from wounds, drained at slaughter, or appearing as a substance replacing water.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular, or plural with suffix in bodily reference); used as subject, direct object, or object of prepositions (בְּ, מִן, לְ, עַל)

senses.definition: The blood of a slaughtered sacrificial animal manipulated in cultic rituals, such as sprinkling, pouring, throwing against the altar, or applying to consecrated persons and objects.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun (often definite or in construct with an offering or animal); direct object of verbs of taking, applying, sprinkling, or pouring, or governed by מִן / בְּ

senses.definition: The vital life-essence or life itself identified with or symbolized by blood, grounding the prohibition against eating blood and figuratively representing risk to human life.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun with possessive suffix or in construct; subject, predicate nominal, or direct object

senses.definition: Lethal violence, murder, or the violent loss of human life.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular or plural noun (frequently plural absolute דָּמִים or plural construct דְּמֵי); object of verbs such as שָׁפַךְ ('shed') or אַרַב לְ ('lie in wait for'), or in construct chains denoting violent people

senses.definition: Moral or legal culpability for a person's death, or the claim for requital and vengeance arising from a killing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular or plural noun; in construct with גֹּאֵל ('avenger of'), or in predicative and prepositional clauses with לְ, בְּ, or מִיַּד ('from the hand of')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Plural forms (דָּמִים, construct דְּמֵי) commonly denote violent bloodshed or guilt for killing, as in דְּמֵיהֶם בָּם ('their bloodguilt is upon them', LEV 20:27), בֵּית הַדָּמִים ('house of bloodshed', 2SA 21:1), אַנְשֵׁי דָמִים ('men of bloodshed', PSA 26:9), and דָּמִים בְּדָמִים נָגָעוּ ('bloodshed touches bloodshed', HOS 4:2). Key idioms include גֹּאֵל הַדָּם ('avenger of blood', NUM 35:27; DEU 19:12), אֵין לוֹ דָם ('he has no bloodguilt', NUM 35:27) contrasted with דָּמִים לוֹ ('bloodguilt belongs to him', EXO 22:2), שָׁפַךְ דָּם ('pour out/shed blood', used both for altar blood in DEU 12:27 and murder in JER 22:17; EZK 22:3; 23:45), דַּם הַנָּקִי ('innocent blood', JER 22:17), and דָּמִים מָלֵאוּ / דָּם בִּידֵיהֶן ('hands full of blood / blood on their hands', ISA 1:15; EZK 23:45). In EZK 5:17, דָּם ('bloodshed') pairs with דֶּבֶר ('pestilence').

entries.core_meaning_summary: First-person singular independent personal pronoun, 'I', serving as subject in nominal and participial clauses or for emphasis and contrast with finite verbs.

senses.definition: First-person singular pronoun functioning as the grammatical subject of a verbless (nominal) or participial clause where person is not otherwise marked.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent pronoun serving as subject of a nominal or participial clause (often introduced by הִנֵּה, כִּי, or relative אֲשֶׁר)

senses.definition: First-person singular pronoun used explicitly alongside a finite first-person singular verb to mark emphasis, speaker focus, inclusion ('I too'), or contrast with another participant.
senses.grammatical_frame: Independent pronoun placed as explicit subject before or after a finite 1st-person singular verb (perfect, imperfect, or cohortative), frequently with contrastive וְ or גַּם

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently introduced by הִנֵּה ('behold, I...', e.g., GEN 25:32, GEN 50:5, EXO 19:9, 1SA 3:11, 1CH 17:1, ISA 54:16, HOS 2:16) to announce present or imminent action. Common in the Deuteronomic formula אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוֶּה/מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם ('which I am commanding you today', DEU 7:11, 11:27, 15:11, 27:10, 30:16). Doubled for heightened emphasis in ISA 43:11 (אָנֹכִי אָנֹכִי יְהוָה). Appears alongside the shorter 1st-person singular pronoun אֲנִי within the same verse in 2SA 3:13 and JON 1:9, and often stands in direct contrast to 2nd-person pronouns אַתָּה/אַתְּ/אַתֶּם (DEU 4:22, JDG 11:35, 1SA 17:8, 1SA 23:17).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Bad, inferior, morally wicked, or harmful; as a substantive, moral wrongdoing or adversity and calamity.

senses.definition: Defective, spoiled, inferior in physical quality, or unattractive in appearance, applied to animals, produce, offerings, or outward look.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective (including construct phrase רָעוֹת מַרְאֶה 'poor of appearance'); also substantive contrasting with טוֹב ('good')

senses.definition: Morally wrong, wicked, malicious, or unacceptable in character, disposition, speech, conduct, or reputation; as a plural substantive, wicked or hostile people.
