senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicate adjective modifying persons, deeds, ways, heart, or reputation (sometimes with בְּעֵינֵי 'in the eyes of'); or plural substantive (רָעִים)

senses.definition: That which is morally wrong, sinful, or contrary to divine standard; moral evil or wrongdoing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular substantive, frequently definite (הָרַע) as direct object of עָשָׂה ('do') with בְּעֵינֵי ('in the eyes of'), or indefinite paired with טוֹב ('good')

senses.definition: Harmful, distressing, or adverse; as a substantive, misfortune, injury, trouble, or calamity affecting a person or community.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular substantive (after prepositions מִן, בְּ, לְ, in construct יְמֵי רָע, or object of הֵבִיא 'bring') and attributive adjective modifying events, spirits, or occurrences (רוּחַ, פֶּגַע, מוֹקֵשׁ, מַעֲשֶׂה)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired as an antonym with טוֹב ('good', e.g., GEN 2:9, LEV 27:33, DEU 1:39, 2CH 18:17, PRO 15:3, AMO 5:15). Common recurring idioms include עָשָׂה הָרַע בְּעֵינֵי יְהוָה ('do what is evil/displeasing in YHWH's eyes', DEU 31:29, JDG 10:6, 1KI 16:30, 2KI 8:18, 2KI 17:2, 2KI 21:16, 2CH 36:5, ISA 66:4), הוֹצִיא שֵׁם רָע ('spread a bad/slanderous reputation', DEU 22:19), and יְמֵי רָע ('days of trouble/adversity', PSA 94:13). In PSA 140:12 (אִישׁ חָמָס רָע יְצוּדֶנּוּ), the syntax admits either an adjectival reading ('wicked man of violence') or a substantive subject ('evil/calamity will hunt him'). Note that the feminine singular form רָעָה also appears in the packet (e.g., 1SA 19:9, JER 35:15) as an adjective agreeing with feminine nouns, whereas substantive instances of 'calamity/evil' in DEU 31:29 and JER 4:6 reflect the feminine noun lemma rather than this entry.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A manufactured object, container, utensil, furnishing, weapon, or piece of personal equipment used for a particular function.

senses.definition: A pot, jar, bowl, or receptacle (made of clay or metal) designed to hold liquids or other contents.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural), often in construct with material (clay) or modifier (drinking, empty)

senses.definition: Utensils, implements, furnishings, or sacred articles belonging to the tabernacle or temple and used in sanctuary service.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (chiefly plural), in construct with sanctuary terms (service, holiness, house of God) or with pronominal suffixes referring to sacred furniture

senses.definition: Finely crafted objects, ornaments, or precious articles of silver or gold used as gifts, tribute, or royal treasure.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural), in construct with precious metals (silver, gold, refined gold) or quality (prized)

senses.definition: Weapons, armor, or military equipment carried into battle; also used poetically for instruments of violence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (plural, or singular in figurative construct), frequently governed by 'carry/bear' (weapon-bearer) or 'strip off', or in construct with 'war' or 'violence'

senses.definition: Personal equipment, baggage, apparel, or an item of domestic furniture (such as a seat); in ritual purity discourse, possibly referring either to personal gear or to the body.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural), with pronominal suffix or in construct (a man's gear, exile's baggage), or absolute for a seat/article

entries.collocations_and_notes: A broad general term whose specific referent is narrowed by construct phrases, materials, or context: e.g., kəlî ḥereś (earthenware vessel), kəlê kesep/zāhāb (silver/gold articles or vessels), kəlê haššārēt / haqqōdeš / hāʿăbōdâ (sanctuary service utensils/furnishings), kəlê hammilḥāmâ (weapons/war gear), and the frequent military title nōśēʾ kēlîm (weapon-bearer / armor-bearer). In 1SA 21:6, kəlê hannəʿārîm appears in a discussion of sexual abstinence and ritual purity, referring either to the young men's gear/packs or, by euphemism, to their bodies.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To draw near or approach in space or time, and causatively to bring near, present, or offer a sacrifice.

senses.definition: To move physically closer to a person, place, or sacred space; to step forward or approach for service, inquiry, or ritual action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple stem (Qal), intransitive with directional preposition (to) or absolute; also causative stem (Hiphil) used intransitively (EXO 14:10), and verbal adjective/participle (NUM 3:38)

senses.definition: To become imminent or at hand (of a time, event, or condition), to be on the point of doing something, or to reach and affect someone adversely (of harm or terror).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple stem (Qal) with an event, time, or affliction as subject; causative stem (Hiphil) with an infinitive construct (GEN 12:11, ISA 26:17)

senses.definition: To approach or present oneself directly before another person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive stem (Piel) with a direct pronominal object suffix

senses.definition: To cause a person, group, or non-sacrificial item to come forward; to bring into someone's presence or present tribute to a ruler.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) with direct object (person, group, or gift) and optional directional preposition (to, before)

senses.definition: To bring and present an animal, grain, salt, wine, or dedicatory gift to God as a ritual sacrifice or offering.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) with sacrificial item as direct object, frequently with indirect object ('to YHWH' or 'before YHWH')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently distinguishes between the simple stem (Qal), used intransitively for moving closer to a place, person, or altar (often with the prepositions 'el 'to' or bə- 'against/in') or for events/times drawing near, and the causative stem (Hiphil), used transitively for bringing someone or something forward or presenting sacrificial offerings (often paired with qorbān 'offering', 'iššeh 'fire-offering', or ḥaṭṭā't 'sin-offering', and directed lə-YHWH 'to YHWH' or lipnê YHWH 'before YHWH'). The causative stem also appears intransitively for approaching (EXO 14:10) and with an infinitive construct for being on the point of doing something (GEN 12:11, ISA 26:17). The intensive stem (Piel) appears once in the sample with a direct pronominal suffix for approaching a person (JOB 31:37).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A collective noun denoting small livestock (sheep and goats) kept in flocks, also used metaphorically for a community led by God or rulers and in the name of a Jerusalem gate.

senses.definition: Domesticated small livestock—sheep and goats collectively, or sheep specifically when contrasted with goats—tended in flocks for wool, milk, offspring, wealth, and sacrifice.
senses.grammatical_frame: Collective noun (taking singular or plural, often feminine plural, verbal/adjectival agreement); frequently paired with בָּקָר, governed by רָעָה/רֹעֶה, or partitive after מִן

senses.definition: Figurative designation for a human group—especially Israel or a community under divine or human leadership, or numerous/vulnerable individuals—depicted as a flock needing care, protection, or guidance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Collective noun in simile (כַּצֹּאן) or construct chains (צֹאן מַרְעִית, צֹאן הַהֲרֵגָה, צְעִירֵי הַצֹּאן), parallel to עַם or עֵדֶר

senses.definition: Component of the proper architectural/topographical name שַׁעַר הַצֹּאן, designating a specific gate in the wall of Jerusalem.
senses.grammatical_frame: Definite collective noun as the second element in the construct proper name שַׁעַר הַצֹּאן

entries.collocations_and_notes: Collective noun that exhibits both singular (e.g., יֻצָּג in EXO 10:24) and feminine plural or masculine plural agreement (e.g., תָּבֹאןָ and וַיֵּחַמְנָה in GEN 30:38; הַמְּקֻשָּׁרוֹת in GEN 30:41; לָהֶם in NUM 27:17; וַתִּהְיֶינָה in EZK 34:8; וּבִקַּרְתִּים in EZK 34:11). Frequently paired with בָּקָר 'cattle/herd' to denote total livestock wealth or sacrificial offerings (EXO 10:24, EXO 34:3, DEU 14:23, 2SA 12:2, 2CH 7:5, ECC 2:7). Common collocations include רֹעֵה צֹאן 'shepherd/herder' (GEN 4:2, GEN 46:34), הִשְׁקָה צֹאן 'to water the flock' (GEN 29:7, EXO 2:16), גִּדְרֹת צֹאן 'sheepfolds' (NUM 32:16), מִן הַצֹּאן 'from the flock' for sacrificial rams (LEV 5:25, EZK 43:25), and צֹאן מַרְעִית 'flock of pasture' in metaphors for God's people (PSA 74:1, PSA 100:3, JER 23:1, EZK 34:31). While encompassing both sheep and goats (GEN 31:10), in 1SA 25:2 צֹאן is listed alongside עִזִּים 'goats' and associated with shearing (גָּזַז), showing it can specifically highlight wool-bearing sheep.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The inner self of a person, functioning as the seat of thought, intention, emotion, courage, and moral or religious character.

senses.definition: The cognitive faculty or inner mind where thoughts arise, understanding takes place, realities are recalled, and silent self-speech occurs.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; object of verbs of cognition/motion (e.g., יָדַע עִם, הֵשִׁיב אֶל, עָלָה עַל) or locative prepositional phrase with verbs of thinking/speaking (אָמַר בְּ/לְ, חָשַׁב)

senses.definition: The seat of will, desire, purpose, and concealed intention, whether directed toward constructive plans, seeking God, obstinate resistance, or hidden malice.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; in prepositional phrases (בְּ, עִם) indicating what one intends, or direct object of verbs of directing/hardening (הֵכִין, אִמֵּץ)

senses.definition: The center of emotional states and morale, encompassing gladness, sorrow, dread, grudgingness, and courage or faintheartedness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; subject of stative/process verbs (יָטַב, רָעַע, מָסַס), head of construct chains of emotion (פַּחַד, שִׂמְחַת), or modified in construct/attribute phrases (רַךְ הַלֵּבָב)

senses.definition: The moral and spiritual core of a person scrutinized by God, representing sincerity, ethical integrity, or wholehearted religious loyalty versus stubbornness or wickedness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; modified by ethical/devotional adjectives (שָׁלֵם, עָרֵל), governed by כֹּל in בְּכָל לֵבָב, or construct with moral nouns (תֹּם, יֹשֶׁר, רֹעַ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in construct with moral/character nouns (תֹּם לֵבָב 'integrity of heart', יֹשֶׁר לֵבָב 'uprightness of heart', רֹעַ לֵבָב 'evil of heart') or in the emphatic devotion phrase בְּכָל לֵבָב 'with all the heart' (often paired with בְּכָל נַפְשְׁךָ in DEU 30:6). Common verbal idioms include הֵשִׁיב אֶל לֵבָב 'to recall to mind / reflect upon' (DEU 4:39), יָדַע עִם לֵבָב 'to recognize internally' (DEU 8:5), אָמַר בְּ/לְ לֵבָב 'to say to oneself / think' (JER 13:22, HOS 7:2, ZEP 2:15), הָיָה עִם לֵבָב 'to be one's intention' (2CH 6:8), מָסַס לֵבָב 'for courage to fail / melt' (DEU 20:8, JOS 5:1), יָטַב לֵבָב 'to be glad/content' (JDG 19:9), רַךְ לֵבָב 'timid/fainthearted' (DEU 20:8, 2CH 13:7), לֵבָב שָׁלֵם 'undivided/loyal heart' (1KI 11:4, 1KI 15:3, 2CH 19:9), and אִמֵּץ לֵבָב 'to harden one's resolve/will' (2CH 36:13). Parallel with נֶפֶשׁ 'soul/inner self' (PSA 13:3) and contrasted with outward speech or hands (כַּפַּיִם, GEN 20:5, PSA 28:3, PSA 73:13, PSA 78:72, LAM 3:41). In all 40 sampled verses, the noun refers to psychological, cognitive, volitional, or moral-spiritual faculties rather than the physical organ.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The God of Israel or a deity/idol in general, alongside two occurrences in the corpus of the homographic plural demonstrative "these" (הָאֵל).

senses.definition: The supreme God, YHWH, the God of Israel, referred to in narrative, prayer, wisdom discourse, and liturgical titles as creator, judge, and deliverer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, used absolutely, with definite article (הָאֵל), with 1cs suffix (אֵלִי), in construct or apposition with attributes/titles, and as vocative

senses.definition: A deity or god in a generic sense, including a fabricated idol or false object of worship, and in plural for other deities/gods.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun (including negated בְלֹא אֵל, object of יָצַר "fashion", and with כָּל־) and masculine plural (אֵלִים in DAN 11:36)

senses.definition: Near plural demonstrative determiner pointing out specific persons or nations already in view ("these"); homographic form grouped under this lemma in the corpus.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural demonstrative with prefixed definite article (הָאֵל) following and agreeing with a definite plural noun (הָאֲנָשִׁים הָאֵל, הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵל)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Predominantly refers to the God of Israel and frequently stands in poetic parallelism with יְהוָה, אֱלֹהִים, אֱלוֹהַּ, and שַׁדַּי (e.g., JOB 5:8, JOB 12:6, JOB 15:25, PSA 7:12, PSA 18:31, PSA 68:36). Forms numerous construct and appositional divine titles: אֵל עֶלְיוֹן (GEN 14:18), אֵל שַׁדַּי (GEN 35:11), אֵל רַחוּם / חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם (DEU 4:31, JON 4:2), אֵל דֵּעוֹת (1SA 2:3), אֵל־נְקָמוֹת (PSA 94:1), אֵל־הַכָּבוֹד (PSA 29:3), אֵל יִשְׂרָאֵל (PSA 68:36), הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ (ISA 5:16), הָאֵל יְהוָה (PSA 85:9), and אֵל אֵלִים (DAN 11:36). Note that two occurrences tagged under this lemma in the corpus (GEN 19:8, DEU 7:22) are instances of the homographic plural demonstrative determiner הָאֵל ("these") modifying definite plural nouns.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Loyal devotion, steadfast covenantal faithfulness, protective care, or personal favor shown between humans or by God toward people, with one rare proverbial occurrence denoting shameful or sinful conduct.

senses.definition: Faithful loyalty, dutiful kindness, or merciful treatment practiced between human beings—especially within kinship, friendship, diplomatic alliances, or just governance, as well as compassion toward the vulnerable.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; frequently object of עָשָׂה with עִם / אֶת / עַל (recipient) or with possessive suffix + אֶת; also in prepositional phrase בַּחֶסֶד (ISA 16:5)

senses.definition: Goodwill, gracious acceptance, or favorable standing granted to someone in the presence of a superior or royal official.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun as object of הִטָּה ("extend/incline") or נָשָׂא ("obtain/lift up") followed by לִפְנֵי ("before")

senses.definition: God's steadfast commitment, covenantal faithfulness, and protective, saving care toward his people or individuals; in the plural, concrete deeds or manifestations of such faithful care.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun (often with divine possessive suffix or in construct חֶסֶד יְהוָה, object of עָשָׂה / שָׁמַר, or in predicate לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ) and masculine plural (חֲסָדִים in PSA 25:6, ISA 63:7)

senses.definition: Disgrace, reproach, or misguided devotion—standing in syntactic antithesis to צְדָקָה ("righteousness" that exalts a nation) and predicated as חַטָּאת ("sin").
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun in construct (וְחֶסֶד לְאֻמִּים חַטָּאת) contrasting with צְדָקָה

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs as the object of עָשָׂה ("to do/show") with prepositions עִם, אֶת, or עַל to express reciprocal loyalty, covenantal obligation, or mercy toward another party (GEN 19:19, GEN 24:49, JDG 1:24, 1SA 20:8, 2SA 9:1, 1CH 19:2, PSA 109:16). Regularly paired with אֱמֶת ("truth/faithfulness", GEN 24:49, ISA 16:5), אֱמוּנָה ("faithfulness", PSA 89:25), בְּרִית ("covenant", 1KI 8:23), רַחֲמִים ("compassion/mercies", PSA 25:6, ISA 63:7, HOS 2:21), and צֶדֶק/מִשְׁפָּט ("righteousness/justice", HOS 2:21). Fixed liturgical and character formulas include כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ ("for his steadfast faithfulness endures forever", 2CH 7:6, PSA 118:2, PSA 136:1, PSA 136:8, PSA 136:14, PSA 136:20, PSA 136:26), עֹשֶׂה חֶסֶד לַאֲלָפִים (EXO 20:6, DEU 5:10, JER 32:18), and רַב־חֶסֶד (JOL 2:13). Appears in the plural (חֲסָדִים) for concrete deeds or expressions of care (PSA 25:6, ISA 63:7), and rarely with נָשָׂא or הִטָּה + לִפְנֵי for gaining favor before a ruler (EZR 7:28, EST 2:9). PRO 14:34 presents a striking contrastive usage where חֶסֶד of peoples is opposed to צְדָקָה ("righteousness") and equated with חַטָּאת ("sin").

entries.core_meaning_summary: An action, practice, labor, undertaking, or the resulting product, handiwork, or design made by God or humans.

senses.definition: An act, course of conduct, or customary practice carried out by humans, nations, or God, often evaluated morally or religiously.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, singular or plural, often in construct with an agent or with יָדַיִם

senses.definition: Daily toil, occupation, enterprise, or purposeful endeavor in which a person engages.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, singular or plural, frequently in construct with יָדַיִם or possessive suffix

senses.definition: The tangible yield or output of labor, such as agricultural harvest from the field or manufactured wares traded in commerce.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, plural with possessive suffix in agricultural or commercial contexts

senses.definition: A crafted object, architectural feature, or created thing, or the specialized manner and skill of its construction and design.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, usually singular construct before an artisan, material, style, or creator (or with כְּ indicating likeness of design)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very common in construct chains: מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַיִם ('work/deeds/handiwork of hands') denotes either human endeavor and moral deeds (DEU 14:29, JER 44:8), crafted idols and artifacts (ISA 17:8, ISA 37:19), or God's creative activity (PSA 102:26, ISA 64:7). Also frequent in technical descriptions of craftsmanship as מַעֲשֵׂה + artisan or material (e.g., מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב in EXO 28:15, מַעֲשֵׂה רֹקֵחַ in EXO 30:25, מַעֲשֵׂה רֶשֶׁת in EXO 27:4). Often contrasted with or paired with דְּרָכִים ('ways', JON 3:10), עֲבֹדָה ('service/work', ISA 28:21), and מַחְשָׁבוֹת ('plans', PRO 16:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To bring to mind, keep in attentive thought, or cause something or someone to be remembered, mentioned, or memorialized.

senses.definition: To call past events, deeds, people, or truths to conscious thought, or to retain them in memory so as to reflect upon them or act rightly in light of them.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), transitive with direct object or clause introduced by כִּי or interrogative

senses.definition: To take attentive notice of or remain mindful of a person, covenant, devotion, or offense in a way that leads to action (such as deliverance, favor, blessing, or reckoning guilt); often takes the preposition לְ for the beneficiary or affected party.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), transitive with direct object (person, covenant, offering, or sin) and optional לְ phrase

senses.definition: To speak aloud or bring up a phrase or formula in speech.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active), transitive with spoken expression as object

senses.definition: To be brought to mind or held in memory (such as being remembered before God for deliverance, or negatively, ceasing to be remembered among people); in one legal passage concerning firstborn livestock, the precise sense is uncertain.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (passive), intransitive with optional לִפְנֵי or locative phrase

senses.definition: To cause someone else to take notice of or remember a person, place, promise, or wrongdoing; to mention or call attention to.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative), transitive with direct object and optional אֶל phrase

senses.definition: To perform a liturgical or sacrificial act of memorializing, such as offering frankincense or using a psalm heading marked for remembrance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative), infinitive construct with לְ or participle with cultic substance

senses.definition: Used substantivally of a high royal official responsible for keeping records or bringing matters before the king.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative) participle functioning as a title noun

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with covenant (בְּרִית), steadfast love (חֶסֶד), and past wonders or sins. In Qal, the verb often carries pragmatic force beyond mental recall: when God remembers a person or covenant, deliverance or blessing follows (GEN 8:1, EXO 6:5, PSA 98:3), and with the preposition לְ it can mean taking account of something for someone's benefit (NEH 13:22) or holding past guilt against someone (PSA 79:8). Infinitive absolute + finite verb expresses emphatic admonition to remember (DEU 7:18). In EXO 34:19, the Niphal form תִּזָּכָר occurs in an obscure syntactic construction regarding firstborn livestock (possibly meaning 'be reckoned/claimed' or referring to male offspring). In Hiphil, the participle מַזְכִּיר functions as a royal administrative title ('recorder/remembrancer', 2SA 8:16), the infinitive לְהַזְכִּיר appears in psalm superscriptions with an unspecified liturgical role (PSA 38:1, PSA 70:1), and the participle with frankincense denotes a ritual memorial offering (ISA 66:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Masculine noun denoting the dark period between evening and morning, used both for a specific nocturnal span or time-setting and adverbially for actions taking place at night or continuously around the clock.

senses.definition: The nocturnal span of darkness between evening and dawn, regarded as a distinct division of the day, a counted temporal unit, or the time frame of an event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (masculine singular, plural לֵילוֹת), used with numerals, demonstratives (בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא / הַזֶּה), prepositions, or in construct chains

senses.definition: Designates the time during which an action occurs, either generally at night or specifically during the immediate upcoming night ('tonight').
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun used adverbially without a preposition (לַיְלָה or definite הַלַּיְלָה) modifying a verb of motion, lodging, or action

senses.definition: Paired with 'day' in a fixed merism expressing continuous, unbroken duration across the entire 24-hour cycle or the ordered cosmic alternation of light and dark.
senses.grammatical_frame: Coordinated adverbial pair יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה or לַיְלָה וְיוֹמָם

senses.definition: Darkness or obscurity used figuratively in poetry for confusion, distress, or concealment in contrast with light.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in similes (כַלַּיְלָה) or poetic parallelism with חֹשֶׁךְ ('darkness') and אוֹר ('light')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly appears with prepositions (בַּלַּיְלָה, עַד לָיְלָה, כַלַּיְלָה) and in construct expressions such as חֲלֹם הַלָּיְלָה ('dream of the night'), חֲצוֹת לָיְלָה ('midnight'), אַשְׁמוּרָה בַלָּיְלָה ('watch in the night'), and שׁוֹדְדֵי לָיְלָה ('plunderers of the night'). Plurals occur as לֵילוֹת (SNG 3:1). Frequently paired with יוֹם or יוֹמָם to express totality of time.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Feminine noun denoting physical soil or dirt, arable farmland and its produce, a people's territory or homeland, and the inhabited surface of the earth.

senses.definition: Physical earth, dirt, clay, or ground surface as a material substance or the terrain beneath one's feet.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine singular), often governed by prepositions (מִן, בְּ) or in construct (מַעֲבֵה הָאֲדָמָה)

senses.definition: Cultivable soil, farmland, or landed property that can be sown, bought, divided, and taxed, and that brings forth crops and vegetation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine singular), frequently with possessive pronominal suffixes or as direct object of verbs of sowing, buying, or dividing

senses.definition: A defined geographical region, territory, or homeland occupied by or promised to a nation or people, from which inhabitants may be exiled or to which they may return.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine singular), in construct with proper national names (e.g., אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל), with possessive suffixes, or modified by relative clauses of gift/inheritance

senses.definition: The surface of the habitable world as the realm where humanity and terrestrial creatures live and move.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine singular), characteristically in the prepositional phrase עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה ('on the face of the earth') or מֵעַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה

senses.definition: Proper name of a fortified town listed in a tribal territorial inventory.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun (toponym) in a list of town names

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears with the definite article or pronominal suffixes (e.g., אַדְמָתְךָ, אַדְמָתָם) and in construct chains such as פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה ('face of the ground/earth'), פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה ('produce of the soil'), and אַדְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל / אַדְמַת יְהוּדָה ('land of Israel/Judah'). Often paired or contrasted with אֶרֶץ ('earth/land') and שָׂדֶה ('field').

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be or become numerous, great, or extensive in number, quantity, or degree, and in the causative stem to make many, enlarge, or do something abundantly or repeatedly; also used in a fixed infinitive form for 'much/many' and once in connection with archery.

senses.definition: To become numerous, increase in number, volume, distance, or duration (used of living beings, floodwaters, a journey's distance, sorrows, and lifespan).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; intransitive with subject (people, animals, water, distance, days, sorrows)

senses.definition: To cause to increase in number, size, or degree; to multiply offspring, people, objects, actions, territory, honor, or events (sometimes with מִן for comparison, 'more than').
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem; transitive with direct object (or לְ + noun), optionally with מִן for comparison

senses.definition: To act abundantly, excessively, or repeatedly in performing the action of a companion verb.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem functioning adverbially before לְ + infinitive construct or a finite verb

senses.definition: Used as an indeclinable quantifier or adverbial modifier expressing a large quantity or high degree ("many," "much," "greatly," "exceedingly"), frequently intensified by מְאֹד.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative infinitive absolute (הַרְבֵּה) modifying a noun, clause, or verb

senses.definition: In a single occurrence paired with קַשָּׁת ("bowman/archer") in a wilderness setting, designating a shooter with a bow (or possibly one growing skilled as an archer); exact nuance within this lemma's range is context-dependent.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active participle (רֹבֶה) in construct with קַשָּׁת

entries.collocations_and_notes: Shows a clear stem distinction between the simple active stem (becoming numerous, increasing in number, quantity, or extent) and the causative stem (making numerous, enlarging, multiplying, or doing something abundantly). Frequently paired with פָּרָה ("to be fruitful," GEN 1:22; GEN 48:4; EZK 36:11) and contrasted with מָעַט ("to be few/diminish," NUM 33:54; JER 30:19). The causative infinitive absolute הַרְבֵּה is heavily grammaticalized as an adverb or quantifier ("much, many"), often reinforced by מְאֹד ("very," GEN 15:1; 2SA 12:2; 1KI 10:10; 1CH 20:2; 2CH 14:12; NEH 2:2). In GEN 21:20, the simple active participle רֹבֶה appears uniquely in construct with קַשָּׁת ("bowman/archer").

entries.core_meaning_summary: To consume liquid by drinking, whether literally for sustenance, festivity, or abstinence, or figuratively as experiencing divine judgment, violence, or nourishment.

senses.definition: To take a liquid (such as water, wine, milk, strong drink, or blood) into the mouth and swallow it, expressed with a direct object, partitive מִן, or a prepositional phrase marking the vessel or source.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; transitive with direct object, or with מִן / בְּ marking liquid, source, or vessel

senses.definition: To take liquid refreshment or partake in a meal or drinking banquet, commonly paired with eating (or negated with eating to indicate fasting); includes drinking by animals.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; intransitive or paired with eating, or infinitive with עִם (person)

senses.definition: Figuratively, to undergo or absorb an experience, especially to suffer divine wrath or judgment (often depicted as drinking a cup or wine), to incur violence, or (of trees) to draw up water as nourishment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem; with direct object (cup, violence, water) or מִן (wrath, wine)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with אָכַל ("to eat") in the narrative idiom "eat and drink" (e.g., GEN 25:34; EXO 24:11; JDG 19:21; 1KI 19:8; 2KI 6:23; ECC 3:13) and in negative pairings to describe fasting ("bread he did not eat and water he did not drink," DEU 9:9; EZR 10:6). Common objects include מַיִם ("water"), יַיִן ("wine"), and שֵׁכָר ("strong drink"). Takes מִן before the liquid (GEN 9:21), the vessel (2SA 12:3), or the water source (1KI 17:6), and בְּ before the drinking cup (GEN 44:5). Infinitive absolute + finite verb expresses certainty or inevitability (שָׁתוֹ יִשְׁתּוּ / שָׁתֹה תִשְׁתֶּה, JER 49:12). The active participle with a suffix (שֹׁתָיו, ISA 24:9) or in construct (שֹׁתֵי מָיִם, EZK 31:16) designates "drinkers (of)." All occurrences in the evidence packet appear in the simple active stem.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To leave, leave behind, abandon, neglect, or forsake a person, place, possession, relationship, or covenant allegiance in the simple active stem, and to be neglected or forsaken in the passive stem.

senses.definition: To depart from or leave behind a person, household, location, or possessions (including leaving objects behind when fleeing, withdrawing before an enemy, or leaving wealth at death).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with direct object (person, place, or object), sometimes with locative adverb or מִן ('from')

senses.definition: To leave behind resources for another's benefit, station someone at a post, or entrust dependents to another's care.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with direct object and לְ- ('for/to') marking the beneficiary or stationed party, or imperative entrusting dependents

senses.definition: To forsake, neglect, or withdraw care, protection, or loyalty from someone, or (in passive participial forms) to be left desolate, unprotected, or at large.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with person, life, or attribute (loyalty) as object, or Qal passive participle describing a desolate or unattended state

senses.definition: To forsake, reject, or turn away from God, his temple, covenant, or moral path, or conversely to give up and abandon idols or counsel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple stem (Qal), transitive with deity, covenant, temple, path, counsel, or idols as direct object

senses.definition: To be neglected, unattended, or forsaken (said of the house of God when its service and support were not maintained).
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive stem (Niphal), intransitive with inanimate subject (the house of God)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In GEN 2:24, leaving parents (עָזַב) is paired antonymically with clinging to a spouse (דָּבַק). In covenant and worship contexts, forsaking YHWH is repeatedly followed by serving or bowing down to foreign/other gods (JOS 24:16, JDG 10:6, 1KI 11:33, JER 5:19, JER 16:11) or breaking his covenant and failing to keep his instruction (DEU 31:16, 1KI 19:14, JER 16:11). In PSA 94:14, it stands in parallel with נָטַשׁ ("cast off"). Idiomatic usages include עָזַב חַסְדּוֹ אֶת ("withdraw/abandon steadfast loyalty toward," RUT 2:20) and the merism עָצוּר וְעָזוּב ("restrained and left-free/abandoned," i.e., all categories of people in Israel, 2KI 14:26) using the Qal passive participle.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To rescue, deliver, or snatch away from danger, oppression, or another's grasp in the active causative stem, and to be spared, escape, or free oneself in the passive/reflexive stem.

senses.definition: To rescue, deliver, or save a person, life, city, or people from enemies, violence, death, hardship, or moral/legal liability, often by intervening between contending parties or removing someone from another's control.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active causative stem (Hiphil), transitive with direct object (person, life, city, or people) and optional prepositional phrase with מִן ('from') or מִיַּד ('from the hand of')

senses.definition: To snatch away, reclaim, recover, or defend livestock, territory, captives, or prey from the possession or mouth of an adversary or predator.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active causative stem (Hiphil), transitive with direct object (livestock, territory, plot, or prey) and optional מִן / מִיַּד / מִפִּי ('from / from the hand of / from the mouth of')

senses.definition: To be delivered, spared, or snatched to safety from destruction or judgment, or reflexively to extricate and free oneself from an entanglement or obligation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal), intransitive, with optional instrumental phrase introduced by בְּ- ('by')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently constructed with מִיַּד ("from the hand/power of") or מִן ("from") to mark the source of danger or control (e.g., GEN 37:22, 2KI 18:34, JER 20:13). Emphatic infinitive-absolute + finite verb combinations occur in הַצֵּל לֹא הִצַּלְתָּ (EXO 5:23), הַצֵּל תַּצִּיל (1SA 30:8), and הַצֵּל יַצִּילֵנוּ (2KI 18:30, ISA 36:15). The participial phrase אֵין מַצִּיל ("there is no one to rescue/intervene") appears in 2SA 14:6 and DAN 8:4. Frequently paired or paralleled with verbs meaning "save" (הוֹשִׁיעַ, 1CH 11:14, PSA 7:2, ISA 19:20) and "deliver" (פִּלֵּט, PSA 22:9, PSA 82:4). EZK 14:16 and AMO 3:12 directly contrast the active causative stem (rescuing others / snatching prey) with the passive/reflexive stem (being spared / escaping). No simple active (Qal) forms occur in the evidence packet.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To lie down to rest or sleep, to lay or be laid down, to have sexual intercourse, or euphemistically to die and lie in death.

senses.definition: To recline horizontally, lie down to rest or sleep, or remain lying in a place or on a surface.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); intransitive, frequently with locative phrases (עַל, בְּ, שָׁם) or paired with verbs of sleeping

senses.definition: To force or gently place someone in a lying position, or passively to be laid down (including placing a corpse on a bed or among the dead).
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil, transitive with direct object) and causative passive stem (Hophal, passive with prepositional location)

senses.definition: To engage in sexual intercourse with someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); taking the partner with עִם or אֶת / direct object marker אֹת־

senses.definition: To die or rest in death and the grave, especially in the idiomatic expression of sleeping/lying with one's ancestors.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); intransitive, commonly with עִם־אֲבֹתָיו or locative phrases referring to dust or the underworld

entries.collocations_and_notes: The simple active stem (Qal) covers resting/lying down (1a), sexual intercourse (1c), and dying/resting in death (1d). In contrast, the causative active stem (Hiphil, 2SA 8:2; 2KI 4:21) means "cause to lie down / lay down," and the causative passive stem (Hophal, EZK 32:32) means "be laid down" (specifically among the dead). Common collocations include שָׁכַב עִם־אֲבֹתָיו ("lie down with one's ancestors") as a standard royal death formula, often followed by burial notices (e.g., 1KI 15:24; 2CH 16:13), and שָׁכַב עִם / אֶת for sexual relations.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To add something to an existing amount or group, increase, or do an action again, further, or no longer.

senses.definition: To add an amount, item, or quality to what already exists, or to cause something to increase in quantity or extent.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal) and causative active (Hiphil) stems; transitive with direct object (or object implied), often with עַל or אֶל marking the base to which addition is made

senses.definition: To be added to an existing group or portion, or to experience an increase.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal); intransitive, with עַל marking the recipient entity

senses.definition: To perform an action again, continue doing something, or do something further or more intensely; when negated, to stop doing something or never do it again.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active (Qal) and causative active (Hiphil) stems; auxiliary with infinitive construct (with or without לְ), coordinated finite verb, or standing elliptically, often modified by עוֹד or negated by לֹא/אַל

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently functions as an auxiliary verb governing an infinitive construct (with or without לְ) or a finite verb to express repetition ("again"), continuation, or intensification ("more"), very often paired with the adverb עוֹד ("again, still") and frequently negated with לֹא or אַל ("no longer, never again"). In 2SA 3:9 it appears in the oath formula כֹּה יַעֲשֶׂה אֱלֹהִים ... וְכֹה יֹסִיף לוֹ ("May God do so ... and do even more to him"). Both the simple active stem (Qal) and causative active stem (Hiphil) occur in both additive (1a) and auxiliary/continuative (1c) constructions without a sharp semantic difference in these forms, whereas the passive/reflexive stem (Niphal, NUM 36:3; PRO 11:24) expresses being added or increasing.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To have the ability, power, or permission to do something, or to prevail over, succeed against, or endure someone or something.

senses.definition: To possess the physical, mental, emotional, or circumstantial capacity or power to carry out an action or reach a state (most often negated to express impossibility or inability).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal; imperfect forms with u-stem vocalization) followed by an infinitive construct (usually with לְ-, occasionally bare).

senses.definition: When negated, to be prevented or forbidden from doing something by law, ritual restriction, a binding oath, or a divine command; not to be permitted or free to act.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) negated with לֹא + infinitive construct with לְ-, in legal, cultic, or vow-bound contexts.

senses.definition: To gain the upper hand, overcome an opponent, or succeed in accomplishing one's aim (or, when negated, to fail to succeed or overcome).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) used absolutely without a complementary infinitive (sometimes reinforced by an infinitive absolute), or with the preposition לְ- marking the opponent or target overcome.

senses.definition: To bear, withstand, or tolerate a person or overwhelming force (used negated to express inability to endure).
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) negated with לֹא, taking a direct object (אֹתוֹ) or used absolutely with a causal מִן-phrase.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears predominantly in negated clauses (with לֹא, or poetically בַּל in PSA 21:12). Simple active imperfect forms consistently exhibit u-vowel prefix vocalization (e.g., אוּכַל, תוּכַל, יוּכַל, נוּכַל). Frequently takes a complementary infinitive construct prefixed with לְ-, though bare infinitives also occur (DEU 1:9; ISA 47:11; JER 49:23). With infinitive absolute reinforcement (NUM 13:30; 1SA 26:25) or in absolute usage without an expressed infinitive (2KI 3:26; PSA 21:12; ISA 16:12; JER 20:7), it denotes prevailing or succeeding. With לְ- before a person (GEN 32:26; JER 1:19), it expresses overcoming an opponent.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The curved or flat inner surface of the hand (palm) or foot (sole), extending to the hand itself as an agent of action, grasp, gesture, or power, as well as hollow anatomical sockets and shallow dish-like vessels.

senses.definition: The palm or open inner surface of the hand, and by extension the hand itself as used for holding, working, gesturing (in prayer, clapping, or pledging), or as representing a person's moral deeds and innocence or guilt.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular, dual, or plural), often with pronominal suffixes or in construct with יָד ('hand'); frequently governed by prepositions בְּ-, עַל, or מֵעַל, or serving as direct object of gesture verbs (e.g., spread, lift, clap, strike, shake).

senses.definition: Figuratively, the grasp, control, power, or hostile reach of an agent, or a state of exposure and vulnerability when something is held in one's own hand.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, in construct before a human agent/enemy (especially with מִן 'from the grasp of') or with prepositional בְּ- indicating vulnerability.

senses.definition: The flat underside or sole of a human, animal, or visionary foot.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular or plural) in construct before רֶגֶל ('foot') or פַּעַם ('step/foot').

senses.definition: The hollow or socket of the thigh/hip joint.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in construct before יֶרֶךְ ('thigh/hip').

senses.definition: A measure of capacity equivalent to what an open palm or single hand can hold; a handful.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun following מְלֹא ('fullness of').

senses.definition: A shallow, palm-shaped metal dish, pan, or ladle used in sanctuary and temple service to hold incense or offerings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular or plural כַּפּוֹת), modified by material (gold, silver), weight, or contents (incense).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly paired or paralleled with יָד ('hand') in expressions of power, deliverance, or craftsmanship (e.g., EXO 4:4; ISA 62:3; PSA 18:1). Frequent fixed idioms include: כַּף רֶגֶל ('sole of the foot', e.g., GEN 8:9; JOS 3:13; EZK 1:7) and מִכַּף רַגְלוֹ וְעַד קָדְקֳדוֹ ('from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head' for the whole body, 2SA 14:25); תַּחַת כַּפּוֹת רַגְלַי ('under the soles of my feet' for subjugation, 1KI 5:17); פָּרַשׂ כַּפַּיִם / נָשָׂא כַפַּיִם ('spread out / lift up the palms' in prayer, 1KI 8:54; 2CH 6:12; PSA 63:5); מָחָא כָף / הִכָּה כַף אֶל כָּף ('clap the palms / strike palm against palm', ISA 55:12; EZK 21:19); תָּקַע כַּף ('strike the palm' to make a pledge/surety, PRO 6:1); נַפְשִׁי בְכַפִּי ('my life is in my palm' for constant peril, PSA 119:109); and מְלֹא כַף ('handful/palm-full', ECC 4:6). Dual and plural forms alternate between כַּפַּיִם (paired hands) and כַּפּוֹת (soles, cut-off hands, or cultic dishes).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A friend, close companion, neighbor, or fellow member of a community, also functioning idiomatically with 'man/each' to express reciprocity.

senses.definition: A personal friend, trusted confidant, or close companion, ranging from a royal or social associate to a cherished beloved.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural רֵעִים), often with possessive suffixes or in construct with a personal name

senses.definition: Another person within one's social, occupational, or covenant community—a neighbor, peer, or fellow citizen—in legal, ethical, and everyday interactions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun with singular pronominal suffixes (רֵעֲךָ, רֵעֵהוּ) governed by verbs of action, speech, lending, or injury, or in construct (e.g., אֵשֶׁת רֵעֵהוּ, 'his neighbor's wife')

senses.definition: Each other or one another, expressing reciprocal action or relation between members of a group.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun with 3rd-person suffix (רֵעֵהוּ) paired idiomatically with אִישׁ ('each one') and a linking preposition (אֶל, לְ-, בְּ-, אֵת, מֵאֵת)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very commonly occurs with a pronominal suffix (especially רֵעֵהוּ 'his neighbor/fellow' and רֵעֲךָ 'your neighbor/fellow'). Frequently paired with אָח ('brother/kinsman') in DEU 15:2, ISA 41:6, JER 34:17, with קָרֹב ('near one/neighbor') in PSA 15:3, and with שָׁכֵן ('neighbor/resident nearby') in JER 6:21. In SNG 5:16, רֵעִי ('my friend') stands in direct poetic parallelism with דוֹדִי ('my beloved') as an affectionate title for a romantic partner. In reciprocal idioms with אִישׁ ('each person'), the prepositions אֶל, לְ-, בְּ-, אֵת, and מֵאֵת specify directionality or opposition ('to/for/against/from one another').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A four-footed land animal, encompassing domesticated livestock, riding beasts, wild or scavenging quadrupeds, and non-human animals broadly.

senses.definition: Domesticated herd or farm animals—such as cattle and sheep/goats—that are owned, pastured, kept in stalls, sacrificed, eaten, or taken as spoil in war.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular collective noun, often with possessive suffixes (e.g., בְּהֶמְתּוֹ), in construct with owners, or expanded by cattle and flocks

senses.definition: An individual pack or riding animal used as a mount by a traveler.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun serving as antecedent to רֹכֵב בָּהּ ('riding upon it')

senses.definition: Land animals or quadrupeds considered broadly as a biological or legal category distinct from humankind, birds, fish, and creeping things, whether ritually clean or unclean.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular collective noun, frequently coordinated with אָדָם ('humankind') or contrasted with עוֹף ('birds'), רֶמֶשׂ ('creeping things'), and דָּגִים ('fish')

senses.definition: Wild land animals, including predators and scavenging beasts that feed on unburied corpses.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular collective noun, frequently in the construct phrase בֶּהֱמַת הָאָרֶץ ('beasts of the earth') or in partitive בַּבְּהֵמָה ('among the beasts')

senses.definition: Beasts used figuratively as a standard of comparison for people regarded as unreasoning, contemptible, or mortal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular or plural (בְּהֵמוֹת) governed by the comparative preposition כְּ- ('like/as')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in merism or coordination with אָדָם ('humankind'), e.g., בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה ('both human and animal') or מֵאָדָם עַד בְּהֵמָה ('from human to beast'), to encompass all earthly life or objects of judgment/blessing (EXO 9:9, EXO 11:5, NUM 18:15, PSA 135:8, JER 31:27, EZK 14:13, JON 3:7). Commonly occurs in the construct phrase בֶּהֱמַת הָאָרֶץ ('beasts of the earth') for scavenging or wild animals alongside עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם ('birds of the sky') (DEU 28:26, ISA 18:6, JER 16:4, JER 34:20). Classified ritually as טְהוֹרָה ('clean') vs. טְמֵאָה ('unclean') (GEN 7:8, LEV 20:25, LEV 27:11). In JON 3:7, הַבְּהֵמָה is immediately appositionally specified as הַבָּקָר וְהַצֹּאן ('the cattle and the flock'). The plural בְּהֵמוֹת appears in PSA 49:21 in a simile for mortal humans lacking understanding.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To perish, vanish, be lost, or go astray in the simple active stem, and to destroy, exterminate, or wipe out in the intensive and causative stems.

senses.definition: Of people, nations, or cities: to die, be destroyed, be wiped out, or suffer total ruin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal), intransitive; subject is persons, peoples, or a city

senses.definition: Of objects, wealth, refuge, memory, counsel, hope, or prophetic visions: to disappear, fail, be lost, or come to nothing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal), intransitive; subject is concrete possessions or abstract states/capacities (often with מִן indicating from whom something vanishes)

senses.definition: As a participle describing straying livestock or a displaced person: to wander lost, go astray, or be in peril of perishing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) participle used substantively or attributively

senses.definition: To destroy, annihilate, or wipe out people, cultic objects and sites, memory, or loud noise.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive active stem (Piel), transitive; takes a direct object (people, idols, shrines, memory, or sound)

senses.definition: To cause to perish, eliminate, or destroy enemies, nations, or military equipment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil), transitive; takes a direct object (adversaries, nations, or chariots)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of dying, ending, or destroying such as גָּוַע (NUM 17:27), כָּלָה (JOB 4:9; PSA 37:20), שָׁמַד (NUM 33:52; EST 3:13; ISA 26:14), הָרַג (EST 3:13; EST 9:12), and כָּרַת (MIC 5:9). Often occurs with abstract subjects like מָנוֹס ("escape/refuge," JOB 11:20; JER 25:35; AMO 2:14) and תִּקְוָה ("hope," PRO 11:7). In DEU 26:5, אֲרַמִּי אֹבֵד אָבִי may describe an ancestor either as "wandering/homeless" or as "perishing/in mortal danger." Across stems, the simple active (Qal) is intransitive ("perish, be lost"), whereas both the intensive active (Piel) and causative active (Hiphil) are transitive ("destroy, wipe out").

entries.core_meaning_summary: Collective noun referring to large domestic bovine livestock—cattle and oxen—used for agriculture, wealth, food, sacrifice, and also depicted in temple metalwork.

senses.definition: Large domestic bovine animals (cattle, oxen, cows) viewed collectively as herds or property, or counted individually with numerals, used for grazing, pulling carts or yokes, meat, and sacrificial offerings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Collective masculine singular noun (often paired with צֹאן; occasionally counted directly with numerals or used after צֶמֶד)

senses.definition: The cattle herd or bovine species designated as the source of an individual young animal (calf or young bull) prepared as a meal or offered in sacrifice.
glosses: cattle (in "young bull / calf of the herd")
senses.grammatical_frame: Genitive noun in construct phrases בֶּן־בָּקָר / בֶּן־הַבָּקָר (often following פַּר / פָּרִים)

senses.definition: Sculpted or engraved representations of oxen or cattle forming decorative panels or supporting bronze furnishings in the temple.
senses.grammatical_frame: Collective noun referring to artistic or bronze figures

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very frequently paired with צֹאן ("flocks / sheep and goats") to designate total livestock holdings or sacrificial animals (e.g., GEN 12:16; EXO 20:24; DEU 16:2; HOS 5:6). Appears with צֶמֶד ("yoke / pair") for draft teams (1SA 11:7; JOB 42:12). Although grammatically singular and usually collective, it is occasionally counted directly with numerals (NUM 7:7; NUM 7:23). In construct after בֶּן/בְּנֵי and often following פַּר/פָּרִים, it identifies a young bovine for food or sacrifice (GEN 18:8; LEV 4:14; NUM 28:19).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A slaughtered animal sacrifice offered to a deity (typically involving a shared meal), a meat-feast, figuratively a spiritual offering, and also a Midianite king's personal name.

senses.definition: A slaughtered animal offering presented to YHWH or another deity, distinguished from a whole burnt offering in that its blood and fat belong to the altar while its flesh is typically eaten by worshippers or priests; includes peace-offerings and thanksgiving offerings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, singular or plural, frequently in construct with šĕlāmîm or tôḏāh, and often paired with ʿōlāh or minḥāh

senses.definition: A communal or household feast of slaughtered meat, whether a covenant or family sacrificial meal or a banquet contrasted with simple food.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, absolute or in construct (e.g., zeḇaḥ mišpāḥāh "family feast", ziḇḥê rîḇ "feasts of strife")

senses.definition: Figuratively, an inner disposition of humility and contrition presented as an offering acceptable to God.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural construct (ziḇḥê ʾĕlōhîm) equated with "a broken spirit"

senses.definition: Zebah, one of the two kings of Midian pursued and captured alongside Zalmunna.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper personal noun, always paired with Zalmunna

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently serves as the cognate object of the verb zāḇaḥ ("to sacrifice a sacrifice": GEN 31:54, LEV 17:7, LEV 22:29, JDG 16:23, 2CH 7:5, 2CH 30:22, PSA 27:6, PSA 107:22, EZK 20:28). Commonly paired with ʿōlāh ("burnt offering") and minḥāh ("grain/tribute offering"). Recurrent construct phrases include zeḇaḥ (haš)šĕlāmîm ("sacrifice of peace-offerings"), zeḇaḥ tôḏāh / ziḇḥê tôḏāh ("sacrifice(s) of thanksgiving"), and ziḇḥê tĕrûʿāh ("sacrifices of joyful shouting"). Plural is normally masculine (-îm / -ê), though a feminine-like plural ending occurs in HOS 4:19 (mizziḇḥôṯām). In JDG 8:5, 12 the identical form functions as the proper name of a Midianite king.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To ask a question, seek information or divine counsel, request something, wish well, or borrow (and in the causative stem, lend or hand over).

senses.definition: To put a question to someone, inquire about a matter, or interrogate in order to learn information or gain counsel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb, often with direct object (person asked) and direct speech (with or without lēʾmōr), or with lĕ- / ʿal marking the topic; intensive/iterative stem paired with simple active infinitive absolute and bĕ- + place for customary inquiry (2SA 20:18)

senses.definition: To consult YHWH, God, or a divinatory object in order to obtain an oracle, decision, or guidance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb + bĕ- (deity or divinatory object), sometimes with lĕ- (beneficiary) and direct speech

senses.definition: To ask for, desire, request, or demand a thing, favor, permission, or requirement from someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb + direct object (thing requested), optionally with min (source) or lĕ- (beneficiary); passive/reflexive stem with min + person and lĕ- + infinitive for earnestly asking leave for oneself (1SA 20:6)

senses.definition: To inquire after or pray for the peace and well-being of a person or city.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb + lĕ- (person) + lĕ-šālôm, or + construct phrase šĕlôm + noun

senses.definition: To ask for the temporary use of items from others; to borrow.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb + direct object (items) + lĕ- (for oneself) + mēʾēṯ (from neighbors)

senses.definition: In the causative stem, to hand over, lend, or dedicate someone upon request; in the simple passive participle, to be lent or dedicated.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem + direct object + lĕ- (recipient); simple passive participle + lĕ-

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently introduces direct questions with lēʾmōr ("saying"). Often forms the figura etymologica with the simple active infinitive absolute + finite verb (1SA 20:6 in the passive/reflexive stem; 2SA 20:18 in the intensive stem). Common collocations include šāʾal bĕ- + divine name or cult object ("inquire of a deity"), šāʾal lĕ- + šālôm / šĕlôm ("ask after/pray for the well-being of"), and šāʾal lĕ- + person ("request for oneself/another"). Stem distinctions observed: the simple active stem covers asking, consulting, requesting, and borrowing, while its passive participle (1SA 1:28) denotes one handed over upon request; the passive/reflexive stem (1SA 20:6) expresses earnestly asking permission for oneself; the intensive/iterative stem (2SA 20:18) expresses customary inquiry for counsel at a place; and the causative stem (1SA 1:28) means to grant, lend, or hand over someone to another.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A verb denoting both the physical or figurative breaking, shattering, and bringing to ruin of objects, bodies, and powers, and, in commercial contexts, the buying or selling of grain and food provisions.

senses.definition: To fracture, smash, snap, or wreck a solid object or structure such as a door, bone, earthenware vessel, yoke-bar, or ship.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), transitive with direct object (or marked with אֶת)

senses.definition: To smash completely or shatter into pieces durable, plural, or formidable objects such as stone tablets, sacred pillars, altars, idols, bronze fixtures, teeth, ships, or trees.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive active stem (Piel), transitive with direct object

senses.definition: To suffer breaking, cracking, or wrecking, used of ships, bones, leaking cisterns, city gate-bars, idols, tree boughs, or a limb.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/middle stem (Niphal), intransitive with affected entity as subject

senses.definition: To cut off sustenance or bring a person, ruler, or nation to ruin and defeat (basic active stem), or to be crushed and ruined beyond recovery (passive/middle stem).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), transitive with 'staff of bread' or personal object; or passive/middle stem (Niphal), intransitive with personal/collective subject

senses.definition: To purchase grain, food, or basic drink provisions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), transitive with grain, food, or drink as direct object, or absolute

senses.definition: To sell or supply grain for payment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil), transitive with grain (שֶׁבֶר) as direct object

entries.collocations_and_notes: Two sharply distinct semantic fields appear under this lemma in the corpus: (1) physical or figurative breaking/shattering (Senses 1a–1d), and (2) commercial trading in grain and provisions (Senses 2a–2b). Within the breaking senses, the basic active stem (Qal) typically takes individual objects (a door, a bone, a pottery vessel, a yoke-bar, a ship) or marks food-supply disruption (בְּשִׁבְרִי ... מַטֵּה־לֶחֶם, LEV 26:26), while the intensive active stem (Piel) characteristically describes violent or total shattering of durable, plural, or formidable targets (stone tablets, cultic pillars, altars, images, bronze temple fixtures, teeth/fangs, ships, trees, sea-monster heads, bones). In commercial contexts, the basic active stem (Qal) collocates with בָּר ('grain', GEN 42:3) and אֹכֶל ('food', GEN 42:10; GEN 43:22) for buying, whereas the causative stem (Hiphil) takes שֶׁבֶר ('grain', AMO 8:5) in parallel with opening wheat stores for selling.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A focusing and qualifying particle that restricts an assertion to a single item or condition, contrasts or limits a preceding statement, confirms the certainty of a declaration, or marks immediate temporal completion.

senses.definition: Marks the following word, phrase, or clause as the sole exception, condition, extent, or characteristic, excluding everything else.
senses.grammatical_frame: Restrictive particle preceding a noun phrase, prepositional phrase, number, or clause

senses.definition: Introduces a qualification, exception, or contrast against a preceding command, rule, or situation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial adversative particle contrasting with a preceding clause

senses.definition: Reinforces the truth, certainty, or intensity of an assertion, exclamation, or exhortation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Asseverative particle preceding a verbal or nominal clause, imperative, or infinitive absolute construction

senses.definition: Marks an action as having taken place immediately prior to the following event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Temporal adverbial particle preceding an infinitive absolute and finite verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently stands at the beginning of a clause or immediately before the focused constituent (such as a noun phrase, prepositional phrase, or verb). Common collocations include אַךְ הַפַּעַם ('just this once', GEN 18:32), אַךְ בְּזֹאת ('only on this condition', GEN 34:22), אַךְ דָּבָר אֶחָד ('only one thing', 2SA 3:13), אַךְ שְׁתַּיִם ('only two things', JOB 13:20), and כִּי אַךְ ('for surely', 2KI 5:7). Repeated in parallel poetic lines for rhetorical emphasis in PSA 39:7, PSA 58:12, PRO 21:5, and JER 32:30. In JDG 7:19, it precedes an infinitive absolute paired with a finite verb (אַךְ הָקֵם הֵקִימוּ) to mark an action just completed.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The cessation of physical life (dying), lethal danger or execution, and poetically the personified power or realm of the dead.

senses.definition: The end or cessation of biological life, whether referring to a specific individual's dying or death in general as the opposite of life (including plural construct מוֹתֵי in EZK 28:10).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (absolute, construct מוֹת/מוֹתֵי, with suffixes, or in temporal phrases with בְּ, עַד, אַחֲרֵי, לִפְנֵי)

senses.definition: A fatal danger, deadly plague, lethal blow, or judicial capital penalty (including idioms for a death sentence or deserving to die).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (absolute or in construct expressions such as בֶּן מָוֶת, מִשְׁפַּט מָוֶת, כְּלֵי מָוֶת, הֲרֻגֵי מָוֶת)

senses.definition: Death personified as an active power or figure, or conceived as an underworld realm/abode parallel to Sheol or Abaddon.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (subject of verbs, addressee, or construct expressions such as חַדְרֵי מָוֶת, חֶבְלֵי מָוֶת, מִשְׁבְּרֵי מָוֶת)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Common construct expressions include יוֹם מוֹתוֹ (the day of his death, GEN 27:2, 1SA 15:35, 2CH 26:21, JER 52:34), אַחֲרֵי מוֹת (after the death of, 2SA 1:1, 2KI 1:1, 2KI 14:17, 2CH 22:4), עַד מוֹת (until the death of, NUM 35:32, JOS 20:6), לִפְנֵי מוֹתוֹ (before his death, DEU 33:1), בֶּן מָוֶת (son of death = one deserving death, 2SA 12:5), מִשְׁפַּט מָוֶת (death sentence, JER 26:16), כְּלֵי מָוֶת (deadly weapons, PSA 7:14), דַּרְכֵי מָוֶת (ways of death, PRO 14:12, PRO 16:25), חַדְרֵי מָוֶת (chambers of death, PRO 7:27), חֶבְלֵי מָוֶת (cords of death, PSA 18:5), and מִשְׁבְּרֵי מָוֶת (breakers of death, 2SA 22:5). Plural construct מוֹתֵי appears as a cognate accusative with מוּת in EZK 28:10, and the poetic form הַמָּוְתָה occurs in PSA 116:15. Frequently contrasted with חַיִּים (life, DEU 30:15, JER 8:3) and paired in parallelism with שְׁאוֹל (Sheol, PSA 89:49, PRO 7:27, ISA 28:18, HOS 13:14) or אֲבַדּוֹן (Abaddon, JOB 28:22).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To move or extend around something in a circle, surround or go about a place, turn in a different direction, or cause something to turn, move, or change.

senses.definition: To move, curve, stand, or extend in a circuit around an object, region, or person (active in the basic stem and intensive stem; intransitive or with direct object in the passive/reflexive stem for borders).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stem (Qal), passive/reflexive stem (Niphal), or intensive stem (Poel); intransitive or + direct object (אֶת / suffix)

senses.definition: To close in on, march around, besiege, or beset a city, dwelling, or person in hostility or threat (observed in the basic stem and once in the passive/reflexive stem in JDG 19:22).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stem (Qal) or passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) + direct object (אֶת / suffix)

senses.definition: To travel or circulate through a city or region, making rounds or patrolling.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stem (Qal) + בְּ (in/throughout)

senses.definition: To change direction or orientation: turn aside, turn back, dodge, return to a place, or turn again to perform a subsequent action (passive/reflexive stem in Ezekiel describes not swerving from a straight course).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stem (Qal) or passive/reflexive stem (Niphal); intransitive, often + אֶל, מִן, לְאָחוֹר, or coordinated with another verb

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to turn, move to another place, roll, or be redirected (including turning one's face toward or away, diverting troops, or inclining a ruler's heart); passive-causative in ISA 28:27 of rolling a cartwheel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) + direct object (or intransitive military maneuver + מֵעַל); passive-causative stem (Hophal) in ISA 28:27

senses.definition: To pass over or transfer from one party to another (basic stem), bring about an outcome (basic stem + בְּ), or alter a name (causative and passive-causative stems).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic stem (Qal) + מִן...לְ or + בְּ; causative stem (Hiphil) or passive-causative stem (Hophal) with שֵׁם

entries.collocations_and_notes: Across stems: the basic active stem (Qal) expresses going around, surrounding, patrolling, turning, or transferring; the passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) expresses curving or turning (e.g., borders, moving figures) as well as surrounding an object (JDG 19:22); the intensive-stem pattern (Poel) highlights continuous encompassing or ritual procession (PSA 26:6, JON 2:4) and appears in the poetic statement "a female shall encompass a man" (JER 31:22, contrasted with turning away); the causative stem (Hiphil) expresses turning/redirecting someone or something (e.g., turning one's face, moving an object, changing a name or heart), with the passive-causative (Hophal) denoting a wheel rolled over grain (ISA 28:27) or names being changed (NUM 32:38). Common collocations include + אֶת (direct object) for encircling a place/person, + אֶל/מִן for turning toward or away from, + בְּ for going about within a region (2CH 17:9, SNG 3:3), סָבַב פָּנִים (turn the face, 1KI 8:14, 2CH 29:6), סָבַב שֵׁם (change a name, NUM 32:38, 2KI 24:17), and coordination with a second finite verb to mean "do again" (PSA 71:21). Frequently paired or paralleled with הִקִּיף (surround, JOS 6:3, 2CH 4:3) and סָבִיב (around, 2CH 4:3, ECC 1:6).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Ordinal adjective and adverb indicating second position in a sequence, the counterpart in a pair, or the repetition of an action a second time.

senses.definition: Occupying position two in a chronological, genealogical, spatial, or organizational sequence (such as days, months, years, sons, architectural stories, wall sections, or marching divisions).
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive or predicative ordinal adjective (masc. sg./pl., fem. sg.), or substantivized with the definite article

senses.definition: Designating the counterpart or remaining member of a pair, or a companion/additional person in contrast to a single individual (ECC 4:8).
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive ordinal adjective or substantive, usually paired with אֶחָד ("one") or negated with אֵין ("there is no")

senses.definition: Indicating that an action or event takes place once more after a prior occurrence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular שֵׁנִית functioning adverbially to modify a verbal clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted with אֶחָד ("the one ... the second/other") in paired items or measurements (EXO 26:5, EXO 29:39, EXO 37:18, NUM 11:26, 1KI 6:26, 1KI 7:15) and continued in sequences with שְׁלִישִׁי ("third": GEN 6:16, 1CH 8:39, 1CH 26:2, ISA 37:30). Common in calendrical expressions such as בַּיּוֹם הַשֵּׁנִי ("on the second day"), בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי ("in the second month"), and בַּשָּׁנָה הַשֵּׁנִית ("in the second year"). Shows masculine singular שֵׁנִי, feminine singular שֵׁנִית, and masculine plural שְׁנִיִּם (GEN 6:16, NUM 2:16); in NEH 3:30 מִדָּה שֵׁנִי appears alongside מִדָּה שֵׁנִית in NEH 3:20. The feminine singular שֵׁנִית regularly serves adverbially for repeated actions ("a second time").

entries.core_meaning_summary: Verb denoting experiencing or expressing gladness, delight, or malicious gloating in the simple active stem, and causing someone or something to be glad in the causative stem.

senses.definition: To feel or express gladness, joy, or contentment over favorable events, worship, deliverance, God's character, or ordinary life blessings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active): intransitive; used absolutely or with בְּ (source/sphere), עַל (occasion), לִפְנֵי (before YHWH), כִּי/לְמַעַן (reason), or cognate accusative שִׂמְחָה

senses.definition: To take malicious delight or exult over another's downfall, ruin, or misfortune.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (simple active): intransitive with לְ or אֶל marking the victim, or absolute in contexts of hostile mockery

senses.definition: To cause a person, community, heart, or soul to experience joy or gladness, or (with לְ of the victim in PSA 30:2) to allow enemies to gloat over someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (causative): transitive with direct object (person, city, לֵב, or נֶפֶשׁ), optionally with בְּ (instrument/place) or cognate accusative שִׂמְחָה

entries.collocations_and_notes: In the Qal (simple active), frequently paired with other verbs of rejoicing and praise such as גִּיל ("rejoice"), שׂוּשׂ ("exult"), רָנַן ("shout for joy"), and עָלַץ/עָלַז ("exult": JOB 3:22, PSA 14:7, PSA 35:27, PSA 68:4, JER 50:11, JOL 2:21, ZEC 2:14). Often takes בְּ to mark the sphere or source of gladness (e.g., בַּיהוָה, בֵּאלֹהִים, בְּחַגֶּךָ, בְּלִבּוֹ), לִפְנֵי יְהוָה in cultic settings (DEU 12:12, PSA 68:4), כִּי for the reason of joy, and occasionally the cognate accusative שִׂמְחָה (JON 4:6). In Ecclesiastes, appears in the refrain לֶאֱכוֹל וְלִשְׁתּוֹת וְלִשְׂמוֹחַ ("to eat, drink, and enjoy oneself": ECC 8:15; cf. ECC 3:12, ECC 11:9). The Piel (causative) contrasts clearly with the Qal by taking a direct object (people, heart, soul, or city) to express causing joy, and in PSA 30:2 takes לְ to indicate allowing enemies to gloat over the speaker.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A verb used primarily in the intensive, passive, and reflexive stems meaning to cover over physically (with water, clouds, garments, or coverings), to clothe oneself, or figuratively to overwhelm, conceal, or overlook wrongs.

senses.definition: To place or spread something over a person, body part, structure, pit, or terrain so as to enclose, shield, adorn, or submerge it; in passive stems (Pual, Niphal), to be covered over or submerged.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive (Piel) + direct object (or ʿal); Passive intensive (Pual) and Passive simple (Niphal) with covered entity as subject

senses.definition: To dress or wrap another person in clothing, or (with an omitted reflexive object in the intensive stem, or in the reflexive intensive stem) to put on a garment or sackcloth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive (Piel) + direct object of person or garment (or bĕ- + garment); Reflexive intensive (Hithpael) + bĕ- + sackcloth

senses.definition: To overtake or overwhelm a person completely with dread, horror, or the violent consequences of wrongdoing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive (Piel) with abstract emotion or violence as subject + direct object of person

senses.definition: To withhold knowledge of an action from someone, keep hostile feelings secret, or conceal one's sins rather than confessing them.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive (Piel) + direct object of deed, emotion, or sin (+ min- 'from' someone)

senses.definition: To cover over an offense so as to pardon sin (by God) or foster reconciliation rather than broadcasting a fault (in human relations).
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive (Piel) + direct object (pešaʿ 'transgression', ḥaṭṭāʾt 'sin')

entries.collocations_and_notes: In the sampled corpus, the verb occurs predominantly in the active intensive stem (Piel), alongside passive intensive (Pual: GEN 7:19; EZK 41:16), passive simple (Niphal: JER 51:42), and reflexive intensive (Hithpael: 2KI 19:1; ISA 37:2); no simple active (Qal) occurrences appear in the sample. Frequently collocates with water, clouds, darkness, fat, or garments/sackcloth (śaq, beged, kĕsût), and in PRO 17:9; 28:13; PSA 32:5; 85:3 with pešaʿ, ʿāwōn, or ḥaṭṭāʾt (contrasted with môdeh 'confessing' in PRO 28:13 and paired with nāśāʾ 'forgive' in PSA 85:3).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A relational preposition and spatial term denoting position directly opposite, facing, or in front of someone or something, extending to presence before witnesses or in one's sight/awareness, as well as distance away from or correspondence to.

senses.definition: Positioned directly across from, facing, or physically in front of a person, object, or architectural feature.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition neged or lĕ-neged + noun or pronominal suffix

senses.definition: In the physical presence, direct sight, or public witness of a person, assembly, or deity, including legal testimony, worship, or conduct observed by others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition neged or lĕ-neged + person, divine name, or ʿênayim ('eyes')

senses.definition: Kept continually before one's mind, attention, or regard.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition lĕ-neged + pronominal suffix (with abstract nouns or offerings as subject)

senses.definition: Positioned at a distance opposite something, or separated and removed away from someone's presence or line of sight.
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound preposition min-neged (+ noun, lĕ-, or pĕnê / ʿênayim)

senses.definition: Matching or corresponding to someone as a suitable counterpart.
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound preposition kĕ-neged + pronominal suffix

senses.definition: Assigned over, attending to, or positioned in charge of a sphere of service or work.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition lĕ-neged + noun phrase denoting work or task

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently combines with prepositions: lĕ-neged (often interchangeable with bare neged for 'in front of, before, in the sight of', and in NEH 11:22 for oversight over work), min-neged ('at a distance opposite' or 'away from the presence/sight of'), and kĕ-neged ('corresponding to', GEN 2:18). Common collocations include lĕ-neged ʿênê / min-neged ʿênê ('before the eyes of' / 'out of the sight of', PSA 5:6; 36:2; ISA 1:16; JER 16:17; AMO 9:3) and public or legal witness formulas (neged hazzĕqēnîm, neged YHWH, RUT 4:4; 1SA 12:3). In 2CH 6:12 it appears alongside lipnê ('before').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A verb denoting physical touching or contact (often with ritual effect), forceful striking or affliction in the simple active stem, and bringing into contact, extending to a limit, or arriving in the causative stem.

senses.definition: To make physical contact with a person, object, or surface, including contact that transmits ritual impurity or holiness, or spatial contact between adjacent structures.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) + preposition בְּ-, עַל, or אֶל introducing the object touched

senses.definition: To strike forcefully, harm, or afflict with suffering or calamity; in the passive participle, to be stricken or afflicted.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) + preposition בְּ- or עַד; also passive participle (נָגוּעַ) without preposition

senses.definition: To cause something to touch a target, or to bring or cast a structure down into contact with the ground.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) with explicit or implied direct object + preposition עַל, לְ-, or אֶל

senses.definition: To extend as far as or reach up to a spatial boundary, height, or extreme degree.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) used intransitively + preposition לְ- or עַד לְ-

senses.definition: To arrive at a place or appointed turn in time, or (of events and outcomes) to come upon or befall someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil) used intransitively, either absolute or + preposition אֶל

entries.collocations_and_notes: In the simple active stem (Qal), the target is most often introduced by the preposition בְּ-, and occasionally by עַל (ISA 6:7, DAN 10:16), עַד (JOB 4:5, JER 4:18), or אֶל (1KI 6:27); in ritual legislation it frequently marks contact that transmits impurity or holiness. In 2SA 5:8, the verb governs בַּצִּנּוֹר in an obscure military instruction where the sense is physical reaching or striking. In the causative stem (Hiphil), it exhibits both transitive causative usage (bringing an object into contact or casting down to the ground) and intransitive usage (reaching a limit, arriving at a place or time, or befalling someone, governed by לְ-, עַד לְ-, אֶל, or absolute).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A grammatically plural noun denoting physical vitality and mortal existence, the temporal span of a lifetime, and flourishing or well-being.

senses.definition: Physical vitality, animating breath, or continued mortal existence as opposed to death or destruction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (absolute, construct, or with pronominal suffixes); object of verbs of saving, loathing, or choosing, or in construct (e.g., נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים, דֶּרֶךְ הַחַיִּים)

senses.definition: The temporal duration or span of earthly existence; a person's age or lifetime, including the period while one remains alive.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun in temporal construct chains (יְמֵי חַיֵּי-, שְׁנֵי חַיֵּי-), or with prepositions בְּ- or לְ- plus suffix or personal name

senses.definition: Health, security, flourishing, and blessed quality of existence associated with wisdom, righteousness, or favor; also lived earthly experience.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (subject, predicate, object, or governed by preposition לְ- or בְּ-; also in wisdom constructs like עֵץ חַיִּים, אֹרַח חַיִּים, חַיֵּי בְשָׂרִים)

senses.definition: The addressee's life invoked as the surety in an oath formula.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun with second-person pronominal suffix in an oath exclamation paired with חֵי נַפְשֶׁךָ and followed by אִם

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in temporal construct chains such as כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֵּי- ("all the days of the life of..."), שְׁנֵי חַיֵּי- ("the years of the life of..."), and מִסְפַּר יְמֵי חַיֵּי- ("the number of the days of the life of..."), as well as with בְּ- + suffix ("during one's lifetime", PSA 49:19, 63:5, 146:2). Regularly paired in parallel with נֶפֶשׁ ("soul/self", e.g., PSA 26:9, LAM 3:58) and רוּחַ ("spirit/breath", JOB 7:7, ISA 38:16), and contrasted directly with מָוֶת ("death", DEU 30:19, PRO 12:28, JER 21:8) and שַׁחַת ("pit", PSA 103:4, JON 2:7). In JOB 24:22, the form ends in -în (חַיִּין). In 2SA 11:11, חַיֶּךָ functions alongside חֵי נַפְשֶׁךָ as a solemn oath formula.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A feminine noun denoting the physical right hand, the right side or direction (usually contrasted with the left), a position of honor or support beside someone, and figuratively the instrument or emblem of power, victory, and oath-taking.

senses.definition: The physical hand on the right side of the body, used for grasping, blessing, skilled action, holding objects, or swearing oaths.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (often with pronominal suffix), or as second element in construct yad yĕmîn ('hand of right')

senses.definition: The right hand conceived metonymically as an agent or emblem of strength, deliverance, victory, support, or forceful action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Subject of active verbs (e.g., 'uphold', 'acquire', 'find', 'do valiantly') or with instrumental preposition b- ('by means of')
