senses.definition: The right side or right-hand direction relative to a person, object, or path (including attributive 'right' for paired body parts, and figuratively the favorable or sound course).
senses.grammatical_frame: With spatial prepositions (min, ʿal, l-), adverbially without preposition after verbs of turning (NUM 22:26, DEU 17:11, 1SA 6:12), or attributively in definite construct/apposition (LEV 7:32, LEV 9:21)

senses.definition: A station immediately beside a person's right side, denoting honored status, attendance, advocacy, or protective accompaniment.
senses.grammatical_frame: With prepositions ʿal or l- + person/suffix after verbs of standing or going

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very frequently paired or contrasted with śĕmōʾl ('left'), forming merisms for 'any direction / any deviation' (NUM 22:26, DEU 17:11, 1SA 6:12, 2SA 2:19), 'on every side' (EXO 14:29, 1KI 7:49, 2CH 4:8, NEH 8:4, ISA 9:19, ZEC 4:11), or basic discernment (JON 4:11; cf. moral/practical inclination in ECC 10:2). Appears in the construct phrase yad yĕmîn ('right hand', JDG 3:15, JDG 7:20, 2SA 20:9) and as an attributive qualifier of anatomical parts (šôq hayyāmîn 'the right thigh', LEV 7:32, LEV 9:21). In 2KI 23:13, mîmîn l- specifies relative location ('to the right of', conventionally south when facing east). In poetic parallelism, yāmîn pairs with yād ('hand', PSA 21:9, PSA 89:14) and zĕrôaʿ ('arm', PSA 89:14).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A verb whose stem distinctions express initiating an action (causative/active Hiphil, passive Hophal), treating something sacred or honorable as profane or open to common use (intensive/factitive Piel, passive Pual and Niphal), or being pierced/wounded internally (simple Qal).

senses.definition: To enter upon or initiate an action, state, or sequence; in the passive Hophal, for an action to be started by people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (active) usually + l- + infinitive, or + imperative (DEU 2:24), or + min / b- indicating starting point (EZK 9:6); Hophal (impersonal passive) + l- + infinitive (GEN 4:26)

senses.definition: To treat what is sacred, consecrated, commanded, or honorable as ordinary, defiled, or violable; to strip of sanctity or honor (or, in passive stems, to be treated as profane).
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (transitive) + direct object (sanctuary, holy things, divine name, Sabbath, statutes, father, bed), or + min 'from' in expulsion as defiled (EZK 28:16); Pual (passive participle, EZK 36:23); Niphal (passive/reflexive, ISA 48:11, EZK 20:9, EZK 22:26, and possibly LEV 21:9)

senses.definition: To open a newly planted vineyard to ordinary, non-restricted use so its produce may be enjoyed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (transitive) with vineyard (kerem) as explicit or implied object

senses.definition: To be pierced, wounded, or stricken internally (said of the heart in distress).
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive/stative) with subject lēb ('heart') + b- 'within'

entries.collocations_and_notes: Strongly polarized by stem in the sampled corpus: (1) Hiphil (with impersonal passive Hophal in GEN 4:26) expresses initiation ('begin'), almost always governing l- + infinitive (e.g., GEN 10:8, DEU 3:24, JDG 16:19) and frequently paired contrastively with kālâ ('finish', 1CH 27:24, 2CH 29:17, 2CH 31:7), or taking min / b- for a starting point (EZK 9:6). (2) Piel (with passive Pual in EZK 36:23 and passive/reflexive Niphal in ISA 48:11, EZK 20:9, EZK 22:26) expresses profanation/desecration of sacred names, sanctuaries, offerings, Sabbaths, or honor, explicitly contrasted with qōdeš ('holy') in EZK 22:26 and paired with ṭimmēʾ ('make unclean') in LEV 20:3. In LEV 21:9, the first verb (tēḥēl l- + infinitive) reflects either passive/reflexive degradation ('she degrades/profanes herself by prostituting') or inception ('she begins to prostitute'), while the second (mĕḥallelēt) is active Piel ('she profanes her father'). (3) A specialized Piel usage with vineyards (kerem) in DEU 20:6 and JER 31:5 denotes releasing a newly planted vineyard from restriction for ordinary consumption. (4) Only one Qal form appears in the sample (PSA 109:22, with lēb 'heart'), denoting internal piercing or wounding.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Predicative particle asserting existence, presence, possession, or availability, also used in affirmative replies, suffixed participial predications, and once substantively for wealth or substance.

senses.definition: Asserts the existence, occurrence, or spatial presence of an entity, state, or event, often in existential statements, questions, or conditional and apprehensive clauses, and with participles or relative markers to denote an indefinite member or subset ('there is one who / some who').
senses.grammatical_frame: existential particle + noun phrase / participle (often with locative prep. בְּ־ / עַל־, or interrogative הֲ־, or conditional אִם / פֶּן / אוּלַי)

senses.definition: Indicates possession, availability, entitlement, or capability belonging to a person or entity, and with an infinitive or the idiom יֶשׁ־לְאֵל יָד־ expresses having the means or power to act.
senses.grammatical_frame: particle + prep. לְ־ or אֵת (+ noun phrase or infinitive construct)

senses.definition: Functions as a predicative copula with an attached pronominal suffix before a participle in conditional clauses to express ongoing or intended action, or with אֵת + noun + adjective to predicate a state or quality.
senses.grammatical_frame: particle + pronominal suffix + participle; or particle + אֵת + noun + adjective

senses.definition: Serves as a standalone elliptical affirmation confirming existence, presence, or agreement in direct speech, including the doubled emphatic form יֵשׁ וָיֵשׁ.
senses.grammatical_frame: standalone predicate in dialogue (or doubled with conjunction וְ־)

senses.definition: Used substantively as a noun denoting tangible property, wealth, or enduring substance bequeathed as an inheritance, paralleled with treasuries.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine-like substantive object of verb (לְהַנְחִיל)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasts with the negative particle אַיִן/אֵין in alternative questions (הֲיֵשׁ ... אִם־אָיִן, EXO 17:7; NUM 13:20) and antithetical clauses (PRO 13:7; NEH 5:5). Commonly takes maqqef and shortens to יֶשׁ־ before nouns or prepositions, and accepts pronominal suffixes as יֶשְׁךָ (GEN 24:42; JDG 6:36). Notable idioms include יֶשׁ־לְאֵל יָדִי ('it is in my power', GEN 31:29), הֲיֵשׁ אֶת־לְבָבְךָ יָשָׁר ('is your heart right?', 2KI 10:15), and the emphatic doubled response יֵשׁ וָיֵשׁ (2KI 10:15). Also combines with אֲשֶׁר (NEH 5:2) or partitive מִן (NEH 5:5) to introduce indefinite subsets. In 1SA 21:9 it follows אִין in an unusual interrogative construction asking whether a weapon is on hand.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Proclitic relative and subordinating particle introducing relative clauses, headless nominalized clauses, possessive expressions with לְ־, complement clauses, causal grounds, and compound temporal or comparative conjunctions.

senses.definition: Introduces a relative clause modifying an explicit nominal, pronominal, or temporal antecedent, including clauses with resumptive pronouns indicating possession or oblique relationships.
senses.grammatical_frame: proclitic particle prefixed to verb, participle, adjective, noun, or prepositional phrase after an antecedent

senses.definition: Introduces a headless relative clause functioning as a noun phrase (subject or object), frequently following מַה־, כֹּל, אֵת, or a preposition.
senses.grammatical_frame: proclitic particle without explicit nominal head, or following מַה־ / כֹּל / אֵת / preposition

senses.definition: Prefixed to the preposition לְ־ with a pronominal suffix to mark emphatic or appositional possession in relation to a preceding noun.
senses.grammatical_frame: proclitic particle + prep. לְ־ + pronominal suffix (שֶׁלִּי)

senses.definition: Functions as a subordinating complementizer introducing an object, explanatory, or circumstantial/concessive clause after verbs of knowing, questions, or evaluative statements.
senses.grammatical_frame: proclitic particle introducing finite verbal or nominal clause after main verb/predicate

senses.definition: Introduces a causal clause stating the reason or ground for a preceding statement or command, either alone or combined in בְּשַׁגַּם ('because indeed').
senses.grammatical_frame: proclitic particle (or compound בְּשַׁגַּם) + nominal or verbal clause

senses.definition: Combines with prepositions or adverbs (עַד־שֶׁ־, כִּמְעַט שֶׁ־, כָּל־עֻמַּת שֶׁ־) to form compound conjunctions marking temporal limits, simultaneity, or exact comparison.
senses.grammatical_frame: preposition/adverb (עַד / כִּמְעַט / כָּל־עֻמַּת) + proclitic particle + clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Proclitic particle regularly causing gemination (with dagesh forte) in the following consonant, vocalized שֶׁ־ (or שַׁ־ in the compound בְּשַׁגַּם in GEN 6:3). Predominates in Song of Songs, Ecclesiastes, and the later ascent psalms. Combines frequently with מַה־ ('what/that which', ECC 1:9; 3:15; 8:7), כֹּל ('all that/who', 1CH 5:20; ECC 2:7), אֵת ('the one whom', SNG 3:1, 4), לְ־ ('my own', SNG 1:6), and prepositions/adverbs such as עַד־, כִּמְעַט, בְּ־, and כָּל־עֻמַּת to form compound conjunctions. In relative clauses with oblique roles, a resumptive pronominal suffix often appears within the clause (e.g., PSA 146:5; ECC 2:21; 10:17).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A chair or elevated seat of honor, especially the ceremonial throne of a king or of God, and by extension royal rule, dynasty, or judicial and administrative authority.

senses.definition: A physical chair or seat for sitting, such as a seat at a doorway, a priest's seat beside a sanctuary entrance, or a seat of honor placed for a guest.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine; object of a preposition (`עַל`) or verb (`שׂים`, 'set/place')

senses.definition: An ornate ceremonial seat or elevated chair occupied by a monarch or envisioned as occupied by God, symbolizing royal rank, precedence, or divine majesty.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine (variant `כִּסֵּה`); commonly with `יָשַׁב עַל` ('sit upon'), `קוּם מִן` ('rise from'), or `שׂים` / `נתן` ('set, place')

senses.definition: Royal office, dynastic succession, sovereign power, or a seat of judicial and administrative authority, whether human or divine.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine (also shortened variant `כֵּס` and plural `כִסְאוֹת`); often in construct before a ruler, kingdom, or quality, or as object of verbs of establishing (`הֵקִים`, `כּוֹנֵן`, `סָעַד`)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently governed by `יָשַׁב עַל` ('sit upon', indicating occupancy of a seat or accession to royal rule) and `הֵקִים` / `כּוֹנֵן` / `סָעַד` ('establish / uphold', indicating continuity of dynasty or government). Note orthographic variants: `כֵּס` in EXO 17:16 (`כֵּס יָהּ`) and `כִּסֵּה` in 1KI 10:19; the plural `כִסְאוֹת` / `כִּסְאֹת` appears in PSA 122:5. Construct expressions include `כִּסֵּא דָוִד` ('throne of David'), `כִּסֵּא יִשְׂרָאֵל` ('throne of Israel'), `כִּסֵּא הַמְּלוּכָה` / `כִּסֵּא מַלְכוּתוֹ` ('royal throne'), and `כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ` ('throne of your glory').

entries.core_meaning_summary: The sun as a luminous celestial body, also used to mark times of day (sunrise and sunset), cardinal directions (east and west), and the earthly sphere of human life.

senses.definition: The sun, the bright celestial body in the sky that supplies daylight and heat, moves across the heavens, serves as an emblem of permanence, and is sometimes treated as an object of worship.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (with both masculine and feminine verbal/pronominal agreement); definite or indefinite, functioning as subject, direct object, or object of a preposition

senses.definition: The sun as a marker of time of day, specifically sunrise (with verbs of shining forth) or sunset (with verbs of going in).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in temporal clauses or construct phrases with verbs or infinitives of rising (`זרח`) or setting (`בוא`)

senses.definition: The cardinal directions east or west, designated by the point of the sun's rising or setting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in construct chains governed by `מִזְרָח` ('rising') or `מָבוֹא` ('going in / setting'), frequently with directional endings or prepositions (`מִן`, `עַד`)

senses.definition: The earthly world of mortal life and human activity, expressed in the spatial idiom 'under the sun'.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun governed by the preposition `תַּחַת` ('under') in the fixed expression `תַּחַת הַשָּׁמֶשׁ`

senses.definition: Figuratively, a person's vitality, well-being, or span of prosperity, whose sudden 'setting' while still day signifies premature ruin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun with a possessive suffix as subject of `בָּא` ('has set') in poetic metaphor

entries.collocations_and_notes: Common collocations include `בּוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ` / `מְבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ` ('going in / setting of the sun', i.e., sunset or west), `זָרַח הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ` / `מִזְרַח הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ` ('rising of the sun', i.e., sunrise or east), and the fixed phrase `תַּחַת הַשָּׁמֶשׁ` ('under the sun', frequent in Ecclesiastes). Frequently paired with `יָרֵחַ` ('moon') and `כּוֹכָבִים` ('stars'). Grammatically, `שֶׁמֶשׁ` displays variable gender agreement, taking masculine verbs and suffixes in most occurrences (e.g., GEN 15:12; EXO 16:21; JOS 10:13; PSA 113:3; JER 15:9) and feminine verbs in others (2SA 2:24; ISA 38:8; JON 4:8). With pronominal suffixes, the stem appears as `שִׁמְשׁ־` (JER 15:9).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To slaughter an animal (or, in condemned or figurative contexts, humans) as a ritual sacrifice to a deity or for a meal/feast.

senses.definition: To slaughter and present an animal as a ritual offering to YHWH or to another deity, often accompanied by a communal meal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb; used transitively with an animal or cognate sacrifice-noun object, with or without לְ ('to') or לִפְנֵי ('before') + deity, or intransitively/absolutely.

senses.definition: To practice sacrificing habitually or repeatedly, especially at high places, to foreign deities, or to objects of devotion, frequently paired with burning incense.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive active verb; typically intransitive with locative בְּ ('at/on') or recipient לְ ('to') or associative עִם ('with').

senses.definition: To slaughter human beings in idolatrous sacrifice, or figuratively to prepare a great slaughter-feast of victims.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb; transitive with human direct objects or cognate זֶבַח ('sacrifice/feast') and recipient לְ ('to/for').

senses.definition: To slaughter livestock for meat or for a communal feast, including non-sanctuary slaughter for food away from the chosen altar.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active verb; transitive with livestock direct object or partitive מִן ('from') + herd/flock, followed by eating/feasting verbs.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes the cognate noun זֶבַח ("sacrifice") as direct object (GEN 31:54, LEV 22:29, DEU 33:19, JDG 16:23, 1SA 1:21, 1KI 8:62, PSA 4:6, PSA 107:22) and marks the divine recipient with לְ ("to", e.g., לַיהוָה "to YHWH", לֵאלֹהֵיהֶם/לַשְּׂעִירִם "to other gods/goat-demons") or לִפְנֵי ("before", LEV 9:4, 1KI 8:62, 2CH 7:4). Often paired in cultic contexts with burning incense/offerings (קטר, 1KI 11:8, 2KI 15:4, HAB 1:16) or offering burnt offerings (הֶעֱלָה עֹלוֹת, 1SA 6:15). Stem usage shows a clear contrast: the simple active stem is used for individual or narrated acts of slaughtering/sacrificing (both cultic and domestic), while the intensive active stem appears predominantly in participles and imperfects expressing habitual or repeated cultic sacrificing, especially at high places or to foreign/idolatrous recipients (1KI 3:2, 1KI 11:8, 2KI 15:4, 2CH 28:23, HOS 4:14, HAB 1:16; note the immediate shift from simple active narrative action to intensive active resolve within 2CH 28:23).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The feminine-agreement numeral component meaning 'ten' ('-teen') used in compound numbers from eleven through nineteen.

senses.definition: Ten, as the second element in cardinal compound numerals (eleven through nineteen) counting feminine nouns of time, measurement, objects, cities, or persons.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine compound numeral element following a unit numeral (1–9); precedes a singular/plural counted noun, follows a plural counted noun, or stands predicatively/elliptically.

senses.definition: Ten, as the second element in compound numerals functioning ordinally (eleventh through eighteenth) in regnal or calendar year dates.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine compound numeral element in chronological phrases: following construct שְׁנַת ('year of'), following the definite noun הַשָּׁנָה with definite unit numeral (1KI 6:38), or in prepositional בְּ + compound numeral + שָׁנָה ('in the Nth year').

entries.collocations_and_notes: Always occurs as the second component of compound numerals for 11 through 19, paired with feminine-form unit numerals: אַחַת/עַשְׁתֵּי (11), שְׁתֵּים/שְׁתֵּי (12), שְׁלֹשׁ/שְׁלוֹשׁ (13), אַרְבַּע (14), חֲמֵשׁ (15), שֵׁשׁ (16), שְׁבַע (17), שְׁמֹנֶה/שְׁמוֹנֶה (18), and תְּשַׁע (19). Consistently modifies feminine nouns (e.g., שָׁנָה 'year', אַמָּה 'cubit', עִיר/עָרִים 'city/cities', יְרִיעֹת 'curtains', אֲבָנִים 'stones', מַצֵּבָה 'pillar', קַעֲרֹת 'dishes', כַּפּוֹת 'spoons', נָפֶשׁ 'person', נָשִׁים 'wives', בָּנוֹת 'daughters'), in explicit contrast to masculine-agreement עָשָׂר in the same verses (EXO 24:4, EXO 39:14, NUM 7:84, EZK 32:1). In EZK 43:16, שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה stands elliptically without an explicit unit of measurement before אֹרֶךְ ('length') and רֹחַב ('width').

entries.core_meaning_summary: As a verb, to complete, make restitution, fulfill a vow, or repay/requite; as an adjective, whole, complete, peaceful, or undivided; also a place name (Salem).

senses.definition: To reach completion or finish a task or structure; in causative/factitive use, to carry a decree through to completion or bring a life to an end.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple intransitive (Qal: subject is structure); factitive active (Piel: with direct object); causative active (Hiphil: with object decree or person)

senses.definition: To make restitution, compensate, or repay for loss, damage, theft, sacred offense, or a financial loan.
senses.grammatical_frame: Factitive active (Piel, frequently reinforced by infinitive absolute שַׁלֵּם יְשַׁלֵּם) with object of loss/debt or recipient with לְ

senses.definition: To fulfill or pay a vow made to God; in the passive stem, for a vow to be fulfilled.
senses.grammatical_frame: Factitive active (Piel) with object נֶדֶר ('vow') and recipient לְ ('to God'); passive (Pual) with נֶדֶר as subject

senses.definition: To repay, reward, or requite someone in kind for good or evil deeds; in the passive stem, to be repaid or recompensed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Factitive active (Piel) with person (with לְ / אֶל or direct object) and deed/requital; passive (Pual) for person or good/evil being repaid

senses.definition: Whole, full, entire, or uncut (of stone left intact from the quarry, full wages, or an entire body of captives).
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective modifying a noun (feminine singular שְׁלֵמָה)

senses.definition: Undivided, wholly devoted, or loyal (especially describing the heart toward God or a ruler), or peaceful and well-disposed toward others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective modifying לֵב/לֵבָב ('heart') or predicate adjective with אֶת ('with' someone)

senses.definition: Salem, a place name of which Melchizedek is king.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun in construct phrase מֶלֶךְ שָׁלֵם ('king of Salem')

entries.collocations_and_notes: The evidence packet spans verbal forms across four stems, adjectival forms, and one proper place name. Stem contrasts in the verb: simple active/intransitive (Qal) denotes reaching completion ('be finished', NEH 6:15); intensive/factitive active (Piel) denotes making something whole or settled—finishing a structure, paying back restitution or a loan, fulfilling a vow, or requiting deeds (often reinforced with an infinitive absolute שַׁלֵּם יְשַׁלֵּם for legal certainty in EXO 21:36, 22:2, 22:5, JER 51:56); passive of Piel (Pual) denotes being fulfilled or repaid (PSA 65:2, PRO 11:31, JER 18:20); causative active (Hiphil) denotes carrying a decree to completion (JOB 23:14) or bringing someone to an end (ISA 38:13). Adjectival uses frequently collocate with לֵב / לֵבָב ('whole/undivided heart', e.g., 1KI 15:14, 1CH 12:39, 1CH 29:19, 2CH 15:17).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To throw, hurl, discard, or cast down/out physically, ritually, or figuratively (used in causative active and passive stems).

senses.definition: To propel, throw, hurl, drop, or scatter a physical object or person onto a surface, into a container/pit/fire, or upon/at someone; in the passive stem, to be thrown.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) with direct object and goal/locative (e.g., 'into', 'upon', 'to the ground'); causative passive (Hophal) for being thrown

senses.definition: To throw away, dispose of, leave behind, or abandon unwanted, defiled, or helpless items or persons; in the passive stem, to lie abandoned or exposed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) with direct object (often with 'outside', 'from oneself'); causative passive (Hophal) with subject exposed/unburied

senses.definition: To cast down from height or standing, overthrow, banish to another place, or expel from someone's presence; in the passive stem, to be cast out or overthrown.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) with personal/spatial object and source/goal ('from before', 'to another land', 'to the earth'); causative passive (Hophal)

senses.definition: To cast lots or a measuring cord in order to apportion land or determine an allotment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) with object גּוֹרָל ('lot') or חֶבֶל ('measuring cord')

senses.definition: To put away or disregard something by figuratively throwing it behind one's back (teaching or sins), or to expose one's life to danger by casting it forward.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active (Hiphil) in idiomatic phrases with אַחֲרֵי גַוּוֹ ('behind one's back') or נַפְשׁוֹ מִנֶּגֶד ('one's life out in front')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Observed in the evidence packet solely in the causative active stem (Hiphil: to throw, cast, discard, banish) and its corresponding causative passive stem (Hophal: to be thrown, left exposed/abandoned, cast out). Frequent directional complements include אֶל ('into/onto'), עַל ('upon/against'), מִפְּנֵי / מִלִּפְנֵי / מֵעַל פָּנַי ('out of someone's sight/presence'), and locatives with directional ה (אַרְצָה 'to the ground', הַבֹּרָה 'into the pit'). Notable idioms: הִשְׁלִיךְ אַחֲרֵי גַוּוֹ/גֵוְךָ ('to cast behind one's back' — of willfully disregarding divine instruction in NEH 9:26 or putting away sins in ISA 38:17); הִשְׁלִיךְ נַפְשׁוֹ מִנֶּגֶד ('to cast one's life out in front', i.e., risk one's life, JDG 9:17); and הִשְׁלִיךְ גּוֹרָל / חֶבֶל בְּגוֹרָל ('to cast a lot / measuring line by lot', JOS 18:8, MIC 2:5). In AMO 4:3, the Hiphil second-person feminine plural form וְהִשְׁלַכְתֶּנָה lacks an explicit direct object and functions either as an idiomatic expression of forced expulsion or with an implied object toward הַהַרְמוֹנָה.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To think, plan, or devise mentally, extending across stems to artistic designing, reckoning or crediting value and status, calculating amounts, pondering, and being regarded in a particular way.

senses.definition: To form an intention, plot, or scheme in the mind toward a good or harmful outcome, either in the simple active stem or the intensive active stem.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb in simple active stem (Qal), or intensive active stem (Piel in DAN 11:24); with direct object (רָעָה, אָוֶן, מַחֲשָׁבָה), לְ + infinitive, or עַל indicating target or beneficiary

senses.definition: To conceive and fashion intricate artistic patterns, textiles, metalwork, or mechanical contrivances; its active participle functions as a title for a skilled designer or master weaver.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb in simple active stem (Qal), infinitive with cognate object מַחֲשָׁבֹת or active participle (חֹשֵׁב / חוֹשֵׁב) used substantively in construct phrases (מַעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב, חֹשְׁבֵי מַחֲשָׁבֹת)

senses.definition: To credit or impute an action or moral quality to someone's account, or to regard and value a person or thing at a given worth or role.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb in simple active stem (Qal); takes direct object with indirect recipient (לְ) and/or predicate noun (with or without לְ), or direct object alone when meaning to esteem/value

senses.definition: In the intensive active stem, to compute a proportional monetary sum, or to reflect thoughtfully upon, consider, and take careful notice of someone or something.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb in intensive active stem (Piel); with direct object (כֶּסֶף, יָמִים, דְּרָכַי, or pronominal suffix) and optional לְ for the person affected
senses.semantic_domain: Cognition and Accounting / Calculation and Reflection

senses.definition: In the passive stem, to be counted, credited, settled in financial accounting, or regarded as having a certain status, classification, or worth.
senses.grammatical_frame: verb in passive stem (Niphal); paired with prepositions לְ, עַל, כְּ, כְּמוֹ, or אֵת, or with a predicate noun or adjective

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes the cognate object מַחֲשָׁבָה / מַחֲשָׁבֹת (EXO 31:4, EXO 35:35, JER 49:30, DAN 11:24) as well as moral or emotional nouns such as רָעָה (GEN 50:20, JER 18:8, NAM 1:11), אָוֶן (PSA 36:5, MIC 2:1), טֹבָה (GEN 50:20), עָוֺן (2SA 19:20, PSA 32:2), and צְדָקָה (GEN 15:6). Distinct stems express clear voice and aspectual differences: simple active (Qal) covers intending, designing, and crediting/regarding; intensive active (Piel) appears for calculating sums, pondering thoughtfully, and scheming; passive (Niphal) consistently marks being counted, accounted for, or regarded as something.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A large flowing watercourse or river, used especially with the definite article for the Euphrates as a geographical landmark, and extended poetically to surging floodwaters or continuous abundance.

senses.definition: A natural or channeled perennial watercourse of substantial flow, whether named in construct or spoken of generally as a geographical feature that waters land, borders settlements, or is divided or dried up.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, masculine singular or plural; frequently in construct before a proper name (e.g., נְהַר פְּרָת, נְהַר כְּבָר) or as subject/object of verbs of flowing, watering, or drying up

senses.definition: Specifically the Euphrates River, referred to absolutely with the definite article as a premier territorial boundary or in the regional expression 'beyond the River.'
senses.grammatical_frame: noun with definite article (הַנָּהָר), often in prepositional boundary phrases (מִן, עַד, בְּעֵבֶר, מֵעֵבֶר לְ) or apposition with נְהַר פְּרָת

senses.definition: Surging currents, deep oceanic waters, or an overwhelming torrent of water, often depicted in poetic parallelism with the sea or breaking waves.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun, plural (נְהָרוֹת) or anarthrous singular in poetry, paired with יָם / יַמִּים or מַיִם רַבִּים

senses.definition: Used figuratively in similes to represent a steady, abundant, and unbroken flow of peace or prosperity.
senses.grammatical_frame: singular noun following comparative כְּ (כַּנָּהָר / כְּנָהָר) with abstract subject or object שָׁלוֹם

entries.collocations_and_notes: Plural forms appear both as נְהָרוֹת (e.g., PSA 24:2, ISA 42:15, EZK 31:15) and נְהָרִים (ISA 18:7). Frequently appears in construct with geographical names: נְהַר פְּרָת (GEN 15:18, DEU 1:7, JER 46:6), נְהַר מִצְרַיִם (GEN 15:18), נְהַר גּוֹזָן (2KI 18:11), נְהַר כְּבָר (EZK 3:15, EZK 10:20). The definite phrase עֵבֶר הַנָּהָר / מֵעֵבֶר לַנָּהָר denotes the territory and later imperial province across the Euphrates (JOS 24:2, 1KI 14:15, EZR 8:36, NEH 3:7). Poetic parallels include יָם / יַמִּים (PSA 24:2, PSA 72:8, PSA 80:12, JON 2:4), מַיִם (PSA 105:41, ISA 43:20, SNG 8:7), and נַחַל (ISA 27:12, ISA 66:12).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To grow up or become great in size, status, or severity; in causative and intensive stems, to raise children, exalt someone or something, increase, or boast arrogantly.

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem, with a child, animal, personified city, or horn as subject, to grow physically, mature into adulthood, or expand in size and territorial reach.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal, intransitive (or with suffixal/comitative complement)

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem, with persons, wealth, power, deeds, pain, reputation, or life as subject (often with מִן "than", בְּעֵינֵי "in the eyes of", or עַל "over"), to become wealthy, powerful, renowned, severe, or highly valued.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal + מִן / בְּעֵינֵי / עַל / עַד

senses.definition: In the intensive (Piel) stem, with children as direct object, to nurture, rear, and bring up offspring.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel + direct object (children)

senses.definition: In the intensive (Piel) stem, with a person or name (שֵׁם) as direct object (often with בְּעֵינֵי/לְעֵינֵי), to elevate in rank, honor, or renown.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel + direct object (person or name) + בְּעֵינֵי / לְעֵינֵי

senses.definition: In the causative (Hiphil) stem, with abstract or concrete objects (such as kindness, wisdom, instruction, or a weight) or with לַעֲשׂוֹת ("to do"), to increase, enlarge, glorify, or perform great deeds.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil + direct object / לַעֲשׂוֹת + עִם

senses.definition: In the causative (Hiphil) stem—frequently with עַל ("against"), בְּפִיכֶם ("with your mouth"), בִּלְבָבוֹ ("in his heart"), or absolutely—and in the reflexive (Hithpael) stem with עַל, to exalt oneself, assert dominance, or boast arrogantly over another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (with עַל / בְּ / absolute) or Hithpael + עַל

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly appears in Qal with בְּעֵינֵי ("in the eyes of") for high valuation, with מִן ("than") for superiority, and with עִם/אֵת ("with") when describing growing up together. In Piel, frequently pairs with רֹמֵם ("to raise/exalt") for rearing children and with לְעֵינֵי/בְּעֵינֵי for elevating a leader. In Hiphil and Hithpael, commonly takes עַל ("against/over") to express arrogance or boasting. In AMO 8:5, Hiphil הַגְדִּיל ("make large") directly contrasts with הַקְטִין ("make small").

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be good, pleasing, or favorable; in the causative stem, to do good, act rightly, improve, or perform an action thoroughly.

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem, used impersonally with לְ ("for/to") to express that circumstances turn out favorably or beneficially for someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal, impersonal + לְ (beneficiary)

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem, with a matter, proposal, or person as subject and בְּעֵינֵי ("in the eyes of") or לִפְנֵי ("before"), to be pleasing, acceptable, or approved by someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal + בְּעֵינֵי / לִפְנֵי (experiencer)

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem, with לֵב or לְבָב ("heart") as subject, to become cheerful, glad, or content, especially after eating and drinking.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal + לֵב / לְבָב as subject

senses.definition: In the basic (Qal) stem with comparative מִן ("than"), to be in a superior or more secure condition than another.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal + מִן (comparative)

senses.definition: In the causative (Hiphil) stem, intransitively or with לְ, עִם, or a direct object (אֶת), to confer benefit, treat kindly, or act beneficially toward someone (often contrasted with doing harm); in 1SA 20:13 with אֶל, to deem good or see fit to bring something about.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil, intransitive or + לְ / עִם / אֶת / אֶל

senses.definition: In the causative (Hiphil) stem, with a direct object (such as ways, deeds, or face) or an infinitival complement, to act rightly, reform or amend conduct, brighten an appearance, or perform an action accurately or stately.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil + direct object / לְ + infinitive / intransitive

senses.definition: As a causative (Hiphil) infinitive absolute modifying another verb, indicating that the action or state is carried out thoroughly, completely, carefully, or rightly.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil infinitive absolute functioning adverbially with a finite verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently collocates in Qal with בְּעֵינֵי ("in the eyes of") or לִפְנֵי ("before") to express approval, and with לֵב/לְבָב ("heart") to describe cheerfulness or contentment. In Hiphil, commonly contrasts with הָרַע ("to do harm/evil") and pairs with דְּרָכִים ("ways") and מַעַלְלִים ("deeds") for moral reform. The Hiphil infinitive absolute הֵיטֵב frequently functions adverbially to express thoroughness. In 1SA 20:13, Hiphil appears with אֶל ("to") and אֶת הָרָעָה ("the harm") to express what seems good or fitting to someone.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A verb whose passive/reflexive stems express feeling regret, relenting from an action, or being consoled, while its intensive/factitive stem means to comfort, console, or bring relief.

senses.definition: To experience regret, remorse, or sorrowful compassion over a past deed, situation, or someone's plight.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (passive/reflexive stem), used absolutely, with כִּי introducing the regretted act, with לְ for the person pitied, or with עַל specifying the state of humiliation

senses.definition: To change one's mind or intention and turn away from an announced judgment, blessing, or anger out of forbearance or compassion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (passive/reflexive stem) used absolutely or with עַל / אֶל ('concerning'); also Hithpael (reflexive stem) with עַל in DEU 32:36

senses.definition: To console, soothe, or bring relief to someone in grief, hardship, or distress; in passive and reflexive stems, to receive consolation or be reconciled to a loss or calamity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (intensive/factitive stem) with direct object (person or place) and optional מִן ('from toil') or עַל ('concerning'); Pual (passive of Piel) 'be comforted'; Hithpael (reflexive stem) 'let oneself be comforted'; Niphal (passive/reflexive stem) in EZK 14:22 'be consoled / reconciled'

entries.collocations_and_notes: Shows a sharp functional division by verbal stem. In the Niphal passive/reflexive stem, it overwhelmingly expresses internal sorrow, regret (with כִּי clauses in GEN 6:7, 1SA 15:11, 1SA 15:35), or relenting/changing an announced course of action (frequently with עַל or אֶל introducing הָרָעָה 'the disaster' or הַטּוֹבָה 'the good', as in EXO 32:12, JER 18:10, JER 26:13, JER 42:10, JOL 2:13, JON 3:10); in EZK 14:22, however, the Niphal describes the exiles being consoled or reconciled regarding Jerusalem's disaster. In the Piel intensive/factitive stem (and its passive Pual counterpart in ISA 54:11, ISA 66:13), it consistently means 'comfort, console, bring relief' (parallel to דִּבֶּר עַל לֵב 'speak kindly' in GEN 50:21, and נוּד 'show sympathy' in JOB 2:11, PSA 69:21, ISA 51:19). In the Hithpael reflexive stem, it means 'allow oneself to be comforted' when paired with מֵאֵן 'refuse' (GEN 37:35, JER 31:15), while with עַל in DEU 32:36 it parallels יָדִין ('vindicate') and means 'have compassion / relent toward'.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To care for or raise (in the simple active participle); to be firm, enduring, established, or trustworthy (in the passive/reflexive stem); and to trust, rely on, or believe (in the causative stem).

senses.definition: One who nurses, cares for, or raises a child as a caregiver, guardian, or tutor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal active participle used substantivally (masculine plural or feminine singular)

senses.definition: To be physically firm, secure, enduring, or long-lasting (used of a secure place, a lasting royal house, enduring mercies, or chronic plagues).
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal participle modifying nouns of place, dynasty, covenant blessing, or affliction

senses.definition: To be confirmed, proved true, established securely, or found faithful and reliable in character or speech.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal finite verb or participle describing words, people, God, or a city

senses.definition: To trust, rely on, accept as true, or be convinced of something.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil verb + בְּ ("in"), לְ ("to/in"), infinitive construct, כִּי clause, or absolute

senses.definition: When negated with "life" as object, to have no certainty or assurance of survival.
senses.grammatical_frame: Negated Hiphil verb + בְּ + חַיִּים ("life")

entries.collocations_and_notes: Shows a clear contrast across stems: the Qal participle denotes a caregiver or tutor raising a child (2SA 4:4, 2KI 10:1); the Niphal expresses being firm, enduring, established, or trustworthy (often modifying בַּיִת "house/dynasty", עֵד "witness", or God's words/commands); and the Hiphil expresses placing trust or belief in someone or something (regularly taking בְּ for trusting a person/God/commandments, לְ for believing a speaker, message, or sign, and כִּי clauses for believing a proposition). Deliberate wordplay pairing the Hiphil ("trust") and Niphal ("be made secure/established") occurs in 2CH 20:20 and ISA 7:9. In JOB 39:24, לֹא יַאֲמִין כִּי קוֹל שׁוֹפָר idiomatically depicts the warhorse's eagerness at the horn blast (scarcely believing or unable to hold back at the sound).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A preposition expressing spatial enclosure or passage through an opening, as well as acting on behalf of, on account of, or in exchange for someone or something.

senses.definition: Spatial enclosure or closing off around a person or object, whether shutting in, hedging about, shielding, or closing in upon.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition following verbs of shutting/closing (סָגַר, עָצַר), hedging (שׂוּךְ), shielding (מָגֵן), or approaching/confronting (קָדַם)

senses.definition: Spatial passage or line of sight passing through an opening, barrier, or covering (such as a window, lattice, cloud, or veil).
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition (or compound מִבַּעַד לְ) with verbs of looking, falling, or judging, or in nominal phrases describing partial visibility

senses.definition: Acting in favor of, in defense of, or as an intermediary for someone, or taking action on account of a situation such as sin or calamity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition with verbs of praying, inquiring of God, making atonement/offerings, fighting/strengthening, giving a bribe/ransom, or fulfilling a purpose

senses.definition: Substitution or equivalence in an exchange or change of state.
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition in nominal comparison or with נָתַן ('give') and הָיָה ('serve as / become')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently takes pronominal suffixes (e.g., בַּעֲדִי, בַּעַדְךָ, בַּעֲדוֹ, בַּעֲדָם) and commonly co-occurs in coordinated series (e.g., בַּעֲדוֹ וּבְעַד בֵּיתוֹ וּבְעַד כָּל קְהַל יִשְׂרָאֵל in LEV 16:17; compare LEV 9:7, LEV 16:6, JOB 1:10, 2KI 22:13). With verbs of closing (סָגַר, עָצַר), it marks the barrier or person/object enclosed inside (GEN 7:16, 2KI 4:5, 2KI 4:21, GEN 20:18, 1SA 1:6). In AMO 9:10, בַּעֲדֵינוּ follows הִגִּישׁ וְהִקְדִּים ('bring near and confront/overtake us' with calamity). Combined as מִבַּעַד לְ in SNG 4:1 and SNG 6:7, it indicates viewing through or from behind a veil. In intercessory and cultic contexts, it regularly pairs with הִתְפַּלֵּל ('pray'), נָשָׂא תְפִלָּה ('lift up prayer'), כִּפֶּר ('make atonement'), and דָּרַשׁ ('inquire of God'). With עָוָה/רָעָה or חַטָּאת (EXO 32:30, JER 11:14), it can specify the offense or calamity on account of which action is taken.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be displeasing, evil, or harmful; to act wickedly or inflict harm (causative); and in a distinct set of poetic contexts, to break, shatter, or come to ruin.

senses.definition: To be displeasing, troubling, or morally offensive to someone, regularly constructed with the prepositional phrase "in the eyes of."
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal stative verb + בְּעֵינֵי ("in the eyes of") + person

senses.definition: Of the eye, to become begrudging, stingy, or hostile toward someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal stative verb with עַיִן ("eye") as subject + בְּ + person

senses.definition: Of the face, to look sad, gloomy, or troubled.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal stative verb with פָּנִים ("face") as subject

senses.definition: To behave wickedly, commit wrong, or act worse than others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil active verb, used intransitively, with infinitive לַעֲשׂוֹת ("to do"), or with מִן ("more than")

senses.definition: Those who habitually do wrong or practice evil.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil participle used substantivally (plural מְרֵעִים)

senses.definition: To inflict harm, mistreat, or bring disaster and affliction upon someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil causative verb + לְ + person, direct object, or absolute

senses.definition: To smash, shatter, or crush violently, or (intransitively) to be broken and ruined.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb, transitive with direct object and instrument בְּ ("with"), or intransitive

senses.definition: To suffer harm, be broken, or come to ruin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal passive/intransitive verb

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the idiom רָעַע בְּעֵינֵי X ("to be displeasing/evil in someone's eyes"), often contrasted with טוֹב בְּעֵינֵי X ("good in someone's eyes", JER 40:4). With עַיִן ("eye") + בְּ, it expresses a begrudging or stingy attitude toward a needy relative (DEU 15:9, DEU 28:54). In the Hiphil, it frequently contrasts with הֵיטִיב ("do good", JOS 24:20) and takes מִן for comparison ("act worse than", 1KI 16:25, 2KI 21:11, JER 7:26, JER 16:12). The Hiphil participle מְרֵעִים functions substantivally as a standard term for "evildoers," parallel to רְשָׁעִים ("wicked", PSA 26:5, PRO 24:19) and פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן ("workers of iniquity", ISA 31:2). A distinct physical-destruction usage ("smash, shatter, be broken") appears in PSA 2:9, ISA 8:9, PRO 13:20, and JER 11:16; in ISA 8:9 the Qal imperative רֹעוּ parallels וָחֹתּוּ ("and be dismayed/shattered").

entries.core_meaning_summary: To put on, wear, or clothe someone (literally or figuratively) with garments, armor, attributes, or conditions.

senses.definition: In the simple active stem (Qal), to put on or wear physical garments, priestly vestments, sackcloth, or woven materials on one's body.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); takes the garment or fabric as direct object (occasionally omitted when contextually understood, as in JOB 27:17), sometimes with עַל ('upon') specifying the body part

senses.definition: In the simple active stem (Qal), used figuratively or metonymically to take on, be enveloped by, or display a quality, status, or condition such as majesty, strength, righteousness, shame, a curse, royal bearing, or desolation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); takes an abstract noun or metonymic expression as direct object, sometimes accompanied by כְּ ('like') comparing the attribute to armor or a garment

senses.definition: In the causative active stem (Hiphil), to dress or clothe another person, or to place garments, armor, or animal skins onto someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil); typically takes two direct objects (the person dressed and the garment/armor), or a direct object of the garment with עַל ('upon') marking the body part, or the person alone when the garment is implied or from a source (מִן)

senses.definition: In the causative active stem (Hiphil), used figuratively or poetically to array, cover, or endow a creature, person, or the skies with a physical feature, darkness, or impoverished attire.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil); takes two direct objects (the recipient or part affected and the feature, darkness, or rags)

senses.definition: In the intensive passive stem (Pual), to be clothed or attired in a specified material.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive passive participle (Pual); followed directly by the noun naming the fabric worn

entries.collocations_and_notes: Demonstrates a clear contrast across verbal stems: the simple active stem (Qal) denotes the subject putting on or wearing clothing or qualities; the causative active stem (Hiphil) denotes causing someone or something else to wear garments, coverings, or conditions (often taking two direct objects); and the intensive passive participle (Pual) describes the state of being attired in a specified material (2CH 5:12). Frequently contrasts with פָּשַׁט ('strip off', LEV 6:4, LEV 16:23, NUM 20:28) or הֵסִיר ('remove', GEN 38:19, ZEC 3:4). In EST 5:1 ('put on royalty'), the abstract noun מַלְכוּת serves metonymically for royal apparel and bearing.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To turn around or over, overthrow in ruin, or change and transform from one state or condition into another.

senses.definition: Used in the basic active (Qal) stem to denote physically turning something upside down or flipping it over (such as a tent or a baked cake), turning around or wheeling back in movement, or directing one's hand or course.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (transitive or intransitive; also passive participle)

senses.definition: Used in the passive/middle (Niphal) stem for turning oneself back toward a pursuer or rolling over from one side to the other.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (+ אֶל / מִן... אֶל)

senses.definition: Used in the reflexive/iterative (Hithpael) stem as a participle to describe continuous whirling, revolving, or tumbling motion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael participle

senses.definition: Used in the basic active (Qal) stem for overturning, devastating, or completely overthrowing cities, lands, or wicked people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal transitive (or infinitive absolute) + object

senses.definition: Used once in the passive of the causative (Hophal) stem with עַל to express calamities or terrors being turned against and overwhelming someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hophal + עַל (affected person)

senses.definition: Used in the basic active (Qal) stem to express changing or transforming something (or becoming changed) into a different substance, direction, character, or condition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal transitive + direct object + לְ (or intransitive + predicate adjective)

senses.definition: Used in the passive/middle (Niphal) stem to express being turned into another substance or state, deteriorating or changing appearance, being transferred to others, or a situation being reversed to its opposite.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (+ לְ / predicate noun or adjective)

senses.definition: Used in the reflexive/middle (Hithpael) stem with a simile to describe the earth changing form or taking on shape like clay beneath a seal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael + כְּ (comparison)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Spanning physical rotation, military/political overthrow, and transformation of state, the verb shows clear stem patterns: Qal expresses either transitive turning/overthrowing/transforming or intransitive turning back or changing color (LEV 13:3); Niphal expresses passive or middle change into another state (typically with לְ, as in EXO 7:15; ISA 34:9; JOL 3:4) as well as bodily turning (JOS 8:20; EZK 4:8) and reversal of circumstances (EST 9:1); Hithpael denotes continuous whirling/rolling motion (GEN 3:24; JDG 7:13) or taking shape (JOB 38:14); Hophal appears once for terrors turned against a sufferer (JOB 30:15). Notable idioms include הָפַךְ יָד ("turn one's hand," i.e., redirect a chariot in 2CH 18:33 or direct repeated blows in LAM 3:3) and turning something into its opposite (curse to blessing in DEU 23:6; justice to wormwood in AMO 5:7; festivals to mourning in AMO 8:10).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Inner gladness and delight, or outward celebration, festivity, and audible rejoicing.

senses.definition: An inner emotional state of gladness, delight, or happy satisfaction, including heartfelt devotion, relief from enemies, or even malicious gloating over another's ruin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; frequently in adverbial prepositional phrase with בְּ ('with/in'), in construct with לֵב/לֵבָב ('heart') or the experiencer, or as cognate object with שָׂמַח ('rejoice')

senses.definition: Public or communal celebration, festivity, and merrymaking expressed audibly or visibly through singing, shouting, musical instruments, processions, and feasting.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; often modified by גְדוֹלָה ('great'), paired with מִשְׁתֶּה ('feasting') or musical terms, or serving as subject/object of verbs of hearing, making, or ceasing

senses.definition: Sensory pleasure or earthly enjoyment derived from food, drink, wine, oil, and the fruits of one's labor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; direct object of verbs such as אָהֵב ('love') or שִׁבַּח ('commend'), or governed by מִן ('from')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with שָׂשׂוֹן ('gladness/joy', e.g., PSA 51:10, ISA 35:10, ISA 51:3, JER 15:16, JER 25:10) and גִּיל ('exultation', e.g., PSA 43:4, ISA 16:10, JER 48:33), and contrasted with יָגוֹן ('sorrow'), אֲנָחָה ('groaning'), תוּגָה ('grief'), and בְּכִי ('weeping'). Very commonly governed by the preposition בְּ ('with/in joy') to express the manner of worship, procession, service, or departure, or used as a cognate accusative with the verb שָׂמַח ('rejoice with great joy', 1KI 1:40, NEH 12:43, JON 4:6). Construct chains include שִׂמְחַת לֵב/לְבָבוֹ ('joy of heart', ECC 5:19, JER 15:16, EZK 36:5), שִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם ('everlasting joy', ISA 35:10, ISA 51:11), and תְּרוּעַת הַשִּׂמְחָה ('shout of celebration', EZR 3:13).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To become intensely angry, indignant, or agitated, and in non-basic stems to fret, be enraged, or act with ardent zeal.

senses.definition: Used in the basic active (Qal) stem with אַף ("anger") as the subject to indicate that wrath or fierce anger kindles and flares up against a person, group, or land.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb + subject אַף (+ בְּ / אֶל / עַל target)

senses.definition: Used impersonally in the basic active (Qal) stem with the preposition לְ marking the experiencer to express becoming angry, deeply vexed, indignant, or distressed over an event or speech.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal 3ms impersonal + לְ (experiencer) (+ עַל / כִּי cause)

senses.definition: Used in the passive/reflexive (Niphal) stem as a participle with בְּ to describe opponents who are incensed or enraged against someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal participle + בְּ (target)

senses.definition: Used in the reflexive (Hithpael) stem in wisdom exhortations to warn against fretting, working oneself into agitation, or getting heated over the success of wrongdoers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael jussive (+ בְּ target, or + לְ + infinitive)

senses.definition: Used once in the causative/intensive (Hiphil) stem immediately before another verb ("repaired/strengthened"), indicating acting with earnest ardor or zeal in carrying out the paired action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil + finite verb (asyndetic pairing)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most commonly occurs in the Qal stem either with אַף ("nose/anger") as grammatical subject (e.g., חָרָה אַף יְהוָה בְּ...) or impersonally in the 3ms with לְ marking the experiencer (e.g., וַיִּחַר לְקַיִן). Targets are usually introduced by בְּ, occasionally אֶל (NUM 24:10) or עַל (JOB 19:11); reasons or triggers are introduced by עַל or כִּי. Frequently intensified by מְאֹד (GEN 4:5; NUM 11:10; 1SA 11:6; 1SA 18:8; 2SA 3:8; NEH 4:1), הֵיטֵב (JON 4:4, JON 4:9), or עַד־מָוֶת (JON 4:9), and paired with physical or behavioral expressions of displeasure such as a fallen face (GEN 4:5), breaking tablets (EXO 32:19), striking the palms (NUM 24:10), or judging a matter evil in one's eyes (NUM 11:10; 1SA 18:8). Polite entreaties use the negated jussive אַל־נָא יִחַר לְ / אַל־יִחַר אַפְּךָ בְּ (GEN 18:30; GEN 44:18; JDG 6:39). In NEH 3:20, the single Hiphil form הֶחֱרָה immediately precedes הֶחֱזִיק without a conjunction, functioning adverbially to convey ardent or zealous effort.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To take delight in or favor a person or thing, or to wish, be willing, and purpose to do something.

senses.definition: To feel attraction toward, take delight in, or show favor to a person, whether in marital/romantic desire or in royal or divine favor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal; with preposition בְּ + person

senses.definition: To take pleasure in, value, or approve of an action, moral quality, offering, condition, or earthly possession.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (including stative/participial forms); with direct object, with בְּ + noun or relative clause, or absolute with locative בָּאָרֶץ

senses.definition: To wish, be willing, purpose, or choose to perform an action or bring about an outcome.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal; with לְ + infinitive construct, bare infinitive, relative clause as object of עָשָׂה ('do'), finite verb complement, or absolute

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs exclusively in the Qal stem (including stative and participial forms such as הֶחָפֵץ and construct plural חֲפֵצֵי in PSA 35:27, and חָפֵץ in MIC 7:18). Frequently parallels אָהֵב ('love', 1SA 18:22), רָצָה ('be pleased with', PSA 51:18; cf. רָצוֹן 'will/pleasure' in PSA 40:9), בָּחַר ('choose', ISA 65:12; ISA 66:4), and חֵשֶׁק ('desire', 1KI 9:1). In prophetic and wisdom literature, it frequently contrasts divine preference for חֶסֶד ('loyalty/steadfast love'), מִשְׁפָּט ('justice'), and צְדָקָה ('righteousness') over animal sacrifices (1SA/PSA 51:18; ISA 1:11; JER 9:23; HOS 6:6; MIC 7:18). In EST 6:6, 6:9, 6:11, the fixed expression אֲשֶׁר הַמֶּלֶךְ חָפֵץ בִּיקָרוֹ ('whom the king delights to honor') denotes royal favor.

entries.core_meaning_summary: In the active intensive stem (Piel), to render judgment or expect/suppose; in the reflexive/middle stem (Hithpael), to pray, make supplication to God, or intercede on another's behalf.

senses.definition: To arbitrate, pass judgment, or render an assessment in a case involving someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel; transitive with direct object suffix, or with preposition לְ ('for/concerning') + person

senses.definition: To anticipate, suppose, or think something would happen.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel; with infinitive construct phrase as clausal object

senses.definition: To address prayer, petition, confession, or praise to God (or, in one poetic context, to Zion/Israel as the place where God is present), often oriented toward a sacred place.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael; absolute, or with אֶל / לִפְנֵי / עַל + addressee, or with directional אֶל / דֶּרֶךְ + sacred place

senses.definition: To intercede or plead with God on behalf of another person or community, especially by a prophet or mediator to avert judgment or obtain favor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael; with בְּעַד, עַל, or לְ + beneficiary (sometimes alongside אֶל + deity)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Clear stem distinction between the active/intensive Piel (judicial assessment or expectation) and the reflexive/middle Hithpael (praying or interceding); 1SA 2:25 displays both stems in direct contrast. In Hithpael, prayers are commonly paired with הִתְחַנֵּן ('implore', 1KI 8:33), חִלָּה אֶת פְּנֵי ('entreat the favor of', 1KI 13:6), הִתְוַדָּה ('confess', DAN 9:20), בָּכָה ('weep', 1SA 1:10; NEH 1:4), and צוּם ('fast', NEH 1:4), as well as the nouns תְּפִלָּה ('prayer', 1KI 8:29; 2CH 6:19; JER 7:16) and תְּחִנָּה ('supplication', 2CH 6:19; 2CH 33:13; DAN 9:20). Divine response is frequently expressed with שָׁמַע ('hear', 1KI 8:29; 2CH 6:21; 2CH 7:14; JER 29:12) or נֶעְתַּר ('be entreated', 2CH 33:13). Note the unusual preposition עַל rather than אֶל with the divine addressee in 1SA 1:10, and directional orientation toward the temple or land with דֶּרֶךְ ('toward', 1KI 8:48; 2CH 6:38) or אֶל הַבַּיִת/הַמָּקוֹם ('toward this house/place', 1KI 8:29, 42; 2CH 6:21, 32).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To be swift, light, or of little weight/esteem, with causative stems denoting lightening a burden or treating lightly, intensive/passive stems denoting cursing, and a reduplicated form meaning to shake swiftly.

senses.definition: To move with great speed or pass rapidly, often compared using מִן ("than") to eagles or a weaver's shuttle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive, often with comparative מִן)

senses.definition: Of floodwaters: to diminish in level, subside, or abate from the surface of the earth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive) with מֵעַל ("from upon")

senses.definition: To become lowered in esteem, diminished in status, or despised in someone's estimation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive) with בְּעֵינֵי ("in the eyes of")

senses.definition: To be a small, easy, or trivial matter; in the adverbial phrase עַל נְקַלָּה (JER 6:14), to act lightly, carelessly, or superficially.
senses.grammatical_frame: Niphal (stative/impersonal with בְּעֵינֵי or מִן + infinitive; feminine participle in prepositional phrase עַל נְקַלָּה)

senses.definition: To reduce the weight or severity of a physical load, cargo, judicial burden, or oppressive labor imposed on someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative, typically with מִן or מֵעַל indicating the person or burden relieved)

senses.definition: To treat someone with disrespect or contempt, or to humble and bring those of high status into dishonor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (transitive with direct object)

senses.definition: To pronounce a curse upon, revile, blaspheme, or speak contemptuously/harmfully against someone or something (including God, parents, rulers, the ground, or neighbors).
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel (transitive with direct object, occasionally used absolutely or with בְּ / לְ)

senses.definition: To be placed under a curse or spoken of as accursed (contrasted with those blessed).
senses.grammatical_frame: Pual (passive counterpart of Piel; finite verb or substantive participle)

senses.definition: To shake or rattle swiftly (used of shaking arrows during a divination ritual).
senses.grammatical_frame: Reduplicated stem (Pilpel) with בְּ + instrument ("arrows")

entries.collocations_and_notes: Contrasts with כָּבֵד ("heavy") and הִקְשָׁה ("make harsh") in contexts of burdens and forced labor (1KI 12:4, 1KI 12:10; 2CH 10:4, 2CH 10:10), and with נִכְבַּדֵּי ("honored ones") in ISA 23:9. In Piel and Pual, it stands in direct opposition to ברך ("bless"; PSA 37:22; PSA 109:28; PRO 30:11) and parallels ארר ("curse"; EXO 22:27). Note the wide stem differentiation: Qal expresses swiftness, subsiding, or low esteem; Niphal expresses ease/triviality; Hiphil expresses lightening a burden or treating lightly; Piel/Pual express verbal cursing; and the reduplicated stem in EZK 21:26 denotes rapid shaking of divination arrows.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A fleeting breath or vapor; by extension, futility, emptiness, or a worthless idol; also the personal name Abel.

senses.definition: A passing breath, puff of air, or vapor; figuratively, the brief and fragile transience of human life and days.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun as subject, predicate, construct modifier (יְמֵי חַיֵּי הֶבְלֶךָ), or object of preposition (בְּ, לְ), sometimes modified by נִדָּף ("driven away").

senses.definition: That which is empty, pointless, or devoid of lasting profit or reliability, applied to futile toil, empty speech, deceptive hope, or paradoxical outcomes.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, predominantly as predicate nominative (זֶה הֶבֶל, הַכֹּל הָבֶל), in superlative construct (הֲבֵל הֲבָלִים), or adverbially (הָבֶל / בַּהֶבֶל).

senses.definition: A worthless idol or false deity considered powerless and unreal.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, chiefly plural in construct or with pronominal suffixes (הַבְלֵיהֶם, הַבְלֵי נֵכָר, הַבְלֵי הַגּוֹיִם, הַבְלֵי שָׁוְא), occasionally singular predicate (הֶבֶל הֵמָּה).

senses.definition: Abel, the second son of Adam and Eve, a shepherd killed by his brother Cain.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper masculine noun, appearing as clause subject, direct object (אֶת הֶבֶל), or object of preposition (אֶל הֶבֶל).

entries.collocations_and_notes: In Ecclesiastes, הֶבֶל recurs in the superlative construct הֲבֵל הֲבָלִים and the refrain הַכֹּל הָבֶל / גַּם זֶה הֶבֶל, frequently paired with רַעְיוֹן רוּחַ ("striving after wind", ECC 4:16). In poetic contexts it parallels רוּחַ ("wind", ISA 57:13), צֵל עוֹבֵר ("passing shadow", PSA 144:4), and רִיק ("emptiness", ISA 30:7). When referring to false gods, it occurs mostly in the plural construct (הַבְלֵי נֵכָר, הַבְלֵי הַגּוֹיִם, הַבְלֵי שָׁוְא) alongside פְסִלִים ("carved images") or לֹא אֵל ("no-god"). In GEN 4:2–9 the identical form serves as the personal name Abel.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To lose moisture, dry up, or wither (of water, vegetation, and bodily or inner vitality), with causative forms meaning to dry something up and certain Hiphil forms in this corpus meaning to be ashamed or put to shame.

senses.definition: Of water, rivers, streams, or floodwaters: to dry up, subside, or lose water completely.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive) with water, stream, or river as subject

senses.definition: Of plants, grass, roots, pastures, or body parts: to wither, shrivel, or lose moisture and vitality; used figuratively of inner strength, a failing limb, or communal hope.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal (intransitive) with vegetation, limbs, bones, or heart as subject; sometimes reinforced by an infinitive absolute

senses.definition: Devoid of moisture; dried, stale, or withered, in contrast to what is fresh, moist, or green.
senses.grammatical_frame: Stative/adjectival use modifying nouns or functioning as predicate adjective

senses.definition: To cause seas, rivers, springs, pools, or living vegetation to dry up or wither.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (causative, taking a direct object) and Piel (causative with pronominal object suffix in NAM 1:4)

senses.definition: To become withered or fail/vanish away (used intransitively of a vine and of human joy).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (intransitive/inchoative)

senses.definition: To feel shame, be disgraced or confounded (as in defeat or idolatry), or to put someone to shame (with "face" as object in 2SA 19:6).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (intransitive, or transitive with direct object in 2SA 19:6)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often contrasted with לַח ("moist, fresh") in descriptions of produce and trees (NUM 6:3; EZK 17:24), and paired with חָרַב ("be parched/laid waste"; JOB 14:11; ISA 42:15; ISA 44:27; JER 50:38; JER 51:36; NAM 1:4) and נָבֵל ("fade"; ISA 40:8). Infinitive absolute + finite verb occurs for emphasis in EZK 17:10 and ZEC 11:17. Notably, this lemma's corpus grouping also includes Hiphil forms (הֹבִישׁ, הֹבַשְׁתָּ) meaning "to put to shame" or "be ashamed/confounded" (2SA 19:6; JER 6:15; JER 10:14; JER 48:1; JER 50:2; ZEC 10:5), where it pairs with בּוֹשׁ (JER 6:15) and חתת ("be shattered/dismayed"; JER 48:1; JER 50:2). In JOL 1:12, הֹבִישׁ appears twice intransitively: first of a withered vine, and second of joy failing or drying up from humanity.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A monumental sacred temple (either as a whole complex or its main central hall) or a grand royal palace.

senses.definition: A sacred building dedicated to God as a place of worship, sacrifice, and divine presence, including both earthly sanctuaries and God's heavenly dwelling.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, commonly in construct (הֵיכַל יְהוָה, הֵיכַל קָדְשְׁךָ) or with pronominal suffixes (הֵיכָלוֹ), often governed by spatial prepositions (בְּ, אֶל, מִן, לִפְנֵי).

senses.definition: The main central chamber or nave of the temple building, distinguished from the inner sanctuary (Most Holy Place).
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun with definite article (הַהֵיכָל), paired or contrasted with דְּבִיר or קֹדֶשׁ, or serving as an architectural reference point (לְפֶתַח הַהֵיכָל, עַל פְּנֵי הַהֵיכָל).

senses.definition: A grand royal residence or imposing public building of a king or city.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular or plural (הֵיכָלוֹת) noun, in construct with מֶלֶךְ ("king") or in royal and urban contexts.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the construct phrase הֵיכַל יְהוָה ("temple of YHWH") and הֵיכַל קָדְשְׁךָ ("your holy temple"). In architectural descriptions of the Jerusalem temple (1KI 6:5, 7:50; EZK 41:4, 41:23), הֵיכָל designates the central main hall inside הַבַּיִת ("the house"), distinct from the inner sanctuary (דְּבִיר / קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים). In poetic and prophetic texts (2SA 22:7, PSA 18:7, PSA 29:9, ISA 6:1, JON 2:8), God's הֵיכָל is the royal-sacred seat from which he hears prayers and exercises rule. In HOS 8:14 (plural הֵיכָלוֹת, parallel to fortified cities and אַרְמְנוֹת "citadels") and AMO 8:3 (שִׁירֹות הֵיכָל), the context admits either royal palaces or sanctuaries.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Deliverance, rescue, or victory from danger and enemies—typically accomplished by God—as well as the resulting state of safety and well-being, or God himself as deliverer.

senses.definition: An act or event of rescue, liberation, or military victory from enemies, peril, or distress, regularly attributed to God (and occasionally performed through a human agent acting with God).
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, singular and plural (יְשׁוּעוֹת 'acts of deliverance/victories'); occurs as object of verbs of performing (עשׂה, פעל), seeing (ראה), or declaring (הודיע), and in construct phrases with the agent or recipient (e.g., 'the deliverance of YHWH', 'day of deliverance').

senses.definition: A condition of safety, stability, vindication, or personal welfare, contrasted with calamity, violence, and ruin.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, singular and plural; appears parallel to nouns for dignity/nobility (נְדִבָה), justice (מִשְׁפָּט), and wisdom/knowledge, or as a symbolic name predicated of city fortifications (חֹמֹתַיִךְ 'your walls').

senses.definition: Metonymic designation or predicate applied directly to God as the protector, refuge, and source of rescue for his people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun with pronominal suffix or in construct after divine titles (אֵל יְשׁוּעָתִי, צוּר יְשֻׁעָתוֹ), as a direct nominal predicate ('I am your deliverance', 'he is my rock and my deliverance'), or in the idiom היה לְ... לִישׁוּעָה ('become deliverance for').

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often governed by verbs of action or perception such as עשׂה ('work/accomplish', EXO 14:13, 1SA 14:45, ISA 26:18), פעל ('do/work', PSA 74:12), ראה ('see', EXO 14:13, 2CH 20:17, PSA 91:16, ISA 52:10), הודיע ('make known', PSA 98:2), and קוה ('wait/hope for', GEN 49:18, ISA 59:11). The plural יְשׁוּעוֹת frequently denotes repeated acts of rescue or triumphant victories (2SA 22:51, PSA 18:51, PSA 42:6, PSA 43:5, PSA 53:7, PSA 74:12, ISA 26:18, ISA 33:6). A poetic form with a final -āh suffix (יְשׁוּעָתָה) appears in PSA 80:3 and JON 2:10. Repeatedly paired with צְדָקָה ('righteousness', PSA 98:2, ISA 51:8), חֶסֶד ('steadfast love', 2SA 22:51, PSA 13:6, PSA 18:51), and עֹז ('strength', PSA 21:2, PSA 118:14, ISA 12:2).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An object cast or drawn to make an impartial decision or selection, and by extension the procedural method of casting lots, the territorial share assigned thereby, or one's appointed destiny.

senses.definition: A marker or object cast or drawn—and by extension the procedure of casting lots itself—used to arrive at an impartial decision, settle disputes, or assign roles, turns, or divisions.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun (singular or plural), object of verbs of casting/placing, subject of verbs of emerging/falling, or adverbial בְּגוֹרָל

senses.definition: A territorial inheritance, share, or allotted portion of land, cities, or property assigned to a tribe, clan, or group.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun, often with pronominal suffix, in construct chains (e.g., עָרֵי גוֹרָלָם, גְּבוּל גּוֹרָלָם), or with הָיָה לְ

senses.definition: One's appointed fate, outcome, or allotted recompense determined by divine decree.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun with pronominal suffix

entries.collocations_and_notes: Common verbal idioms for casting or drawing lots include: הִפִּיל גּוֹרָל / גּוֹרָלוֹת ('cause a lot/lots to fall', 1CH 25:8; 26:13, 14; NEH 11:1; EST 9:24; PSA 22:19; PRO 1:14; ISA 34:17; JON 1:7); נָתַן גּוֹרָלוֹת עַל ('place lots upon', LEV 16:8); הִשְׁלִיךְ גּוֹרָל ('throw a lot', JOS 18:8); יָדָה גוֹרָל ('cast a lot', OBA 1:11). The result of the lot is expressed with נָפַל ('fall [upon]', 1CH 26:14; JON 1:7), יָצָא ('go out [to/for]', NUM 33:54; JOS 19:1, 17, 24, 40; 21:4; 1CH 24:7; 26:14), or עָלָה ('come up [upon/for]', LEV 16:9; JOS 18:11). In EST 9:24, גּוֹרָל explicitly translates the foreign term פּוּר. In JER 13:25 it stands in direct parallelism with מְנָת מִדַּיִךְ ('your measured portion').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A verbal or silent petition, intercession, or devotional address directed to God, as well as a composed liturgical text or psalm.

senses.definition: An earnest spoken or inner address directed to God—whether personal appeal, confession, thanksgiving, or intercession on behalf of others—seeking God's attention, mercy, or intervention.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun; serves as object of verbs of hearing or attending (שׁמע, האזין, פנה אל) or lifting up (נשׂא + בְּעַד 'on behalf of'); occurs as cognate object of התפלל in the reflexive stem ('to pray'); used in construct before place/person nouns (e.g., 'house of prayer', 'prayer of your servant').

senses.definition: A formal devotional poem, psalm, or liturgical song/address directed to God, including recorded prayers and collections of such compositions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, singular (in psalm superscriptions with לְ 'of/for', in liturgical leadership notices with לְ, or parallel to שִׁיר 'song') and plural (תְּפִלּוֹת) for a collected body of compositions.

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired in hendiadys or poetic parallelism with terms for urgent appeal or outcry, including תְּחִנָּה / תַּחֲנוּנִים ('supplication/plea for favor', 1KI 8:28, 1KI 8:45, PSA 55:2, PSA 86:6, PSA 143:1, DAN 9:17), רִנָּה ('ringing cry', 1KI 8:28, PSA 17:1, JER 11:14), and שַׁוְעָה ('cry for help', PSA 102:2). Common verbal collocations are שׁמע ('hear/listen to'), האזין ('give ear to'), פנה אל ('turn toward'), and נשׂא תְפִלָּה בְּעַד ('lift up a prayer on behalf of', 2KI 19:4, JER 11:14). Appears as the cognate object of the verb התפלל in the reflexive/iterative stem (meaning 'to pray', 2SA 7:27, 1KI 8:28-29, 1KI 8:54, NEH 1:6). Associated physical actions include kneeling, spreading hands toward heaven (1KI 8:54, ISA 1:15), fasting in sackcloth (PSA 35:13), and weeping (ISA 38:5). In PSA 109:7, the speaker wishes that an adversary's תְּפִלָּה in the context of judgment might turn into offense/sin (לַחֲטָאָה). Construct expressions such as בֵּית תְּפִלָּה ('house of prayer', ISA 56:7) and תְּפִלַּת הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה ('the prayer of this place', 2CH 6:40, 2CH 7:15) designate the temple as the locus of prayer.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The belly, abdomen, or womb—denoting both the physical midsection/stomach and the reproductive organ of gestation—and figuratively the innermost being as the seat of thoughts, breath, and moral intention.

senses.definition: The physical belly, abdomen, or stomach cavity of the human body, either externally as the front midsection of the torso or internally as the cavity that receives food and drink.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, commonly with pronominal suffix or preposition בְּ/מִן

senses.definition: The womb as the organ of pregnancy and gestation; also used in temporal expressions with מִן ('from the womb' = from birth) and in the construct phrase פְּרִי בֶטֶן ('fruit of the womb' = offspring, children), as well as metaphorically of natural origin.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, often in construct (with אֵם or following פְּרִי) or with preposition מִן/בְּ

senses.definition: The inner self or innermost parts of a person, conceived as the hidden interior where thoughts, words, breath/spirit, and intentions are stored or formed.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun, commonly in construct חַדְרֵי בָטֶן or with pronominal suffix

entries.collocations_and_notes: Common collocations include: פְּרִי בֶטֶן / פְּרִי הַבָּטֶן ('fruit of the womb', i.e., offspring, DEU 7:13; 28:11, 18; 30:9; PSA 127:3; MIC 6:7); מִבֶּטֶן אִמִּי / אִמּוֹ ('from my/his mother's womb', meaning from birth, JDG 16:17; JOB 1:21; 31:18; PSA 22:11; ECC 5:14) and shorter מִבֶּטֶן / מִן הַבָּטֶן ('from the womb / since birth', JDG 13:5; JOB 10:19; PSA 58:4; ISA 44:2; 46:3; 49:1, 5); דַּלְתֵי בִטְנִי ('the doors of my womb', JOB 3:10); חַדְרֵי בָטֶן ('the chambers of the inner being/belly', PRO 18:8; 20:27; 26:22); ר֣וּחַ בִּטְנִי ('the spirit/breath within me', JOB 32:18). Often paired or in parallelism with רֶחֶם ('womb', PSA 22:11; 58:4; ISA 46:3; JER 1:5) and מֵעַיִם ('inward parts/womb', GEN 25:23; NUM 5:22; ISA 49:1). Note that in DEU 7:13 and 28:11, 18; 30:9, 'your בֶּטֶן' refers generally to human reproductive capacity/offspring alongside livestock and crops.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To cry out aloud in distress, lamentation, alarm, or urgent supplication for help, and in causative and passive/reflexive forms to summon or be rallied together.

senses.definition: To cry out urgently to God, a ruler, or allies for rescue, mercy, or intervention in a time of threat, oppression, or need.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), usually with אֶל ("to"), לְ ("to"), directional accusative הַשָּׁמָיִם ("toward heaven"), or direct person object (JDG 12:2, NEH 9:28); also causative stem (Hiphil) used intransitively in poetry (JOB 35:9).

senses.definition: To utter a loud cry of grief, physical pain, terror, or mourning, often in the context of disaster, bereavement, or childbirth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), intransitive, with cognate object זְעָקָה ("outcry"), or with עַל / לְ ("over/for") indicating the cause or object of lament.

senses.definition: To raise a vocal outcry in alarm, protest, or urgent proclamation of wrong or danger.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), absolute or introducing direct speech.

senses.definition: To call people, citizens, or armed forces together; to muster or summon for military action.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative stem (Hiphil), transitive with direct object marker אֶת denoting troops or fighting men.

senses.definition: To be called together, mobilized, or rallied in response to a summons or alarm to pursue or confront an enemy.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal), intransitive, often with purpose infinitive or directional phrase אַחֲרָיו ("after him").

entries.collocations_and_notes: Demonstrates clear stem distinctions in context: the basic active stem (Qal) denotes raising one's voice in outcry, lament, or urgent supplication; the causative stem (Hiphil) ordinarily takes a direct object of troops or citizens to mean summoning or mustering (JDG 4:13, 2SA 20:4), though in poetic parallelism with שִׁוַּע ("cry for help") it functions intransitively for crying out under oppression (JOB 35:9); the passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) denotes being summoned or rallying together in response to a call (JOS 8:16, JDG 6:35, JDG 18:23). In Qal, frequently followed by אֶל ("to"), especially אֶל יְהוָה, or by לֵאמֹר introducing the plea; also takes a cognate accusative זְעָקָה גְדֹלָה וּמָרָה ("a great and bitter outcry," EST 4:1) and pairs with הֵילִיל ("wail," ISA 14:31, JER 47:2, JER 48:31, EZK 21:17).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Hardship, affliction, or calamity that besets a person or community, as well as the acute inner anguish and distress it produces.

senses.definition: An external situation of severe hardship, danger, oppression, or calamity from which a person or nation needs rescue, protection, or endurance; often plural when referring to repeated or varied adversities.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular and plural); frequently in construct after יוֹם ("day") or עֵת ("time"), as object of prepositions בְּ ("in") or מִן ("from, out of"), or as subject of verbs of coming, approaching, or rising.

senses.definition: Acute emotional or physical anguish, torment, or panic experienced internally, often depicted as seizing a person like labor pains or paired with terms for sorrow, darkness, and constraint.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular); used in construct with נֶפֶשׁ ("soul/life"), paired with nouns of grief or constraint, or as subject of verbs of seizing (הֶחֱזִיק, אָחַז).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in fixed temporal construct phrases: בְּיוֹם צָרָה / צָרָתִי ("in the day of [my] distress," GEN 35:3, PSA 77:3, PSA 86:7, PRO 25:19, JER 16:19, OBA 1:12) and בְּעֵת צָרָה / צָרָתָם ("in the time of [their] distress," JDG 10:14, NEH 9:27, ISA 33:2, JER 14:8, DAN 12:1). Commonly governed by מִן / מִכֹּל ("from [every] distress") with verbs of rescue, salvation, or redemption such as הִצִּיל, הוֹשִׁיעַ, פָּדָה, and הוֹצִיא (1SA 10:19, 1SA 26:24, 1KI 1:29, PSA 25:22, PSA 34:7, PSA 34:18, PSA 54:9, PSA 143:11). Frequently paired with רָעוֹת ("evils/calamities," DEU 31:17, 1SA 10:19), צוּקָה / מְצוּקָה ("anguish/constraint," PRO 1:27, ISA 8:22, ZEP 1:15), יָגוֹן ("sorrow," PSA 116:3), and חִיל / חֲבָלִים ("birth pangs/writhing," JER 6:24, JER 49:24). In NEH 9:27 it stands alongside the verb וַיָּצֵרוּ ("they oppressed/harassed them").

entries.core_meaning_summary: To direct one's eyes or attention toward a person, object, direction, or situation, whether in physical looking, attentive consideration, or caring/judicial regard.

senses.definition: To direct one's visual gaze toward a person, object, or direction; to look or stare.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (active stem), absolute or with directional adverb, אֶל, לְ, עַל, בְּ, or direct object; Niphal (once, ISA 5:30) with לְ in the same active sense; occasionally with 'eye' as subject

senses.definition: To turn one's mind or attention to something so as to examine, observe, or contemplate it.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (active stem), absolute, with direct object, or with אֶל + noun
