senses.definition: To look upon someone or a situation with notice, concern, favor, or moral/judicial assessment (most often predicated of God in prayer or complaint).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil (active stem), imperative or imperfect, absolute or with direct object, אֶל, or לְ

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs overwhelmingly in the Hiphil stem, with one Niphal occurrence (ISA 5:30) showing the same active sense ('look') rather than a passive meaning. Frequently paired in parallelism or sequence with רָאָה ('see') and occasionally with חָזָה ('behold') or שָׁמַע ('hear'). Common prepositional complements include אֶל ('toward, at'), לְ ('to, toward'), עַל ('upon'), and בְּ ('on, from'), as well as directional ה- (הַשָּׁמַיְמָה) and אַחֲרֶיךָ ('behind you'). In poetic and wisdom texts, עַיִן ('eye') can serve as the grammatical subject (PSA 92:12; PRO 4:25). In laments and prayers, imperative forms (הַבֵּט / הַבִּיטָה) regularly appeal to God to take notice of suffering or covenant faithfulness.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The eastern compass direction or side, and the dry or forceful wind blowing from the east.

senses.definition: The eastern compass point, direction, side, or border.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (often with directional suffix -āh), used adverbially, as object of prepositions (לְ, מִן), or as genitive in construct phrases (דֶּרֶךְ הַקָּדִים, פְּאַת קָדִים, גְּבוּל קָדִימָה, רוּחַ הַקָּדִים)

senses.definition: A strong, dry, or scorching wind blowing from the east; also used figuratively for empty or futile things.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, either standing alone substantively as subject/object/genitive or as genitive following רוּחַ ('wind')

entries.collocations_and_notes: In directional and boundary descriptions (especially EZK 40–48), frequently takes the directional suffix -āh (קָדִימָה, occasionally spelled קָדִמָה) and appears in fixed phrases such as דֶּרֶךְ הַקָּדִים(ָה) ('facing/toward the east'), הַפֹּנֶה קָדִים/קָדִימָה ('facing east'), פְּאַת קָדִים/קָדִימָה ('the east side'), and גְּבוּל קָדִימָה ('east border'). Notably, the construct phrase רוּחַ (הַ)קָּדִים exhibits two distinct uses: 'east wind' in meteorological and narrative contexts (EXO 10:13; EXO 14:21; JER 18:17; EZK 19:12; JON 4:8), vs. 'east side/quarter' in architectural measurement (EZK 42:16). In wisdom and prophetic poetry (JOB 15:2; HOS 12:2), 'east wind' is paired with רוּחַ ('wind') as a figure for empty or futile pursuits.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To flee or hurry away from danger, pursuit, or a location (Qal), or to put to flight and cause to pass across from end to end (Hiphil).

senses.definition: To run away, escape, or take flight from danger, pursuit, mistreatment, or authority, often secretly or toward a place of refuge.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal; intransitive, frequently followed by מִפְּנֵי / מִלִּפְנֵי / מִן (source of threat) and/or אֶל, אַחֲרֵי, or locative expression (destination)

senses.definition: To hurry away, depart swiftly, or leave a post or place quickly, whether in response to urgent dismissal, abandonment of an unsupported duty, or swift movement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal; imperative (often with ethical dative לְךָ + אֶל) or finite verb + לְ

senses.definition: Figuratively of time or mortal life: to pass away rapidly, slip away, or vanish without remaining.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal; intransitive with non-human or abstract subject (e.g., days, mortal human compared to a shadow)

senses.definition: Causative of the Qal: to drive away, scatter, or put enemies or an adversary to flight.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil; transitive with direct object (אֶת or pronominal suffix)

senses.definition: Of a structural crossbar: to run through, pass across, or extend continuously from one end to the other.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil participle; with מִן ... אֶל marking span

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with מִפְּנֵי ('from before / from the presence of'), מִלִּפְנֵי (JON 1:10), or מִן (2SA 19:10, JOB 27:22) to mark the threat or authority escaped from, and with אֶל, אַחֲרֵי (1SA 22:20), לְ (NEH 13:10), or directive -āh (2SA 4:3) to mark destination. Often occurs in narrative chains alongside נוּס ('flee', JDG 9:21), מָלַט Niphal ('escape', 1SA 19:12, 1SA 19:18), הָלַךְ, and יָצָא (JER 52:7). Appears with an infinitive absolute for emphasis (בָּרוֹחַ יִבְרָח, JOB 27:22) and with the reflexive ethical dative לְךָ in urgent commands to leave (בְּרַח לְךָ, NUM 24:11, AMO 7:12). Clear stem contrast between the basic intransitive Qal ('flee, hurry away, vanish') and the causative/transitive Hiphil ('put to flight, drive away' in 1CH 12:16, JOB 41:20, or 'run/extend across from end to end' of a crossbar in EXO 26:28).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The subterranean realm of the dead beneath the earth, also personified as the insatiable, threatening power of death and the grave.

senses.definition: The subterranean realm or abode of the dead beneath the earth, conceived as a dark, deep, gated, and silent place of no return to which mortals descend at death and where remembrance and praise of God cease.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine); used as locative or goal with directive -āh, prepositions (בְּ, לְ, עַד, מִן), or in construct phrases denoting parts/depths (e.g., שַׁעֲרֵי שְׁאוֹל, פִּי שְׁאוֹל)

senses.definition: Death and the grave personified as an insatiable, devouring, or entangling adversary, or metonymically for mortal peril and the brink of death from which one seeks deliverance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (feminine); subject of active verbs, partner in covenant/address, or nomen rectum in idioms of peril and power (e.g., חֶבְלֵי שְׁאוֹל, יַד שְׁאוֹל, בֶּטֶן שְׁאוֹל)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Grammatically feminine in agreement (e.g., רָגְזָה in ISA 14:9; לֹא תִשְׂבַּעְנָה with אֲבַדּוֹ in PRO 27:20). Regularly occurs with verbs of downward motion such as יָרַד ('go down') and הוֹרִיד ('bring down'), frequently marked with directive -āh (שְׁאֹלָה) or prepositions בְּ, לְ, עַד, and מִן. Commonly paired in poetic parallelism with מָוֶת ('death'), בּוֹר ('pit'), שַׁחַת ('pit/corruption'), אֲבַדּוֹן ('destruction/Abaddon'), אֶרֶץ תַּחְתִּית ('nether earth'), and רְפָאִים ('shades of the dead'). Notable construct and figurative phrases include שְׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּית / תַּחְתִּיָּה ('lowest Sheol'), שַׁעֲרֵי שְׁאוֹל ('gates of Sheol'), פִּי שְׁאוֹל ('mouth of Sheol'), בֶּטֶן שְׁאוֹל ('belly of Sheol'), חֶבְלֵי שְׁאוֹל ('cords of Sheol'), מְצָרֵי שְׁאוֹל ('distresses of Sheol'), and יַד שְׁאוֹל ('hand/power of Sheol').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A feminine noun (here in construct and suffixed forms) denoting work, labor, skilled craftsmanship, official or cultic service, a crafted item, or entrusted property.

senses.definition: Work, labor, or daily occupation, whether God's creative activity or human agricultural, household, and routine toil; frequently in the legal prohibition כָּל מְלֶאכֶת עֲבֹדָה ('any laborious/occupational work') on sacred days.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in construct or with pronominal suffix, commonly object of עָשָׂה or with מִן after שָׁבַת

senses.definition: Skilled craftsmanship, artisan trade, or organized construction work, especially in fabricating sanctuary furnishings or building temples, fortifications, and royal structures.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct noun before material, artisan role, or structure (e.g., מְלֶאכֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ, מְלֶאכֶת הַחוֹמָה) or with suffix

senses.definition: A manufactured article or finished piece of workmanship made from a given material.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct noun before material noun (מְלֶאכֶת עוֹר)

senses.definition: Official duty, administrative business, cultic temple service of priests and Levites, or a divinely mandated commission.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct noun before institutional/personal authority (e.g., מְלֶאכֶת בֵּית יְהוָה, מְלֶאכֶת הַמֶּלֶךְ, מְלֶאכֶת יְהוָה) or with suffix

senses.definition: Material goods, belongings, or property entrusted to or owned by another person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct noun with בְּ after שָׁלַח יָדוֹ ('put his hand to') before possessor noun (בִּמְלֶאכֶת רֵעֵהוּ)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In this lemma sample (the construct/suffixed form מְלֶאכֶת / מְלַאכְתּ-), the noun frequently occurs as the object of עָשָׂה ('to do/perform work'), כָּלָה ('to finish', GEN 2:2), שָׁבַת ('to cease/rest from', GEN 2:2–3; Hiphil in 2CH 16:5), and נָצַח ('to oversee/supervise', 1CH 23:4, EZR 3:8). Fixed expressions include כָּל מְלֶאכֶת עֲבֹדָה ('any laborious/occupational work') in festival Sabbath prohibitions (LEV 23, NUM 28–29), מְלֶאכֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ / מְלֶאכֶת בֵּית יְהוָה ('the work/service of the sanctuary/house of the LORD'), and מְלֶאכֶת עוֹר ('leatherwork/article of leather', LEV 13:48). Note that in EXO 35:35, 1KI 7:14, and NEH 5:16 the absolute form מְלָאכָה also co-occurs in the immediate context.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A masculine noun denoting either the eastern direction and eastern regions/peoples in space, or antiquity, ancient times, and temporal priority in time.

senses.definition: The eastern cardinal direction, eastern side, or eastern territory; with מִן (מִקֶּדֶם) it indicates location on the east, movement from or toward the east, or with לְ- relative position east of a landmark.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, commonly with מִן (מִקֶּדֶם, often + לְ-) or in construct (אֶרֶץ קֶדֶם, הַרְרֵי קֶדֶם)

senses.definition: In the construct phrase בְּנֵי קֶדֶם ('sons/people of the east'), the inhabitants or nomadic tribes of the eastern territories relative to Israel.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in construct phrase בְּנֵי קֶדֶם

senses.definition: Ancient times, primeval antiquity, or the distant past; used in construct expressions for former eras or enduring realities, with prepositions (מִקֶּדֶם, מִנִּי קֶדֶם, כְּקֶדֶם), or adverbially to mean long ago.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in construct (e.g., יְמֵי קֶדֶם, אֱלֹהֵי קֶדֶם), with מִן or כְּ, or adverbial

senses.definition: Prior to or before in time, marking what precedes a set of events or works.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun functioning as a temporal preposition before a noun phrase (קֶדֶם מִפְעָלָיו)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears with the preposition מִן (מִקֶּדֶם, poetic מִנִּי קֶדֶם) in both spatial and temporal senses, and with כְּ (כְּקֶדֶם). Spatial collocations include מִקֶּדֶם לְ- ('east of [a place]'), contrast with מִיָּם ('on the west', GEN 12:8) or מֵאָחוֹר ('from behind/the west', ISA 9:11), אֶרֶץ קֶדֶם ('land of the east', GEN 25:6, alongside directional קֵדְמָה), הַרְרֵי קֶדֶם ('mountains of the east', NUM 23:7), and the recurring group name בְּנֵי קֶדֶם ('peoples of the east', JDG 6:33, JDG 7:12, 1KI 5:10, JOB 1:3, EZK 25:4). Temporal collocations include construct chains such as יְמֵי קֶדֶם ('days of old'), יַרְחֵי קֶדֶם ('months of old', JOB 29:2), מַלְכֵי קֶדֶם ('ancient kings', ISA 19:11), אֱלֹהֵי קֶדֶם ('God of ancient times', DEU 33:27), and שְׁמֵי קֶדֶם ('ancient heavens', PSA 68:34), often paired in parallelism with עוֹלָם ('everlasting/ages past'), מֵאָז ('from long ago'), and רֵאשִׁית ('beginning').

entries.core_meaning_summary: Physical violence, destructive aggression, or grave social and legal wrongdoing inflicted unjustly upon others.

senses.definition: Physical aggression, bloodshed, or destructive force committed against people, cities, or lands, including warfare and murder; used in construct with either the perpetrator or the victim, and as an urgent cry for help against attack.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; subject, object of verbs of filling or coming, governed by min ('from') or lə ('for'), construct with victim (objective) or agent (subjective), or exclamatory cry; paired with šōḏ ('devastation') or kəlê ('weapons').

senses.definition: Unjust, oppressive, or deceitful conduct in social, economic, or judicial spheres, including extortion, ill-gotten gain, and wrongful acts contrasted with righteousness and innocence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural ḥămāsîm); object of verbs of doing, loving, concealing, or removing; governed by bəlōʾ/lōʾ ('without/no') in idioms with kap ('hand'); paired with mirmāh ('deceit'), šeqer ('falsehood'), or contrasted with mišpāṭ ('justice') and ṣəḏāqāh ('righteousness').

senses.definition: Cruel, unscrupulous, or malicious character when used as an attributive modifier in construct after nouns denoting a person, witness, or hostile attitude.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural ḥămāsîm) in construct after a head noun (e.g., ʾîš 'man', ʿēḏ 'witness', śinʾāh 'hatred', or participle yîp̄ēaḥ 'breathing out').

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs as the object of mālēʾ ('be full of', GEN 6:11, GEN 6:13, EZK 8:17, MIC 6:12) and in the paired expression ḥāmās wāšōḏ ('violence and devastation/plunder', JER 6:7, JER 20:8, EZK 45:9; cf. HAB 2:17). Idioms for innocence or guilt include lōʾ ḥāmās bəḵappay ('no wrong/violence in my hands', 1CH 12:18, JOB 16:17; cf. ISA 59:6). In construct phrases, it takes either an objective genitive naming the victim (JDG 9:24, JOL 4:19, OBA 1:10, HAB 2:17) or a subjective/attributive genitive (EZK 12:19; ʾîš ḥāmās / ḥămāsîm 'violent/unscrupulous person', PSA 140:5, PSA 140:12, PRO 16:29; ʿēḏ ḥāmās 'malicious witness', EXO 23:1). Note the plural form ḥămāsîm in PSA 140:5 and PRO 4:17 denoting repeated or intense acts of violence. Can also function as a direct exclamation/cry for rescue (HAB 1:2, JER 20:8).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A solemn promise or conditional pledge made to a deity, and by extension the sacrificial offering or payment owed to fulfill that pledge.

senses.definition: A solemn verbal promise or conditional commitment made to God (or another deity, JER 44:25), binding the speaker to an action, dedication, or devotion once made or confirmed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; cognate object of nāḏar ('to vow'), object of verbs of hearing, performing (ʿāśāh), fulfilling (šillēm), confirming (hēqîm), or annulling (hēp̄ēr); often followed by lə ('to' a deity) and direct speech introduced by lēʾmōr.

senses.definition: The concrete sacrificial animal, gift, or sanctuary meal brought and offered in discharge of a vow, regularly distinguished from or paired with freewill offerings (nəḏāḇāh).
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular or plural); object of verbs of bringing (hēḇîʾ), eating (ʾāḵal), offering/fulfilling (pillēʾ, šillēm), or governed by lə ('for'); listed alongside burnt offerings, peace offerings, tithes, and freewill offerings (nəḏāḇāh).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly appears as the cognate object of the verb nāḏar ('to vow', e.g., GEN 28:20, NUM 6:2, NUM 21:2, DEU 23:22, 1SA 1:11, 2SA 15:8, ECC 5:3, JON 1:16). Fulfilling a vow is expressed primarily with šillēm in the intensive stem (Piel: 'pay, fulfill', e.g., DEU 23:22, 2SA 15:7, PSA 22:26, PSA 50:14, PSA 66:13, PRO 7:14, ECC 5:3, ISA 19:21) or pillēʾ in the intensive stem (Piel: 'fulfill/perform a vow', LEV 22:21, NUM 15:3; cf. hiphil hiplîʾ 'make a special vow', LEV 27:2, NUM 6:2). In NUM 30, paired with ʾissār ('binding obligation/pledge') and subject to hēqîm ('confirm/establish') or hēp̄ēr ('annul'). In cultic law, frequently paired with nəḏāḇāh ('freewill offering', LEV 7:16, LEV 22:21, LEV 22:23, NUM 15:3, NUM 29:39, DEU 12:6, DEU 12:17). While most contexts address vows to YHWH, JER 44:25 applies the term to vows directed to another deity.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The left side, direction, or hand, as well as figurative deviation when paired with the right.

senses.definition: The left-hand side or direction relative to a person, object, or path, including geographical orientation toward the north when facing east.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (used with prepositions מִן, עַל, אֶל, or adverbially with verbs of turning and motion, often paired with יָמִין)

senses.definition: The left hand or left arm of a person (often personified).
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine/masculine noun with pronominal suffix, or genitive after יַד (יַד שְׂמֹאל)

senses.definition: Moral or behavioral deviation (in the merism "right or left" with verbs of turning aside from instruction or command) or the unfavorable inclination contrasted with wisdom.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverbial noun paired with יָמִין after verbs of turning aside (סור, נטה), or with prepositional לְ contrasted with יָמִין

entries.collocations_and_notes: Almost always paired or contrasted with יָמִין ("right"). Frequently occurs in the merism יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל ("right and left") to express comprehensive extent or strict adherence without deviation. Appears in construct with יַד ("hand") in יַד שְׂמֹאלוֹ / יַד שְׂמֹאולֶךָ ("his/your left hand"). In east-facing geographical descriptions (GEN 14:15, JOS 19:27, EZK 16:46), the left side corresponds to the north. Both plene (שְׂמֹאול) and defective (שְׂמֹאל) spellings occur.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A physical shadow or shade cast by an object blocking sunlight, used figuratively both for protective shelter/refuge and for fleeting, transitory existence.

senses.definition: An area of darkness or relief from sunlight and heat cast by a tree, rock, cloud, mountain, structure, or sundial steps, including lengthening evening shadows.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular צֵל, plural צְלָלִים, construct צֵל / צִלְלֵי); used as subject, direct object, or in prepositional phrases (בְּצֵל, לְצֵל) often contrasted with חֹרֶב ('heat').

senses.definition: Protective shelter, refuge, or patronage (extended by God, a roof, a city, a ruler, wisdom, or wealth), often portrayed through imagery of wings, hands, or spreading tree branches.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prepositional phrase בְּצֵל + genitive/pronoun (often with verbs of dwelling, hiding, or taking refuge such as חָסָה, יָשַׁב, שָׁכַן, סָתַר, כִּסָּה) or predicate/subject noun (NUM 14:9; PSA 121:5).

senses.definition: An emblem of brevity, transience, and fleeting human existence, likened to a shadow that stretches out, passes by, or flees.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate noun (צֵל יָמֵינוּ) or object of comparison introduced by כְּ־ (כַּצֵּל, כְּצֵל עוֹבֵר) with verbs of motion or duration (בָּרַח, הָלַךְ, עָבַר, הֶאֱרִיךְ).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Exhibits geminate inflection with singular suffixed forms צִלִּי, צִלּוֹ, צִלָּהּ, צִלָּם, צִלְךָ (and צִלֲלוֹ in JOB 40:22) and plural forms צְלָלִים / צִלְלֵי. Common idioms include בְּצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ ('in the shadow of your wings', PSA 17:8; 36:8; 63:8), חָסָה בְצֵל ('take refuge in the shadow of', JDG 9:15; ISA 30:2), and יָשַׁב בְּצֵל ('dwell in the shadow of', EZK 31:6; HOS 14:8; JON 4:5). In 2KI 20:10–11 and ISA 38:8, הַצֵּל denotes the cast shadow moving across the steps of Ahaz. EZK 17:23 and 31:6, 12 blend literal tree shade with political shelter under an imperial power.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Falsehood, emptiness, or futility in speech, conduct, religious devotion, or outcome.

senses.definition: Untruth, deceit, or fabricated claims in testimony, rumor, speech, or prophetic/divinatory visions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, used as direct object of verbs of speaking, hearing, or seeing/prophesying, or as second noun in construct chains (e.g., עֵד שָׁוְא, שֵׁמַע שָׁוְא, מַחֲזֵה שָׁוְא)
senses.semantic_domain: Truth and Falsehood / Speech and Prophecy

senses.definition: Lack of substance, reality, value, or worth, describing vain idols, insincere offerings, futile deliverance, or empty existence.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, used as predicate, object of verbs of trusting or looking, or as second noun in construct chains (e.g., הַבְלֵי שָׁוְא, מִנְחַת שָׁוְא)

senses.definition: Without effect, to no purpose, or for an empty and improper end, including the empty or false invocation of God's name and fruitless human or disciplinary effort.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adverbial prepositional phrase לַשָּׁוְא or predicative/interrogative שָׁוְא / עַל מַה שָּׁוְא modifying a clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the prepositional phrase לַשָּׁוְא ("in vain / for falsehood / to an empty end"), especially with נָשָׂא ("lift up [the name/soul]"). Regularly paired or paralleled with כָּזָב ("lie"), שֶׁקֶר ("falsehood"), מִרְמָה ("deceit"), אָוֶן ("iniquity/emptiness"), הֶבֶל ("vapor/vanity"), and תָּפֵל ("insipid/unsubstantial"). Common construct expressions include מְתֵי שָׁוְא ("false/worthless men"), הַבְלֵי שָׁוְא ("worthless idols/vanities"), עֵד שָׁוְא ("false witness"), and מַחֲזֵה שָׁוְא ("false vision"). Orthographic variants in the sample include בַּשָּׁיו (JOB 15:31) and הַשָּׁוא (ZEC 10:2).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A dove or pigeon (used literally, sacrificially, and figuratively as an emblem of beauty, affection, or mourning), and also the masculine proper name of the prophet Jonah.

senses.definition: A dove or pigeon, noted for flying, nesting in rock clefts or chasms, cooing or moaning, and offered (especially as young birds, בֶּן/בְּנֵי יוֹנָה) in temple sacrifices.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular יוֹנָה, plural יוֹנִים, construct plural יוֹנֵי); often in construct chain בֶּן־יוֹנָה / בְּנֵי (הַ)יּוֹנָה as object of sacrificial verbs (הֵבִיא, הִקְרִיב, לָקַח, עָשָׂה) or following comparative כְּ־.

senses.definition: A figurative or poetic designation derived from the bird: a term of endearment for a beloved woman, a comparison for beautiful eyes, or an element in a psalm superscription.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun with 1cs suffix (יוֹנָתִי) as vocative, plural predicate (עֵינַיִךְ יוֹנִים), or singular construct (יוֹנַת) after preposition עַל in a superscription.

senses.definition: Jonah, an Israelite prophet (identified in 2KI 14:25 as son of Amittai from Gath-hepher) and the protagonist of the Book of Jonah.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine proper noun used as subject, direct object (with אֶת), or object of prepositions (עַל, אֶל, לְ־).

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in sacrificial law in the construct plural/singular phrases בְּנֵי (הַ)יּוֹנָה and בֶן יוֹנָה ('young of a dove') paired as an alternative with תֹּרִים ('turtledoves'). In poetry and prophecy, serves as a standard comparison for moaning/cooing (הגה, המה), trembling flight, or naivety (פּוֹתָה אֵין לֵב in HOS 7:11). In Song of Songs, יוֹנָתִי is paired with רַעְיָתִי and תַמָּתִי as an affectionate address. The construct יוֹנַת in PSA 56:1 appears in the superscription עַל יוֹנַת אֵלֶם רְחֹקִים, whose precise liturgical or musical reference cannot be determined from the text alone. As a masculine proper name (2KI 14:25; Book of Jonah), it identifies the prophet Jonah son of Amittai.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To swallow down or engulf physically (as by a creature, the earth, or deep water), and in derived stems to destroy completely, squander, overwhelm, or confound.

senses.definition: To take something down through the throat into the stomach, or figuratively to ingest and consume food, people, or wealth (including a great fish swallowing Jonah, thin ears of grain devouring healthy ones, or an enemy/stranger consuming victims or produce).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal) + direct object (animals, grain, people, or wealth)

senses.definition: To engulf and take down completely out of sight, used of the earth opening to swallow people and their possessions, of deep water overwhelming a person, or of criminals compared to Sheol swallowing victims alive.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal) with earth, deep water, or persons as subject + direct object (often paired with 'opened its mouth')

senses.definition: To ruin, wipe out, or bring to total destruction—applied to cities, fortifications, individuals, or death itself; in the passive stem, to be destroyed or overwhelmed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive/factitive active stem (Piel) + direct object (city, person, citadels, death), or passive stem (Pual) without expressed agent in JOB 37:20

senses.definition: To use up or squander accumulated goods and resources recklessly, contrasted with keeping treasure and oil in a wise household.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive/factitive active stem (Piel) + pronominal direct object referring to treasure and oil

senses.definition: To throw into confusion, obliterate direction or plans, or bring wisdom to nothing; in passive and reflexive/passive stems, to be overwhelmed and befuddled (by wine) or to vanish in bewilderment (of sailors' skill).
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive/factitive active stem (Piel) + abstract object (paths, counsel); passive stem (Niphal) + causal מִן ('from/by wine'); reflexive/passive stem (Hithpael) with abstract subject ('all their wisdom')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Clear stem distribution across the attested forms: the basic active stem (Qal) denotes concrete or vivid swallowing and engulfing (by ears of grain, a great fish, a sea-monster, strangers consuming produce, or the earth, deep water, and Sheol); the intensive/factitive active stem (Piel) and its passive (Pual) express total destruction, ruin, abolition (such as abolishing death in ISA 25:8), reckless squandering of wealth (PRO 21:20), or confounding plans and paths (ISA 3:12, ISA 19:3); while the passive/middle stem (Niphal) in ISA 28:7 and the reflexive/passive stem (Hithpael) in PSA 107:27 describe being overwhelmed or confounded (by wine or disorientation). Frequently parallels verbs of eating/devouring (אָכַל), crushing/ruining (הָמַם, שִׁחֵת, הִשְׁחִית), putting to death (הֵמִית), sweeping away (שָׁטַף), or causing to stray/stagger (תָּעָה, מַתְעִים). In NUM 16:30 and DEU 11:6 it follows the idiom 'the earth/ground opened its mouth' (פָּצְתָה אֶת פִּיהָ). In JOB 37:20 the concise poetic clause with the passive Pual form (יְבֻלָּע) expresses the dire consequence ('be destroyed/overwhelmed') of daring to speak before God.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A coarse woven bag or sack used for carrying goods such as grain and silver, and a rough garment of the same material typically worn as a sign of mourning, distress, penitence, or supplication.

senses.definition: A woven bag or sack used to hold, transport, and empty provisions such as grain and bundles of silver.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular and plural) with possessive suffixes, governed by prepositions of location or direction (אֶל 'into', בְּ 'in') or as the direct object of 'empty' (הֵרִיק)

senses.definition: Coarse woven fabric or an article made from it, grouped with wooden utensils, garments, and leather as everyday work items subject to ritual impurity regulations.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun in a coordinated list of materials introduced by מִן ('from/of') and אוֹ ('or')

senses.definition: A rough garment worn around the loins, directly against the skin, or over the body as an expression of mourning, distress, penitence, humility, or supplication (and in one prophetic sign-act as a simple waist-garment, or metaphorically as a dark covering over the sky).
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular and plural) as direct object of verbs of wearing, girding, covering, or removing, as object of בְּ ('in'), or as the second member of construct phrases (לְבוּשׁ שָׂק, מַחֲגֹרֶת שָׂק, חֲגֻרַת שָׂק)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with verbs of putting on, girding, covering, or removing: שִׂים בְּמָתְנַיִם / עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ ('place on the loins / on one's flesh', GEN 37:34, 1KI 20:31, 1KI 21:27), חָגַר שַׂק / שַׂקִּים ('gird on sackcloth', 2SA 3:31, JER 4:8, LAM 2:10, EZK 27:31, JOL 1:8), הִתְכַּסָּה / כִּסָּה בַּשַּׂק ('cover oneself with sackcloth', 2KI 19:2, ISA 37:1, JON 3:6), פִּתַּח שַׂק ('untie/loose sackcloth', PSA 30:12, ISA 20:2), and הֵסִיר שַׂק ('remove sackcloth', EST 4:4). Commonly accompanies tearing garments (קָרַע בְּגָדִים/שִׂמְלֹתָיו), fasting (צוֹם), ashes/earth on the head (אֵפֶר, עָפָר, אֲדָמָה), shaved heads/beards (קָרְחָה), weeping, and lamentation (סָפַד, הֵילִיל). In ISA 20:2, untying the śaq from the loins leaves the prophet naked, indicating it functioned there as a lone waist-garment. In ISA 50:3, it serves as a metaphor for dark gloom clothing the heavens.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Sentence-initial particle indicating possibility, tentative hope, or hypothetical supposition ('perhaps, maybe'), along with a homographic proper name for a river in Elam.

senses.definition: Marks an uncertain possibility, supposition, or apprehended contingency ('perhaps', 'maybe', 'what if').
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial adverbial particle preceding nominal, participial, or imperfect verbal clauses

senses.definition: Expresses hopeful expectation or a tentative wish for a favorable outcome, often following a proposed action, plea, or prayer ('perhaps', 'it may be that', 'hopefully').
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial particle introducing an imperfect or nominal clause expressing an anticipated result

senses.definition: Introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition ('suppose', 'if perhaps', or 'unless' when followed by an apodosis introduced by כִּי עַתָּה).
senses.grammatical_frame: Clause-initial particle introducing a conditional protasis with a qatal or yiqtol verb

senses.definition: Proper name of a waterway or canal (Ulai) in the province of Elam near Susa, grouped under this lemma by spelling.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun in construct phrase עַל אוּבַל אוּלָי ('beside the Ulai canal')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Almost always stands at the beginning of its clause and governs imperfect/yiqtol verbs (for future possibilities or hopes), participles/nominal clauses (GEN 43:12, JOS 9:7, 1KI 18:27, LAM 3:29), or perfect/qatal verbs (NUM 22:33). Frequently follows imperatives or cohortatives expressing an attempted action aimed at an uncertain favorable outcome (e.g., GEN 16:2, NUM 22:6, NUM 23:3, 1SA 6:5, 1SA 14:6, JON 1:6). Note that DAN 8:2 contains the homographic geographical name אוּלָי (Ulai) grouped under this entry in the corpus.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To drive out, expel, or banish from a place, home, or office; in the Qal passive participle, to be divorced; and of water or earth, to toss up or be churned into agitation.

senses.definition: To forcefully drive out, expel, or banish a person, group, or nation from a place, land, dwelling, or community.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive stem (Piel) transitive with direct object and prepositional phrase of separation (מִן, מִפְּנֵי, מֵעַל פְּנֵי, מֵאֵת פְּנֵי); passive of the intensive stem (Pual) in JOB 30:5 ('be driven out')

senses.definition: To remove or dismiss a person from holding an official role or position.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active intensive stem (Piel) with direct object + מִן + infinitive construct (מִהְיוֹת כֹּהֵן, 'from being priest')

senses.definition: Put away or separated from one's husband; used substantively or adjectivally for a divorced woman.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple passive participle (Qal passive participle feminine singular, גְּרוּשָׁה), alone or with מֵאִישָׁהּ ('from her husband')

senses.definition: Of water or surging land: in the simple active stem, to cast up or fling forth sediment; in the middle/passive stem, to be tossed, churned up, or driven into restless surging.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal) transitive with direct object (וַיִּגְרְשׁוּ מֵימָיו רֶפֶשׁ וָטִיט, ISA 57:20); middle/passive stem (Niphal) intransitive of sea or overflowing land (ISA 57:20, AMO 8:8)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In the Piel stem it regularly takes a direct object (person, people, or nation) and a prepositional phrase marking the point of departure or exclusion (מִן, מִפְּנֵי, מֵעַל פְּנֵי, מֵאֵת פְּנֵי, מִלְּפָנֶיךָ). In EXO 11:1 the Piel infinitive absolute precedes the Piel finite verb (גָּרֵשׁ יְגָרֵשׁ) for emphasis. The Qal passive participle גְּרוּשָׁה appears consistently in legal/cultic contexts as a term for a divorced woman (often paired with אַלְמָנָה, 'widow'). ISA 57:20 contrasts the passive/middle Niphal participle (נִגְרָשׁ, 'tossed about') with the active Qal (וַיִּגְרְשׁוּ מֵימָיו רֶפֶשׁ וָטִיט, 'its waters cast up mire and mud').

entries.core_meaning_summary: Small in physical size or weight, young in age or junior in birth order, minor in importance, or low in social rank (also used as a personal name).

senses.definition: Small in physical size, dimensions, weight, or quantity (of animals, objects, weights, or food).
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective (attributive, predicate, or substantive plural construct קְטַנֵּי אָרֶץ; genitival כְּלֵי הַקָּטָן)

senses.definition: Young in age or junior in birth order (younger or youngest sibling or child, often contrasted with גָּדוֹל or בְּכִירָה).
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective (attributive with kinship terms, substantive with definite article הַקָּטָן/הַקְּטַנָּה, or comparative with מִן in EZK 16:61)

senses.definition: Modest, minor, or limited in scope or significance (of a request).
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective modifying an abstract noun (שְׁאֵלָה אַחַת קְטַנָּה)

senses.definition: Low or humble in social standing, prominence, or age, used substantively opposite גָּדוֹל to encompass an entire community without exception.
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantive adjective in the prepositional merism מִגָּדוֹל וְעַד קָטָן or מִקְּטַנָּם וְעַד גְּדוֹלָם

senses.definition: Used as a personal or ancestral name ('Hakkatan').
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper name with definite article in patronymic phrase בֶּן הַקָּטָן

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently contrasted directly with גָּדוֹל ('large/old/great') or בְּכִירָה ('firstborn'). Common in the fixed merism מִגָּדוֹל וְעַד קָטָן / לְמִקְטַנָּם וְעַד גְּדוֹלָם ('from the greatest to the least') to denote totality across all ranks and ages. In EZR 8:12 (בֶּן הַקָּטָן), it appears as a personal/family name ('Hakkatan').

entries.core_meaning_summary: Emotional dread or terror, awe-inspiring majesty, and especially reverent devotion and ethical piety toward God.

senses.definition: An acute feeling of alarm, dread, or terror provoked by physical danger, divine wrath, or an overwhelming situation.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun; used as cognate accusative after the verb יָרֵא, in construct before a feared object (יִרְאַת שָׁמִיר וָשָׁיִת), or with a pronominal suffix denoting the awe/dread due to God

senses.definition: An awe-inspiring or terrifying quality possessed by something seen.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun in existential/possessive clause with לְ (וְיִרְאָה לָהֶם)

senses.definition: Reverent awe, devotion, and loyal piety toward God, characterized by moral restraint, turning away from evil, and faithful worship.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun; commonly in construct before a divine name (יְהוָה, אֱלֹהִים, שַׁדַּי), with a subjective or objective pronominal suffix, or governing a direct object with אֵת (ISA 29:13)

senses.definition: By metonymy, the revealed religious teaching, discipline, or body of pious duty associated with revering the LORD.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular construct noun (יִרְאַת יְהוָה) functioning as the object of teaching (לִמֵּד) or parallel to divine ordinances (מִשְׁפָּטִים)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most frequently appears in construct with divine names (יִרְאַת יְהוָה, יִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים, יִרְאַת שַׁדַּי). Takes the preposition בְּ ('in/with fear') for manner of conduct or worship (NEH 5:9, PSA 2:11, PRO 16:6, ISA 11:3), and מִן ('from/out of fear') for motivation or separation (JOB 22:4, ISA 63:17). In ISA 29:13 it takes a direct object marker (יִרְאָתָם אֹתִי, 'their fearing me'), and in JON 1:10 it serves as a cognate accusative with the verb יָרֵא (וַיִּירְאוּ ... יִרְאָה גְדוֹלָה). In wisdom literature (PRO 1:7, PRO 8:13, PRO 14:27, PRO 15:33) it is regularly equated with rejecting evil, receiving discipline, and gaining life.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Free from guilt, liability, or obligation; morally or legally innocent, especially in the phrase 'innocent blood.'

senses.definition: Cleared of culpability, liability, or binding obligation toward another person, an oath, or bloodshed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate adjective, often with מִן specifying the oath, curse, or bloodguilt

senses.definition: Exempted or excused from a royal summons for public labor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Predicate adjective negated by אֵין

senses.definition: Morally upright or judicially innocent of wrongdoing, frequently paired with צַדִּיק (righteous) or used substantively for an innocent victim; also in the negated form אִי נָקִי (not innocent).
senses.grammatical_frame: Substantive or construct adjective (e.g., נְקִי כַפַּיִם)

senses.definition: Modifying דָּם (blood) to designate the life or blood of blameless persons unjustly killed or condemned.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive adjective or genitive plural modifying דָּם (blood)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears with the orthographic variant נָקִיא in JOL 4:19. Common collocations include דָּם נָקִי / דַּם הַנָּקִי / דַּם נְקִיִּם (innocent blood, frequently as object of שָׁפַךְ 'to shed' or בִּעֵר 'to purge'), הָיָה נָקִי מִן (to be free/cleared from an oath or bloodguilt), and נְקִי כַפַּיִם (innocent of hands, parallel to בַר לֵבָב in PSA 24:4). In JOB 22:30, אִי נָקִי negates the adjective ('one who is not innocent').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A wooden or metal crossbar used either to join and brace the tabernacle frames or to bolt and secure the gates of a city or stronghold.

senses.definition: A long wooden rod or crossbar, overlaid with gold and fitted through rings, used to connect and hold together the upright frames of the tabernacle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (sing. and pl.), often with עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים or tabernacle parts

senses.definition: A heavy bar (of wood, bronze, or iron) set across gate doors to lock a city, fortress, or palace; used figuratively of insurmountable barriers of strife or of the earth/depths enclosing someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, commonly coordinated with דְּלָתַיִם (doors) or מַנְעֻלִים (locks)

senses.definition: Poetic usage in a lament over Moab reaching as far as Zoar, referring either to Moab's protective bars/defenses or to its fleeing fugitives.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun with feminine possessive suffix + עַד (as far as)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Very frequently paired with דְּלָתַיִם (double doors) and sometimes מַנְעֻלִים (locks/bolts) in descriptions of city fortifications, and with קְרָשִׁים (planks/frames) in tabernacle construction. In ISA 15:5, בְּרִיחֶהָ עַד צֹעַר occurs in a lament over Moab's destruction and is contextually ambiguous between Moab's defensive bars/barriers and its fleeing inhabitants.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Fierce, burning anger or wrath—predominantly divine wrath in the phrase חֲרוֹן אַף—and in one poetic simile possibly blazing heat.

senses.definition: Intense, burning anger or wrath, most often God's fierce judgment directed against people or nations, frequently expressed in the construct phrase חֲרוֹן אַף.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, most commonly in construct with אַף (anger) or alone as object/subject of divine judgment verbs

senses.definition: Blazing heat or fierce burning (or personified wrath) paired in contrast with חַי (green/raw) in a simile about thorns heating a pot before being swept away.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun following כְּמוֹ, contrasted with כְּמוֹ חַי

entries.collocations_and_notes: Predominantly appears in the construct chain חֲרוֹן אַף (or with pronominal suffix חֲרוֹן אַפּוֹ / אַפֶּךָ), especially in phrases like שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַף (turn back from fierce anger) and מִפְּנֵי חֲרוֹן אַף (before the fierce anger), and alongside עֶבְרָה and זַעַם (PSA 78:49, ISA 13:9, 13:13). In JER 25:38 it is parallel with חֲרוֹן אַפּוֹ as חֲרוֹן הַיּוֹנָה. In PSA 58:10 it is contrasted with חַי (raw/green) in a cooking-pot and thorn-fire simile.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To count, reckon, or assign/appoint (as a verb across active, passive, and intensive stems), and an allotted portion or share (as a feminine noun).

senses.definition: To count, enumerate, or muster items, people, livestock, or days, including assembling and counting out troops for battle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Active simple verb (Qal) + direct object or בְּ + object

senses.definition: To be counted, numbered, or reckoned as belonging to a group.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive simple verb (Niphal), often with אֶת (with)

senses.definition: To assign, allot, or appoint a portion, responsibility, hardship, or creature to a specific task or person; passively, to be placed in charge over something.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive verb (Piel active; Pual passive participle) + direct object, often with לְ or עַל

senses.definition: An allotted share or portion, especially of sacrificial meat, festive food, or personal provisions given or sent to someone.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (מָנָה, pl. מָנוֹת), often with לְ or as object of נָתַן / שָׁלַח

entries.collocations_and_notes: As a verb, the simple active stem denotes counting or mustering (with direct object or בְּ in 1CH 21:17; with מִסְפָּר in 1CH 27:24 and PSA 147:4; parallel to סָפַר in 1KI 8:5), the passive stem denotes being counted or reckoned among (with אֶת in ISA 53:12), and the intensive stem denotes appointing or assigning roles, provisions, or creatures (with לְ in JOB 7:3 and DAN 1:5; with עַל in 1CH 9:29 and DAN 1:11). As a feminine noun (מָנָה, pl. מָנוֹת), it frequently denotes food or sacrificial portions given or sent (לְתֵת מָנָה / שִׁלְחוּ מָנוֹת / מִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A worm or grub that consumes plants or corpses (also used figuratively of lowliness), and, in ritual textile phrases, a dyed spun yarn or material.

senses.definition: A worm or larva that feeds on grapevines or dead bodies; used metaphorically in PSA 22:7 to express extreme lowliness and humiliation in contrast to a human being.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, singular (collective in DEU 28:39 and ISA 66:24; predicate nominative in PSA 22:7)

senses.definition: In construct phrases with שָׁנִי (תּוֹלַעַת [הַ]שָּׁנִי or שְׁנִי [הַ]תּוֹלָעַת), a spun and dyed yarn or fabric material used alongside תְּכֵלֶת, אַרְגָּמָן, and שֵׁשׁ for sanctuary hangings, priestly vestments, and purification rituals.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in construct chain with שָׁנִי (as head or genitive)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most occurrences in the Torah belong to the fixed textile collocations תּוֹלַעַת (הַ)שָּׁנִי (Exodus, Numbers) and שְׁנִי (הַ)תּוֹלָעַת (Leviticus), consistently listed alongside תְּכֵלֶת, אַרְגָּמָן, and שֵׁשׁ. Outside those ritual/textile contexts, it denotes a destructive worm or grub.
entries.uncertainty_note: The verses in the sample do not specify the exact biological species of the worm in 1a, nor do they explicitly name the color hue or dye source of the textile material in 1b beyond its pairing with שָׁנִי and grouping with תְּכֵלֶת and אַרְגָּמָן.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An interrogative adverb asking location, direction, origin, or selection ('where?', 'which?', 'from where?').

senses.definition: Interrogative adverb inquiring after the location or presence of a person or thing ('where?'), either before a noun phrase or with attached pronominal suffixes; used rhetorically in PRO 31:4 regarding strong drink.
senses.grammatical_frame: Interrogative adverb standing before a noun phrase or taking pronominal suffixes

senses.definition: In combination with the demonstrative זֶה (ʾê zeh), asks 'where?' or 'which?' regarding a route, place, person, or quality, often rhetorically to deny existence or adequacy.
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound interrogative אֵי זֶה before nouns, verbs, or pronouns

senses.definition: In combination with מִזֶּה (ʾê mizzeh), asks about a person's origin, starting point, or people/homeland ('from where?', 'from which?').
senses.grammatical_frame: Compound interrogative אֵי מִזֶּה before verbs, pronouns, or a noun (עַם)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Takes pronominal suffixes in the form אַיֶּ- / אַיָּ- (e.g., אַיֶּכָּה 'where are you?', אַיּוֹ 'where is he?', אַיָּם 'where are they?'). Very frequently compounded as אֵי זֶה ('which / where?') and אֵי מִזֶּה ('from where?'). In rhetorical questions (ISA 50:1; ISA 66:1; PRO 31:4), it implies nonexistence or unsuitability.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A vast, deep body of water, referring either to ocean depths or to primordial and subterranean waters beneath the earth.

senses.definition: The deep waters or abyssal troughs of the sea, characterized by depth, surging waves, and vastness, and often parallel with 'sea' or 'many waters'.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (singular or plural), subject, object, or object of prepositions (e.g., בְּ, אֶל, עַל)

senses.definition: Primordial or subterranean watery depths beneath the earth, serving as the source of springs, rivers, floodwaters, and fertilizing moisture (and used in simile for abundant water in PSA 78:15).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (singular or plural), often in construct after 'springs/fountains of' (מַעְיְנֹת / עִינֹת) or 'surface of' (פְּנֵי)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in both singular (תְּהוֹם) and plural (תְּהֹמוֹת / תְּהוֹמוֹת). Frequently paired in poetic parallelism with יָם ('sea'), מַיִם ('waters'), or מַעְיָנוֹת ('springs'), and modified by רַבָּה ('great/abundant'). Notice feminine agreement even on the singular form in GEN 7:11 (רַבָּה), DEU 33:13 (רֹבֶצֶת), EZK 31:4 (רֹמְמָתְהוּ), and AMO 7:4 (רַבָּה), though masculine in JOB 28:14 (אָמַר).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Gentilic adjective and noun denoting a Hebrew person or the Hebrew people, and once a masculine personal name (Ibri).

senses.definition: Belonging to the Hebrew people, modifying nouns denoting an individual, man, youth, brother, or enslaved person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Gentilic adjective (masculine singular/plural and feminine singular עִבְרִיָּה), attributive or appositional to personal nouns

senses.definition: A member or the collective body of the Hebrew people (including feminine plural "the Hebrew women"), especially in contrast to Egyptians or Philistines.
senses.grammatical_frame: Gentilic substantive, masculine plural (עִבְרִים / הָעִבְרִים) and feminine plural (הָעִבְרִיֹּת)

senses.definition: Masculine personal name of a Levite descended from Merari.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper personal name in a genealogical list

entries.collocations_and_notes: Used both as a gentilic adjective modifying terms for men, servants, youths, and women (with feminine singular עִבְרִיָּה and feminine plural עִבְרִיּוֹת) and as a substantive, predominantly in contexts where Israelites/descendants of Abram are distinguished from or interacting with non-Israelites (Egyptians, Philistines) or in legal provisions concerning enslaved fellow countrymen (EXO 21:2, DEU 15:12, JER 34:9, JER 34:14). Frequently appears in the divine title אֱלֹהֵי הָעִבְרִים ("God of the Hebrews") in Exodus. In 1CH 24:27, עִבְרִי occurs once as a masculine personal name among the Merarite Levites.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A proper name for a distant maritime trading center (and of a class of ocean-going ships associated with it), a personal name, and the name of a lustrous precious stone.

senses.definition: A distant maritime region, port, or city reached by sea from Joppa, associated with islands/coastlands, kings, merchants, and exports of beaten silver and exotic luxury goods.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun (place/region), often as destination with directional suffix or after מִן, or in construct after 'kings of', 'merchants of', 'daughter of'

senses.definition: In the construct expression 'ships of Tarshish', a class of large ocean-going merchant vessels capable of long voyages and heavy cargo (even when bound for other destinations such as Ophir).
glosses: Tarshish (as a type of sea-going ship)
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in construct chain after אֳנִי or אֳנִיּוֹת ('ships of')

senses.definition: A personal or ancestral name: a descendant of Javan in genealogies, and one of the seven high officials of Persia and Media.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun (personal name) in genealogical and court lists

senses.definition: A lustrous precious stone set in gold in the fourth row of the priestly breastpiece and used as a visual comparison for the gleaming appearance of the wheels in Ezekiel's visions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun (singular), standalone in gem lists or in construct after עֵין / אֶבֶן ('appearance of / stone of')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the construct phrase אֳנִי / אֳנִיּוֹת תַּרְשִׁישׁ ('ships of Tarshish'), which functions both for fleets associated with that port and as a designation for large sea-going vessels (even when sailing to Ophir in 1KI 22:49). In EZK 10:9 and EZK 28:13 it is associated with אֶבֶן ('stone') and listed among precious stones. Also takes directional he (תַּרְשִׁישָׁה) in 1CH 1:7 and JON 1:3.
entries.uncertainty_note: The texts do not identify the exact geographical location of the port or the specific mineralogical identity of the gemstone beyond its luster and grouping with other precious stones.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A heap of stones or rubble, a wave of the sea, and once in poetic parallelism an enclosed spring or water source.

senses.definition: A piled mound or cairn of stones, erected as a boundary/covenant witness, raised over a grave, or accumulated in fields.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun (singular גַּל, often with אֲבָנִים; plural גַּלִּים in HOS 12:12)

senses.definition: A heap of rubble or ruins resulting from the destruction of cities or buildings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular (לַגָּל) and plural (גַּלִּים) noun, typically after שִׂים, הָיָה לְ, or שָׁאָה

senses.definition: A surging wave or billow of the sea.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun (גַּלִּים) with possessive suffixes or construct הַיָּם

senses.definition: An enclosed spring or pool of water, paralleling a locked garden and a sealed fountain.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun modified by passive participle נָעוּל

entries.collocations_and_notes: Displays two major groups of meanings: (1) a mound or heap of stones (singular גַּל in GEN 31 and JOS 7–8, often paired with אֲבָנִים or מַצֵּבָה as a covenant witness or burial cairn; plural גַּלִּים for ruined cities or stone piles in fields) and (2) sea waves (consistently masculine plural גַּלִּים with pronominal suffixes or in construct with הַיָּם, frequently paired with מִשְׁבָּרִים "breakers" or verbs of roaring and stilling). In SNG 4:12, singular גַּל appears once in strict parallelism between גַּן נָעוּל ("a locked garden") and מַעְיָן חָתוּם ("a sealed spring"), denoting an enclosed spring or water source.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To bind around, strap, or wrap, used for saddling pack or riding animals, fastening headgear or cords, bandaging wounds or brokenness, and exercising governing restraint.

senses.definition: To fasten a saddle or harness onto a donkey in preparation for riding or carrying provisions.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal active (with direct object אֶת + animal, often with לְ for beneficiary) and Qal passive participle

senses.definition: To wrap, tie, or bind headgear onto the head, cords around merchandise, or a covering over faces.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal active (direct object + לְ or עַל, or with בְּ instrumental) and Qal passive participle

senses.definition: To bandage, splint, or bind up physical injuries and fractures, or figuratively to soothe and restore those suffering grief or affliction (passive in Pual: to be bound up).
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal active (direct object or לְ + injured person/part), Piel participle + לְ (PSA 147:3), and Pual passive perfect (EZK 30:21)

senses.definition: To hold in check, govern, or act as a restorer and leader over a community.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal imperfect (intransitive/absolute) and Qal active participle used substantively

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs predominantly in the Qal stem (active and passive participle) across three main domains: saddling donkeys (frequently with חֲמוֹר or אָתוֹן and לְ marking the rider), wrapping headgear (מִגְבָּעוֹת, פְאֵר) or cords (חֲבָלִים), and binding up wounds or fractures (paired with רָפָא in JOB 5:18, ISA 30:26, HOS 6:1, and contrasted with שָׁבַר/נִשְׁבֶּרֶת in ISA 30:26, ISA 61:1, EZK 30:21, EZK 34:4, EZK 34:16). In EZK 30:21, the passive Pual perfect (לֹא־חֻבְּשָׁה, "it has not been bound up") is followed directly by the active Qal infinitive construct (לְחָבְשָׁהּ, "to bind it up") with חִתּוּל ("bandage"). In PSA 147:3, the Piel participle (מְחַבֵּשׁ לְעַצְּבוֹתָם) parallels רֹפֵא לִשְׁבוּרֵי לֵב, functioning analogously to the Qal in ISA 61:1. In JOB 34:17 and ISA 3:7, Qal forms extend from binding/restoring to restraining or exercising governing authority (paralleled in ISA 3:7 with קְצִין עָם, "commander of the people").

entries.core_meaning_summary: As a noun, marsh reeds and the geographical designation for the Sea of Reeds (יַם־סוּף); as a homographic Qal verb, to come to an end, cease, or perish.

senses.definition: Reeds or marsh plants growing along the water's edge of the Nile.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular collective noun with definite article (בַּסּוּף, בְּתוֹךְ הַסּוּף)

senses.definition: Proper geographical designation, predominantly in the construct phrase יַם־סוּף ("Sea of Reeds", also יָמָּה סּוּף) denoting the body of water crossed at the exodus and bordering the wilderness and Edom, and once standalone סוּף in the Arabah (DEU 1:1).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun in construct chain (יַם־סוּף) or standalone toponym (מוֹל סוּף)

senses.definition: To come to an end, cease to exist, or be swept away in destruction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal perfect and imperfect, intransitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: This lemma entry groups both nominal/toponymic forms (סוּף, "reeds" and geographical designations) and homographic Qal verbal forms (סָפוּ, יָסוּף, יָסֻפוּ, "to come to an end, perish"). In EXO 2:3 and EXO 2:5, סוּף denotes marsh vegetation along the Nile bank alongside גֹּמֶא ("papyrus"). Most occurrences appear in the geographical compound יַם־סוּף ("Sea of Reeds", associated with Israel's departure from Egypt and also situated near Ezion-geber/Edom in 1KI 9:26). In DEU 1:1, מוֹל סוּף ("opposite Suph") appears without יַם in an Arabah itinerary; whether this is an abbreviated reference to the sea or a distinct Transjordanian locality cannot be determined from that verse alone. The Qal verb (EST 9:28, PSA 73:19, ISA 66:17, AMO 3:15) is consistently intransitive and pairs with תָּמַם ("be finished"), אָבַד ("perish"), or עָבַר ("pass away").

entries.core_meaning_summary: An indefinite pronoun denoting any object, matter, or deed whatsoever ('anything' or 'something'; with negation, 'nothing').

senses.definition: Any item, action, or matter at all, used in negated clauses (with לֹא, אַל, or אֵין) to mean 'nothing', as well as in questions, negative oaths, or statements of impossibility.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indefinite pronoun as object or subject in negative, interrogative, oath, or impossibility clauses

senses.definition: Any unspecified object or matter in an affirmative or conditional clause.
senses.grammatical_frame: Indefinite pronoun as object or nomen rectum in affirmative or conditional clauses

senses.definition: Anything of worth or account, occurring with the preposition לְ after a negated passive verb of reckoning (נֶחְשָׁב).
glosses: of any value (negated: of no account)
senses.grammatical_frame: Preposition לְ + מְאוּמָה complementing passive verb of reckoning (נֶחְשָׁב)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most frequently appears in negative clauses with לֹא, אַל, or אֵין as the direct object or subject (often corresponding to English 'anything' in negative scope, i.e., 'nothing'). Notable constructions include מְאוּמָה כִּי אִם ('nothing except', GEN 39:6, GEN 39:9), כָל מְאוּמָה ('anything at all', 2SA 3:35), מְאוּמָה מִן ('anything from', DEU 13:18), מְאוּמָה רָּע ('anything harmful', JER 39:12), and the construct phrase מַשַּׁאת מְאוּמָה ('a loan of anything', DEU 24:10). Note the occasional dagesh in מְאוּמָּה (GEN 22:12).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The internal organs or abdominal cavity of a living creature, extending to the reproductive organs as the source of offspring and to the inner being as the seat of deep emotion.

senses.definition: The physical internal viscera, bowels, intestines, or digestive stomach cavity of a human or large sea creature.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun (anatomical)

senses.definition: The womb of a mother or the reproductive body of a father viewed as the physical origin of children and descendants.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun, typically with מִן or בְּ, or in construct phrases denoting offspring

senses.definition: The inward parts conceived figuratively as the seat of intense emotion—such as compassion, yearning, grief, or distress—or of inner devotion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun (figurative/psychological), often subject of verbs of churning or roaring (הָמָה, חמרמר) or after בְּתוֹךְ

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs exclusively in the plural form (often with pronominal suffixes or in construct מְעֵי). Frequently paired in poetic parallelism with בֶּטֶן ('belly/womb'), קֶרֶב ('inward parts'), and לֵב ('heart'). Common idioms include יָצָא מִמְּעֵי ('to issue from the body/womb of', indicating biological descent, e.g., GEN 15:4, 2SA 16:11; cf. יְצִיאֵי מֵעָיו in 2CH 32:21 and צֶאֱצָאֵי מֵעֶיךָ in ISA 48:19), and הָמוּ מֵעַי ('my inward parts stir/yearn', SNG 5:4, ISA 16:11, JER 31:20).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The day immediately following a preceding day, event, or designated occasion ('the next day', 'the day after').

senses.definition: The calendar day immediately following the day previously mentioned in the narrative or legal instruction.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in absolute state, usually preceded by מִן (מִמָּחֳרָת) or in construct יוֹם הַמָּחֳרָת

senses.definition: The day immediately following a specified occasion, festival, or time reference (such as the Sabbath, Passover, the new moon, or a given day).
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in construct state (מָחֳרַת) or with pronominal suffix (מָחֳרָתָם), governed by מִן or לְ

entries.collocations_and_notes: Almost always introduced by a preposition, predominantly מִן (מִמָּחֳרָת / מִמָּחֳרַת) or less often לְ (לְמָחֳרַת / לְמָחֳרָתָם). Frequently appears in the narrative transition formula וַיְהִי מִמָּחֳרָת ('and it happened on the next day', e.g., GEN 19:34, EXO 18:13, 1SA 11:11, JER 20:3) and with the verb שׁכם ('to rise early on the next day', EXO 32:6, JDG 6:38, 1SA 5:3, 1SA 5:4). Contrasts directly with בַּיּוֹם / בְּיוֹם ('on the [first] day', LEV 7:16, LEV 19:6, 2SA 11:12).

entries.core_meaning_summary: An expression of gratitude and praise to God—whether through vocal song, sacrificial thank-offering, or public confession—and, by extension, an organized choir singing thanksgiving.

senses.definition: Vocal or musical praise and gratitude offered to God, often accompanying worship, song, or festive celebration.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, often governed by בְּ or לְ or paired with terms for song and voice (קוֹל, שִׁיר, רִנָּה, זִמְרָה)

senses.definition: A ritual sacrifice of thanksgiving brought to the sanctuary as a subcategory of well-being offerings (שְׁלָמִים), accompanied by bread cakes and eaten on the day of offering.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun in construct chains with זֶבַח or as direct object of sacrificial verbs (הִקְרִיב, זָבַח, הֵבִיא, קִטֵּר)

senses.definition: Open acknowledgment of wrongdoing and of God's righteous judgment, paired with giving glory to God and declaring what one has done.
senses.grammatical_frame: Object of נָתַן ('give תּוֹדָה to God')

senses.definition: An organized choir or processional company singing thanksgiving during a public dedication ceremony.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular and plural תּוֹדֹת) as object of העמיד (Hiphil: 'appoint/station') or subject of הלך ('march')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Shows a fluid connection between vocal thanksgiving and cultic thank-offering (e.g., PSA 50:14, PSA 50:23, PSA 100:1, JER 33:11, where vocal praise and temple sacrifice intersect). In sacrificial contexts, commonly appears in זֶבַח [הַ]תּוֹדָה, זֶבַח תּוֹדַת שְׁלָמָיו, זִבְחֵי תוֹדָה, or coordinated as זְבָחִים וְתוֹדוֹת. In praise contexts, frequently paired with שִׁיר, רִנָּה, זִמְרָה, קוֹל, or musical instruments.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A watercraft or seagoing vessel used for maritime travel, trade, and naval expeditions, also personified for seafaring merchants.

senses.definition: A vessel built for traveling on water, ranging from swift reed skiffs to large ocean-going merchant or military ships.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun (singular and plural); often after preposition בְּ ('in/by ships') or in construct chains (e.g., אֳנִיּוֹת תַּרְשִׁישׁ)

senses.definition: Maritime trading fleets addressed or depicted by personification as weeping merchants or carriers of Tyre's commerce.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine plural noun; vocative with imperative הֵילִילוּ ('wail') or subject of mercantile predicates

entries.collocations_and_notes: Feminine noun occurring most frequently in the plural אֳנִיּוֹת. Common fixed phrase: אֳנִיּוֹת תַּרְשִׁישׁ ('ships of Tarshish', denoting large long-distance merchant vessels). Also appears in אֳנִיּוֹת אֵבֶה ('reed boats/skiffs', JOB 9:26) and אַנְשֵׁי אֳנִיּוֹת ('seamen/sailors', 1KI 9:27). Verbs commonly paired with it include עָשָׂה ('build/make'), נִשְׁבַּר/שִׁבֵּר ('be wrecked/shatter'), הָלַךְ/בּוֹא ('sail/come'), and יָרַד ('go down' to the sea or disembark).

entries.core_meaning_summary: In the simple active stem, to make a solemn, binding religious promise to a deity or to pledge a specific offering by such a promise.

senses.definition: In the simple active stem, to bind oneself by a solemn religious promise to a deity—often conditional upon divine help—to perform an act, devotion, or sacrifice.
senses.grammatical_frame: simple active verb (Qal); used intransitively, with cognate object נֶדֶר/נְדָרִים, or with indirect object לְ ('to God/YHWH') and often an אִם conditional clause

senses.definition: In the simple active stem, to promise or dedicate a particular offering, freewill gift, or action by means of a solemn vow.
senses.grammatical_frame: simple active verb (Qal) + direct object (e.g., קָרְבָּן, נְדָבָה, or relative אֲשֶׁר) + optional לְ ('to')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Only the simple active stem (Qal) is attested in these texts. Very frequently governs the cognate accusative נֶדֶר/נְדָרִים ('vow a vow') and takes indirect recipient לְ (usually לַיהוָה or לֵאלֹהִים, once to another deity in JER 44:25). Often introduces a conditional 'if... then...' commitment (אִם) and is paired with שִׁלֵּם ('pay/fulfill' what was vowed).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A temporary hut or booth made of light materials or branches, used for everyday or military shelter, annual ritual observance, an animal's covert, or figurative protection and royal lineage.

senses.definition: A temporary, lightly built shelter, hut, or pavilion providing shade or basic cover for livestock, watchmen, soldiers in camp, or travelers.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun; often object of עָשָׂה ('make') or locative with בְּ ('in') and יָשַׁב ('sit/dwell')

senses.definition: A temporary leafy booth inhabited by Israelites for seven days in the seventh month, and in construct with חַג ('festival') the name of that annual pilgrimage festival.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine plural noun; in חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת ('Festival of Booths') or with יָשַׁב בַּסֻּכּוֹת ('dwell in booths')

senses.definition: A thicket or concealed lair where a predatory animal crouches in ambush.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine singular noun; locative with בְּ ('in') and יָשַׁב ('sit/lie') parallel to מְעוֹנוֹת ('dens')

senses.definition: Figurative canopy or refuge formed by dark storm clouds or divine protection, or a modest/ruined dwelling representing David's fallen dynasty.
senses.grammatical_frame: feminine noun; used metaphorically as predicate/object of שִׂית ('set'), locative with צָפַן בְּ ('hide in'), or in construct סֻכַּת דָּוִיד

entries.collocations_and_notes: Feminine noun commonly paired with verbs of building or making (עָשָׂה) and inhabiting (יָשַׁב בְּ). In plural with the definite article, חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת is the fixed title of the seven-day autumn pilgrimage festival in the seventh month. In 2SA 22:12 and its parallel PSA 18:12, paired with סִתְרוֹ ('his hiding place') and thick rain clouds surrounding God.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Compensation paid for work, service, or rental use, extended to divine or moral reward for deeds, and also attested as a personal name.

senses.definition: Payment or agreed compensation given to a worker, nurse, priest, or military force in return for labor or service rendered.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun; often object of נתן ('give') or predicate with היה ('become') or construct with worker/recipient

senses.definition: Fee paid for the temporary hire of an animal or for passage on a ship.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun; with preposition בְּ ('for/at its hire'), object of נתן ('give/pay'), or in construct with בְּהֵמָה ('beast')

senses.definition: Benefit, blessing, or favorable outcome granted by God or resulting from toil and faithful action, including children or deliverance.
senses.grammatical_frame: masculine noun; often existential with יש / אין ('there is / is no') + לְ ('for'), or with pronominal suffix

senses.definition: Masculine personal name borne by the father of one of David's warriors and by a son of Obed-edom.
senses.grammatical_frame: proper masculine noun; in patronymic phrase בֶּן־שָׂכָר or genealogical list

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently serves as the direct object of נתן ('give/pay wages') and שקל ('weigh out wages'), or predicate with היה / יש / אין ('become/there is/there is no reward or wage'). Construct chains specify the recipient or source: שְׂכַר עֲבָדֶיךָ ('wages of your servants'), שְׂכַר הָאָדָם ('wages of human labor'), שְׂכַר הַבְּהֵמָה ('hire of livestock'). Also parallels פְּעֻלָּה ('work/recompense') in ISA 62:11 and נַחֲלַת יְהוָה ('heritage of YHWH') in PSA 127:3. In Chronicles, the identical form appears as a masculine personal name.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The flank, rear side, innermost recess, or remotest reaches of a territory, building, region, the earth, or the underworld pit.

senses.definition: The flank or far border of a tribal territory adjacent to a neighboring region.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun with 3ms suffix (ירכתו) plus prepositional על

senses.definition: The back wall, rear end, or private innermost recesses of a tent-shrine, temple, chamber, or dwelling.
senses.grammatical_frame: Dual absolute (ירכתים) or dual construct (ירכתי) before architectural nouns (המשׁכן, הבית), often with directional ימה ('westward') or prepositions ב, ל, מן

senses.definition: The far, remote, or uttermost recesses of hill country, mountains, the northern horizon, the earth, or the subterranean pit.
senses.grammatical_frame: Dual construct (ירכתי) governing geographic or cosmic nouns (הר אפרים, לבנון, צפון, ארץ, בור) after prepositions ב, מן, אל, עד

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs almost exclusively in the dual (absolute יַרְכָתַיִם or construct יַרְכְּתֵי), with only one singular suffixed instance (יַרְכָתוֹ, GEN 49:13). Frequently combines with directional or spatial nouns: הַמִּשְׁכָּן ('the tabernacle') + יָמָּה ('westward'), בַיִת ('house/temple'), צָפוֹן ('north/Zaphon'), אָרֶץ ('earth'), and בּוֹר ('pit'). In PSA 48:3 and ISA 14:13, יַרְכְּתֵי צָפוֹן refers to the far/sacred reaches of Mount Zion or the mount of assembly.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Voluntary abstention from food as an act of personal humility, grief, or supplication, as well as a publicly proclaimed or calendrical religious observance.

senses.definition: Abstinence from food accompanied by grief, repentance, humility, or earnest prayer, resulting in physical weakening when prolonged.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, used as cognate object of צום or after prepositions ב ('in/with') and מן ('from', indicating physical effect)

senses.definition: A publicly proclaimed, consecrated, or scheduled communal day or period of fasting, sometimes paired with a solemn assembly.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular (or plural צמות) noun, direct object of קרא ('proclaim') or קדשׁ Piel ('consecrate'), or in construct (יום צום, צום הרביעי)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Regularly co-occurs with weeping (בכי), mourning/lamentation (מספד, אבל), sackcloth (שׂק), ashes/earth (אפר, אדמה), prayer (תפלה), and the expression עִנָּה נַפְשׁוֹ ('afflict one's soul', PSA 35:13; ISA 58:3, 5). Verb collocations include צום ('fast', cognate accusative in 2SA 12:16), קרא צום ('proclaim a fast'), and קדשׁ צום ('consecrate a fast', JOL 1:14; JOL 2:15). ISA 58:5–6 contrasts ritual self-affliction with ethical justice as the 'fast' YHWH chooses, and ZEC 8:19 lists four calendrical fasts of specific months to be turned into joyful festivals.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To come in front of or go ahead, hence to meet (favorably or hostilely), greet with aid or worship, precede in order, or act beforehand.

senses.definition: To come out to meet, welcome, or attend someone favorably with food, care, blessings, mercy, or worshipful offerings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel transitive verb taking a personal object or פָּנִים ('face'), often with instrumental ב ('with') denoting what is brought

senses.definition: To confront, advance against, or come upon someone in hostility, military assault, or sudden calamity and distress.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel transitive verb with hostile agents, weapons, or afflictions as subject and a person, city, or פָּנִים as object

senses.definition: To go in front in a procession, arrive early, anticipate a point of time, or act beforehand.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel intransitive (or with temporal object / infinitive with ל) denoting spatial priority or temporal earliness

senses.definition: In the causative Hiphil stem, either to take the initiative toward someone first (putting them in one's debt to repay, JOB 41:3) or to advance upon and confront/overtake someone (of disaster, AMO 9:10).
senses.grammatical_frame: Hiphil active verb: transitive with personal suffix object (JOB 41:3), or paired with נגשׁ Hiphil and prepositional בעד (AMO 9:10)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In the evidence packet, only Piel (23 verses) and Hiphil (2 verses: JOB 41:3; AMO 9:10) stems appear; no Qal forms are attested. Piel frequently takes direct personal objects or פָּנִים ('face/presence') to express greeting with provisions (לחם ומים, DEU 23:5; NEH 13:2; ISA 21:14), approaching God in worship (PSA 95:2; MIC 6:6), or hostile encounter (PSA 17:13; 2SA 22:6, 19). Temporal uses in Piel take an infinitive with ל (JON 4:2) or time words (נשׁף, אשׁמרות, PSA 119:147–148).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To feel pity, compassion, or protective concern for someone or something, especially so as to spare from harm or loss.

senses.definition: To look with pity or compassion upon people (or a city and its inhabitants and livestock) and consequently withhold punishment, violence, or destruction, or to appeal for such mercy.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb + עַל (or used absolutely, often with עַיִן 'eye' as grammatical subject)

senses.definition: To feel concern, attachment, or regret over losing or leaving behind an inanimate possession or plant.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal verb + עַל with a non-human object (with a person or עַיִן 'eye' as grammatical subject)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Attested exclusively in the Qal stem across all 24 occurrences. In 15 of the 24 verses, the grammatical subject is עַיִן ('eye', feminine singular), producing formulas such as לֹא תָחוֹס עֵינְךָ/עֵינִי עַל ('my/your eye will not spare/pity'); in 1SA 24:11, וַתָּחָס עָלֶיךָ either has an implied feminine subject ('[my eye] spared you') or functions impersonally. Frequently coordinated with חָמַל ('have compassion/spare') and רִחֵם ('show mercy') in contexts of judgment and warfare.

entries.core_meaning_summary: First light of daybreak before full morning, used literally as a time marker and poetically for radiant emergence, swift expanse, or hopeful illumination.

senses.definition: The first light of daybreak at the end of night, marking the start of morning and daytime activity.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, often with definite article as subject of עלה ('ascend') or in temporal prepositional phrases (עד, כ, מן, ב + עלות השחר)

senses.definition: Dawn personified or used in poetic comparison for gleaming early rays, rapid expansion across the sky, dependable arrival, or radiant appearance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun in construct chains (עפעפי שחר, כנפי שחר, בן שחר), object of עור Hiphil ('awaken'), or in similes with כ / כמו

senses.definition: Figuratively, enlightenment, hopeful outcome, or the breaking/onset of a situation; also in a psalm title of uncertain musical reference.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun in existential negation (אין לו שחר), with 3fs pronominal suffix (שחרה), or in construct heading (אילת השחר)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the temporal phrase עֲלוֹת הַשַּׁחַר ('the rising of the dawn') preceded by כְּ, עַד, מִן, or בְּ (e.g., GEN 32:25; JOS 6:15; NEH 4:15; JON 4:7) and paired with rising early (שׁכם Hiphil). Poetic idioms include עַפְעַפֵּי שָׁחַר ('eyelids of dawn', JOB 3:9; JOB 41:10), כַנְפֵי שָׁחַר ('wings of dawn', PSA 139:9), and בֶּן שָׁחַר ('son of dawn', ISA 14:12). In ISA 47:11, לֹא תֵדְעִי שַׁחְרָהּ is parallel to שׁוֹאָה לֹא תֵדָעִי and לֹא תוּכְלִי כַּפְּרָהּ, making its exact nuance (whether 'its breaking/onset' or a figurative means of warding it off) contextually less certain. In PSA 22:1, עַל אַיֶּלֶת הַשַּׁחַר serves as a musical or liturgical superscription.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A dug pit or trap-pit, and by extension the subterranean pit of death and the grave.

senses.definition: An excavated pit or trench, especially one dug and concealed as a snare to trap animals or bring down enemies, or (in JOB 9:31) a foul ditch of filth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun, concrete (object of digging verbs or governed by בְּ)

senses.definition: The subterranean pit or realm of the dead, representing death, the grave, or fatal destruction from which one cannot return unaided.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (often with definite article or prepositions מִן, לְ, אֶל, בְּ, and once in construct בְּאֵר שַׁחַת)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Grammatically feminine where agreement appears (PRO 26:27 בָּהּ; EZK 19:4, 8 שַׁחְתָּם). In sense 1a, it frequently collocates with verbs of digging (כָּרָה, חָפַר), falling into (נָפַל בְּ), or being caught (נִתְפַּשׂ בְּ) alongside רֶשֶׁת ('net') and בּוֹר ('cistern/pit'). In sense 1b, it collocates with verbs of descent (יָרַד אֶל/לְ), perception (רָאָה), or rescue/ascent (פָּדָה, גָּאַל, הֵעֱלָה, הֵשִׁיב מִן/מִנִּי), standing parallel to שְׁאוֹל, רִמָּה ('worm'), and עָפָר ('dust'), and in contrast to 'light' and 'life'.

entries.core_meaning_summary: The powdery residue remaining after combustion, widely used as a ritual sign of mourning or penitence and as a figure for frailty and worthlessness.

senses.definition: The physical ash residue produced by burning (such as the remains of a sacrificed animal or something consumed by fire), or fine powder resembling it.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, concrete (singular, absolute or construct)

senses.definition: Ashes placed on the head, sat upon, spread out as a bed, or rolled in as a customary expression of grief, humiliation, fasting, or repentance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, often with prepositions (בְּ, עַל) or paired with שַׂק ('sackcloth')

senses.definition: Ashes used metaphorically to denote human lowliness and mortality, fragile or valueless speech, or futile, deluded pursuits.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun, in idiomatic pairing עָפָר וָאֵפֶר or figurative predicates/constructs

entries.collocations_and_notes: Commonly paired in the fixed phrase שַׂק וָאֵפֶר ('sackcloth and ashes', EST 4:1, EST 4:3, ISA 58:5, DAN 9:3) to signify public or personal mourning and penitence, and in the pairing עָפָר וָאֵפֶר ('dust and ashes', GEN 18:27, JOB 30:19, JOB 42:6) expressing mortal humility and degradation. Frequently governed by verbs of putting on the head (לָקַח עַל רֹאשׁ), sitting in/on (יָשַׁב בְּתוֹךְ / עַל), spreading out (יָצַע), or rolling in (הִתְפַּלֵּשׁ בְּ).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To cry out aloud in distress, oppression, or urgent need, especially as a plea to God or a deliverer for help.

senses.definition: To raise a loud cry of distress, suffering, or oppression in appeal for relief, justice, or rescue, without an explicit directional preposition.
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel verb, intransitive (used absolutely or with מִן indicating the source of oppression or place/time phrases)

senses.definition: To direct an urgent plea or cry for deliverance toward God (or figuratively of young ravens crying to God for food).
senses.grammatical_frame: Piel verb + אֶל (or עַל in PSA 18:42) marking the deity addressed

entries.collocations_and_notes: Attested exclusively in the Piel stem across all 21 occurrences. Frequently paired in poetic parallelism with verbs of calling or crying out such as צָעַק/זָעַק (JOB 19:7, JOB 35:9, LAM 3:8, HAB 1:2), קָרָא (PSA 18:7, ISA 58:9, JON 2:3), and נָאַק (JOB 24:12), and contrasted with being answered (עָנָה) or heard (שָׁמַע). Often describes the vulnerable—the poor (עָנִי) and needy (אֶבְיוֹן)—pleading for rescue. In PSA 18:42, עַל marks the deity as addressee instead of the usual אֶל.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A fish or aquatic creature (singular or plural), also denoting fish as market food and appearing in the name of Jerusalem's Fish Gate.

senses.definition: An aquatic vertebrate or sea creature, whether an individual large fish able to swallow a person or, in the plural, fish generally as inhabitants of the seas and targets of nets or harpoons.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; singular for an individual creature (with adjective גָּדוֹל or definite article) and plural (often construct דְּגֵי הַיָּם) for the class of aquatic animals

senses.definition: Fish gathered, transported, or sold as food or commercial merchandise.
