senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; singular collective (spelled דָּאג in NEH 13:16) or plural construct as object of verbs of gathering or bringing to market

senses.definition: Part of the proper compound name שַׁעַר הַדָּגִים ('the Fish Gate'), identifying a specific gate in the wall of Jerusalem.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine plural noun with definite article serving as nomen rectum after שַׁעַר ('gate')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in the plural construct phrase דְּגֵי הַיָּם ('fish of the sea', GEN 9:2, NUM 11:22, JOB 12:8, PSA 8:9, EZK 38:20, HOS 4:3, HAB 1:14, ZEP 1:3), often grouped with birds of the sky, land beasts, and creeping things. The plural also forms the fixed Jerusalem landmark שַׁעַר הַדָּגִים ('the Fish Gate', 2CH 33:14, NEH 3:3, NEH 12:39, ZEP 1:10). An orthographic variant with aleph (דָּאג) appears in NEH 13:16. In Jonah 2, the masculine הַדָּג alternates with the feminine הַדָּגָה (JON 2:2) for the creature that swallowed Jonah.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To rise, shine forth, or break out into view, used primarily of the sun and light, figuratively of divine appearance, and once of a skin affliction.

senses.definition: Of the sun or light: to rise above the horizon, come out, or shine forth into darkness or upon a surface.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active/intransitive stem; takes celestial or luminous subjects (שֶׁמֶשׁ, חֶרֶס, אוֹר), sometimes with prepositions לְ ('for') or עַל ('upon') or בַּחֹשֶׁךְ ('in darkness')

senses.definition: Of God, divine glory, or a metaphorical sun of righteousness: to dawn, appear radiantly, or shine forth in blessing and vindication upon people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active/intransitive stem; takes divine or figurative subjects (יְהוָה, כְּבוֹד יְהוָה, שֶׁמֶשׁ צְדָקָה) with prepositions מִן ('from'), עַל ('upon'), or לְ ('for')

senses.definition: Of a skin disease (צָרַעַת): to break out suddenly and visibly on the body.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active/intransitive stem; takes הַצָּרַעַת as subject with locative בְּ ('on his forehead')

entries.collocations_and_notes: All occurrences appear in the basic active/intransitive stem without causative or passive stem forms attested in this corpus. Most frequently takes הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ ('the sun') or אוֹר ('light') as its subject, often marking daybreak (GEN 32:32, JDG 9:33, 2KI 3:22, JON 4:8) or contrasting with the setting of the sun (בָּא, ECC 1:5). In poetic and prophetic texts, it pairs with terms for coming, appearing, or radiance (בָּא, הוֹפִיעַ, יֵרָאֶה in DEU 33:2, ISA 60:1-2) and contrasts with darkness (חֹשֶׁךְ, PSA 112:4, ISA 58:10).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Nineveh, a major Assyrian city and royal seat, also used metonymically for its ruler and inhabitants.

senses.definition: The major Assyrian city built by Asshur, serving as the royal residence of Sennacherib and repeatedly described as an exceptionally large city subject to divine warning or judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun (toponym); appears as direct object, subject, or object of spatial prepositions (בְּ, אֶל, עַל, בֵּין)

senses.definition: The populace, civic body, or kingdom of Nineveh as an entity represented by its king and citizens or addressed in prophetic pronouncements.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun in construct chains (אַנְשֵׁי נִינְוֵה 'men of Nineveh', מֶלֶךְ נִינְוֵה 'king of Nineveh', מַשָּׂא נִינְוֵה 'oracle concerning Nineveh') or personified as devastated

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently paired with the appositional title הָעִיר הַגְּדוֹלָה ('the great city', GEN 10:12, JON 1:2, JON 3:2, JON 4:11; cf. JON 3:3 עִיר גְּדוֹלָה לֵאלֹהִים). Associated with Asshur/Assyria (GEN 10:11, 2KI 19:36, ISA 37:37, ZEP 2:13) and the neighboring cities Rehoboth-Ir, Calah, and Resen (GEN 10:11-12). In Jonah, its enormous size is measured as a three-day walk and over 120,000 inhabitants plus livestock (JON 3:3, JON 4:11).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Fish as a collective category of aquatic life (and once an individual sea creature), along with a single verbal usage meaning to multiply abundantly.

senses.definition: Aquatic animals viewed collectively as a group or population inhabiting seas, rivers, or waters generally, whether under human rule, eaten as food, caught by fishermen, or dying during plagues and droughts.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular collective noun; frequently in construct before a body of water or with pronominal suffixes

senses.definition: An individual large marine creature inside whose belly Jonah remained and prayed.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun with definite article, denoting a single specific animal

senses.definition: To increase, swarm, or multiply into great numbers, said of descendants receiving a patriarchal blessing.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active/intransitive stem, third-person masculine plural imperfect verb followed by adverbial לָרֹב ('to abundance')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most commonly appears in construct chains specifying habitat, especially דְּגַת הַיָּם ('fish of the sea', GEN 1:26, GEN 1:28, EZK 47:10) and דְּגַת יְאֹרֶיךָ ('fish of your Nile-streams', EZK 29:4, EZK 29:5), as well as relative clauses locating them in the river or waters (EXO 7:18, EXO 7:21, DEU 4:18). Often paired in creation and dominion lists with birds of the sky, livestock, and creeping things (GEN 1:26, GEN 1:28). In JON 2:2, the feminine singular form הַדָּגָה refers to the same individual great sea creature called הַדָּג in adjacent verses. GEN 48:16 contains the lone verbal form tagged under this lemma (וְיִדְגּוּ לָרֹב).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Having great length physically, or metaphorically slow to anger, patient, and forbearing.

senses.definition: Having considerable physical length or span, describing the long wing-feathers of an eagle.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective in construct state (אֶרֶךְ) before definite concrete noun הָאֵבֶר

senses.definition: Restrained in expressing wrath, patient, and forbearing toward provocation or wrongdoing, predicated of both God and wise human beings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective in construct state (אֶרֶךְ) before אַפַּיִם (or singular suffixed אַפְּךָ in JER 15:15)

senses.definition: Patient and enduring in disposition or spirit, explicitly contrasted with arrogance ("haughty in spirit").
senses.grammatical_frame: Adjective in construct state (אֶרֶךְ) before רוּחַ, contrasted with גְּבַהּ־רוּחַ

entries.collocations_and_notes: Attested in this corpus exclusively in the construct state (אֶרֶךְ). Most frequently appears in the fixed idiom אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם ("slow to anger"), especially in liturgical formulas describing God alongside חַנּוּן ("gracious"), רַחוּם ("compassionate"), and רַב־חֶסֶד ("abounding in loyal love") (EXO 34:6; NUM 14:18; NEH 9:17; PSA 86:15; 103:8; 145:8; JOL 2:13; JON 4:2; NAM 1:3), as well as in wisdom proverbs contrasting self-control with quick temper (PRO 14:29; 15:18; 16:32). In JER 15:15, the idiom appears with a singular suffixed noun (לְאֶרֶךְ אַפְּךָ).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To throw, hurl, or cast an object, person, or force, and by extension to banish into exile or knock down.

senses.definition: To propel a weapon, cargo, or a person forcefully through the air or into water.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) + direct object + directional phrase (אל or על)

senses.definition: To be thrown or tossed (of a lot into the fold of a garment) to determine a decision.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative passive stem (Hophal) with location phrase בַּחֵיק and retained object marker אֶת־הַגּוֹרָל

senses.definition: To send forth or unleash a violent natural force, specifically a strong wind upon the sea.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil) with divine subject + רוּחַ גְּדוֹלָה + אֶל־הַיָּם

senses.definition: To cast out or fling people violently from their land into foreign exile or open exposure; in the passive, to be expelled or cast out.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative active stem (Hiphil), causative passive stem (Hophal), and reduplicated intensive active stem (Pilpel) with personal object + directional phrase (עַל / מֵעַל)

senses.definition: To be knocked flat, laid low, or overwhelmed helplessly, whether through terror or downfall.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative passive stem (Hophal), intransitive

entries.collocations_and_notes: Only attested in causative and reduplicated stems in the corpus (never in the basic active stem). Frequently pairs with directional prepositions such as אל ("into, toward") or על ("at, onto, upon"). Commonly governs objects like חֲנִית ("spear"), כֵּלִים ("cargo/vessels"), גּוֹרָל ("lot"), or people sent into exile. In ISA 22:17, the reduplicated active form takes the cognate noun טַלְטֵלָה ("a hurling") for emphasis; in JER 22:28, the causative passive stands in parallel with הֻשְׁלְכוּ ("they were thrown").

entries.core_meaning_summary: Dry land, solid ground free of water, or parched terrain, typically contrasted with the sea or bodies of water.

senses.definition: The solid landmass or shoreline of the earth as distinct from the sea and waters.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun, usually with definite article (הַיַּבָּשָׁה), paired or contrasted with יָם / יַמִּים / מַיִם

senses.definition: Firm, water-free ground, especially an exposed seabed or riverbed crossed on foot, or solid earth upon which liquid is poured.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun in prepositional phrases (בַּיַּבָּשָׁה, לְיַבָּשָׁה) or adverbial accusative of direction (EXO 4:9)

senses.definition: Arid, moisture-starved soil that receives poured water or streams, parallel to "thirsty ground."
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun without article governed by preposition עַל, parallel to צָמֵא

entries.collocations_and_notes: Feminine singular noun, almost always occurring without pluralization. Frequently paired or contrasted with יָם ("sea") or מַיִם ("waters") to form the cosmic pair "sea and dry land" (GEN 1:9–10; JON 1:9) or to mark the transition from water to land (JON 1:13; 2:11). The prepositional phrase בַּיַּבָּשָׁה ("on dry ground") is a recurring formula in narratives of Israel crossing the sea or the Jordan river (EXO 14:16, 22, 29; 15:19; JOS 4:22; NEH 9:11). In EXO 4:9, it appears as an adverbial accusative of direction ("onto the dry ground") alongside the distinct noun form בַּיַּבָּשֶׁת in the same verse.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To cover or enwrap, and in other contexts to grow faint, languish, or be overwhelmed in body or spirit.

senses.definition: To cover over, clothe, or enwrap completely, used figuratively of valleys covered with grain or violence enveloping arrogant people like a garment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal) + direct object (בָּר, שִׁית)

senses.definition: To conceal oneself or turn aside out of sight, describing God's elusiveness when sought by a sufferer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), intransitive with adverbial direction יָמִין ("on the right")

senses.definition: To lose strength, faint, collapse from hunger or exhaustion, or become emotionally and spiritually overwhelmed in distress.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active stem (Qal), passive/reflexive stem (Niphal, LAM 2:11), and reflexive stem (Hithpael), often with subjects לֵב, רוּחַ, נֶפֶשׁ, or starving people, frequently with עָלַי

senses.definition: Of livestock, to be in a feeble or weakened condition (or to lag behind/bear weakly), contrasted with vigorous animals.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative/inchoative stem (Hiphil) infinitive construct with בְּ + subject הַצֹּאן

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs across the basic active (Qal), passive/reflexive (Niphal), causative (Hiphil), and reflexive (Hithpael) stems. In lament and prayer contexts (PSA 61:3; 77:4; 102:1; 107:5; 142:4; 143:4; LAM 2:11–12; JON 2:8), it regularly pairs with inner-life nouns such as לֵב ("heart"), רוּחַ ("spirit"), or נֶפֶשׁ ("soul/life"), often with the preposition עָלַי ("upon/within me"). In GEN 30:42, the Hiphil infinitive is associated with הָעֲטֻפִים (the weaker animals) in contrast to הַקְּשֻׁרִים (the stronger/sturdy ones).
entries.uncertainty_note: In JOB 23:9, context establishes that God cannot be seen on the right, but does not decisively narrow whether יַעְטֹף means "he veils/covers himself" (related to sense 1a) or "he turns aside/away." In GEN 30:42, contrast with הַקְּשֻׁרִים indicates weakness or lesser vigor in the flock, though whether בְּהַעֲטִיף denotes general feebleness or late-season breeding cannot be determined from the verse alone.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An urgent interjection of entreaty or earnest address used to introduce a plea, prayer, or solemn appeal.

senses.definition: An urgent particle of entreaty introducing an imperative or jussive request, appealing to a superior or to God for mercy, deliverance, or action.
senses.grammatical_frame: interjection + (vocative) + imperative or jussive verb (often with נָא)

senses.definition: An earnest exclamation or solemn invocation introducing a confession, praise, or appeal in direct address to God without an immediate command.
senses.grammatical_frame: interjection + (vocative divine title) + declarative clause or question

entries.collocations_and_notes: Always occurs at the beginning of direct speech. Often spelled with final ה (אָנָּה) in 2KI 20:3, PSA 116:4, PSA 116:16, ISA 38:3, JON 1:14, JON 4:2, and with final א (אָנָּא) elsewhere. Frequently followed directly by a vocative divine name/title (יְהוָה or אֲדֹנָי) and paired with the enclitic particle נָא on a following imperative or jussive (e.g., GEN 50:17, 2KI 20:3, NEH 1:11, PSA 118:25, ISA 38:3, JON 1:14). Only GEN 50:17 addresses a human (Joseph); all other 12 occurrences address God in prayer or intercession.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adjective describing a disposition to show favor, kindness, and readiness to hear and forgive, almost exclusively applied to God.

senses.definition: Inclined to show favor, kindness, and readiness to help or forgive, used predicatively or as a substantivized epithet.
senses.grammatical_frame: predicative adjective in a nominal clause (often paired with רַחוּם or צַדִּיק)

senses.definition: Characterized by gracious favor and readiness to forgive, modifying a noun or title for God.
senses.grammatical_frame: attributive adjective modifying אֵל ('God') or אֱלוֹהַּ סְלִיחוֹת ('God of forgiveness')

entries.collocations_and_notes: In 11 of 13 occurrences, paired directly with רַחוּם ('compassionate/merciful'), either in the order רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן (EXO 34:6, PSA 86:15, PSA 103:8) or חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם (2CH 30:9, NEH 9:17, NEH 9:31, PSA 111:4, PSA 112:4, PSA 145:8, JOL 2:13, JON 4:2). Frequently forms part of a liturgical formula describing God as slow to anger (אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם) and abounding in steadfast love (רַב־חֶסֶד). In EXO 22:26 it grounds God's promise to hear the cry of the poor; in NEH 9:17, 31 it grounds forgiveness and refusal to abandon. In PSA 112:4, the subject of the descriptive adjectives ('gracious and compassionate and righteous') is syntactically implicit and may characterize either the upright person or God.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A masculine noun denoting physical taste or flavor, and figuratively mental discernment, sound judgment, rational demeanor, or an official decree.

senses.definition: The sensory flavor or taste perceived when eating or drinking (also used metaphorically for the preserved quality of undisturbed wine).
senses.grammatical_frame: noun (subject, construct, or with possessive suffix), often compared with כְּ ('like')

senses.definition: One's normal rational bearing, sanity, or sensible demeanor, specifically in the idiom of altering it to appear mad.
senses.grammatical_frame: direct object of the Piel verb שִׁנָּה ('to change/alter')

senses.definition: Sound judgment, practical discernment, or wise discretion in thought, speech, and conduct.
senses.grammatical_frame: noun in construct chains (טוֹב טַעַם, סָרַת טָעַם, מְשִׁיבֵי טָעַם) or as direct object of verbs of removing/blessing

senses.definition: An authoritative command, edict, or official decree issued by a ruler and nobles.
senses.grammatical_frame: מִן + noun in construct with royal authority (מִטַּעַם הַמֶּלֶךְ וּגְדֹלָיו) + לֵאמֹר

entries.collocations_and_notes: Common collocations include שִׁנָּה אֶת־טַעְמוֹ ('to alter one's rational bearing/sanity', i.e., feign madness, in 1SA 21:14 and PSA 34:1), סָרַת טָעַם ('lacking/turning away from discretion' in PRO 11:22), and מְשִׁיבֵי טָעַם ('those who give a reasoned/discerning answer' in PRO 26:16). In JER 48:11, sensory flavor (paired with רֵיחַ, 'scent') is used metaphorically in a comparison with settled wine to describe Moab's unchanged character. In JON 3:7, מִטַּעַם functions prepositively to introduce the authority issuing an official proclamation.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adjective describing deep compassion and mercy that withholds destruction and forgives, used almost exclusively of God.

senses.definition: Full of compassion and mercy, sparing from destruction and faithful to covenant, modifying a noun or title for God.
senses.grammatical_frame: attributive adjective modifying אֵל ('God') or אֱלוֹהַּ סְלִיחוֹת ('God of forgiveness')

senses.definition: Compassionate and merciful, acting to forgive iniquity and restrain wrath, used predicatively or as an appositional epithet.
senses.grammatical_frame: predicative or appositional adjective in a nominal or verbal clause (often paired with חַנּוּן)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears in 11 of 13 occurrences alongside חַנּוּן ('gracious'), and frequently in the broader formula 'slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love' (EXO 34:6, NEH 9:17, PSA 86:15, PSA 103:8, PSA 145:8, JOL 2:13, JON 4:2). Contexts consistently link this quality with withholding destruction, forgiving sin, turning back anger, and keeping covenant (DEU 4:31, NEH 9:17, 31, PSA 78:38). In PSA 112:4, the epithet lacks an explicit subject and may describe either the upright person or God.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An outer cloak, mantle, or royal robe; also attested once as splendor/majesty and once adjectivally as noble or splendid.

senses.definition: A large outer garment, cloak, mantle, or robe, whether fine and royal, prophetic, or coarse and hairy.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun; in construct (אַדֶּרֶת שֵׂעָר, אַדֶּרֶת שִׁנְעָר, אַדֶּרֶת אֵלִיָּהוּ), with possessive suffixes, or as object of verbs of wearing, taking, casting, and removing

senses.definition: Glory, splendor, or prized flourishing domain (parallel to גְּאוֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן 'the pride/majesty of the Jordan') whose devastation causes shepherds to wail.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun with 3mp possessive suffix (אַדַּרְתָּם); subject of passive verb שֻׁדְּדָה ('is devastated')

senses.definition: Noble, splendid, or majestic, used to describe a thriving, fruit-bearing vine.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular adjective modifying the feminine noun גֶּפֶן ('vine')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Most occurrences denote a prominent outer garment—ranging from a prized Babylonian garment (אַדֶּרֶת שִׁנְעָר, JOS 7:21) and a king's robe (JON 3:6) to a prophet's mantle (1KI 19:13, 19; 2KI 2:8, 13, 14) and a hairy cloak (אַדֶּרֶת שֵׂעָר, GEN 25:25; ZEC 13:4). In ZEC 11:3, אַדַּרְתָּם is subject of שֻׁדְּדָה ('is devastated') and stands in poetic parallelism with גְּאוֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן ('the pride/majesty of the Jordan'), denoting either the shepherds' glory/splendor or their flourishing domain. In EZK 17:8 (pausal אַדָּרֶת), it functions as a feminine singular adjective modifying גֶּפֶן ('vine').

entries.core_meaning_summary: To eat or sample a small amount of food, to perceive flavor with the palate, or figuratively to experience and recognize something as good.

senses.definition: To eat or take in even a small portion of food or nourishment, especially in contexts of fasting, abstinence, or sampling.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb taking a direct object of food or indefinite pron. (לֶחֶם, מְעַט דְּבַשׁ, מְאוּמָה)

senses.definition: To perceive the flavor of food or drink, or for the palate to discern taste.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb with human subject or חֵךְ (palate) as subject, taking food/drink as object or infinitive לֶאֱכֹל (to eat)

senses.definition: To experience personally, perceive, or recognize through direct encounter that someone or something is good or beneficial.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb introducing a content clause with כִּי־טוֹב (that ... is good)

entries.collocations_and_notes: All occurrences are in the basic active (Qal) stem. Frequently takes `לֶחֶם` ("food/bread"), `דְּבַשׁ` ("honey"), or `מְאוּמָה` ("anything at all") in contexts of fasting or solemn oaths (`1SA 14:24`, `2SA 3:35`, `JON 3:7`). In `1SA 14:43` it uses the emphatic infinitive absolute construction `טָעֹם טָעַמְתִּי` ("I indeed tasted"). In wisdom and poetic texts (`JOB 12:11`, `JOB 34:3`), the subject is `חֵךְ` ("palate"), paralleled by the ear testing words (`אֹזֶן מִלִּין תִּבְחָן`). In `PSA 34:9` and `PRO 31:18` it governs a `כִּי־טוֹב` ("that ... is good") object clause.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Deep water or watery depths of a sea or river, extended metaphorically to overwhelming distress, darkness, or total disposal.

senses.definition: The deep water or lowest parts of a sea, ocean, or river, into which objects sink or are cast, or where aquatic creatures and ships operate.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular and plural); frequently after בְּ ('in/into'), as an adverbial accusative of direction after הִשְׁלִיךְ (JON 2:4), or in construct with יָם or יְאֹר

senses.definition: Overwhelming depths or a dark abyss used figuratively for mortal peril, profound distress, or complete, irretrievable removal (as of sins).
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine noun (singular and plural); in construct (יְוֵן מְצוּלָה, מְצֻלוֹת יָם), after בְּ, or as subject of בָּלַע ('swallow')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently occurs in the plural (מְצוֹלֹת / מְצֻלוֹת) and in construct with יָם ('sea', PSA 68:23; MIC 7:19) or יְאֹר ('Nile/river', ZEC 10:11). Parallel to תְּהֹמֹת ('deeps', EXO 15:5), מַעֲמַקֵּי מַיִם ('deep waters', PSA 69:3), לְבַב יַמִּים ('heart of the seas', JON 2:4), and בּוֹר תַּחְתִּיּוֹת ('lowest pit', PSA 88:7). Often governed by the preposition בְּ ('in/into') or used with verbs of throwing/casting (הִשְׁלִיךְ) and descending (יָרַד).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To exert strenuous effort, labor, or toil at productive tasks, livelihood, or arduous investigation.

senses.definition: To work hard, labor, or exert strenuous effort in building, tending, earning sustenance, or pursuing human undertakings.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); intransitive, with בְּ ('at/on'), לְ ('for'), or infinitive לַעֲשׂוֹת ('to accomplish'), often with cognate noun עָמָל

senses.definition: To strive strenuously or exert mental effort in attempting to investigate and discover something.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal); followed by purpose infinitive לְבַקֵּשׁ ('to seek')

entries.collocations_and_notes: All 11 occurrences in this packet are in the simple active stem (Qal). Heavily concentrated in Ecclesiastes, where it characteristically appears in a cognate construction with the noun עָמָל ('toil that one toils') and the phrase תַּחַת הַשָּׁמֶשׁ ('under the sun', ECC 1:3; 2:19; 2:20; 5:17). Also collocates with בְּ marking the object worked on (PSA 127:1; ECC 2:21; JON 4:10) and with לְ marking beneficiary or goal (PRO 16:26; ECC 5:15).

entries.core_meaning_summary: As a verb, to vomit up or figuratively spew out inhabitants; as a noun, vomit or regurgitated matter.

senses.definition: To eject food, a swallowed person, or (figuratively) swallowed wealth from the stomach through the mouth.
senses.grammatical_frame: Causative-type verb stem (Hiphil); transitive with direct object (pronominal suffix or אֶת + noun)

senses.definition: Used figuratively of the land expelling or spewing out its inhabitants because of defilement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Simple active stem (Qal, LEV 18:28) and causative-type stem (Hiphil); transitive with הָאָרֶץ ('the land') as subject and אֶת + inhabitants as object

senses.definition: Matter ejected from the stomach; vomit associated with drunkenness and defilement.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine noun; after מָלֵא ('be full of') or governed by preposition בְּ ('in') with pronominal suffix

entries.collocations_and_notes: This packet groups both verbal and nominal forms under this lemma. Verbally, it occurs chiefly in the causative-type stem (Hiphil) as a transitive verb taking a direct object (marked by אֶת or a pronominal suffix), and once in the simple active stem (Qal, קָאָה in LEV 18:28) with the exact same transitive syntax and meaning as the adjacent causative-type form (תָקִיא). Nominally, קִיא denotes vomit, associated with drunkenness and filth (ISA 19:14; ISA 28:8; JER 48:26).

entries.core_meaning_summary: The numeral ten thousand, or in the dual/plural an indefinitely vast multitude (myriads).

senses.definition: The exact numerical unit of ten thousand (10,000), used either alone or multiplied by a preceding numeral when counting people, coins, or metal weights.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine numeral (singular or plural), standalone or following a multiplier (2, 4, 6, 12) in apposition to counted nouns

senses.definition: An indefinitely huge number or vast multitude of troops, chariots, or people.
senses.grammatical_frame: Dual (רִבֹּתַיִם) or plural (רִבֹּאוֹת) noun without a preceding multiplier, in poetic parallelism or as a direct object

entries.collocations_and_notes: Exhibits varied orthography across the corpus: singular `רִבּוֹ` / `רִבּוֹא`, plural `רִבּוֹת` / `רִבֹּאוֹת`, and dual `רִבֹּתַיִם`. In `1CH 29:7` it appears both for a standalone 10,000 and combined with `וּשְׁמוֹנַת אֲלָפִים` ("and eight thousand", i.e., 18,000). In `EZR 2:64` and `NEH 7:66`, `אַרְבַּע רִבּוֹא` totals 40,000 within 42,360. In `NEH 7:70-71` both plural `שְׁתֵּי רִבּוֹת` and singular `שְׁתֵּי רִבּוֹא` denote 20,000.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To dig, bore, or break through a barrier or surface, or to row vigorously through water.

senses.definition: To dig, bore, or break through a wall, house, or into the underworld so as to create an opening or gain entry or exit.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb taking a direct object (houses) or prepositional phrase with בְּ- (in a wall, into Sheol), optionally with לְ- (for oneself) or בְּיָד (by hand)

senses.definition: To row vigorously with oars (literally digging into the water) in an effort to bring a vessel back to shore.
glosses: to pull hard at the oars
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb used intransitively with an infinitive of purpose (לְהָשִׁיב, to bring back) in a nautical context

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs exclusively in the basic active (Qal) stem. Commonly takes `בַּקִּיר` ("in/through the wall") as a prepositional complement (`EZK 8:8`, `EZK 12:5`, `EZK 12:7`, `EZK 12:12`), sometimes with reflexive `לְ-` ("for oneself") or instrument `בְּיָד` ("by hand"). In `JOB 24:16` it takes a direct object (`בָּתִּים`, "houses"), and in `AMO 9:2` it takes `בִשְׁאוֹל` ("into Sheol") as a hyperbole for extreme subterranean hiding. In `JON 1:13` it describes sailors rowing against a raging sea.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A violent windstorm or tempest, also used figuratively for overwhelming divine wrath or disaster.

senses.definition: A fierce storm or tempest of wind, especially a violent gale threatening ships at sea.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, often with the adjective גָּדוֹל (great) or parallel to רוּחַ (wind)

senses.definition: A figurative storm representing overwhelming divine judgment, anger, or military devastation sweeping down upon enemies or the wicked.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun, often with preposition בְּ- (with/in) or modified by participles (מִתְחוֹלֵל, מִתְגּוֹרֵר) and paired with חֵמָה (wrath) or סוּפָה (whirlwind)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Often modified by `גָּדוֹל` ("great") in narrative and prophecy (`JER 25:32`, `JON 1:4`, `JON 1:12`) or by reflexive/whirling participles `מִתְחוֹלֵל` (`JER 23:19`) and `מִתְגּוֹרֵר` (`JER 30:23`). Frequently paired in poetic parallelism with `רוּחַ` ("wind"), `סוּפָה` ("whirlwind/tempest"), `חֵמָה` ("wrath"), and `סַעֲרַת יְהוָה` ("tempest of YHWH").

entries.core_meaning_summary: To rage or surge like a storm (of the sea or attackers), to be inwardly agitated or storm-tossed, and in intensive stems to whirl away or scatter violently as by a tempest.

senses.definition: To surge violently, rage, or grow tempestuous (said of the sea).
senses.grammatical_frame: Base stem (Qal) active participle following hōlēk ("going/increasing"), with "the sea" as subject and optional preposition ʿal ("against")

senses.definition: To rush forward furiously or charge like a storm against an adversary.
senses.grammatical_frame: Base stem (Qal) finite verb with plural subject and infinitive of purpose ("to scatter")

senses.definition: To be storm-tossed, battered, or thrown into turmoil (used substantively/attributively of an afflicted, uncomforted city).
senses.grammatical_frame: Base stem (Qal) feminine singular active participle used as a vocative descriptor

senses.definition: To become deeply agitated, disturbed, or enraged in one's mind or heart over an event.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) finite verb with lēb ("heart/mind") as subject and preposition ʿal ("over")

senses.definition: To be whirled or blown away like chaff from a threshing floor.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive stem (Poel) finite verb used intransitively/passively with "chaff" as subject and preposition min ("from")

senses.definition: To sweep away or scatter people violently across foreign lands as by a storm.
senses.grammatical_frame: Intensive transitive stem (Piel/Poel) finite verb with direct object suffix and preposition ʿal ("among/upon")

entries.collocations_and_notes: Observed across three stems: the base active stem (Qal) describes the sea growing tempestuous (paired with hōlēk "going/increasing" in JON 1:11, JON 1:13), an army rushing storm-like into attack (HAB 3:14), and a personified city tossed in turmoil (ISA 54:11, parallel to "afflicted" and "uncomforted"). The passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) in 2KI 6:11 takes lēb ("heart/mind") as subject to denote inner agitation or distress. Two intensive-stem forms appear with long vowels: in HOS 13:3 yəsōʿēr describes chaff whirled from a threshing floor (parallel to smoke from an opening), and in ZEC 7:14 ʾēsāʿărēm takes a direct object suffix with ʿal ("upon/among") to denote God sweeping people away in storm-like scattering across the nations.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To fall into or be in a state of deep sleep, unconsciousness, or overwhelming stupor (attested solely in the passive/reflexive stem).

senses.definition: To fall fast asleep or remain in heavy slumber, especially when vigilance or labor is expected.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) finite verb or participle, intransitive (with optional temporal preposition bə- "during")

senses.definition: To sink into a deep stupor, unconsciousness, or visionary swoon, whether from overwhelming awe, divine rebuke, or lethal exhaustion.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive/reflexive stem (Niphal) finite verb or participle (including periphrastic hāyîtî + participle), often with spatial phrase ("upon my face to the ground") or causal preposition min ("at/because of")
senses.semantic_domain: Physiology and Perception / Stupor and Trance

entries.collocations_and_notes: All seven occurrences appear exclusively in the passive/reflexive stem (Niphal). In ordinary sleep contexts it follows šākab ("lie down", JON 1:5), stands in contrast to gathering crops in summer (PRO 10:5), or is addressed with mah ləkā ("what is with you?", JON 1:6). In extraordinary/crisis contexts it combines with ʿal pānay ("upon my face [to the ground]") during an overwhelming vision (DAN 8:18, DAN 10:9, once periphrastically with hāyîtî "I was"), follows miggaʿărātəkā ("at your rebuke") for stunned chariotry (PSA 76:7), or appears alongside yāʿap̄ ("faint/exhausted") and mût ("die") when Sisera is struck down while sleeping/unconscious (JDG 4:21).

entries.core_meaning_summary: Fierce, surging anger or wrath of humans or God, and by extension the violent raging of a stormy sea.

senses.definition: Intense anger, fury, or indignation felt by a human ruler, warriors, or God, often manifested in harsh punishment, slaughter, or judgment.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun; governed by preposition bə- ("in/with"), or as subject/object in construct phrases (with king, YHWH, or ʾap̄ "anger")

senses.definition: Violent turbulence, storminess, or raging motion of the sea.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun with possessive suffix referring to the sea, governed by preposition min ("from") after verb of ceasing

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently governed by the preposition bə- ("in, with") to express the manner or emotional state accompanying violent or punitive action (2CH 16:10, 2CH 28:9, ISA 30:30). Construct phrases include zaʿap̄ ʾap̄ ("furious rage of anger", ISA 30:30) and zaʿap̄ YHWH ("wrath of YHWH", MIC 7:9). In PRO 19:12 it is likened to a young lion's growl and contrasted with rāṣôn ("favor, goodwill"). In JON 1:15 it governs the preposition min ("from") after ʿāmad ("stand still") to describe the subsiding of a storm at sea.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Coercive physical force or harshness, intense vehemence in speech or outcry, and structural repair or reinforcement of a building.

senses.definition: Coercive strength, physical force, or severe harshness used in oppressing, seizing property, or ruling over others.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun governed by preposition bə- ("with/by"), functioning adverbially with verbs of oppressing, taking, or ruling

senses.definition: Great intensity, sharpness, or earnestness in verbal contention or desperate outcry.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun governed by preposition bə- ("with"), functioning adverbially with verbs of quarreling or calling out

senses.definition: Physical repair, reinforcement, or structural maintenance of a building.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun governed by preposition lə- ("for"), expressing purpose regarding a building

entries.collocations_and_notes: Five of the six occurrences appear in the adverbial prepositional phrase bəḥozqâ ("by force / harshly / vehemently / earnestly"), modifying verbs of oppression, quarreling, seizing, ruling, or crying out. In EZK 34:4 it is paired with bəp̄ārek ("with harshness/rigor"). In 2KI 12:13 it takes the preposition lə- ("for") in parallel with the verb phrase ləḥazzēq ʾet bedeq ("to repair the breach of"), denoting structural repair/upkeep of the temple.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To surround, encompass, or close in upon someone, especially used of threatening waters or overwhelming peril.

senses.definition: In the basic active (Qal) stem, of deep waters: to engulf or close in around a person on all sides.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb with direct object suffix (person)

senses.definition: In the basic active (Qal) stem, figuratively of mortal perils, deathly breakers or cords, or innumerable calamities (רָעוֹת): to encompass, beset, or close in upon a person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb with direct object suffix or with עַל + object

entries.collocations_and_notes: All occurrences appear in the basic active (Qal) stem in 3rd-person plural suffix conjugation (qatal) forms. Commonly takes an accusative pronominal suffix on the verb (2SA 22:5; PSA 18:5; PSA 116:3; JON 2:6), or the preposition עַל (PSA 40:13). Parallel verbs in context include סבב ('to surround', JON 2:6), בעת ('to terrify', 2SA 22:5; PSA 18:5), מצא ('to come upon/find', PSA 116:3), and נשׂג ('to overtake', PSA 40:13).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A skilled mariner, ship's pilot, or seafarer; in the compound title רַב הַחֹבֵל, the ship's captain.

senses.definition: A skilled seafarer or ship's pilot/navigator responsible for steering or managing a vessel, contrasted with rowers (EZK 27:8) and grouped with sailors and oar-handlers (EZK 27:27, 27:29).
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine plural (with suffixal forms or construct חֹבְלֵי הַיָּם)

senses.definition: In the construct title רַב הַחֹבֵל ('chief of the seafarer[s]/crew'), collective or generic singular designating the ship's crew or pilots under a captain's authority.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine singular determined, governed in construct by רַב (רַב הַחֹבֵל, 'captain')

entries.collocations_and_notes: In EZK 27:8, Tyre's חֲכָמִים ('wise/skilled men') are identified as her חֹבְלִים, contrasted with the inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad who serve as rowers (שָׁטִים). In EZK 27:27 and 27:29, it stands alongside מַלָּחִים ('sailors') and תֹּפְשֵׂי מָשׁוֹט ('oar-handlers'). In JON 1:6, the singular form appears in the construct phrase רַב הַחֹבֵל ('chief of the seafarers/pilots'), denoting the ship's commanding officer.
entries.uncertainty_note: While EZK 27:8 contrasts חֹבְלִים (identified with skilled/wise men) against rowers (שָׁטִים), EZK 27:27 and 27:29 pair חֹבְלִים closely with מַלָּחִים ('sailors'), leaving it somewhat uncertain whether חֹבֵל always denotes a specialized pilot/helmsman or can also function more broadly as a term for seafarer/crewman.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Breaking sea waves or surges, frequently used poetically for overwhelming distress, mortal peril, or divine wrath.

senses.definition: Crashing waves or surges of the sea, attested in plural form (in JON 2:4 within a poetic lament spoken from the deep of the sea).
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun; in construct with יָם ('sea') or with possessive suffix + עָבַר עַל ('pass over')

senses.definition: Figuratively, overwhelming surges of mortal danger, sorrow, or divine anger that engulf or afflict a person.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun; in construct with מָוֶת ('death') or with possessive suffix as subject of אָפַף ('encompass') or עָבַר עַל ('pass over'), or object of עִנָּה ('afflict')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Attested only in the plural (construct `מִשְׁבְּרֵי` in 2SA 22:5 and PSA 93:4; with 2ms suffix `מִשְׁבָּרֶיךָ` in PSA 42:8, PSA 88:8, and JON 2:4). Frequently paired with `גַּלֶּיךָ` ("your waves") in the identical formula `כָּל־מִשְׁבָּרֶיךָ וְגַלֶּיךָ עָלַי עָבָרוּ` (PSA 42:8; JON 2:4). Paralleled with `נַחֲלֵי בְלִיַּעַל` ("torrents of ruin") in 2SA 22:5 and `מַיִם רַבִּים` ("many waters") in PSA 93:4.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A journey, walking distance, physical walkway/passage, or freedom of movement/access among others.

senses.definition: The act, duration, or spatial distance of a journey or walk on foot, including the span of an expedition or a city's extent measured in days of walking.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun; subject of הָיָה with עַד־מָתַי ('how long will your journey be') or in construct with a time span ('a walk of X days')

senses.definition: A paved walkway, corridor, or open passage alongside building chambers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun in architectural description followed by dimensional measurement (אֶת/עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת רֹחַב)

senses.definition: Right of access, free passage, or ability to walk and move about among a group of attendants.
senses.grammatical_frame: Plural noun as direct object of נָתַן ('give') + לְ + בֵּין ('between/among')

entries.collocations_and_notes: In construct with time expressions (`מַהֲלַךְ שְׁלֹשֶׁת יָמִים` in JON 3:3; `מַהֲלַךְ יוֹם אֶחָד` in JON 3:4) to indicate spatial distance measured by walking duration. In EZK 42:4 juxtaposed with `דֶּרֶךְ` ("way/path"). In ZEC 3:7 appears in the plural `מַהְלְכִים` governed by `נָתַתִּי לְךָ ... בֵּין הָעֹמְדִים הָאֵלֶּה`.
entries.uncertainty_note: The exact nuance of the plural מַהְלְכִים in ZEC 3:7 is somewhat uncertain from context alone: it most likely denotes abstract free access or goings among the standing figures, though a concrete sense of 'walking companions/attendants' cannot be entirely ruled out.

entries.core_meaning_summary: To cover, overlay, or wrap up; and to faint, swoon, or collapse from exhaustion, heat, thirst, or affliction.

senses.definition: To be overlaid, covered, or encrusted with decorative gemstones.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive of the intensive stem (participle) + noun of material (סַפִּירִים)

senses.definition: To wrap or shroud oneself in garments or a veil so as to conceal one's appearance.
senses.grammatical_frame: Reflexive-intensive stem (Hithpael), intransitive, paired with כָּסָה ('cover') + בַּצָּעִיף ('with a veil')

senses.definition: To faint, grow weak, or collapse physically from severe thirst, intense heat, or overwhelming distress.
senses.grammatical_frame: Passive of the intensive stem (ISA 51:20) or reflexive-intensive stem (AMO 8:13, JON 4:8); intransitive, optionally with בְּ marking the cause (e.g., בַּצָּמָא 'from thirst')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs in the passive of the intensive stem (Pual: SNG 5:14, ISA 51:20) and in the reflexive-intensive stem (Hithpael: GEN 38:14, AMO 8:13, JON 4:8). In GEN 38:14 it immediately follows `וַתְּכַס בַּצָּעִיף` ("and she covered herself with the veil"). Causes of fainting/collapse include thirst (`בַּצָּמָא`, AMO 8:13), intense sun/heat (`וַתַּךְ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ עַל־רֹאשׁ יוֹנָה`, JON 4:8), and divine wrath (`מְלֵאִים חֲמַת יְהוָה`, ISA 51:20).

entries.core_meaning_summary: A fast-growing, shade-producing plant that sprouts rapidly and withers quickly when attacked by a worm.

senses.definition: A rapidly growing plant tall or broad enough to cast shade over a person's head, vulnerable to being attacked by a worm and quickly withering.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine singular noun; object of מָנָה ('appoint'), נָכָה ('strike'), and חוּס עַל ('have pity on'), and subject of עָלָה ('grow up'), יָבֵשׁ ('wither'), and אָבַד ('perish')

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears only in the narrative of JON 4:6–10 (twice in JON 4:6: once indefinite, once with the definite article). Associated verbs and phrases: `וַיַּעַל מֵעַל לְיוֹנָה לִהְיוֹת צֵל עַל־רֹאשׁוֹ` ("it grew up over Jonah to be shade over his head"), `וַתַּךְ ... וַיִּיבָשׁ` ("struck ... and it withered"), `לֹא עָמַלְתָּ בּוֹ וְלֹא גִדַּלְתּוֹ` ("you did not labor over it nor make it grow"), and `שֶׁבִּן־לַיְלָה הָיָה וּבִן־לַיְלָה אָבָד` ("which came up in a night and perished in a night").
entries.uncertainty_note: All occurrences appear within the single episode of Jonah 4:6–10. While the context clearly establishes that it is a fast-growing, shade-giving, perishable plant, the exact botanical species is not specified in the primary text.

entries.core_meaning_summary: Proper name of a coastal port city (Joppa) on the sea, serving as a harbor for maritime travel and timber transport toward Jerusalem as well as a geographic border landmark.

senses.definition: A coastal city and maritime port used for embarking on sea voyages and receiving sea-borne cargo such as timber from Lebanon destined for Jerusalem, and cited as a landmark opposite a tribal border.
senses.grammatical_frame: Proper noun: object of the preposition מוּל ("opposite"), nomen rectum after יָם ("sea of"), or directional complement after יָרַד ("go down to")

entries.collocations_and_notes: Frequently appears in the construct chain יָם יָפוֹ / יָם יָפוֹא ("the sea of Joppa") as the coastal landing point for cedar timber floated from Lebanon on the way up to Jerusalem (2CH 2:15; EZR 3:7). Spelled with a final aleph (יָפוֹא) in EZR 3:7 and without it (יָפוֹ) in the other three passages.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A sailor or mariner who crews and works aboard a seagoing ship.

senses.definition: A person who works aboard a ship on the sea; a sailor or seafarer.
senses.grammatical_frame: Noun, masculine plural (attested in absolute, determined, and suffixal forms)

entries.collocations_and_notes: Attested exclusively in the masculine plural (absolute, definite, and with pronominal suffixes referring to ships or Tyre). Frequently paired with or placed alongside חֹבְלִים (EZK 27:27, 27:29) and תֹּפְשֵׂי מָשׁוֹט ('oar-handlers', EZK 27:29), and directly associated with ships (אֳנִיּוֹת, EZK 27:9; אֳנִיָּה, JON 1:5) and cargo/gear (כֵּלִים, JON 1:5).

entries.core_meaning_summary: To grow calm, subside, or cease from turbulent movement or conflict.

senses.definition: In the basic active (Qal) stem, of the sea or turbulent waters: to subside, grow still, and cease raging (often with מֵעַל indicating relief for those threatened by the storm).
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb, intransitive; optionally followed by מֵעַל + person

senses.definition: In the basic active (Qal) stem, figuratively of strife or contention (מָדוֹן): to die down, subside, or cease when its instigator is absent.
senses.grammatical_frame: Basic active (Qal) verb, intransitive with abstract subject (מָדוֹן)

entries.collocations_and_notes: All occurrences appear in the basic active (Qal) stem in prefix conjugation (imperfect/jussive) forms. In JON 1:11–12, takes the prepositional phrase מֵעַל ('from upon [someone]') to denote the storm-tossed sea calming down so as no longer to endanger those on board. In PRO 26:20, parallels תִּכְבֶּה אֵשׁ ('a fire goes out').

entries.core_meaning_summary: A noun denoting either the uniform form, shape, or cut of crafted objects alongside their dimensions, or (in the plural) the lowest extremities or bases of mountains.

senses.definition: The uniform shape, form, or standardized proportion shared by matching crafted items, paired directly with measurement (מִדָּה).
senses.grammatical_frame: Singular noun modified by אֶחָד ("one") in apposition/coordination with מִדָּה אַחַת ("one measure") and followed by לְ ("for")

senses.definition: The lowest parts, bases, or extreme limits of mountains reached when descending into the subterranean depths.
senses.grammatical_frame: Construct plural noun (קִצְבֵי) governed by the directional preposition לְ ("to") before הָרִים ("mountains") with a verb of downward motion (יָרַדְתִּי)

entries.collocations_and_notes: In both 1KI 6:25 and 1KI 7:37, קֶצֶב occurs in the fixed phrase מִדָּה אַחַת (וְ)קֶצֶב אֶחָד לְ... ("one measure [and] one shape/form for..."), describing paired or serial crafted temple furnishings. In JON 2:7, it appears in the construct plural לְקִצְבֵי הָרִים ("to the bases/extremities of mountains") as the goal of יָרַדְתִּי ("I went down").
entries.uncertainty_note: While the craftsmanship sense alongside מִדָּה is well supported by 1KI 6:25 and 1KI 7:37, the exact distinction between קֶצֶב and מִדָּה ("measure") is not fully specified by those formulas. The poetic plural קִצְבֵי הָרִים appears only in JON 2:7, so whether it refers specifically to mountain bases/roots or more generally to subterranean boundaries/extremities rests on a single context.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A masculine personal name identifying the father of the prophet Jonah.

senses.definition: Proper name of the father of the prophet Jonah.
senses.grammatical_frame: Masculine proper noun as the second element of the patronymic construct phrase יוֹנָה בֶן אֲמִתַּי ("Jonah son of Amittai")

entries.collocations_and_notes: Appears exclusively in the patronymic construct phrase יוֹנָה בֶן אֲמִתַּי ("Jonah son of Amittai"). In 2KI 14:25 it is further apposed with הַנָּבִיא אֲשֶׁר מִגַּת הַחֵפֶר ("the prophet who was from Gath-hepher").

entries.core_meaning_summary: A verb attested in two distinct stems with separate contextual meanings: in the Qal, growing sleek or plump alongside becoming fat; in the Hithpael, giving thought or showing favorable regard toward someone in danger.

senses.definition: To become sleek, smooth, or plump in physical condition, paired directly with growing fat in a description of prosperous wrongdoers.
senses.grammatical_frame: Qal suffix-conjugation (perfect), 3rd person plural, intransitive, paired asyndetically with שָׁמְנוּ

senses.definition: To give thought to, turn attention toward, or take account of someone so as to spare or help them.
senses.grammatical_frame: Hithpael prefix-conjugation (imperfect), 3rd person masculine singular, with divine subject and prepositional complement לָנוּ ("to/for us")

entries.collocations_and_notes: In JER 5:28, the Qal plural עָשְׁתוּ is placed asyndetically right after שָׁמְנוּ ("they grew fat"), forming a pair describing physical thriving among those who neglect justice. In JON 1:6, the Hithpael יִתְעַשֵּׁת takes הָאֱלֹהִים as subject and is followed by the prepositional phrase לָנוּ ("for/to us") and a result clause ("so that we do not perish"). No shared collocations link the two stems in these verses.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only twice in the corpus, once in the Qal (JER 5:28) and once in the Hithpael (JON 1:6), with no overlapping context. In JER 5:28, whether the Qal verb specifically denotes physical sleekness/glossiness, stoutness, or general prosperity cannot be narrowed further from its sole pairing with שָׁמְנוּ. In JON 1:6, whether the Hithpael denotes mental reflection, compassionate regard, or active intervention remains slightly open, as does any semantic relationship between the two stems.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A relational particle attested only with prefixed prepositions and pronominal suffixes, marking group affiliation ("belonging to") after מִן and causation ("on account of") after בְּ.

senses.definition: Indicates belonging, membership, or partisan alignment with a group when compounded with partitive מִן ("from/of") and a pronominal suffix.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prefixed by מִן and followed by a pronominal suffix (מִשֶּׁלָּנוּ), modifying the interrogative pronoun מִי ("who")

senses.definition: Indicates the person who is the cause or reason for an event or condition when compounded with בְּ and a pronominal suffix.
senses.grammatical_frame: Prefixed by בְּ and followed by a pronominal suffix (בְשֶׁלִּי), functioning as a causal prepositional predicate in a verbless clause

entries.collocations_and_notes: Attested exclusively in prefixed prepositional compounds with pronominal suffixes: מִשֶּׁלָּנוּ ("from/of those belonging to us" after the interrogative מִי in 2KI 6:11) and בְשֶׁלִּי ("because of me" introducing the reason for a storm in JON 1:12).
entries.uncertainty_note: Appears only twice in the corpus and exclusively inside the prepositional compounds מִשֶּׁלָּנוּ and בְשֶׁלִּי with pronominal suffixes; its independent syntactic behavior, use before nouns, and any broader range of relational meanings cannot be determined from these two occurrences alone.

entries.core_meaning_summary: An adjective describing a harsh, oppressive quality of an east wind that accompanies intense sun and causes distress or faintness.

senses.definition: Characterizing an east wind appointed at sunrise as harsh, oppressive, or scorching in a context where the sun beats down and causes faintness.
senses.grammatical_frame: Attributive feminine singular adjective modifying the noun phrase רוּחַ קָדִים ("east wind")

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs once in the feminine singular form חֲרִישִׁית modifying the feminine construct phrase רוּחַ קָדִים ("east wind") in a narrative sequence where God appoints the wind at sunrise and the sun beats on Jonah's head, causing him to grow faint.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once in the corpus (JON 4:8). While the narrative context indicates that the wind contributes to Jonah's distress and faintness alongside the beating sun, the single occurrence does not narrow whether the adjective specifically denotes scorching heat, sultry stillness, or another harsh atmospheric quality.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A seagoing vessel or ship having lower interior spaces into which a passenger can descend.

senses.definition: A seagoing ship or vessel containing lower interior quarters into which one may go down to lie down and sleep.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun with definite article as the second member of a construct phrase (יַרְכְּתֵי הַסְּפִינָה), following the preposition אֶל ("to, into") after the verb יָרַד ("go down")

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs once with the definite article in the construct phrase יַרְכְּתֵי הַסְּפִינָה ("the inner/lower recesses of the ship"), following an earlier clause in the same verse that refers to the vessel as אֳנִיָּה and mentions sailors (הַמַּלָּחִים) throwing gear into the sea.
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once in the corpus (JON 1:5). The maritime setting with sailors, cargo, and the parallel noun אֳנִיָּה clearly identifies it as a seagoing ship, but a single occurrence does not reveal whether it carries a specialized nuance distinguishing a particular type or decked vessel from other terms for ships.

entries.core_meaning_summary: A spoken message or public announcement delivered as a proclamation to a city.

senses.definition: A public message or announcement spoken by divine instruction and proclaimed to a population.
senses.grammatical_frame: Feminine singular noun with definite article marked by אֶת as the direct object of the Qal imperative verb קְרָא ("call out, proclaim")

entries.collocations_and_notes: Occurs once with the definite article as the direct object of the imperative verb קְרָא ("proclaim, call out") addressed to Nineveh (אֵלֶיהָ), and qualified by the relative clause אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי דֹּבֵר אֵלֶיךָ ("which I am speaking to you").
entries.uncertainty_note: Occurs only once in the corpus (JON 3:2). While its role as the object of a verb of proclaiming and the modifying clause "which I am speaking to you" clearly establish the sense of a spoken proclamation or message, a single attestation cannot establish whether the noun also had broader uses such as a summons, cry, or reading.
